Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_open_cover: Each point of the pulled-back support maps into the original support. Use the inverse image of its original neighborhood, which contains that point. The open restriction of the map gives the local order certificate by hypothesis. Its structural map, pulled-back ideals and memory agree with the required restrictions because the maps through the two open inclusions have equal composites. Apply the localization constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_orderCertificat: Apply simultaneous induction to the order and principalization certificates. The elementary constructors remain valid under pullback of supports, ideals and memory. For a principalization certificate built from an order certificate, pull back the factorization and use the induction hypothesis for that order certificate. For both localization cases take inverse images of the specified neighborhoods. For an order certificate built by descent, use the smooth-divisor restriction result and the induction hypotheses for the descended principalization certificates. This supplies the restriction for the given order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_smoothDivisor_c:
For each point of the pulled-back support, choose the inverse image of the original neighborhood of its image. Pull the smooth divisor back to this open. Stability gives smoothness and the support containments pull back. Transport any present auxiliary ideal along the induced map of hypersurfaces, and keep absent values absent.

For an absent ideal the required support preimage is open by the pulled-back openness result. For a present ideal the hypersurface map preserves nonvanishing on components. It also transports the local equality away from memory and, by the all-opens hypothesis on the original hypersurface, the descended principalization certificate. Thus the new data satisfy the descent conditions and give the order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_support_subset: The inverse image of the support lies in the inverse image of memory. The support of the pulled-back ideal is that inverse image, so the memory constructor gives an order certificate on every open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_two_le: The marking does not change under restriction. Its lower bound still applies, so the large-marking case gives the required order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_mul_: Pullback preserves the ideal product and sends the support of the first factor to its inverse image, which lies in the pulled-back memory. The marking inequality stays the same. A point in the pulled-back target support maps to a point where the second factor has the required order. The order inequality for pullback gives at least that order at the source point. The order certificate for the second factor pulls back by hypothesis. These data assemble the principalization certificate on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_open: For each point in the pulled-back target support, its image lies in the original support. Choose the given original neighborhood of that image and take its inverse image. The restricted map to the original neighborhood is an open immersion, so the local hypothesis supplies a principalization certificate there. The commuting square of open inclusions identifies its structural map, ideals and memory with the restrictions of the new ambient data. The localization constructor assembles these certificates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_prin: Induct simultaneously on principalization and order certificates, requiring each to restrict along every open immersion. The memory and large-marking cases follow by support containment and the same marking. The factorization case uses the pulled-back product and the induction hypothesis on its order certificate. The localization cases follow by taking inverse images of the chosen covering opens. The descent case follows by pulling back the smooth divisors, optional ideals and descended certificates using the open-immersion stability assumptions. These cases establish the required restriction property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_supp: For any open immersion, the pulled-back target support is the inverse image of the original support. It is contained in the inverse image of memory by the given containment. The memory case therefore gives a principalization certificate on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_two_: The marking is retained on any open and is at least two. The large-marking constructor supplies a principalization certificate for the pulled-back data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubscheme_comp: The map of closed subschemes is induced by the given ambient morphism and the pulled-back ideal. The defining compatibility of that map is that its composite with the original inclusion equals the pulled-back inclusion followed by the ambient morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubscheme_comp_assoc: Compose the compatibility of the induced subscheme map with the remaining morphism. Associativity gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_comap_eq_comap_morphismRes: The composite through the new subscheme and open into the original ambient scheme agrees with the route through the original subscheme. A point outside the inverse image of memory therefore maps to a point outside the original memory. Choose the neighborhood of that point on which the two original ideals agree. Its inverse image contains the given point. Pull the equality of ideals back along the restricted subscheme map and use the commuting inclusions to identify the result with the asserted local equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_comap_morphismRe: The support on the new open is the inverse image of the relevant support on the old open, by compatibility of ideal pullback with the restriction square. The subscheme map commutes with the two inclusions. Thus the further inverse image on the new subscheme is the inverse image of the given open on the old subscheme. It is open by continuity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_morphismRestrict: Restrict the open immersion to the inverse image of the chosen target open. This is again an open immersion, so the smooth divisor pulls back to a smooth divisor by the stability assumption. The open restriction square identifies its composite structural map with the one in the statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_comapSubscheme: The restricted ambient map is an open immersion, so the induced map of closed subschemes is an open immersion by the stated stability assumption. Componentwise nonvanishing pulls back along it by that same assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr: Replace each of the structure map, input ideal, memory and target ideal by its equal value. This gives the required order certificate directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_comp: A point maps into the given set under the composite exactly when its image under the first map is in the inverse image under the second. This is the nested inverse-image formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_preimage_base_of_comp_eq: Each nested inverse image is the inverse image under its composite. Equal composites have the same inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comapSubsche: The restricted map of hypersurfaces is an open immersion by the stability assumption. Apply the hypothesis giving certificates on all opens of the original hypersurface to that map. The commuting open and subscheme inclusions identify its structural map, inverse image of memory and pullback of the target ideal with the prescribed data. The input ideal is already the required pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_congr: Use the equalities of the structure maps, input ideals, memory sets and target ideals to identify all certificate parameters. The given certificate then has the required data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_morphismRestrict_subset: The open restriction square identifies pulling back the restricted ambient ideal with restricting the pulled-back ideal. Both supports on the new open are therefore inverse images under the restricted map. Pulling back the original containment gives the result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_ambientBlowupSe: The induced map from S′ to S is flat because it is a base change of the ambient flat map. Form strict base changes of both original sequences. By flat base change of pushforwards, the strict ambient base change is a pushforward of the strict source base change. Removing empty-center steps preserves that pushforward relation. The resulting source sequence is isomorphic to the given sequence on S′, since both are pullbacks with empty centers omitted. Thus the pruned ambient base change is a pushforward of the given sequence on S′. Pushforward uniqueness identifies it with the ambient construction over Y. Transport the pullback comparison after removing empty steps across this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_ambientBlowupS: Form the stagewise flat base change of the ambient sequence over X to Y. The ambient stages and their pullbacks are Noetherian, so the flat base-change theorem for pushforwards applies to the closed immersion square and the two strict comparisons. It identifies this base-changed ambient sequence as a pushforward of the given sequence on S′. The ambient construction over Y is another pushforward of that same sequence. Pushforward uniqueness gives a sequence isomorphism between them, and transporting the strict pullback comparison along it proves the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.commutesWithClosedImmersion_forall_codim:
Induct on the positive coordinate codimension. Codimension zero cannot satisfy the positive codimension hypothesis. First, if the source is empty, its ideal has empty support and its ambient image ideal is the unit ideal. The two order-one cosupports are empty, so correctness gives zero-length sequences, which have the required pushforward relation.

For a nonempty source, take the finite maximal-contact cover of the ambient scheme by adapted étale charts. Let W be the disjoint union of the cover, S the pullback of the source to W, and H the smooth hypersurface in W assembled from the chosen coordinates. The map from S to W factors through H, and the ideal on H is the image of the pulled-back source ideal. Its image on W is the pullback of the original ambient ideal. Smooth pullback gives admissibility on S and W. The ideal on H is also admissible. When the original codimension is one, S is isomorphic to H, so nonvanishing on components is transported from S. For higher codimension, the embedding of S in H is locally cut out by a nonempty set of coordinates, which gives nonvanishing on components there.

Use correctness for smooth surjective pullback in codimension one to identify the sequence on S as a strict pullback of the sequence on H over their isomorphism. Such a strict pullback is a pushforward along the isomorphism. In higher codimension the map from S to H has coordinate codimension one less than the given immersion, so the induction hypothesis gives the corresponding pushforward. The ambient image ideal has order at most one since it contains the kernel of the original smooth closed immersion, whose order is bounded by one in adapted charts. This bound pulls back to W. Moreover, H has strictly smaller dimension than W, since its smooth divisor contains no component. Choose a dimension level above all the schemes involved. The order-reduction pushforward property then uses the sequence on H at the preceding level to give the order-reduction sequence on W. Stabilization identifies the input sequence with the final one on H, and the order bound identifies the output with the maximum-order reduction on W up to isomorphism. Compose these two pushforwards to get the desired relation over the cover.

To descend it, first construct an ambient pushforward of the original source sequence. Its centers contain no component by admissibility and the center property of a marked sequence. After flat base change to W, it is a pushforward of the sequence on S because the smooth surjective comparison from S to the original source is a strict pullback of the source sequence. Pushforward uniqueness identifies this base change with the sequence on W already obtained. The latter is also the strict pullback of the prescribed original ambient sequence. Descent along the smooth surjective cover identifies the two ambient sequences, and transport across that isomorphism proves the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.commutesWithClosedImmersion_of_isCorrect: Admissibility is stable under smooth pullback by the marked-ideal theorem. Supply that stability to the closed immersion compatibility result for the dimension-recursive rules.

For the given embedding, take its positive coordinate codimension and apply the codimension induction theorem. The smoothness, finiteness, structure-map compatibility, coordinate, and nonvanishing conditions are precisely the hypotheses for that result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_pullbackAlong_of_smooth: Take an admissible marked ideal with boundary and a smooth morphism over its base field whose source has quasi-compact structure map. The smooth pullback theorem for marked ideals with boundary shows that the pulled-back ideal and boundary satisfy the admissibility conditions. The resulting statement applies to every such input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_schemeAt: Every stage up to the last is obtained by finitely many blowups of the Noetherian base, up to the initial isomorphism. The Noetherian stage theorem gives Noetherianity, which implies local Noetherianity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_disjointUnion: The map from the covering disjoint union to the field is locally of finite type, because the cover projection is étale and the ambient structure map is locally of finite type. The field is Noetherian, so the total scheme of this cover is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_subscheme_iInfImageIdeal: The hypersurface is a closed subscheme of the Noetherian disjoint union of the cover. Its immersion is locally of finite type, which gives Noetherianity of the hypersurface.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardSequenceOfBlowups_congr_hom: Substitute the given equality of base embeddings. The pushforward relation is then the one already supplied.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderReduction_outputLevelData_eq_mar: The dimension-level construction agrees with the final maximum-order reduction at any level at least the dimension bound of the input scheme. Apply this stabilization to the marked triple with multiplicity one, whose underlying scheme is the given scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ker_of_hasEtaleCoord: The support of the kernel is the image of the closed immersion. Every point of that image therefore has the indicated local coordinate description from a source point. Its coordinate set has size c≥ 1, so it is nonempty. The Noetherian ambient space has finitely many irreducible components, and the criterion for ideals locally generated by nonempty coordinate sets shows that the kernel support contains no component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_toSequenceOfBlowups_: Converting to data and back retains the length, stages, adjacent transitions, centers, and initial isomorphism. Take the identity isomorphism at each stage. These identities commute with the initial and adjacent maps and pull each center back to itself, giving the sequence isomorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_le_map_idealSheaf: The zero ideal of the source is contained in the given ideal. Direct image of ideal sheaves preserves inclusion, and the direct image of the zero ideal is the morphism's kernel ideal. The resulting inclusion is the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_lt_of_isClosedImmersion_of_: A closed immersion identifies the source topologically with its closed image, and this image is nonempty because the source is. It cannot contain an ambient irreducible component, since the image lies in the support of the kernel and that support contains no component. The ambient scheme has finite Krull dimension by finite type over the field. The dimension bound for a nonempty closed subset that contains no irreducible component now gives the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_map_le_one_of_isClosedImmersion: The image ideal contains the kernel, so its order is at most the kernel order. Outside the kernel support that order is zero. At a point of the support, the kernel subscheme and ambient scheme are smooth over the field. Choose adapted étale coordinates in which the kernel is generated by a subset of the coordinate functions. If the subset were empty, the support would contain the whole chart. Its intersection with an irreducible component through the point is dense in that component, so closedness of the support would force it to contain the component, contrary to the assumption. With a nonempty coordinate subset, the local coordinate-ideal order bound gives order at most one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ker_subschemeι_comp: A closed immersion identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image. Under that isomorphism, the inclusion of the kernel subscheme is the original immersion. Its composite to the field is therefore the given smooth morphism precomposed with an isomorphism, so it is smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_ι_eq_topIso_inv: On sections, the open inclusion identifies the original sections over the given open with the global sections of the corresponding open subscheme. The ring map in this direction is the inverse of the canonical identification from the global sections to the original section ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iInfImageIdeal_summandι: Work on an affine open of summand i. Its image in the disjoint union is affine because the summand inclusion is an open immersion. There all image ideals from other summands are unit, since their images are disjoint. Thus the intersection of image ideals on this affine image is the contribution from i alone. Pulling it back along the summand inclusion recovers the original ideal of that summand. Equality on every affine open gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf_summandι: The summand inclusion is a closed immersion. The image ideal of a closed subscheme pulls back through that immersion to the original defining ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjointUnionMap_summandι_mem: The composite is the inclusion of the given open into the original scheme, whose image is that open. Evaluating the composite at the summand point gives the membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_map_eq_of_bijective: For any element of one ideal, its image belongs to the common image ideal. Surjectivity of the ring map realizes that image as the image of an element of the other original ideal. Injectivity makes the two original elements equal. This proves both inclusions by interchanging the ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_disjointUnionMap: On each open summand the total map is the original open inclusion, which is étale. Étaleness is local on the source, and the summands cover the disjoint union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_summandIso_inv_comp_map: The inverse summand isomorphism is étale, as is the original chart map. Étale morphisms are closed under composition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_summandOpen: Represent the point as the image of a summand point. This puts it in the range of that summand inclusion, which is the designated summand open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_summandι_base_eq: The underlying point space of the scheme coproduct is the disjoint union of the summand point spaces. Represent the point by a summand index and a point in that summand. Its image under the corresponding inclusion is the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ext_of_comap_summandι: The summand opens cover the disjoint union. On each summand open, restriction of each ideal is its given summand pullback transported by the same isomorphism. These restrictions agree by hypothesis, and equality of ideals can be checked on an open cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ext_of_comap_ι_eq_of_iSup_eq_top: Refine the given open cover by all affine opens contained in one of its members. They still cover the scheme because affine opens form a basis. On each of them the pulled-back ideals agree by factoring its inclusion through the original cover member. The affine evaluation result gives equality of the ideals on that affine open. The resulting local equalities imply equality globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_disjointUnionMap: The disjoint union map is étale and hence smooth. Smooth morphisms are flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iInfImageIdeal_eq_iInf: The assembled ideal is defined as the intersection of the image ideals of all the summand ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_comap_ι_eq: Evaluate the two pulled-back ideals on the whole affine open subscheme. These evaluations are the images of the original ideals on that affine open under its section-ring isomorphism. They agree by hypothesis. A ring isomorphism reflects equality of ideals, so the original ideals agree there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_imageIdealSheaf_eq_top_of_ne: The subscheme giving the image ideal maps into summand j, while the affine open lies in summand i. Distinct coproduct summands have disjoint images, so the inverse image of the affine open is empty. Its kernel ideal on that open is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_ker_eq_top_of_disjoint: The affine open misses the image, so its inverse image is empty. On that inverse image the section ring has one element, so the map on sections sends one to zero. The kernel ideal on the affine open thus contains one and is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_of_comap_ι_le: Evaluate the pullback inclusion on the whole affine open subscheme. The two evaluated ideals are the images of the original affine ideals under a ring isomorphism. This isomorphism reflects inclusion, giving the claimed inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_of_map_le_of_bijective: Take an element of the first ideal. Its image lies in the image of the second ideal by the assumed inclusion. Surjectivity expresses it as the image of an element of that ideal, and injectivity identifies the two preimages. This proves the original inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_ker: By definition the image ideal is the kernel of the map from the closed subscheme to the target, obtained by composing its inclusion with the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffineOpen_summandOpen: The scheme of the original open is affine by hypothesis. Its image under the coproduct open immersion is isomorphic to it, so the resulting summand open is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_disjointUnion: Each scheme in the finite coproduct is affine by hypothesis. A finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, with coordinate ring the finite product of the section rings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_summandι: A summand of the disjoint union is an open and closed subscheme with the induced structure sheaf. Its coproduct inclusion is therefore also a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_summandι: The summand inclusion of a scheme coproduct identifies its source with an open subscheme, namely the component corresponding to that summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iInfImageIdeal_of_exists: At a point of the total space choose its summand open and transport the given étale chart from that summand. The assembled ideal restricts to the given local ideal under this identification. It is therefore either unit or generated by the chosen single étale coordinate. The local coordinate criterion for a smooth divisor applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iInfImageIdeal_of_forall: On a summand with unit ideal, choose any available étale chart. On a summand with a coordinate ideal, use the chart supplied with that coordinate description. In either case there is a chart in which the local ideal is unit or a single coordinate ideal, so the assembled ideal defines a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_comap_summandι_le: For every point choose a summand open containing it. An affine open contained in this summand open factors through the original summand inclusion by the open immersion property. Pullback preserves the given inclusion along that factorization. Evaluation on the affine open gives an inclusion of the original ideals there. The local criterion for inclusion now gives the global inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_ideal_le_locally: Refine the pointwise neighborhoods by affine opens, which still cover the scheme. On each of these affine opens the first ideal is contained in the second, so their intersection equals the first ideal. Equality of ideal sheaves can be checked on the affine cover. Thus the intersection is the first ideal globally, which is equivalent to the desired inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_disjointUnionMap: On the open summands the map is the inclusion of an open, which is locally of finite type. These summands cover the source, so the total map is locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_disjointUnionMap_comp: The finite disjoint union of the affine cover opens is affine and therefore quasi-compact. The spectrum of the base field has one point. The inverse image of an open there is either empty or the whole quasi-compact source, so the composite is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_summandι: The inclusion is that of an open and closed summand. Its inverse image of a quasi-compact open is a closed subset of that open and is therefore quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_summandι: The associated summand open is defined to be the image of the summand inclusion. The inclusion of this open has that same image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_disjointUnionMap_sum: Use functoriality to write the left side as pullback along the summand open inclusion followed by the total map. This composite is the inverse summand isomorphism followed by the original open inclusion. Pulling back in that order gives the right side.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_iInfImageIdeal_summandOpen: Express restriction to the summand open as pullback to the summand followed by transport along the inverse image isomorphism. The first pullback of the assembled ideal is the original local ideal, leaving its stated transport.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_summandOpen: The inclusion of the summand open is its inverse image isomorphism to the summand followed by the coproduct inclusion. Restriction is pullback along that composite, which factors into the two stated pullbacks.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_disjointUnionMap: The disjoint union map is étale. Every étale morphism is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subsingleton_sections_bot: The sheaf condition for the empty cover makes the ring of sections on the empty open terminal. Its two projections from its square are therefore equal. Evaluating them on any pair of sections shows those sections are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subsingleton_spec: A field has only one prime ideal, its zero ideal. Hence its spectrum is a subsingleton.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.summandEtaleChart_coordIdeal: Each coordinate ideal is the pullback of the corresponding coordinate-subspace ideal on affine space. The transported chart map is the inverse summand isomorphism followed by the original chart map. Functoriality writes its coordinate ideal as the original coordinate ideal pulled back along the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.summandEtaleChart_map: The transported chart map is defined by first identifying the summand open with the original open and then using the given chart map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.summandIso_inv_comp_map_comp_affineSpace: The original chart followed by the affine-space structure map agrees with the original open's map to the field. Precompose by the inverse summand isomorphism. The resulting map to the original scheme is the summand open inclusion followed by the total cover map, giving the claimed structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.summandOpen_ι_comp_disjointUnionMap: Identify the summand open with the original summand by the inverse of the image isomorphism. Its inclusion then factors through the coproduct summand inclusion. Composing with the total map gives the original open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.summandι_comp_disjointUnionMap: The map from the coproduct is determined by the original open inclusions on its summands. The defining coproduct identity gives the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_disjointUnionMap: For an arbitrary target point, the open cover assumption puts it in one of the original opens. The corresponding point on that summand maps to the chosen point, proving surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_preimage_opens: Every point of the open subscheme is a point of the ambient scheme lying in the given open. Thus the preimage of that open under its own inclusion contains the whole open subscheme.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.card_complEmbPreimage: The complement order embedding maps the indicated indices bijectively onto S with a removed. It is injective, and any element of S different from a has a preimage in the complement. Since a belongs to S, erasing it reduces the cardinality by one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iInfImageIdeal_subschemeι_eq_bot: Apply the fact that an ideal pulls back to zero on its defining closed subscheme to the covering hypersurface ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_subschemeι_self: Pulling back an ideal to its own zero subscheme gives the zero ideal. Equivalently, the pullback of its closed immersion along itself has identity first projection, whose kernel is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasEtaleCoordCodim_pullbackFiberToHypers: At a fiber point, choose the cover summand containing its image in the total space. The pullback square shows that its image in the original ambient scheme comes from the closed source, so this summand cannot be disjoint from the source. In its adapted chart the source fiber is defined by a coordinate set S of size c, and the hypersurface is the coordinate j in S. Restrict the chart to that hypersurface. The fiber kernel there is the restriction of the total-space fiber kernel and is generated by the remaining coordinates. Their indexing set is in bijection with S with j removed, giving the specified codimension c−1.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullbackFiberToHypersurface_of_eq_: Compare the fiber's defining ideal with the assembled hypersurface ideal on each cover summand. On a disjoint summand both restrict to the unit ideal. On an adapted summand the fiber uses a coordinate set of size one, so its only coordinate is the chosen hypersurface coordinate and the two ideals agree there as well. The summands cover the total space, so the ideals agree globally. The kernel of the map into the hypersurface is the pullback of this ideal to its own zero subscheme and is zero. A closed immersion with zero kernel is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_pullbackFiberToHypersurface: The map from the fiber to the total space factors through the hypersurface inclusion. Its kernel is the direct image of the kernel of the map to the hypersurface. Since the inclusion is a closed immersion, pulling back this image along it recovers the kernel on the hypersurface.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_forall_mem_support_of_coordIdea: At every point, membership in the support means that the coordinate germ generates a proper ideal, so the germ is never a unit. The coordinate's basic open is empty. On the affine scheme this makes the coordinate nilpotent. It is also a nonzero divisor by the étale coordinate property, so multiplication by a sufficiently high power can kill one only if one is zero. The resulting zero stalk at the given point contradicts the properness of the stalk ideal there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_hypersurfaceScheme: The total disjoint union is affine and the defining hypersurface inclusion is a closed immersion, hence an affine morphism. Its source is therefore affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_pullbackFiber: The fiber is a closed subscheme of the affine total disjoint union, since its inclusion is the base change of the original closed immersion. A closed subscheme of an affine scheme is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_pullbackFiberToHypersurface_le_ideal: The ideal on the hypersurface is the image of the pulled-back original ideal under the fiber inclusion. An image ideal contains the kernel of the morphism, since it contains the image of the zero ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_hypersurfaceScheme_lt: The total space is locally of finite type and quasi-compact over the field. The nonempty hypersurface is closed in it, and its inclusion's kernel is the assembled ideal, which has support containing no component. Apply the strict Krull dimension bound for such a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_iInfImageIdeal: The Noetherian total space has finitely many irreducible components. At a point of the assembled ideal's support, choose a cover summand containing the point. Its local ideal cannot be unit, since that would put the point outside the support. The local ideal is therefore the ideal of the chosen single coordinate in the summand's étale chart. The criterion for locally nonempty coordinate ideals shows that the assembled support contains no component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_idealOnHypersurface: The kernel support contains no irreducible component by the local coordinate condition. The support of the hypersurface ideal is contained in that kernel support, so it also contains no component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ker_pullbackFiberToH: The closed immersion of the fiber into the hypersurface has closed image, and that image equals the support of the kernel. Thus every support point is the image of a fiber point and admits the specified chart with a nonempty set of coordinate generators. The hypersurface has finitely many irreducible components by Noetherianity. Apply the local coordinate criterion to the kernel ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_of_locally_eq_coordI: Suppose the support contains an irreducible component. Since there are finitely many components, irreducibility and maximality give a point of this component outside all other components. Choose an affine open around that point inside the given coordinate chart and disjoint from all other components. Every point of this affine open then lies in the component and in the support of the restricted ideal. Select one coordinate from its nonempty set of generators. The support of its principal coordinate ideal contains that of the restricted ideal, hence is the whole affine open. This contradicts the fact that a single étale coordinate cannot vanish everywhere on a nonempty affine chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_top_coordIdeal: The coordinate ideal is the pullback of the coordinate-subspace ideal along the chart map. Restricting it to the whole open subscheme pulls it back along the additional open inclusion. By functoriality this is pullback along the composite defining the new chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_hypersurfaceStructureMap: The assembled ideal defines a smooth divisor for the composite map from the total space to the field. In particular, the divisor's closed subscheme is smooth under its induced structural map, which is the displayed map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_idealOnHypersurface_subset_suppo: At any point outside the kernel's support the kernel stalk is the unit ideal. The ideal on the hypersurface contains the kernel, so its stalk there is unit as well. This proves the required support containment.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPushforwardBlowupSeq.of_isStrictPullba: The stage-zero comparison is the base isomorphism transported by the two initial isomorphisms. Inductively each next comparison is its pullback along a transition, hence is also an isomorphism and is a closed immersion. The initial and step compatibilities come from the strict pullback witness. Since the center pulls back along an isomorphism, its image along that isomorphism recovers the original center. All comparison kernels are zero, and the strict transform of the zero ideal under a blowup is zero, so the required kernel update also holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: Take an affine-open section in the kernel, so it vanishes on the part outside the ideal's support. Near each point choose an affine open where the ideal is generated by a nonzero divisor f. Refine the intersection with the section's domain to a basic open in this neighborhood. The basic open of f lies outside the support, and vanishing there implies vanishing on the smaller basic open by injectivity of localization at a nonzero divisor. The section is consequently zero near every point and hence zero. The kernel ideal is therefore zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_basicOpen: The sections on the basic open form an algebra over the sections on the containing open through the restriction map. Its structural ring map therefore sends the section to exactly its restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_subschemeι_comap_bot: The zero ideal pulls back to zero. The closed subscheme defined by the zero ideal is the entire scheme, so its inclusion is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_preimage_ι_comp_of_isIso: Restricting an isomorphism to the inverse image of an open gives an isomorphism onto that open. The composite in the assertion is this restricted isomorphism followed by the given open inclusion. Precomposition by an isomorphism preserves the kernel ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_basicOpen_eq_zero_of_app_ι_eq_zero: On the affine basic open of b, the restriction of f remains a nonzero divisor because the ring of sections is a localization. Its basic open is the intersection of the basic opens of b and f, hence lies in W and in V. The section vanishes on this intersection by the assumed vanishing over W. Thus the section on the basic open of b becomes zero after localization at the restricted f. Some power of that nonzero divisor annihilates it, so the section was already zero there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_zero_of_app_ι_eq_zero: Restricting a section on V along the inclusion of W gives its restriction to V∩ W, viewed on the open subscheme. By assumption this is zero. The smaller open V′ lies in that intersection, so the restriction to V′ factors through zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_homOfLE_map_homOfLE: The two inclusions between the nested opens compose to the direct inclusion. Functoriality of the presheaf identifies the successive restriction maps with the direct restriction map. Evaluate the equality on the section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_of_mem_basicOpen: On the affine open the support of the ideal is its common zero locus. A point in the basic open of a section belonging to the ideal is a point at which that section is invertible, so it cannot belong to the common zero locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.section_eq_zero_of_locally_zero: For each point of the open, choose a smaller open on which the section vanishes. Its germ at the point equals the germ of the restriction, so every germ is zero. Equality of sections in a sheaf follows from equality of their germs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_bot_of_isBlowupAlongIdea: The inverse image of the zero ideal still defines the entire blowup scheme. Its strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the complement of the exceptional support. The exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor by the blowup property, so the ideal of this closure is zero by the kernel result for that complement.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_imageIdealSheaf_comp_eqToHom: After identifying the equal stage indices, the extra map is the identity. The two descriptions of the center therefore reduce to the given image-ideal equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eqToHom_comp_transitionMap: Identify the equal pairs of indices in the stage schemes. The inserted identification maps are then identities, and the displayed commutativity reduces to the given equality of composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_projectionToBase: Replace the two equal indices by a common index. The inserted identification is the identity of that stage and leaves the projection unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_top_iff: The image of the unit ideal is unit because its subscheme is empty. Conversely, pulling an image ideal back through the closed immersion recovers the original ideal. If the image is unit then so is its pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_top: The unit ideal defines the empty subscheme. Its composite map to the target is quasi-compact, since all inverse images are empty. The support of the kernel of that composite is the closure of its image, which is empty. Thus the image ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_comp_eqToHom: Substitute the equality of indices. The appended map is then the identity of the target stage, so the composite is the given closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardSequenceOfBlowups_withoutIs: At every step the ambient center is the image of the source center, so either both centers are empty or both are nonempty. Consequently the retained indices and lengths after deleting empty-center steps agree. Use the old closed immersions at the retained indices. Their squares commute for arbitrary longer transitions by composition of adjacent squares, and the original centers and projection identities give the corresponding conditions at retained stages. For the kernel update, take the strict transform for the first blowup of a retained transition. Each subsequent step in that transition has empty center and is an isomorphism, so its strict transform is pullback. By compatibility with composition by isomorphisms, these pullbacks give the strict transform along the full retained transition. This verifies the last pushforward condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_eqToHom_eq_strictTransform: Identify each of the equal indices in the source and target stages. The inserted maps are identities, so the new kernel and strict transform statements are exactly the ones in the hypothesis.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_mono: Inclusion of the index sets gives inclusion of their sets of coordinate generators, hence inclusion of the ideals they generate on affine space. Sheafification by restriction and pullback along the chart both preserve inclusion. The resulting ideal sheaves are the two coordinate ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_ker_eq_range: The support of the kernel ideal is the image of the inclusion of its closed subscheme. A closed immersion identifies its source with this kernel subscheme compatibly with their maps to the ambient scheme. The two images therefore coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapImageIdealSheaf_eq: The ideal on the cover total space is defined by pulling the original image ideal back along the cover projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapImageIdealSheaf_eq_imageIdealSheaf_: The kernel of the hypersurface inclusion is the assembled ideal, which is contained in the pulled-back original kernel. The latter is contained in the pulled-back image ideal because an image ideal contains the embedding kernel. An ideal containing the kernel of a closed immersion is recovered by pulling it back to the closed subscheme and taking its image. The pullback here is the hypersurface ideal in the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_restrict: The restricted chart is obtained by composing the smaller-open inclusion with the original chart. Its coordinate ideal is the pullback of the corresponding affine-space ideal along this composite. Functoriality identifies it with the original coordinate ideal pulled back to the smaller open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverHypersurfaceIdeal_inl: On an adapted chart the local hypersurface ideal is defined to be the ideal generated by its chosen coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverHypersurfaceIdeal_inr: On a chart disjoint from the source image the local hypersurface ideal is defined to be the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverOpens_inl: For an index from the adapted-chart family, the combined cover takes the open of that adapted chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverOpens_inr: For an index from the disjoint-chart family, the combined cover takes the open of that disjoint chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_adaptedEtaleChart: At the image of the given source point, choose a chart from the coordinate codimension hypothesis. Shrink to an affine open still containing the point, and restrict the chart. The coordinate ideal description of the kernel remains valid by compatibility with restriction. Since its coordinate set has positive size, choose a coordinate in it. These data give an adapted affine chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_disjointEtaleChart: Take a chart containing the ambient point. The image of the closed immersion is closed and misses that point, so intersect the chart with the open complement of the image. Choose an affine neighborhood of the point inside this intersection. The chart restricts to that neighborhood and its open misses every point in the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_factor_pullbackFiberToTotal: The fiber's kernel in the total space is the pullback of the original immersion's kernel. On a disjoint summand both this ideal and the hypersurface ideal are unit. On an adapted summand the hypersurface uses one coordinate from the set generating the fiber ideal, so the hypersurface ideal is contained in it. The summandwise inclusions give a global inclusion of ideals. The criterion for factoring through a closed immersion now provides the required lift to the hypersurface.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_pullbackFiberToBase: The cover projection is flat, since it is étale. The fiber map to the original source is its base change, so it is flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iInfImageIdeal_le_comap_ker: The assembled ideal pulls back to the chosen local ideal on each summand. The pulled-back kernel restricts there to the kernel on the original cover open, since the sum map restricts to its inclusion. The local inclusion holds on every summand and therefore holds globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOnHypersurface_eq_comap: The hypersurface ideal in the assertion is defined by pulling the total-space ideal back along the hypersurface inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOnHypersurface_eq_imageIdealSheaf: Flat base change along the cover projection identifies the pulled-back original image ideal with the image in the total space of the pulled-back source ideal on the fiber. The fiber map factors through the hypersurface. By functoriality of images the total-space ideal is the image of the indicated fiber ideal on the hypersurface, followed by the hypersurface inclusion. Pulling back along that closed immersion recovers the intermediate ideal, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_disjointUnion: The covering opens are affine and there are finitely many of them. Their disjoint union is affine by the finite coproduct result for affine schemes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_pullbackFiberToHypersu: The composite with the hypersurface inclusion is a closed immersion. A morphism whose composite with a closed immersion is a closed immersion is itself a closed immersion, giving the claim.
The composite agrees with the fiber's projection to the total space. That projection is a closed immersion because it is obtained by base change from the original one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_pullbackFiberToTotal: The projection to the cover total space is the base change of the given closed immersion along the cover projection. Closed immersions are stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_pullbackFiber: The fiber is defined as the categorical pullback of the closed immersion and the cover projection. Its two displayed maps are the projections of that pullback, so they form a pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iInfImageIdeal: On each cover open the local ideal is either unit or a one-coordinate ideal in an étale chart. The assembled ideal has these same restrictions on the summand opens of the disjoint union. The local smooth-divisor criterion gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_pullbackFiberToTotal: The map to the cover total space is the pullback of the closed immersion along the flat cover projection. The kernel theorem for a flat pullback square identifies its kernel with the pullback of the original kernel ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.localIdeal_le_restrictIdeal_ker: On a disjoint summand both ideals are unit, since the immersion's image misses that open. On an adapted summand the local ideal uses a single coordinate from the coordinate set of the restricted kernel. Inclusion of these coordinate sets gives the ideal inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_projection_comp: The projection from the cover is locally of finite type, since it is given by open immersions on its summands. Composing with the locally finite type ambient structure map preserves this property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOfIdeal_ideal: The ideal sheaf in the marked ideal is the one used to form it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOfIdeal_scheme: The construction takes the supplied scheme as the underlying scheme of the marked ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOfIdeal_structureMorphism: The structural morphism in the marked ideal is the supplied map to the spectrum of the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_maximalContactCover: The ambient scheme is quasi-compact because its map to the quasi-compact spectrum of the field is quasi-compact. At each point of the closed immersion's image use an adapted affine étale chart, and at each point outside use a disjoint affine étale chart. These opens cover the ambient scheme, so choose a finite subcover. On each adapted chart take the chosen one-coordinate ideal. On each disjoint chart take the unit ideal. Every chosen open remains affine and carries its chart. The adapted charts retain the full coordinate description of the immersion, and the disjoint charts retain disjointness. These are the required data of the finite maximal-contact cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIdealTop_mono: For each affine open, the associated sheaf ideal is the image of the given global ideal under the restriction map. Image under a ring homomorphism preserves inclusion. This gives the sheaf ideal inclusion on each affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projection_eq: The projection of the cover is defined to be the map from its disjoint union of opens to the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackFiberToHypersurface_comp_subsche: The map to the hypersurface is chosen from the factorization of the fiber's total-space map. Its composite with the hypersurface inclusion is therefore that total-space map.

Regroup the composite so that the fiber-to-hypersurface map is followed first by the hypersurface inclusion. Their composite is the fiber-to-total-space map. Postcompose this identity with the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_projection_comp: The finite disjoint union of the affine cover opens is quasi-compact. Since the target of the composite is the one-point spectrum of a field, the composite is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_ker_eq_top_of_not_mem: The support of the kernel is the image of the closed immersion. Restriction to the open pulls back that support to its intersection with the open, which is empty by hypothesis. An ideal with empty support is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projection_comp: The projection is étale on the disjoint union of the covering opens, hence smooth. Its composite with the smooth ambient structure map is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_pullbackFiberToBase: The cover projection is smooth. The fiber map to the original source is its base change along the original immersion, so that map is smooth as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_projection: Every ambient point lies in a cover open. The corresponding point of that open regarded as a summand maps to the original point, so the projection is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_pullbackFiberToBase: The cover projection is surjective since the opens cover the ambient scheme. The fiber map to the original source is its base change, which preserves surjectivity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp: The two given length equalities give equal lengths for the first and third sequences. Compose the two closed immersions at each stage. Their initial and adjacent compatibilities compose, and functoriality of the image ideal shows that the last sequence's center is the image of the first center. For the strict transform condition, express the later kernel of the composite immersion as the image of the later kernel of the first immersion. In the middle sequence this latter kernel is a strict transform. The second immersion square identifies its image with the strict transform of the earlier image, since the later second immersion itself cuts out the strict transform of the earlier one. The earlier image equals the earlier composite kernel. This gives all the pushforward conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp: The kernel ideal of a composite is the image under the second morphism of the first kernel ideal. That image ideal is defined by the kernel of the first kernel subscheme's inclusion followed by the second morphism. Combining these descriptions gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_isomorphic_source: Use the inverse stage isomorphisms from the new source to the old one. They commute with the initial identifications and transitions, and the adjacent squares are pullbacks because the comparison maps are isomorphisms. The center equalities transport under the inverse isomorphisms by functoriality of pullback. Thus the new source is a strict pullback of the old one over the identity of the base. Compose this comparison with the given pushforward, using that the identity followed by the closed immersion is the same closed immersion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_projectionToBase_of_comp_blowupMorp: At stage zero the projections are the initial isomorphisms, so the assertion is the initial compatibility. At the next stage, express each projection as the adjacent transition followed by the preceding projection. Commute the comparison across that transition by the step hypothesis and apply induction to the preceding projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_of_isPullback: Identify the upper-left scheme with the fiber product. The map to the upper right is the base change of the given flat map, up to this identification. Flatness is preserved by base change and by composition with an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_of_isPullback: Use the pullback isomorphism to identify the map across the top with the base change of the closed immersion along the right-hand arrow. Base change and isomorphism preserve closed immersions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_flat_isPullback: The given length equalities make the two new sequences have equal length. At each stage the strict comparisons give pullback squares over the bases, by composing their adjacent pullback squares. Lift the original closed immersion comparison to the new ambient stage using its pullback square and the base closed immersion square. Pullback pasting shows the lifted comparison is itself a base change of the old closed immersion. Its initial and step compatibilities follow by projecting to both factors of the relevant pullback. Its center formula follows because direct image along a closed immersion commutes with flat pullback. Finally its kernel is the flat pullback of the old kernel, and strict transform commutes with the flat pullback of the Noetherian blowup stages. This gives the required kernel formula at every step.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPushforwardBlowupSeq.isomorphic: Choose the stage data provided by each pushforward witness for the same closed immersion and source sequence. The stagewise uniqueness result applied to these two choices gives an isomorphism of the ambient sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_center_eq_of_sequenceOfBlowupsPush: Both centers are the image of the same source center under their respective stage embeddings. The second embedding is the first followed by the given isomorphism. Functoriality writes the second center as the image of the first center under that isomorphism. Pulling it back recovers the first center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf_of_isIso: For an isomorphism the image ideal is the direct image along a closed immersion. Pulling that image ideal back along the same immersion recovers the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_succ_comp_blowupMorphism: The stage isomorphism matches center ideals, and pulling back along its inverse gives the converse center equality. Thus the composite of either blowup map with the appropriate direction of the stage isomorphism pulls back the other center to an ideal locally generated by a nonzero divisor. The universal properties give maps between the two blowup schemes in both directions over the stage isomorphism. Each composite lies over the original blowup map, so uniqueness of the lift identifies each composite with the identity. The two maps define the required next-stage isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic: Inductively build ambient stage isomorphisms that commute with the common source embeddings. At zero, compose the first initial isomorphism with the inverse of the second. Both source embeddings agree after mapping to the common base. Given the isomorphism at a stage, the two centers correspond because both are images of the same source center. The universal property of blowups extends the isomorphism to the next stage compatibly with the adjacent maps. The two proposed maps from the next source stage are lifts of the same map to the preceding ambient stage. The center there pulls back to the source center, so uniqueness of the blowup lift makes those maps equal. The induction supplies all stages, and the same image-ideal argument supplies the center equalities required for the sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_length: Each ambient sequence has the length of the same source sequence. Transitivity of these equalities identifies their lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_of_isPushforward: Choose stage embeddings from the given pushforward witness. Their length equality lets us index the embeddings by the ambient length. The closed immersion, initial, adjacent, and center conditions are already part of the witness, so these data give an element of the indicated structure.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_ker_of_mono: The pullback ideal is the kernel of the first projection of the fiber product with the closed subscheme. The factorization through the monomorphism defines a map from the closed subscheme to this fiber product. Its second projection is the identity, and its composite with the first projection is the given factorization. The second projection followed by the factorization equals the first projection by cancellation of the monomorphism. Thus the map to the fiber product and its second projection are inverse, and the two kernels agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_strictTransform_eq_strictTransform: The inverse image of the ambient open away from the center is the open away from the source center. On that ambient open, the kernel of the restricted closed immersion is the restriction of the pullback of the old immersion's kernel, by the strict-transform hypothesis. It is contained in the restricted pullback of the image ideal of D, because that image subscheme factors through the old closed immersion. The comparison for restricted image ideals now identifies the two inverse images off the centers after embedding into the ambient scheme. Taking the kernels of the resulting maps into that scheme identifies their scheme-theoretic closures, which define the strict transforms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_comp_eq_of_ker_le: The kernel containment allows the closed subscheme cut out by L to factor through the closed immersion. The kernel of the factorization is the pullback of L along that immersion, hence is K. The composite of the subscheme defined by this kernel with the immersion has the same kernel as the original factorization followed by the immersion. That composite is the inclusion of the closed subscheme defined by L, whose kernel is L.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp: The kernel of the composite is the image under the outer morphism of the inclusion's kernel. The kernel of the inclusion of the closed subscheme is its defining ideal. Substitution gives the direct image formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_ker_subschemeι_comp_restrict: Restrict the commuting square to the chosen target open and its inverse image. Pulling back the restricted ambient image ideal through the restricted immersion gives the restricted source ideal, since pulling the original image ideal back through its closed immersion recovers the original ideal. The assumed kernel containment then identifies the image of the resulting source subscheme in the target open with the subscheme given by the ambient restriction. Composing with the target open inclusion gives equality of their kernels in the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_strictTransform_eq_strictTransform_m: Write the images of the center, the ideal being transformed, and its strict transform as kernels of their subscheme inclusions followed by the closed immersions. The strict-transform hypothesis and the asserted equality then have exactly the form of the kernel comparison for strict transforms, which proves the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_complComapSupport_eq: The commuting square identifies the pullback of the ambient image center to the new source with the pullback of the original center. Here pulling the image center back through the original closed immersion recovers its ideal. Supports of pulled-back ideals are inverse images of supports. Taking complements now identifies the two indicated opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_eq_ker_complComapSupport: The strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image off the center. The open used in this construction is the complement of the support of the pulled-back center. On that open, the inverse image is the closed subscheme defined by the restriction of the pulled-back ideal. Its inclusion into the open followed by the open inclusion has kernel equal to the strict-transform ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_hom_comp: The descent case of order certificates has the established invariance under ambient isomorphisms. Apply the certificate transport theorem with that descent result and the given isomorphism to pull back the structural map, ideal, memory, and target ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_of_eq_iso_hom: The order certificate pulls back under the isomorphism by the established descent invariance and the certificate transport theorem. Substitute the stated equality to write its structural map as the specified new map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso_of: Transport the principalization certificate along the ambient isomorphism using invariance of the order-certificate descent case. The given equality identifies the new structural map with the transported one, yielding the claimed certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_iso: Support is the locus where the order is at least one. This locus pulls back along an isomorphism, so the support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubschemeIso_hom_comp: The isomorphism was chosen to factor the pulled-back subscheme's inclusion followed by the ambient isomorphism through the original subscheme inclusion. Its forward map therefore satisfies the displayed identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_preimageOpens_ι_comap_iso: Each iterated pullback is the pullback along a composite. The composite through the inverse image inclusion and the ambient isomorphism agrees with the composite through the restricted isomorphism and original open inclusion. Hence the ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_subschemeι_comap_iso: Pullback along a composite equals successive pullback. Compatibility of the subscheme isomorphism with the two closed immersions identifies the two composite maps, giving the stated equality of ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_none_of_map_comap_eq_none: Pullback in an optional ideal changes its value only when an ideal is present. A present ideal yields a present pulled-back ideal. Hence an absent result forces the original optional ideal to be absent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_eq_some_of_map_comap_eq_some: If the pulled-back optional ideal is present, the original one must also be present. Its original ideal pulls back to the given value because equality of present values identifies their underlying ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_comap_eq_comap_preimageOpe: The identity of the inverse images of memory shows that the image of the given point on the original subscheme lies outside the old memory. Choose the open around that point on which the two original ideals agree. Take its inverse image under the subscheme isomorphism. It contains the given point, and functoriality of ideal pullback along the compatible open and subscheme maps transports the equality to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_comap_comm: The kernel containments allow the forward and inverse ambient maps, restricted to the two closed subschemes, to factor through the opposite closed immersions. Their composites become the respective inclusions because the two ambient maps are inverse. Each inclusion is a monomorphism, so the composites are identities. The forward factorization is the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_mem_irreducibleComponents_of_homeo: The image of the component is irreducible by continuity. If an irreducible set contains this image, its inverse image under the homeomorphism is irreducible and contains the original component. Maximality makes that inverse image equal to the original component, so the containing set is the original image. Thus the image is a component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_comap_preimageOp: First carry the support of the ideal on the original open back through the open isomorphism. Compatibility of the closed immersions with the induced subscheme isomorphism then identifies the desired inverse image with the inverse image of the given open set along this subscheme isomorphism. It is open by continuity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_iso: The effective Cartier property of the ideal is preserved by transport through an isomorphism. Its closed subscheme is identified with the original smooth divisor over the field. Thus the pulled-back ideal again defines a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_preimageOpensIso: Pull the smooth divisor back along the isomorphism of the inverse image open with the original open. Compatibility of this isomorphism with open inclusions identifies its structural morphism with the prescribed composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoInvariantOrderCertificateDescend:
At a point of the pulled-back target support, take the inverse image of the original neighborhood and transport its smooth hypersurface along the open isomorphism. The pullback identities preserve both support containments. For each optional hypersurface ideal, transport a present value along the induced subscheme isomorphism and keep an absent value absent.

When the ideal is absent, the original openness condition transfers by the subscheme isomorphism. When it is present, the original ideal supplies the pulled-back ideal, and nonvanishing on components transfers under the isomorphism. The equality of local ideals away from memory also transfers, because the inverse images of the old and new memory agree under the same identification. Finally the hypothesis for the descended principalization certificates applies to the induced subscheme isomorphism. These transported data meet every condition of the descent constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comap_subschemeι_le_ker_subschemeι_c: The two inclusions have kernels equal to their defining ideals. Pulling the pulled-back ideal back along the inverse isomorphism recovers the original ideal. The image–pullback adjunction for that inverse map therefore puts the pulled-back ideal inside the kernel of the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_le_ker_comap_subschemeι_c: The defining ideal is the kernel of the original subscheme inclusion. The kernel of the composite from the pulled-back subscheme is the image of the pulled-back ideal along the forward map. The image–pullback adjunction contains the original ideal in that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_iso: If a component of the new scheme were contained in the pulled-back support, its image would be a component of the original scheme, since the ambient isomorphism is a homeomorphism. The image would lie in the original support by the formula for pulled-back supports. This contradicts original nonvanishing on components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpens_ι_comp_hom: The isomorphism from the inverse image open to the original open is the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. After composing with the original open inclusion it gives the restriction of the ambient map to the inverse image open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_comp: A point maps into the set under the composite exactly when its image under the first map belongs to the inverse image under the second. This is the asserted equality of inverse images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_comap_subschemeι_preimageOpens_: Compose the maps used for the nested inverse images. The compatibility of the subscheme and open isomorphisms says that these composites into the original ambient scheme are equal. Their inverse images of the memory set therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_preima: Apply the hypothesis about principalization certificates to the isomorphism from the pulled-back subscheme to the original one. The inclusion identities identify its structural map with the specified composite. The same identities identify the inverse images of the memory set and the pullback of the target ideal. Substituting gives the required certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_preimageOpens_ι_comp_hom: First use compatibility of the open inclusions with the ambient isomorphism. Then use compatibility of the subscheme isomorphism with its closed immersions. Associating these maps gives equality of the two routes to the original ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_iso_subset_of_subset: Both supports are inverse images of their original supports under the same isomorphism. Inverse images preserve the given containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_preimageOpens_subset: Restricting the pulled-back ambient ideal to the inverse image open agrees with pulling its original restriction back by the restricted isomorphism. Pullback along that isomorphism preserves the support containment, giving the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_apply: The family at the chosen boundary index is obtained by applying the divisor rule to the input. Each strictly smaller request is answered by the supplied assignment, which is exactly the displayed rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_isMaxOrderReduction: Induct on the level. At zero there are no natural dimension indices strictly below zero, so the specification holds vacuously. Given the specification for the input at level n, the rule hypotheses give the divisor reduction specifications and their boundary invariance through dimension n. These yield the new order reduction specification. Applying the maximal-order rule gives the maximal-order specification through dimension n for the output. This output is the next input, and being at most n is equivalent to being strictly below n plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_reductions_eq_of_dim_lt: Induct on the given dimension bound. Both levels under comparison are positive, so compute their values by applying the next-level construction to the preceding inputs. At dimension bound zero there can be no strictly smaller auxiliary dimension. The next-level comparisons therefore give equality of both reductions. At a successor bound, every strictly smaller auxiliary input has dimension index at most the preceding bound. The preceding levels are still above that bound and are in the given order. Thus induction gives equality of their maximal-order reductions on each auxiliary input. The next-level comparisons use exactly these equalities to show that both current reductions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_succ: The recursion defines the successor input by applying the next-level construction to the preceding input, which is exactly the preceding output.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_zero: The recursion begins at level zero with the trivial order reduction data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_outputLevelData: The order reduction of the output level satisfies its specification through the current dimension. The maximal-order rule uses this order reduction, so its specification hypothesis gives the required maximal-order reduction property at that level.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_outputLevelData: The input level's maximal-order and order reductions satisfy the specification below the current dimension. Thus the rule hypotheses give the boundary divisor reductions and their boundary invariance through the current dimension. Applying the order rule specification to these procedures gives the claimed order reduction property of the output.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderFamily_apply: The maximal-order family applies the maximal-order rule to the input and answers each auxiliary request by the supplied order assignment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_maxOrderReduction: The next level first constructs its new order reduction from the divisor family of the previous maximal-order reduction. It then applies the maximal-order rule with this new order reduction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_maxOrderReduction_congr: The maximal-order rule consults the new order reduction only on inputs of at most the original dimension index. For each such input the hypothesis gives agreement of the previous maximal-order reductions on all strictly smaller indices. The next-level order reduction comparison thus gives equal replies to every request. Hence the maximal-order rule has the same output.
