Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_orderReduction: The next level obtains its order reduction by first forming the divisor family with the previous maximal-order reduction and then applying the order rule to that family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_orderReduction_congr: For a request from the order rule, the auxiliary marked ideal has dimension index at most that of the original input. Its divisor rule uses the previous maximal-order reduction only on strictly smaller inputs. All those inputs are strictly smaller than the original input, so the two previous reductions agree there by hypothesis. The auxiliary divisor procedures are therefore equal at every request. Applying the same order rule gives equal outputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderFamily_apply: The order family applies the order rule to the given input. Its auxiliary procedure uses the supplied divisor assignment at the requested boundary index, on each permitted input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_eq_nextLevel: The output at a level is obtained by applying the next-level construction to that level's input data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq: The maximal-order reduction of the output is constructed by applying the maximal-order rule to the order reduction at the same output level.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq_at_: Take the smaller level to be the dimension index of the marked ideal itself. The ideal satisfies this bound by equality, so the comparison with any larger level applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq_of_: The two outputs are the inputs at their respective successor levels. The dimension index of the marked ideal is at most the smaller bound, and both successor levels are strictly above that bound. The stabilization theorem for input levels gives equality of their maximal-order reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_orderReduction_eq_orderF: The order reduction of the output level is the order rule applied to its divisor family. At every boundary index that family uses the maximal-order reduction from the input level.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMarked.of_comap_isoObjZero_eq: The given equalities of the initial pullbacks propagate to equality of all the controlled ideals and of all the transformed boundary lists. Thus each exceptional divisibility condition and center order condition transfers through the ideal equality, and each center normal crossings condition transfers through the boundary equality. The center smoothness condition uses the same geometric maps. These are the required marking conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_ambientBlowupS: The going-up induction yields the invariant at the indicated stage, since it is at most the length. Its controlled-ideal comparison identifies the restriction along the ambient embedding with the marked ideal of the lower sequence at that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_of_containedCo: Use the untwisted ideal and boundary identities to transfer derivative balance and strict normal crossings to the ambient construction's input. The chosen boundary entry matches, and removing it leaves the full truncated list. The general controlled-transform comparison then identifies the restriction with the lower ideal. Since the untwisted initial ideal equals the original ideal, the ambient transform in this comparison is the asserted one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.goingUpInvariant_of_le: At zero the initial boundary identifications, truncation condition, and strict normal crossings give the initial going-up invariant. At a successor below the length, the preceding invariant applies by induction. The successor theorem uses derivative balance, the positive mark, lower admissibility and the lifting of normal crossings to extend the invariant to that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_ambientBlowupSeq: The ambient sequence has the length of the lower sequence. For any adjacent step, the going-up invariant at the next stage supplies exceptional divisibility, and the invariant at the current stage puts the center in the order locus and gives its strict normal crossings condition. The ambient center is smooth over the field by the center smoothness comparison with the lower sequence. These four facts give the ambient marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_ambientBlowupSeq_of_containedCo: The untwisted ideal and boundary equal the originals, since they are obtained by identity pullback. Thus derivative balance and strict normal crossings hold for the untwisted data. The selected boundary entry is the same, and removing it leaves exactly the number of entries kept by the truncation. The ambient marking theorem applies using lower admissibility and positive multiplicity. Transport its marking along the initial ideal and boundary equalities to the original data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_eq_ideal: The untwisted lower ideal is the original ideal pulled back along the identity. This pullback fixes the ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_center_eq_imageIdealShe: The ambient sequence is the general ambient construction for the closed immersion of the selected boundary divisor. Its center formula takes the image ideal of the lower center under the induced stage embedding. Converting the lower marked sequence to blowup data preserves that center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_length: The general ambient construction inserts one ambient transition for each step of the lower sequence and so preserves length. Passing from the lower marked sequence to its unmarked data also preserves length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embeddingIntoAmbient: The base embedding is the closed immersion of the selected divisor. The ambient blowup construction lifts it at every stage as a closed immersion. Apply that result to the blowup data of the lower sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_scheme_of_isAdmissible: The structure map of an admissible input is locally of finite type over a field, which is Noetherian. The Noetherianity result for such admissible schemes gives the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_prepend_succ: At the first shifted stage the given boundary is the pullback of E₁ along the original initial isomorphism, exactly the old stage-zero boundary. At each later stage, the adjacent transition and center are the original ones. The two boundary updates apply the same strict transforms and append the same exceptional ideal to equal preceding lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_prepend_succ: At the first shifted stage the asserted equality is the hypothesis, since the old stage-zero transform is the pullback of I₁ along its initial isomorphism. At the next shifted stage, the adjacent transition and center are the old ones. The two transforms are obtained by the same pullback and residual operation from ideals equal by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_ker_subscheme: A closed immersion identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image. This image is the subscheme of the target defined by its kernel ideal, and the identification followed by inclusion is the original map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp: The image ideal is by definition the kernel of the map obtained by including the subscheme defined by Z and then applying the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_prepend_succ: At the first shifted stage, the map to the new stage zero is the original initial isomorphism, and the projection of that new stage is the identity. This gives the old projection at zero. At each subsequent stage the adjacent map is the original adjacent map at the preceding index. The two projection recursions give the same composite by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_prepend_zero: The new stage zero is the original base and its initial isomorphism is the identity. The projection at zero is the forward map of that isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ambientBlowupSeq_center_comp: The lower center is smooth over the field by the marking of the lower sequence. The embedding commutes with projection to the original base, so the map of that lower center to the field agrees with its map through the ambient stage. The ambient center is its image under the stage closed immersion. Its closed subscheme is isomorphic to the lower center over the field and is therefore smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_imageIdealSheaf_subschemeι_comp: The composite of the subscheme inclusion with the given closed immersion is a closed immersion. It identifies the original subscheme with the subscheme of its image ideal. The structural map of that image subscheme is smooth after precomposition with this isomorphism by the given hypothesis. Cancel the isomorphism to conclude smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_smooth_iso_hom_comp: Precompose the given smooth composite with the inverse isomorphism, which is smooth. The two isomorphisms cancel, so the resulting smooth map is p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ambientBlowupSeq_center_eq_image: The ambient center ideal is the image of the lower center ideal along the stage closed immersion. The support of an image ideal along a closed immersion is the image of the original support. Conversion of the lower marked sequence preserves its center ideal, giving the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_imageIdealSheaf_eq_image_support: The support of the image ideal is the closure of the image of the composite from the subscheme defined by Z. The image of that subscheme in the source is the support of Z, so the composite image is the image of this support under the closed immersion. A closed immersion sends this closed support to a closed subset. Taking its closure therefore leaves it unchanged.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientMarkedSeq_boundary: The pushed marked sequence uses the boundaries obtained by starting with the original ambient boundary and applying the boundary recursion of the ambient blowup data. The equality identifies the stage-t lists in these two descriptions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_eq_apply_of_comp_eq: Evaluate the equality of composite morphisms at the given point and expand each composite as successive application of its maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundaryLocus_subset_preimage_otherBound: Without a preparatory blowup, the lower ambient boundary is the original boundary, so j remains an admissible index. Apply the general boundary-locus inclusion. The stage boundary of the pushed marked sequence is the iterated ambient boundary from that same original list. Taking the union over indices other than j gives precisely its other boundary locus.

The preparatory blowup takes strict transforms of all original boundary entries and appends one exceptional entry, so j still lies in the lower ambient list. Apply the general inclusion to this lower boundary. The shifted boundary recursion identifies the ambient stage-t list with the prepended marked sequence's list at stage t+1. Their unions of supports at indices different from j therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundaryLocus_subset_preimage_otherLocus:
At stage zero any entry of the divisor boundary is obtained by pulling back an entry of the starting ambient boundary with index different from j. The stage-zero projection square therefore puts the image of any point of that support in the corresponding ambient support.

For a successor stage, consider first a strict transform of an old divisor-boundary entry. Away from the inverse image of the center, the projection of a point in the transform lies in the old support. By induction its ambient image lies in an old ambient boundary support with index different from j. The transition square and the equality of the inverse image of the ambient center support with the divisor center support put the point's ambient lift in the strict transform of that ambient entry. This entry keeps its index. The ambient union of these supports is closed, as is its inverse image in the divisor. Taking the closure of the inverse-image locus off the center proves the same inclusion for the whole strict-transform support.

For the new exceptional entry, its support is the inverse image of the divisor center support along the transition. The same transition square puts its image in the ambient exceptional support. The ambient exceptional entry is appended after the old entries, so its index differs from j. These are all successor boundary entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_embeddingIntoAmbient_center_ambien: The ambient center is defined as the scheme-theoretic image of the divisor center under the stage embedding. Since the stage embedding is a closed immersion, pulling its image ideal back along the immersion recovers the divisor center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_comp_: At stage zero the embedding is the initial smaller-scheme isomorphism followed by the original closed immersion, and the ambient projection is the identity. This gives the first commuting square. At each successor the two transition maps commute with the embeddings. Compose that square with the preceding projection square and use the successor rule for projections to obtain the next square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbient_comp_projectionToBa: Apply the ambient projection square to the chosen boundary divisor and the underlying blowup data of its marked sequence. The comparison of marked and underlying data identifies their projections, giving the desired formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbient_zero_comp_isoObjZer: Specialize the commuting projection square to stage zero. The ambient and divisor stage-zero projections are the forward maps of their initial isomorphisms, so the two paths in the square are the stated composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_support_of_mem_otherLocusOfLi: Membership in the union yields an index in the finite index set. The corresponding inner union yields both the condition that this index differs from j and membership in its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_iUnion_prop: The index set of proofs of the proposition has at most one element and is therefore finite. Every member is the given closed set, so their finite union is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_otherLocusOfList: For each list index the conditional union is closed, since the support is closed and the condition has at most one witness. The outer union is finite, so it is closed as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_boundary_subscheme: The boundary subscheme is closed in the Noetherian ambient scheme. Its inclusion is quasi-compact and locally of finite type, which makes the boundary subscheme Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt_restrictToBoundary: The chosen divisor is Noetherian as a closed subscheme of the ambient scheme. The blowup sequence over it preserves Noetherianity at every stage bounded by the sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundaryLocus_iff: The boundary locus is the union of supports over all entries of the boundary list. A point in the union has a witnessing entry containing it, and such an entry in turn puts the point in the union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.otherBoundaryLocus_eq_otherLocusOfList: Both sets are defined by taking the supports of the stage-t boundary entries at indices different from j and forming their union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_support_center_ambientBlowupSeq: The inverse image of the ambient center support is the support of its ideal pulled back to the stage divisor. The pullback of the ambient center ideal is exactly the divisor center ideal, so this inverse image is the divisor center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_boundary_succ_eq: At the first prepended stage the boundary is the lower ambient boundary transported through the initial ambient isomorphism, which is the ambient stage-zero boundary. At each later stage the prepended morphism and center are the corresponding ambient morphism and center with the index shifted by one. Equal preceding boundaries give equal strict transforms and equal appended exceptional entries. Induction proves the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_boundary: The marked sequence is formed from the prepended blowup data with the original boundary. By the boundary formula for that construction, its stage-t boundary equals the iterated boundary of the prepended data from the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_eq_comp_ambientMarkedSe: The marked ambient projection to the ground field is the projection to the original ambient scheme followed by its structure map. Compose this with the stage embedding and use the projection square to factor through the original divisor. The divisor inclusion followed by the ambient structure map is the original divisor structure map, so the result is the divisor-stage projection to the ground field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_eq_comp_prependedAmbien: The ambient projection at stage t+1 of the prepended sequence agrees with the unprepended ambient projection at t. After embedding the divisor stage, the projection square identifies the resulting map with the divisor projection followed by the original divisor inclusion. Compose with the ambient structure map. Since this composition gives the divisor's structure map on the original divisor, the full composite is its stage-t projection to the ground field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_otherLocusOfList: The union includes the support at every valid index other than j. Use the given index i to witness membership for any point of its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_otherLocusOfList_append_l: An index in the first list remains valid after a second list is appended, and the entry it selects is unchanged. Since the index differs from j, the same support occurs in the union for the concatenated list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_otherLocusOfList_append_s: The appended entry occurs at the old list length. This index differs from j because j lies in the old list, so the support of the appended entry appears in the union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_projectionToBase_eq: Adding the marked ideal and boundary and passing to the marked sequence preserves the underlying sequence of blowups. Its projection at each stage is therefore the same as the projection in the original data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionProperties_of_blowupPres: Use the normal crossings lifting theorem to mark the ambient sequence from the ordinary restriction. For the twisted restriction, the preliminary center is smooth, has strict normal crossings with the boundary, and lies in the order locus. Its marked power divides the ideal, and its preimage in the chosen divisor is open. These facts give the marking after prepending its blowup. The twisted lower input is admissible by the restriction theorem. In each case the marked controlled-transform theorem preserves the order bound, and the corresponding going-up invariant gives the exceptional factors comparing the ambient and lower ideals. Thus emptiness of the final lower cosupport forces the final ambient order locus to miss the last embedded divisor. In the prepended case this comparison uses the clopen neighborhood supporting the going-up invariant and the controlled-transform formula for the first step. Flat base change gives both ambient tower comparisons. The controlled ideal pullback formulas and the selected center comparisons under field and smooth base change give the remaining properties, including the unit selected center for a marked image ideal on the divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.goingUpInvariant_length_of_isBalanced: The lower ideal before any preliminary blowup equals the original balanced ideal, and the lower boundary is the original strict normal crossings boundary. The chosen divisor is therefore the same entry in both descriptions. Removing that entry leaves a list of length one less than the original length, so truncation at that length keeps the whole list. Apply the going-up induction with these initial data, the positive mark, the admissible restriction, and the lifting property for normal crossings. Evaluate it at the last stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDerivBalanced_of_isBalanced: The balanced condition for the marked input is precisely derivative balance for its ideal at its marking. The property uses the given finite-type structure and therefore applies with the indicated instance of that structure.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_eq_ideal: Without a preliminary blowup the lower ideal on the ambient scheme is the original ideal pulled back along the identity, which fixes it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_mult_of_isOrderBoundedByMult: The order bound by the mark is the pointwise requirement that every stalk order is at most the multiplicity. Applying it at an arbitrary point gives the stated inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap: Pullback of ideal sheaves is contravariantly functorial. Pulling the ideal back along the second morphism and then the first therefore equals pullback along their composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_fieldBaseChangeProjection_ne_top: The field-extension projection is surjective. The general support argument for pullback along a surjective morphism therefore shows that a nonunit ideal remains nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ne_top_of_surjective: A nonunit ideal has a point in its support. Surjectivity lifts this point to the source, and the support of the pullback ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Thus that support is nonempty and the pullback ideal is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_fieldBaseChangeProjection: A field extension is flat as an algebra over the original field, so its map of spectra is flat. The stated projection is the base change of this map along the original structure morphism. Flatness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_id: The identity of a scheme is an isomorphism. An isomorphism is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_fieldBaseChangeProjection: The two field spectra each have a single point, so the map of spectra is surjective. The projection of the base change is its pullback, which preserves surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_id: For each point of the target, the same point in the source maps to it under the identity. Hence the map is surjective.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_ker_of_isOpe: The component locus in this formulation is the same open locus used in the definition of the selected center ideal. Under its openness hypothesis that definition gives the kernel of the composite inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_top_of_not_i: The indicated component locus is the one tested for openness when forming the selected center ideal. If it is not open, the definition yields the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_containedCompone: In the open branch the selected center ideal is the kernel of the composite inclusion. By hypothesis its support pulls back on the divisor to the chosen open component locus. In the other branch the ideal is unit, so its support and the inverse image of the support are both empty and open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_boundary_comap_isoObjZer: The selected boundary entry is a smooth divisor by the strict normal crossings condition. The structural map at stage zero is the original structural map after the stage-zero isomorphism. Smooth divisors are preserved by pullback along this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ker_comp_subschemeι: The kernel of the boundary inclusion is its defining ideal D. Every function vanishing under that inclusion also vanishes after precomposing with the given map into the boundary, so D is contained in the composite kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_mult_of_isAdmissible: Admissibility requires the marking to be a positive natural number. This is the asserted lower bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_containedComponentsIdeal_subset_: If the component locus is open, its composite inclusion into the base factors through the boundary inclusion. The kernel therefore contains the boundary ideal, so its support is contained in the boundary support. If the component locus is not open, the selected ideal is unit and its support is empty.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBoundaryPositionInvariant_divisorFamil: The ambient sequence description gives strict boundary reindexing invariance over the identity. The result relating strict reindexing to boundary position invariance then applies at the stated dimension bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_id_divisorFami: Changing the boundary leaves the ideal and marking fixed. If the order locus is empty, both sequences have zero length and their comparison over the identity is strict. Otherwise the equality of the selected divisor ideals makes the two preliminary center ideals equal, so the construction takes the same branch for both. In the unit branch, the corresponding ordinary lower sequences have a strict comparison by the lower-dimensional boundary reindexing result. The selected divisor embeddings form a pullback square over the identity, so the flat ambient comparison gives the strict comparison of the lifts. In the nonunit branch apply the lower reindexing result to the twisted restrictions and lift the comparison in the same way. The equal preliminary centers allow both first blowups to be prepended to that comparison. The ambient descriptions of the canonical sequences give the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictBoundaryReindexingInvariance_of_di: For arbitrary admissible lists with equal selected ideal and matching remaining nontrivial boundary, the identity-base comparison theorem supplies the strict pullback. This proves the required reindexing property.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_withBoundary_co: The selected center is determined by the marked ideal, its multiplicity, and the selected boundary divisor. Boundary replacement leaves the marked ideal and multiplicity fixed, and the selected divisor ideals agree. The resulting selected centers are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_comap_id_of_eq: The identity pullback of B is B, so the proposed equality is the supplied equality of A and B.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eraseIdx_append_cons_length: The index is just after the first list, so it selects D. Deleting it leaves the first and second lists concatenated in their original order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_append_cons_length: The index is the length of the first list. It skips precisely that prefix of the concatenation, and the first subsequent entry is D.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_comap_id: Pullback along the identity fixes the first selected ideal. The assumed equality of the two selected entries therefore gives the claimed pullback formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBoundaryPositionInvariant_divisorFamil: In each list the distinguished divisor lies at the index given by the length of the preceding list. At those indices the two entries equal that divisor. Deleting the two entries leaves the respective prefixes and suffixes concatenated, so their nontrivial parts agree by the two given comparisons. Strict reindexing invariance gives a strict pullback over the identity. Such a comparison gives an isomorphism of sequences, proving position invariance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_restrictToBoun: The two selected divisor ideals agree after pullback along the ambient identity. Their inclusion square is therefore a pullback of the identity, so the induced divisor map is smooth and surjective. It preserves the structural maps. The lower ideal equality and the commutative square give the restricted ideal equality by composition of pullbacks. The comparison of the shortened boundaries also persists after restriction along that square. The strict smooth comparison for the restricted inputs now applies.

The given ideal equality identifies the new restricted ideal with the pullback of the old restricted ideal. The boundary assumption identifies the nontrivial part of the prescribed new boundary with that of the pulled-back boundary. Together with the structural map compatibility this makes the new input the smooth surjective pullback with the prescribed boundary replacement. Both inputs are admissible below dimension n, so maximum-order reduction gives the strict comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_restrictToDivi: Equal selected divisor ideals give equal selected centers, so both centers are unit. In the ordinary restriction the lower ideals are the same under identity pullback. Removing the selected entry leaves a list of the length retained by the truncation, so the given correspondence of shortened nontrivial boundaries is the required comparison. The ordinary restrictions are admissible, and their dimensions drop strictly below n because the order loci are nonempty. Apply the strict comparison for equal selected divisor entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_restrictTwiste: Equal selected divisor ideals give equal selected centers, so both centers are nonunit. The reindexing formulas identify the lower twisted ideals and the nontrivial parts of the shortened twisted boundaries. Identity pullback fixes these ideals and lists. The twisted inputs are admissible and their dimensions strictly decrease below the original bound. Apply the strict comparison for equal selected divisor entries to these lower data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_of_isStrictPullbackAlongId: At stage zero the strict comparison is the first initial isomorphism followed by the inverse of the second one. Inductively each next comparison is a pullback of the preceding isomorphism, so is also an isomorphism. The commuting squares give transition compatibility, and the center pullback equalities give the center compatibility. These stage isomorphisms, with the given equal lengths and initial compatibility, give a sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_id: Pulling an ideal sheaf back along the identity fixes it. Applying this equality to each entry shows that the mapped list is the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_map_comap_id: Pulling all entries of B back along the identity reproduces B. The given comparison of nontrivial entries therefore applies to the mapped list.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionHypotheses_canonicalAlgo: Begin with the canonical step properties and extract the termination properties. These supply the smooth and field-extension comparisons, and smooth morphisms are flat. Use the separate results for a pulled-back empty center, reindexing the boundary, comparing lower-dimensional data under field extension, and verifying the ambient pushed sequence. Finally, if the order locus becomes empty after pullback, the empty-order-locus theorem identifies any length-zero sequence with the required pullback of the canonical divisor sequence. This gives the remaining clause.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionStepProperties_canonical: The geometric divisor reduction properties apply with the chosen strict-transform result and the Noetherianity of blowups. The theorem converting those geometric properties to step properties then gives the required package.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorRestrictionFieldBaseChange: Use functoriality of ideal pullback and the fact that the field-extension projection detects whether an ideal is unit. The lower-dimensional comparison for restriction to a divisor provides a smooth surjective map and the required ideal and boundary identifications. The untwisted lower ideal and boundary comparisons hold by their base-change formulas. In the twisted case, use the factorization by the selected center power and its identity blowup to transport the lower ideal and boundary. These results give the stated field base-change properties of restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyPulledBackCenterCompatibility: If the selected center pulls back to the unit ideal, its exceptional ideal contributes a unit after pullback. The comparison for the lower ideal identifies the pulled-back twisted and untwisted ideals in this case. The boundary comparison identifies their pulled-back nontrivial boundary entries, giving both required conclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mul_containedComponentsIdeal_pow_: The factorization theorem for the selected center gives an ideal whose product with the selected center raised to the mark is the original ideal. Ideal multiplication is commutative, so the same factorization has the order of factors asserted here.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.fieldBaseChangeCompatibility_of_divisorR: The order locus after field extension is the inverse image of the original order locus. The field extension projection is flat and surjective. The field-extension comparison for selected components identifies the selected center, with admissibility transported across the specified correspondence of nontrivial boundary lists. This supplies the field base-change compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtComapOffExceptionalLocus: For any admissible marked input and blowup, apply the order comparison off the exceptional support. At such a point the pullback ideal has the same order as the original ideal at its image. This supplies the stated comparison for all allowed inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pushedBlowupSequenceProperties_canonical: The preimage of the selected center in the boundary divisor is the open union of its selected connected components. The kernel formulas identify the starting embeddings with the pullbacks of the boundary ideal, using the original initial identification in one case and the prepended transition in the other. The boundary-locus comparisons and the smooth divisor results apply to these same ambient embeddings. For the prepended sequence the smooth divisor argument uses order comparison off the exceptional support together with compatibility of the embedding and projection to the original base. The projections to the field agree with the ambient marked projections in both constructions. Admissibility gives positive multiplicity, and the general support containments for a composite kernel and the selected center supply the remaining conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackCompatibility_of_divisorRe: Under smooth pullback, surjectivity detects nonunit ideals and the order locus pulls back to its inverse image. The maps of the defining subschemes form pullback squares, and smoothness is preserved by those squares. Use the factorization of the selected center power and its identity blowup to transport the post-blowup lower ideal and the list of nontrivial boundary entries. Finally the smooth comparison for selected connected components identifies the selected center ideals. These give all the stated smooth pullback properties.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_base_comp: On an underlying point the composite first applies the point map of the first morphism and then that of the second. This is the stated equality of functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comap_ι_eq_self_of_suppo: Every point of the closed subscheme defined by Z maps into the given open, so the inverse image open in that subscheme is the whole subscheme. Its open inclusion is therefore an isomorphism. Restricting Z to the open and taking its image back in the ambient scheme gives the kernel of the composite from this inverse image open. Precomposition by the open isomorphism preserves the kernel, so this is the original defining ideal Z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedEmbedding_base_opens_ι_comp_of_i: The open inclusion is a topological embedding onto the given subset, which is closed by hypothesis. It is therefore a closed embedding. The second map is also a closed embedding, so the composite is one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_preimage_ι_comp_eq_strictTransform_o: The inverse images of the two given opens cover the new ambient scheme. On the first, commutativity makes the inverse image along the new immersion lie entirely in the selected lower open. There the kernel of the selected inclusion equals the full embedding kernel, both before and after the transformation. Apply the full strict-transform equality and the locality of strict transform. On the second open the selected original image is empty by hypothesis, and the selected new image is also disjoint by commutativity. The restricted kernels are unit there, and the transform of the unit ideal is unit. The two local equalities prove the global equality.

The clopen subset and its complement have disjoint closed images in the original ambient scheme under the closed immersion. Their open complements cover the ambient scheme. The complement of the image of the unselected part has inverse image inside U, and the complement of the image of U misses every selected point. The inverse image of U under the lower transition remains clopen. The two-open strict-transform comparison now applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_of_isClosedEmbedding_base: A closed embedding identifies the inverse image of a quasi-compact open with its intersection with the closed image. That intersection is closed in the quasi-compact open and is quasi-compact. This gives quasi-compactness of the morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_base_comp: The underlying point map of the composite is the composite of the two underlying functions. Its range is the image of the range of the first function under the second.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_base_preimage_ι_comp_ι_eq_of_le: The composite inclusion has image the intersection of U with the inverse image of W under f. That inverse image is contained in U by hypothesis, so the intersection equals the full inverse image. This is the range of its own inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_exceptionalIdeal: The exceptional ideal is the pullback of the center. Restricting it is pullback along the inclusion of the inverse-image open. The composite with the original morphism equals the restricted morphism followed by the original open inclusion. Functoriality identifies this with the pullback of the restricted center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_ker_opens_ι_comp_of_preima: The hypothesis gives equal images in the original source for the inverse-image open of W under f and the inverse-image open under its restriction to U. Both are open immersions into the original source, so their domains are canonically isomorphic over it. The induced maps to W coincide under that isomorphism, since their composites with the open inclusion agree. The restrictions of the kernel ideals are the kernels of these two maps, which agree under precomposition by the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_congr: Restricting a strict transform to the inverse image of W computes the strict transform of the restrictions along the restricted morphism. The center is the same in both computations and the two restricted input ideals agree by hypothesis. Their strict transforms therefore agree on this open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_preimage: First restrict the strict transform on the source by composing the morphism with the inverse-image open inclusion. This composite is the restricted morphism followed by the open inclusion of W. The strict-transform rule for composition with that open inclusion replaces the center and input ideal by their restrictions, giving the stated formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ker_opens_ι_comp: The composite of the clopen inclusion and the closed immersion is a closed embedding on points and is quasi-compact. Its kernel support is the closure of its image. The image is the closed image of the given open subset under f, so its closure is itself.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_withBoundary_ba: Restore the original base-changed boundary to deduce admissibility of the unreplaced base-changed input, since the nontrivial entries agree. Equality of the prefixes gives equality of the selected entries at j. The selected center is therefore the same with either boundary. Without the replacement, the field base-change formula identifies this center with the pullback of the original selected center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_withBoundary_of: The selected ideal is determined by the ideal and mark of the input and the boundary entry at the selected index. The first two are fixed by boundary replacement, and the two selected entries agree by hypothesis. Substitution gives the same selected ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_of_withBoundary_isAdmissibl: The equality of nontrivial boundary lists is symmetric. Apply the assumed admissibility transport to the replaced input with the original boundary as the new list. Replacing that boundary restores the original input, so it is admissible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_eq_ideal: In the absence of the preliminary blowup the lower ideal is the original ideal pulled back along the identity, so it equals the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_withBoundary_bas: Before a preliminary blowup the lower ideal in either input is its given ideal. Changing the boundary does not change that ideal, and the ideal of the field-base-changed input is the pullback along its projection. This is the required equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_baseChange: The field-extension projection is flat. The boundary is pulled back entry by entry, and the field-extension order comparison makes the new order locus the inverse image of the original closed order locus. The flat comparison of selected component kernels then gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_comap_of_flat: The two admissible boundary divisors are Noetherian, and their selected unions are open. The original boundary has irreducible connected components because it is smooth. The assumptions identify the new boundary ideal with the pullback of the original one and the new order locus with the inverse image of the original order locus. Thus the two selected ideals are the kernels of the open and closed parts related by the flat kernel comparison for the given closed order locus. This yields the pullback equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_pullbackAlong_o: The smooth map is flat. The new boundary entry is the pullback of the original one by the entrywise boundary formula. In characteristic zero the order locus for the original smooth input is closed, and its smooth pullback is its inverse image. Apply the flat comparison for selected components to these data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_comap_get_of_eq_map: The replacement list is obtained by applying pullback to each entry of the original list in order. Evaluation at the valid index thus gives the pullback of the original entry at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducible_connectedComponent_boundar: The boundary divisor is smooth and Noetherian, so its irreducible components are pairwise disjoint and open and closed. The connected component of the point is contained in an irreducible component through it. That irreducible component is connected, hence is contained in the connected component. They are therefore equal and the connected component is irreducible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.openSubschemeKer_comap_of_flat_of_noethe: Both selected loci are unions of connected components in Noetherian spaces, hence are closed in addition to the assumed openness. The original connected components are irreducible and the original ambient locus is closed. These are the hypotheses for the flat pullback formula for the kernel of an open and closed part of a subscheme. Applying it gives the equality of the new selected ideal and the pullback of the original one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_openSubschem: When the indicated union of components is open, the contained-components ideal is defined as the kernel of the inclusion of that open subscheme into the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_top_of_not_i: In the branch where the selected union of components fails to be open, the defining rule for the contained-components ideal assigns the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_containedComponentsIde: A point of the support forces the selected union to be open, since otherwise the ideal is unit. It is then an open and closed union of boundary components, and the point lies in its image. Choose an ambient neighborhood whose inverse image in the boundary lies in that union. Intersect it with a strict normal crossings chart around the point. On the intersection the contained-components ideal agrees with the chosen boundary ideal. That boundary entry cannot restrict to the unit ideal, since the point lies in its support, so the original chart assigns it a coordinate b. The restricted chart retains all the individual boundary coordinate or unit descriptions and their distinctness. The contained-components ideal is the ideal of b there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mul_pow_containedComponentsIdeal_: The selected center has strict normal crossings with the boundary and its support lies in the order-at-least-multiplicity locus. The corresponding ideal power containment gives inclusion of the marked ideal in the selected center ideal to the marked power. That power is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. Dividing an ideal contained in an invertible ideal by the latter gives an ideal sheaf, whose product with the center power recovers the marked ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_containedCo: At each point of the center support use the adapted chart for the contained-components ideal. Every boundary entry is unit or a distinct coordinate ideal, and the center is cut out by a single coordinate from that chart. These local descriptions give the strict normal crossings condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_id_containedComp: The selected ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. It is therefore already invertible as an ideal, and its blowup is the identity by the blowup universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_divisorComponentsInOrderLocus: The boundary subscheme is Noetherian, so it has finitely many connected components, each of which is closed. The indicated set is the union of the connected components contained in the inverse image of the order locus. It is therefore closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_conta: For an open selected union, the union is also closed in the boundary divisor. Its defining ideal agrees locally with the smooth divisor ideal along that union and with the unit ideal off it. Both ideals are locally generated by a nonzero divisor. In the other case the ideal is unit everywhere, so one is a generator.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_boundary_get: Admissibility states that the boundary has strict normal crossings, in particular each entry defines a smooth divisor over the field. The given index is in range, so the chosen entry has that property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_boundary_subscheme: Admissibility makes the ambient scheme Noetherian. The boundary subscheme is closed in it, so its underlying topological space is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_containedComponentsIde: If the selected union is open, it is also closed and its kernel subscheme is that open and closed part of the smooth boundary divisor. Its map to the field is smooth by restriction. If the union fails to be open, the selected ideal is unit, so its zero subscheme is empty and its map to the field is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_containedComponentsIdeal_subset_: If the selected union is open, it is also closed in the boundary divisor. The support of the kernel of its inclusion is then its image. Each point in that image comes from a point whose full connected component maps into the order locus, so its image lies there. In the other case the ideal is unit and has empty support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_top_of_eq_im: Pullback to the boundary divisor recovers J from its image ideal. The mark is one, so the order locus is the support of the image ideal, and its inverse image lies in the support of J. If any connected component lay in that inverse image, an irreducible component through one of its points would lie there as well, since an irreducible component is connected. This contradicts nonvanishing of the admissible ideal J on components. Thus the selected union is empty. Its kernel ideal has empty support and is unit. If the selected union is treated by the non-open branch of the definition, that branch also gives the unit ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_pullbackAlong_o: The ordinary pulled-back boundary has the same length as the original boundary, so the selected position exists there. Restore this boundary to recover admissibility of the ordinary pulled-back input by the given transport. Equality of the prefixes makes the selected divisor and hence the selected ideal unchanged by replacement. Apply the selected-component pullback formula for the ordinary smooth pullback.

Admissibility of the ordinary pullback follows by restoring its original boundary from the admissible replacement. Supply this admissibility transport to the theorem that compares the selected ideal under smooth pullback with boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_of_withBoundary_isAdmissibl: Reverse the equality of nontrivial boundary lists. The admissibility transport theorem now allows the original boundary to replace the new one. This replacement recovers the original input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_pullbackAlong_of_withBounda: Apply the boundary restoration result to the pulled-back input. The two lists have the same nontrivial entries, so admissibility of the replacement gives admissibility of the unreplaced pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_of_smooth: Admissibility gives characteristic zero and a smooth original structure morphism. The order of an ideal is preserved at points under smooth pullback in this setting. The locus where the pulled-back order reaches the specified threshold is therefore the inverse image of the original locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_isPullback: The pullback square identifies the map between the closed subschemes as the base change of the given smooth ambient map. Smoothness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_withBoundary: Boundary replacement replaces the list while keeping the other data. Applying it a second time leaves the second list as the boundary, exactly as direct replacement by that list does.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_congr: The pulled-back boundary lists agree at stage zero by hypothesis. Each successor boundary is the list of strict transforms of the previous entries followed by the same exceptional ideal. Induction therefore gives equal lists at each stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iSup_le_nat: At upper bound zero both sides are the pullback of the single term at zero. At a successor bound the supremum is the sum of the preceding supremum and the new term. Pullback preserves this sum, and induction identifies the pullback of the preceding supremum with the preceding supremum of pullbacks.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_congr: At stage zero the two controlled transforms are the pullbacks of the two given ideals along the initial projection, which agree by assumption. At a successor, both transforms apply the same pullback and exceptional division to the previous ideal. The induction hypothesis makes those previous ideals equal, so the next transforms agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbient_comp_projectionToBa: At stage zero the ambient initial isomorphism is the identity. The embedding at zero is the initial projection of the divisor sequence followed by the original divisor embedding, giving the base case. At the next stage, express the ambient projection as the new transition followed by the preceding projection. Move the new embedding across the transition by the commutative blowup square. Apply induction to the preceding stage and then use the projection recursion on the divisor sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iSup_le_zero_nat: The only natural index at most zero is zero. Thus the bounded supremum consists of the single term at zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iSup_le_nat: At the point in question every stalk ideal lies in the maximal ideal, because the point lies in its support. The stalk of the bounded supremum is the finite sum of those stalk ideals, so is also contained in the maximal ideal. Hence the point is in the support of the supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_orderAtLeastLoc: The ideal power containment gives an order inequality in the reverse direction. Order of a power multiplies the order of the original ideal by the exponent. At a point where A has order at least m, it follows that m times the order of K is at least m times m−l. Since m is positive, cancel it to get order of K at least m−l. This is membership in the asserted locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_controlledTransform_le_pow_controlle: Pull the preceding containment back along the transition morphism. By the two divisibility hypotheses, these pulled-back powers are powers of the successor transforms times exceptional factors. The two exceptional exponents both equal m times m−l. The exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, so this common factor can be canceled from the containment. This gives the inclusion for the successor transforms.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_eq_comap_controlledTransf: The center has strict normal crossings with the boundary and is contained in the order-at-least-n locus. Hence the current ideal lies in the nth power of the center ideal. Under the blowup that power pulls back to the corresponding exceptional power, which is invertible. Dividing the pulled-back ideal by it yields the claimed factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_ambientDerivIdeal_le_pow_controlledT: The initial derivative power inclusion is the derivative balance of I₀ at order l. The ambient derivative ideal sequence is the controlled transform of this initial derivative ideal with marking m−l, where m is the original mark. The ambient and divisor sequences have equal lengths, so the stage is within range. Apply the iterated transform power comparison with marks m−l and m and the given exceptional divisibility at every preceding step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_controlledTransform_le_pow_controlle: Induct on the stage. Initially the ideal powers are pulled back along the initial isomorphism, which preserves their inclusion. At a successor stage the step is a blowup and its exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. Both input transform ideals are divisible by the requisite exceptional powers after pullback. The one-step comparison preserves the power inclusion by canceling the common exceptional power from the pulled-back inclusion supplied by induction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_isoObjZero_hom: The initial isomorphism of the ambient sequence is the identity isomorphism on the original scheme. Its forward map is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_embeddingIntoA: At stage zero the ambient initial isomorphism is the identity. Its ideal pulled back to the lower zero stage is the original ideal pulled back along the divisor inclusion and the lower initial isomorphism, which is the lower initial ideal. Assume the comparison at a stage before the last. The ambient center is the image of the lower center, and the two blowup maps form a commuting closed immersion square. The given divisibility supplies the ambient product formula, while the marked lower sequence supplies the lower formula with the compatible preceding ideal. The lower exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. The one-step controlled-transform comparison now gives equality of the next ideals after restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_of_closedImmer: Pull back the ambient controlled-transform product equality to the lower blowup scheme. Pullback preserves products and powers, and the exceptional ideal pulls back to the lower exceptional ideal. Commutativity makes the pulled-back total ideal the same one as in the lower product equality. The two transformed ideals therefore become equal after multiplication by the same exceptional power. This power is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, so cancel it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_exceptionalIdeal_of_closedImmersio: The ambient exceptional ideal is the pullback of the image center along the ambient blowup. Pulling it back again to the smaller source equals pulling back along the composite across the square. By commutativity this is the pullback along the lower blowup of the restriction of the image center to the original closed subscheme. That restriction recovers the original center. Its pullback is the lower exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbient_comp_blowupMorphism: The embedding and ambient sequence are those constructed from the selected divisor immersion and the lower sequence. The construction makes each adjacent square commute. Conversion to blowup data preserves the lower adjacent map, giving the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbient_zero: The general ambient construction starts by taking the lower initial isomorphism followed by the closed immersion used as input. Here that immersion is the inclusion of the chosen boundary divisor.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_ideal_eq_top_of_not_me: Choose an affine neighborhood of the point. The point lies outside the common zero locus of the ideal there, so some section in the ideal is invertible at that point. Restrict to its affine basic open. The section belongs to the restricted ideal and is a unit on that open, which makes the restricted ideal unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDerivBalanced_of_pow_mul: Check each derivative power inclusion on an affine neighborhood of each point. At a point in the support of Z, the residual ideal I₀ is unit on a suitable affine neighborhood, so the target ideal power in the inclusion is unit. Outside that support, choose an affine neighborhood on which Z is unit. There the factorization identifies I₀ with I, and their iterated derivative ideals agree on that neighborhood. The assumed derivative balance of I gives the inclusion there. The local inclusions give derivative balance of I₀.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_mem_support_of_mem_support_of_pow_mu: At a point of the support of Z, the stalk ideal of Z lies in the maximal ideal. If the stalk of I₀ also lay in the maximal ideal, the factorization would put the stalk of I in the (m+1)st power of the maximal ideal. Its order would then be at least m+1, contrary to the order bound.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReduction.divisorReductionSeq_cen: If the order locus is empty, the sequence has zero length and there are no genuine steps. Otherwise use the two ambient descriptions. In the ordinary case, a step index is a step of the lower sequence because the lengths agree. The lower input is admissible and has dimension below the reduction bound. Its center is nonempty by lower-dimensional correctness, and the ambient center is the image of that center under the stage closed immersion, so it is nonempty. In the prepended case, the first center is nonempty because its ideal is nonunit. Every later center is an image of a genuine center of the lower twisted sequence and is nonempty by the same lower-dimensional result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReduction.divisorReductionSeq_eq_: The nonempty order locus gives the strict dimension drop for restricting to the chosen divisor. If the selected center is unit, the ordinary lower input is admissible. Its sequence has centers containing no component, and the ambient lift carries the original marking. The unit-center branch of the construction therefore returns this marked lift. If the center is nonunit, its identity blowup exists and the twisted lower input is admissible. The resulting lower sequence again has centers containing no component, and the lift after prepending the first blowup is marked. The nonunit branch returns that prepended marked lift. The corresponding equality holds for any witness of the given marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReduction.divisorReductionSeq_ord: When the order locus is empty the sequence has only its initial stage, with the original ideal and the assumed order bound. For a nonempty locus, use the appropriate ambient description according to whether a preliminary blowup is inserted. In each case the stage ideals are precisely the controlled transforms of the original ideal in the ambient sequence, and the length formulas give the matching index range. The order bounds for controlled transforms in the ordinary and prepended cases give the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_canonicalAlgorithmRules_ce: Replace the canonical divisor family by its equivalent divisor reduction construction. Lower-dimensional correctness and the divisor-reduction hypotheses then give nonempty center support at each genuine step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_canonicalAlgorithmRules_eq: Evaluating the canonical rules' divisor family uses the divisor reduction construction with blowups that preserve Noetherianity. Its lower-dimensional algorithm is the given assignment evaluated on the restricted input. Expanding the rule gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_canonicalAlgorithmRules_le: The canonical divisor family evaluates to the divisor reduction sequence for the chosen divisor. With an empty order locus this construction gives the empty marked sequence, whose length is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_canonicalAlgorithmRules_or: The canonical sequence is the divisor reduction sequence for the same assignment. Apply the stagewise order bound for the latter sequence to each of its transformed ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_imageIdealSheaf_nonempty: Choose a point of the support of J. It comes from a point of the closed subscheme defined by J. The image of this point under the composite to the target lies in the support of the composite kernel, since that support contains the image. The composite kernel is the image ideal, so its support is nonempty.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReductionHypotheses.divisorReduct: Admissibility gives the Noetherian ambient scheme needed for the ambient sequence construction. The formula for a nonempty order locus has two cases. If the selected center is empty it gives the ambient sequence of the ordinary restriction, and if the center is nonempty it gives a preliminary blowup followed by the ambient sequence of the twisted restriction. In each case use the supplied marking of that sequence to obtain the comparison as a marked blowup sequence.
Take the divisor step properties from the hypotheses and use the construction of termination properties from those step properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReductionHypotheses.trivialPullba: The hypotheses give a pullback comparison for a zero-length pulled-back sequence when its order locus is empty. Apply the characterization of pullbacks of empty sequences to this comparison, for each allowed input and divisor index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBoundaryDivisorReduction_divisorFamily: For a nonempty order locus use the construction's formula as an ambient divisor sequence, with the preliminary step exactly when the selected center is nonempty. Apply the two field-extension comparisons and the two smooth-pullback comparisons to that formula and to lower-dimensional maximum-order reduction. Use the empty-center comparison in the smooth case where steps disappear. The controlled transforms satisfy the marked order bound, and each step has nonempty center, by the corresponding canonical sequence properties. The pushforward and smooth-divisor sequence results give the required closed immersion and boundary comparisons. When the order locus is empty the canonical sequence has length zero. These properties are exactly the boundary divisor reduction conditions at the given dimension level.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBoundaryPositionInvariant_divisorFamil: The canonical divisor sequence has the ambient description supplied by the divisor hypotheses. The boundary reindexing theorem for sequences with this description uses smooth pullback compatibility and the given reindexing invariance of the divisor data. Applying it with the lower-dimensional maximum-order reduction proves the required invariance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullbackOfSmoothBaseChangeOnDiviso: For a unit selected ideal on both sides, use strict smooth pullback compatibility of the ordinary divisor restriction of the lower-dimensional reduction. For a nonunit selected ideal, use the corresponding theorem for the twisted restriction. These provide the two cases of strict pullback on the divisor.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReductionProperties.toDivisorRedu: Use the assumed divisor properties for the ambient marking, order bounds, cosupport, comparisons, and transformed ideals. The selected component ideal factors off to the marked power and has identity blowup because it is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. Its center is smooth with strict normal crossings and lies in the required order locus. In the case of unit selected ideal, the admissibility theorem for the ordinary restriction supplies the lower-dimensional input. These results fill the additional requirements for the step.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_of_eq_imag: The untwisted lower ideal is the original ideal, since identity pullback does nothing. By hypothesis this is the image of J along the closed divisor inclusion. Pulling back that image along the same inclusion recovers J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.heq_toSequenceOfBlowups_of_eq: Substitute the equality of the marked inputs. Both assigned sequences now come from the same input and the underlying sequences are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_divisorFamily_can: The mark is one, so an empty ambient order locus implies that the ambient ideal has empty support and is unit. Its pullback to the divisor is J and is also unit. The two reductions then have length zero by the empty-order-locus properties, and the length-zero pushforward result applies. If the order locus is nonempty, the selected preliminary ideal is unit because the ambient ideal is the image of an admissible divisor ideal at mark one. The canonical sequence is therefore the ambient lift of the ordinary restriction. That restriction has ideal J and the original boundary with the selected entry deleted and the others pulled back. The ambient tower is the pushforward of this lower sequence by construction. Converting its marking and the lower sequence data preserves the pushforward comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_of_ofSequenceOfBl: Converting the source to blowup data and back preserves its length, stages, initial isomorphism, adjacent maps, and centers. The stage embeddings in the given pushforward comparison therefore have the same types and satisfy the same compatibility conditions for the original source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_toSequenceOfBlowu: The unmarked data of the marked sequence are obtained by converting its underlying sequence. The given comparison for the converted source therefore gives the same comparison for the original source by the conversion result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardSequenceOfBlowups_of_length: Both sequences consist of their initial stages. Identify each initial stage with its base, and use the given closed immersion between the bases to define the stage embedding. It is a closed immersion and commutes with those identifications. There are no transitions, centers, or strict-transform conditions at indices below length zero. These data witness the pushforward.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_take_eraseIdx_lowerBoundaryWit: The untwisted lower boundary is the original list because pulling each entry back along the identity fixes it. Removing the selected entry leaves exactly the original length minus one entries, so the truncation retains them all. Pulling this list back along the divisor inclusion then gives the asserted list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictToDivisor_eq_withSchemeIdealBoun: The ordinary divisor restriction uses the boundary subscheme with its induced structural map. Its ideal is J because the ambient ideal is the image of J, which pulls back to J. Its boundary is the restriction of the original list with the selected entry removed, by the deletion and truncation formula. These are precisely the data on the right.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_ker: The chosen boundary components form an open subset by assumption. The definition then takes the kernel of its inclusion into the boundary followed by the boundary inclusion into the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_top_of_not_i: The selected union fails the openness condition in the definition. The other branch assigns the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionSeqFromLowerDim_eq: The lower-dimensional form is defined by applying the divisor reduction construction with the same algorithm, marked input, and divisor index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionSeq_eq_empty_of_orderAtL: The divisor index is valid, so the construction reaches the order-locus test. That locus is empty by hypothesis, and the definition returns the empty marked sequence in this case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionSeq_eq_liftSeqFromDiviso: The index is valid and the order locus is nonempty. The selected center is unit, so the construction lifts the divisor sequence from the ideal and boundary pulled back along the identity, with no initial step inserted.

The valid index and nonempty order locus allow the reduction to proceed. The selected center is nonunit and its identity blowup property is given. Thus the construction uses the residual ideal obtained by dividing off the marked exceptional power and the boundary given by strict transforms with the exceptional ideal appended. The lifted sequence is preceded by the blowup of the selected center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_prependMap: At index zero the new map is the original initial isomorphism. The given blowup property of the identity along Z is preserved by precomposing it with this isomorphism, so the new first map is a blowup along Z. At index n+1, the new map and center are the original ones at n. The length bound ensures that this original index is a genuine step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftSeqFromDivisor_eq_toMarkedSequence: The strict dimension inequality and Noetherianity allow the construction to apply the lower-dimensional algorithm. The lower sequence has proper centers, so its ambient lift exists. The transformed ambient sequence satisfies the required marking, so the last test also succeeds. The construction therefore returns that marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_blowupMorphism_succ: At successor index n+1, the transition in the prepended sequence is defined to be the original transition at n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_blowupMorphism_zero: The new first transition goes from the original initial stage to the base scheme. It is defined to be the forward map of the original initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_succ: After the inserted center, the center at the new index n+1 is the original center at n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_zero: The inserted first step uses the supplied center ideal Z on the base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_isoObjZero: The new initial stage is the base itself, and its specified isomorphism to the base is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_length: The new sequence keeps all original steps and adds one initial step, so its specified length is the original length plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_schemeAt_succ: The old stage n is placed at the new stage n+1, giving the stage equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_schemeAt_zero: By construction, the newly inserted initial stage is the base scheme X.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.DivisorReductionStepProperties.toDivisor: Use the supplied step properties for the factorization, marking, lower-dimensional admissibility, controlled order, cosupport, and the geometric comparisons. The remaining requirements follow from the dimension bound for restriction to a boundary divisor, the no-component result for centers of an admissible marked sequence, and openness of the union of selected connected components. Together these give the termination properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersContainNoComponent_of_isAdmissibl: In an admissible marked sequence every center lies in the order locus of positive multiplicity. The theorem on centers of such sequences uses the effective Cartier property to show that a center cannot contain a component. Apply it to the given marked sequence and its underlying blowup data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dim_restrictToBoundaryDivisor_lt: Nonemptiness of the order locus implies nonemptiness of the ambient scheme. The selected entry of the strict normal crossings boundary is a smooth divisor and its ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. The ambient scheme has finite topological Krull dimension by admissibility. The restricted marked ideal lives on the divisor's closed subscheme, whose successor dimension is strictly smaller by the divisor dimension bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_mem_boundary: The selected boundary ideal is the list entry at a valid index, so it is a member of that list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_range_subschemeι: The subscheme inclusion is a closed immersion, so its underlying map has closed image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_setOf_connectedComponent_subset: For any point whose connected component is contained in the given set, the component is open by Noetherianity. Every point of that component has the same connected component and therefore satisfies the same containment. Thus the component is an open neighborhood inside the specified set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_setOf_connectedComponent_subset_o: The ambient scheme is Noetherian by admissibility. The boundary closed subscheme is homeomorphic to a subspace of it, so is Noetherian. Apply the openness result for unions of connected components to the inverse image of the order locus in that boundary subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_zero_of_isEmpty: An empty space has no nonempty irreducible closed subsets. Its topological Krull dimension is therefore bottom, and the successor dimension sends bottom to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_subscheme_lt_of_isLocallyGe: If the subscheme is empty its successor dimension is zero, while the nonempty ambient scheme has successor dimension at least one. Otherwise identify it topologically with its nonempty closed image. This image is the support of D, which contains no ambient irreducible component because D is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. The dimension bound for nonempty closed subsets of finite-dimensional schemes gives a strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_homeomorph_subscheme_range_subs: A closed immersion is a topological embedding. It restricts to a homeomorphism from its source onto its image, here the range of the closed subscheme inclusion.
