Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_krullDimSucc: Nonemptiness places the topological Krull dimension above the bottom value. For such a dimension, the conversion to the natural-number successor dimension is one plus its natural-number value, which is at least one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_ne_bot_of_nonempty: Choose a point of the nonempty scheme. Its closure is a nonempty irreducible closed subset, so the ordered set of irreducible closed subsets is nonempty. Its Krull dimension is therefore above the bottom value.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isPullbackBlowupSequence_f: Use lower-dimensional correctness to obtain the two strict comparisons for restricted divisors. The canonical center theorem makes every actual center nonempty. Therefore removing empty-center steps from the field-extended sequence yields an isomorphic sequence. The field-extension pullback theorem uses these facts to give the asserted comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_: Lower-dimensional correctness provides strict comparisons for field extension and smooth surjective pullback. The restricted divisor theorem combines them to give the lower comparisons for both kinds of divisor input. Supply these comparisons to the strict field-extension theorem for the ambient divisor family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictToBoundaryDivisor_isStrictPullba: Compare the divisor cut out after field extension with the field extension of the original restricted divisor. The restriction comparison gives a smooth surjective map to the latter, with matching projections and nontrivial boundary entries and with admissibility transported to the intermediate input. The strict dimension drops on both sides put the original, intermediate, and final divisor inputs below n. Apply the field-extension comparison to the original input and the intermediate one. The ideal pullback around the divisor square and the boundary comparison identify the final restricted input with the smooth pullback of the intermediate one with its prescribed boundary. Apply the smooth surjective comparison to this second map. Composing the two strict comparisons gives the stated one over the induced divisor map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedFieldBaseChange_of_strictPullb: In the unit-center case the ordinary restricted ideals and boundaries match under field extension, and both ordinary restrictions are admissible. Apply the strict comparison for restricted divisors. In the nonunit case the field-extension projection preserves nonunit ideals, so both twisted restrictions are admissible. Their ideals and nontrivial boundaries match by the post-blowup field-extension formulas. Apply the same strict comparison to the twisted data. These are the two required properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullbackFieldBaseChangeOfDimLT_of_: Maximum-order reduction correctness below dimension n includes the strict field-extension comparison for admissible inputs below that bound. Applying this clause gives the stated lower-dimensional property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullbackSmoothSurjectiveOfDimLT_of: The strict smooth surjective pullback requirement of maximum-order reduction correctness applies to the given admissible inputs below dimension n. This supplies the indicated compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_heq_of_eq: Replace the marked inputs by their common value. The assignment gives the same marked sequence and hence the same underlying sequence.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_mem_orderAtLeastLocus: Write the positive mark as n+1. The center lies in the order-at-least-n locus and has strict normal crossings, so the stage ideal is contained in the nth power of the center ideal. The transform of mark n therefore exists. The marked product formula identifies it with the product of the exceptional ideal and the given transform of mark n+1. At the chosen point this product still has order at least n+1, since multiplying by an ideal cannot decrease order. The order estimate for the controlled transform of mark n sends this locus into the preceding order-at-least-n+1 locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_disjoint_range_of_preimage_orderA: Every center point lies in the current order locus, and its projection lies in the original order locus by the iterated comparison. If that projection were the image of a point of Y, that point would lie in the inverse image of the original order locus. The hypothesis says that inverse image is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isPullbackSequenceOfBlowup: Smooth pullback identifies the pulled-back order locus with the inverse image of the original order locus. Replacing the boundary leaves the ideal used for that locus fixed, so the assumed empty locus makes this inverse image empty. The smooth map is flat. Apply the comparison for disjoint centers to the canonical divisor sequence and the given length-zero sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_of_preimage_: The center projections all miss the image of Y by the disjointness result. Under flat base change every center is consequently empty and its blowup is omitted. The comparison for sequences whose centers miss the base-change image therefore gives the pullback relation with the arbitrary length-zero sequence on Y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_mem_orderAtLeastLocus: At zero the ideal and order locus are obtained from the original ideal and locus by the initial isomorphism. At a later stage, the single-step order comparison sends a point in the order locus to the preceding order locus. The stages are smooth and Noetherian by the admissible sequence results, so this comparison applies at each step. Induction along the composite projection gives the result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isPullbackBlowupSequence: If the original order locus is empty, its smooth pullback is empty as well, so both divisor sequences have zero length. If only the pulled-back locus is empty, the pulled-back sequence has zero length and the empty-cosupport comparison gives the desired pullback. Suppose both loci are nonempty. The selected center on the source of the smooth morphism is the pullback of the original selected center. In particular, a unit center on the original scheme stays unit on pullback. For two unit centers, the lower-dimensional ordinary restrictions give a pullback sequence on the divisors, and flat compatibility of the ambient construction lifts it to the full schemes. For a nonunit original center whose pullback becomes unit, use the mixed comparison between the twisted original restriction and the ordinary restriction after pullback. Lift that comparison to the ambient sequences and omit the prepended step after pullback because its center is empty. When the selected center remains nonunit, use the two twisted restrictions, lift their comparison, and prepend the paired blowups along the original and pulled-back centers. These cases give the asserted comparison.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isPullbackSequenceOfBlowup: Use the strict field-extension comparison first. Deleting the empty-center steps of the pulled-back sequence gives its pullback comparison with omissions. By the center assumption every actual step of that sequence has nonempty support, so its center ideal is nonunit. The deletion theorem therefore identifies the shortened sequence with the original pulled-back sequence, and transport gives the stated comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_: Field extension gives a flat surjective projection, keeps the mark, and pulls the order locus back to its inverse image. If the original locus is empty, both sequences have length zero and their comparisons are strict pullbacks. Otherwise both loci are nonempty by surjectivity. The selected center commutes with this base change, and surjectivity means that it is unit on both sides or nonunit on both sides. In the unit case the lower-dimensional ordinary sequences are strict pullbacks by hypothesis. Apply the flat ambient comparison to the pullback square of the divisor inclusions. In the nonunit case use the strict comparison for the twisted lower sequences and the same ambient result. The selected centers are related by pullback, so their preliminary blowups can be prepended to the strict comparison. The descriptions of the canonical divisor sequences identify these comparisons with the asserted one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_comap_fieldBaseChangeProjection: The two prefixes of length j+1 agree. Since the replacement list has an entry at j, this equality shows the base-changed list also has one there, and the two entries agree. The base-changed boundary is obtained by pulling each original entry back along the field-extension projection. Taking its jth entry gives the stated pullback.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_boundary_zero: The initial boundary of a sequence is the given list pulled back entry by entry along its initial isomorphism. For the ambient sequence this is the identity, so the boundary is the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientDerivIdeal_at_zero_eq_derivIdealS: The ambient derivative term is the controlled-transform sequence of the given iterated derivative ideal. At stage zero the transform is pullback along the initial ambient isomorphism, which is the identity. Thus it is the initial iterated derivative ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientDerivIdeal_le_center_pow: When l is below the mark, the power comparison and the order condition of the ambient center put the center in the order-at-least-m−l locus of the derivative term, where m is the mark. Its strict normal crossings then give containment in the corresponding center power. When l equals m the center power is unit and contains every ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientDerivIdeal_order_zero_eq_controll: An iterated derivative of order zero is the original ideal, and subtracting zero from the mark leaves it unchanged. The ambient derivative term is therefore the original ideal's controlled transform with the original mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform: The invariant gives the exceptional divisibilities needed at every stage before t, by using derivative order zero. The stagewise comparison of ambient controlled transforms with their divisor restrictions therefore applies. It identifies the restriction at t with the marked lower ideal there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_congr: Substitute the equality of the two structural morphisms. Both iterates are then formed with the same field, structural morphism, ideal, and order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_eq_comap: Apply the derivative divisibility clause of the invariant at order zero and the indicated earlier stage. At order zero the derivative ideal is the ordinary controlled transform and the exceptional exponent is the original mark. Its factor is the desired witness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_ker_subschemeι: A closed immersion is an isomorphism onto its scheme-theoretic image. That image is the subscheme cut out by its kernel. The isomorphism followed by the image inclusion is the given immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_eq_comap_ambientDerivIdea: For derivative order l below the mark m, the preceding exceptional divisibilities and derivative balance give the power inequality comparing the derivative term with the ambient controlled ideal. Hence the ambient center, lying in the latter ideal's order-at-least-m locus, lies in the derivative term's order-at-least-m−l locus. Normal crossings give containment in the corresponding center power. After blowing up, this power becomes an invertible exceptional power, so the pulled-back derivative ideal has the claimed factorization. When l equals m the exponent is zero and the pulled-back ideal itself is the factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.goingUpInvariant_zero: The initial ambient structure map, ideal, and boundary are the given ones, because the initial ambient isomorphism is the identity. There are no earlier steps requiring divisibility. For each derivative order n below the mark, the term with index n in the logarithmic sum is the original ordinary derivative of order n, since its remaining logarithmic order is zero. This gives the derivative bound. The selected boundary entry equals the initial embedding kernel, and the boundary with that entry deleted pulls back to the lower initial boundary because the truncation retains all remaining entries and the lower initial isomorphism composes with the divisor inclusion. The original strict normal crossings and smoothness give the remaining conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center_boun: The center lifting result gives the condition for the boundary with the selected entry moved to the front, since that entry is the embedding kernel. Reindex the chart assignments back to their original positions to obtain the condition for the original boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center_ker_: Move the selected boundary entry to the front. The ambient boundary remains in strict normal crossings position, and the invariant identifies that entry with the embedding kernel. The remaining entries pull back to the lower boundary, and the structural map restricts to the lower structural map. The lower center has strict normal crossings by its marking. The lifting result gives strict normal crossings for its image, which is the ambient center, with the reordered boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_imageIdealS: Identify the source with the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of the given immersion. Its structural map and lower boundary agree under this isomorphism with the ambient structural map and boundary restricted to the kernel subscheme, by functoriality. The lower center condition is preserved by this identification. Apply the given normal crossings lifting property to that kernel divisor and the shortened ambient boundary. The image of the transported lower center under the kernel inclusion equals its image under the original immersion, giving the desired ambient condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comp: Taking the image ideal twice corresponds to taking the kernel of the composite of the two maps with the original subscheme inclusion. This is the image ideal along the composite, by functoriality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_hom_eq_comap_inv: Direct image of an ideal along an isomorphism transports it by that isomorphism. This is the same ideal obtained by pulling it back along the inverse, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientBlowupSeq_schemeAt: The induction along the ambient blowup sequence establishes Noetherianity for every stage at most its length. The given bound is within this range because the ambient length equals the lower length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_le_center: The ambient center is the image of the lower center under the stage embedding. Its ideal is the kernel of the lower center inclusion followed by that embedding. Any section in the kernel of the embedding also vanishes on this composite, so the embedding kernel is contained in the ambient center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_zero_eq_boundar: The initial embedding is the lower initial isomorphism followed by the selected divisor inclusion. Precomposing by an isomorphism preserves the kernel. The divisor inclusion has kernel equal to its defining boundary ideal, giving the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length_imp_isNoetherian_ambientBlowup: Induct on the stage. At zero the ambient stage is isomorphic to the Noetherian original scheme. At a successor within range, the preceding stage is Noetherian by induction. The ambient and lower lengths agree, so the transition is a blowup. The next stage is Noetherian because blowups preserve Noetherianity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_map_comap_id_eq_self: The identity pullback fixes each ideal. Mapping this pullback over the list fixes every entry and its position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_map_comap_map_comap_eq_map_comap_co: For each entry the two consecutive pullbacks equal pullback along the composite. Applying that equality throughout the list proves the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.logDerivIdealSheafIterate_congr: The equal structural maps define the same logarithmic derivative operation with the given distinguished ideal. Substituting the equality gives identical iterates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_eq: Replace the first morphism by the equal second morphism. Its smoothness is then the given property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_ambientBlowupSeq_zero: At stage zero the ambient projection is the identity initial isomorphism. Following it by the original structural map gives that map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_subset_orderAtLeastLocus: An ambient center point is the image of a point of the lower center. The marking puts the lower point in the lower order locus, and the transform comparison identifies the lower ideal with the restricted ambient ideal. The ambient and embedded lower schemes are smooth over the field, with compatible structural maps. The invariant bounds the ambient ordinary derivative of order m−1, where m is the mark by the corresponding logarithmic derivative sum, and derivative balance with the earlier divisibilities supplies the associated power bounds on its terms. The order comparison from the divisor to the ambient scheme therefore sends the lower point to the ambient order locus.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_of_eq_map_append: The first list after mapping has the original length. The specified index therefore lies in this first part of the concatenation, where the entry is the image of the original entry under the map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succ: Use the invariant to obtain the center's normal crossings with the ambient boundary and the restricted divisor. The ambient step is a blowup, so its composite structure map is smooth and its new boundary still has strict normal crossings. The kernel of the next restricted embedding is the strict transform of the preceding kernel. The chosen boundary index remains within the transformed original part of the list, so this kernel is again the chosen boundary entry. For the boundary comparison after deleting that entry, restrict the strict transform and exceptional ideal to the next lower open. The restriction formulas identify these with the updated lower boundary. Unit ideals remain unit under strict transform, so the agreement of nontrivial entries persists. For the derivative conditions, keep the earlier exceptional divisibilities and use the center power bound to add divisibility at this step. The logarithmic derivative estimate for a blowup then transports the preceding derivative bound to the next stage, using the new structural map and the new restricted kernel. These are all the conditions of the next invariant on the open.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientDerivIdeal_le_center_pow: The center has strict normal crossings. If l is below the mark m, the power comparison makes its order for the derivative term at least m−l, by the ambient center order result. If l equals m the order bound is zero and holds everywhere. The power containment criterion for a center with strict normal crossings then puts the derivative term inside the stated power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_of_commSq: Each iterated pullback is the pullback along its corresponding composite. Commutativity identifies the two composites and hence the two ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform: The invariant on the open gives ambient exceptional divisibility at each preceding step by taking derivative order zero. Use these divisibilities in the stagewise comparison along the full embedding. The ambient controlled transform restricts to the lower marked ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_embeddingIntoA: At zero the square of the two initial projections and the original divisor embedding commutes. Pullback around it identifies the restricted ambient ideal with the initial lower marked ideal. For a successor, the ambient center restricts to the lower center because it is its image. The ambient divisibility gives the controlled-transform product formula, and the lower marking gives the corresponding formula below. Use the commuting square and the preceding ideal equality from induction to compare the two formulas. Cancel the common lower exceptional power, which is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. This identifies the next ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_restrictedEmbe: The restricted embedding is the lower open inclusion followed by the full embedding. Pullback along it first restricts the ambient ideal along the full embedding, giving the lower ideal by the previous result. Pulling back along the open inclusion then gives the stated restricted ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_of_pow_mul_comap_eq: The exceptional ideal in the ambient sequence pulls back to the lower exceptional ideal by commutativity and the center restriction formula. Pull the ambient product formula back to the lower scheme. Its right side is the same as the lower product formula by commutativity and the preceding ideal equality. Consequently the two candidate successor ideals agree after multiplication by the same exceptional power. Cancel this power using its local nonzero divisor generators.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_eq_comap_ambientDerivIdea: For derivative order l below the mark m, derivative balance and prior exceptional divisibilities give the power inequality comparing the current derivative and controlled ideals. The order-locus inclusion places the center in the derivative ideal's order-at-least-m−l locus. The center has strict normal crossings, so the derivative ideal lies in this power of the center. Pullback along the blowup makes the center an invertible exceptional ideal and hence gives the claimed factorization. At l equal to m there is no exceptional factor to divide out, so use the whole pullback as the witness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_eq_comap_controlledTransf: At an earlier step the derivative divisibility clause holds in particular for derivative order zero. This term is the ambient controlled transform itself, and its exceptional exponent is the original mark. Thus the supplied witness gives the desired product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_append: Filtering a concatenation retains precisely the accepted entries of the first list followed by the accepted entries of the second. Apply this with acceptance of nonunit ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_congr: If the common head is unit it is removed from both lists. If it is nonunit it is retained as the same first entry on both sides. In either case equality of the filtered tails gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_of_eq_top: The first entry is unit, so filtering out unit ideals removes it. The remaining filtered entries come from the tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_of_ne_top: The first ideal is nonunit, so the filter retains it at the front. The remaining entries are exactly the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_map_append_congr: Distribute the filter across the appended entry. This entry contributes the same filtered list to both sides. For the mapped parts, filtering before mapping makes no difference to the final filter because the map preserves unit ideals. The given equality of the original filtered parts therefore gives equality of the mapped and filtered parts.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_map_filterNeTop: Induct on the input list. A unit head is removed before mapping and also after mapping because the map preserves the unit ideal. A nonunit head appears in both mapped lists and is treated the same by their final filter. The induction hypothesis gives equality for the remaining tails.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.goingUpInvariantOnOpen_zero: The ambient initial ideal, boundary, and structural map are the starting ones. There are no preceding divisibility conditions. In the logarithmic derivative sum for order n, the term with index n has logarithmic order zero and is the ordinary derivative of the starting ideal of order n. This gives the initial derivative bound. The selected index and the embedding-kernel equality are given, as is agreement of nontrivial boundaries on the chosen open. The initial smoothness and strict normal crossings provide the other clauses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center: The preceding result works with the kernel divisor at the front, which is the selected boundary entry moved there. Transport the coordinate assignments back to the original list order. The center maintains strict normal crossings with the original boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center_cons: Move the selected boundary entry to the front. The invariant identifies it with the restricted embedding kernel, and the reordered ambient list retains strict normal crossings. The restricted lower center has strict normal crossings with the restricted lower boundary. By the invariant, the remaining ambient boundary pulls back to a list with the same nontrivial entries, so the condition also holds for that list. Identify the restricted lower scheme with the subscheme defined by the embedding kernel. This transports the lower structural map, center, and boundary to that divisor. The lifting property gives strict normal crossings for its image center on the ambient scheme. This image is the ambient center because the chosen open contains the lower center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_iso_hom_comp_eq: Transport of the ideal through the isomorphism is pullback by its inverse. Taking its image under the remaining morphism gives the same image as taking the original ideal's image under the composite, by functoriality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp: The closed immersion is its kernel subscheme inclusion after precomposing with the isomorphism from its source to that subscheme. The new composites differ by this same source isomorphism, which leaves the kernel unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_restrictedEmbedding_le_center: The ambient center is the image of the restricted lower center under the restricted embedding. Its ideal is therefore the kernel of the lower center inclusion followed by that embedding. A section in the kernel of the embedding also vanishes on the composite, giving inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_subset_orderAtLeastLocus: The ambient center is the image of the lower center restricted to the chosen open, since that open contains its support. Take a point of this restricted center mapping to the given ambient center point. It has the required order for the restricted lower ideal, which is the pullback of the ambient controlled ideal by the invariant. Both structural maps are smooth. The invariant's logarithmic derivative bound at order m−1, where m is the mark, and the derivative power inequalities from balance and previous divisibilities give the hypotheses of the order-locus comparison for this closed immersion. It puts the image point in the required ambient order locus.

The index is smaller than the original list length and mapping preserves that length. It therefore lies in the mapped part of the concatenation. Evaluation there gives the image of the original entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_succ: The adjacent ambient embedding theorem identifies the next kernel with the strict transform of the preceding kernel for every genuine step. Apply it to the closed immersion of the chosen divisor and the blowup data from the lower sequence, whose length is the lower length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_ambientBlowupSeq_succ: The structural map is projection to the ambient base followed by the original map to the field. At the next stage the projection is the current transition followed by the preceding projection. Associativity gives the asserted structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succ: The ambient step is a blowup. The preceding invariant and the normal crossings lifting result give strict normal crossings for the center with the transformed boundary, including its presentation with the embedding kernel distinguished. Thus the next stage is smooth and its updated boundary still has strict normal crossings. The new embedding kernel is the strict transform of the old one. Since the exceptional ideal is appended, the selected index still addresses that transformed kernel. After deleting that entry, the strict-transform and exceptional restriction formulas, together with the previous boundary comparison, give the updated lower boundary. The ambient center restricts to the lower center because it is its image under the closed immersion. Retain the existing derivative divisibilities and use the preceding center power bounds and exceptional transform products for the new divisibilities. The logarithmic estimate for a blowup propagates the derivative inequality, with the new structural map and the strict transform of the distinguished embedding kernel. This gives the successor invariant.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_pullback_subschemeι_comap: The first projection from the fiber product has kernel equal to the pulled-back ideal. This is the defining ideal of the new closed subscheme. The kernel containment required for factorization through its inclusion therefore holds by equality, giving the stated lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_subschemeMapOfComap: The square commutes by construction, so the new closed subscheme maps to the categorical fiber product. Conversely, the first projection of the fiber product factors through that closed subscheme, giving a reverse map. One composite is the identity by cancellation of the new closed immersion. The other is the identity because its composites with both fiber-product projections agree with those of the identity. For the second projection this follows from commutativity and cancellation of the original closed immersion. Thus the given square identifies with the pullback square.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_le_ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_eq_bo: At zero the embedding kernel is the pullback of the original kernel along the initial ambient isomorphism. The chosen boundary entry is the original kernel, so its initial pullback is equal to that kernel at zero. At a successor, the new embedding kernel is the strict transform of the preceding kernel. The chosen boundary entry is still within the preceding list because the boundary length only grows. Its new value is the strict transform of its preceding value, since the new exceptional ideal is appended. Induction identifies the two ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_ker_embeddingIntoAmbient: The embedding kernel at the given stage is the transformed entry corresponding to the chosen original boundary divisor. The marked ambient sequence has that transformed boundary list, and its length is the lower sequence length, so the stage is within range. A marked sequence from an admissible input preserves strict normal crossings of its boundary. Each entry of that boundary therefore defines a smooth divisor for its stage structure map, including the embedding kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_e: The stagewise induction identifies the kernel with the transformed original boundary entry at every stage through the length. Evaluate it at the given stage and index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_z: At zero the embedding is the lower initial isomorphism followed by the original closed immersion. Precomposition with an isomorphism preserves the kernel ideal, so its kernel is the original kernel. The ambient initial isomorphism is the identity, hence pulling that kernel back along it fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_zero_eq_comap_b: The unprepended ambient embedding at zero has kernel equal to the boundary ideal pulled back along the unprepended initial isomorphism. The prepended sequence starts with the identity isomorphism and its first transition is precisely the unprepended initial isomorphism. Thus the two successive pullbacks in the assertion equal the original single pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_zero_eq_comap_i: Use the general zero-stage kernel formula with the original closed immersion equal to the selected divisor inclusion. Its kernel is the selected boundary ideal. The ambient marked conversion retains the original initial isomorphism, giving the asserted pullback.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_le_biSup_logDeriv: The center and boundary conditions make the next scheme smooth over the field and the exceptional ideal invertible. The center power condition for the zeroth term gives a center power bound for each successive ordinary derivative. Form their controlled transforms with marks decreasing by derivative order. The zeroth transform equals the given zeroth successor ideal by cancellation of its exceptional power. For each derivative order up to n, pull back the hypothesized logarithmic bound and distribute pullback through its finite sum. The logarithmic blowup estimate for the term indexed by j gives the successor logarithmic term times an exceptional power. This power has exponent m minus the derivative order, independent of j. Cancel that common power to bound the ordinary derivative's controlled transform by the sum of successor logarithmic terms. The estimate for derivatives of the zeroth controlled transform bounds them by logarithmic derivatives of these transformed ordinary derivatives. Applying the new bounds, distributing the iterated logarithmic derivative through each finite sum, and adding the derivative orders yields the asserted bounded sum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_mul_le_mul_left: On an affine open the product of ideal sheaves evaluates to the product of the evaluated ideals. The original inclusion gives containment of the corresponding second ideals, and multiplication by a fixed first ideal preserves it. This proves the sheaf inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_iSup_le_iSup_ideal: The ideal sheaf with the pointwise supremum on affine opens is an upper bound for the original sheaves because every component ideal lies in that supremum. The sheaf supremum is therefore contained in that upper bound. Evaluating on the chosen open gives the inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.logDerivIdealSheafIterate_biSup_le: Apply the iterated logarithmic derivative bound to the outer supremum over natural indices. Apply it again to the inner supremum over the indices allowed by the bound. Each resulting term occurs in the asserted bounded supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.logDerivIdealSheafIterate_iSup_le: For zero iterations both sides are the original supremum. For one more iteration, apply one logarithmic derivative to the preceding inclusion, using monotonicity. The single-step supremum bound then puts the result inside the supremum of the logarithmic derivatives of the preceding iterates, which are exactly the next iterates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.logDerivIdealSheaf_iSup_le: Evaluate on an affine open and bound the evaluated sheaf supremum by the supremum of evaluations. The logarithmic derivative operation preserves inclusion, so the logarithmic derivative of that supremum bounds the result. The affine logarithmic derivative estimate puts it inside the supremum of the logarithmic derivatives of the component ideals. Each of these is contained in the affine evaluation of the claimed sheaf supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pointwiseSup_ideal: The pointwise construction assigns to each affine open the supremum of the given ideals on that open. This is the asserted evaluation.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_support_strictTransform_contain: At any point of the selected center support, choose the adapted chart in which the center and the selected boundary are the same coordinate ideal. Saturating that ideal by itself gives the unit ideal. Thus the strict transform is unit near the point and the point does not lie in its support. This proves disjointness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eraseIdx_map_eq: Induct on the list, with the empty case immediate. For deletion at index zero, every entry of the tail is fixed, so the mapped tail equals the tail. At a successor index the head is fixed, and the condition on the remaining indices gives the induction hypothesis for deletion from the tail. Reattach the fixed head.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_low: The deletion and truncation formula identifies the retained list with the original boundary minus the chosen entry. Restricting the remaining entries of a strict normal crossings boundary to the chosen smooth divisor preserves strict normal crossings. This is the stated list and structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_containedComponentsIdeal: The selected component ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, and its closed subscheme is smooth over the field. These are the two defining properties of the smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_self_of_getElem: Induct on the list. The empty list is fixed. For a nonempty list the hypothesis fixes its head at index zero and fixes every entry of its tail using the corresponding successor index. By induction the mapped tail is the original tail, so the whole list is fixed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closeds_compl: The open complement of a closed subset has precisely the points outside that closed subset, by definition of complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_mul: Restriction is pullback along the open inclusion, and pullback of ideal sheaves preserves products.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_id: Strict transform restricts to an open by restricting the morphism and the ideals to that open. The restricted identity is again the identity. Its strict transform is the saturation by the restricted center because identity pullbacks fix the restricted ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturation_top_eq_top: The total pullback of an ideal is contained in its strict transform. For the identity and the unit ideal, the pullback is unit and the strict transform is its saturation. Thus the saturation contains the unit ideal and is itself unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_comap_boundary_of_ne: Check equality locally. Away from the selected center support, the strict transform for the identity is the original ideal. At a point of that support, choose an adapted étale chart. The selected center is a single coordinate ideal. The distinct boundary entry is either unit or cut out by a different coordinate. Saturation by the selected coordinate fixes a unit ideal and fixes the ideal of a distinct coordinate. These local equalities prove the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_mul_containedComponentsI: Check the product locally. On a chart at a point of the selected center, the selected center and boundary entry are the same coordinate ideal. Its strict transform for the identity is the saturation by itself, hence unit. Multiplication by the center gives the boundary ideal there. Off the center support, the center is unit and the strict transform agrees with the original boundary ideal. This proves the product identity on a cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.take_eraseIdx_lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup: The updated list consists of the strict transforms of the original entries and an appended exceptional ideal. Deleting the selected index removes one of the transformed entries. All other transformed original entries equal their original ideals. They occupy exactly the first original length minus one places, so taking that prefix removes the appended exceptional ideal and gives the original boundary with the selected entry deleted.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_ker_ι_comp_s: The selected subset of the boundary is open by hypothesis. In this branch of the definition, the chosen ideal is the kernel of its open inclusion followed by the boundary inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_top_of_not_i: The openness test for the selected union of connected components fails by hypothesis, so the selected ideal is unit by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionSeq_eq_of_containedCompo: The nonempty order locus and unit selected center put the construction in the ordinary divisor restriction branch. The dimension inequality and Noetherianity allow the lower sequence and its ambient lift, since its centers contain no component. The given marking then identifies the output of the lift with the marked form of this ambient tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionSeq_eq_of_isBlowupAlongI: The nonempty order locus and nonunit selected center put the construction in the preliminary blowup branch. Its lower ideal and boundary are the residual and updated data for that blowup. The lower dimension bound, Noetherianity, and proper centers give the ambient tower for the twisted restriction. Prepend the selected blowup. The given marking identifies the lift with the marked form of this prepended tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryWithoutBlowup_eq: The initial boundary before any preliminary blowup is obtained by pulling each entry back along the identity. Each entry stays equal to itself, in the same list order.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_setOf_connectedComponent_subset: If the connected component of a point is not contained in P, the same is true for every point of that component. The component is open and is an open neighborhood in the complement of the indicated set. The complement is therefore open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryWithoutBlowup_baseChange_sa: Without a preliminary blowup the lower boundary is the original list. The field extension pulls back this list entry by entry. The deletion formula for lists with matching nontrivial parts and matching prefixes applies at the specified index, giving the asserted comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageSupportEqComponentsInOrderLocus_: The selected locus is a union of connected components of the Noetherian boundary divisor, and its complement is also a union of open components. Hence the selected locus is closed. Its image in the ambient scheme is closed because the divisor inclusion is a closed immersion. The support of the kernel of the composite inclusion is the closure of that image, so is the image itself. Taking its inverse image under the injective divisor inclusion recovers exactly the selected locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_take_eraseIdx_com: Removing the selected entry from each list leaves exactly its old length minus one entries, so both truncations keep their entire shortened lists. Entrywise pullback commutes with deleting an index. The lists had the same nontrivial entries and equal prefixes through the deleted entry, so deleting that entry preserves agreement of their nontrivial parts.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_ofSequenceOfBlowups_transitionMap: Induct on the source index of the transition. A transition between equal indices is the identity in both sequences. For a transition from a larger successor index, factor it through the preceding index. Conversion to data and back preserves the adjacent transition, and the remaining transition is preserved by induction. The composites agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_ofMarkedSequenc: The unmarked data of either marked sequence are the data obtained from its original underlying sequence. Converting each back recovers that original sequence. Thus the given pullback relation applies unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_restrictToBound: The selected new divisor is the pullback of the original one, so their inclusion square is a pullback. Its induced map is smooth and respects the structural maps to the field. The two routes around that square give equal pullbacks of the lower ideal. The hypothesis on shortened boundaries also gives the same nontrivial boundary after restriction to the divisor. Consequently the newly restricted marked input is the smooth pullback of the original restricted input with this boundary replacement. Both are admissible and below the dimension bound, so the assumed lower-dimensional compatibility gives the pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_apply_congr: Identify the two equal marked inputs first. The domain schemes agree, so the given equality of comparison maps is an ordinary equality. Substitute it into the pullback relation to obtain the desired one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_of_length_eq: The only relevant stage of either sequence is zero. The projection from the original stage zero to its base is an isomorphism, so its fiber product with the new base is canonically isomorphic to the new base. The new sequence's stage zero is also identified with that base by its initial isomorphism. Compose these identifications to obtain the pullback comparison. All conditions involving a genuine blowup step or an omitted center are vacuous because both lengths are zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_ideal_congr: Substitute the equality of the two ideals. All other data already agree, so the marked inputs coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_toSequenceOfBlowups: The tower comparison gives equality of the reconstructed tower with the original. The conversion also preserves the original length, initial isomorphism, and center ideals. These data determine the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_tower: The converted tower has the same object at every index. Every arrow of the opposite natural-number category corresponds to an inequality of indices and its image is the transition for that inequality. These transitions are preserved under conversion, so the two functors agree on arrows and objects.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_transitionMap: Apply the transition comparison proved by induction to these two stage indices and their given order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackOfEmptySequence_of_isPullbackSeq: The supplied empty-cosupport comparison gives the first requirement. The comparison for two sequences of length zero gives the second, and preservation of comparison under conversion of marked sequence data gives the third. Together they give the stated empty-sequence comparison property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackSmoothOfDimLT_of_isMaxOrderReduc: Maximum-order reduction correctness below dimension n includes compatibility with smooth pullback for admissible inputs in that dimension range. Apply that clause to the two given inputs and the prescribed boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedSmoothPullback_of_isMaxOrderRe: The lower-dimensional maximum-order reduction hypothesis supplies smooth pullback compatibility below the bound. Use this in the three-case restricted comparison to obtain the required property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedSmoothPullback_of_pullbackSmoo: In each case the selected new boundary divisor is the pullback of the selected original one. The nonempty order loci supply strict dimension drops on both sides, and the appropriate ordinary or twisted admissibility theorem applies. When both selected centers are unit, the ordinary lower ideals and boundaries match under smooth pullback. When the original center is nonunit but becomes unit, the empty-center formulas identify the pullback of the twisted data with the ordinary data on the new side. When both centers are nonunit, the twisted data match by the lower ideal and boundary comparisons for smooth pullback. The pullback theorem for restricted divisors applies to the corresponding data in each case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sequenceOfBlowups_eq_of_tower_eq: Identify the lengths and the towers by their equalities. This aligns the types of the centers and the initial isomorphisms. Their given equalities then identify both remaining data fields. The blowup conditions are propositions, so the resulting sequences are equal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_prepend_ambientBlowupSeq_one: The initial boundary is unchanged by the identity identification. At the prepended step, take the strict transforms for the preparatory blowup and append its exceptional ideal. This is the lower ambient boundary by definition. The ambient initial isomorphism pulls the resulting list to stage one of the prepended sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comp_comp: Pull back first along the last two morphisms and then along the first. Applying the composition rule once more to the pullback along the last two morphisms gives the three successive pullbacks in reverse order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_prepend_ambien: Use the closed open supplied for the lower sequence and its going-up invariant through stage t. The stage-one transform of the prepended sequence is the lower ambient ideal pulled back by the ambient initial isomorphism. Compatibility of the transform recursions identifies the stage-(t+1) prepended transform with the stage-t ambient transform of that lower ideal. The comparison in the going-up invariant pulls this ambient transform back to the divisor ideal at stage t.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_self_of_eq_id: Replace the endomorphism by the identity using the given equality. Pullback along the identity fixes the ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_restrictedEmbedding_zero: Factor the stage-zero restricted embedding as the open inclusion, the initial divisor isomorphism, and the divisor embedding. The composition rule for ideal sheaves gives the pullbacks along those three maps in reverse order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_prepend_ambientBlowu: At stage zero of the prepended sequence the identification is the identity, so the starting transform is the original ideal. The first blowup map is the initial projection of the ambient sequence and the center is the contained-components ideal. The residual for the identity blowup is the lower ambient ideal by definition. Transporting this residual through the ambient initial isomorphism gives the stage-one controlled transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_eq_comap_of_eq_: The exceptional ideal is the pullback of the center ideal along the first endomorphism, so it equals the center ideal because that endomorphism is the identity. The two pullbacks of the starting ideal are also along identities and leave it unchanged. After these identifications, the asserted equation is the given factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosed_opens_goingUpInvariantOn: Take the inverse image at stage zero of the part of the divisor outside the support of the contained-components ideal. It is closed by openness of the inverse image of the center support on the divisor. It contains the support of the initial lower ideal by the order bound and the factorization of the original ideal. The same factorization and the assumed derivative balance give derivative balance for the lower ambient ideal. For the going-up induction, the lower boundary has strict normal crossings by the blowup boundary theorem, its entry j is the kernel of the restricted embedding, and its remaining entries agree with the divisor boundary after pullback and deletion of unit ideals. Admissibility supplies the positive marking. With these initial conditions, the invariant holds through every stage of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_append_top: Filtering a concatenation filters each part and concatenates the results. The newly appended list consists of the unit ideal alone, so its filtered list is empty and the result is the filtered original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_comap_restrictedEmbedding_er: Let L be the list of strict transforms of the original boundary with entry j erased. The erased lower boundary is L followed by the exceptional entry, and L has length n−1 for an original boundary of length n. Taking those first n−1 entries and pulling them to the divisor therefore gives precisely the initial twisted divisor boundary. Transport by the initial isomorphism and restrict to the specified open. By composition of pullbacks, the resulting list is the pullback of L along the restricted embedding. The appended exceptional ideal is the center ideal, and its pullback to the open is the unit ideal because the open lies off its support. Deleting all unit entries therefore gives the same list on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.goingUpInvariantOnOpen_of_le: Use induction on the stage. The initial normal crossing condition, the selected kernel ideal, and the filtered equality of boundaries give the invariant at stage zero. If the next stage is within the sequence, the current stage lies strictly before its end. The successor theorem then advances the invariant using derivative balance, the positive marking, lower admissibility, the crossing lift, and the closed open containing the initial support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_lowerBoun: Transporting the starting boundary by the identity leaves it unchanged, so it is still in strict normal crossing position and the center still has strict normal crossings with it. Apply the boundary transformation theorem to the identity blowup. The strict transforms together with the appended exceptional divisor are in strict normal crossing position for the composite structure map, which here is the original structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_complOpens_of_isOpen: The inverse image of the center support on the divisor is open by assumption. Its pullback by the continuous initial isomorphism is open at stage zero. The specified open is its complement, hence is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDerivBalanced_lowerIdealAfterBlowup: The factorization identifies the original ideal with the marked power of the contained-components ideal times the lower ideal. Apply the derivative-balance descent result for such a factorization, using the upper bound by the marking on the original order and the derivative balance of the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_prepend_ambientBlowupSeq:
Choose the closed open and the going-up invariant for the lower ambient sequence. At the prepended center, the given factorization supplies divisibility by the marked exceptional power, the given support inclusion places the center in the marked order locus, and the assumed smoothness and normal crossing condition give the two geometric requirements. There the initial projection and initial ideal and boundary transports are identities.

At a later step n+1 of the prepended sequence, the center and blowup are those of ambient step n, and the controlled transform and boundary agree with the ambient lower transforms at stage n by the stage-one formulas and their recursions. Divisibility follows from the invariant at stage n+1. Containment in the order locus and normal crossings with the current boundary follow from the invariant at stage n on the chosen open. Smoothness is the ambient center smoothness theorem. The prepended sequence has one more step than the divisor sequence, so these verifications cover every center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_opensι_comp_subschemeι_congr: Substitute the equal center and divisor ideals into the two composites. The divisor inclusion and the inverse image of the complement of the center then agree term for term, so their kernel ideal sheaves agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_opensι_preimage_iso_comp: The isomorphism restricts to an isomorphism from the inverse image of the open to the open itself. The square of open inclusions commutes, so the first map to the target is the second map preceded by this restricted isomorphism. Precomposing by an isomorphism preserves the kernel ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_map_comap_id: Pullback along the identity fixes each ideal sheaf. The empty list is fixed, and if the tail is fixed, the head is also fixed by the identity pullback. Induction therefore gives equality of the ordered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_eq_map_comap_id: The lower boundary is the boundary after the preparatory step. Its rule first transports the starting list through the initial identity, takes the strict transform of each entry for the identity blowup, and appends the exceptional ideal at the end.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_eq_map_strictTr: In the definition of the lower boundary, the first list operation pulls each original entry back along the identity. That operation fixes the whole list, leaving the strict transforms of the original entries followed by the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_getElem_eq_ker_: The index j lies in the transformed original boundary, ahead of the appended exceptional entry, so the selected ideal is the strict transform of the selected divisor. For the identity blowup, the strict transform is the kernel ideal of the map from the part of that divisor lying off the center into the ambient scheme. At stage zero the restricted embedding is this same map after the isomorphism from the corresponding open of the divisor stage. That isomorphism preserves the kernel ideal, giving the required equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealAfterBlowup_eq_residualByPow: In the formula for the lower ideal, both pullbacks of the starting ideal are along identities. The exceptional ideal is the identity pullback of the contained-components ideal. Replacing these three pullbacks by their original ideals gives the residual with respect to the contained-components ideal itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealAfterBlowup_eq_residualByPow_e: Expand the definition of the lower ideal at the preparatory identity blowup. It is the residual of the pulled back starting ideal by the marked power of the exceptional ideal, with one identity pullback from the initial identification and a second from the blowup morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup: Taking strict transforms preserves the length of the starting list, as does the initial identity pullback. The exceptional divisor adds one entry, so an index smaller than the starting length is smaller than the new length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_map_strictTransform_boundary: Applying the strict transform to every boundary entry preserves the list length. The original index bound is therefore also the index bound for the transformed list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_comp_comp: Both expressions preserve order and send each entry to its three successive pullbacks. For the empty list both sides are empty. For a list with a head and a tail, the new heads are equal by construction and the new tails agree by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_complOpens_iff: The open at stage zero is obtained by pulling the complement of the center support back first to the divisor and then through the initial isomorphism. A point belongs to this inverse image exactly when its image in the ambient scheme lies outside the center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_mul_lowerIdealAfterBlowup_eq_ideal: Write Z for the contained-components ideal and m for the marking. The lower ideal is the residual of the original ideal by Zᵐ. The assumed factorization supplies at least one factor whose product with Zᵐ is the original ideal. The defining factorization property of the residual then gives the same equation with the lower ideal as factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictTwistedToDivisor_boundary: To form the twisted boundary on the divisor, erase entry j from the lower ambient boundary, take its first n−1 remaining entries where n is the original boundary length, and pull those entries back to the divisor. This is the stated list by the definition of the restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedEmbedding_zero_eq: The restricted embedding factors through the inclusion of the specified open in the initial divisor stage. At that stage the full embedding into the ambient sequence is the initial identification with the divisor followed by the divisor embedding. Substituting gives the required three maps in order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_ambientBlowupSeq_eq_pr: By definition, the stage-t structure map of the ambient sequence first projects to the starting ambient scheme and then applies the original structure map to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ideal_zero_subset_complOpens: Take a point in the support of the stage-zero ideal. Under the initial isomorphism and the divisor embedding, it maps to a point in the support of the lower ambient ideal, because that ideal pulls back to the stage-zero ideal. The original ideal is the product of the marked power of the center ideal with the lower ideal. The order bound and the support-disjointness result for this factorization put the image point outside the center support. Thus the stage-zero point belongs to the specified complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_orderAtLeastLocus_comap_o: The endomorphism is the identity, so the pulled back ideal is the original ideal and their order loci coincide. The claimed inclusion is therefore the given inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_sameNontr: The selected center pulls back to the unit ideal. In this case restricting a strict transform along the identity gives the same pullback as restricting the original entry. Deleting the selected position and taking the shortened original length discards the appended exceptional ideal and retains only transforms of the remaining entries. After pullback those entries agree with the corresponding original entries. Thus the indicated lists agree, in particular in their nontrivial parts.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_lowerIdealAfterBlowup_eq_comap_low: Factor the original ideal as the marked power of the selected center times its residual. Pull the product back to Y. The selected center pulls back to the unit ideal, whose marked power is unit, so the pulled-back residual equals the pulled-back original ideal. The residual is the lower ideal after the preliminary blowup, and the original ideal is the lower ideal before it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_fieldBaseChange: A field extension gives a flat projection. The two admissible schemes are Noetherian and the original boundary pulls back entry by entry under this projection. With the specified selected-center equality, matching nontrivial entries and matching prefixes, the flat comparison of strict transforms and deleted boundary entries gives the stated result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerBoundaryAfterBlowup_sameNontrivialB: The smooth map is flat, and the two admissible schemes are Noetherian. The pulled-back original boundary is the entrywise pullback, and the selected centers agree under pullback. Apply the flat strict-transform list comparison to the two updated boundaries, with the given matching prefixes and nontrivial entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealAfterBlowup_fieldBaseChange: The original order bound gives divisibility by the marked power of the selected center. The new selected center is locally generated by a nonzero divisor because it is exceptional for its identity blowup. It equals the pullback of the original center by assumption. Apply the residual pullback formula along the field-extension projection. The residuals for these identity blowups are precisely the corresponding lower ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealAfterBlowup_pullbackAlong_of_s: The original order bound supplies the factorization by the selected center to the marked power. The pulled-back selected ideal has an identity blowup, so it is locally generated by a nonzero divisor as the exceptional ideal of that blowup. The pullback comparison for the residual applies to the given equality of selected ideals. Since the preliminary blowup maps are identities, their exceptional ideals are the selected centers, and the residual comparison is the asserted lower ideal equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_id: Pullback along the identity fixes each ideal sheaf. Applying it entry by entry fixes the whole list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.residualByPow_comap_of_isLocallyGenerate: Multiply the original residual by the given power to recover A, using the assumed divisibility. Pull that equality back. The pullback of the original residual now multiplies by the new divisor power to give the pulled-back A, so it witnesses the new divisibility. By the residual product formula, the new residual also satisfies this equality. Cancel the common power, which is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, to identify the residuals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_eraseIdx_strictTr: Discard the identity pullbacks, then delete the selected original entry and take the prefix of the shortened original length. This removes the appended exceptional ideal and retains the strict transforms of all other entries. Flat base change of strict transforms identifies the transforms pulled back from the original list with the transforms of its pulled-back entries. Strict transform preserves the unit ideal, so applying it to lists with the same nontrivial parts preserves their agreement. The equal prefixes through the selected index remain equal after transforming, so deletion of that entry preserves the agreement as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.take_eraseIdx_append_singleton: The deleted index lies in the original list, so deletion leaves the appended entry at the end of the shortened original list. The shortened list has length one less than the original length, which is the number of entries taken. Thus the prefix is exactly the shortened original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.take_length_sub_one_eraseIdx: Deleting an in-range entry reduces the list length by one. Taking that many entries of the shortened list retains the entire list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_pow: The unit ideal is the multiplicative identity for ideal multiplication. Any natural power of it is unit.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundaryReindexingInvariance: The identity of a scheme is smooth and surjective. Equal chosen divisor entries give the same lower ideal, and matching remaining nontrivial boundaries give matching lower boundaries after the update. Together these are the conditions for boundary reindexing invariance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filter_map_eq_of_filter_eq: Filtering after mapping gives the same result whether or not the original list was filtered first. Indeed, by induction on the list, any entry rejected at the first stage also gets rejected after the map, and every retained entry is treated identically in either order. Thus equal original filtered lists give equal filtered mapped lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealAfterBlowup_withBoundary_eq_of: Equal selected divisor ideals give equal selected center ideals. The input ideal and marking are fixed by boundary replacement. The residual-by-power construction for the lower ideal uses only these data, so the two lower ideals coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_lowerBoundaryAfte: The chosen divisor ideals agree, so the two constructions use the same selected center. Apply the list comparison for strict transform along the identity with this center to the two boundaries after removing their respective selected entries. The given agreement of the nontrivial shortened lists supplies its hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_map: The nontrivial boundary is obtained by discarding unit entries. Since the map sends unit to unit, discarding such entries before mapping gives the same filtered result as discarding after mapping. Apply the filter comparison to the two equal initial nontrivial lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_take_eraseIdx_str: On either list, removing the selected index after mapping removes the corresponding original entry. The first original length minus one places then consist exactly of the mapped remaining entries, before the appended exceptional ideal. The mapping is identity pullback followed by strict transform, which sends the unit ideal to itself. Agreement of the original shortened nontrivial lists therefore persists after this mapping.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_mem_orderAtLeastLocus_of_mem_comap: Pull the given power containment for each K term back to the smooth closed subscheme. At the point in question the restricted A has order at least m, so the power inequality gives the restricted K term indexed by l order at least m−l. The derivative support formula puts the point in the support of the derivative ideal of this term of order m−l−1. The comparison of logarithmic derivatives with derivatives after restriction then puts the image point in the support of the corresponding ambient logarithmic term. This holds for every index, hence the image belongs to the support of their sum. The assumed containment in that sum puts it in the support of the ambient derivative ideal of A of order m−1, which is the desired order locus.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_controlledTransform_in: The first-step formula identifies the first transform of the prepended sequence with the initial residual ideal. Thus its final controlled transform agrees with the final transform of the unprepended ambient sequence starting from that residual ideal. The restriction theorem identifies the latter transform on the embedded divisor with the final twisted lower ideal. Its order locus is empty, so the ambient order locus misses the support of the final embedding kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_ker_support_eq_e: The kernel support of a closed immersion is its image. If a point belonged to both this support and the order locus, choose its preimage in the closed subscheme. Pulling an ideal back can only increase its order at this point. The preimage would therefore lie in the order locus of the restricted ideal, which is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_support_ker_eq_e: The untwisted lower initial ideal equals the original ideal. At the last stage the controlled-transform restriction theorem identifies the restriction of the ambient transform along the stage embedding with the final lower ideal, using the given divisibilities. That lower ideal has empty order locus. Apply the disjointness result for a closed immersion to this last embedding.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_withBoundary_baseChang: The base field has characteristic zero by admissibility, and the extension field does too since the field homomorphism is injective. The original structural map is smooth. Changing the boundary leaves the pulled-back ideal fixed, so the order-locus theorem for field extensions identifies this locus with the inverse image of the original one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_isoObjZero_hom: The ambient lift starts with the original ambient scheme and its initial isomorphism is the identity isomorphism. Its forward morphism is therefore the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_isoObjZero_inv: The initial isomorphism of the ambient lift is the identity isomorphism of the starting ambient scheme. Its inverse is again the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_projectionToBase_comp_i: The inverse of the ambient initial isomorphism is the identity on the starting ambient scheme. Postcomposing the stage projection with it leaves the projection unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSeq_projectionToBase_zero_c: At stage zero the projection to the starting scheme is the forward map of the initial isomorphism, which is the identity. Its composite with the original structure map is the structure map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_get_eq_strictTransform: The first part of the successor boundary consists of the strict transforms of the preceding entries in the same order, and it has their length. Since j lies in this first part, its entry is the strict transform of preceding entry j.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_zero_get_eq_comap: The stage-zero boundary is obtained by pulling back every original entry through the initial isomorphism. Pullback of an ordered list preserves the index, so entry j is the pullback of original entry j.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_pow_mul_lowerId: Admissibility supplies some factor whose product with the marked power of the contained-components ideal is the original ideal. The prepended blowup uses the identity, so the exceptional ideal is the contained-components ideal and the two identity pullbacks of the original ideal leave it unchanged. The factorization property of the residual therefore gives the desired product with the lower ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_support_center_iteratedComap_co: Every ambient center point comes from a center point of the divisor sequence. The marked center condition and positivity of the marking place that divisor point in the support of its current ideal. Projecting to the initial divisor and then embedding in the original ambient scheme puts its image in the support of the lower ambient ideal. On the other hand, membership in the support of the transported contained-components ideal would put the same image in the original contained-components support. Here the two projections agree by the assumed comparison square, and the initial ambient identification is the identity. The lower and contained-components supports are disjoint, giving a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_support_lowerIdealAfterBlowup_c: If a point lies in both supports, each factor has order at least one there. The original ideal is the product of the marked power of the contained-components ideal and the lower ideal. Additivity of order for products and the power rule imply that the original order is at least m+1, where m is the marking. This contradicts the upper bound m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_ker_embeddingIntoAmbient:
At stage zero, the embedding kernel is the original boundary entry. It is the product of its preparatory strict transform and the contained-components ideal, whose supports are disjoint. The contained-components ideal is a smooth divisor. Along the ambient sequence, both the embedding kernel and the preparatory strict transform evolve by strict transform. The latter stays a smooth divisor because at every stage it is the selected boundary entry of the admissible prepended sequence.

The centers avoid the iterated pullback of the contained-components support by the comparison with the divisor sequence and the disjointness of the two starting supports. The ambient stages are locally Noetherian and their maps to the ground field are smooth by admissibility of the prepended sequence. Apply the theorem on transporting the product of disjoint divisor factors with centers avoiding the pulled back factor. It makes the kernel a smooth divisor at every stage, for the structure map that agrees with the prepended projection one stage later.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_prependedAmbientSeq_boun: The stated bound on i is the length bound of the prepended marked sequence. Admissibility is preserved by the marked transform through that stage, using that an effective Cartier divisor contains no component of the ambient scheme. Each boundary entry of the transformed admissible object is a smooth divisor for its structure map. Its boundary and structure map are exactly those of the prepended sequence at stage i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_zero: The comparison at stage zero identifies the kernel with the pullback of boundary entry j first by the new initial identification and then by the first blowup morphism. Both are identities, so both pullbacks leave the ideal unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_le_length_boundary: At stage zero the boundary is the original list pulled back by the initial isomorphism and therefore has the original length.
