At every subsequent step, taking strict transforms preserves length and appending the exceptional divisor adds one. Induction gives the bound at every stage through the end of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_natCast_add_one_le_self: A natural number is finite in the extended natural numbers. For a finite n, the inequality n+1 ≤ n would give n < n, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_blowupMorphism: Passing from the prepended blowup data to a marked sequence retains the underlying blowup morphism at every index. Thus the successor transition is the corresponding morphism from the prepended data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_blowupMorphism_succ: The marked sequence keeps the underlying blowup morphisms. After the prepended step, the morphism at index n+1 in those data is the morphism at index n of the ambient sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_blowupMorphism_zero: The first transition of the marked sequence is the first blowup morphism of the prepended data. This morphism is the forward map of the ambient initial isomorphism, which is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_boundary_succ_get: An original boundary index remains in range at every stage because boundary length never decreases. At stage one, the first transition is the identity and its center is the contained-components ideal. Thus entry j is the strict transform of the initial entry for this preparatory blowup. At later stages, taking the next boundary entry applies the strict transform along the next blowup to the preceding entry. The prepended morphisms and centers have shifted by one, so induction identifies this update with the recursion for the ambient iterated strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_center: The marked sequence constructed from the prepended data retains its center ideals. Its center at the given index therefore equals the center at that index in the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_center_succ: After the first center has been inserted, the center of the data at index n+1 is the old ambient center at index n. Forming the marked sequence leaves those centers unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_center_zero: The marked sequence preserves its underlying centers. By construction the first center of the prepended data is the contained-components ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_isoObjZero_hom: The prepending construction takes its new starting identification to be the identity isomorphism. Passing to a marked sequence retains it, and its forward map is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_length: Packaging the ambient sequence as a marked sequence preserves its length. The ambient lift has the same number of steps as the divisor sequence, and the prepended blowup adds one step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedAmbientSeq_projectionToSpec_suc: The marked sequence's structure map is its stage projection followed by the original structure map. For a successor stage of the prepended data, that projection equals the projection at the preceding index in the ambient lift. Substitute this equality before composing with the structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_mem_support_of_mem_supp: At stage zero the ideal is pulled back via the initial isomorphism, which is also the stage projection. For the induction step, write the pullback of the previous ideal as the exceptional ideal to the marked power times the current ideal. At a point of the current support, the current order is at least one. The order inequality for products gives order at least one for the pulled back previous ideal, so the point maps to the previous support. The induction hypothesis then puts its image in the original divisor ideal's support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIter_succ: At each successor stage the iteration applies the strict transform for that stage's blowup and center to the preceding ideal. Evaluating this recursive rule gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_iteratedComap: Write pₜ for the projection from stage t followed by the inverse of the initial isomorphism. At stage zero p₀ is the identity and the transported ideal is the starting ideal. At a successor stage the transported ideal is pulled back from the previous one. Its support is therefore the inverse image of the previous support. By induction that support is the inverse image of the original support under pₜ, and composing with the transition map gives pₜ₊₁.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ambientMarkedSeq_eq_imageIdealShe: The center of the ambient lift is the scheme-theoretic image of the divisor center under the stage embedding. The marked sequence retains this center, giving the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_prependedAmbientSeq_succ_eq_image: After the initial step, center t+1 of the prepended sequence is center t of the ambient lift. That center is the scheme-theoretic image of the lower center under the stage-t embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_prependedAmbientSeq_zero: By construction the first center of the prepended blowup data is the contained-components ideal. Adding the marked data preserves that center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_boundary_isoObjZero_prependedAmbie: The initial isomorphism is the identity, so its forward morphism pulls the selected boundary ideal back to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf_eq_self_of_isClose: A closed immersion identifies the source with the closed subscheme cut out by its kernel. Taking the scheme-theoretic image of a further closed subscheme and pulling it back to the source recovers its defining ideal, as given by the image and pullback formula for closed immersions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionShape_ambientBlowupSeq: Use the stage embedding kernels as the family of divisor ideals. The ambient sequence has the lower length, the kernels are smooth divisors, and the initial one is the pullback of boundary entry j. The center images lie in these divisors and successive kernels are strict transforms. Lower termination gives final disjointness, and the lower certificates transfer to the divisor subschemes at each step. Together these are the hypotheses of the construction with strict transforms at every step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionShape_of_orderAtLeastLoc: Use the original divisor transported to stage zero and choose the strict-transform option. At length zero only the initial stage is in range, where smoothness is given. All conditions involving an actual blowup step hold vacuously. The stage-zero ideal comes from the original ideal by an isomorphism, so its marked order locus remains empty and is disjoint from the stage-zero divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionShape_of_pullback_then_s: Define the family by using D₀ at stage zero and the supplied divisor with index t at stage t+1. Choose the option with a preparatory pullback. Smoothness and center containment follow from the stage-zero hypotheses at zero and the shifted hypotheses at positive stages. The sequence has length one more than the lower sequence, so it has a first step, where the openness and pullback conditions are given. Strict transforms and certificates apply at each later step using the shifted index. At the last stage the ambient ideal and divisor are those in the final disjointness hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionShape_of_strictTransform: Use the given family of divisors and choose the option with no preparatory pullback. The smoothness, initial equality, center containment, strict-transform rule, and certificates are the supplied hypotheses after identifying the sequence length. The terminal ideal is the ideal at that length, so the final disjointness hypothesis gives the terminal condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorReductionShape_prependedAmbientBl: Use the transported starting boundary entry at stage zero and the embedding kernels at subsequent stages. The starting entry and the kernels are smooth divisors. The first center lies in the starting divisor, and the inverse image of its support is open there. The first divisor update is pullback. Each successor center lies in the corresponding kernel divisor and the later updates are strict transforms. Lower termination gives final disjointness, and the lower certificates yield certificates at the subsequent steps. With the shifted length, these data give the claimed family with a preparatory pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorTransform_succ_eq_strictTransform: The marked sequence inherits its blowup maps and centers from the ambient blowup data. With those identifications, the desired formula is the strict-transform recursion for the stage embedding kernels.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorTransform_zero_eq_comap_isoObjZer: The divisor ideal is the kernel of the embedding. The assumed stage-zero kernel formula for the unit-center construction identifies it with the initial pullback of boundary entry j.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_nonzeroOnComponents_certificate_a: At the given stage the divisor embedding is a closed immersion and its kernel defines the ambient divisor. The projection comparison identifies the structure maps, the divisor boundary locus lies in the inverse image of the other ambient boundary locus, and the ambient ideal restricts to the lower ideal. The ambient center is the scheme-theoretic image of the lower center. The lower stage ideal is nonzero on components by admissibility of the lower marked sequence. Apply the certificate transfer along the closed immersion to the supplied lower certificate. It produces the ideal on the kernel subscheme, its local agreement with the restricted ambient ideal, and the certificate for the restricted center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_nonzeroOnComponents_certificate_p: Compare lower stage t with prepended stage t+1 by the closed immersion. The structure map factors along this immersion, the lower boundary locus lies in the inverse image of the other ambient boundary locus, and the ambient ideal restricts to the lower ideal. The ambient center is the image of the lower one. The lower ideal is nonzero on components by admissibility, and it has the given lower certificate. The certificate transfer to the kernel subscheme yields the desired ideal with local agreement, nonvanishing, and the certificate for the restricted ambient center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_principalizationCertificate_ker_o:
The closed immersion identifies X with the subscheme cut out by its kernel. Transport I to that subscheme by the isomorphism and call the resulting ideal J. This preserves nonvanishing on components. Commutativity with the inclusion into Y identifies J with the restriction of the ambient ideal on the whole subscheme, which gives the required local agreement.

Transport the given certificate by the same isomorphism. The structure maps agree by the assumed factorization through Y. The restricted ambient center pulls back from the original center because the ambient center is its scheme-theoretic image under the closed immersion. The transported memory set lies in the inverse image of the ambient memory set by the given inclusion. Enlarge it to that inverse image using monotonicity of the certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_smoothDivisorSeq_divisorFamily_ca:
The canonical rule gives the divisor reduction sequence. If the marked order locus is empty, that sequence has length zero. The transported initial boundary entry is a smooth divisor and the empty-sequence argument supplies the required family.

Otherwise the construction gives either an ambient lift of the ordinary divisor restriction, when the contained-components ideal is the unit ideal, or a preparatory blowup followed by the ambient lift of the twisted restriction. In each case the relevant lower object is admissible and has dimension strictly below the ambient bound. The lower-dimensional assignment therefore supplies certificates at all its steps and an empty marked order locus at its last stage. Apply the strict-transform construction in the first case and the preparatory-pullback construction in the second. The description of the canonical sequence identifies the resulting family with the one asserted.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_center_zero_prep: Replace the first center by the contained-components ideal and the transported boundary entry by the original selected divisor. The asserted inverse image is then open by the supplied openness property on that divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_ambientMarkedSeq: The divisors are defined by the kernels of the stage embeddings. Apply the assumed smoothness property of those kernels for the admissible ambient and lower objects in the unit-center case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_prependedAmbientSeq: At prepended stage t+1 the divisor is the kernel of the stage-t lower embedding. The supplied smoothness property for the nonunit-center construction says that this kernel defines a smooth divisor over the structure map of that prepended stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoObjZero_prependedAmbientSeq_eq_refl: Inserting the preparatory blowup makes the new starting object the original ambient scheme with its identity isomorphism. The marked sequence retains that starting identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbient_succ_eq_strictT: Apply the kernel recursion for the ambient lift of a closed subscheme, taking the subscheme to be the selected divisor. Passing to the underlying blowup data preserves the sequence length, so the given bound allows the strict-transform recursion at this stage.

The morphism and center at step t+1 of the prepended data are the morphism and center at step t of the ambient lift. Substitute these identifications and apply the strict-transform recursion for the stage embedding kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_ambientMarkedSeq: The ambient lift has the same number of steps as the divisor sequence. Adding the marked data leaves the underlying sequence and its length unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_prependedAmbientSeq: The ambient lift of the lower sequence has the lower sequence's length. Inserting the preparatory blowup adds one, and forming the marked sequence preserves the resulting length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_eq_empty: Under an isomorphism the order locus of the pulled back ideal is the inverse image of the original order locus. An inverse image of the empty set is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_divisorTransform: The final divisor is the kernel of the final embedding. The assumed termination comparison for a unit contained-components ideal states that the ambient marked order locus is disjoint from this kernel support when the final lower order locus is empty. Apply it with the given lower termination.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_prependedDivisor: The final ambient stage is one step later than the final lower stage. Apply the assumed termination comparison for the prepended construction to the empty final lower order locus. It makes the final ambient marked order locus disjoint from the support of the corresponding embedding kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedDivisorTransform_succ_eq_strict: The successor divisor ideals are the consecutive kernels of the lower-stage embeddings. The marked sequence keeps the morphisms and centers of the prepended blowup data, so the shifted kernel recursion gives the asserted strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependedDivisorTransform_zero_eq_comap_: The first divisor after the prepended step is the kernel of the initial lower embedding. The corresponding initial kernel formula identifies it with the starting boundary ideal after pullback by the initial ambient identification and then by the first blowup morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_ambientBlowupSeq_subset: The ambient center is the image of the lower center under the stage closed immersion. Its support is therefore contained in the support of the embedding kernel, by the assumed support property for closed-immersion images. This kernel is the specified divisor ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_succ_prependedAmbientBlow: The successor center is the image of the lower center under the stage closed immersion. The support of that image is contained in the support of the immersion kernel, which is exactly the chosen divisor at the corresponding prepended stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_zero_prependedAmbientBlow: At stage zero the prepended center is the contained-components ideal and the starting boundary transport is the identity. Its support lies in the selected divisor's support by the given property of the contained-components ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_congr: Substitute the equality of the two morphisms. Both sides are then the pullback of the same ideal along the same morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_smooth_surjective_to_restrictToBo: The selected divisor after field extension and the base-changed original divisor both realize the same pullback square over the field spectra. The unique isomorphism between these pullbacks respects their projections to the original divisor and to the extension field. Use its forward map as the required smooth surjective comparison. Transport the shortened replacement boundary to the base-changed divisor by pulling it back along the inverse isomorphism. The given agreement of nontrivial boundaries, restricted to the divisor and transported through the isomorphism, identifies this list with the base-changed original boundary up to unit entries. Pulling it back again recovers the shortened replacement list. The given pullback identity for the lower ideal and the commutative squares identify the transported ideal with the base-changed ideal. Admissibility is preserved by this isomorphism, and the two underlying divisors have equal successor dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_subschemeMapOfComap_comp_stru: The square of the selected divisor inclusions is a pullback because the new divisor ideal is the pullback of the original one. The square defining the field extension is also a pullback. Paste the two squares to obtain the stated pullback over the field spectra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_congr: Replace the two equal morphisms by their common value. Each entry is then pulled back by the same morphism on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_map_comap_eq_map_comap_comp: For each boundary entry, successive pullback is pullback along the composite by functoriality. Applying that equality entry by entry gives the two lists in the same order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_of_eq_right: Substitute the equality of the two right-hand lists in the given nontrivial-boundary comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_isIso: An isomorphism of schemes is an open immersion onto the entire target, hence is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_of_isIso: Each target point is the image of its preimage under the inverse isomorphism. This gives surjectivity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_comap_iteratedPreimage_succ: Use the boundary update for the marked lower sequence. The next open is the inverse image of the preceding open under the transition. Restriction to this inverse image commutes with each strict transform and sends the exceptional ideal to the exceptional ideal for the restricted morphism and center. Applying these identities to the list and its last entry gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ambientBlowupSeq_eq_imageIdealShe: The full lower center support lies in the chosen clopen open. Restricting its ideal to that open and pushing it back to the full lower stage recovers the center ideal. The ambient center is the image of this full lower ideal under the stage embedding. Compose the two image operations to obtain the image of the restricted center along the restricted embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_iteratedPre: The marking gives strict normal crossings of the stage center with the stage boundary. Restrict through the open immersion. The normal crossings charts restrict to this open, and their relevant ideals and structural map are exactly the pulled-back center, boundary, and structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comp_of_eq: Image ideals compose with the morphisms. Taking the image of J along the first map gives Z by hypothesis, so taking the image along the composite gives the image of Z along the second map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_restrictedEmbedding: The inverse-image open is closed by induction from the clopen initial open, so its inclusion is a closed immersion. The full embedding into the ambient stage is also a closed immersion. The restricted embedding is their composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_iteratedPreimage: At stage zero the assertion is the hypothesis. At each successor the chosen subset is the inverse image of the preceding one under a continuous point map. The inverse image of a closed subset is closed, so induction applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedPreimage_succ: At a successor stage the chosen open is defined as the inverse image of the preceding open under the adjacent blowup morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedPreimage_zero: At stage zero the recursively chosen open is the original open U₀.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_restrictedEmbedding_succ: At a genuine step the next ambient scheme is Noetherian, and the full new embedding kernel is the strict transform of the full preceding embedding kernel. The successive embedding squares commute and the preceding selected open is clopen. The strict-transform formula for a clopen part of a closed subscheme therefore identifies the kernel of its inverse image at the next stage with the strict transform of the preceding restricted kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedBlowupMorphism_comp_ι: The restricted transition is the unique map from the inverse-image open to the given open that restricts the original transition. Composing it with the target open inclusion equals the original transition preceded by the source open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedEmbedding_comp_blowupMorphism: Expand the restricted embeddings as open inclusions followed by the full embeddings. The full embedding square commutes with the ambient and lower transitions. The square for restricting the lower transition to the inverse-image open also commutes. Pasting these identities gives the asserted equality of composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedEmbedding_comp_structureMorphi: The full embedding followed by the ambient projection to the base equals the lower projection followed by the original divisor inclusion. Composing with the field structure map gives the lower projection to the field. Precomposing by the chosen open inclusion gives the same equality for the restricted embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictedEmbedding_eq_ι_comp_embeddingI: The restricted embedding is defined as the inclusion of the iterated inverse-image open followed by the full stage embedding into the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_iteratedPreimage_ι_comp_projectio: The stage projection to the field is smooth for an admissible marked sequence. The chosen open includes by a smooth open immersion. Their composite is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_comap_subset_orderAtLeast: A point in the support of the restricted center maps to the support of the whole center, since support pulls back by inverse image. There the stage ideal has order at least the multiplicity by the marking. Pullback along an open immersion identifies the local rings and stalk ideals, so it preserves this order at the chosen point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_center_subset_iteratedPreimage: Every center point has stage ideal order at least the positive mark, so in particular has order at least one and belongs to the stage ideal support. That entire support lies in the chosen iterated inverse-image open, giving the containment for the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ideal_subset_iteratedPreimage: The initial support containment is assumed. At a successor stage the support of the controlled ideal lies in the inverse image of the preceding ideal support. Induction places that preceding support inside the chosen preceding open. Taking inverse images therefore puts the next support inside the next chosen open.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.prepend_toSequenceOfB: Substitute one equal center ideal for the other. The prepended schemes, transitions, and center ideals are then the same. The two witnesses of the blowup property establish the same proposition, so both constructions give the same sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.ofMarkedSequen: The blowup data underlying each marked conversion are obtained by converting its underlying sequence to data. The strict comparison is preserved when both sequences are converted to data and back, giving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_: The smooth map is flat and both admissible schemes are Noetherian. If the original order locus is empty, its inverse image is empty. The divisor sequences both have length zero and are strict pullbacks. Otherwise surjectivity makes both order loci nonempty. The selected center on the pullback is the pullback of the original selected center, so surjectivity makes the two centers unit simultaneously. In the unit case, the ordinary lower sequences are strict pullbacks along the map of divisors. The corresponding divisor square is a pullback, so flat compatibility gives the strict comparison for their ambient lifts. In the nonunit case use the twisted lower sequences and apply the same ambient comparison. Prepend the original and pulled-back selected blowups to this strict comparison. The ambient descriptions of the canonical sequences give the result in both cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_ofSequenceOfBl: Converting to data and back preserves each length, stage, initial isomorphism, adjacent transition, and center. The given comparison maps are therefore defined on the same range of indices and have the same initial compatibility, pullback squares, and center relations. They witness the strict comparison for the converted sequences.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.SameNontrivialBo: The two boundary lists have equal ordered lists after removing unit ideals. The filtered pullback depends only on those filtered lists, because an original unit ideal pulls back to a unit ideal. Equal filtered lists therefore have equal filtered pullbacks.

Interpret the boundary equivalence as equality of the lists after removing unit ideals. The common prefix through j lets us delete that index from both lists while preserving this filtered equality. Interpreting the resulting filtered equality gives the claimed boundary equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ne_top_of_surjective: The assumed pullback compatibility for surjections applies to the given ideal, which differs from the unit ideal. It gives that the pulled back ideal also differs from the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_subschemeMapOfComap: Pull back the ambient ideal along the commuting square of closed subschemes. The two paths from the pulled back subscheme to the original ambient scheme are equal, so pulling back in two stages along these paths gives the same ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.componentsInOrderLocusIdeal_congr: Substitute the equality of the divisor ideals. With the ambient ideal and marking fixed, the selected component construction is then applied to the same divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.cons_take_succ_inj: The first j+1 entries of a nonempty list consist of its head followed by the first j entries of its tail. Equality of the two prefixes therefore gives equality of both heads and both shortened tails.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_eq_componentsIn: Consider the union of components of the selected divisor contained in the marked order locus. When this union is open on the divisor, both ideals are the kernel of its inclusion into the ambient scheme. Otherwise both are the unit ideal by their defining convention.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_withBoundary: The original pulled back boundary and its replacement agree in the prefix through j. Thus their selected divisor ideals are equal. Replacing the list leaves the ambient ideal and marking unchanged, and the contained-components construction depends only on these data and the selected divisor. The two center ideals are therefore equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_subscheme_hom_comp_subschemeι_eq: The map from the pulled back subscheme to the original ambient scheme has kernel containing D. The universal property of the closed subscheme defined by D therefore gives a factorization through its inclusion. Pulling any ambient ideal back along the two equal composites gives equal ideals, and the composition rule expresses them as the asserted two successive pullbacks.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_comap_get_boundary: The boundary of the pulled back marked object is obtained by pulling back every original boundary entry and keeps the original length. The given equality of prefixes through j identifies its entry j with entry j of the replacement boundary. The former is the pullback of the original entry at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_get_of_take_add_one_eq: The bounds make both lists nonempty. At index zero, equality of the one-entry prefixes gives equality of the heads. At successor index j+1, equality of the prefixes gives equality of the first j+1 entries of the tails. The index j is valid in both tails, so induction gives equality of those entries, which are the desired entries of the original lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_eq_get_of_take_succ_eq: Apply the prefix comparison at index j. The equal prefixes include entry j, and the two bounds ensure that this entry exists in each list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.heq_toSequenceOfBlowups_of_eq: Substitute the equality of the two marked objects. Both assigned sequences now come from the same object with the same ambient type, so their underlying sequences are equal by reflexivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_id_comap_contain: By the given center equality, the pulled back contained-components ideal is the contained-components ideal for the admissible replaced object. The supplied preparatory blowup property says that the identity is a blowup along that center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_divisorPullbackMap: The divisor map is the induced map from the closed subscheme defined by the pulled back ideal. The assumed pullback compatibility for induced maps of these closed subschemes gives the stated square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_restrictToDivi:
The common prefix identifies the chosen divisor on the new ambient scheme with the pullback of the original divisor. Its induced map is smooth and surjective by the pullback square, and the square also shows that it respects the structure maps to the ground field. With unit contained-components ideals on both sides, use the lower ideal without a preparatory step. Its pullback formula and the commuting square identify the two lower ideals. After deletion of the selected boundary entry, the lower boundaries agree up to unit entries, and this equivalence survives restriction to the pulled back divisor.

Thus the pulled back lower object with the replacement boundary is precisely the lower object constructed on the new ambient scheme. Both lower objects are admissible by the unit-center case and have dimension below the induction bound by the dimension-drop result. The strict smooth pullback property of the lower-dimensional assignment applies. Substituting the identified marked object gives the claimed strict pullback of sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_restrictTwiste:
The chosen divisor is pulled back from the original one because the boundary prefixes agree through its index. The induced divisor map is smooth and surjective by base change and respects the structure maps. The new contained-components ideal is the pullback of the original one and differs from the unit ideal by surjectivity. The assumed compatibility for the preparatory transform identifies the two lower ideals after pulling back and restricting along the commuting square. The corresponding compatibility for the truncated boundaries, followed by pullback to the divisor, gives equivalence after removing unit entries.

It follows that the pulled back twisted lower object, equipped with the new lower boundary, equals the twisted lower object on the new ambient scheme. The nonunit-center admissibility result and dimension drop put both objects within the lower-dimensional assignment. Applying its strict smooth pullback property and substituting the equality of lower objects proves the claimed comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_of_heq: The two sequences over the same ambient scheme have the same type, so the given heterogeneous equality yields an ordinary equality. Substituting it transfers the strict pullback property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_le_ker_comp: The kernel of the original closed immersion is D. The kernel of the composite from the pulled back subscheme is the image ideal under h of the pullback of D. The adjunction for pullback and image of ideals gives inclusion of D in this image ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerIdealWithoutBlowup_withBoundary: Without a preparatory blowup the lower ideal is the starting ideal, since its identity pullback fixes it. The replacement boundary leaves that ideal unchanged, and the starting ideal of the pulled back object is the pullback of the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_comap_subschemeι: The square of subscheme inclusions gives the same two-step pullback for each ideal. Applying this entrywise preserves order, so the two resulting lists agree. Equivalently, compare the heads using the pullback equality and the tails by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_cons_congr: Filtering the common head either prepends that head to each filtered tail or leaves each filtered tail as it stands. Since the filtered tails are equal, the resulting lists agree in either case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_eq_of_cons_eq: If the common head is kept, cancel it from the two equal filtered lists. If it is removed, the equality is already the equality of the filtered tails.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_eraseIdx_eq_of_take_succ_: Use induction on the erased position. Equal prefixes of positive length force both lists to be empty or both to have the same head. In the empty case the two erased lists agree. In the nonempty case the filtered tails agree by cancellation of the common head. If the erased index is zero, this gives the result. At a successor index, the prefixes of the tails agree through the smaller index. Apply induction to the tails and then restore the common head before filtering.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_map_comap: Proceed down the list. A unit ideal can be dropped before pullback because it pulls back to the unit ideal and would be dropped afterwards. For an entry other than the unit ideal, both procedures pull back the same entry and keep it exactly when its pullback is different from the unit ideal. The tails agree by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_withBoundary_pullbackA: Changing the boundary leaves the ideal of the pulled back marked object unchanged. The assumed smooth pullback rule for order loci therefore identifies the locus at any given threshold with the inverse image of the original locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_comap_subschemeι: Pull back the given boundary equivalence to the pulled back divisor. Equivalence is preserved by pullback. On the side obtained from the original ambient boundary, the commuting square lets each entry be pulled back first to the original divisor and then along the induced divisor map. This gives the stated lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_lowerBoundaryWith: Both lower boundaries before restriction are their respective starting boundaries. The selected index is valid on each side, so the prefixes of length one less than the corresponding original lengths retain the full erased lists. The equivalence of the pulled back and replacement boundaries persists after deletion of j because their prefixes through j agree. Deleting an index commutes with entrywise pullback, which identifies the first erased list with the pullback of the erased original boundary. This proves the required equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeMapOfComap_comp: The induced map is chosen from the factorization of the composite through the original closed subscheme. The equality is the commutativity of that factorization square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_snd_of_isPullback_of_surjecti: In the given pullback square, the morphism to S is the base change of the surjection from Y to X. Surjectivity of scheme morphisms is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.take_length_sub_one_eraseIdx: Deleting a valid index reduces the list length by one. Taking exactly that many entries of the shortened list returns the full shortened list.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartAssignment_comp_of_injective: Assign each new position the coordinate assignment of its corresponding original position. If two new positions get the same coordinate, distinctness of the original assignment makes their old indices equal, and injectivity makes the new indices equal. Each new boundary entry is the corresponding old one, so the unit and coordinate-ideal descriptions transfer to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_eq_getElem_moveToFront: If the old index is j, its entry becomes the new head. If it is below j, deletion leaves its position in the tail unchanged and insertion of the head shifts it one place. If it is above j, deletion reduces its position by one and insertion increases it by one. Thus the entries agree at the corresponding indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_moveToFront: For index zero, the new head is the original entry at j. For a positive index i+1, take the entry at i in the list with index j removed. Before j it is the old entry at i, and otherwise it is the old entry at i+1. These are the stated index map cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_of_moveToFr: At a point of the center choose the chart adapted to the center and the moved boundary. Keep the chart and its center coordinate set. Reindex the boundary assignment by the injective map from original to moved positions, which selects equal boundary entries. The assignment comparison preserves the required boundary descriptions and coordinate distinctness. The chart then works for the original boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_moveToFro: Every entry after the move is an original smooth divisor. At each point use the original adapted chart and reindex its coordinate assignment by the injective map from new positions to old positions. The assignment comparison preserves the unit or coordinate descriptions and the distinctness of those coordinates. This gives strict normal crossings for the moved list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexBeforeMoveToFront_injective: The new index zero maps to j. Positive indices of the form i+1 map to i for i below j and to i+1 otherwise. The two positive-index branches have disjoint ranges, strictly below and strictly above j, and each is injective. This makes the whole index map injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexBeforeMoveToFront_lt_length: For index zero use the bound on j. For a positive index i+1, the original index is either i or i+1. Both are below the original length by the given index bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexBeforeMoveToFront_succ: At new index i+1, the entry comes from the shortened list at i. Before the deleted position this is old index i. At or after the deleted position it is old index i+1.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexBeforeMoveToFront_zero: The new index zero represents the entry moved from its original position j, by definition of the index map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexInMoveToFront_injective: The selected index alone goes to zero. Lower indices are increased by one and have images from one through j. Higher indices keep their values, which are greater than j. Each branch is injective and their ranges are disjoint.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexInMoveToFront_lt_length: The move preserves length. The selected index goes to zero within this nonempty list. An index below the selected one increases to at most j, which is still within range. An index above j keeps its valid value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.indexInMoveToFront_self: The selected index is the equality case of the forward index map, so it goes to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_moveToFront: Deleting the selected in-range entry decreases length by one. Inserting that entry as the head restores the original length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_mem_moveToFront: An entry in the moved list is either the selected head, which was in the original list, or an entry of the list after deletion. Every entry surviving deletion also belonged to the original.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.moveToFront_eq_cons: The index is in range. The move takes the entry at that index as its head and removes it from the original list to form the tail.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_exceptionalIdeal_of_commSq: Write both exceptional ideals as pullbacks of center ideals. The two iterated pullbacks are pullbacks of the same center along the two routes in the commuting square, so they agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransform_of_closedImmersion: Identify the two closed subschemes with the ambient kernel subscheme and its strict transform. These identifications commute with the map from the strict transform to the original kernel subscheme. The coordinate normal crossings restriction theorem identifies the restriction of the ambient transform of D to that strict transform with the transform of the restricted D along the induced blowup. Pull this equality back along the later source isomorphism. Strict transform is compatible with this isomorphism, and commutativity identifies the resulting pulled-back center and ideal with those along the given lower map. This gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransform_of_iso: By functoriality, the strict transform along the composite can be computed along the isomorphism using the center and ideal already pulled back by the original map. The total inverse image of the ideal's subscheme is transported by this isomorphism, and the opens away from the two center supports correspond. Restrict the transported map and its inverse to these opens. The resulting immersions into the isomorphic ambient schemes factor through each other after identifying their targets, so their kernel ideals agree by inclusion in both directions. These kernels give the strict transforms, and transport of a kernel along the isomorphism is its pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_of_ker_eq_strictTra: The two closed immersions identify their sources with the closed subschemes defined by their kernels. The later kernel is the strict transform of the former by hypothesis, so this gives the claimed source isomorphisms. To compare the resulting maps between the kernel subschemes, compose both with the original kernel subscheme inclusion. The defining property of the strict-transform lift and the given commuting square make the composites agree. The inclusion is a monomorphism, hence the maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_le_ker_of_comp_eq: A section vanishing after pullback along the second morphism vanishes after the additional pullback along the first. The composite is the given map, so the second kernel is contained in the composite kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_strictTransform_append_excepti: For each original boundary entry the strict-transform restriction theorem identifies the pullback of the ambient transform with the lower transform of the restricted entry. These equalities hold in the list's original order. The appended exceptional ideal restricts to the lower exceptional ideal by the commuting square. Combining the transformed list with this last entry gives equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.containedComponentsIdeal_pow_mul_lowerId: The initial ideal is divisible by the marked power of the selected center ideal. The residual-by-power formula therefore recovers the initial ideal on multiplying the residual ideal by that power. For the identity blowup the exceptional ideal is the center ideal and identity pullbacks fix all ideals, so this residual ideal is exactly the post-blowup lower ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_irreducibleComponents_boundary_: Admissibility implies that the selected boundary entry is a smooth divisor over the field. Distinct irreducible components of a scheme smooth over a field are disjoint. Apply this to the smooth divisor subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_restrictTwistedToDivisor: The restricted input uses the same characteristic-zero field and positive marking. Its underlying divisor is smooth over the field, locally of finite type, and quasi-compact. The residual ideal pulled back to the divisor is nonzero on components by the preceding order argument. The theorem on the updated boundary after the preliminary blowup gives strict normal crossings after restriction to the divisor. Together these give all admissibility conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDerivBalanced_of_isBalanced: For this marked input the balance condition is derivative balance of its ideal at the specified marking. The given finite-type structure makes this the asserted property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_mem_support_comap: The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. The given membership therefore says that the image point belongs to that original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_lowerIdealAfte: The original ideal factors as the selected center raised to the mark times the lower ideal, so its order is the mark times the center order plus the lower ideal order. Suppose an irreducible component of the divisor lay in the support of the restricted lower ideal. If the entire component maps into the original order locus, the connected component of any chosen point stays in it by disjointness of the smooth divisor's irreducible components. The point then maps into the selected center support. Both factors have positive order there, and the order formula gives original order greater than the mark, a contradiction. Otherwise choose a point of the divisor component mapping outside the order locus. Derivative balance forces the original order there to be zero, so the order formula forces the lower ideal order to be zero. This is again incompatible with belonging to the support of the restricted lower ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_mult: The assumed bound on the order of the marked ideal is pointwise. Evaluate it at the given point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.connectedComponent_subset_of_mem_irreduc: The irreducible component is open and closed by the disjointness and Noetherianity hypotheses. A connected subset containing the chosen point cannot meet both this clopen component and its complement. Apply this to the connected component of the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_restrictToDivisor: The selected divisor is smooth over the same characteristic-zero field, locally of finite type, and quasi-compact as a closed subscheme of the original scheme. Its marking remains positive. The result for the untwisted ideal gives nonvanishing on components. Removing the chosen boundary entry and pulling back the others to its divisor preserves strict normal crossings. The untwisted boundary is the original list and its truncation keeps all entries after removal, giving exactly this boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClopen_of_pairwise_disjoint_irreducibl: An irreducible component is closed. Every point outside the chosen component belongs to a different irreducible component, and pairwise disjointness makes every other component lie outside the chosen one. The complement is therefore the union of the other components. There are finitely many by Noetherianity, so their union is closed, proving that the chosen component is also open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_ι_comp_ne_top: The point in the open lifts to its open subscheme. The composite morphism is quasi-compact since its source is Noetherian. Its kernel support contains the image of the lifted point, so the support is nonempty and the kernel cannot be the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_boundary_subscheme: The admissible ambient scheme is Noetherian. A closed immersion identifies the boundary's underlying space with a closed subspace of it. This subspace is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_lowerIdealWith: The lower ideal before any blowup is the original ideal. Derivative balance and the positive mark identify its support with its marked order locus. If the restricted ideal's support contained a divisor component, that component would map into the order locus. The smooth divisor has pairwise disjoint irreducible components, so the connected component of a point on it stays within that irreducible component. The point thus belongs to the open union selected for the preliminary center. The inclusion of this nonempty open into the ambient scheme has nonunit kernel, contrary to the assumption that the selected center ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_comp_structureMorphism: The selected boundary entry is a smooth divisor since the boundary has strict normal crossings. The smooth-divisor condition includes smoothness of its closed subscheme over the base field along the indicated composite.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.IsAdmissible.top: Admissibility gives a locally finite-type and quasi-compact structural map to the base field. The finite-dimension result for schemes with those properties applies to the marked ideal's ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_preimage_val_eq: The two closed sets have equal intersections with the open. The intersection with the larger irreducible set is nonempty because the smaller set meets it. This intersection is dense in the larger set and is contained in the smaller closed set. Thus the larger set lies in the smaller one, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_le_natCast_of_lt_top: An element below top in this ordered set is either bottom or an embedded natural number. In the first case zero bounds it, and in the second the corresponding natural number bounds it by equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natCast_withBot_lt_top: The embedded natural number is below top and distinct from it, so it is strictly below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natCast_withBot_ne_top: A natural number is finite in the extended natural numbers. Adjoining a bottom element preserves the distinction between that finite number and the top element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_lt_top_of_finiteType: A finite-type algebra over the field is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables. A surjection does not increase Krull dimension, since it identifies prime ideals of the quotient with prime ideals containing the kernel. The polynomial ring has finite dimension by the preceding result, so the quotient does as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_mvPolynomial_lt_top: Induct on the number of variables. With no variables the polynomial ring is the coefficient field and has dimension zero. With one more variable it is a univariate polynomial ring over the preceding multivariate polynomial ring. The polynomial-ring dimension bound is twice the preceding dimension plus one. By induction the preceding dimension is below top, so this bound is still below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_closure_inter_of_isPreirreducible: Take a point of the preirreducible set and any open neighborhood of it. That neighborhood meets the set, and so does the given open by hypothesis. Preirreducibility gives a point of the set in both opens. Thus every such neighborhood meets the intersection with the given open, proving the closure assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_affineOpen_lt_top: Local finite type of the structural map gives a finite-type map from the sections on the field spectrum to the sections on the affine open. The former ring identifies with the field, so the affine open's coordinate ring is a finite-type algebra over that field. The affine open is homeomorphic to the spectrum of this coordinate ring, whose dimension is finite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_natCast_of_isOpen: Apply the open-cover chain bound with the embedded natural number as the common bound for the dimensions of the open sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_iUnion_eq_univ: Take any finite strict chain of irreducible closed subsets. A point of its smallest member lies in some covering open, and this same point lies in every member. Intersect the chain with that open. Each intersection is nonempty, irreducible and closed in the open. The inclusions remain strict because equality of consecutive intersections would, by density in the irreducible sets, identify the two original closed subsets. Thus there is a chain of the same length in that covering open, whose dimension is bounded by the given bound. Taking the supremum over all original chains gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_finiteType: The field spectrum is quasi-compact, and the inverse image of its whole space is quasi-compact by the given property of the structural map. Hence the affine opens admit a finite subcover of the scheme. Every member has finite dimension by local finite type and the affine-open result. The finite-cover dimension bound then gives finite dimension of the whole scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_finite_isO: Choose a natural upper bound for the dimension of each covering open. Their finite supremum is still a natural number and bounds every open's dimension. By the chain bound for open covers it bounds the dimension of the whole space. It lies strictly below top, as required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_homeomorph: A homeomorphism identifies the posets of irreducible closed sets and preserves the lengths of their strict chains. The two topological Krull dimensions are therefore equal, so finiteness transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_primeSpectrum_lt_top: Topological Krull dimension of a prime spectrum equals the ring's Krull dimension. Apply the finite-type algebra bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_spec_lt_top: The underlying space of the affine scheme is the prime spectrum of its coordinate ring. The dimension bound for spectra of finite-type algebras therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_mul_add_one_lt_top: Since the element is distinct from top, it is bottom or an embedded natural number. In the bottom case multiplying by the nonzero element two and adding one still gives bottom. In the finite case the result is the embedded natural number given by twice the number plus one. Both are strictly below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_mul_natCast_add_one: For embedded finite numbers, multiplication and addition agree with multiplication and addition of natural numbers before embedding. This gives the equality for twice the given number plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_ne_zero_withBotENat: Two and zero are distinct natural numbers. Both embeddings into the extended naturals and then into the order with a bottom element are injective, so their images remain distinct.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMapOfFieldHom_eq: The map of field spectra is defined by taking the spectrum morphism induced by the given field homomorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso: The simultaneous induction proves transport of the order certificate along any isomorphism under the stated descent assumption. Apply it to this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_of_eq: Use the order certificate transport theorem for the isomorphism, then identify its composite structural map with the new one by the given equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso: The simultaneous transport theorem applies to the given principalization certificate. Evaluate it at the specified scheme and isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso_of: Pull the certificate back along the isomorphism by the transport theorem. The equality of structure maps lets that certificate be viewed over the stated new structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_iso_hom: A point belongs to the support of the pulled-back ideal exactly when its image belongs to the original support. This identifies the support with the inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_preimageOpensIso_hom: Both iterated pullbacks are pullbacks along composites. The identity for the restricted isomorphism and its inclusions makes those composites equal, so the ideal sheaves agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_resLE_of_iso: Restricting the ambient isomorphism to the inverse image of an open is the base change of that isomorphism to the open. Base changes of isomorphisms are isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso: Induct simultaneously on order and principalization certificates with the assertion that each transports under every isomorphism. The memory and marking cases use the underlying pulled-back support and the same marking. The principalization factorization case transmits the factorization and the smaller order certificate. The localization cases transport through isomorphic opens. For a descent step, the assumed invariance applies using the transported principalization certificates supplied by induction. This proves transport for the order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_opens_cove: Every point of the new target support maps to one of the original support points. Use the inverse image of its specified open neighborhood. The local order certificate transports through the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. Its structure map, ideals and memory match those of the new open because the inclusions commute with the isomorphism. The localization constructor assembles the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_smoothDivi: The assumed invariance of the descent step applies to the given local smooth divisors, support conditions and auxiliary ideals. It takes the original descended principalization certificates together with their transported versions supplied by the hypothesis. Its conclusion is precisely the order certificate after the ambient isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_support_su: Under the isomorphism the support becomes the inverse image of the original support. It remains inside the inverse image of memory, so the order certificate follows from the memory case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_two_le: The marking stays at least two under pullback. The large-marking constructor therefore supplies the transported order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr: Use the four equalities to identify the parameters of the two certificates. The original order certificate has the required parameters after substitution.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom: The isomorphism of the inverse image open with the given open is constructed from the restricted ambient map, which is therefore its forward map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom_comp_ι: The isomorphism between the opens is the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. Composing it with the original open inclusion agrees with following the inverse image inclusion by the ambient map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom_comp_ι_comp: Postcompose the equality for the restricted isomorphism and open inclusions with the structural map. Associativity gives the stated identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_comp_base: A point lies in the successive inverse images exactly when its image under the composite lies in the set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_preimageOpensIso_hom: Each nested inverse image is the inverse image along the corresponding composite into the original scheme. Those composites agree by compatibility of the open isomorphism with inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_iso: Use simultaneous induction on principalization and order certificates, asking for transport along every isomorphism. Support containments, markings and products are preserved, which gives the memory, large-marking and factorization cases using the relevant induction hypotheses. Charts in the two localization cases transport by inverse image and the restricted isomorphism. The descent case follows from the assumed invariance for smooth divisors applied to the original principalization certificates on the hypersurfaces and their transported versions. These cases prove the required transport.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_iso_of: For a point of the new support, its image lies in the original support. Take the inverse image of the chosen original neighborhood. The local hypothesis transports its principalization certificate along the restricted isomorphism. The open inclusion compatibility identifies the transported structure map, ideals and memory with the desired local data. These local certificates give the new global certificate by localization.

The ideal factorization persists under pullback. The support of the first factor is the inverse image of its old support and remains in the pulled-back memory. Order loci are preserved under the isomorphism, so the pulled-back target support satisfies the order bound for the second factor. Together with the same marking inequality and the transported order certificate from the hypothesis, these give the transported principalization certificate.

The pulled-back target support is the inverse image of the original support. It lies in the inverse image of memory by the given containment, which yields a principalization certificate by the memory case.
The isomorphism transport retains the marking. Since that marking is at least two, use the large-marking principalization constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_congr: Substitute the equal structure map, input ideal, memory set and target ideal. The given certificate is then a certificate for the specified data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_irreducibleClosedsImageVal: The irreducible closed set in the larger space is constructed as the image of the given set under the inclusion of the closed subspace. Its underlying set is this image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_irreducibleClosedsMapOfHomeomorph: The transported irreducible closed set is defined by taking the image under the homeomorphism. Its underlying subset is that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_irreducibleComponents_superse: Extend the given irreducible set to a maximal preirreducible subset. It is nonempty because it contains the original set, hence irreducible. Its closure is preirreducible and contains it, so maximality makes it closed. The same maximality makes it an irreducible component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleClosedsImageVal_subset: Every point in the image of the closed subspace inclusion is a point of that subspace, so the image of the specified set is contained in the subspace.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_lt_of_homeomorph_isClosed: The closed subset has strictly smaller topological Krull dimension because it is nonempty and contains no ambient irreducible component. The given homeomorphism transfers its dimension to the scheme in the statement. Since the greater dimension is finite, passing to successor indices preserves the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_lt_of_topologicalKrullDim_l: The dimension index is given by the successor conversion of topological Krull dimension. The monotonicity result for that conversion preserves the strict inequality because the greater dimension is below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_irreducibleCloseds: The closure of the singleton of the given point is closed and irreducible, since singletons are irreducible and closure preserves irreducibility. It is nonempty because it contains the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_irreducibleClosedsImageVal: Taking images preserves inclusions. Since the subspace inclusion is injective, equality of images would imply equality of the original sets. Strict inclusions therefore remain strict.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_irreducibleClosedsMapOfHomeom: Images under the homeomorphism preserve inclusions, and injectivity makes equality of images imply equality of the original sets. Hence the image operation preserves strict inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_length: Topological Krull dimension is defined as the supremum of the lengths of finite strict chains of irreducible closed sets. This gives the displayed expression.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_homeomorph: The homeomorphism sends chains to chains of the same length, giving one dimension inequality. Its inverse gives the reverse inequality, so the dimensions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_homeomorph: The homeomorphism sends irreducible closed sets to irreducible closed sets and preserves strict inclusions. Every finite strict chain in the first space therefore has an image chain of the same length in the second. Taking suprema gives the dimension inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_isClosed_of_no:
Take a finite strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace. Its images are irreducible and closed in the ambient space and remain a strict chain because the inclusion is injective. The last image lies in some ambient irreducible component. No component is contained in the subspace, so this containment is strict. Appending the component produces an ambient chain one step longer.

The subspace has a point, whose closure gives a chain of length zero. The extended chain shows the ambient dimension is at least one. Since the ambient dimension is finite, write it as a positive natural number. Every chain in the subspace has length at most one less than that number by the extension argument. Their supremum is therefore strictly smaller than the ambient dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_lt_withBotSuccToNat: The upper value is below top and has a smaller value, so it is an embedded finite natural number. Its successor index is positive. If the lower value is bottom, its index is zero. Otherwise it too is finite and its natural value is strictly smaller, so adding one to both values preserves strict inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.dim_baseChange: Admissibility makes the original structure map smooth. Extending the field preserves the ambient topological Krull dimension by the comparison for smooth schemes. Applying the common successor conversion gives equality of the marked ideals' dimension indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_bot_of_formallyUnramified_of_comap_le:
Localize the target domain at the images of elements outside the kernel prime of the base. These images are nonzero, so the localization remains a domain and the localization map is injective. The base map to the localization kills the kernel prime and inverts every nonzero class modulo that prime. It therefore factors through the fraction field of the quotient base. The localized domain is essentially of finite type and formally unramified over that field by the corresponding composition and restriction properties. It is consequently a field.

The prime in the statement avoids the inverted elements because its contraction is contained in the kernel prime. It therefore extends to a proper prime in the localization. If it contained a nonzero element, that element would remain nonzero by injectivity and become a unit in the field. This would put one in the extended prime, a contradiction. Thus the original prime is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_le_of_comap_eq: Quotient the target by the smaller prime. The resulting domain is still essentially of finite type and formally unramified over the base. The kernel of the new base map is the contraction of the smaller prime. The image of the larger prime is prime in the quotient, and its contraction is contained in the kernel prime by the given equality of contractions. The domain result makes this image prime zero. Hence the larger prime lies in the smaller one and they are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_dim_le_topologicalKrullDim: Choose a closed point of the nonempty affine chart. At that point the local ring is Noetherian, and the local dimension theorem for an étale chart identifies its dimension with the number of coordinates. That local ring agrees with the ambient local ring at the same point. The dimension of any ambient local ring is at most the topological dimension of the scheme, giving the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isField_of_formallyUnramified: Pass from the domain to its fraction field. Localization is formally unramified and essentially of finite type, and both properties are preserved by composition over the base field. For this field extension formal unramifiedness gives separability, hence algebraicity. Every element of the domain is then integral over the base field because the domain embeds in its fraction field. A domain integral over a field is a field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_of_smooth_over_field: Sections on each affine open of a smooth scheme over a field are a finite-type algebra over that field and hence Noetherian. This is the local Noetherian condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_stalk_of_opens: The stalk map of an open inclusion is a ring isomorphism. It transfers Noetherianity of the ambient local ring to the local ring on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_of_topologicalKrullDim_e: The dimension index is the same successor conversion of topological Krull dimension for both schemes. Applying that conversion to the given equality gives equal indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_le_of_etale: The étale dimension inequality bounds the source by the target. Since the target dimension is finite, the conversion to successor indices preserves the weak inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_essFiniteType_formall: Every finite strict chain of target primes contracts to a strict chain of the same length by the contraction result. Taking the supremum of chain lengths gives the dimension bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_isLocalization_etale: The given étale ring map is finite type and formally unramified. Composing with localization of the target gives a map from the original source ring to the localized target that is essentially of finite type and formally unramified. The commutative diagram factors this map through the localized source. These two properties pass to that factor over the localized source by the localization and composition results. The dimension bound for essentially finite-type formally unramified maps now applies to the given local rings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etaleChart_of_i: The local ring of the chart domain is Noetherian because it is isomorphic to the ambient local ring. An étale morphism to affine space bounds the dimension of that local ring by the number of coordinates. Transfer the bound to the ambient local ring through the open-inclusion isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale_of_isNoet: Choose an affine neighborhood of the target point and an affine neighborhood of the source point within its inverse image. The latter can be taken to be a basic open of an initial affine neighborhood. On sections the induced map is étale. The local rings are localizations of those section rings at the relevant primes, and the germ maps commute with the map on stalks. Apply the dimension inequality for localizations of an étale map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_opens: The inclusion of an open subscheme induces an isomorphism of the local rings at corresponding points. Isomorphic rings have the same Krull dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_comap_of_formallyUnramified: Contraction preserves inclusion of primes. For a strict inclusion, equal contractions would force the two primes to be equal by the preceding prime comparison theorem. Thus contraction preserves strict inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_base_pullback_fst_specMapOfFi: A field spectrum is a single point, so the map of field spectra is surjective. The projection in question is its base change, and surjectivity is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_etale: An étale morphism is locally of finite type, so its source is locally Noetherian because its target is. At each source point the dimension of the local ring is at most the dimension of the target local ring by the étale stalk bound. The latter is at most the topological dimension of the target. Bounding every source local ring in this way bounds the source's topological dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_specMapOfFi: The projection of the field base change is surjective by stability of surjectivity under base change. The dimension comparison for a smooth scheme with such a projection therefore gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_spec_map_of:
The original and extended schemes are smooth over their fields, hence locally Noetherian. For a point of the extended scheme, choose an affine étale chart around its image and pull this chart back to the extended scheme. The extended local dimension is at most the chart's number of coordinates, which is at most the original scheme's dimension by the bound for nonempty affine charts. This bounds the extended scheme's dimension from above.

For the reverse direction, choose an affine étale chart at any point of the original scheme and use surjectivity to choose a point above it. The original local dimension is at most the number of chart coordinates. The extended chart has that same number and is nonempty and affine, so this number is at most the extended scheme's dimension. The bounds on all original local rings give the reverse inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_center: The ambient center at a stage is defined by taking the image of the original center ideal through its stage embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_isoObjZero: Since the initial ambient is the given ambient itself, the construction uses its identity isomorphism at stage zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_length: The ambient blowup sequence is assigned the same number of active steps as the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_schemeAt_zero: The recursive ambient sequence starts with the given ambient scheme.
