Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf_of_isClosedImmersi: The image ideal sheaf is the image of the original ideal along the closed immersion. Pulling this image back along the closed immersion recovers the original ideal by the ideal image formula for closed immersions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_succ_: The two maps at consecutive stages are the recursive embeddings, with the ambient transition given by the successor construction. Its compatibility with the original transition is the successor commutative square already established.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_zero: The initial embedding is defined as the original sequence's stage-zero isomorphism followed by the given ambient immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoBlowupImageIdealSheaf_comp_: The chosen immersion identifies the source blowup with the strict transform in the ambient blowup over the preceding embedded scheme. Its projection to the old ambient is therefore the source transition followed by the old embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closedImmersion_blowup_imageIdeal: At a valid stage the transition is a blowup of the specified center. The ambient is Noetherian and hence locally Noetherian. Apply the result on embedding a blowup into the ambient blowup of the image ideal, using the given closed immersion and center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closedImmersion_blowup_of_isBlowu: Push the center ideal forward through the closed immersion. Its pullback is the original center ideal. If an irreducible component of the embedded scheme mapped entirely into the pushed-forward center support, the support pullback identity would put it inside the original center support, contrary to the hypothesis. The strict-transform blowup theorem therefore identifies the ambient strict transform of the embedded scheme as a blowup along the original center. The given source is also such a blowup, so their universal properties give mutually inverse maps over the embedded scheme. Compose this isomorphism with the inclusion of the ambient strict transform. This is a closed immersion compatible with both blowup projections. Its kernel is the strict-transform ideal because the first map is an isomorphism and the second is the inclusion defined by that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_ambientBlowupMor: The transition map of the recursive ambient sequence is the successor ambient map at the chosen stage. At every valid index this map is a blowup along the image of the current center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_succAmbientEmbed: At an active step the construction uses the canonical projection from the blowup of the image of the center ideal. This projection is a blowup along that image ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embeddingIntoAmbientBl: Every stage of the recursive ambient construction supplies a closed immersion. At zero it is the original immersion composed with the initial isomorphism, at an actual successor it is the strict-transform immersion, and beyond the active stages the construction uses the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embeddingIntoBlowupIma: The chosen next-stage embedding is the one supplied by the ambient blowup comparison, which is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_isoObjZero_hom_comp: The stage-zero isomorphism is a closed immersion, and the original embedding is a closed immersion by hypothesis. The property is preserved by composition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientBlowupSequence_schem: The initial ambient is Noetherian, and each actual subsequent ambient arises by blowing up the preceding Noetherian ambient along the image center. The preservation assumption gives Noetherianity throughout the stated range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_blowup_of_isNoetherian: The canonical projection is a blowup along the given ideal. The assumed Noetherian preservation for blowups applies because its target is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_ambientBlowupSequ: The two sequences have equal length. Take the recursive closed immersion at every stage. At zero it agrees with the original immersion through the initial isomorphisms. The successor squares commute by the stage compatibility. Each ambient center is the image of the original center, and the defining ideal of each successor embedding is the corresponding strict transform. These are the required pushforward comparison data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_s: At this actual step, the next stage is embedded as the strict transform of the previous stage in the ambient blowup. The successor kernel formula therefore identifies its ideal with the strict transform along the ambient map and center of that step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoBlowupImageIdealSheaf: The chosen new embedding has image the ambient strict transform of the preceding embedded scheme. Its defining kernel is the strict transform of the preceding embedding ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_succAmbientEmbedding_eq_strictTransf: At a valid step the new embedding is the chosen strict-transform embedding, and the ambient map is the canonical blowup of the image center. The kernel calculation for that embedding gives the stated strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_support_subset_support_comap: The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. In particular, the indicated inverse image is contained in it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succAmbientEmbedding_comp_blowupMorphism: At an active step the compatibility follows from the chosen embedding into the ambient blowup. After the active range, the new embedding is the identity and the new ambient map is the source transition followed by the old embedding. The same equality then follows from the identity law.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsBlo: Identify the source and target with the equal schemes. The inserted maps are identities, and pulling the center back along the target identity leaves it unchanged. The asserted blowup property reduces to the original one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendBoundary_length_succ: Choose the second branch for the appended boundary at one step after the join. The second sequence's offset there is one, so the formula is precisely the entrywise pullback of its stage-one boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendBoundary_of_le_length: At or before the join the boundary definition takes the first list at that stage and pulls back every entry along the stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendBoundary_of_length_lt: Beyond the join the boundary definition selects the second list at the offset and pulls its entries back through the second-stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendBoundary_succ: Before or after the join use the boundary update of the corresponding sequence, transported through the adjacent stage identifications. At the join the second initial boundary is the pullback of the first final boundary. Its first update is therefore the list of strict transforms along the first transition of the second sequence, applied to that pulled-back list, followed by the exceptional ideal. Compatibility with the initial target isomorphism rewrites these as the strict transforms and exceptional ideal for the appended join transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendBoundary_zero: The stage-zero boundary comes from the first initial boundary pulled back along the appended stage identification. That first boundary pulls the given initial list back along the first initial isomorphism. Combine these pullbacks entrywise to get the list pulled back along the appended initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendIdeal_length_succ: Use the second branch for the stage just past the join. Its offset is one. Replacing the offset by one and the corresponding stage identification by the one to stage one yields the claimed ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendIdeal_of_le_length: At or before the join, the appended ideal is defined as the first sequence's ideal pulled back through the stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendIdeal_of_length_lt: Past the join, the appended ideal is defined as the second sequence's ideal at the offset, pulled back through the corresponding stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendIdeal_zero: At zero the ideal is the first initial ideal pulled back through the appended stage identification. The first initial ideal is the original ideal pulled back by the first initial isomorphism. Compose the two pullbacks to obtain the pullback along the appended initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendProjectionToBase_of_le_length: The projection definition at or before the join uses the first sequence's projection, preceded by the identification of the appended stage with that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendProjectionToBase_of_length_lt: Beyond the join the projection uses the stage identification, the second sequence's projection from the offset stage to its base, and the first sequence's final projection to the original base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendProjectionToBase_succ: Before the join apply the first sequence's projection recursion and cancel the intermediate stage identification. At the join the second projection at one is its first transition followed by its initial isomorphism, which is the appended transition after identifying the stages. It is followed by the first final projection. After the join the second projection recursion applies at the offset index, and the first final projection is the same in both composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendProjectionToBase_zero: At zero the projection is formed from the first sequence's projection and the initial stage identification. The first projection at zero is the forward initial isomorphism, giving the forward map of the appended initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_of_eq_length: Substitute the first length for i. The first branch includes equality, so the join stage is the final stage of the first sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_of_le_length: At or before the length of the first sequence, the stage definition selects the stage of that sequence at the given index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_of_length_lt: Strictly after the first length, the stage definition selects the second sequence at the index obtained by subtracting the first length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_succ_of_eq_length: At one more than the first length, use the second branch of the stage definition. Subtracting the first length leaves one, so this is stage one of the second sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_succ_of_length_lt: The next index is still beyond the first length. Since subtraction of the first length from i is exact, subtracting it from i+1 gives one more than the offset for i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_succ_of_lt_length: If i is strictly below the first length, i+1 is at most that length. Thus the new successor stage is the first sequence's stage i+1.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendSchemeAt_zero: Zero is at most the first length, so the first branch of the stage definition gives the original initial stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_blowupMorphis: The join transition in the underlying data is the second sequence's first transition followed by its initial isomorphism to the first final stage. Identify the source and target with the corresponding appended objects to obtain the stated map.
After the join the underlying adjacent map is the second sequence's map at the offset index, transported by the source and target stage identifications.
Before the join the underlying adjacent map is the first sequence's adjacent map, preceded and followed by the identifications with the appended stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_center_length: The underlying center at the join is the initial center of the second sequence transported to the first sequence's final stage by the inverse initial isomorphism, then pulled back to the join object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_center_of_len: The underlying append after the join uses the second sequence's center at the offset index, pulled back through the identification with the appended stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_center_of_lt_: The unmarked center formula before the join pulls the first sequence's center back along the stage identification. Forgetting the markings leaves this formula intact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_isoObjZero_ho: The initial isomorphism of the underlying append is assembled from the stage-zero identification and the first sequence's initial isomorphism. Taking its forward map composes the corresponding forward maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_length: The underlying unmarked data are formed by appending the two unmarked sequences. Their length is the sum of those lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt_leng: Because the second length is positive, the final stage falls in the second part. Its offset is precisely the second length, so the stage is the final object of the second sequence.
In the underlying append, the stage just beyond the first length has second-sequence offset one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt_of_l: The underlying append uses the first sequence's stage at any index at most its length.
For the underlying append, any index strictly beyond the first length uses the stage of the second sequence indexed by the offset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt_succ: After the join the underlying append uses the second sequence, with indices measured from the first length. Advancing one stage advances this offset by one.
At a successor of an index strictly below the first length, the underlying append is still at or before the join. Its stage is the first sequence's corresponding successor stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendToBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt_zero: The underlying append starts with the first sequence's stage zero, since zero lies in the first part of the stage definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_length: At the join both strict inequalities in the piecewise definition fail. The remaining transition goes through stage one of the second sequence, then its first transition and initial isomorphism, and finally identifies the target with the join stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_of_eq_length_add_s: The given index is past the first length, with offset j+1. Use the second branch for the adjacent map, replace the offset by j+1, and carry the resulting source and target identifications into the stated ones.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_of_length_lt: For an index strictly above the join, the transition definition uses the second sequence's adjacent map at the offset index. Its source and target are identified with the corresponding appended stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_of_lt_length: For an index strictly below the join, both stages come from the first sequence. The transition definition uses its adjacent map between the two stage identifications.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_boundary: The boundary field of the marked append is the piecewise list that was defined for the append construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_boundary_length_add_length: Since the second sequence has positive length, the total length lies past the join and its offset is the second length. Apply the second branch of the boundary definition at that offset to get the second final boundary pulled back entry by entry through the final stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_length: At the join the center is the second sequence's initial center pulled back through its inverse initial isomorphism and then through the appended stage's identification with the first sequence's final stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_of_length_lt: After the join the center definition chooses the second sequence's center at the offset index and pulls it back through the appended stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_of_lt_length: Before the join the center definition chooses the first sequence's center at the given index and pulls it back through the identification of the appended stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_ideal: The appended marked data use the piecewise appended ideal in their ideal field at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_ideal_length_add_length: A positive second length puts the final stage strictly beyond the join. Its offset is the second length. The second branch of the ideal formula therefore gives the second final ideal pulled back through the identification with the appended final stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_isoObjZero_hom: The appended initial isomorphism first identifies its stage zero with the first sequence's stage zero and then uses the first sequence's initial isomorphism. The forward map is the composite of those two forward maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_length:129: The length assigned to the append construction is the sum of the lengths of the two sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_length:824: The marked append has the length of its underlying unmarked data, obtained by adding the two original lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase: The appended marked data use the piecewise appended projection as their prescribed projection at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_length_add_length: The positive second length makes the total length strictly larger than the first. The piecewise definition therefore uses the second sequence, and subtracting the first length leaves exactly the second length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_length_succ: Just after the join, the second-sequence offset is one, hence the appended object there is the second sequence's first successor stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_of_eq_length_add_succ: At index equal to the first length plus j+1, the index is strictly beyond the join. Its offset from the join is j+1, so the second-stage formula gives the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_of_le_length:131: The appended data take their stage objects from the piecewise stage definition. Up to and including the first length this is the stage of the first sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_of_le_length:842: The underlying data of the marked append select the first sequence's stage at every index up to and including its length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_of_length_lt:134: Strictly beyond the first length, the appended stage is the second-sequence stage with the first length subtracted from the index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_of_length_lt:846: The underlying data of the marked append select the second sequence's stage beyond the join, at the index obtained by subtracting the first length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_succ_of_length_lt: Both the given index and its successor lie beyond the first length. Subtracting that length from the successor gives the successor of the old offset, which is the index of the stage in the second sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_succ_of_lt_length: Adding one to an index strictly below the first length stays at or below that length. The next stage of the appended sequence is therefore the corresponding stage of the first sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_zero: The appended stage at zero lies in the first part, so it is the original initial stage of the first sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_toBlowupSequenceData: The marked append is built on the already constructed unmarked append, which is its underlying blowup data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_toMarkedSequence_length: Converting marked data to a marked sequence retains the underlying length. The append data have length equal to the sum of the original lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_eq_eqToHom_comp_of_eq: Substitute the equality of the two indices. The source and target identifications are identities, so the composite is the adjacent map at that common index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_support_subset_orderAtLeastLocus_: Before and after the join, use the center-order property of the corresponding sequence and transport it by the stage identification. At the join, the second sequence has a first step and its initial ideal is the pullback of the first final ideal. Pull the inclusion for its initial center back along the inverse initial isomorphism. Support and the order locus both pull back under that isomorphism, and the two consecutive pulls of the initial ideal cancel. Transporting this inclusion to the join stage proves the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_hom_inv: Pulling back along the forward isomorphism and then its inverse is pulling back along their composite on the original scheme. That composite is the identity, whose pullback fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_inv_hom: Pullback first by the inverse and then by the forward isomorphism equals pullback by their composite on the original scheme. It is the identity, so the ideal is recovered.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_congr: Substitute one equal index for the other. The selected ideal sheaf is then the same and both maps arise from the same identification of schemes, so their pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_appendIdeal_suc: Before and after the join, use the exceptional-ideal product equality of the relevant sequence and transport it along the stage identifications. At the join, express the exceptional ideal as the pullback of the center. Pulling the transported center back through the second initial isomorphism recovers the second initial center, so the exceptional ideal agrees with that of the second first blowup. The first final ideal pulls back to the second initial ideal along the same isomorphism. The successor relation for the second sequence's first step now gives the desired formula at the join.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_comap_eqToHom: Replace the source and target schemes by their equal counterparts. The identifying maps become identities and the transported ideals become the given ideals. The displayed relation is then the original exceptional-ideal product equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_appendBound: Away from the join, the center, boundary, and structural map come from one sequence and the given strict normal crossings condition transports through the stage identification. At the join use the second sequence's initial center and its initial boundary, which is the pullback of the first final boundary. Pull its condition back along the inverse initial isomorphism. This restores the first final boundary and its structural map, and transports the center to the join. The appended stage identification gives the stated condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_comap_eqToH: Substitute the given equality of schemes. The induced map is the identity, so it preserves the structural map, the center ideal, and every entry of the boundary. The required condition is the given strict normal crossings condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_comap_iso_i: Pull the given strict normal crossings condition back along the inverse isomorphism. The structural map simplifies to q because the two isomorphisms cancel. Each boundary entry also returns to its original value by functoriality of pullback. The resulting center is the pullback of the given center along the inverse, as asserted.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_appendBlowupMorp: Before the join, the appended transition and center come from the first sequence. After the join, subtract the first length and use the indexed transition and center of the second sequence. In each case, the length bound makes this a genuine step and the stage identifications preserve the blowup property. At the join, the second sequence has positive length. Its initial transition is followed by its initial isomorphism, with the center pulled back along the inverse isomorphism. Transport of a blowup by this target isomorphism gives the property at the join.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_eqToHom_comp: Identify the equal schemes. The equality-induced map is the identity and its pullback fixes each ideal. Both lists then consist of the pullbacks along the given morphism, in the same order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_eqToHom_congr: Identify the two equal indices. They give the same list and the same map identifying its scheme with the source, so the entrywise pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_hom_map_comap_inv: Each entry is pulled back along the forward isomorphism and then along the inverse. This composite is the identity on the original scheme, so every entry returns to its original value and list order is preserved.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_strictTransform_comap_eqToHom: Identify the two equal source schemes and the two equal target schemes. All inserted identifications are identity maps and leave the ideals unchanged. The transported boundary formula becomes the given list of strict transforms followed by the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_strictTransform_comp_iso_hom: Transport the center through the inverse target isomorphism. Its pullback through the forward map recovers the original center. By compatibility of strict transform with target isomorphisms, taking the strict transform after pulling back each boundary entry equals taking its strict transform along the composite blowup map with the transported center. The exceptional ideals also agree, since each is the pullback of the corresponding center. This gives the equality of the two boundary lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_append_of_eq_length_add: Induct on j. At offset one the appended transition goes through the second sequence's first map and its initial isomorphism, then the first sequence's final projection. This is the second projection at one followed by the first final projection. At a later offset, use the second sequence's adjacent map and the induction hypothesis for the previous projection. The intermediate stage identifications cancel and the second projection recursion gives the required formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_append_of_le_length: At zero the projection is the initial isomorphism of the appended data, which is the first projection after identifying the two initial stages. For a successor stage at most the first length, the adjacent transition is from the first sequence. Combine it with the preceding projection by induction, cancel the intermediate stage identifications, and use the first sequence's projection recursion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_append_of_length_lt: Write any index strictly past the first length as that length plus j+1. The positive-offset projection formula expresses it as the second projection at j+1 followed by the first final projection. Since j+1 is the original index minus the first length, this is the desired expression.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_congr:31: Replace n′ by the equal index n. Then the source identification is the identity on stage n, and the composite is the original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_congr:455: Use the equality of the indices to identify the two stage schemes. The identification map is then the identity, and composing it with the prescribed projection gives the original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_center_comp_appendProjectionToBas: Away from the join the center and its structural map to the field come from the corresponding step of one sequence, transported through a stage identification. Smoothness is preserved by this isomorphism. At the join take the second sequence's smooth initial center and pull it back along the inverse initial isomorphism. Its map to the field becomes the first final projection followed by the original structure map, since the inverse cancels the initial isomorphism. Transport once more to the appended join object.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_eqToHom: Identify the two equal indices at both the source and the target of the transition. The identification maps then become identities, and both composites are the same transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_ofMarkedSequence: To recover marked data from a marked sequence, first recover blowup data from its underlying unmarked sequence. The remaining fields record the marking, so the underlying blowup data are the claimed data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_eq_map_strictTransform_app: Apply the given successor boundary formula in the marked data. The converted sequence uses the same adjacent map and center, so each strict transform and the appended exceptional ideal agree with those in that formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_support_subset_orderAtLeastLocus: At an index below the length, the marked data require the support of the center to lie in the locus where the stored ideal has order at least the specified mark. This is exactly the asserted inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyBlowupSequenceData_blowupMorphism: All adjacent maps in the empty data are defined to be the identity of the base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyBlowupSequenceData_center: The constant stage data for an empty sequence use the unit ideal sheaf at every index, so all stored centers are empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyBlowupSequenceData_isoObjZero: The initial stage of the empty sequence is the base scheme and its chosen identification with the base is the identity isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyBlowupSequenceData_length: The empty blowup data have length zero by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt: Every stage in the empty blowup data is defined to be the base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_boundary: The boundary family for the empty marked data is constant with value the original boundary list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_center: The underlying empty unmarked data take the unit ideal sheaf as their center at every index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_ideal: The family of ideals for the empty marked data is constant with value the given initial ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_length: The underlying empty unmarked data have length zero, and the marking adds no steps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_projection: All stages are the base scheme, and the prescribed projection at every index is its identity map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_schemeAt: The underlying empty unmarked data use the base scheme at each index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_toBlowupSe: The empty marked data are built on top of the empty unmarked data on the same base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_toMarkedSe: Conversion to a marked sequence retains the length of the underlying data. This length is zero for the empty data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_iteratedBlowupMorphism: Replace the second length by the equal first length. The source identification becomes the identity, so the two sides agree by the left identity law.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_iteratedBlowupMorphism_of_e: Substitute zero for the length. The two stages now coincide, so the identification of their objects is the identity. A composite of zero transitions is also the identity, and composing these identities gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_ideal_succ_eq_c: The adjacent transition of the converted sequence is the stored map, and the center and stage ideals are retained. The exceptional ideal and the pullback ideal in the asserted relation thus agree with those in the marked data. The stored successor ideal relation gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center_boun: The marked data give strict normal crossings of the center with the current boundary for the stage map to the field. The converted sequence uses the same projection to the base and hence the same map to the field. The normal crossings condition therefore still holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_tower_map: Below the length of the sequence, the stored adjacent map is a blowup along the stored center. The tower map for these consecutive indices agrees with that adjacent map, so it has the same blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_comp_iteratedBlow: Induct on the number of steps in the part of the composite starting farthest from stage i. With zero steps, the assertion is the identity law. For the successor, extract the first transition and apply induction to the rest. Move the index identification past that transition, using the equalities of its source and target indices obtained by associating the sum. The resulting composite is the recursion for the sum of the two lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_congr_length: Replace either length by the other along the given equality. The composites now have the same source, and the intervening identification is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_congr_start: Substitute one starting index for the other. The source and target identifications are identities, so the two sides are the same composite of the specified length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_one: Expanding the one-step composite gives the adjacent transition followed by the zero-step identity. The right identity law removes that identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_succ: In the recursion for a composite of k+1 steps ending at stage i, the first map goes from stage i+k+1 to i+k. The remaining k steps form the composite ending at i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedBlowupMorphism_zero: The zero-length composite in the recursive definition is the identity on its starting stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_blowupMorphism: The underlying recovered data store the original adjacent transition at every index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_boundary_apply: At the specified index the recovered data use the original stage's boundary list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_center: The recovered unmarked data use the center of the original sequence at each index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_ideal: The marked ideal field of the recovered data is the original family of stage ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_length: The length comes from the unmarked data extracted from the sequence, which store the original sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_projectionToBase: The projection field of the recovered data assigns to each stage the original sequence's projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_blowupMorphism: The recovered data store the original sequence's transition from stage i+1 to stage i as the map at index i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_center: The recovered data take their center at each index from the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_isoObjZero: The recovered data take their initial isomorphism directly from the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_length: The data recovered from the sequence store the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_projectionToBase: At stage zero, the sequence's projection is the zero-to-zero transition followed by the initial isomorphism. The first map is the identity, leaving the initial isomorphism, which is also the data projection. The two projections satisfy the same successor recursion with the original adjacent maps, so induction gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_schemeAt: The object stored at stage i in the recovered data is the scheme of the original sequence at stage i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq: The prescribed projection at stage zero is the initial isomorphism, just as for the projection constructed from the unmarked data. Their successor rules both compose the adjacent map with the preceding projection. Induction identifies the projections stage by stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq_toSequenceOfBlowups: The prescribed projection agrees with the recursive projection on the underlying data. Conversion of those data to a sequence preserves that recursive projection, so the prescribed and converted projections coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_succ: The recursive definition of the projection at the next stage takes the transition to the current stage and then the current projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: The projection at stage zero is defined to be the forward map of the initial isomorphism to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_center_comp_projection: Use the smoothness of the center over the field from the marked data. Its structural map first includes it in the stage scheme and then projects to the base and to the field. The converted sequence has the same stage projection, so the structural map remains smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_blowupMorphism: The underlying unmarked sequence is the one constructed from the data. Its adjacent transition was already identified with the stored adjacent map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_boundary: The conversion takes the boundary list at each stage directly from the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_center: The underlying unmarked conversion uses the same center ideal sheaf at each stage, so adding the marked data leaves that center unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_ideal: The conversion takes the marked ideal at each stage directly from the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_lastIdeal: The length and the indexed ideals are preserved by conversion. The last ideal is therefore the stored ideal evaluated at that length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_length: The marked conversion uses the unmarked data conversion underneath, and that conversion has the original stored length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_projectionToBase: The converted underlying sequence has the same projections as its unmarked data. Those projections agree stage by stage with the projections explicitly supplied by the marked data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_projectionToSpec: The converted stage's map to the spectrum of the field is the projection to the original scheme followed by its structure map. The first map agrees with the projection supplied in the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_schemeAt: The underlying tower of the converted marked sequence uses the stored stage object at every index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_toSequenceOfBlowups: The underlying sequence of the converted marked sequence is defined by converting the underlying unmarked data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_blowupMorphism: The adjacent transition of the converted sequence is the corresponding consecutive-index map of the tower. This tower map is the original adjacent map by the one-step computation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_center: The conversion uses the stored center ideal sheaf at each stage as the center of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_isoObjZero: The conversion keeps the original isomorphism between stage zero and the base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_length: The conversion builds the sequence of blowups with the length in the original data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_projectionToBase: At stage zero, both projections are the initial isomorphism, since the zero-to-zero transition is the identity. At a successor stage, both projections first take the common adjacent map and then the projection at the preceding stage. Induction gives equality at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_projectionToBase_suc: The map stored at index i is the original transition from i+1 to i. Composing it with the transition from i to zero gives the transition from i+1 to zero by functoriality. Following both composites by the initial isomorphism gives the successor rule for projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_projectionToBase_zer: The transition from stage zero to itself is the image of the identity in the index category, hence is the identity on the stage. The projection to the base is that identity followed by the stage-zero isomorphism. This isomorphism is the one stored by conversion to data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_schemeAt: The stage of the converted sequence is the corresponding object of its tower, which is the stage object originally given.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_tower: The tower of the converted sequence is the functor constructed from the original stage objects and their adjacent maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.towerMorphism_comp: Write the transition from l to j as a composite of l−j steps and the transition from j to i as a composite of j−i steps. Identify j with i+(j−i). Concatenation gives (j−i)+(l−j) steps, which equals l−i because i≤ j≤ l. The initial identifications compose to the one defining the transition from l to i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.towerMorphism_eq_iteratedBlowupMorphism: When j=i+k, subtraction gives j−i=k. Thus the composite defining the tower map has length k. After this replacement its initial identification is exactly the one induced by j=i+k.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.towerMorphism_refl: A transition from stage i to itself is defined using the length i−i=0. Both the index identification and the composite of zero steps are identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.towerMorphism_succ: The difference between consecutive indices is one. Replace the length in the tower map by one and cancel the resulting inverse source identifications. A one-step composite is the specified adjacent transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tower_map_succ: By construction the tower sends the consecutive-index arrow to the transition from stage i+1 to stage i. The consecutive-index calculation identifies this transition with the stored map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tower_obj: The tower assigns to the opposite index corresponding to i the stored stage object at i.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_length: At zero the pullback of the original list has its original length. At each successor, taking strict transforms preserves the length and appending the exceptional ideal increases it by one. Induction gives the original length plus the number of steps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_succ: The successor boundary first takes the strict transforms of the ordered preceding list and then appends the exceptional ideal of the transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_zero: The boundary recursion starts by pulling back every member of the original ordered boundary along the stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.controlledTransform_s: For the successor pull back the preceding transform along the transition and take its residual ideal with respect to the exceptional ideal raised to the marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.controlledTransform_z: The recursion begins with the original ideal pulled back along the stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.eq_of_pow_exceptional: At the valid stage the map is a blowup, whose exceptional ideal is locally generated by non-zero-divisors. The cancellation theorem for powers of such ideals gives equality of the two factors.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.pow_exceptionalIdeal_: The successor transform is the selected residual ideal. The given divisibility supplies a factorization, so multiplying that selected ideal by the exceptional power recovers the pulled-back preceding transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.toMarkedBlowupSequenc: The marked sequence retains the original transition map at the given stage.
The marked data use the boundary list produced by the boundary recursion at the given stage.
The center of the marked sequence is the original center at the specified stage.
The ideal assignment of the marked data is defined to be the recursively computed controlled transform.
The marked construction keeps the length of the underlying blowup sequence.
The projection of the marked sequence data is assigned to be the projection to the base of the underlying blowup data.
The marked construction uses the same scheme at every stage as the original sequence data.
The construction adds marking, ideals, boundary and compatibility data to the given blowup sequence. Its underlying blowup sequence data are the original data.
Passing from marked data to the sequence retains the underlying ordinary blowup data. Applying the ordinary sequence construction to those data therefore gives the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_and_boundary_eq: At each valid step any two residual factors satisfying the marked transition equation have equal products with the same exceptional power. This power can be cancelled by the blowup cancellation theorem. Thus the uniqueness hypothesis of the simultaneous ideal and boundary comparison holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_and_boundary_eq_of_c: Induct on the stage. The initial ideal and boundary from the recursions coincide with the marked data's initial pullbacks. At a successor, the recorded next ideal is a residual factor for the pulled-back previous ideal by the marked transition equation. The recursively chosen ideal satisfies the same equation, because that factorization exists and the preceding ideals agree by induction. The assumed cancellation identifies the two residual factors. The boundary recursions agree because both take the same strict transforms of the equal old lists and append the same exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor: At every point cancel the common locally principal factor in the stalk by the non-zero-divisor argument. Equal stalk ideals give equal ideal sheaves.
The power of the common factor is still locally generated by non-zero-divisors. Apply the cancellation theorem to that power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_span_singleton_mul_eq_mul: The cancellation argument gives containment of the first ideal in the second. Apply it to the reversed product equality to obtain the reverse containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_stalkIdeal_eq: On any affine open, the localizations of its two section ideals at a maximal ideal are the corresponding stalk ideals. These are equal by hypothesis. Ideals in a ring are determined by their localizations at all maximal ideals, so the section ideals on every affine open are equal. They determine the ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_excep: The exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back to the blowup. For a blowup this pullback is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, giving the asserted property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_pow: On an affine neighborhood where the ideal is generated by a non-zero-divisor, its power is generated by the same power of that element. Powers of non-zero-divisors are non-zero-divisors, giving the required local generators.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_toBlowupSequenceData: At every active step take the recorded successor ideal as the divisibility witness, using equality of the recorded preceding ideal with its recursive controlled transform. The same equality transfers the center's order condition. The projections to the base agree with those of the marked sequence, so the center's smoothness carries over. The recursive and recorded boundaries agree as well, so the same center has the required strict normal crossing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_span_singleton_mul_eq_mul: Take an element of the first ideal. Its product with the given generator belongs to the product of the principal ideal and the first ideal, hence also to the product with the second ideal by equality. It is therefore the generator times an element of the second ideal. Cancel the generator using that it is a non-zero-divisor. The initial element lies in the second ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_boundary: The marked sequence data retain the sequence's boundary list at each stage. Its comparison with the boundary recursion yields the required equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_controlledTransform: The data associated to a marked sequence retain its stage ideals. Apply the comparison with the recursive controlled transform to those data at the specified valid stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq_toBlowupSequenceData: Both projections at zero are the chosen initial isomorphism. For a successor both compose the same transition map with the preceding projection. Induction therefore gives equality at every index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_eq_of_mul_eq_mul: Near the given point the common factor is generated by a non-zero-divisor on an affine open. Its germ remains a non-zero-divisor because the stalk is a localization there. Taking stalks of the equality of products gives equality of the products of the stalk ideals with the principal ideal of this germ. Cancel the principal ideal to conclude.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_boundary_eq_boundar: The simultaneous comparison gives equality of the recursive boundary and the original marked boundary at this stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_controlledTransform: The simultaneous comparison of the recursive and recorded data gives equality of the two ideals at the specified valid stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dimensionNonincreasingAlongBlowups: Induct on the stage of the marked sequence. At zero the scheme is isomorphic to the original ambient, so their dimension indices agree. At a successor the preceding marked ideal is admissible and its scheme is locally of finite type and quasi-compact over the field. The center has strict normal crossings with the boundary and the transition is its blowup. The blowup dimension inequality therefore bounds the successor dimension index by the preceding one. Compose with the induction bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_krullDimSucc_of_iso: A scheme isomorphism induces a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces. Their topological Krull dimensions agree, so applying the successor conversion gives equal dimension indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_eq_filterNeTop: Both list filters keep an entry exactly when its ideal differs from the unit ideal. They therefore produce the same sublist.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.validOfSameNontrivialBoundary: Replacing the boundary retains the field, scheme, structure map, ideal and marking. The old and new lists agree after deleting unit ideals. The strict normal crossing criterion under this agreement therefore transfers the one admissibility condition involving the boundary. All other conditions are inherited.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq: The new boundary is defined by taking the strict transform of each entry of the old list in order and then appending the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_eq_map_strictTransform_app: The transition rule in the sequence takes the strict transforms of the entries of the current boundary and appends the exceptional ideal of the step. Apply that rule at the given valid index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_eq:39: The exceptional ideal of a blowup is the pullback of the center ideal along the blowup map. This is the exceptional ideal of the given step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_eq:94: At this stage the exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back by the transition map of its blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center: The sequence's center condition gives strict normal crossings with the current boundary at every valid index. Apply it at the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_eq: The last boundary is the boundary at the final index, which is the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_eq: The last ideal is defined by evaluating the stage ideals at the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_center_subschemeι: The sequence includes smoothness of each actual center over the field. The composite in that condition is exactly the center inclusion followed by this stage's structure morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_def: The structural map at this stage is the projection to the original scheme followed by that scheme's morphism to the field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_eq: The structure morphism of the blown-up scheme is defined by following its blowup map with the original structure morphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_comap_i: Choose an étale coordinate chart for the boundary at the image point. Pull its open back along the isomorphism and compose the restricted isomorphism of opens with the chart. The composite is étale and respects the new structure map. Keep the same assignment of coordinates to the boundary entries. Distinct assigned coordinates remain distinct, since pullback preserves the list's positions. An entry described by the unit ideal remains the unit ideal. An entry described by one coordinate ideal pulls back to that coordinate ideal under the composite chart, by functoriality of ideal pullback. This is the required local normal crossing presentation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_boundary: Induct on the stage. At zero, the boundary is pulled back from the original one along the isomorphism at stage zero, so it has strict normal crossing position. At a successor the underlying space is Noetherian by hypothesis. The preceding boundary has strict normal crossings by induction, and the current center satisfies the normal crossing condition with it. The blowup boundary theorem gives strict normal crossing position for the strict transforms with the exceptional divisor appended. This is exactly the successor boundary with its successor structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_boundary_: Every actual stage of the sequence is Noetherian because the starting scheme is Noetherian, so its underlying space is Noetherian. These bounds supply the Noetherian hypotheses of the boundary induction theorem.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comp_iso_: The local chart transport gives strict normal crossing coordinates at every point of the new scheme. For any boundary entry these charts give either the unit ideal or the ideal of a single coordinate near each point. The local coordinate criterion makes each entry a smooth divisor. Along with the pointwise presentation, this gives strict normal crossing position globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: The underlying sequence of blowups begins on a Noetherian scheme. The theorem on Noetherianity along blowup sequences applies to every stage up to its length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_structureMorphism: Induct on the stage within the sequence. At zero the structure map is the original smooth map preceded by an isomorphism. For the successor, the preceding stage is smooth over the field by induction. Its center has strict normal crossings with the boundary, so the theorem for blowup of such a center gives smoothness of the successor over the field. The successor formula identifies its map with that composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_succ: The projection of the successor stage to the base is its transition map followed by the preceding projection. Compose this identity with the original structure map to obtain the successor formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_zero: The projection of stage zero to the base is its chosen isomorphism with the original scheme. Following this with the original structure morphism gives the formula.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersContainNoComponent_ofMarkedSequen: At a valid stage the transformed ideal is nonzero on components by the preceding induction. Every center point lies in its locus of order at least the marking. Since the marking is at least one, this locus lies in the support of the ideal. A whole component in the center would therefore lie in that support, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_eq_preimage: The support of the pulled-back ideal sheaf is the inverse image of its original support. Taking underlying sets gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.effectiveCartierSupportContainsNoCompone: A divisor ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor avoids the generic point of each irreducible component. Equivalently, its support contains no irreducible component. Apply this effective Cartier divisor property to the given ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_irreducibleComponent_subset_of_se: Intersect the source component with the inverse image of the given open. It is a nonempty open in that irreducible component. Its image is irreducible, so choose a target irreducible component containing it. This target component meets the open, and their intersection is irreducible. Its inverse image in the source is the continuous image of that intersection under the section, because the section is inverse to the map over the open. Thus this inverse image is irreducible and contains the open part of the source component. Its closure then contains the entire source component by density. Maximality makes that closure equal to the source component. Consequently the target component's open part maps back into the source component and lies in the given closed target set. Its density in the target component puts the whole target component in that closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_section_off_center: The blowup is an isomorphism over the complement of the center. Take the map on points of its inverse there and include its values in the blowup scheme. This map is continuous. The two inverse identities for the restriction give a section on that open and show that its image contains every blowup point lying above the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPreirreducible_inter_of_isOpen: Take two opens meeting the intersection. Intersect each open with the given open. The two resulting opens meet the original preirreducible set, so they meet it in common. This point also belongs to the original intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPreirreducible_preimage_val: Two opens in the subspace come from opens in the larger space. If they both meet the preimage of the given set, their ambient opens meet that set. Preirreducibility yields a common point in the given set, which lies in the subspace by containment. This proves preirreducibility in the subspace.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_iso_hom: The support pulls back under the isomorphism, and the corresponding homeomorphism sends each irreducible component to an irreducible component. The isomorphism invariance of componentwise nonvanishing gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ideal_of_isAdmissibl: Induct on the stage. The initial ideal is pulled back from the admissible marked ideal along the stage-zero isomorphism, preserving nonvanishing on components. For the successor, the controlled-transform identity multiplies the new ideal by the exceptional ideal to the power of the marking to obtain the pulled-back preceding ideal. The exceptional ideal is the pulled-back center ideal. The nonvanishing result for this identity applies to the blowup and induction hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_of_pow_mul_eq_comap: Suppose an irreducible component of the blowup were in the support of the transformed ideal. The given formula makes the pulled-back original ideal a product with this transform, whose stalk ideals are contained in those of the transform. Thus the component lies in the pullback of the original support. The exceptional ideal is effective Cartier, so its support does not contain the component. Choose a point of the component off that support. Its image is off the original center, where the blowup has an inverse section covering the entire inverse image. The component comparison for a map with such a section produces a component of the original scheme contained in the original support, contradicting componentwise nonvanishing.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.ofIso_coordIdeal: A chart coordinate ideal is the corresponding coordinate ideal of affine space pulled back along the chart map. The transported chart map first uses the restricted isomorphism and then the original chart. Functoriality of pullback gives the original chart ideal pulled back along that restricted isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapIsoInvariance: The order locus comparison supplies transport of the cosupport. The chart argument supplies transport of the center's crossing condition with the boundary, and the pullback of the closed subscheme gives smoothness of the transported center. The kernel description of strict transform gives its compatibility with the isomorphism. These four statements are the required invariance properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_resLE_comp_map_of_iso: The restricted ambient isomorphism is étale, as is the original chart map. Their composite is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_subschemeι_eq_comp_of_eq_ke: Replace the ideal by the kernel of the closed immersion. Its canonical subscheme inclusion and the given closed immersion then have the same kernel. The lifting property factors each inclusion through the other. Their two composites become the original inclusions after composition, so monomorphism of both inclusions makes the factors inverse. This gives the isomorphism and the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_comap_iso: A point of the pulled-back center support maps to the original center support, so choose normal crossing coordinates for the center and boundary there. Transfer the chart to the inverse image open using the restricted ambient isomorphism. Keep the same coordinate indices for the center and list entries. Unit boundary ideals are preserved by pullback, and each original equation expressed by a coordinate ideal becomes the same equation for the transported chart. This applies both to boundary entries and to the center, giving the required normal crossing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_resLE_iso_hom: The inverse scheme map takes the original open into the inverse image open because the two maps are inverse. Restrict it to give the candidate inverse to the restricted forward map. After composing with the respective open inclusions the two composites are identities by ambient compatibility. Since the open inclusions are monomorphisms, the restricted maps are inverse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_base_inv_base_apply: The inverse followed by the forward isomorphism is the identity of the target. Apply the induced maps to the specified target point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_inv_base_hom_base_apply: The forward isomorphism followed by its inverse is the identity, so their maps on points have the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIso_map_comp_affineSpaceFinToSpec: The original chart has structure map given by the open inclusion followed by the original structural map. Precompose with the restricted isomorphism, then use its compatibility with the two open inclusions. This gives the structure map of the inverse image open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_hom_eq_preim: The order inequality for pullback compares the original order at the image point with the pulled-back order. Apply it also to the inverse isomorphism. The inverse sends the image point back and pulls the ideal back to the original ideal, giving the reverse order inequality. Thus the two orders agree, and the loci of order at least the given marking correspond by inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap: Restriction of an ideal to an open is pullback along the open inclusion. The two composites from the new open to the original ambient agree because the open restriction square commutes. Pulling back the ideal along these composites gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comap_iso: Pull back the closed center inclusion along the ambient isomorphism. The second projection of the pullback is an isomorphism to the old center, while the first is a closed immersion with the pulled-back defining ideal. The closed subscheme of that ideal is isomorphic to this pullback over the new ambient. Thus its structure map is the old center's smooth structure map preceded by the composite isomorphism of centers, and is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_comp_iso_hom: Pulling back the center and divisor ideals along the composite is the same as first pulling them back along the isomorphism and then along the given map. The constructions of the strict-transform open and the subscheme immersion use exactly these two pullbacks. The corresponding immersions therefore have the same kernel, which is their strict transform ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iteratedComap: Induct on the stage up to the given bound. The initial divisor is smooth by hypothesis. At a successor, both ambient structural maps are smooth and the transition is a blowup whose center is disjoint from the preceding divisor. The smooth-divisor pullback theorem for a blowup away from the divisor applies. The recursion of the ideal and the formula for the successor structure map give the desired result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_strictTransform_of_disjo: At each stage the transformed ideal factors as the prescribed smooth divisor times the iterated pullback of the initial divisor, with disjoint supports. The iterated pullback is a smooth divisor by the disjoint-center induction. The product of these two smooth divisors with disjoint supports is a smooth divisor, yielding the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedComap_succ: The successor in the recursion pulls the preceding ideal back along the transition from the new stage, giving the displayed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedComap_zero: Before any transition, the iterated pullback is defined to be the original divisor ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_eq_mul_iteratedComap: Induct on the stage, with the given product and disjointness as the initial case. At the next blowup the pulled-back divisor factor is disjoint from the center at the preceding stage. The strict transform of its product with the other ideal is therefore the strict transform of the other factor times the pullback of the divisor factor. This is the asserted new product by the two transform rules. The support of the strict transform of the other factor lies in its old support's inverse image, while the pulled-back divisor support is exactly its old support's inverse image. The old disjointness gives new disjointness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_strictTransform_subset_preimage: The strict-transform support is the closure of the inverse image of the original support away from the center. That set is contained in the full inverse image of the support, which is closed. Its closure is therefore contained there as well.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.krullDimSucc_eq_: The dimension index of the marked ideal is defined to be the dimension index of its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.mk_eq_mk: The two marked ideals already have the same field, ambient and marking. Substituting the equal structure maps, ideals and boundaries makes every component agree, so the data are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.toMarkedSequence: The conversion retains the underlying sequence and the ideal at every stage. Evaluating the same ideals at the same final index gives equal last ideals.
The conversion to an ideal blowup sequence adds the properties of the ideal transforms but retains the same underlying sequence of schemes and blowup maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationAssignment.toSequenceOfB: Identify the two marked ideals using the given equality. The assignment is then applied to the same input on both sides, so the underlying blowup sequences are equal under that identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedSequenceOfBlowups_length: The empty marked sequence uses the empty ordinary sequence as its underlying sequence, so its length is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptySequenceOfBlowups_length: The empty sequence is defined with length zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalDivisor_eq: The exceptional ideal of the stage is the center ideal pulled back along that stage's blowup transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isResolution_iff: The sequence is a resolution precisely when the final ideal's locus of order at least the marking is empty. This is its defining resolution condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_withBotSuccToNat_topolog: The dimension index is defined by applying the successor conversion to the topological Krull dimension of the underlying space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_le_krullDimSucc_of_topologi: If the first dimension is bottom, its successor index is zero. Otherwise both dimensions are non-bottom because the first is at most the second. The upper dimension is below top, so both are embedded finite natural numbers. Their natural-number values have the same order, and adding one to both preserves the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_eq: The last boundary is the boundary list at the final index, which is the length of the underlying sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_eq: The last ideal is the ideal at the index given by the sequence's length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_boundary_zero: The initial boundary is the pullback of the input list along the stage-zero isomorphism. Since the projection at zero is that same isomorphism, the displayed formula follows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_exceptionalIdeal: Apply the controlled-transform identity at the given valid stage. The marking is one, so the first power of the exceptional ideal is the ideal itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_ideal_vanishesAl: The center support is in the locus where the stage ideal has order at least one. This locus is the ideal's support. The reduced-center condition turns that containment of supports into containment of the stage ideal in the center ideal, which means it vanishes along the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_ideal_zero: The stage-zero ideal is pulled back along its chosen isomorphism to the base. This isomorphism is the projection at stage zero, giving the claimed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_eq: The projection from the stage to the field is defined by composing its projection to the base with the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_bot: The successor conversion assigns zero to the bottom element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_coe: On an extended natural number viewed in the larger ordered set, the conversion takes its natural-number value and adds one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsAdmissible.transformAt: The field and positive marking are those of the original admissible input. The stage is smooth over the field and its boundary has strict normal crossings by the stage induction. Smoothness gives local finite type. The stage is Noetherian, so inverse images of quasi-compact opens are compact and its structural morphism is quasi-compact. The transformed ideal is nonzero on components by the controlled-transform induction. These give every admissibility condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_iso: A pulled-back boundary entry is a pulled-back smooth divisor because the original list has strict normal crossing position. At each point start with an étale chart at its image and transport the chart through the isomorphism of inverse image opens. The boundary indices and their distinct assigned coordinates are unchanged. Pullback preserves unit ideals, and each coordinate ideal pulls back to the same coordinate ideal of the transported chart. These are the required local normal crossing presentations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_projectio: Take the boundary conclusion of the simultaneous induction on stage smoothness and strict normal crossings at the specified valid stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: The original scheme is Noetherian by admissibility, and the initial stage is isomorphic to it. Induct along the sequence. At each actual step the transition is a blowup of the preceding Noetherian scheme, hence its source is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_succ: The successor projection to the base is the transition map followed by the preceding projection. Compose with the base field map and associate the arrows to obtain the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_zero: The stage-zero projection to the original ambient is its chosen isomorphism. Composing with the original structural map gives the stage-zero structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_and_inStrictNormalCrossingPositio: Induct on the stage. Initially the scheme is identified with the original one, transferring smoothness and the strict normal crossing condition of the initial boundary. At a successor the preceding ambient is smooth and its boundary has strict normal crossings by induction. The center is in strict normal crossing position with that boundary and the transition is its blowup. The smooth blowup theorem gives a smooth successor structure map. Since the successor is Noetherian, the boundary blowup theorem gives strict normal crossing position for the strict transforms of the old boundary with the exceptional ideal appended. The stage formulas identify these with the desired structure morphism and boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToSpec: The simultaneous induction on ambient smoothness and the boundary condition supplies smoothness at every stage in the allowed range. Take its smoothness conclusion at this stage.
