Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_baseField: The transformed marked ideal retains the original base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_boundary: The transform takes the boundary list from the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_dim: The transform's dimension index depends only on its ambient scheme, which is the scheme at the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_dim_le: Dimension nonincrease along blowups bounds the dimension index of the specified stage by the original one. The transform uses exactly that stage as its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_ideal: The ideal of the transformed datum is the ideal assigned to that stage in the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_mult: Transforming the marked ideal retains its marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_scheme: The transform uses the ambient scheme of the specified blowup stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_structureMorphism: The structure map of the transform is the map from the specified stage to the field spectrum.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPullbackBlowupSequence.prepend_of_coma: Choose a comparison for the original pullback relation. The new target center pulls back to the unit ideal, so the target's initial stage is omitted by the comparison. Shift its old matching indices by one, retaining the source sequence and its maps. The constructed comparison then witnesses the claimed pullback relation.

Choose a comparison witnessing the original pullback relation. Extend it by matching the new initial stages and shifting the old matching indices by one. The given blowup identifications and nonunit pullback ideal supply the new first step, and the established stage comparisons verify the pullback relation for the extended sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.prepend: The two sequences originally have equal lengths, so their lengths remain equal after adding one step to each. Use the base-change morphism at the new initial stage and the old levelwise map at each later stage. The initial compatibility holds because the new base identifications are identities. The first step square is the old initial compatibility square, whose vertical maps are the old initial isomorphisms, hence it is a pullback. Each later step is an old pullback square. The first centers are related by pullback by their choice, and the later centers inherit the given center relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_comparisonMapOfComap: At the two consecutive source indices the comparison maps agree with the old ones. The target transition between their shifted images equals the old transition between the unshifted images. The desired commutativity is then the old step commutativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_prependComparisonMap: At the new initial step, the two transitions down to zero identify with projections from the relevant old stages. The square commutes because the old comparison at stage zero commutes with those projections and the base-change map. At each later step, remove the shift by one from both sets of indices. The resulting square is an original comparison square for a source transition, which commutes by assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_prepend_center_succIndex: At the new target index the center is the old target center, because that index was shifted up by one. The new comparison uses the old comparison under the same target identification. Transport the original equality that pulls this center back to the source center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_prepend_comap_eq_top: The source sequence stays at its original stages in this construction. At each genuine source step the nonunit condition is already part of the original pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_comp_eqToHom_of_heq: Identify the two target schemes by their specified equality. The two target ideals then become equal, and the equality-induced map in the composite is an identity. The resulting pullback equality is the assumed one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_eqToHom_comp_comp_eqToHom: Use the specified identifications of the source and target schemes. Under these identifications the two transported ideal sheaves are the originally given ideal sheaves, and the extra maps on either side of the pullback morphism are identities. The equality is then the assumed pullback equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eqToHom_refl: The equality-induced map from the target to itself is its identity. The right identity law then leaves the original morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eq_comp_of_heq: Identify the four objects using the given equalities. The four equalities between arrows with initially different types are now ordinary arrow equalities. Substituting them identifies the two composites with the two routes in the prescribed commuting square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comparisonMapOfComapEqTop_eq_map: The two target stage descriptions identify the same scheme. Consequently the new comparison is the old comparison followed by the identity of its target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_comp_eqToHom_refl: An identification from an object to itself induced by equality is its identity morphism. Remove the identity on each side of the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_conj_comp_eq_comp_of_heq_id: Substitute the two object identifications. Each of the given arrows then equals the identity of its corresponding scheme, and the identification maps also become identities. Both composites reduce to the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_comparisonMapOfComapEqTop: The new comparison map is the original map with its target identified with the shifted stage. The projection of that shifted stage is the old projection. Under these identifications the square is the original pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_congr: Replace all four morphisms by their specified equals. The resulting square is the given pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_prependComparisonMap: Split the index into zero and a successor. At zero the comparison square is the identity square for the base-change morphism. At a successor it is the square of the corresponding original comparison. Both squares are pullbacks.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_prependComparisonMap_succ: At shifted stage n+1, the comparison is the old comparison at n. The projections on its source and target are the two original projections from the corresponding stages. Hence the new square is the old pullback square at n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_prependComparisonMap_zero: The top and bottom of the new initial square are the base-change morphism, and both vertical maps are identities. This is a pullback, since any compatible pair of maps factors uniquely through the upper left object by its given map to the lower left object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length_of_succ_le_prepend_length: Express the new length as the old length plus one. Cancel one from the two sides of the assumed inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ne_projectionToBase_of_forall_prependInd: The inserted target index zero is used by the inserted source index zero, so an omitted target index must have the form n+1. If old index n occurred in the original comparison, its matching shifted source index would hit n+1. Thus n was omitted originally. The center and projection at the shifted stage agree with those at old stage n, so the original omission condition excludes any equality with a base-change point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ne_projectionToBase_of_forall_succIndex_: If the omitted target stage is zero, its center is the new ideal and its projection is the identity. A point of the source mapping to its support would belong to the support of the pulled-back ideal, impossible because that ideal is the unit ideal. If the omitted stage is n+1, the old index n was omitted, since all original comparison indices are shifted by one. The shifted center and projection are the old ones, so the old omission condition applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependComparisonMap_succ: The stage n+1 on the source identifies with old stage n, and its target identifies with the original image of n. The new comparison is the original comparison there composed with these identifications, which are identity maps on the identified objects.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependComparisonMap_zero: The maps identifying the two new initial stages with their base schemes are identities. The stage-zero comparison is therefore the base-change morphism with an identity on either side.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependIndex_length_eq_prepend_length: The new source length is the old source length plus one. The shifted index evaluated there takes the old index at the old source length and adds one. This is the old target length plus one, which is the new target length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependIndex_lt_prependIndex_succ: The shifted value at zero is zero, while the next value is positive. At a later stage n+1 below the new source length, n is below the old source length. The original comparison strictly increases from n to n+1. Adding one to both values keeps that inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependIndex_lt_prepend_length: The new index is zero at stage zero, and the new target length is positive. At stage n+1 below the new source length, n is below the old source length. Its original image is below the old target length, and adding one gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependIndex_succ: After the inserted initial stage, the shifted index function applies the original function at the preceding index and adds one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prependIndex_zero: The shifted index function is defined to send the newly inserted initial stage to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_blowupMorphism_succ: Conversion to sequences represents adjacent transitions by their stored maps. At index n+1, the prepended data store the same map as the original data at n, so the two sequence transitions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_blowupMorphism_zero: Conversion preserves adjacent maps and the initial isomorphism. The stored first transition of the prepended data is the old initial isomorphism's forward map, which gives the asserted transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_blowupMorphism_zero_eq_projectio: The new initial adjacent map is the original initial isomorphism to the base. The old projection at zero is also that isomorphism, since its stage-zero transition is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_eq_comap_prependIndex: At stage zero the two new centers are the chosen ideal and its pullback under the base-change morphism, which is the initial comparison map. At stage n+1 the two centers and the comparison map identify with those of the original comparison at n. Its center pullback equality supplies the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_ne_top: At the new stage zero, the center is the assumed nonunit pullback ideal. At each later index below the new length, the center is an old center at an index below the old length. Its ideal is nonunit by the original comparison property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_succ: The prepended data at stage n+1 use the old center at stage n. Conversion to sequences preserves both centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_center_zero: The prepended data place the chosen ideal at the new initial center. Conversion to a sequence retains that center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_isoObjZero_hom: Conversion keeps the chosen initial isomorphism of the data. In prepended data it is the identity isomorphism of the base, so its forward map is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_length: Both conversions to sequences retain the lengths of their input data. Prepending adds one transition to the original data, so it also adds one to the sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_projectionToBase_succ: For the first shifted stage, the new first transition is the old initial isomorphism and the new projection from stage zero is the identity. This gives the old projection at zero. Inductively, the next shifted transition is the corresponding old transition, and composing with the preceding projection preserves the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_schemeAt_succ: Stage n+1 of the prepended data is stage n of the original data. Both conversions to sequences preserve the stage objects, giving the claimed identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_schemeAt_zero: Converting the prepended data to a sequence preserves all stage objects. The data at the new stage zero use the base scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_toSequenceOfBlowups_projectionTo: Convert both projections to the projections of their respective data. For the prepended data the projection from stage n+1 is the old projection from stage n, as shown by their common recursion.
The conversion from data to a blowup sequence keeps the projection to the base. At the new stage zero that projection is the forward map of the identity isomorphism, hence is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_transitionMap_succ_self: For consecutive indices the general transition is the adjacent blowup transition. The adjacent transitions after the new initial step are the old adjacent transitions shifted by one, which proves the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_transitionMap_succ_succ: Induct on the distance from a to b. At distance zero both transitions are identities. At the successor, factor each transition through its penultimate stage. The first factors agree by the result for adjacent steps, and the remaining factors agree by induction. Composing gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prepend_transitionMap_zero: The projection to the base is the transition to stage zero followed by the new initial isomorphism. That isomorphism is the identity, so the transition and projection are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPrependComparisonMap_succ: After the inserted initial stage, stage n+1 identifies with old stage n in both sequences. The new map is the old levelwise map at n composed with the identity on each of those identified stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPrependComparisonMap_zero: The newly inserted stages are the two base schemes. Their identifications with those bases are identities, leaving the base-change morphism as the levelwise map at stage zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succIndex_apply: The successor shift adds one to the original index value at every argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succIndex_length_eq_prepend_length: The original index function sends the original source length to the original target length. Adding one gives the new target length since only the target was prepended.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succIndex_lt_prepend_length: An index below the original source length has image below the original target length. Add one to both sides and identify the new target length as the original length plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succIndex_lt_succIndex_succ: The original comparison indices strictly increase at this step. Adding one to each of the two successive values preserves the strict inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_id: The exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back along the morphism. With the identity morphism this pullback equals the center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_singleBlowupRes: At the only active index, zero, the exceptional ideal is the center pulled back to the blowup, and the preceding ideal is the original ideal. The successor ideal is chosen as a residual factor. The assumed divisibility ensures that multiplying this factor by the exceptional power gives the pulled-back original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_singleBlowu: The only index in range is zero. The initial projection is the identity and pulling back the original boundary along it leaves the list unchanged. Thus the crossing condition is exactly the original hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_singleBlowupMap: The only index below one is zero. At that index the map is the canonical blowup projection of the given ideal, which has the required blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_id_list_idealSheafData: Pullback along the identity fixes every ideal. Applying it in order to every entry therefore returns the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_blowupMorphism_zero: The transition at zero is defined to be the canonical map from the blowup of the given center to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_boundary_one: At the positive stage the boundary consists of the strict transforms of the original list followed by the exceptional ideal of the blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_center_zero: The center assignment uses the given ideal at the initial stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_ideal_one: The ideal at the positive stage is defined by taking a residual factor of the pulled-back original ideal with respect to the indicated power of the pulled-back center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_length: The sequence data are defined with one active transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_projectionToBase_one: The projection at the first positive stage is defined as the blowup projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_schemeAt_succ: The scheme assignment uses the blowup scheme at every positive index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_schemeAt_zero: The scheme at index zero is defined to be the given original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_mul_residualByPow: The hypothesis supplies a residual ideal whose product with the given power is the original ideal. The residual construction chooses one such ideal, so it satisfies that identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupBoundary_succ: There is only one active transition. The initial boundary is the original list, since its defining pullback is along the identity. The boundary on the blowup is defined by taking its strict transforms and appending the exceptional ideal, giving the successor identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupCenter_support_subset_orderA: The bound on the index forces it to be zero. There the center is the given ideal and the stage ideal is the original ideal pulled back along the identity. The asserted support containment is therefore the given order condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupProj_succ: At index zero the transition is the blowup projection and the preceding projection is the identity on the original scheme. At any later index the transition is the identity on the blowup and the preceding projection is the blowup projection. Both composites give the stated successor projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_singleBlowupCenter_of_smooth: The only active center is at index zero, and its stage projection is the identity. Its composite field map is the given smooth center map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleComponentsDisjointOfSmooth: Every local ring of the smooth scheme over the field is a domain. If two irreducible components met at a point, the local ring there being a domain would force the two components to be equal. Thus distinct components are disjoint.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.IsAdmissible.isN: The field spectrum is Noetherian. Admissibility makes the structure morphism locally of finite type and quasi-compact, so the source is Noetherian by the finite-type theorem over a Noetherian base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ideal_le_ideal_succ: The controlled-transform identity expresses the pulled-back ideal as the product of an exceptional factor and the successor ideal. An ideal product is contained in each factor, so the pulled-back ideal is contained in the successor ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_succ_apply: The successor projection is the transition to the preceding stage followed by its projection to the base. Evaluating the composite on the given point yields the displayed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: The projection at stage zero is the zero-stage transition followed by the chosen initial isomorphism. The transition from zero to itself is the identity because the sequence is a functor. Thus the projection is the chosen isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ideal_succ_subset_preimage: The pulled-back old ideal is contained in the successor ideal. Support reverses inclusion of ideals, so the successor support lies in the support of the pulled-back old ideal. The latter is the inverse image of the old support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendObjIsoRight_congr: Substitute the equality of the two tail indices. The stage comparisons then use the same scheme identifications and the same tail isomorphism. The proofs of the bounds do not affect the resulting map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendObjIsoRight_hom: At a positive stage of the appended tail, the isomorphism first identifies the source with the relevant stage of the first tail, applies the given stage isomorphism, and uses the inverse identification with the appended target. The forward map is their composite by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendObjIso_eq_right_of_pos: Writing the stage as the common length plus a positive j places it after the join. The definition there uses the shifted index given by subtracting the common length, which is j. Substitute this equality in the tail comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendObjIso_hom_of_le: For a stage at or before the joining index, both appended schemes are identified with the same stage of the common sequence. The definition uses these identifications to compare them, so its forward map is the asserted equality-induced map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_isomorphic_of_iso:
The tails have equal length, so both appended sequences have equal length. Compare stages through the join using their identifications with the common prefix. At later stages use the given tail isomorphisms at shifted indices. At stage zero both comparisons preserve the initial isomorphism of the prefix.

For a step before the join, the maps and center ideals come from the common prefix, so the comparisons commute with the maps and preserve centers by transport. At the join, the transition map is the first tail map followed by its initial identification. The given first transition square and agreement of initial isomorphisms make those composites commute. Their inverse-identification formula likewise gives equality of the transported first tail centers. Afterwards the commuting squares and center equalities are exactly the given tail comparisons with indices shifted. This gives an isomorphism of the appended sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_isomorphic_of_isomorphic:138: Extract the equal lengths, stage isomorphisms, initial compatibility, commuting transitions, and center identities from the isomorphism of the tail sequences. Their underlying blowup data have the same lengths and maps as the displayed sequences. Apply the append isomorphism construction to these data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_isomorphic_of_isomorphic:158: Forget the marked data in the given isomorphism of the tails. The underlying blowup data of a marked append are the append of the underlying blowup data. Apply invariance of append under isomorphism of its second sequence and read the result as the isomorphism of the two underlying marked appends.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.projectionToBase_toSe: The projection of the reconstructed sequence is the projection in its data. Those data were formed using the original sequence's projection, so the two agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.toSequenceOfBlowups_o: Converting the sequence to data records its length, and constructing a sequence from the data uses that recorded length. The round trip therefore preserves length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_map_of_ofSequenceOfB: Apply the commuting step relation in the reconstructed sequences, using equality of lengths for its bound. Their successor and longer transitions are the original transitions. The transported comparison maps are also the given comparison maps, so substituting these equalities gives the required relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_transportedMap: Use equality of lengths to apply the reconstructed center formula at j. The original center ideals and comparison map agree with the reconstructed ones after transport. The formula therefore gives the original center as the asserted pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_pullback_ofSequenceOfBl: The original step lies within the reconstructed length, which is the same length. Its center is the same ideal as the reconstructed center, which differs from the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ofSequenceOfBlowups_eq_comap: The reconstructed center ideals are the original ones, and the comparison map is the original map because the inserted scheme identifications are identities. The bound on j is unchanged by reconstruction. Apply the original pullback equality for centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ofSequenceOfBlowups_ne_top: The given reconstructed step is an original step because the lengths agree. Its center is the original center and hence differs from the unit ideal by the supplied pullback property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_refl_comp_comp_eqToHom_refl: The maps induced by the two self-equalities are identities on their respective schemes. Composing f with these identities gives f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_index_succ_of_lt_length: Translate the original index bound using preservation of length. Strict increase for the reconstructed matching gives the same strict increase at the original index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_index_succ_of_lt_length_ofSeque: The reconstructed length equals the original length, so j is an actual step in the original sequence. Strict increase of the matching indices there gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_ofSequenceOfBlowups_length: The strict bound in the reconstructed source sequence is the same strict bound in the original source. Its matched index lies before the original target length, which equals the reconstructed target length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_ofSequenceOfBlowups_length: Replace the two reconstructed lengths by the original lengths. The index at the original endpoint is the original target endpoint by the pullback data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_congr: The two upper marked objects have the same scheme and field. Substituting the equal structure maps, ideals, markings, and boundaries makes them the same object. The assumed pullback relation for its assigned sequence is then the required relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_congr: Substitute the four equalities of the arrows. The second square then has the same arrows as the square known to be a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_projectionToBase_ofSequenceOf: The comparison map in the reconstructed square is the original comparison map under the stage identifications, and both projections are the original projections. Substitute these equalities into the original pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_transportedMap: Transport preserves the comparison map and both stage projections agree with those of the reconstructed sequences. The reconstructed pullback square therefore supplies the pullback square for the original stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length_of_le_ofSequenceOfBlowups_leng: The length after conversion to data and back equals the original sequence length. Substitute this equality into the given bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ofSequenceOfBlowups_length_of_le_leng: Conversion to data and back preserves length. The original upper bound for j therefore also bounds it in the reconstructed sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_blowupMorphism_comp_: The reconstructed length gives the same bound on the step as the original length. The reconstructed step, comparison maps, and transition between matching indices are the corresponding original maps. Substitute these identifications and use the original compatibility of transitions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_index_length: The matching sends the endpoint of the reconstructed source to the endpoint of the reconstructed target. Both reconstructed lengths equal their original lengths, giving the endpoint formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_index_lt_length: Translate the original source index bound to the reconstructed source. The matching index is then strictly below the reconstructed target length, which equals the original target length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_map_eq: The stage schemes are unchanged by conversion to data and back. The equality-induced maps inserted on both sides of the original comparison are consequently identities. Cancelling them gives the original comparison map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_ne_of_mem_unmatched_: The reconstructed lengths identify both the given target step and the set of source steps with the originals. Its center and projection to the base also agree with the originals. The omission condition then says that the projection of the given center point differs from the image of every point of the new base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_projectionToBase_ne: Use preservation of length to turn the original bounds and unmatched condition into the corresponding reconstructed ones. The center support at the chosen stage is unchanged. Apply the reconstructed omission property and replace the reconstructed projection by the original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_toSequenceOfBlowups_: In each sequence the blowup morphism is the transition between consecutive stages. Equality of those transitions gives equality of the blowup morphisms.
The data record the original scheme at every stage, and the reconstructed sequence takes its stage scheme from the data. Composing the two identifications gives the original stage scheme.
The transition of the reconstructed sequence is the transition of the underlying data. The transition comparison identifies that data transition with the one in the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_transitionMap: Induct on the number of steps in the transition. A transition to the same stage is the identity in both descriptions. Adding one step composes the new blowup map with the previous transition. Conversion records the original blowup map, and the previous transitions agree by induction, so the longer transitions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toMarkedSequence_projectionToBase: The marked sequence and its underlying sequence use the projections of the original marked blowup data. Apply the projection comparison in the direction that identifies the sequence projection with the data projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportedMap_eq_map: The maps used to transport between the original and reconstructed stage schemes are induced by equalities and here are identities. Composing the reconstructed comparison map on either side with these identities leaves it unchanged.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionContinues_of_cont: Induct on the iteration index. At zero the iterate is the starting sequence. For a successor, if the previous iterate continued, apply induction to it. If the previous iterate stopped, the successor equals it and the assumed continuation of the successor gives continuation of that same previous iterate. Induction then again gives continuation at the start.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionTriple_isAdmissible: The final original marked object is admissible. The continuation condition makes the nonmonomial maximum s positive, and this maximum bounds the nonmonomial order on the original marked order locus. Apply the admissibility result for the sum of powers with marking equal to the original marking times s.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByCompanionIdeal_ideal_eq: At stage zero the continuation ideal is the original final ideal pulled back along the initial isomorphism of the companion sequence. At each successor both descriptions use the same blowup morphism, exceptional ideal, and original marking to form the residual. Induction identifies the two recursions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByCompanionIdeal_length: The continuation keeps the blowup data of the assigned companion sequence and endows them with the original marking. Its underlying length is unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendByCompanionIdeal_eq_append: The dimension bound allows the recursive call on the companion triple. The assigned blowup data are marked for the current original ideal and marking, so the recursive extension is the append of those data with that marking, which is the stated continuation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.foldr_ofFn_mul_eq_prod: For no entries, both products are the unit ideal. Adding one entry multiplies the first factor by the product of the remaining entries in each description. Induction on the number of entries gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_companionIdealReduction: The full companion reduction is its iteration starting from the nonmonomial reduction and run for the specified number of steps. The center theorem for every iterate applies at that number.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_companionIdealReductionIter: At iteration zero the center property is the one for the nonmonomial reduction. At a successor, a stopped iterate is unchanged and retains the property. If it continues, the initial nonmonomial reduction also continued when given as input to the companion iteration. Thus the marking is at least two. The induction hypothesis supplies the property on the existing sequence, and the theorem for the companion extension supplies it on the enlarged sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_extendByCompanionIdeal: The assigned companion sequence has nonempty centers because its triple is admissible and meets the dimension and order bounds. The continuation uses the same centers, and the marking at least two supplies its certificates. The companion extension is the append of this continuation. The required center property holds on the previous sequence by hypothesis and on the continuation by these verifications. Since it is invariant under isomorphisms, the append property gives it at every actual stage of the extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isInvariantUnderIso_hasPrincipalizationC: The pullback of the center under an isomorphism has nonempty support because the original center does. At marking at least two, the certificate is provided by the certificate clause for such markings. Together these give the center property for the transported data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyMonomialTriple_tripleAtLength_c: The final marked object is admissible by transform invariance. At a point of its marked order locus the nonmonomial order is zero. The local consequence of the monomial splitting therefore gives a neighborhood on which the ideal is a product of powers of the boundary ideals. The finite-product identity expresses that product in the form required for local monomiality. This proves the condition at each point of the locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_seqAtEnd_companionIdeal: At the final stage the original marked object is admissible and its ideal has the chosen monomial splitting. The nonmonomial order on the original marked locus is bounded by the positive maximum used to form the companion ideal. The comparison theorem for a marked sequence of that companion ideal therefore gives markedness of its blowup data for the original final ideal and marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomialOnOrderLocus_extendBy:
Let s be the positive current maximum on the marked locus. The companion triple is admissible and has dimension and order within the bounds for the assignment, so its assigned sequence resolves the companion ideal. At its last stage the strict nonmonomial order estimate makes the controlled nonmonomial transform have order below s throughout the marked locus of the controlled original ideal.

The continuation uses that original controlled ideal and the same final boundary. The transformed splitting and uniqueness on the admissible final object identify its nonmonomial factor with the controlled nonmonomial transform. This factor has bounded order, so the pointwise strict bound implies that its maximum on the marked locus is below s. The continuation has positive length. Thus the final data of the append are the continuation's final data transported along the stage identification, which preserves that maximum. This gives the required decrease.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomialOnOrderLocus_iter_add: At iteration zero the maximum is the starting maximum. If the successor iterate continues, the preceding iterate must also have continued, since a stopped iterate is fixed. By induction the preceding maximum plus its iteration index is bounded by the starting maximum. The extension strictly decreases the natural-number maximum, so the successor maximum plus the incremented index has the same bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomial_transport_eqToIso: Substitute the equality of the ambient schemes. The induced isomorphism is the identity, and transporting the marked data by the identity leaves them unchanged. The maximum assigned to those data therefore agrees.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_companionIdealReductionContinues_com: The full companion reduction runs for one more than the starting maximum on the marked locus. If it still continued, the bound for a continuing iterate would put its nonnegative maximum plus that number of iterations at most the starting maximum. The iteration count alone exceeds this bound, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empty_of_comap_iso: Pulling the ideal back along the isomorphism and then along its inverse returns the original ideal. The inverse map is smooth, so the image of the resulting order locus lies in the given empty locus. A set whose image is empty is empty, giving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_companionIdeal_le: The final marked object is admissible. Its nonmonomial factor has order at most its maximum s on the marked order locus, and the continuation condition makes s positive. The order bound for the sum of powers therefore applies to the companion ideal and gives the bound by the original marking times s.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_lastNonMonomialPart_companionIde: The full reduction has stopped, so its maximum nonmonomial order on the final marked locus is zero. The nonmonomial order has a finite global bound. The zero-maximum equivalence therefore makes the nonmonomial order zero at every point of that locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_lastNonMonomialPart_le_maxOrderN: The order of the last nonmonomial factor has a finite global bound. At any point of the last marked order locus it is therefore at most its maximum on that locus, by the supremum bound for orders on a set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.seqAtEnd_companionIdeal_length_pos: The companion triple is admissible, lies in the prescribed dimension range, and has order bounded by its marking. The assignment therefore resolves it. If its sequence had length zero, resolution would give emptiness of the order locus of the initial companion ideal after transport by the initial isomorphism. Emptiness then holds on the original final scheme as well. The two positive exponents in the companion ideal show that every nonmonomial order on the original marked locus would be strictly below its maximum s. The bounded-order supremum comparison would then give s < s, a contradiction. Hence the assigned sequence has positive length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_iso_hom_nonempty: Choose a point in the original support and take its inverse image under the isomorphism. Its forward image is the chosen point, so it lies in the support of the pulled back ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_le_mult_of_continues_after_nonMonomi: After the nonmonomial reduction, the nonmonomial order is strictly below the original marking at all points. Its orders are bounded, so its maximum on the remaining marked locus is also strictly below the marking. The continuation condition makes that maximum at least one. The marking, a natural number strictly above it, is therefore at least two.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_of_eq_length: Substitute the joining index. The map there is the first tail blowup followed by the tail's initial isomorphism, with the source and target transported to the appended stages by their identifications.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_eq_comap_concatComparisonM:
Before the join, both appended centers are transported from their prefixes. The prefix comparison pulls the lower center back to the upper one, and composition with the stage identifications gives the formula. After the join, apply the same argument to the tail centers at the shifted index.

At the join, the step bound makes the first tail center available. Both appended centers come from their stage-zero tail centers by the respective inverse initial isomorphisms. The tail's initial comparison respects the last map of the prefix. Consequently its center pullback identity transports to a center pullback along that last map between the joining schemes. The comparison for the append at the join is just that last map with the scheme identifications, so this is the required identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_eq_comap_concatObjIsoRight: At tail index zero, the appended center is the first tail center pulled back through the inverse initial isomorphism and then the join identification. Composition of pullbacks makes this exactly pullback along the stage comparison. At a positive index the appended center is the pullback of the tail center at the shifted index. That shift gives i, and the comparison is the same stage identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_of_eq_length: Substitute j equal to the first length. The appended center at the join is the initial tail center pulled back first by its inverse initial isomorphism and then by the join identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_isomorphic_of_length_eq_zero: Appending a length-zero tail does not increase the length. Through the last stage, identify each scheme of the append with its corresponding prefix scheme. The initial isomorphism, every transition within the length, and every center are transported from the prefix. These comparisons give an isomorphism of the underlying data sequences, and hence an isomorphism of the displayed sequences after forgetting the marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_length_eq_of_strictPullbackBlowup: Strict pullback gives equal lengths for the two prefixes and for the two tails. Conversion preserves those lengths. Each appended length is the sum of its prefix and tail lengths, so the sums agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_eq_last_of_eq_length: The specified index is the length of the first sequence, so it is in the part of the append that uses the first sequence's schemes. At that index the scheme is its last scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_eq_right_of_pos: A positive tail index puts j strictly after the join. At such an index the appended scheme equals the tail scheme at j minus the first length. The given index equality makes this difference i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_eqToHom_congr: Substituting the equality of indices identifies the two blowup maps. The comparison maps at their domains and codomains are induced by the same respective equalities, so the composites agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_eq_eqToHom_conj: Substitute equality of the indices. Both blowup maps are then the same, and the comparisons at their endpoints come from self-equalities, hence are identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_eqToHom_congr: Substitute the equality of the tail indices. The centers agree and the two comparison maps are induced by the same scheme equality, so the pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_comap_eq: After identifying A with B, both equality-induced maps become the identity. The left side is then the pullback along f followed by the identity pullback, which equals the right side.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_eq_comap_of_eq_comap: Replace J by the pullback of K under c. Pulling this back through the upper scheme identification is pullback of K along the resulting composite. On the other side the lower identification cancels its inverse in f, leaving that same composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_iso_hom_of_eq_comap: Replace J by the pullback along c. On the right the two self-equality maps are identities, and the inverse of β cancels its forward map after composing the pullbacks. Both sides are therefore the pullback of K along u followed by c.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iso_inv_eq_comap_of_comm_sq: The commuting square, after composing with the inverse isomorphisms, identifies the composite of the inverse upper isomorphism and u with G followed by the inverse lower isomorphism. Replace J by the pullback along u and combine successive pullbacks on both sides. The two composite maps are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eq_of_eq_of_eq: Substitute the two given equalities on the arrows. The asserted equality is then the original equality of composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatComparisonMap_eq_dite: Expand the definition of the comparison. Through the prefix endpoint it uses the transported prefix map. Beyond that endpoint it subtracts the prefix length and uses the transported tail map. These are the two displayed branches.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatComparisonMap_of_le: The index bound places the comparison in the prefix branch of the definition. There it identifies the source with the upper prefix stage, applies the prefix comparison, and transports to the corresponding appended lower stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatComparisonMap_of_not_le: The index lies after the join, so use the tail branch of the comparison. Its shifted index is a by the given equality. Substituting this index gives the composite of upper identification, tail comparison, and inverse lower identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatComparisonMap_zero_comp_isoObjZero: At zero the comparison for the append is the prefix comparison transported along the stage identifications, and the appended initial isomorphisms are the prefix ones under those identifications. These maps cancel in the composite by the transport rule. The original prefix comparison commutes with its initial maps, giving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjIsoRight_hom_comm_blowupMorphis: At a positive tail index the appended transition is the tail transition with its endpoint schemes identified by equalities. The matching index is i after subtracting the first length, so the two paths agree by composing these identifications. At tail index zero, the appended transition is the first tail transition followed by the tail's initial isomorphism and the join identification. The stage-zero comparison uses their inverses, which cancel and give the same first tail transition as on the other path.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjIsoRight_hom_of_pos: At a positive tail index, the comparison is defined by the equality between the appended scheme and the corresponding tail scheme. Its forward morphism is the one induced by that equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjIsoRight_hom_succ: The successor index is positive, so apply the formula for the forward comparison at a positive tail stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjIsoRight_hom_zero: At tail index zero, the appended scheme is the joining scheme. The comparison first uses this identification and then the inverse of the tail's initial isomorphism. The final index identification is an identity, so the forward map is the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjIsoRight_inv_of_pos: For a positive tail index the stage isomorphism is induced by the equality of the appended scheme and the tail scheme. Its inverse is induced by the reverse equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_append_iso: The empty prefix has length zero, so the appended sequence and the tail have equal lengths and matching stage indices. Use the isomorphisms from appended stages to tail stages, including the inverse tail initial isomorphism at zero. This makes the initial maps commute. The transition and center comparisons for an append identify each blowup map and center with those of the tail under these isomorphisms. The data comparison therefore gives an isomorphism of the underlying sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceData_toBlowupSe: The empty marked construction uses the empty blowup data of the starting scheme and adds only marked ideal and boundary data. Forgetting those data leaves the stated empty blowup data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.empty_isoObjZero: For the empty data the stage-zero object is the original scheme, and the initial identification is defined as its identity isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.empty_length: The empty blowup data record no steps. Their length is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.empty_schemeAt: The empty data use the original scheme at every index by their definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_eqToHom_conj_eq: The three successive source identifications induce the same morphism as the direct source equality. Likewise the three target identifications induce the direct target morphism. Cancel the intermediate transports by composing the equality-induced maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_conj_comp_eq_comp_of_heq: Identify the schemes using the specified equalities. The equalities between the structure maps then have common domains and identify those maps. All inserted equality-induced morphisms become identities, reducing the assertion to the given commuting composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_trans_comp_comp_eqToHom_trans: On either side of the middle map, the composite of the two equality-induced maps is the direct map for the resulting equality. Replace each pair by this direct map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_trans_comp_comp_eqToHom_trans_eq: The source identifications compose to the direct source comparison. The two target paths induce the same comparison between the same schemes, and associativity allows the middle morphism to be grouped with the first target map. The composites therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_comap_eqToHom_conj_of_heq: Substitute the scheme equalities first, so the ideals being compared are on the same schemes. Their heterogeneous equalities then identify the respective ideals, and the comparison maps from scheme equalities are identities. The assertion becomes the given pullback equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_iso_inv_comp_comp_hom_of_comm_sq: Using the commuting square, replace the composite of u with the target isomorphism by the source isomorphism followed by the old map. Precomposing with the inverse source isomorphism cancels that isomorphism. Transport at the two endpoints by the equalities to obtain the displayed formula for the same map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_blowupMorphism_of_strictPullb: The successor maps in the sequences are the blowup maps of the underlying data. Substitute these equalities in the step square of the strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_blowupMorphism_zero_of_strict: Specialize the pullback square for a blowup morphism to the first step, which exists by the positive length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_concatComparisonMap:
Strictness gives equal prefix lengths and equal tail lengths. Before the join, both transitions and both comparisons are those of the prefix under the stage identifications. The pullback square is therefore the transported prefix square. After the join the index shifts by the prefix length, and all four arrows come from the corresponding tail square. The tail pullback property transfers along the stage identifications.

At the joining step, the tail has positive length. Use its first pullback square. At the current stage, transport the tail's initial schemes through their initial isomorphisms to the joining schemes. Initial commutativity of the tail comparison identifies the transported comparison with the last comparison of the prefix. The first appended transitions are likewise the tail transitions composed with the initial isomorphisms, and the successor comparison uses the first positive tail stage. The resulting square is a transport of the first tail pullback square and is therefore a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_conj_eqToHom: Substitute the four scheme equalities. The corresponding morphisms are identities, so the given arrow equations identify each new arrow with the old one. The original pullback property then applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_conj_eqToHom_iso: Substitute the two scheme equalities. The relevant comparison maps become identities. Apply invariance of a pullback square under the remaining two vertex isomorphisms, using the stated formulas for its four arrows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_conj_iso: The four vertex isomorphisms identify the arrows of the new square with the transported arrows of the original square. The equalities make all four diagrams commute by cancellation of inverse isomorphisms. Transporting the pullback universal property through these isomorphisms proves that the new square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_toSeqComparisonMap: The step bound is unchanged by conversion, and the converted comparison maps agree with the data maps under the stage identifications. The successor maps in the sequences are the blowup morphisms in the data. With these identifications, the given pullback square for the data is the required square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_append:809: Use the comparison assembled from the prefix and the tail. The appended lengths agree, the comparison respects the initial maps, each step square is a pullback, and the centers pull back under the comparison. These properties give the strict pullback of the two appended sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_append:897: The marked append has the append of the underlying blowup data as its unmarked sequence. The two given strict comparisons are the comparisons of those underlying prefixes and tails. Apply the strict pullback theorem for appended blowup data to obtain the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastMap_eq: The last comparison is defined by the comparison at the final upper index followed by the identification of the lower scheme at that index with the lower final scheme. Equality of the lengths gives this identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSequenceOfBlowups_toSequenceOfBlowups_: The sequence recovered from its data has the same length and the same scheme at every stage. Compare stages by the identity. The initial isomorphism and each transition map were preserved, so the required diagrams commute. The centers were also preserved, and pulling back by each identity fixes them. These identities give the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullback_map_eqToHom_congr: Substitute the equality of indices to use the same comparison map. The successive equality maps on each side of that comparison compose to the direct equality map, giving the same composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullback_map_eq_lastMap_of_eq: Substitute a equal to the last upper index. By definition the last map is the comparison at that index followed by the equality identification of the two lower endpoint indices. Composing with its inverse cancels this extra identification, giving the endpoint comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSeqComparisonMap_zero_comp_isoObjZero: The conversion of the comparison map adds only equality-induced identities at stage zero, so it equals the original stage comparison. The initial isomorphisms of the sequences are also the original ones. Substituting these observations gives the assumed initial commutativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_center_eq_comap_toSe: At the given index, both sequence centers are the centers of their underlying data, and the comparison map is the data map transported along the stage equalities. Transport the assumed center pullback equation along these equalities to obtain the statement for the converted sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_isomorphic_of_iso: Converting the two sets of data to sequences preserves their lengths, stage schemes, initial identifications, successor maps, and centers. Use the given stage isomorphisms. The assumed compatibility with the initial maps, commuting transition squares, and pullback identities for centers therefore give all the conditions of a sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_length_eq_of_length_: Conversion from data to sequences preserves both lengths. The given equality of lengths therefore gives equality of the sequence lengths.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.controlledMonomi: At a successor stage the recursion pulls back the previous monomial factor, multiplies by the c-th exceptional power, and takes the residual by the a-th exceptional power.
At stage zero the monomial transform is defined to be the original monomial factor pulled back by the initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.controlledNonMon: The successor rule pulls the previous nonmonomial ideal back along the next blowup and takes its residual by the c-th power of the exceptional ideal.
The recursion starts by pulling the nonmonomial ideal back to stage zero along the initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_eq_comap_ofMar: The controlled transforms on the marked sequence and on its underlying data agree at the given stage. Pull both ideals back along the next transition, which is the same morphism in both descriptions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_eq_ofMarkedSequence_: Both recursions start by pulling back the same ideal through the same initial isomorphism. At each successor they pull back the preceding ideal by the same blowup map and take the residual by the same exceptional power. Induction gives equality at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_exceptionalDivisor_pow_mul_eq_com: At the current stage the companion ideal is the sum of the two transformed powers. On the center its order is at least ms, so the minimum formula and positivity of both exponents give order at least s for the nonmonomial transform and at least m for the original transform. The bound for the nonmonomial transform on the latter locus gives equality with s. Thus the center lies in the two required order loci. Normal crossings gives containment of the two transformed ideals in the respective powers of the center ideal. On the blowup these containments give factorizations by the powers of the exceptional ideal. The monomial splitting and exact order s on the center now supply the third factorization for the weighted pullback of the monomial factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_withIdealAndMult_pow_sup_po: The sum-of-powers order estimate gives the global bound by ms, where m is the original marking. Outside the support of the original ideal, its order is zero. The order of the sum of powers is the minimum of the two weighted orders and is therefore also zero there. Its support lies in the original support, so it contains no irreducible component. The new marking is positive because both factors are positive. All conditions on the scheme, structure map, and boundary are inherited, giving admissibility and the asserted bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_ofMarkedSequence_of_isMonomialS: Smoothness of the centers and their normal crossing position depend on the existing blowup maps and boundaries, and so are inherited. For each center, the companion comparison gives divisibility of the pulled back original transform by the original marking's exceptional power. It also places the center inside the order locus of the original transform at that marking. The controlled transform computed in the underlying data agrees with the one computed in the marked sequence, so these are the required divisibility and order conditions. The underlying sequence is therefore marked for the original object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_controlledTransform_:
Write m for the original marking. At stage zero the initial isomorphism preserves order, carries the given monomial splitting to stage zero, and preserves sums and powers of ideals. This gives the companion formula, the splitting, and the bound on the nonmonomial order.

At a successor step, the companion formula identifies its current marked order locus with the intersection of the original transform's locus at m and the nonmonomial transform's locus at s. The induction bound forces the nonmonomial order to equal s on the center. Power containment for a center with strict normal crossings gives the divisibilities needed to remove exceptional powers m and s from the original and nonmonomial transforms. The monomial-factor divisibility theorem supplies the remaining factor after multiplying its pullback by the s-th exceptional power and dividing by the m-th. The exceptional divisor is Cartier, so these residuals satisfy the factorization identities. Applying the transform theorem to those identities gives the successor splitting. Raising the two residual identities to powers s and m, adding, and cancelling the common exceptional power ms gives the successor companion formula.

On the exceptional divisor the controlled-transform estimate bounds the new nonmonomial order by s. Off the exceptional divisor the removed factor has order zero and order of the total pullback agrees with order at the image. A point of the new original order locus maps into the preceding original order locus, where the induction bound applies. This gives the bound everywhere on the new locus and closes the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledNonMonomialTransform_l: At the last stage the companion ideal is the sum of the m-th power of the nonmonomial transform and the s-th power of the original transform. Their positive exponents identify its order locus at ms with the intersection of their order loci at s and m, respectively. Emptiness of that intersection means the nonmonomial order is strictly less than s at every point of the original marked order locus.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderReductionHypotheses.of_strictTransf: Use the controlled-transform order bound for the first requirement. The strict-transform component property and the monomial case are already part of the supplied hypotheses and give the other two requirements directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le_of_orderA: Every center point has order c for J. The power containment theorem for a center with strict normal crossings gives J contained in the c-th power of the center ideal. The given factorization of the pulled back J identifies J′ with its controlled transform, by uniqueness of division by the exceptional power. A point on the exceptional divisor maps into the center and its image therefore has order exactly c. The controlled-transform order estimate at a point whose image has order at most c bounds the order of J′ there by c.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_comp_apply: The underlying point map of the composite acts by applying f first and then g. At x this gives the stated expression.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_mapToLastOfLengthEqZ: There is no index strictly below the upper length, which is zero. The step compatibility has an impossible premise.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_of_append_length_eq_: At each original upper step the stage identifications commute with the original transition and the corresponding transition of the append. The upper length is unchanged, so the given comparison commutes with that appended transition. Compose the two equalities to obtain the step compatibility with the transported maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_of_disjoint_centers: The upper sequence is empty, so the bound for an actual upper step is impossible. The transition compatibility consequently holds vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_of_length_eq_one: The length bound forces j to be zero. The consecutive transitions are the two given blowup maps, and the comparison maps are the initial comparison induced by g and the given stage-one map. Their commutativity is the equality of the two composites in the given pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_lastCenter_of_disjoint: The upper sequence has length zero, so it has no actual center to compare. The stated center equality holds vacuously at every index of an upper step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_lastCenter_of_disjoint_o: The length of the upper sequence is zero. There is no index below that length, so no center pullback identity needs to be checked.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_of_append_length_eq_zero: At each upper step the appended center is the pullback of the original upper center through the stage identification from the appended scheme. The original comparison to the lower center gives this appended center by pullback. Pull it back along the inverse stage identification to recover the original upper center. Composition of pullbacks gives the required transported map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_of_length_eq_one: Only j equal to zero is in range. The initial comparison is g transported through the starting isomorphisms, and both centers are the underlying stage-zero data. The assumed pullback equality of those centers is therefore the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_append_length_eq_zero: The appended center at an original step is a pullback of the original upper center. It differs from the unit ideal by hypothesis on the comparison. If the original center were the unit ideal, its pullback would be the unit ideal too, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_length_eq_one: The only possible step is zero. Converting to a sequence does not change its center, which is assumed to differ from the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_length_eq_zero: In a length-zero sequence there is no valid step index. Thus the nonunit condition on an actual center holds vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_comap_eqToHom: The two equality-induced morphisms are inverse to each other. The successive pullbacks equal pullback by their identity composite and fix the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_top_of_forall_support_not_mem_r: Commutativity of the square gives equality between the image of y under g and the projection of its image under u. If y lay in the support of the pulled back ideal, its image under u would be a point of the given support with this same projection. That contradicts the range-disjointness assumption. The pulled back support is empty, so the pulled back ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eqToHom_eq_eqToHom_comp: The formula for f′ conjugates f by the source and target identifications. Composing on the source with the inverse of the source identification cancels that factor, giving the displayed equality. This also follows by substituting both equalities and cancelling identity maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_centers_lastMap_of_append: If a tail center point had projected image equal to the image of a point under the last comparison map, transport that center point to the appended sequence at its shifted index. Its ambient projection is the lower prefix's last projection of the tail projection. Commutativity of the final pullback square then equates this ambient projection with the image of the upper point's projection under the original base map. This contradicts the range-disjointness assumption for the appended center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_omitted_centers_of_append_lengt: An index is unmatched for the original upper sequence exactly when it is unmatched for its append with a zero tail, because the lengths and matching indices agree. Apply the existing omission property for the append to the given lower center point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_omitted_centers_of_disjoint_cen: Conversion preserves the lower length, center support, and projection. An actual lower step therefore falls under the disjointness assumption, which excludes equality of its projected center point with the image of any new base point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_omitted_centers_of_length_eq_on: The only original step is at index zero, which is also the unique matched step of the upper sequence. The assumption that this index is unmatched contradicts the match at zero. The omitted-center assertion therefore has no applicable step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_base_mem_support_center: Substitute equality of the indices so the two centers agree. The equality-induced map on their stage scheme is the identity, so it preserves the given membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_base_self: The endomorphism induced by equality of A with itself is the identity, so its underlying map fixes x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_base_trans: The comparison induced by the composite equality is the composite of the two equality-induced morphisms. Evaluating at x gives the equality. Equivalently, substituting both equalities reduces both sides to x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_append_projectionToBase: Through the joining stage the appended projection is the original projection preceded by the identification of the appended scheme with the original scheme. The displayed map preceding it is the inverse identification, so the two cancel and yield the original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_eqToHom_comp_eq: The two comparisons induced by opposite scheme equalities cancel. The resulting identity before g leaves g unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_of_comap_eq_top: The second projection of the canonical pullback is an isomorphism. Use its inverse followed by the first projection to define the lift on Y. Transporting the canonical pullback square along that isomorphism gives the claimed square. Its commutativity shows that the lift followed by the blowup equals u.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_of_forall_comap_eq_top: At stage zero, compose g with the inverse of the starting isomorphism to obtain the pullback square. At a successor within the length, induction provides the lift to the previous stage. The hypothesis makes its center pullback the unit ideal, and the successor lifting theorem supplies the next lift and its pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_schemeAt_length_of_disjoint_: At each stage, any lift that gives a pullback square pulls the step's center ideal back to the unit ideal, by disjointness of the projected support. Apply the inductive lifting result with this property through the full length. It supplies a lift to the final scheme and its pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_succ_of_comap_center_eq_top: Apply the unit-center lifting theorem to the next blowup and the current map u. The resulting lift composes with the next blowup to u. Pasting its pullback square with the existing square gives the pullback over the original base, since the projection from the successor is the next blowup followed by the current projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_support_center_append: At tail index zero, transport the center point first along the tail's initial isomorphism to the joining scheme and then along the identification with the appended stage. The formula for the center at the join and the inverse-image rule for support put this point in the appended center. The projection formula gives the asserted image. At a positive tail index, the appended stage at the shifted index is identified directly with that tail stage. Transport the point by this identification. The shifted center formula preserves support membership, and the appended projection factors through the tail projection and the prefix's last projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_length_of_append_length_eq_zero: Appending a length-zero tail leaves the upper length unchanged. The existing matching sends that endpoint to the lower endpoint, and the index itself has not changed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_index_succ_of_append_length_eq_: The zero tail changes no length, so the given strict increase of indices for the append applies at every original upper step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_length_of_append_length_eq_zero: The original upper sequence and its append have the same length. Thus j is an actual step of the append, and the given comparison places its match strictly below the lower length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_strictMono_of_length_eq_one: A natural number is strictly less than its successor. This gives strict increase of the identity matching.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inv_base_hom_base: The inverse composed after the forward isomorphism is the identity. Evaluate this identity at x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullbackSnd_of_flat_of_disjoint: The given disjointness makes the center ideal pull back to the unit ideal on Y. This ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, so the blowup universal property gives a lift from Y to the next stage. Pair the lift with the identity of Y to obtain a map to the pullback. It is a right inverse to the projection to Y. For the other composite, the second projection agrees automatically, and the first agrees by uniqueness of blowup lifts because the center still pulls back to the unit ideal on the pullback. Hence the projection is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullback_snd_of_comap_eq_top: The center ideal on Y is the unit ideal, so the universal property of the blowup gives a lift of u. Pair this lift with the identity to obtain a map from Y to the pullback. Composing with its second projection yields the identity. The reverse composite agrees with the identity on the second projection, and also on the first by uniqueness of lifts to the blowup, since the center stays the unit ideal after further pullback. The two composites are therefore identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_chosenLiftToLastOfIsDisjointF: The lift is chosen from the existence theorem that includes its pullback property. The chosen lift therefore gives the claimed final square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_comp_isoObjZero_inv: The stage-zero projection is the initial isomorphism. Composing g with its inverse gives the commutative square with identity on Y. After exchanging the legs, the horizontal arrows are isomorphisms, so the square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_liftSuccOfIsDisjointFromCente: The pullback of the next blowup along the current lift is isomorphic to Y by the second projection.
