Under this isomorphism the first projection is the defined successor lift and the second is the identity. Paste this pullback square with the one for the current lift. The successor projection formula identifies the resulting outer square with the one asserted.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_mapToLastOfLengthEqZero: Only stage zero of the empty upper sequence is in range. Its comparison map is its initial isomorphism followed by the chosen lift to the last lower stage. The initial isomorphism gives a pullback over identity maps, and the lift gives a pullback over g. Pasting them yields the required square with the two stage projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_append_length_eq_zero: The original upper stage is isomorphic to the appended upper stage, and the two projections to the upper base commute with that identification. This identification gives a pullback square over the identity of the upper base. Paste it with the given pullback square for the append. The new comparison is the old one preceded by the identification, as required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_disjoint_centers: The only upper stage in range is zero. The lift to the last lower stage has a pullback square by the construction that lifts through the disjoint centers. Precompose with the upper initial isomorphism, whose square over Y is a pullback. The resulting pasted square has the stage-zero upper projection and the last lower projection. The comparison at zero is exactly the composite of the upper initial isomorphism with the lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_length_eq_one: There are only stages zero and one. At zero, the comparison map is g transported by the two initial isomorphisms. The stage-zero square commutes and is a pullback because the horizontal maps after exchanging the legs are isomorphisms. At stage one, paste the given comparison square of the blowup maps with that initial pullback square. The stage-one projections are the blowup maps followed by the initial isomorphisms, so the pasted square is the asserted one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length_append_of_length_eq_zero: The appended length is the original length plus zero, hence is the original length. This transfers the bound on j.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_of_length_eq_one: Converting either set of data to a sequence preserves length. Both lengths are one by hypothesis, so they agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_toSequenceOfBlowups_length: Passing from the data to its sequence uses the length recorded in the data. Reverse that length equality to obtain the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_lt_length_of_lt_length_of_eq_zero: Conversion preserves the zero length of e. There is consequently no j strictly below that length, so the implication follows from the impossible premise.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_lt_toSequenceOfBlowups_length_of_: The sequence of e has length zero, so no natural number is strictly below it. The proposed bound is vacuous.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_of_length_eq_one: The two sequence lengths are equal because both underlying lengths are one. Substitute that equality into the given index bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_append_of_disjoint_centers: Disjointness of the projected centers of the appended tail implies that its centers miss the image of the comparison map at the join. Pulling back the tail along this map gives an empty sequence on the upper last scheme, using the lift through all the disjoint centers. Concatenate this tail comparison with the existing comparison of prefixes. The new upper sequence is the old upper sequence followed by a zero-length tail. Remove that tail from the comparison to obtain the desired pullback with the original upper sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_base_eqToHom_base: Substitute the equality of indices. The two projections then agree, and the intermediate comparison sends z to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.schemeAt_eq_schemeAt_append: Through the original endpoint the appended data use the original stage schemes. The bound on j is the same for the original data and their sequence, so converting the two stage schemes gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.schemeAt_eq_schemeAt_zero_of_length_eq_z: The sequence obtained from the data has length zero. An index bounded by zero is zero, and the stage-zero scheme is the stage-zero object of the data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeCompatible_baseChangeProj_of_i: The field extension projection is flat and preserves order in all test squares. The comparison for the order-reduction assignment gives the required rule. Flatness and the order invariance supply the comparison for monomial principalization, and flatness gives the pullback formula for the nonmonomial part. These properties are the components of the asserted base-change compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_hom_comap_inv_eq_self: The two successive pullbacks equal pullback along the forward map followed by the inverse map. This composite is the identity on the original scheme, so the ideal is unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.commutesWithBaseChange_baseChangeProj_of:
The pasted square identifies the upper scheme with the direct extension of the lower scheme to the new field. Its canonical isomorphism commutes with both projections. Transport the chosen upper boundary along the inverse isomorphism. This boundary is equivalent to the direct field-change boundary because pullbacks compose and remove unit ideals in the same way. Admissibility and the dimension bound persist under transport, and the order bound follows from order invariance under field extension and along the isomorphism. The lower dimension bound follows from the marked square.

Apply the field-change property of the assignment on the direct field extension. The isomorphism from the upper scheme is smooth and surjective, so the strict smooth pullback property compares its assigned sequence to the sequence on the direct field extension. Pullbacks in the two directions of the isomorphism cancel on the boundary, and the ideal and structure-map identities identify the transported object with the given upper one. Composing the two sequence comparisons and identifying the composite projection with the original vertical map gives the desired pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_comap_of_iso: An isomorphism preserves smoothness and quasi-compactness of the structure map and gives local finite type for the transported map. It also carries irreducible components and the strict normal crossing configuration to their counterparts, preserving nonvanishing and the crossing condition. The field and positive marking are unchanged. These are all the admissibility requirements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_of_eq_of_heq: First substitute the equality of the marked objects so that the two maps have the same domain. The given equality of those maps then has a common type. Substituting it makes the pullback statement exactly the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_comp_baseChangeStructMap: Paste the marked square with the defining pullback square for the extension of the ground field. The lower composite is the lower object's structure map by its compatibility with the original structure map. The pasted square is therefore the claimed field-extension pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_of_iso: The scheme isomorphism induces a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces. Topological Krull dimension is invariant under homeomorphism, and applying the same successor and natural-number conversion gives equality of the stated dimensions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_congr: The scheme and field are fixed. Substituting the equalities of the structure maps, ideals, markings, and boundaries makes the two marked objects equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.monomialPrincipalizationBaseChange_of_fl: In the marked pullback square the vertical map is flat, and the test-square order invariance for the original map passes to that vertical map by pasting. Use the flat pullback theorem for monomial principalization with this order invariance, the two locally monomial objects, and the equivalence between the pulled back boundary and the upper boundary. It gives the required comparison of their sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPartBaseChange_of_flat: The vertical map in each marked pullback square is flat. Choose a monomial splitting of the lower ideal using admissibility. Its pullback is a splitting for the pulled back boundary, and equivalence of boundaries makes it a splitting for the designated upper boundary. Uniqueness on each admissible object identifies the chosen nonmonomial parts with these lower and upper factors. The upper factor is the pullback of the lower factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_eq_of_isMonomialSplittin: The given splitting witnesses existence, so the definition selects some pair that also satisfies the splitting condition. By uniqueness, its second entry is N. That entry is the defined nonmonomial part.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtPullbackInvariant_verticalMap: Given a test pullback square for the vertical map, paste it with the marked pullback square. Its composite lower map respects the structure map by commutativity of the two structure triangles. Use the original marking on the test lower scheme, keeping its geometric and ideal data and taking positivity from the admissibility of T. The original order invariance then applies to the pasted square and gives the needed equality for its left projection.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MonomialStrictTransformComponents.transf: The boundary-intersection theorem describes the transformed components for a blowup along the specified ideal sheaf. The strict-transform component theorem supplies the description of each irreducible component by the closure of a point off the exceptional locus. Together they give the two required component properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationGeometryHypotheses: Begin with the two component properties for transformed boundaries and strict transforms. These supply the residual hypotheses for the monomial strict-transform construction, which in turn give the strict-transform and monomial case hypotheses. Add the controlled-transform order estimate to obtain the order-reduction hypotheses. The construction of principalization geometry from those hypotheses then gives the claimed result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_center_mapToEarlierScheme_eq_top_o: The bound on the matched index puts i within the original steps. If the pulled back center had a point in its support, its image in stage i would be a center point. Its further image in the initial scheme lies in the image of the base map because the comparison commutes with projections. This contradicts the omission property for an unmatched step. The pulled back support is therefore empty and the ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comp_eqToHom: After substituting the equality of indices, the induced comparison between the schemes is the identity and the two stage ideals are the same. The composite is simply f, giving equal pullbacks.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ideal_boundary_succ_of_comap_cente: On W the pullback of the center ideal is the unit ideal. Pulling back the controlled-transform factorization therefore removes the exceptional power, leaving equality of the old ideal pulled back through the transition and the new ideal pulled back directly. Every strict transform pulls back to the pullback of its original ideal because W lies off the center support. The new exceptional entry pulls back to the unit ideal, which disappears from the nontrivial boundary. This gives the boundary equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_map: The matched stage comparison occurs in a pullback square for the given flat base map. Therefore it is flat by stability under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_boundary_last_eq_comap_lastMap:
First fix a stage of the pulled back sequence and compare pullbacks of the original ideal and boundary between two earlier stages separated only by unmatched steps. At each such step the center pulls back to the unit ideal, so the one-step formulas give equality of ideals and equivalence of boundaries. The maps to successive earlier stages compose through the original transition, so induction along the interval gives the comparison for the entire run of unmatched steps.

Next induct over the pulled back stages. At zero, the initial ideal and boundary comparison, together with the projection formula, identifies the pulled back data with the data from original stage zero. The unmatched-step comparison advances this to the first matched stage. For a successor, the two blowups at the current match form a pullback square and their exceptional ideals agree after pullback. Comparing the controlled-transform factorizations and cancelling the marked power of the exceptional ideal gives equality of successor ideals. Flat pullback commutes with strict transform, and the exceptional entries agree. Since the strict transform of a unit ideal is a unit ideal, the boundary equivalence also advances to the next original stage. Apply the unmatched-step comparison between that stage and the next matched index.

The last pulled back index matches the original last index. Transporting the stage comparison along that equality yields the stated ideal equality and boundary equivalence for the final map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_le_length: At a stage strictly before the end of the pulled back sequence the matched index is strictly smaller than the original length. At the last stage the matched index equals the original length. Both cases give the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_mono: Induct on the upper index b. At zero the two indices must agree. At b equal to n+1, if a is at most n, induction gives the comparison with the matched index of n, and strict increase then gives the comparison with the matched index of n+1. If a equals n+1 the comparison is reflexive.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_ne_of_index_lt_of_lt_index_succ: If a pulled back index is at most j, monotonicity puts its matched index at most the match of j and below i. If it is at least j+1, monotonicity puts its match at least the match of j+1 and above i. Thus no pulled back step matches i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_ne_of_lt_index_zero: Monotonicity makes the matched index at stage zero a lower bound on all matched indices. Since i is smaller, no actual step has i as its match.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_blowupMorphism: The matched original step is a blowup, and the new center is the pullback of its center under the flat stage comparison. Flat base change of blowup gives a comparison map from the new next stage to the original next stage making a pullback square. On the other hand, the compatibility of transitions shows that the map obtained by going back from the next matched stage also has the required composite to the original current stage. On the new scheme the pulled back center is locally generated by a nonzero divisor, since it is the exceptional ideal of its blowup. Uniqueness in the blowup universal property therefore identifies the two comparison maps. The stated square is the pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapToEarlierScheme_comp_projectionToBase: The projection from the earlier original stage composed with the transition from the matched original stage is the matched stage's projection. The pullback square at the matched stage then identifies the composite with the projection from the new stage followed by the original base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapToEarlierScheme_eq_comp_blowupMorphis: The transition from the matched stage down to i factors through i+1, followed by the single blowup map. Compose this factorization with the comparison map on the pulled back stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapToEarlierScheme_eq_map_comp_transitio: By definition, the map to the earlier stage first takes the pullback comparison map to the matched stage, then follows the original sequence's transition to the earlier index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapToEarlierScheme_index: At the matched index the extra transition goes from that stage to itself and is the identity. The composite is the original comparison map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_comp_eqToHom: Substitute the equality of indices to identify the two lists and make the last map in the composite the identity. Every entry is now pulled back along f on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedMapToEarlierScheme_comp_projection: The projections of the marked data are the underlying sequence projections. Apply the projection formula for the map to the earlier stage and identify those projections with the marked ones.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedMapToEarlierScheme_index: When the earlier index is the matched index itself, the underlying comparison is the ordinary stage comparison. The marked maps use these same morphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_append_top: The nontrivial boundary is obtained by deleting every unit entry. The appended unit is deleted, so the filtered list is the same as the original filtered list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_of_eq: Substitute the equality of the second and third lists in the boundary equivalence. The given equivalence then has the required form.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_pow_mul: The unit ideal is the multiplicative identity. Every power of it is the identity, which leaves J fixed under multiplication.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_verticalMap: The vertical map on the left is the base change of the given flat map on the right. Flatness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_verticalMap: Use the lower marked object with the marking of the original object T. It is admissible because its geometric and ideal conditions are unchanged and the marking of T is positive. The given order-pullback property now applies to the square, whose lower map respects the structure map. It identifies the order of the pulled back ideal with the order at the image point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_verticalMap_le: The order equality for the vertical map replaces the pulled back order by the order at the image in the lower scheme. The assumed bound applies at that image.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_dataAt_last: The second sequence has positive length, so the last appended stage lies after the join. Apply the formula for stages after the join. Subtracting the first length from the total leaves the length of the second sequence. Transport along the equal index gives the stated final data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_dataAt_length: At the joining stage the appended scheme is identified with the last scheme of the first sequence. The inverse of the second sequence's initial isomorphism transports its stage-zero ideal and boundary back to this last scheme. These are the last ideal and boundary of the first sequence, because the two initial pullbacks cancel against their inverses. The analogous composition of projections gives the structure map. The center at the join is the transport of the first center of the second sequence along the same identifications. All the fields therefore agree with the stated double transport.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_dataAt_of_forall: If the stage precedes the join, use the property for the corresponding stage in the first sequence and transport it by the stage isomorphism. At the join, the given strict bound implies that the second sequence has a first step. Apply the property there and transport it through its inverse initial isomorphism and then through the join identification. After the join, the corresponding stage of the second sequence lies strictly below its length. Transport its property along the scheme identification. The assumed invariance supplies the result in all three cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_dataAt_of_length_lt: After the join, position i of the appended sequence corresponds to position i minus the first length in the second sequence. The ideal, boundary, and center are pulled back from that stage along the scheme identification. The appended projection similarly gives its structure map after composition with the first sequence's final projection and the original structure map. These formulas identify the complete marked data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_dataAt_of_lt_length: Before the joining stage, the appended sequence is identified with the first sequence at the same index. Its ideal, boundary, and center are the pullbacks of those for the first sequence through this identification. Its structure map is the corresponding composite by the formula for the appended projection. These are the fields of the transported stage data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_inv_comap_hom: The successive pullbacks equal pullback along the inverse followed by the forward isomorphism. This composite is the identity, which fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dataAt_ambient: By definition the ambient scheme of the data at stage i is the scheme at stage i in the underlying sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dataAt_boundary: The boundary of the stage data is defined to be the stage-i boundary list of the marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dataAt_center: The stage data take their center from the underlying blowup sequence at the same index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dataAt_ideal: The construction assigns the stage-i ideal of the marked sequence as the ideal of the stage data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dataAt_structMap: The construction defines the structure map by the stage-i projection to the initial scheme followed by its map to the ground field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mk_congr: The two marked objects have the same ambient scheme and equal ideals, boundary lists, structure maps, and centers. Substituting these equalities makes the two objects identical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_ambient: Transport is defined on the source of the isomorphism, so the ambient scheme of the transported data is A.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_boundary: The transported boundary is formed by pulling back each original boundary ideal along the forward isomorphism, keeping the order of the list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_center: The definition transports the center by pulling back its ideal along the forward isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_dataAt_congr: Substitute the equality of the indices. The stage data are then equal and the two identifications of their ambient scheme come from proofs of the same equality. Thus the two transports agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_ideal: Transport of the marked data defines the new ideal by pulling the old ideal back along the forward isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_projectionToBase: The new structure map is defined by applying the forward isomorphism to the old ambient scheme and then its original structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transport_refl: Pullback along the identity fixes the ideal, each boundary entry, and the center. The composite of the identity with the structure map is the original map. Thus every field of the transported marked data agrees with the original.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bddAbove_setOf_le_orderAt: A natural number in the set is bounded by the order at some point. That order is at most B, so the same inequality holds between the natural number and B. Thus B bounds the entire set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bddAbove_setOf_le_orderAt_of_mem: For each number in the set there is a point of S where the order is at least that number. The global bound B also holds at this point. Consequently B is an upper bound for these natural numbers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_orderAt_eq_maxOrder: Since the scheme is nonempty, zero lies in the set of attained lower bounds for the orders. The given bound makes this a bounded set of natural numbers, so its supremum belongs to the set. Choose a point witnessing that membership. Its order is at least the supremum, while its finite order is itself in the set and is therefore at most the supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_orderAtLeastLocus_comap_subset: Smooth pullback makes the order locus of the pulled back ideal the inverse image of the original order locus. The image of this inverse image lies in the original locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderOn_eq_zero_iff: If the maximum on S is zero, the inequality with the maximum gives that every order on S is at most zero, hence is zero. Conversely, if every order on S is zero, then every natural number witnessed by a point of S is at most zero. The supremum is bounded by zero and, being a natural number, equals zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderOn_lt_of_forall_lt: Every number in the defining set is at most the order of a point of S and hence strictly less than c. Because c is positive and the numbers are natural, c−1 bounds the set. Its supremum is therefore less than c.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrder_lt_of_orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empt: Any natural number in the set defining the maximum is at most the order of some point. If that number were at least c, the point would belong to the empty order locus at c. Therefore every number in the set is at most c−1. The supremum is at most c−1 as well, which is strictly below c by positivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_maxOrder_nonempty: Choose a point attaining the maximum order, which exists by boundedness and nonemptiness. Its order is at least the threshold defining the locus, so it belongs to that locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_pow_sup_pow: The order locus of the sum is the intersection of the order loci of the two powers. The positive exponent m cancels from both sides of the first threshold inequality, leaving order at least s for N. For the other summand, the positive exponent s cancels and leaves order at least m for I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_pow_sup_pow_eq_empty_i: The locus of the sum of powers is the intersection of the order locus of I at m and that of N at s. If this intersection is empty, each point in the first locus has order for N less than s. Conversely, that strict bound at every point of the first locus leaves no point in both loci.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_sup: The order of the sum of two ideals is the minimum of their orders. A point has that minimum at least c exactly when both individual orders are at least c. This is membership in the intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_maxOrder: The finite bound makes the order at x a natural number, say m. The point x witnesses that m belongs to the set defining the maximum order, and the set is bounded. Its supremum is therefore at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_maxOrderOn: By the finite bound, the order at x is a natural number. Since x lies in S, this number is a member of the bounded set used to define the maximum order on S. It is at most the supremum of that set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_lt_of_maxOrder_lt: The order at the given point is at most the maximum order, and the maximum order is strictly below c. The asserted strict inequality follows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_pow_sup_pow: The order of the sum is the minimum of the two summand orders. The order of each power is its exponent times the order of its base ideal. Substituting both power formulas gives the stated minimum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_pow_sup_pow_le: Use the expression as the minimum of the two weighted orders. On the order locus of I at m, the bound on N makes the first weighted order at most ms. Off that locus, the order of I is below m, so the second weighted order is at most sm. In either case the minimum is at most ms.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_canonicalAlgorithmRu: The canonical maximum-order family is this order-reduction construction with the established invariance under isomorphism. Apply the specification for the order-reduction sequence with that invariance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_orderReductionSeq:
Use the monomial principalization specification to apply the results for the order-reduction sequence. They give stage certificates, nonempty centers, resolution, agreement with the original assignment when the boundary is empty and the order is bounded, and a trivial sequence when the marked order locus is empty.

For pullback, the comparison of the constructed sequences applies using the base-change data for a field extension or for a smooth map, respectively. Field extension is surjective, and in the strict smooth case surjectivity is an assumption. In either surjective case the nonempty center supports ensure that every original center ideal differs from the unit ideal. The pullback comparison is therefore strict in both cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.monomialPrincipalization_spec: Apply the monomial principalization theorem with the dimension condition that holds for every dimension. The given geometry and the field-change invariance supply the hypotheses. Its certificates, nonempty centers, resolution, and zero length when the marked locus is empty give the stated specification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtBaseFieldChangeInvariance_of_geom: Identify the test square with the canonical pullback of B along the field-change projection. The comparison isomorphism for an iterated pullback identifies this scheme with the direct field change of B. Its projection to B is the map in the test square, so pulling back the ideal can be done through the direct field change and then through the isomorphism. Order is unchanged under the isomorphism, and the geometric field-change property identifies the remaining order with the original order at the image point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.monomialCaseHypotheses_of_monomialCenter: The supplied conditions give smoothness and normal crossings for centers, the boundary total-transform formula, the criterion for a component to lie in a boundary divisor, and the description of transformed components. For the other fields, use the codimension bound for nonempty strata, smoothness of boundary intersections, order invariance off the exceptional locus, and order one for a boundary divisor on its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformHypotheses_of_residualHyp: Use the given strict-transform component property directly. Apply the monomial case construction to the underlying center hypotheses to obtain the second required property.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMonomialIn.comap: At a point of the source, choose a neighborhood of its image on which the target ideal belongs to the submonoid generated by the boundary. Pull the neighborhood back to the source. The restriction square identifies the restriction of each pullback with the pullback of the corresponding restriction. Each generator thus maps to one for the pulled back boundary, and products and the unit are preserved. Consequently the pulled back ideal belongs to the required submonoid on this neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMonomialSplitting.comap_iso: Pullback preserves the product factorization and local monomiality. The support of the pulled back monomial factor is the inverse image of its original support, so it lies in the union of the pulled back boundary supports. For transversality, the underlying homeomorphism carries each irreducible component of a pulled back boundary support to an irreducible component of the original support. This preserves maximality because the inverse homeomorphism pulls any larger irreducible subset back. Containment in the pulled back nonmonomial support would then give containment of the corresponding original component in the original nonmonomial support, contrary to transversality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.IsAdmissible.wit: The nonmonomial factor is nonzero on components because the whole ideal is and the splitting puts the factor's support inside the whole support. The new marking is at least the original positive marking. The geometric conditions on the field, scheme, structure map, and boundary persist because those fields are retained. Thus the new marked object is admissible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.withIdealAndMult: Changing the marked ideal and marking retains the original base field by definition.
The operation retains the original ordered boundary list.
The operation takes N as the new ideal, which gives the ideal formula.
The marking in the new data is the supplied natural number μ.
The new marked data use the original ambient scheme by construction.
The operation retains the original structure morphism to the ground field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.controlledTransf: The recursion takes the pullback of the preceding transform and forms its residual by the m-th exceptional power. This is the value at the successor stage.
The initial term of the controlled transform is the starting ideal pulled back by the initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.monomialFactor_s: At the next stage the recursion pulls the preceding monomial factor back along the blowup and multiplies by the exceptional ideal to the power μ−m. This is the stated successor value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.monomialFactor_z: The monomial factor recursion starts by pulling the original factor back through the stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.cast_sub_le_of_cast_le_add: If a is infinite it bounds every natural number. Otherwise write it as a natural number n. The hypothesis then gives m ≤ n+s, which implies m−s ≤ n for natural-number subtraction. This remains true in the extended natural numbers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_controlledTransform_eq_comap_seque: The two controlled transforms at stage i agree. Pulling this equality back along the same successor morphism gives the stated identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_one_of_forall_notMem_support: Every point of the open avoids the ideal support. The restricted support is the inverse image of the original support and is therefore empty. The restricted ideal is the unit ideal, which is the multiplicative identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_homOfLE: The inclusion of U in Y factors through V via the inclusion of U in V. Composition of ideal pullbacks along this factorization gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_homOfLE_mem_closure_comap: A generator on V is a restriction of a boundary entry, so its restriction to U is the corresponding generator on U. The unit restricts to the unit and products restrict to products. Induction on generation by these operations shows every given member restricts to the submonoid generated on U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_list_prod: The empty product is the unit ideal, preserved by pullback. In the inductive step pullback preserves the product of the first entry and the remaining product. Apply induction to the latter.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_one: The multiplicative identity is the unit ideal. Extension of the unit ideal along any morphism is still the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_eq_sequenceData: At stage zero both recursions pull back the starting ideal through the same isomorphism. At each successor they pull back along the same blowup morphism and take the residual by the same exceptional power. Induction with these recursions gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalDivisor_eq_exceptionalIdeal: Both descriptions give the center ideal pulled back along the next blowup morphism. Substituting this pullback formula identifies them.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalDivisor_pow_mul_comap_mul_eq_: Write F for the exceptional ideal. Since m ≤ μ, the factors Fᵐ and F raised to μ−m multiply to F raised to μ. Multiplying that power by the next nonmonomial ideal gives the pullback of the current nonmonomial ideal by the marked transform formula. After reordering factors, the product is therefore the pullback of the monomial factor times the pullback of the current nonmonomial ideal. This equals the pullback of C.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalDivisor_pow_mul_controlledTra: Translate the given factorization to the underlying blowup data using equality of the two transforms and transition maps. The power times residual formula for the controlled transform in those data gives the factorization with the successor transform. Translate its terms back to the marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closure_singleton_eq_closure: The closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible and closed. The underlying space of a scheme is sober, so that closure has a generic point whose singleton closure is the whole closure.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_eq_comap: Write F for the exceptional ideal and r for the order of the nonmonomial factor on the center. If m ≤ r, take the pullback of the monomial factor times F to the power r−m. Multiplication by Fᵐ restores the required total exceptional exponent. If r < m, additivity of order in the original splitting and the order bound on the whole ideal show that the monomial factor has order at least m−r on the center. Normal crossings gives containment in that power of the center ideal. On the blowup the pullback of the monomial factor is therefore divisible by F to the power m−r. Use the residual factor and multiply its factorization by F to the power r. This gives the required factorization by Fᵐ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_list_prod_eq_of_mem_closure: Induct on membership in the generated submonoid. For a generator use the single boundary entry giving it. For the unit use the empty list. For a product concatenate the lists representing the two factors. Their entries all belong to the boundary, and the product over the concatenated list is the required product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_comap_list_prod_eq_mul_exce: Induct on the list. The empty product uses the whole scheme, the unit monomial, and exceptional exponent zero. For a head entry use its local total-transform factorization and intersect its neighborhood with the neighborhood for the tail. The product of the restricted strict transform of the head and the monomial for the tail is generated by the strict transforms, and the exceptional exponent is the sum of the two exponents. The head exponent is one exactly when the center locally lies in that boundary support. The assumptions about z then give order one there in that case and order zero otherwise. Additivity of order for the product identifies the sum of exponents with the order of the full list product at z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_forall_comap_mem_closure: Induct on the list. For an empty list use the whole scheme. At the next step take a neighborhood where the head is monomial in the second list and one where every tail entry is monomial, provided by induction. On their intersection each generating-submonoid membership persists by restriction. This supplies one neighborhood for the full list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_isIrreducible_support_inter: Lift y to the smooth center, where it lies in a unique irreducible component because the components of the smooth scheme are disjoint. The center is Noetherian, so there are finitely many components. The union of the images of the other components is closed in the ambient scheme because the center inclusion is a closed embedding. Its open complement contains y. In this open the center support is the intersection of the image of the component through y with the open. The component image is irreducible and this intersection is nonempty, so the intersection is irreducible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducibleComponentOf_of_maximal: The set C is irreducible and lies in S. Any irreducible subset of S containing C lies in C by the assumed maximality and hence equals C. These are the defining conditions for an irreducible component of S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducible_inter_isOpen: The intersection is nonempty by hypothesis. If two opens each meet it, their intersections with O are opens meeting S. Irreducibility of S gives a common point in S that belongs to both of these opens. That point lies in the intersection with O, proving irreducibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducible_subset_maximal_of_isIrredu: A component is an irreducible subset of S. Maximality says that any irreducible subset of S containing it equals it, and hence lies in it. This gives the three stated properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_excep: The indicated step is an actual blowup, so its exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzero divisor. The exceptional divisor in the marked sequence is defined by that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_sequenceData_of_orderAt_le: The underlying sequence already has smooth centers in the required normal crossing position. The controlled splitting result gives containment of every center in the order locus of the whole transform at its original marking and divisibility by the required exceptional power. The controlled transform and the successor map agree with those of the underlying data. Hence the two algebraic markedness conditions hold for the original object as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_comap_blowup: Pullback makes the starting monomial ideal monomial in the total transforms of the boundary entries. Locally each total transform is its strict transform times a power of the exceptional ideal. Both are entries in the new boundary list, so each total transform is monomial in that list. Substituting these local monomial descriptions gives monomiality of the pulled back ideal in the new boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_mul: At a point, intersect neighborhoods on which each factor belongs to the submonoid generated by the boundary. Restriction to the intersection preserves membership. The restricted product then belongs to the same submonoid because it is closed under multiplication.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul:
Off the exceptional support, shrink a neighborhood of monomiality of the total pullback to the complement of the support. The exceptional factor becomes a unit, so the residual agrees with this monomial total pullback there.

On the exceptional support, the image point is on the center. Choose an open on which the center support is irreducible and intersect it with a neighborhood where the original monomial ideal is a product of boundary entries. The resulting nonempty irreducible set has a generic point η in its closure, lying on the center and in the chosen open. For a boundary entry, its support contains η exactly when it contains the center on a neighborhood of the image point. One direction uses closedness of the support and the generic point property. The other uses that η belongs to any open meeting the irreducible set.

The local total-transform formula for the product gives a strict-transform monomial times an exceptional power with exponent equal to the product order at η. The containment in the d-th power of the center ideal forces this order to be at least d. Restrict to the preimage of the neighborhood where the original product expression holds and cancel the common Cartier exceptional power of degree d. The residual is the strict-transform monomial times a nonnegative exceptional power, so it is monomial in the new boundary there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_forall_mem: Choose a neighborhood where P is generated by the first list and another where all entries of the first list are generated by the second. On the intersection both properties persist. Thus the submonoid generated by the first entries there lies in that generated by the second. The restriction of P belongs to the second submonoid.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_locally_eq_mul_pow: Choose the given local product expression at each point. The two restricted factors are generators of the submonoid because they are listed boundary entries. Their product with the indicated exponent is therefore in the submonoid.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_mem: On the whole scheme the restriction of D is among the generating boundary ideals. It therefore belongs to their generated submonoid, providing the required neighborhood at every point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_pow: Choose a neighborhood where the restriction of P belongs to the generated submonoid. Its power also belongs, and it equals the restriction of the power because pullback preserves powers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_controlledTransform_:
At stage zero, pull back the original splitting through the initial isomorphism. For a successor stage, the marked transform formula for the nonmonomial factor and the inequality m ≤ μ give a factorization of the pullback of the whole ideal. After removing the m-th exceptional power, the remaining factors are the new nonmonomial ideal and the pulled back monomial factor times the exceptional power μ−m. The exceptional ideal is Cartier, so cancellation identifies their product with the controlled transform of the whole ideal.

The local total-transform formula makes each old boundary pullback monomial in its strict transform and the exceptional divisor. Thus the new monomial factor is monomial in the new boundary and its support is contained in their union. For transversality, a component of a strict-transformed boundary entry has a generic point projecting to the generic point of an old boundary component. If the new nonmonomial support contained the transformed component, the old nonmonomial support would contain the image point, by the product factorization and pullback of supports. Closedness would then force containment of the old component, contrary to the previous splitting. For an exceptional component, the noncontainment estimate applies because the old nonmonomial order is exactly μ on the center. This proves the successor splitting.

At each actual step, exact order μ on the center follows from the upper bound and the marked center condition. Since μ ≥ m, the product order bound places the center in the order locus of the whole controlled transform at m. The factorization used in the induction supplies the requested divisibility of its pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_of_isBlowupAlongIdea:
The three given factorizations and the original product splitting show that the transformed whole ideal and the product of the two new factors become equal after multiplication by the m-th exceptional power. Cancel that Cartier power to get the splitting equality. The support of the new monomial factor lies in the support of its product with the exceptional power. The old monomial support and the total-transform formulas put this product support in the union of the new boundary supports.

If the nonmonomial center order r is at least m, cancellation writes the new monomial factor as the total monomial pullback times the exceptional power of degree r−m. This is monomial in the new boundary. If r < m, the old monomial ideal is contained in the center power of degree m−r by the order and normal crossing hypotheses. Cancelling the r-th exceptional power gives the corresponding residual expression for the new monomial factor. The monomiality theorem for such a residual applies.

For transversality at a strict-transformed boundary component, its generic point projects to a generic point of an original boundary component. Containment in the new nonmonomial support would put this image point and its closure in the old nonmonomial support by the pullback factorization, contradicting the original splitting. For an exceptional component, apply the controlled-transform noncontainment result with the exact center order r. These facts give transversality for every new boundary entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_spec_field: A field is a Noetherian ring, so its affine spectrum is a Noetherian scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_subscheme_of_smooth: The center scheme maps smoothly to the field spectrum, so the map is locally of finite type. The closed immersion and the original quasi-compact structure map make the center's structure map quasi-compact. A quasi-compact locally finite type scheme over the Noetherian field spectrum is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrder_ideal_length_lt_of_orderAtLeast: The order bound along the sequence applies at the final stage. Its order locus at the positive marking is empty, so the maximum-order bound for an empty locus makes the final maximum strictly smaller than that marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closeds_compl_iff: By definition, the open complement of a closed set contains exactly the points outside that closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_isOpen_of_closure_singleton_eq: If the generic point were outside O, its singleton closure would be contained in the closed complement. That closure is the closure of S, so S would also be disjoint from O. This contradicts the nonempty intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_opens_ι: An open inclusion identifies the local ring and the ideal stalk at the point with their originals. Thus the order is unchanged on restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_of_mem_center_support: By markedness, a center point has order at least μ. The global bound makes its order at most μ, so it equals μ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_controlledTr: The controlled splitting writes the whole transform as the product of the current monomial factor and the nonmonomial ideal. The monomial factor is supported in the boundary locus. The nonmonomial ideal has the given order certificate with marking μ, and the center lies in its μ-order locus. Use the certificate comparison for such a splitting and the inequality between the markings. It gives a principalization certificate for the whole transform at the original marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_of_closure_singleton_eq_closure: A closed subset containing η contains the closure of its singleton. By the given equality it contains the closure of S, hence contains S itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_orderAtLeastLocus_of_eq_mul: At every point of S the order of the second factor is at least m. The order of the product is at least the sum of the two factor orders, which is at least the second order. By the product equality the same bound holds for C.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_coe: The support of a pulled back ideal sheaf is the inverse image of the original support. Taking its underlying set gives the stated identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_mul_subset: The support of a product of two ideal sheaves is the union of their supports. The claimed inclusion follows from this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_pow_subset: For a positive exponent the power has the same support as the ideal. For exponent zero the power is the unit ideal, whose support is empty. The inclusion holds in both cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_support_mul_right: The support of the product is the union of the two supports, which contains the support of its second factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_subset_union_of_locally_eq_mul_p: At a point outside both indicated supports, choose an open with the given product expression. The two restricted factors have unit stalks there, since restriction preserves the local rings and stalk ideals. So does the product, including the case of exponent zero. The original ideal therefore has unit stalk at the point, proving the support inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.SameNontrivialBo: The filtered lists of nonunit entries agree. An ideal belongs to either filtered list precisely when it belongs to the corresponding original list and differs from the unit ideal. Hence the two membership sets agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_top_eq_empty: At every point the unit ideal has the whole local ring as its stalk. Thus its support is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comap_eq_prod_pow_of_orderAt_eq_z: Choose a neighborhood on which the monomial factor is a product of powers of boundary entries. Order zero of the nonmonomial factor means the point is outside its support, so intersect the chosen neighborhood with the open complement of that support. The nonmonomial factor restricts to the unit ideal there. Restrict the monomial product, using that pullback preserves products and powers, and substitute in the splitting to get the required expression for the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_comap_prod: Pullback preserves the unit ideal, giving the result for the empty product. For a union with one new index, pullback preserves the product of the new factor and the smaller product. Induction gives the formula for the finite product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_iff_forall_exists_mem_closu: On an open neighborhood of a point, the monomial condition asks for a product of powers of the restricted boundary entries. Those products are precisely the elements of the submonoid generated by the restricted entries. Apply this equivalence on each proposed neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_mem_of_ne_top: On a neighborhood where the ideal is monomial in the first boundary, each restricted generator either comes from an entry of the second boundary or comes from a unit ideal. In the latter case its restriction is the multiplicative identity. Thus every first-boundary generator lies in the submonoid generated by the second boundary, and so does the restricted monomial ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialIn_of_setOf_mem_ne_top_eq: Equality of the sets of nonunit entries gives inclusion of every nonunit entry of the first list in the second. The monomial transfer under this inclusion applies to the given ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_congr: The boundary equivalence gives equality of the sets of nonunit entries. Transfer a splitting along this equality for the forward implication and along the reverse equality for the converse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_monomialPart_nonMono: Admissibility and the geometric splitting hypothesis give a pair of factors satisfying the monomial splitting condition. The named monomial and nonmonomial parts select such a pair, so they satisfy the condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_nil: The product of the unit ideal with I is I, and the unit ideal has empty support. It is monomial in the empty boundary by the empty product formula, which works on the whole scheme. There are no boundary entries to test for transversality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_of_setOf_mem_ne_top_: The product factorization is unchanged, and the monomial factor remains monomial by equality of the nonunit entries. A point in the monomial support belongs to the support of some old boundary entry. That entry cannot be the unit ideal, whose support is empty, so it is an entry of the new list. For transversality, any irreducible component of the support of a new boundary entry requires that entry to have nonempty support, so the entry also belongs to the old list. The original transversality applies to it. These verify the splitting for the new boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_nonMonomial: The splitting expresses I as the product of M with N. On every open the product of two ideals is contained in the second one, giving the sheaf inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closure_image_iff_exists_prod_pow: Induct on membership in the generated submonoid. A generator has exponent one at an index realizing it in the list and zero elsewhere. The identity has every exponent zero, and multiplying two represented elements adds the exponents at each index by commutativity. Conversely, every generator lies in the submonoid, so its powers and every finite product of them lie there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_nontrivialPart_iff: The nontrivial part filters a list by the condition of differing from the unit ideal. Its members are exactly the original entries satisfying that condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_comap_of_sameNontrivialB: The original chosen factors form a monomial splitting. Smooth pullback gives a splitting of the pulled back ideal for the pulled back boundary. By uniqueness, its nonmonomial factor is the pullback of the original factor. Replacing the boundary by the equivalent list preserves the chosen nonmonomial part, which gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_eq_ideal_of_boundary_eq_: For the empty boundary the unit ideal and the original ideal form a splitting. Uniqueness identifies the second factor with the chosen nonmonomial part.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_eq_of_isMonomialSplittin: The selected factors give one splitting and the given pair gives another. Uniqueness for the admissible object identifies both factors, in particular the selected nonmonomial part with N.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_eq_of_sameNontrivialBoun: The chosen factors for the replacement boundary give a splitting because the modified object is admissible. Boundary equivalence makes this pair a splitting for the original boundary as well. Uniqueness there identifies the two chosen nonmonomial parts.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_nonMonomial: If an irreducible component lay in the support of the nonmonomial factor, it would also lie in the support of the original ideal by the support inclusion. This contradicts the assumed nonvanishing on components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_add: Replace the original ideal by the product of its monomial and nonmonomial factors. Additivity of order on the smooth scheme then gives the sum of their orders at the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_nonMonomial_subset: At a point where the stalk of N is proper, the stalk of I is contained in it by the ideal inclusion. The stalk of I is therefore also proper, giving membership in its support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByNonMonomialPart_boundary_l: The continuation uses the underlying blowup sequence and the same starting boundary as the assigned nonmonomial sequence. The comparison of boundary recursions identifies their boundaries at the common final index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByNonMonomialPart_ideal_leng: The continuation records the controlled transforms of the original final ideal with its original marking on the assigned nonmonomial blowup sequence. The comparison between controlled transforms on the sequence and its underlying data therefore gives the displayed identification at the last stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByNonMonomialPart_length: The continuation uses the underlying blowup data of the assigned nonmonomial sequence and changes its marking. The underlying data retain the original number of steps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationByNonMonomialPart_length_pos: The continuation length equals that of the assigned nonmonomial sequence. The latter is positive by resolution and nonemptiness of the starting nonmonomial order locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_ofMarkedSequence: The two descriptions start with the same pullback along the initial isomorphism. At the next stage the exceptional ideal and blowup map agree, so applying the same residual construction to equal previous transforms gives equal successor transforms. Induction proves equality at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_orderAt_lastNonMonomialPart_le: The final ideal is nonzero on components by admissibility of the final marked object. The nonmonomial factor in its splitting is then nonzero on components as well. Apply the geometric bounded-order theorem on that final scheme to obtain a finite uniform bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendByNonMonomialPart_eq_append: The final dimension bound permits the recursive call with the last nonmonomial factor and its maximum marking. The resulting data meet the markedness test for the original final ideal and marking. The recursive rule therefore appends those data with the original marking, which is the stated continuation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_continuationByNonMonomialPart: The nonmonomial triple meets the assignment's admissibility, dimension, and order bounds. Its assigned sequence therefore has nonempty centers and certificates, and its stage orders satisfy the required bound. The certificate comparison for a monomial splitting transfers each certificate to the original controlled transform with the original marking. The continuation has that transformed ideal, the same center and projection, and the same boundary. The last equality follows from the common boundary recursion, so their boundary loci also agree. Together with nonemptiness of the center, the transferred certificate gives the asserted stage property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_nonMonomialOrderReduction: The completed nonmonomial reduction is the iterate at its prescribed stopping bound. The stage property established for every iterate therefore holds for this one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_nonMonomialOrderReductionIter: At zero the sequence is empty, so there is no center to check. If an iterate has stopped, the successor is the same sequence and the induction hypothesis applies. Otherwise the successor appends the nonmonomial continuation. The previous stages have the property by induction, and the continuation stages have it by the certificate comparison. Invariance under isomorphism lets the append theorem combine the two.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasPrincipalizationCenter_of_principaliz: The data at i have the given center and its support is nonempty. Their boundary support is the marked sequence's boundary locus, so the given certificate is exactly the certificate required for those data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_congr: Substitute the equalities of the structure map, ideal, marking, and boundary. The target carries exactly the admissibility conditions of the given object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_nonMonomialTriple: Use admissibility of the final original marked object for the scheme, structure map, and boundary. Its nonmonomial factor is nonzero on components by the splitting and the nonvanishing of the original final ideal. The continuation condition puts the new marking at least as high as the original positive one. Thus replacing the ideal and marking gives an admissible object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_tripleAtLength: The conversion to a marked sequence preserves its length, so the final stage is within range. The marked transform results give a smooth structure map, nonvanishing of the final ideal on components, strict normal crossing position of the boundary, and a Noetherian final scheme. Smoothness gives local finite type and the Noetherian source gives quasi-compactness. The characteristic and positive marking remain those of the original admissible object, proving all the conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_seqAtEnd_lastNonMonomialPart: The nonmonomial triple is admissible, its dimension is within the assignment bound, and its order is bounded by its own marking, the maximum nonmonomial order. Thus the assignment supplies the order bounds along its sequence. The continuation condition makes that marking at least the original marking. Apply the theorem on reusing a sequence for the nonmonomial factor as a marked sequence for the entire split ideal, using the admissibility and splitting of the original final object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_lastNonMonomialPart: The last original marked object is admissible. Its chosen monomial and nonmonomial parts therefore form a splitting by existence of a splitting on admissible objects. These two parts are exactly the factors in the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_of_boundary_eq_of_id: Substitute the equality of boundary lists and the equality of starting ideals. The splitting condition is then exactly the one assumed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_map_comap_id: Pullback along the identity leaves each ideal unchanged. The empty list is fixed, and the head and tail of each nonempty list are fixed by this fact and induction, respectively.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_of_smooth: A smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation and therefore locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomial_emptyMarkedBlowupSeq: The empty data end at stage zero with the starting ideal and boundary. Their final nonmonomial factor is therefore the original nonmonomial factor, and their maxima are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomial_extendByNonMonomialP: The extension appends a continuation of positive length. Its final data are the final continuation data under the stage identification, which preserves the maximum nonmonomial order. The continuation's final nonmonomial factor equals the last ideal of the assigned nonmonomial sequence by the transformed splitting. Resolution of that sequence makes its maximum strictly smaller than the previous maximum. These identities transfer the decrease to the extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomial_iter_add_le_of_foral: At index zero the maximum is the starting maximum. At each successor in range the previous iterate continues, so the extension strictly decreases its natural-number maximum. By induction the previous maximum plus its index is bounded by the initial maximum. The decrease by at least one offsets the increment of the index, giving the bound at the successor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrder_idealAtLength_lt_maxOrderNonMon: The current maximum marking is positive. The assignment resolves the nonmonomial triple since it is admissible and meets the dimension and order bounds, so its final locus at this marking is empty. Its specification also bounds order along the sequence. Apply the maximum-order estimate for an empty locus at a positive threshold to obtain the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_eq_of_maxO: At one more than the original maximum, the iterate is by definition the completed reduction and its continuation condition fails. All subsequent iterates are equal to this stopped iterate. Apply this stability at the given later index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrder_transport_eqToIso: After substituting the equality of ambient schemes, transport is along the identity isomorphism. It fixes the ideal and boundary, so it fixes the nonmonomial factor and its maximum order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialPart_continuationByNonMonomia: The assigned sequence has order bounds because the nonmonomial triple is admissible and meets the dimension and initial order bounds. The original marking is at most the nonmonomial marking. The splitting theorem along this sequence identifies the transformed original ideal as a product whose nonmonomial factor is the current ideal of the assigned sequence. At the last stage the continuation has that transformed original ideal and the same boundary. Its final marked object is admissible, so uniqueness of the monomial splitting identifies its chosen nonmonomial factor with the final ideal of the assigned sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_nonMonomialOrderReductionContinues_n: If the final iterate continued, every earlier iterate would have continued as well, since any stopped iterate stays fixed forever. The maximum-decrease bound would then give that the final maximum plus the iteration count is at most the starting maximum. The iteration count is already one greater than the starting maximum, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_boundary_eq_of_le: At stage zero both boundaries are the original entries pulled back along the initial isomorphism. At each actual step both descriptions take strict transforms of the same previous entries and append the same exceptional ideal. Induction through the sequence length gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eqToHom: Substitute the equality of schemes. The comparison morphism is the identity, which fixes the ideal by pullback and fixes its locus by inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_nonempty: Take a point of the original order locus and map it by the inverse isomorphism. Pullback along this inverse of the already transported ideal recovers the original ideal. By smooth invariance under the inverse morphism, the image point lies in the order locus of the transported ideal. It witnesses nonemptiness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_lastNonMonomialPart_le_maxOrderN: Choose a finite uniform bound for the order of the last nonmonomial factor. The order at each point is then bounded by its maximum, defined as the supremum of the witnessed natural-number orders. This is the desired maximum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_lastNonMonomialPart_nonMonomialO: The given point makes the final scheme nonempty. The final nonmonomial order has a finite upper bound, so its maximum is attained and its maximum-order locus is nonempty. Since the reduction has stopped, the other continuation condition must fail, meaning this maximum is strictly below the original marking. The order at the given point is at most that maximum, giving the claimed strict bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_of_isNoetherian: An inverse image of an affine open is an open subset of the Noetherian source. Every such subset is quasi-compact, so the morphism is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.seqAtEnd_lastNonMonomialPart_length_pos: The assignment resolves the admissible nonmonomial triple because the dimension and order bounds hold. If its sequence had length zero, resolution would make the order locus of its initial ideal empty at stage zero. But the continuation condition gives a point of the original nonmonomial order locus at its maximum marking. Transport through the initial isomorphism preserves nonemptiness, a contradiction. The length is therefore positive.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tripleAtLength_dim_le: The object with the new ideal and marking uses the final stage scheme. The geometric dimension comparison bounds the dimension of that stage by the original dimension. Passing from the data to the marked sequence preserves the scheme and length, so the same bound applies to this object.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtComapOffExceptionalLocus_of_monom: The supplied monomial geometry includes invariance of order for a pulled back ideal off the exceptional locus. Taking that property gives the desired statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_preimage_of_isB: Take a point of the transformed order locus. If it lies on the exceptional divisor, it maps into the center, where the original ideal has order at least μ and hence at least c. Elsewhere the order of the total pullback equals the original order at the image. The total pullback is the exceptional power times the transformed ideal, so its order is at least the order of the transformed ideal by the order inequality for products. This is at least c, proving the inclusion in both cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_preimage_transi: Induct on the number of steps from i to j. When the two stages agree, the transition is the identity. At a successor, the one-step inclusion maps each point of the successor order locus into the order locus at the preceding stage. Induction then maps its image into the locus at stage i. The composition rule identifies these successive maps with the direct transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_succ_subset_preimage_b: The current transformed object is admissible, and the next morphism is the blowup at its chosen center. Markedness places the center in the current order locus at the marking. The next ideal satisfies the exceptional-power factorization of the current pullback. Apply the one-step inclusion at the threshold c, which is at most the marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_comp_apply: Evaluate the composition rule for the transition maps at x. Applying the map from the last stage to the middle stage and then the map to the first stage therefore gives the image under the direct transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_refl_apply: The transition map from a stage to itself is the identity morphism. Its underlying map sends every point to itself.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtPullbackInvariant_baseChange_fiel: Paste the test pullback square with the ground-field extension square. The resulting pullback describes Q as a base change of B to the larger field, because the map from B to the starting scheme respects the structure maps. The canonical pullback isomorphism commutes with the projections to B. Factor the projection through this isomorphism and pull back the ideal in two steps. Order is unchanged by the isomorphism and is preserved under field extension by the given geometric hypothesis. The resulting value is the order at the image in B.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtPullbackInvariant_of_smooth: In the test pullback square, the projection to B is a base change of the given smooth morphism, so it is smooth. Admissibility of the marked object on B gives a smooth structure map over a characteristic-zero field. The smooth invariance theorem for order gives equality at each point of the pullback and its image in B.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMonomialSplitting_monomialPart_nonMono: A splitting exists by assumption, so the definition selects a pair satisfying the splitting condition. The monomial part and nonmonomial part are the two entries of this selected pair. Their splitting property is the property of the chosen pair.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionIter_exists_seque:
The zero iterates are the completed nonmonomial reductions, which already have a pullback comparison. At the successor of a stopped lower iterate, keep the existing comparison. At a continuing lower iterate, the final ideal and boundary comparison gives that the upper nonmonomial maximum on the marked locus is at most the lower one.

If the upper maximum is smaller, the pulled back lower companion ideal has empty locus at its marking, so its appended steps are omitted upstairs. If the maxima agree, the upper companion step is active and its ideal and marking are the pullback of the lower ones. The markedness tests succeed for both new sequences, so compare the two appends and increment the upper iteration index. This completes the induction. The flat final-stage comparison supplies the final ideal and boundary for the chosen matched iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_congr: Substitute the two equalities of marked blowup data. The existing comparison then has the required source and target sequences, and its last ideal and boundary comparisons are exactly those asserted.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendByNonMonomialPart_sequenceOfBlowup:
The flat comparison gives the pullback of the last ideal and the equivalence of last boundaries. The last nonmonomial factor therefore pulls back, and its maximum upstairs is at most the lower maximum. If the upper sequence continues and the two maxima agree, the new marked nonmonomial ideals are compatible for pullback. The markedness tests succeed on both sides, so the comparison for recursive appends gives the result with both sequences extended.

If the upper maximum is smaller, the pullback of the lower nonmonomial ideal has empty locus at the lower marking, so the added lower steps can be omitted upstairs. The remaining case has equal maxima with the upper continuation condition false. Equality of markings transfers the lower inequality between the marking and the maximum, so the failed upper condition means its locus at that maximum is empty. This again gives the comparison with only the lower sequence extended.
