Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyMonomialTriple_tripleAtLength_c: The two final objects use the same stage, structure map, and boundary. Substitute the equal ideal and marking to identify them, then use the given local monomiality property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt_of_isAdmissible: The data and their marked sequence have the same length, so the indicated stage is in range in the sequence. Admissibility and the preservation of Noetherianity along marked blowups give a Noetherian stage scheme, which is also the stage scheme of the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_monomialPrincip: Substitute the equality of the upper ideal and the equality of the upper marking. The upper input to monomial principalization is now the same object, so its given pullback relation is the desired one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_monomial_of_: The lower final object is admissible and has dimension at most the original dimension, so the final stage comparison provides a marked pullback square. The upper final ideal is the pullback of the lower one, and their markings are equal. These identifications express upper local monomiality in the form required by the compatibility assumption. Apply the monomial sequence comparison with the equivalent final boundaries, then substitute the actual upper ideal and marking back into the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_and_boundary_comap_of_flat: Substitute the equality of markings so that both sequences use the same exponent for controlled transformations. Under the initial pullback and boundary comparison and the stage Noetherian hypotheses, the flat comparison theorem identifies their final ideals and nontrivial boundaries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_and_boundary_comap_of_isAdmiss: Each stage in either sequence is Noetherian by admissibility and preservation along the marked blowups. These are the stage hypotheses needed by the flat final-stage comparison, which gives the stated equations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_zer: At zero iterations the construction uses the empty marked blowup data, of length zero. Passing to the marked sequence and forgetting the marking preserve that length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedDataOfSeq_companionIdeal_ne_none: Substitute the given companion ideal and its marking. The companion sequence is marked for the original final object by the companion transform theorem. Its markedness test therefore succeeds and returns data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedDataOfSeq_ne_none_of_isMarked: The supplied markedness makes the test succeed. The construction returns the blowup sequence with its new marking, so the result is a present value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_exists_seq: At zero, both iterations are empty and there is a pullback comparison. Induct on the lower iteration index. If the lower iterate has stopped, its successor is unchanged. If it continues, the one-extension comparison says either to extend both sequences, increasing the upper iteration index by one, or to extend only the lower sequence and retain the upper index. Thus there is a matching upper iterate in each case. Apply the flat final-stage comparison to its pullback data to obtain the ideal and boundary assertions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_nonMo: Apply the iteration comparison at the stopping bound of the lower nonmonomial reduction. It yields an upper iterate and the final ideal and boundary identifications. The lower iterate has stopped. The continuation comparison shows that if its matched upper iterate continued, so would the lower one, so the upper iterate has stopped as well. Compare the upper index and the prescribed upper stopping bound at their maximum. Stability of stopped iterates identifies the matched upper sequence with the full upper reduction. Substitute both final identifications in the comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_of_ce: Convert the sequences to blowup data, preserving the lengths, centers, and projections. The original centers miss the image of the flat map by hypothesis, and the proposed pulled back data have length zero. The construction for missed centers gives a pullback comparison with these empty data upstairs. Transfer it back through the conversion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_of_le: An empty original sequence has no center, so its centers vacuously miss the image of the flat map. The pulled back candidate also has length zero. Apply the comparison construction for centers that miss the image to the underlying data, then transfer the comparison back to the original sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionSeq_isPullbackBlowupSequen: In the constructed upper object, the ideal is the original ideal pulled back along g and the marking is the original marking. Together with the given equivalence of boundaries, admissibility, dimension, and base-change compatibility, these are the hypotheses of the general pullback result.

If the initial marked order locus upstairs is empty, the upper sequence has length zero. Every lower center lies in its stage's marked order locus and its projection lies in the original lower order locus. The order compatibility would put any point upstairs mapping to such a projection in the empty upper locus. Thus all lower centers miss the image, so the empty upper sequence is the required pullback.

Otherwise the lower initial locus is nonempty too, since pullback preserves order and the markings coincide. Match a companion iterate upstairs to the completed companion reduction downstairs. Its final data obey the pullback comparison. The lower reduction has stopped, so the upper matched iterate has stopped by the continuation comparison. Its stability, and that of the prescribed final upper iterate, identify it with the completed upper companion reduction. Both resulting final objects are locally monomial. The monomial sequence comparison applies to the final square, and the append theorem combines that comparison with the one for the companion prefixes. The nonempty-locus formulas identify the completed appends with the requested sequences.

The pulled back object with the replacement boundary has precisely the new field and structure map, pulled back ideal, original marking, and specified boundary used by the explicit construction. Its admissibility and dimension bounds therefore apply to that construction, and the preceding pullback result gives the sequence comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_mem_orderAtLeastLocus: All stages within the marked sequence are admissible. The order-locus inclusion along a composite of blowup transitions sends the point to the initial stage's marked order locus. That locus is the inverse image of the original locus under the initial isomorphism. Since the stage projection is the composite with that isomorphism, its image lies in the original marked locus.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.geometricHypotheses_of_orderReductionHyp:
The maximal-contact certificate descends under isomorphisms. For an irreducible component of the exceptional locus, its defining maximality supplies the maximal irreducible subset condition in the theorem that excludes containment in the controlled-transform support. Admissibility gives the smoothness, characteristic, and Noetherian hypotheses used there. It also allows application of order invariance under field extension.

The order estimate for the controlled transform and the strict-transform component description are part of the supplied hypotheses. Monomial splitting is preserved by flat pullback along a field extension and by smooth pullback. Existence and uniqueness of the splitting follow from the smooth normal crossing geometry and nonvanishing on components. The monomial geometry construction supplies the remaining inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.monomialGeometryHypotheses_of_monomialCa:
Use the supplied monomial hypotheses for codimension, smoothness and normal crossings of centers, boundary transforms, incidence, transformed components, smooth strata, and the two order formulas. The center built from a union of components has that union as its support and commutes with flat pullback. The flat component theorems describe images of components and find components above a given point. For smooth maps, apply the same theorems using flatness and the agreement of the boundary indices for pullbacks over the unchanged field.

Smoothness of the strata gives disjointness of their components and openness of the designated unions in the stratum. Noetherianity gives finiteness. The marked transform results give stage admissibility and the dimension bound, and the finite-order theorem gives a uniform bound for ideals nonzero on components. Replacing the boundary by one with the same nonunit entries preserves admissibility. Together these are the monomial geometry requirements.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_support_nonempty_orderReductionSe: If the initial marked order locus is empty, the sequence has length zero, contrary to the stage bound. Otherwise it is the marked sequence of the order-reduction data. The center property for those data gives nonemptiness of the center support at the indicated stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.certificate_orderReductionSeq: The stage bound excludes the empty sequence, so the initial marked order locus is nonempty and the construction uses the order-reduction data. The center property for those data includes a principalization certificate. Passing to the marked sequence retains the stage ideal, structure map, center, and boundary locus, so it retains that certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasCenter_orderReductionData: The companion reduction ends in a locally monomial marked object. Every actual stage of the companion reduction has the prescribed center property. The monomial sequence has nonempty centers and certificates by its specification, and these give the same center property at its actual stages after conversion to data. The property is invariant under scheme isomorphism, so the append theorem gives it at every actual stage of the order-reduction data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasPrincipalizationCenter_ofMarkedSequen: The converted data at this stage retain the given center, so its support is nonempty. The stage ideal and structure map are unchanged and the boundary support is the original sequence's boundary locus. The given certificate thus gives the required certificate on the converted data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isResolution_orderReductionSeq: Resolution means that the last ideal has empty marked order locus. If the initial locus is empty, there are no steps and the last ideal is the initial ideal transported by an isomorphism, so the locus remains empty. Otherwise the companion reduction ends in a locally monomial object. The monomial specification resolves that object, giving empty order locus at the last stage of its sequence. The append comparison transfers that emptiness to the last stage of the complete order-reduction sequence, proving resolution.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_of_lt_ofMarkedSequence_length: Conversion from a marked sequence to its data preserves length. Substitute that equality into the given index bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_append_last_eq_empty: If the second sequence has positive length, the final ideal of the append is the final ideal of the second sequence transported by the scheme identification. Its empty order locus remains empty after transport. If the second sequence has length zero, the append ends at the last stage of the first sequence. The second sequence's final ideal is its stage-zero ideal, which is pulled back from the first sequence's final ideal by the second initial isomorphism. Emptiness descends through this isomorphism and then persists under the scheme identification at the join. These cases give the claimed final emptiness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eqToHom_eq_empty: Transport by the scheme equality pulls the order locus back along the induced map. The inverse image of the given empty order locus is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empty_of_comap_iso_: The order locus of the pulled back ideal is the inverse image of the original order locus under the isomorphism. If the original locus contained a point, its inverse image under the isomorphism would give a point in the empty pulled back locus. Hence the original locus is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_ideal_congr: Substitute the equality of the indices to identify both ideals and their order loci. The original emptiness applies to the resulting stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_ofMarkedSequence_last_: Conversion of a marked sequence to data preserves its length and stage ideals. The final order locus of the data is therefore the given final order locus of the sequence and is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionData_eq_append: The order-reduction data first run the companion-ideal reduction, then run monomial principalization on the final marked object of that reduction. The second sequence is expressed using its underlying marked blowup data, so the construction is exactly the stated append.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionSeq_length_eq_zero_of_orde: The construction tests whether the initial marked order locus is empty. Under the hypothesis it returns the empty marked sequence, whose length is zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.isomorphic_of_length_e: Both sequences have only stage zero within their length. Identify these stages by going from the first stage to the common base by its initial isomorphism and then back to the second stage by the inverse of its initial isomorphism. The composite commutes with the initial maps by cancellation. There are no actual transition maps or centers to compare. This gives the isomorphism of the data sequences and hence of the originals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_append_eq_empty: Because the second sequence has positive length, the last ideal of the append is the last ideal of that sequence transported along the stage identification. At the sum of the two lengths its order locus is the inverse image of the given empty locus, hence is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionSeq_isomorphic_of_boundary:
If the initial marked order locus is empty, both sequences have length zero by their respective triviality properties. Their initial isomorphisms identify their sole stages over the starting scheme.

Otherwise the bounded order attains the marking, so the maximum order is exactly the marking. The boundary is empty, hence the initial nonmonomial part is the original ideal. The first nonmonomial step therefore applies the assignment to the original marked data. That step strictly lowers the maximum order of the nonmonomial part below the marking, so the nonmonomial iteration takes no further steps. The assigned sequence resolves its marked object, and the original controlled transforms here are the same transforms because the starting ideal and marking are the same. Its final marked order locus is therefore empty after transport to the appended sequence.

The companion iteration does nothing because the maximum on that empty locus is zero. The final monomial sequence has length zero by its specification. Removing this empty tail and the initial empty prefix leaves the single continuation, whose underlying sequence is that of the original assignment. The resulting isomorphisms give the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationAssignment_mk_isomorphic: Substituting the equalities of the structure map, ideal, marking and boundary makes the reconstructed marked object the original one. Both assignments then give the same sequence, which is isomorphic to itself.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundarySupport_dataAt: The marked data at stage i use the same boundary list as the stage-i marked sequence. Both sets consist of points lying in the support of some entry of that list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundarySupport_transport: The boundary of the transported marked object consists of the pullbacks of the original boundary entries. A point is in the support of one of these pullbacks exactly when its image lies in the support of the corresponding original entry. Taking the union proves the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isInvariantUnderIso_hasPrincipalizationC: Choose a point of the original center and take its inverse image under the isomorphism. It lies in the transported center by the support formula for pullback, so the new center is nonempty. Transport the certificate by the same isomorphism. The transported boundary support is the inverse image of the old one, so the certificate has the required memory set and center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundarySupport_iff: The boundary support is defined as the set of points lying in the support of at least one boundary entry. The stated existence condition is that definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_comap_support_iff_base_mem_support: The support of a pulled back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Thus membership is equivalent to membership of the image point in the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_center_and_certificate_of_hasPr: The underlying data and the resulting marked sequence have the same length, so the assumed property applies at each actual stage. The centers are the same, giving nonempty supports. The stage data and sequence also agree on the ideal, structure map, and boundary locus, so the certificate in the stage property gives the desired sequence certificate.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MonomialGeometryHypotheses.isAdmissible_: The level admissibility property applies to the final transform of the marked sequence. Its scheme, ideal, and boundary are the final data, and its structure map is the final projection composed with the original one. This is precisely the marked object in the conclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MonomialGeometryHypotheses.krullDimSucc_: Apply the dimension bound in the monomial geometry hypotheses to the marked sequence at its final stage. The sequence has the same stage schemes and length as its data, so this bounds the dimension of the stated final scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendRecursivePrincipalization_congr: Substitute the equal ideal and marking. The two recursive append constructions now have identical inputs and are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendRecursivePrincipalization_eq_appen: The dimension bound allows the recursive call and the markedness test returns d. Reading the successful branch of the conditional append gives the original sequence followed by d.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendRecursivePrincipalization_eq_self_: The dimension bound permits evaluation of the recursive sequence. The markedness test returns no data, so the conditional append returns the input sequence.

Evaluate the dimension test. If it fails, the result is the starting sequence. If it succeeds, evaluate the markedness test of the assigned sequence. A failed test again returns the starting sequence, while a successful test supplies a marked tail and returns its append.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendRecursive_proj_center_ne_of_orderA: If the dimension test fails or the recursive sequence fails its markedness test, the result is the original sequence. There could then be no index at or beyond the original length strictly smaller than the resulting length. Thus the stated index belongs to a successful append. Apply the image-disjointness result for centers of such an append to the empty pulled back locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_proj_center_ne_base_of_orderAtLea: The appended center point projects via a point x of the locus of J on the final lower scheme. If its further image were the image of an upper base point, the final pullback square would lift this pair to a point of the final upper scheme. Order invariance in that square gives order at least μ for the pullback of J at the lifted point. This contradicts emptiness of that locus, so the two images differ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_comp_comp_apply: The underlying point map of a composite is the composite of the underlying point maps. Evaluate the three arrows in their order of application at a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_pow_sup_pow: Ideal pullback preserves sums and powers. Apply these properties to the sum of the two powers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionContinues_of_pull: The upper continuation condition gives a maximum on the upper marked locus of at least one. The pullback bound makes this maximum at most the lower one, so the lower maximum is also at least one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdeal_eq_comap_lastMap_of_pullb: The last ideal and its nonmonomial factor both pull back along the final comparison. The exponents in the companion ideal agree because the markings and the maxima on the marked loci agree. Pullback preserves the two powers and their sum, giving the desired companion ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_orderAtLeastLocus_of_mem_cent:
At the joining index, the center is the first center of the appended sequence transported by its initial isomorphism and the join identification. A point of this center corresponds to a point at the first tail stage of order at least μ for the tail ideal. Projecting this point to the joining scheme puts it in the locus of J, and the projection formula for the append identifies its original ambient image with that of z.

After the join, shift the index by the prefix length. The center point corresponds to a point of the tail center at that index, hence belongs to the tail stage's marked order locus. Its projection to the joining scheme belongs to the locus of J by the order-locus comparison. The projection of the append factors through this tail projection and the prefix's last projection, giving the claimed equality of images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_mk_congr: Substitute the equal ideal and marking. All remaining fields were already fixed, so admissibility is the same proposition for both constructions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_tripleAtLength_congr: The final marked objects differ through the given ideal and marking, which are equal by assumption. Substituting the equalities transfers admissibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastNonMonomialPart_eq_comap_lastMap_of_: The final lower object is admissible and its dimension is bounded by that of the original object. This makes the comparison of the final stages a marked pullback square. By the final ideal and marking identities the upstairs object is admissible with the corresponding pullback ideal, and the last boundaries are equivalent. The nonmonomial part clause of base-change compatibility therefore gives the equality of the final factors.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomialOnOrderLocus_le_of_pu: The final ideal and its nonmonomial factor both pull back. Order compatibility in the final square gives equality of the respective orders at an upper point and its lower image. Since the markings agree, a point of the upper marked locus maps into the lower marked locus. Thus each natural number witnessed by the upper nonmonomial order there is bounded by the lower maximum on that locus. Taking the supremum gives the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderNonMonomial_le_of_pullback: The last upper nonmonomial factor is the pullback of the lower one. The final pullback square and order compatibility identify its order at an upper point with the lower order at the image. The lower maximum bounds that value. Therefore every natural number witnessed by an upper point is at most the lower maximum, so its supremum has the same bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderOn_le_of_forall: Every element of the set defining the maximum on S is a natural number witnessed by a point of S with order at least that number. The given hypothesis bounds each such number by K. Hence their supremum is at most K.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natCast_le_of_natCast_mul_le_mul: If a is infinite, the bound by a holds automatically. Otherwise write a as a natural number. Commute the factors on the left so both sides have the positive factor p. Cancelling this factor in the natural-number inequality gives m at most a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionContinues_of_pu: The upper maximum is bounded by the lower maximum, so the common marking is at most the lower maximum. The upper continuation condition supplies a point, whose image shows the lower final scheme is nonempty. The lower nonmonomial order is bounded by its finite maximum. Hence that maximum is attained and its locus is nonempty, giving the second continuation condition downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_appen: The geometric dimension bounds permit both recursive calls. The hypothesis on the markedness tests gives either two failed tests or two successful tests. In the failed case both appends leave the existing comparison unchanged. In the successful case the final marked pullback square, admissibility, order and dimension conditions, and boundary equivalence let the assignment's base-change rule compare the two recursive sequences. Their underlying blowup comparison persists after giving them the original markings. Append that comparison to the existing comparison to obtain the required one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_exten: The equality of the maxima and of the original markings gives equal companion markings. The companion ideal comparison identifies the upper companion ideal with the pullback of the lower one. Both companion triples are admissible by continuation, and the lower companion ideal has order bounded by its marking. The recursive append comparison now applies using the simultaneous markedness tests. These appends are the stated companion extensions after substituting the ideal and marking identities.

The nonmonomial continuation conditions give admissibility of both final nonmonomial objects. The upper final nonmonomial ideal is the pullback of the lower one, and the equal maxima give the same marking. The lower maximum bounds all lower orders. With these identifications, the simultaneous markedness-test assumption is the one in the recursive append comparison. Apply it and identify those appends with the two nonmonomial extensions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_of_ma: Each given output is present, so each markedness test has succeeded. Uniqueness of a present value identifies d and d′ with the reassigned marked data for the two sequences. Reassigning those markings keeps the underlying blowup data, and the conversion of a sequence comparison to its underlying data supplies the required comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_sequenceOfBlowupsPullback_of_or: If the recursive operation leaves the lower sequence unchanged, retain the given pullback comparison. If it appends a tail, the empty pulled back order locus guarantees that the projections of all appended center points miss the image of the upper base. The marked append has the underlying append of blowup data with the same centers and projections. The comparison theorem for an appended tail with centers missing the upper image therefore extends the lower side while retaining the existing upper sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_companionIdeal_e: The pulled back lower companion ideal is the sum of the powers of the upper nonmonomial factor and upper final ideal, with the lower exponents. The lower maximum is positive by the strict inequality, and the marking is positive. If a point attained the lower companion threshold, the minimum formula would make both weighted orders at least that threshold. Cancelling the respective positive exponents shows that the point lies in the upper marked order locus and its nonmonomial order there is at least the lower maximum. This exceeds the upper maximum on that locus, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eq_empty_of_base: A point in the pulled back marked locus would have order at least the marking. Order compatibility gives the same order at its image, placing that image in the original empty locus. Thus the pulled back locus is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_lastNonMonomialP: Identify the pulled back lower factor with the upper nonmonomial factor. Its order at every point is at most the upper maximum, which is strictly less than the lower maximum. Hence no point reaches the lower threshold.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_sSup_nonempty: Zero belongs to the defining set because the scheme has the point x₀. The assumed order bound makes the supremum a finite upper bound for every natural number in the set. A nonempty bounded set of natural numbers contains its supremum. The point witnessing that membership is in the order locus at the supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_of_baseChangeCompatible: Use the marked pullback square whose lower map is the identity of the original scheme. Its vertical map is g, so the order comparison in the base-change compatibility gives the stated pointwise equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_sup_pow_eq_comap_pow_sup_pow: Replace the two upper ideals by the pullbacks and identify their exponents with the lower ones. Pullback commutes with the sum and both powers, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_mem_orderAtLeastLocus_t: Admissibility of the starting triple gives admissibility at every stage. The order-locus inclusion along the transition to stage zero sends z into the stage-zero locus at μ. The initial ideal is pulled back from J along the initial isomorphism, so its order locus is the inverse image of the locus of J. The projection to the starting scheme passes through that isomorphism, and its image of z therefore lies in the locus of J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_eq_mk: The stage transform is defined using the stage scheme, its projection followed by the original structure map, the current ideal and boundary, and the unchanged marking. These are exactly the fields shown.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPullbackBlowupSequence.nonempty_sequen: Use the given matching, and take each comparison to be the given stage isomorphism followed by the second pullback projection. The index conditions follow from the matching, and the first projection condition and the stage isomorphism give the required pullback squares. Postcomposing compatibility of the stage isomorphisms with the second projection gives the step equation, because the induced transition on pullbacks projects to the lower transition. The center equation is part of the given relation. Each matched lower center has nonempty support after pullback, and transporting that support across the stage isomorphism makes the corresponding upper center proper. Finally, a lower center point sharing its image with an upper base point would lift to a point of the canonical pullback in the support of the pulled-back center. The support criterion would then match this lower index, contrary to its omission.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_comp_concatObjAddI: At offset zero the comparison includes the inverse initial isomorphism of the second sequence, so use the blowup identity at the join. At every positive offset use the identity for an appended blowup strictly beyond the join. These cases exhaust the blowups of the second sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_succ_comp_concatOb: At a positive offset from the join the appended morphism is the blowup of the second sequence at that offset, transported along the two stage identifications. Subtracting the length of the first sequence recovers the offset. Composing with the comparison at the target cancels the target transport and leaves the comparison at the source followed by the same blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_blowupMorphism_zero_comp_concatOb: At the join, the appended blowup is the first blowup of the second sequence followed by the isomorphism from its initial stage to the last stage of the first sequence, using the designated identifications at the source and target. The comparison at the join uses the inverse initial isomorphism. Cancelling this pair and the intervening scheme identifications leaves the comparison at stage one followed by the first blowup of the second sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_eq_comap_concatMap: Before the upper join, both centers are transported from the first sequences. Pull the lower center back along the appended comparison and cancel the inverse identifications of the lower stages. The first comparison gives the upper first-sequence center, and the remaining upper identification gives the appended center. At or beyond the join, express each center as the pullback of its second-sequence center along the stage isomorphism. The appended comparison followed by the lower stage isomorphism is the upper stage isomorphism followed by the second comparison. Thus the second comparison's center equation and functoriality of pullback give the appended center equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_length_add: At the join the appended center is obtained from the first center of the second sequence via the inverse initial isomorphism and the identification of the joining scheme. Functoriality of ideal pullback makes this the pullback along the stage comparison. At any positive offset the appended center is the center of the second sequence at the index obtained by subtracting the first length, pulled back along the stage identification. This index is exactly the positive offset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_center_ne_top: Before the upper join the center is transported from the upper first sequence, where it is proper by the first comparison. At the join, the given bound guarantees the second sequence has a first blowup. Its center is proper by the second comparison, and the appended center is its pullback along the inverse initial isomorphism and the scheme identification. After the join the center comes from the corresponding positive offset of the second sequence, again proper by the second comparison. Each transport is an isomorphism, so all these centers remain proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_eq_of_eq_length_: Replace the index by the first length plus the stated offset. The change of identification for this equality is then the identity. Apply the factorization of the appended projection through the second sequence and the last stage of the first, which also holds after reconstruction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_eq_of_le_length: Use the equality of indices to work at the earlier index. The append preserves the first sequence at stages up to its end, so the projection is the projection of the first sequence preceded by the identification of the stage schemes. Reconstruction preserves these projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_length_add: At offset zero the formula is the projection at the join. At a positive offset it is the projection from a stage strictly beyond the join. The two preceding identities give the same factorization in their respective cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_length_add_succ: The positive offset places the stage beyond the join. Its projection thus goes through the second sequence at the index obtained by subtracting the first length, then through the final projection of the first sequence. The difference is the stated positive offset, and the initial change of identification is exactly the comparison at that offset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_length_add_zero: At the join the projection is the projection of the last stage of the first sequence under its identification with the appended stage. The comparison with the second sequence then applies the inverse initial isomorphism, while the second projection at stage zero applies that initial isomorphism. These two maps cancel, giving the join projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_projectionToBase_ne_of_forall_con: Suppose a point on an omitted lower center projects to the image of an upper base point. Before the lower join, identify the center and projection with those of the first sequence. A first-sequence match would also be an appended match, so the omission condition for the first comparison excludes this common image. At or after the lower join, use the lower stage isomorphism to take the center point to the corresponding center in the second sequence. Its projection to the lower joining scheme and the upper base point have the same image in the lower base by the projection factorization. The last-stage pullback square of the first comparison lifts them to a point of the upper joining scheme. The offset of the lower center is omitted in the second comparison, since a match at any upper second offset would give an appended match. The lifted point and the lower center point now contradict the omission condition for the second comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_concatIndex_of_le: At or after the upper join, the matching index is the lower first length plus the lower second-sequence match of the upper offset. Taking the lower appended scheme at this expression gives the same scheme as taking it at the matching index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_concatIndex_of_lt: The matched index is that of the first comparison and is strictly below the length of the lower first sequence. At that index the lower append uses the scheme of the lower first sequence, giving the identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_eq_length_add_sub: At or beyond the join, subtracting the first length and then adding it recovers the index. Taking the scheme at the two equal indices gives the identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_length_add_succ: This stage is strictly beyond the end of the first sequence. There the appended sequence uses the second sequence, with its index obtained by subtracting the length of the first. The resulting index is the given positive index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_schemeAt_length_add_zero: Adding zero to the length of the first sequence leaves its length. The appended sequence agrees with the first one through that stage, so the scheme is the last scheme of the first sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_transitionMap_comp_concatObjAddIs: Induct on the number of steps in the transition. At distance zero both transitions are identities. For the next step, split off the last blowup, commute the preceding transition past its stage comparison by induction, and commute the last blowup past its comparison by the adjacent-stage identity. The resulting blowups on the second sequence compose to its full transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_transitionMap_of_le_length: Induct on the distance between the chosen stages. At distance zero both transitions are identities and the scheme identifications cancel. For a longer transition, split off the last adjacent blowup. It is a blowup of the first sequence under the stage identifications because its source lies at or before the join. Substitute the induction formula for the shorter transition, cancel the identifications at the intermediate stage, and compose the two first-sequence transitions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_concatMap: If both upper stages precede the join, their lower matches lie in the lower first sequence. Identify the appended maps with those of the first comparison and apply its step equation. If the second upper stage is the join, its second-sequence comparison starts at offset zero. Split the lower transition at the lower join, and use the stage-zero square of the second comparison to replace the initial second-sequence composite by the last map of the first comparison. The upper initial isomorphism cancels its inverse, reducing the result to the last step equation of the first comparison. If both upper stages are at or after the join, write their offsets as consecutive integers. The stage isomorphisms carry the blowup and the lower transition to those in the second sequences. The step equation of the second comparison then gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_lowerMap: Use the compatibility of the first comparison with a blowup in the upper first sequence. The corresponding lower transition goes between the two matched lower stages, and the comparisons are the same maps on the reconstructed sequences and the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_lowerMap_assoc: The step equation for the first comparison equates the two maps to the earlier lower stage. Compose each with the given map out of that stage and reassociate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_upperMap: Apply the step equation for the second comparison, whose base morphism is the last-stage map of the first comparison. The adjacent upper blowup is the stored morphism and the lower transition runs between the matched second-sequence indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_upperMap_assoc: Postcompose the step equation for the second comparison with the given morphism from the earlier lower stage. Associativity gives the displayed composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_blowupMorphism_comp_m: Apply the step equation of the pullback comparison at the given upper index. Reconstruction uses the stored upper blowup as its adjacent transition and the reconstructed lower transition as the transition on the data. Those identifications give the stated equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_index_lt_index_succ: The bound on the upper index holds in the reconstructed sequence because reconstruction preserves the length. Apply the strict-increase condition of the pullback data to this consecutive pair.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_index_lt_length: Reconstructing a sequence preserves its length. Thus the given index is before the end of the upper sequence. Its match is before the end of the lower sequence by the pullback data, and this is also the length stored in the lower data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_comp_eqToHom: After identifying the indices the final identification morphism is the identity. Composing with it leaves the original morphism and the same ideal to pull back.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_comp_eqToHom_congr: Identify the two center indices. The ideals and their final scheme identification morphisms coincide. The preceding maps are the same, so the pullback ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_eqToHom_congr: Substitute the equality of indices. The centers are then the same ideal sheaf, and the morphisms for the two scheme identifications coincide. The two pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_ne_top: Equality of the schemes gives an isomorphism whose forward map is the stated identification. Pullback along an isomorphism preserves nonempty support and hence preserves a proper ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iso_hom_ne_top: Choose a point of the support of the proper ideal. The inverse isomorphism gives a point upstairs whose image is the chosen point. The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the support, so this point lies in the support upstairs. The pulled-back ideal is therefore proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_assoc_inner_pair: Combine the second and third morphisms using associativity. The full composite is unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_assoc_outer: Both sides compose the same five morphisms in the same order. Successive applications of associativity give the displayed grouping.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_comp_eqToHom_comp_eqToHom: Identify the last two schemes using their equality. The two changes of identification are inverse and compose to the identity, leaving the first two morphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_comp_inv_comp_hom: Reassociate so that the inverse isomorphism and its forward morphism are adjacent. Their composite is the identity, leaving the first two morphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatIndex_length_add_length: At the last upper stage the offset beyond the upper first sequence is the full length of the upper second sequence. The second comparison matches that to the full length of the lower second sequence. Adding the lower first length gives the last lower stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatIndex_lt_concatIndex_succ: If both indices precede the upper join, the first comparison is strictly increasing at this step. If the step crosses the join, the first match is below the lower first length and the second is at least that length. If both indices are at or beyond the join, their offsets differ by one, so the second comparison is strictly increasing and adding the same lower first length preserves the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatIndex_lt_length_add_length: Before the upper join the matched index is below the lower first length, hence below the total. At or after the join, subtract the upper first length to get an offset strictly below the upper second length. The second comparison matches this to an offset strictly below the lower second length. Adding the lower first length gives the desired strict bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatIndex_of_ge: At or after the join, subtract the length of the upper first sequence to get an index in the upper second sequence. Match that index in the lower second sequence and add the length of the lower first sequence to express it as an index in the append.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatIndex_of_lt: Before the end of the upper first sequence, the matching for the append uses the matching of the two first sequences. This gives the original lower index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatMapAddLength_comp_concatObjAddIso_: The appended comparison at the given offset is formed by the upper stage isomorphism, the second-sequence comparison and the inverse lower stage isomorphism. Postcomposing with the lower stage isomorphism cancels its inverse, leaving the first two maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatMapAddLength_congr: Replace the two offsets by their common value. The source identification becomes the identity, and the two comparisons and their target identifications coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatMap_eq_lowerMap_of_lt: Before the upper join the definition chooses the first comparison. Its source and target identifications are the specified identifications between the two first sequences and the appended stages, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatMap_eq_map_of_lt: Before the upper join the comparison is obtained by identifying the source with the upper first stage, using the first comparison, and identifying the lower first stage with its stage in the append. This is the first branch of the comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatMap_eq_upperConcatMap_of_le: At or after the upper join the definition takes the comparison of the second sequences at the difference between the stage index and the upper first length. Replace that difference by the equal given offset. The corresponding endpoint identifications give the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjAddIso_inv_comp_transitionMap: Start with the commuting square for the direct comparisons of the two stages. Precompose it with the inverse of the later comparison and postcompose it with the inverse of the earlier comparison. Cancelling both inverse pairs gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjAddIso_inv_comp_transitionMap_a: The inverse comparison commutes with the transition between the two stages. Postcompose this equality with the given morphism out of the earlier appended stage and use associativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjAddIso_inv_comp_transitionMap_o: Split the appended transition at the join. The inverse comparison carries the first segment to the transition in the second sequence down to stage zero, followed by the inverse comparison at the join. That inverse uses the initial isomorphism to reach the last stage of the first sequence. The remaining segment is a transition of the first sequence transported by the stage identifications. Cancel the two identifications at the join to obtain the formula.
Apply the factorization of the inverse comparison followed by the transition across the join. Postcompose the factorization with the given morphism out of the earlier appended stage and reassociate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatObjAddIso_zero_hom: At offset zero the appended stage is identified with the last scheme of the first sequence. The comparison then uses the inverse initial isomorphism to reach the zero stage of the second sequence. Its forward morphism is this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_blowupMorphism_congr: Use the equality of indices to identify the two stages and their blowup morphisms. The opposite changes of identification at the target then cancel, and the two changes at the source come from the same equality. The composites coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_blowupMorphism_zero_isoObjZ: The two changes of scheme identification following the initial isomorphism are inverses. After they cancel, the initial isomorphism and its inverse are adjacent and cancel as well. The remaining change of identification at the source is the unique one coming from the given equality of schemes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_projectionToBase_length_add: Adding zero leaves the index equal to the length. The two changes of scheme identification and the two projections therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_support_of_ne_top: An ideal sheaf has empty support exactly when it is the unit ideal. Since this ideal is proper, its support contains a point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_preimage_of_isPullback: Two points with the same image have a lift to the canonical scheme pullback with those projections. Carry this lift to the given pullback by the inverse of the canonical isomorphism. This inverse intertwines the given first projection with the canonical first projection, so the resulting point projects to the required point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_length_eq_length: The last upper index is matched to the last lower one. Reconstruction leaves both lengths equal to those of the original data, giving the same equality for the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_index_of_lt: Induct on the later index. There is no smaller natural number in the zero case. At a successor, strict increase from its predecessor is part of the data. A smaller index either is the predecessor or lies before it. In the latter case compose the strict inequality from induction with the last strict increase.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_append_of_two_f: For each field, passing from a marked append to its unmarked blowups gives the append of the unmarked factors. The concatenation of the two comparisons is a construction on these unmarked schemes and morphisms over the given base map, so it applies with either field for the markings. Passing from its comparison data to the pullback relation proves the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_append_same_fie: Forget the markings on both pairs of sequences. The underlying blowups of a marked append are the append of its underlying blowups. Compose the two given pullback comparisons by the append construction, which uses the last-stage comparison of the first pair as the base map for the second. The resulting stage data give the asserted pullback relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups: Use the given matching indices and the canonical isomorphisms supplied by the stage squares. Strict increase for any two stages follows from strict increase at consecutive ones, and the bounds and final index come from the data. If a lower center is omitted, a point in its pulled-back support would give an upper base point and a lower center point with equal image, contrary to the omission condition. If a lower center is matched, its pullback has nonempty support because its further pullback under the stage isomorphism is the specified proper upper center. The stage isomorphisms preserve the maps to the upper base by the first projection formula. They preserve transitions because the two composites into the pullback have equal first projections by transitivity of the base projection and equal second projections by the step equation. The center equation follows from the second projection formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_comp_eqToHom: Identify the two indices using their equality. Their stage schemes and their projections coincide, and the intervening identification morphism becomes the identity. The new square is the original pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_comp_iso_hom: The isomorphism on the top right and the identity on the lower right form a pullback square, with the projection from the replacement scheme obtained using the inverse isomorphism. Paste this on the right of the original square to obtain the new one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_concatMap: Before the upper join, the new comparison is the first comparison transported by the appended stage identifications, which also carry the projections to the base. At or beyond the join, the comparison for the second sequences gives a pullback square over the last-stage map of the first comparison. Paste it vertically with the last-stage pullback square of the first comparison. The resulting projections are the successive projections through the second and first sequences. Transport the stage schemes to the corresponding appended stages. The projection factorization and the definition of the comparison identify the resulting square with the stated one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_iso_hom_comp: The isomorphism on the source and the identity on its base form a pullback square for the source projection. Paste this square horizontally with the given pullback square. The pasted maps are the two given maps precomposed with the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_lastMap: The pullback data give a pullback square at the last upper stage. Its matching lower index is the last lower index. Transport the lower stage along this equality to get the square with the designated last-stage map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_iso: First transport the right-hand scheme along its isomorphism, using its inverse to adjust the projection. Then transport the upper left scheme, precomposing its two arrows by the source isomorphism. Both transports preserve the pullback property, and the prescribed equalities identify the resulting maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastMap_eq_lowerMap: The last-stage map is defined by taking the comparison at the last upper stage and then identifying the matched lower stage with the last lower stage. The matching of endpoints supplies precisely that identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lowerMap_congr: Identify the two upper indices by their equality. This also identifies their matched lower indices, so both scheme identification morphisms are identities and the comparison maps coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_toSequenceOfBlowups_center_support: The reconstructed sequence retains the ideal of the center at every index. Its support is therefore the same set, and the given point belongs to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_append_length_add: At offset zero, the projection is the projection of the last stage of the first sequence under the scheme identification. In the proposed factorization the inverse initial isomorphism of the second sequence cancels its stage-zero projection, giving this same map. For a successor offset, factor through the preceding appended stage by its blowup. Substitute the induction formula and use the adjacent-stage comparison to move that blowup into the second sequence. There the blowup followed by the preceding projection is exactly the successor projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackIso_hom_fst: Order the factors with the upper base first. The canonical isomorphism from the upper stage to the pullback is induced by the upper projection and the comparison to the lower stage. Its composite with the first projection is therefore the upper projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackIso_hom_snd: The canonical isomorphism from the upper stage to the pullback is induced by the upper projection and the comparison to the lower stage. The universal property identifies its composite with the second projection as that comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullback_condition_base_apply: The two composites from the pullback to the common target agree by the pullback square. Evaluating their underlying maps at the given point equates the two images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sub_length_le_of_le_length_add: The total length is the first length plus the second length. Subtracting the first length from the upper bound gives the second length. If the index lies before the join, the nonnegative difference is zero and the bound still holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_blowupMorphism_comp_: The reconstructed upper sequence uses the stored appended morphism for the step. The lower transition is the one in the data at the given matched indices. Apply the appended step equation on the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_transitionMap: The transition on the data is defined as the transition on the reconstructed sequence, so the two descriptions give the same morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_comp_transitionMap: A transition from a later stage to an earlier one is the composite of the intervening blowups. Cutting this string at an intermediate stage and composing the two pieces gives the full transition by associativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_congr: Substitute the equalities of both endpoint indices. The scheme identifications become identities and the two transitions are the composite over the same interval.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_refl: The transition from a stage to itself is the empty composite of blowup morphisms. The empty composite is the identity of that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_succ: A transition between adjacent stages contains exactly one blowup morphism. The reconstructed sequence uses the morphism stored at that position in the data, so the transition equals that morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_zero_comp_isoObjZero_hom: In the reconstructed sequence the projection to the base is the transition to stage zero followed by the initial isomorphism to the base. Reconstruction preserves the projection, transition and initial isomorphism, giving the formula on the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.upperConcatMap_congr: Use the equality of offsets to identify the two instances of the second comparison. The endpoint scheme identifications are those associated to the same equalities on both sides. Hence the full composites agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.upperMap_zero_comp_isoObjZero: The pullback square for stage zero of the upper second sequence commutes. The projection from the matched lower stage is the transition to stage zero followed by the lower initial isomorphism. The projection at upper stage zero is the upper initial isomorphism. Substituting these two expressions into the commutative square gives the equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.upperMap_zero_comp_isoObjZero_assoc: Use the stage-zero equation for the second comparison, then postcompose both sides with the given map from the last lower stage of the first sequence. Reassociate the composites.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPrefix.refl: Use the identical length and stage schemes. The induced stage maps are identities, so the projections and transitions commute with them and the pullbacks fix the stage ideals, boundary entries, and centers. These are the prefix conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPrefix.trans: The length bounds compose, and the stage identifications compose at all indices through the first sequence's end. For the projections and transitions, paste the two comparison diagrams. For the ideals, boundaries, and centers, the two pullbacks equal pullback along the composed stage identifications. The index bounds ensure the two comparisons apply wherever needed. This gives all the prefix conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendRecursivePrincipalization_eq_appen: The dimension bound allows the recursive call. The resulting blowup data meet the supplied markedness condition for the original final ideal, marking, and boundary. The marked-data construction therefore returns those data endowed with this marking. In the append operation this successful case appends that continuation.

The stated dimension bound permits the recursive principalization call on the final marked object with ideal J and marking μ. The definition then appends its sequence precisely through the operation that tests markedness for the original data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_blowupMorphism_comp_e: Substituting the equality of the data makes the blowup morphisms identical. The identifications at their two endpoints then induce identity maps, and both composites equal that morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequenceData_center_eq_comap_eqToH: Substitute the equality of the blowup data. The two centers at i then agree, and transporting along the resulting equality of the scheme with itself leaves the ideal unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_self: The map induced by a scheme's equality with itself is the identity. Pullback by that map fixes J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_trans: The comparison map for the composite equality is the composite of the two equality-induced maps. Successive pullbacks along these maps therefore give pullback along the composite equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eqToHom_eq_eqToHom_comp_of_eqToHom_: Identify the three source schemes by the given equalities and do the same for the targets. Every comparison map becomes an identity. The two hypotheses then give M equal to N and N equal to f. Reversing and composing these equalities gives the conclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionContinues_iff: The continuation condition is defined by positivity of the maximum order of the nonmonomial factor on the marked order locus. For a natural number this means it is at least one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionIter_eq_of_not_co: Start the induction at f, where the equality holds. If an iterate equals the one at f, its continuation condition fails as at f. The successor rule leaves it unchanged, so the equality holds at every later iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionIter_succ_of_cont: Under the continuation condition, the successor rule extends the current iterate by the recursive principalization of its companion ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionIter_succ_of_not_: If the companion continuation condition fails, the successor rule returns the current iterate unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReductionIter_zero: The companion iteration begins at the supplied sequence, so its zero iterate is that sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.companionIdealReduction_eq: The companion reduction starts from the completed nonmonomial reduction. The number of iterations is one more than the maximum order of that sequence's final nonmonomial part on its marked order locus. Evaluating this definition gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_eqToHom_comp_of_eq_eqToHom_symm_comp: Identify A with B using the given equality. The two equality-induced maps become identities, so the hypothesis becomes g equal to f. Symmetry gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPrefix_append: The length of the append is the sum of the lengths, so it is at least the first length. Through the joining stage, the appended scheme, projection, ideal, and boundary are the corresponding first-sequence data under the stage identification. Pulling back along the inverse identification gives the required orientation of the comparison. For steps strictly before the join, the center and transition also come from the first sequence. The marked append has the same underlying data as the unmarked append, so these comparisons apply to its centers and maps as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_eqToHom_self: The self-equality of the scheme induces the identity, which fixes every ideal under pullback. The entrywise pullback then fixes the whole list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_eqToHom_trans: Each entry transported through the two equalities equals that entry transported through their composite. The list orders agree, so equality entrywise proves equality of the lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionContinues_iff: By definition, a nonmonomial iteration continues when the maximum order of the final nonmonomial factor is at least the marking and the locus at that maximum is nonempty. The two conditions give precisely the displayed equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_eq_of_not_: Induct from iteration f. At f the equality is reflexive. If the later iterate equals the iterate at f, its continuation condition also fails. The successor rule therefore leaves it unchanged, proving the equality at the next index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_succ_of_co: When the continuation condition holds, the successor rule appends the reduction obtained using the current nonmonomial factor. This is exactly the stated extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_succ_of_no: When the continuation condition fails, the successor rule returns the previous sequence unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReductionIter_zero: The initial value of the nonmonomial iteration is the empty marked blowup sequence on the given object.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonMonomialOrderReduction_eq: The full nonmonomial reduction is defined by running its iteration for one more than the starting nonmonomial factor's maximum order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionData_eq: The construction appends monomial principalization to the companion reduction. The input to that principalization is the marked object at the end of the companion sequence with its final transformed ideal and the original marking. Passing to marked blowup data for this tail gives the stated append.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionSeq_eq_of_nonempty: A nonempty initial marked order locus rules out the empty-sequence branch of the definition. The remaining branch returns the marked sequence obtained from the order-reduction data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tripleAtLength_dim: The marked object at the end of the sequence uses the final stage scheme. Changing its ideal to J and its marking to μ leaves that scheme and its dimension the same.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeCompatible_of_smooth: Smoothness of g gives order invariance for its pullbacks. In each marked square the vertical map is smooth and respects the indicated structure maps. The lower dimension bound follows from the square's dimension comparison, and vertical order invariance preserves the order bound on the upper ideal. Thus the smooth compatibility of the order-reduction assignment gives the first sequence comparison. For monomial triples, apply smooth compatibility of monomial principalization to the same vertical map. For the nonmonomial part, the equivalence of boundaries gives admissibility for the actual pulled back boundary by boundary replacement. Apply the geometric formula for pullback of the nonmonomial part. These comparisons and the smooth order invariance give the required base-change data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_verticalMap_le_of_forall_o: Apply the vertical pullback order comparison to the ideal of the square and the bound by the marking at every point of the lower scheme. The resulting bound holds for the pulled back ideal at the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackOverField_isAdmissible_of_sameNo: The pulled back lower triple has the same scheme, structure map, ideal, and marking as the upper triple. Its boundary is the entrywise pullback of the lower boundary. By hypothesis this boundary and the chosen admissible boundary agree after dropping unit entries. The monomial geometry's boundary-replacement property therefore gives admissibility for the pulled back triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_verticalMap: The left map in the marked pullback square is the base change of the smooth map on the right. Smoothness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.verticalMap_comp_lowerStructMap: The lower structure map factors through the bottom map, and the given structure map on Y factors through g. The two composites then agree by commutativity of the pullback square.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformHypotheses_of_transformed: The two component descriptions are exactly the given hypotheses. The geometric results on component unions give smoothness and strict normal crossings of the center. The total-transform theorem supplies the local exceptional factor for each boundary divisor, and the incidence theorem says that a stratum component lies in a boundary divisor exactly when that divisor is indexed in the stratum. These results supply all remaining fields.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_baseField: The blown-up triple is constructed over the base field of the original triple. That field is its base field by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_boundary: The new boundary is defined by the strict transforms of the original boundary ideals in order, followed by the exceptional ideal of the blowup at the monomial center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_ideal: The ideal field of the blown-up triple is defined to be the supplied ideal on the blown-up scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_mult: The blowup changes the ideal and boundary and carries over the original mark. Thus the marks are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_scheme: The construction takes the source of the blowup morphism as the scheme of the new triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupTriple_structureMorphism: The given structural morphism from the blown-up scheme to the base field's spectrum is the one used in the new triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.card_preimageStrictTransformIndex_add_on: The strict-transform index map takes the preimage set onto the selected set with the exceptional index removed. Every old index maps to a position before the exceptional one, and each selected nonexceptional position has an old index. The map is injective, so the preimage has the cardinality of that smaller set. Adding the one removed member gives the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.card_preimageStrictTransformIndex_of_not: The strict-transform index map is injective and takes the preimage set onto the specified selection because it excludes the exceptional index. The preimage and selection therefore have the same cardinality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_foldr_mul: The empty list product is the unit ideal and so is its pullback. For a nonempty list, pullback preserves the product of the first factor with the product of the rest. Applying induction to the tail gives the product of all pulled-back factors.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_exceptionalIndex_or_exists_strictTran: The transformed boundary has the original length plus one. If the index is below the original length, the original index with that numeric value maps to it. Otherwise its value equals the original length and it is the exceptional index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIndex_not_mem_of_orderAlong_e: Suppose the exceptional index occurs in the maximizing upper selection. Its component's generic point maps to the lower center, and hence to a selected center component and to the cosupport where a local monomial expression exists. The exceptional order formula gives the upper component order plus the mark as the sum of the selected strict-transform exponents and the old center component order. Both component orders equal the common finite maximum, so the strict-transform exponents sum to the mark. The mark is positive and thus there is at least one old index in that sum. The image point belongs to all those old divisor supports, because a selected strict transform lies in the support of the total transform. Choose a component of their old intersection containing the image. Its order is the same sum of exponents, so it gives a positive-size lower candidate. Its cardinality is the upper selection's cardinality minus one, since the exceptional index was removed. This is below the common minimum, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_orderAt_comap_eq_strictTransform_: The local total-transform formula writes the pulled-back divisor ideal as the strict transform times the exceptional ideal to exponent ε. The exponent is zero or one and is one exactly when the center is locally contained in the divisor near the image point. Restriction to the open preserves orders at the given point. Additivity for products and the order formula for powers give the displayed local order equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_transformedBoundary_exceptionalIndex: The exceptional position equals the length of the initial list of strict transforms. It is therefore the first position in the appended singleton, whose entry is the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_transformedBoundary_strictTransformI: The index for the strict transform keeps the original numeric position. That position is in the initial list of strict transforms, before the appended exceptional ideal. Its entry is the strict transform of the original entry at that position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_strictTransformIndex_preimageStric: The image of the preimage selection is contained in the given selection by definition. Conversely, every selected index other than the exceptional one comes from an old index. Since the exceptional index is excluded, this gives a preimage for every selected index and the sets agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderCandidatePairs_ncard_lt_of_blowu: Send each maximizing upper pair to the preimage of its index selection and the closure of the image of its component. The upper selection excludes the exceptional index, so its cardinality is preserved. The transformed-component theorem makes the image closure a lower intersection component outside the center family, and describes the upper component as its strict transform. The generic points correspond off the exceptional divisor, so their orders agree. With equal minima and maxima the lower pair is again maximizing. The map is injective because the old indices recover the upper selection by the strict-transform index map, and the lower component recovers the upper one as its strict transform. The chosen lower selection has a maximizing component in the center. That pair is absent from the image because image components are outside the center family. The image is therefore a proper subset of the finite lower maximizing family, so the upper family has strictly smaller cardinality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAlong_transform_add_mult_of_excepti: Evaluate at the generic point of the upper intersection component. It lies on the exceptional divisor, whose ideal has order one. Thus the controlled-transform identity makes the total order equal to the transformed order plus the mark. Pull back the given local monomial expression to the inverse-image open. Orders add across the factors, so each old exponent is weighted by the order of the corresponding pulled-back divisor. Its strict transform has order one precisely when the strict-transform index is selected upstairs. The exceptional contribution is one precisely when the center is locally contained in the old divisor near the image point. This condition holds for every chosen center index.
