Irreducibility would place it inside one removed piece, and maximality would make that piece equal to it, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_of_specializes_of_isBlowupAl: Restrict the blowup to the complement of the center. There the center ideal is the unit ideal, so the restriction is an isomorphism. Both specified target points lie in this complement. Use its homeomorphism with the preimage to lift the more general point and carry the given specialization back upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_specializes_of_homeomorph: Take the inverse image of the specified target point under the homeomorphism of subspaces. Its ambient image is the specified point by the compatibility of the homeomorphism with the underlying map. The image of y also belongs to the closure of the target point in the target subspace, because subspace closure is the intersection with ambient closure. The inverse homeomorphism carries the singleton closure back to the source subspace. Passing to the ambient space gives the desired specialization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_exceptionalIdeal: The exceptional ideal is the pullback of the center ideal. Its support is the inverse image of the support of the center. Since the image of y lies outside the latter, y lies outside the exceptional support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.genericPoint_notMem_support_exceptionalI: Suppose the generic point lies on the exceptional divisor. Near it the transformed boundary has strict normal-crossing coordinates. Each selected strict transform through the point is given by one of these coordinates, and the exceptional divisor is given by a distinct coordinate. Thus the intersection ideal on the chart is generated by the selected coordinates, excluding the exceptional one. Choose an open that meets the intersection support only in the given component. It contains the generic point, so restrict to an affine neighborhood inside this open and the chart. The assumed exceptional support is closed and contains the generic point, hence contains the whole component and thus the intersection on this affine neighborhood. But the extra coordinate is a nonzerodivisor modulo the selected coordinate ideal, by étale flatness from the polynomial chart. The prime containing the selected coordinates at the point has a generalization that still contains them and omits the exceptional coordinate. This contradicts the asserted containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_length_map_strictTransform_appen: The list of strict transforms has the same length as the original boundary. The index equal to that length is the first index of the appended singleton, which contains the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_map_strictTransform_append_of_lt: Mapping the list to the strict transforms preserves its length. The given index lies in this first list, so appending the exceptional entry does not affect its value. The value there is the strict transform of the original entry at the same index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.intersectionComponents_transformedBounda: The center, being a union of components of a boundary intersection, has strict normal crossings with the boundary. The generic-point argument puts the given upper component's generic point off the exceptional support. Its image is then outside the center and lies in the old selected intersection. The closure of the image is irreducible and contained in that intersection. If a larger irreducible set existed there, a generic point of its closure would generalize the image and hence lie outside the center. Lift it through the blowup isomorphism off the center. Its closure is in the transformed intersection and contains the given upper component, so maximality forces equality. Mapping back places the larger set inside the closure of the original image. The resulting downstairs component is unselected, since every selected component lies inside the center. Off the exceptional divisor the same isomorphism identifies the preimage of this component with the part of the given upper component there, by lifting specializations of the image point. Its closure is the full upper component since it contains the upper generic point. Finally, uniqueness of generic points makes the image equal to any generic point of the downstairs component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_intersectionIdeal_iff: The support of a sum of two ideals is the intersection of their supports, since both ideals must lie in the maximal ideal of the stalk. Apply this fact inductively to the finite sum. For the empty sum the zero ideal has full support, as required by the vacuous membership condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_intersectionIdeal_transforme: Membership in the support of the new intersection ideal is membership in every selected transformed boundary support. These selected indices are exactly the images of the old indices, and the ideal at each image index is the strict transform of the corresponding old ideal. This identifies the two membership conditions.

Test each intersection by membership in every selected boundary support. The selected transformed indices are the images of the old ones, and the ideal at such an index is the corresponding strict transform. Because the point maps outside the center, membership in each strict transform is equivalent to membership of its image in the corresponding old divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_strictTransform_iff_of_notMe: The strict-transform support is the closure of the preimage of the divisor support outside the center. That preimage lies in the closed inverse image of the full divisor support, so its closure lies there too. Conversely, if the given point maps into the divisor support and outside the center, it already lies in the preimage whose closure defines the support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformedBoundary_get_strictTransformI: The strict-transform index has the same numeric position as the old boundary index. This position lies in the initial list of transformed ideals, and its entry is the strict transform of the original boundary ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.add_mem_eqModIdealSet: The difference of the images of the sum is the sum of the two differences. Each is in the ideal, so their sum is too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_congr_hom: Replace the two morphisms by their common value. They induce the same map on sections of the specified opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_top_top: The inverse image of the whole target is the whole source. The restricted map on sections thus has the same domain and codomain as the map on global sections and agrees with it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_lift_affineBlowupChart_apply: The lift to the affine chart followed by the chart inclusion equals the stated composite to the blowup. On sections this factors the induced map through the chart section isomorphism and then the map of the lift. The chart section isomorphism identifies the pullback of a chart element with its global section on the affine chart. Evaluating the factorization gives the same section as applying the map to the blowup and then restricting to the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.app_subschemeι_eq_zero_of_mem_ideal: The section map of the closed immersion is the quotient map followed by the identification of the quotient section ring. An element of the ideal has zero quotient class, hence maps to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartFraction_sub_mem_of_congr: Let the multiplier relating the two images of the chart generator be u. The congruence at the generator says their difference is the first image of the generator times an element of the error ideal. Cancellation of the nonzerodivisor shows that one minus u belongs to that ideal. At a numerator from the center ideal, express each of its images as its chart fraction times the corresponding generator image. Substitute these into the congruence for the numerator and cancel the first generator image. The first fraction image minus u times the second then belongs to the error ideal. Subtracting the second fraction image changes this difference by a multiple of one minus u, which is also in the error ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartSectionsRingHom_sub_mem: The chart ring is generated by the images of base elements and the chart fractions. On base elements the stated difference lies in the product with the error ideal and hence in the error ideal. On chart fractions the fraction comparison gives the same containment by cancellation of the generator. The elements satisfying the congruence form a subring containing these generators, so the congruence holds throughout the chart ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closure_chartRingHom_union_chartFraction: For any chart element, multiplication by a power of the chart generator gives the image of a coefficient in the corresponding ideal power. That coefficient image is also the same generator power times an element of the generated subring. The generator is a nonzerodivisor on its chart, so its power cancels and the original element belongs to the generated subring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eq_of_chartSectionsRingHom_sub_mem: On the indicated open of the closed subscheme, both maps factor through the same affine blowup chart because their images lie in it. Every difference of the two induced images of a chart element lies in the ideal of the closed subscheme. Pulling back sections to the closed subscheme kills these differences. The two factorizations therefore give the same map on global sections of the affine chart, and hence are equal as morphisms to it. Composing with the chart inclusion gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eq_on_chart_of_mul_eq_of_agree: On the common chart the images of the chart generator span the two pulled-back center ideals. Equality of those ideals makes the second generator image a multiple of the first. Agreement on the original closed subscheme gives congruence of the base sections modulo the product of the first generator with the second ideal. Apply the chart ring congruence, using that the first generator is a nonzerodivisor. The chart maps then agree on the closed subscheme of the second ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_mul_pow_zero: The zeroth power is one, so multiplying by it fixes the element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_common_chart_affineOpen: Choose an affine neighborhood of the point where the first lift lands in a blowup chart and the chart generator pulls back to a nonzerodivisor. The congruence on the original closed subscheme and the factorization of its ideal express the second generator image as the first multiplied by one minus a section from the second ideal. Restrict to the basic open where this multiplier is invertible. Its restriction to the closed subscheme of the second ideal is one, so this shrinking leaves the inverse image open on that closed subscheme unchanged. Localization preserves the nonzerodivisor, and the multiplier is now a unit, so the second generator also spans the common center ideal on the smaller open. The criterion for membership in the blowup chart puts the second lift in the same chart there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_closure_chartRingHom_eq_mul_p: At exponent zero take the image of the given ring element in the generated subring. At a successor, the ideal power consists of sums of products of an element from the previous power and an element of the ideal. For a product, the first factor has the required expression by induction and the second is its chart fraction times the chart generator. Multiply the expressions to get the next power of the generator. Sums of these products retain the same factor and their coefficients lie in the generated subring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_eq: Write the chart element as a homogeneous fraction with denominator a power of the Rees generator, say of exponent n. If the numerator and denominator are represented in degree n, the numerator is a degree-n monomial with coefficient in the nth power of the ideal. Multiplying the fraction by the nth power of the chart image of the generator yields the chart image of this coefficient by cross multiplication. If the recorded homogeneous degree differs from n, the degree-n coefficient of the denominator is zero. This is the nth power of the original generator in the base ring. Both sides of the desired equality are then zero by taking the coefficient to be zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.localization_mk_eq_mk_one_of_eq_mul: Substitute the expression for the numerator into the fraction. Its denominator belongs to the localized multiplicative set, so cancellation gives the fraction with denominator one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_ideal_of_app_subschemeι_eq_zero: On the affine open the map of sections to the closed subscheme identifies with quotient by the ideal of sections. If the image is zero, the quotient class is zero, so the section belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_add_mul_eq_add_mul: Apply right distributivity to the product of the sum and the common factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_mem_eqModIdealSet: Expand the difference of the two products as the first image of the first factor times the difference of the second images, plus the difference of the first images times the second image of the second factor. Each summand is a ring multiple of an element of the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.neg_mem_eqModIdealSet: Applying either map to the negative negates its image. The new difference is therefore the negative of an element of the ideal, which belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_mem_eqModIdealSet: Both ring homomorphisms send one to one. Their difference is zero, which belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsRingHom_comp: The map on sections of the composite is the composite of the maps on sections, with the second restriction made to the indicated smaller open. Evaluate the identity on the chosen ring element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsRingHom_sub_mem_ideal: The two base maps agree after composing with the closed-subscheme inclusion. Hence the images of each base element restrict to the same section on the closed subscheme. Their difference restricts to zero and by the quotient description belongs to the ideal of sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsRingHom_sub_mem_span_mul_of_agre: Agreement on the closed subscheme puts the difference of sections in its ideal. The product factorization writes that ideal as the pulled-back center times the second ideal. On the chart the center ideal is generated by the indicated section, giving the stated product containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.self_sub_self_eq_zero: Subtracting an element from itself gives zero by the additive inverse identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sub_mem_ideal_of_subring_closure_eq_top: The elements on which the maps agree modulo the ideal form a subring. The hypothesis puts every generator in that subring, so it contains their generated subring. The latter is the whole ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_eq_of_affineBlowup_lifts: Around each point choose an affine open and a smaller common-chart open as above. Their inverse images in the closed subscheme of the second ideal agree, so the smaller opens still give a cover of that subscheme. The comparison on a common chart makes the two lifts agree on each of its members. Equality of morphisms is local on the source, so they agree on the closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.val_chartRingHom: The chart map represents an original ring element by its degree-zero representative in the Rees algebra with denominator one. Forgetting the grading gives that same fraction in the underlying localization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zero_mem_eqModIdealSet: Both ring homomorphisms send zero to zero. Their difference is therefore in the ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupLiftEqOnControlledTransform: The factorization of the pulled-back ideal implies that the two maps into the original scheme agree on the controlled-transform subscheme. At each point of that subscheme choose an affine open around the common image. The intersection of its two inverse images is an ambient neighborhood of the point on which both maps land in this affine open. The affine comparison of blowup lifts gives equality on the restriction of the controlled-transform subscheme there. These inverse-image neighborhoods cover the controlled-transform subscheme, so the two lifts agree on it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_mul_of_isOpenImmersion: Take an affine open of the source. Its image under the open immersion is affine, and the open lies in the inverse image of that image. On these affines pullback of an ideal is extension along the map on sections. Extension of ideals commutes with products, so the two sheaves have the same ideals on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_comp_ι_eq: An open inclusion is a monomorphism. Cancel it from the two equal composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isoSpec_of_isAffineOpen: Take the ring of sections on the affine open. The canonical map from the affine open to the spectrum of that ring is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_preimage_subscheme_to_subscheme_c: On the inverse image open of the closed subscheme the closed immersion restricts to a map into the given ambient open. Together with the inverse-image open inclusion it defines a map into the pullback of the closed immersion. Identify this pullback with the closed subscheme of the restricted ideal. The defining projection formula then gives the required composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_specIdealSheaf_eq: Take the ideal of sections on the whole affine scheme and identify the global section ring with the given ring. The affine correspondence between ideals and ideal sheaves recovers the original sheaf. Transporting the ideal along the global-sections isomorphism and back cancels the two changes of ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hom_ext_of_comp_ι_eq_of_opens_cover: The open inclusions form a cover because every point lies in one of their images. Morphisms from a scheme agree if they agree on all members of an open cover, which is the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_le_right: On each affine open, the product of two ideals is contained in their intersection, hence in the right factor. The sectionwise inclusions give the ideal sheaf inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_ι_subschemeι_comp_eq_of_comap_ι: The inverse image open of the closed subscheme maps to the closed subscheme of the restricted ideal compatibly with their inclusions into the ambient scheme. Precompose the assumed agreement there with this map to obtain agreement on the inverse image open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comap_comp_eq_of_subschemeι_c: The closed subscheme defined by the pulled-back ideal is the base change of the original closed subscheme. Its inclusion followed by the base map factors through the original closed subscheme by the pullback square. Precompose the original agreement with this factorization to obtain the two equal composites upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comap_ι_comp_eq_of_blowup_lif: Restrict the target to the chosen affine open and identify it with a spectrum. Open restriction of the blowup is the blowup of the restricted center. Both maps from the source open to the affine target lift to this restricted blowup by the pullback square. The two pullbacks of the restricted center agree because they are restrictions of the equal center pullbacks. The center remains locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and the product factorization persists because restriction commutes with products. The original agreement on the closed subscheme also pulls back to the source open. Cancellation of the target open inclusion gives agreement of the restricted maps on that subscheme. The comparison over a spectrum therefore gives equality of the two lifts on the subscheme of the restricted second factor. Projecting back to the original blowup gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_eq_of_blowup_lifts_spec: Express the center sheaf on the spectrum as the sheaf of an ideal of the ring. The affine blowup for this ideal and the given blowup have maps to each other over the spectrum by their universal properties. The composite on the given blowup is the identity by uniqueness. Send both proposed lifts to the affine blowup, where the affine comparison theorem makes them agree on the subscheme of the second factor. Compose back to the given blowup to obtain the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_eq_of_mul_comap: The product of the two upstairs factors lies in the second factor. The second factor's closed subscheme therefore maps into the closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal. The two composites agree on that entire pulled-back closed subscheme by base change of the given agreement. Restrict to the smaller closed subscheme.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqComparison.exists_preimage_of_m: The left stage comparison and the projections form a pullback square over the left base map. The coverage condition puts the chosen center point's projection in that base map's range. The point therefore has a preimage in the common sequence's stage.

The right stage comparison is the projection of a pullback square over the right base map. By the right coverage condition the center point projects to the range of that map. The pullback projection then provides a preimage in the common stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqLevelIso.center_comap_iso_hom_e: On the common center support the two stage comparisons agree after applying the inverse stage isomorphism. Indeed, the auxiliary ideal is contained in the center ideal, so each point of the center support comes from its closed subscheme, where agreement is assumed. Now lift a point of the left center support to the common stage using coverage. Its lift lies on the common center because centers pull back, and its right image lies on the right center. Agreement of the two comparisons sends the original left point into the right support under the stage isomorphism. The symmetric lifting argument gives the reverse inclusion after transport. Each center is determined by its support in the stated sense, so these inclusions give opposite ideal inclusions after transport by the inverse isomorphisms. Hence the two center ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqLevelIso.exists_iso_succ_comp_b: Transport the right blowup along the inverse stage isomorphism to the left stage. The center comparison says its transported center is the left center. Both successors are therefore blowups of the same ideal on the left stage. The universal property gives an isomorphism over that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqLevelIso.hom_comp_blowupMorphis: Postcompose the given identity with the forward stage isomorphism. It cancels the inverse on one side, producing the desired square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqLevelIso.isoSucc_hom_comp_blowu: The chosen successor isomorphism is a witness from the blowup uniqueness result. Its compatibility with the two blowup maps is part of that witness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSeqLevelIso.subschemeι_comp_eq_com: Use the current stage isomorphism to view both comparison maps into the left stage. Their center pullbacks are equal because both give the common center. They agree on the closed subscheme of the current auxiliary ideal by the stage hypothesis. The successor comparison maps, with the right one transported by the inverse successor isomorphism, lift these maps through the left blowup by commutativity of the comparison squares. The auxiliary ideal at the next stage is obtained by removing one exceptional factor from the total transform. The controlled-transform comparison for blowup lifts therefore gives agreement on its closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.isomorphic_of_isStrict: The strict pullback relations give a common length and two stagewise comparisons with the same source. Together with coverage, determination of the centers by support, and the auxiliary ideal identities, they give the comparison data for constructing stage isomorphisms. At the initial stage use the two initial identifications. At each successor the current isomorphism identifies the centers, so the universal property identifies the two blowups. The lift comparison preserves agreement on the auxiliary subscheme at that successor, enabling the induction. The resulting stage isomorphisms commute with the initial and transition maps and identify all center ideals, which is the required sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSeqLevelIsoZero_iso_hom_comp_isoOb: The initial stage isomorphism is the left initial identification followed by the inverse right identification. Following it by the right identification cancels the inverse and leaves the left identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_hom_comap_inv: The two pullbacks compose to pullback along the inverse followed by the isomorphism. That composite is the identity, which fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_preimage_of_isPullback: Identify the given square with the canonical scheme pullback. The range of the first projection is unchanged by precomposing with this isomorphism. The hypothesis supplies a preimage under the canonical projection and therefore under the given projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pullbackFst_base_eq: The range of the first projection from a scheme pullback is the inverse image of the range of the other input map. The given membership puts the point in that range, providing a preimage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_subschemeι_base_eq: The closed-subscheme inclusion has image equal to the ideal's support. Membership in that support thus supplies a point of the closed subscheme mapping to the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_le: Inclusion of ideals reverses inclusion of supports. The support of the larger ideal is therefore contained in that of the smaller one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_iso_hom_comp: Every image of the composite is an image under the second map. Conversely, a point in the domain of the second map has a preimage under the isomorphism, so its image also belongs to the range of the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_zero_eq_comp_isoObjZero_: Compose both sides with the left initial isomorphism. The stage-zero comparison identities express the composites as the common initial identification followed by the left and right base maps respectively. They agree on the closed subscheme by the initial ideal hypothesis. Cancel the left initial isomorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_getElem_eq_iteratedStrictTransf: The stage boundary is the list of iterated strict transforms of the original boundary followed by the exceptional entries. The specified index lies in the original list, so the corresponding entry is the strict transform of that original component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_ne_top: An equality of schemes gives an isomorphism. Pullback along its forward identification preserves nonunit ideals by the support argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_hom_ne_top_of_ne_top: A nonunit ideal has nonempty support. Take a point of the support and send it through the inverse isomorphism. Its image belongs to the inverse image of the support, which is the support of the pulled-back ideal. Thus the pulled-back ideal is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iso_inv_ne_top: Apply preservation of nonunit ideals to the inverse isomorphism, viewed as the forward map of the reversed isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_cover_eq_separateAllBoundary_appe: The cover triple is admissible and its ideal is order bounded. On the final boundary-separation stage the structural map is locally of finite type. The transformed maximal-contact hypersurface is in strict normal crossing position with the exceptional portion of the final boundary, so the derived triple with this supplemental hypersurface is admissible. Its dimension is at most the cover dimension and hence at most the reference dimension, giving the dimension predicate. The hypersurface gives a first boundary entry. The separation invariant gives disjointness for every original boundary entry that is dropped. Apply the append theorem at the first entry to get the marked continuation and its order-locus comparison. The cover sequence is defined by exactly this append operation after separating the whole boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_mem_take_of_forall_lt: Induct on the list. The empty list and an initial segment of length zero have no members. In the successor case the head is covered by index zero. Entries in the tail are covered by applying the induction hypothesis with each tail index shifted by one in the full list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_eq_of_list_eq: Equal lists have the same entry at a fixed index. The bounds witness that both lookups are defined.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_map_append_of_lt: Induct on the list being mapped. An index within its length always lies in the mapped prefix. The head returns the image of the original head, and a later index reduces to the tail with the same appended suffix. The inductive lookup then gives the mapped entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_map_of_lt: Induct on the list. An empty list has no valid index. For a nonempty list the first mapped entry is the image of its head. A later lookup moves to the tail at the preceding index, where the induction hypothesis applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ne_top_of_support_nonempty: At a point of the support the ideal has order at least one. The unit ideal has order zero everywhere, so the ideal cannot be the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_append_succ_subset_pre: The appended sequence is marked. Each center lies in the current order locus, and multiplication by the exceptional power recovers the total transform from the next ideal. Apply the marked order-locus comparison for a blowup to these two properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eqToHom_inter_su: The identification of equal schemes is an isomorphism. Pulling both ideals back along it preserves the empty intersection of the order locus and support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_inter_suppor: Under an isomorphism, the pulled-back order locus and support are the inverse images of the original sets. Their intersection is the inverse image of the empty original intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_support_eq_empty: If a point lay in the original intersection, its inverse image under the isomorphism would belong to the pulled-back order locus and support. This contradicts emptiness upstairs.
The equalities identify the marked ideal and the boundary ideal. Their order locus and support are therefore the sets in the assumed empty intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundaryInvariant_append:
The support of the strict transform of the distinguished component is contained in the support of the tracked continuation divisor. Both start from the same ideal, and at each stage the tracked divisor is transformed strictly or totally. The support comparison thus makes the final strict transform disjoint from the order locus because the tracked divisor is disjoint. With a positive-length continuation this disjointness transports to the final append stage, where the distinguished entry is exactly that strict transform. With a zero-length continuation the initial isomorphism transports the disjointness back to the join. The previously separated entries are also disjoint at the join, and all these disjointness conditions persist because order loci and strict-transform supports at a step lie over the preceding ones.

The centers of the append are centers of the first sequence or of the continuation transported by stage isomorphisms. Their ideals remain nonunit. The initial hypersurface meets the required strict normal crossing condition after pullback along the initial isomorphism of the append.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundaryInvariant_appendLowerDim: At the final stage the original boundary still has the required index, and stage admissibility gives local finite type and strict normal crossings. With no supplemental or dropped entries, these conditions make the derived triple admissible. Its dimension fits the reference bound, and tuning gives order boundedness and balance. The append formula expresses the reduction as the original sequence followed by the marked continuation of the boundary reduction. The shape of that reduction tracks the distinguished divisor by strict transforms, with a possible initial total transform, and makes it disjoint from the final order locus at the tuned mark. The continuation comparison transfers this disjointness to the original mark. The centers are nonunit by the boundary reduction specification. Apply the append invariant to obtain the next separation step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundaryInvariant_separateBounda: At zero the cover separation sequence is empty, so no boundary or center conditions need checking. The initial hypersurface has strict normal crossing position by the cover property transported along the initial isomorphism. At a successor, the recursive definition appends one lower-dimensional reduction. The cover triple is admissible, order bounded, and within the reference dimension. The append invariant therefore propagates separation through the new boundary index and preserves the other properties.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_length_pullbackTriple: The pulled-back boundary is obtained by pulling back each entry once. Entrywise pullback preserves the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_pullbackAlong_eq_map_comap: By definition, pullback of the triple takes entrywise pullback of its boundary. Substitute the given expression for that boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dim_derivedTriple_le_dim: The derived triple uses the final stage as its scheme. The dimension bound for stages of a marked sequence makes its successor dimension at most the original successor dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_index_of_mem_take: Induct on the original list. Membership is impossible when the list or the number of entries taken is zero. Otherwise an entry in the retained prefix is either its head, with index zero, or belongs to the retained prefix of the tail. Shift the tail index from the induction hypothesis by one. The shifted index is within both the original length and the requested prefix.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_derivedTriple_nil: Admissibility of the original triple gives admissibility of its marked transform at the final stage. In particular the final boundary has strict normal crossings for the final structural map. With no entries added or dropped, this is the boundary of the derived triple. Apply the derived-triple admissibility theorem.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_derivedTriple_pullbackTripl: The final comparison map is smooth. Its composite to the base is quasi-compact by admissibility of the final upstairs transform and the identity of structural maps. Pullback of the admissible derived triple downstairs is therefore admissible. Its boundary is the pullback of the supplemental list followed by the truncated final boundary, because pullback preserves concatenation and positions. The boundary comparison identifies this with the list used in the derived triple upstairs. The derived-triple pullback identity then transfers admissibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_withBoundary_of_eq: Replacing the boundary by an equal list gives the same marked triple. The existing admissibility certificate applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_schemeAt: Admissibility of the starting triple and the marked stage theorem give a Noetherian scheme at the chosen index. Passing between the marked data and marked sequence preserves the stage, and a Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_comap_lastMap: The final comparison map is smooth, and the composite structural map is locally of finite type because it equals the upstairs final structural map. Smooth compatibility of maximal contact therefore gives the condition for the pulled-back hypersurface and pulled-back tuned ideal. The tuned-ideal pullback identity identifies this ideal with the final tuned ideal upstairs. Substitute that identity and the equality of structural maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_derivedTriple: The derived triple uses the final structural map with the tuned final ideal and its tuned mark. The given maximal-contact condition is expressed in exactly these data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_strictTransform: The strict transform of the original hypersurface remains of maximal contact at the final stage. The final ideal is still order bounded by the original mark. Apply preservation of maximal contact under balanced tuning at this stage to obtain the condition at the tuned mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_reduceAlongHyp:
Smooth pullback preserves the order bound and the boundary length. Compare boundary separation by induction on the number of processed components. At zero both sequences are empty. At each successor their derived triples with the full final boundary are admissible, their dimensions fit the reference bound, and the next index is valid on both sides. Smooth-surjective compatibility of the appended reduction then extends the strict pullback relation.

After processing the entire original boundary, its transforms are disjoint from the final order loci. The distinguished hypersurface transforms give admissible derived triples with the remaining boundary. Appending with the pullback of the downstairs transformed hypersurface gives a strict pullback by the append comparison. That pulled-back hypersurface is of maximal contact for the tuned final upstairs ideal, as is the strict transform of the separately chosen upstairs hypersurface. Independence of the appended reduction from the choice of maximal contact identifies the two upstairs sequences up to isomorphism. Transport the strict pullback relation along that isomorphism to obtain the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_length_eq_zero: For the only stage, compose the upstairs initial isomorphism, the base map, and the inverse downstairs initial isomorphism. The initial square commutes. Both lengths are zero, so there are no center or transition conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_appendLowerDimReduction_of_is: The two derived triples have admissible boundaries with a distinguished first entry, and their dimensions fit the reference bound. The append theorem writes each reduction as the same initial sequence followed by its marked continuation. If the final order locus is nonempty, the original mark is the maximum order. The tuned ideal has maximal-contact invariance, and both distinguished hypersurfaces give maximal contact for it. Independence of the first-boundary reduction from the chosen maximal-contact hypersurface gives isomorphic continuations, after identifying the underlying data. Appending to the common sequence preserves the isomorphism. If the locus is empty, both continuations have length zero, and each append is isomorphic to the initial sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_separateBoundaryOfFamily_zero: Boundary separation at index zero is defined as the empty marked data. Its underlying blowup data are empty, with length zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_toMarkedSequence_eq_zero: Equipping the underlying data with markings preserves the number of steps. The given zero length is therefore also the length of the marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_nil_append_boundary_drop_zero: The final boundary begins with the strict transforms of the full original boundary and then has the exceptional entries. Its length is at least the original length. Prepending an empty list and dropping zero entries do not change it, so the index remains in range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactIdeal_comap: The maximal-contact ideal is the iterated derivative ideal at index one less than the mark. The smooth-pullback theorem for iterated derivative ideals gives the equality at this index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_inter_support_eq_empty: A member of the retained initial segment has an index below the segment length in the final boundary. The boundary separation hypothesis gives disjointness at that index. Replace the indexed entry by the given member.
Taking zero entries gives the empty list. There is no boundary component satisfying the membership hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_mult_of_isOrderBoundedByMult: The order-bounded condition is the pointwise bound by the mark, so evaluate it at the specified point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_pullbackTriple_le_mult: Smooth pullback preserves the order at every point, equating it with the original order at the image. Apply the original pointwise bound. The mark is the same in the pulled-back triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundaryInvariant_separateBounda: Induct on the number of boundary components processed. At zero the sequence is empty, so there are no separated entries or centers to check. The initial strict normal crossing condition survives the initial isomorphism. At a successor the recursive definition appends the lower-dimensional boundary reduction at the preceding index. That index is in range, and the append theorem preserves the invariant for the earlier entries while separating the new one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_separateBoundaryPullbackCompari: Induct on the number of original boundary entries processed. At zero both sides have empty sequences, giving the base pullback. At a successor the induction hypothesis compares the current sequences, with the upstairs index equal to the number of surviving entries. Their final structural maps are locally of finite type, and the derived triples are admissible with dimensions bounded by the reference dimension. The dimension predicate descends along those bounds, and smooth pullback preserves the order bound. If the next boundary entry pulls back to the unit ideal, the surviving count stays fixed and the corresponding final transform also pulls back to the unit ideal. The trivial-divisor continuation theorem then compares the appended downstairs reduction with the current upstairs sequence. If the entry survives, the upstairs count increases by one. Use the continuation comparison at the two corresponding indices, supported by boundary-position invariance, to compare the appended reductions. These are the defining successors of the separation sequences.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_of_eq: An equality of marked triples identifies their component data and hence their admissibility conditions. Transfer the given certificate along it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_of_eq: The two tuples of data defining balance agree after identifying the triples. The certificates of local finite type witness the same property, so the given balance condition transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderBoundedByMult_of_eq: Equal triples have the same ideal and mark, so the given pointwise order bound applies to either one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_appendLowerDimR: The two distinguished indices are in range in the corresponding final boundaries. The hypotheses allow the append formula on both sides, with no dropped boundary entries to check. It expresses each reduction as the given sequence followed by its marked continuation. The derived-triple comparison gives a pullback relation for the continuations over the final-stage map. Regard it as a comparison of their underlying blowup data and append it to the given comparison of the initial sequences over the original base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_derivedTriple: The smooth final-stage comparison identifies the derived triple upstairs with the pullback of the downstairs derived triple equipped with the final upstairs boundary. Both triples have the needed order bounds and are balanced by tuning. The final boundaries retain the indices from the original lists, and the distinguished component corresponds to the index counting the preceding surviving components upstairs. The comparison of final boundaries matches the whole lists after removing unit ideals and also matches the prefixes before the distinguished entry and through it. Cancel the latter prefixes to match the suffixes. The smooth pullback comparison with a change of boundary position now applies to the derived triple downstairs and the identified triple upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_pullbackAlong: Pulling back the original boundary preserves its length and identifies the distinguished entry with the corresponding entry in the modified boundary. Since the modified triple is admissible and the two full lists have the same nontrivial entries, the unmodified pullback triple is also admissible. Its dimension, order, and balance conditions are unchanged by the replacement of the boundary. Apply smooth functoriality of divisor reduction to this unmodified pullback at the original index. Split both lists at the common distinguished entry. Their prefixes and suffixes have the same nontrivial entries by hypothesis, and their prefix lengths give the desired two indices. Boundary-position invariance transports the pullback relation to the reduction for the modified list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_congr: Substitute the equality of the source sequences into the given pullback relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_congr_marked: Identify the triples, so the two comparison maps have the same source and the equality of maps applies there. The assignment gives the same sequence on the common triple. After the two identifications the existing pullback relation is the required one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_sameNontrivialBoundary: The boundary-position invariance property compares the reductions at the distinguished component, since the two prefixes and the two suffixes agree after ignoring unit entries. The given lengths identify the reduction indices with the two prefix lengths. Transport the existing pullback relation through the resulting isomorphism of source reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_of_eq: The two structural maps coincide after identifying the triples, so local finite type transfers to the first structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pred_dim_of_eq: Equal triples have the same underlying scheme and successor dimension. The given dimension predicate therefore holds for the first triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_congr: Identify each list with its equal list in the given relation. The same nontrivial boundary condition immediately transfers to the original pair.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_congr_right: Substitute the equality of the second boundary lists. The given relation then applies to the required pair.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.take_append_getElem_cons_drop: Since the index is in range, the tail beginning there consists of the entry at that index followed by the tail after it. Prepending the initial segment reconstructs the whole list.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_inv_comap_hom: The two pullbacks compose to pullback along the inverse followed by the forward isomorphism. This is the identity on the original target and fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ι_le_comap_ι_of_le: The inclusion of the smaller open factors through the larger open. Pullback along that factorization preserves the given inclusion of the two restricted ideals and gives their restrictions to the smaller open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_le_center_pow: The upstairs center is in strict normal crossing position and its support lies in the order locus. The local order criterion therefore puts the upstairs ideal inside the marked power of that center. By the ideal comparison, the center pullback identity, and preservation of powers under pullback, this is the pullback of the desired inclusion. The stage comparison is a surjective local isomorphism, so the inclusion descends.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_etaleChartOnRangeOpens: The coordinate ideal of the transported chart is the pullback from the coordinate subspace along the transported chart map. Factor the map through the inverse image isomorphism, the open restriction, and the original chart. Pulling back in those steps gives the same ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_isoRangeOpens_inv_comp_map: The transported chart is the composite of an isomorphism, an open inclusion, and the original étale chart. Each map is étale, so the composite is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_rangeOpens: Surjectivity gives a preimage of the target point. Around that preimage choose an open on which the map is an open immersion. The point is the image of the preimage regarded as a point of this open, so it belongs to the associated image open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_smul_mem_of_map_mem: The section ring on the basic open is the localization at powers of the defining function. Membership of the image in the extended ideal writes it as a fraction with numerator in the ideal and denominator some power of the function. Clear that denominator in the localization, then multiply by a further power to obtain the equality in the original ring. The resulting power times the original element is a multiple of an ideal element and hence belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_of_comap: At a point on the center downstairs choose a preimage on the pulled-back center by surjectivity and the support formula. Take a strict normal crossing chart there and shrink it to an open where the cover map is an open immersion. The image open contains the original point, and its isomorphism with the smaller source open transports the chart. The pulled-back list preserves the original indices. Restrictions of unit entries stay unit, assigned boundary coordinate ideals transport to the same coordinate ideals in the new chart, and the center coordinate ideal transports in the same way. The distinctness of the boundary assignments is unchanged. This gives the required chart downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_comap_controlledTransform: At stage zero the two ideals are pullbacks of the original ideal along equal composites. At a successor the inductive comparison descends the inclusion of the downstairs ideal in the appropriate center power. Thus the next downstairs controlled transform satisfies the exceptional-power factorization. Pull it back along the next comparison map. Pullback commutes with products and powers, and the exceptional ideals agree by pullback. The comparison square and the inductive equality identify the two total transforms upstairs. Both candidate ideals have the same product with the exceptional power, so cancellation by this locally nonzerodivisor-generated ideal proves equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_ideal_of_comap_ι_le: Evaluate the pullback inclusion on the whole affine open viewed as a scheme. Under the section-ring isomorphism for the open immersion, these two ideals are the images of the original ideals on the affine open. Applying the inverse ring isomorphism reflects their inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_pullback_snd: Around the image of a point under the first projection choose an open on which the original map is an open immersion. Its inverse image under that projection is an open neighborhood of the point. The second projection restricted to this neighborhood is the base change of the chosen open immersion, hence an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_balancedTunedIdeal_of_isStrictP: The cover map is flat, and the marked cover sequence starts from the pullback of the balanced tuned ideal and boundary at the tuned mark. The strict pullback data give the stage comparisons, which are local isomorphisms by hypothesis. Apply descent of marking to these data and the local Noetherian stages to obtain the stated marking downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_of_strictPullbackBlowupSeq: The marked ideals upstairs are pullbacks of the downstairs controlled transforms. The center-power inclusions descend at every stage, giving exceptional divisibility and the required order bound on each downstairs center. The comparison maps are surjective local isomorphisms, and the structural maps commute with them. Smoothness of the upstairs centers thus descends to the downstairs centers. Their boundaries and centers also agree by pullback, so the strict normal crossing conditions descend by the local chart argument. These four properties give the marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoRangeOpens_hom_ι: The two open immersions have the same image. The forward image isomorphism is the factorization of the restricted map through the inclusion of its image open. Composing this factorization with the inclusion recovers the restricted map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoRangeOpens_hom_ι_assoc: Postcompose the forward image-isomorphism identity with the given morphism. Associativity yields the displayed composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoRangeOpens_inv_comp: The inverse image isomorphism factors the inclusion of the image open through the original restricted map. Composing with that map gives the inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoRangeOpens_inv_comp_assoc: The inverse image isomorphism followed by the original restricted map is the image-open inclusion. Postcomposing that identity with the given morphism proves the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoRangeOpens_inv_comp_map_comp_affineSp: Restrict the original chart to the smaller open. Its composite to the base is the smaller open inclusion followed by the cover map and structural map. Precompose with the inverse image isomorphism. The resulting inclusion followed by the cover map is the image-open inclusion, yielding the required compatibility over the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_comap_le: The image opens of the local isomorphisms cover the target by surjectivity. On each image open, pull the two restricted ideals back along its isomorphism from the corresponding source open. These are the restrictions of the already compared pulled-back ideals. Pulling their inclusion back along the inverse recovers inclusion on the image open. The open-cover criterion for inclusion now gives the result on the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_forall_comap_ι_le: Work on an affine open and take an element of the first section ideal. Refine the given cover there by basic opens subordinate to its members. The defining functions of these basic opens generate the unit ideal. On each basic open the assumed comparison restricts to inclusion of the section ideals, so the element lies in the localization of the second ideal. Clearing denominators puts a power of each defining function times the element in the second ideal. Since the basic opens cover the affine, those powers also generate the unit ideal, so the element itself belongs to the second ideal. This proves inclusion on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_map_le_of_leftInverse: Take an element of the first ideal. Its image lies in the image ideal of the second by inclusion. Applying the left inverse sends this element into the ideal obtained by extending the second ideal along the composite. The composite is the identity, so the original element belongs to the second ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_rangeOpens_iff: The image open of the restricted map is defined by its range on points. Membership means that the point has a preimage in the restricted source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_ι_comp_eq_range_rangeOpens_ι: The image of the inclusion of the image open is that open itself, whose points are exactly the range of the restricted map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_rangeOpens: The inclusion of the image open factors through the inverse image isomorphism to the smaller source open, its inclusion into the larger open, the larger open inclusion, and the cover map. Pullback along this composite equals the stated successive restrictions and transports.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_markedBlowupSequenceData_projecti: At stage zero the structural map is the given smooth map composed with an isomorphism. At each successor, the center is in strict normal crossing position and the transition is its blowup. The smoothness theorem for such a blowup over the smooth previous stage makes the next structural map smooth. Induct through the chosen index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_smooth_comp_of_isLocalIsomorph: Cover the target of the local isomorphism by its image opens, using surjectivity. On each corresponding source open the composite with the given morphism is smooth by restriction. Its identification with the image-open restriction is through an isomorphism, so the image-open restriction is smooth. Smoothness is local on the source, giving smoothness of the map out of the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_smooth_iso_hom_comp: Precompose the smooth composite with the inverse isomorphism, which is smooth. The inverse cancels the forward isomorphism, leaving the desired map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_comp_of_smooth_comap_c: The closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal is isomorphic to the fiber product of the original closed subscheme with the cover. Transport the given smooth composite to this fiber product. Commutativity expresses it through the projection to the original closed subscheme. That projection is a surjective local isomorphism by base change, so smoothness descends to the original closed subscheme's structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ι_comp: The open inclusion is smooth, and the given morphism is smooth. Their composite is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_forall_mem_basicOpen: On the affine open the distinguished opens of the indicated functions form a cover by hypothesis. The affine correspondence between basic opens and localizations says their union is the whole open exactly when the functions generate the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullbackComparisonMap_comp_project: At stage zero this is the initial compatibility of the strict pullback. At the next stage the projection to the base factors through the blowup map and the previous projection. Commute the comparison through the blowup square, then apply the inductive compatibility at the preceding stage. The resulting composite is the upstairs projection followed by the original base map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_coverMap: The chosen maximal-contact opens cover the original scheme. The cover map is induced by their inclusions from the disjoint union of the opens. Each point belongs to one of those opens and is the image of its copy in that summand, so the map is surjective.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.comapEtale_map: The pulled-back chart is defined by the restricted morphism to the original open followed by the original chart map. This composite is its map to affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapEtale_map_comp_affineSpaceFinToSpec: The old chart map followed by the affine-space structural map is the original open inclusion followed by the structural map. Precompose with the restricted étale map. Its restriction square identifies the resulting composite with the inclusion of the inverse-image open followed by the new structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_eq_of_comp_eq: Each successive pullback equals pullback along the corresponding composite. The two composites agree, so the pulled-back ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_comapEtale_map: The restriction of the given étale map to the inverse-image open is étale by base change along the open immersion. The chart map is étale. Their composite is therefore étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_coverMa: Choose the cover open containing the point and use the restriction equality with its local ideal. If that local ideal is the unit ideal, it stays the unit ideal after transport. The cover structural map is smooth, so take an étale chart around the point inside this open and assign no coordinate to the singleton ideal. If the local ideal is a coordinate ideal, transport its chart to the cover open. The singleton ideal restricts to its designated coordinate ideal there. Each case gives the required local normal-crossing chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_coverMaxC: The sole boundary entry is a smooth divisor by hypothesis. At every point the cover chart argument gives strict normal-crossing position for this entry locally. The smooth-divisor condition and the local charts together give the global singleton condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_coverMaxContact:
Choose a cover piece containing the given point in the cover. Its image open is affine, since the piece is affine and identifies with that open. Its points map into the original open corresponding to the piece. If the original open misses the tuned order locus, the cover open misses its pullback, since smooth pullback preserves the order locus. The local ideal is the unit ideal there and its transported ideal on the cover open is the unit ideal as well.

Otherwise the original open has an étale chart whose chosen coordinate ideal is the local hypersurface and lies in the restricted maximal-contact ideal. Transport this chart to the cover open. Its coordinate ideal is the transported local ideal and hence is the restriction of the cover hypersurface. The maximal-contact ideal for the cover is the pullback of the original maximal-contact ideal by the smooth derivative formula. The cover piece square identifies the restriction of this pullback with transport of the original restriction. Pulling back the coordinate inclusion therefore proves maximal contact on the cover open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_ι_base_subset: The inclusion of the open has image the open itself. In particular, the image is contained in the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_coverTripleOpen_coverMaxCo: The open associated to this cover piece is isomorphic to the piece. Restricting the global ideal to the open equals first pulling it back to the piece and then transporting it along the inverse isomorphism. The assumed identification on the piece gives exactly the transported local ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq_map_iteratedStrictTransform_: Write the starting boundary as its list of original components followed by the empty list. The boundary formula for concatenated lists transforms those original components one by one and appends the new exceptional divisors to the second list. The strict transforms of the empty list contribute no entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_coverMaxC: The good cover supplies strict normal crossing position of its maximal-contact hypersurface relative to the pulled-back boundary. The ideal and boundary in that clause are the ones used in the cover triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_iteratedS: At stage zero the transform is pullback along the initial isomorphism. Pullback along an isomorphism preserves strict normal crossing position, so the condition on the singleton boundary persists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_coverTriple: The order bound provides the data for the chosen good cover of the derived triple. Its admissibility clause is exactly the admissibility of the triple on this cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_derivedTriple: Validity of the original sequence gives smoothness and quasi-compactness of the stage. Its structural map is locally of finite type, the base field has characteristic zero, and the tuned mark is positive. The given condition supplies strict normal crossings for the new boundary. The tuned ideal contains a power of the old ideal, and the support of that power lies in the old support. Thus the tuned support lies in the old support and contains no component on which the old ideal was generically nonzero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_tunedMarkedBlowupSeq: The derived triple is admissible, so the stage theorem for marked blowup sequences makes each stage locally Noetherian. The underlying sequence data specify those same stage schemes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_balancedTunedSh: If the old marked order locus is nonempty, the order bound makes the original mark the maximum order. Tuning then preserves both the marked order locus and the maximal-contact ideal. The given local hypersurface data work for the tuned ideal. If the locus is empty, it stays empty after tuning, and both maximal-contact ideals are the unit ideal. The same local data give the required hypersurface in this case as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_coverMaxContact: Take the chosen good cover, with its cover scheme locally of finite type over the base. Its hypersurface clause gives maximal contact with the pulled-back tuned ideal at the tuned mark. This is the ideal and mark of the cover triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_eq_toBlowupSeque: Induct on the stage. At stage zero both descriptions pull back along the same initial isomorphism. At a successor, the reconstructed sequence has the same center and blowup morphism. Apply their common strict-transform operation to the equality from the preceding stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_projectionToBase_com: Reconstruct the marked blowup sequence from the given data and its validity certificate. The structural map of a stage is the projection to the initial scheme followed by its structural map. The finite-type property for the reconstructed stage supplies the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactIdeal_eq_top_of_orderAtLeastLo: The maximal-contact ideal is the derivative ideal at index one less than the mark. Its order-at-least-one locus equals the original marked order locus. This is also its support. If that locus is empty, every stalk is the unit ideal, so the sheaf itself is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_balancedTunedSheaf_eq_: Since the old marked order locus is empty, the derivative ideal at index one less than the mark is the unit ideal. Give that factor the tuning exponent and all other factors exponent zero. Its weight is one, so the product occurs in the tuned sum. The product has unit stalk everywhere, forcing the tuned ideal to have unit stalk everywhere. The tuned mark is positive, so its order locus is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_coverTriple_ideal_le_mult: A point of the given nonempty marked order locus attains the mark, since the mark is also an upper bound everywhere. The tuning theorem then bounds the order of the tuned ideal by the tuned mark. The cover map is smooth and preserves the order of the pulled-back ideal, so the same bound holds on the cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_tuningExponent_le_balancedTunedSheaf: In the tuning formula put the entire tuning exponent on the derivative ideal at index zero, which is the original ideal. The weight at index zero is the positive mark, so the weighted degree is at least the tuning exponent. The resulting product is the claimed power and is a summand of the tuned ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_derivIdealSheafIter_pow_le_balanced: The balanced tuned ideal is the sum of all products of derivative ideals whose weighted exponent sum reaches the tuning threshold. The stated exponent condition puts this product among those summands, so the tuned ideal contains it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_range_succ_eq_apply_zero: The range contains index zero exactly once. Every other indexed factor is the unit, so removing those factors leaves precisely the factor at zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToBase_comp: Reconstruct the marked blowup sequence using the validity certificate. Its stages have smooth structural maps. The stage structural map is the stated projection to the initial scheme followed by the original structural map, giving smoothness of this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_prod_eq_top: Take the stalk at the chosen point. The empty product is the unit ideal, and taking a stalk commutes with each ideal multiplication. If every factor has unit stalk, the product has unit stalk as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_iteratedStrictTransform_subset_o: Induct on the length of the sequence. At stage zero both ideals pull back along the same isomorphism, so support inclusion is preserved. At a successor stage, the induction hypothesis compares the two ideals on the previous stage. If both undergo strict transform, use the assumed monotonicity. If the comparison ideal undergoes total transform, the support of the strict transform lies in the inverse image of the old support, which lies in the inverse image of the comparison support. That last inverse image is the support of the total transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_iteratedStrictTransform_subset_s: At each blowup the support of a strict transform is the closure of the inverse image of the old support with the center removed. Difference with the same center, inverse image, and closure each preserve inclusion. The locally Noetherian stage hypotheses allow this support formula at every blowup. Apply the iterated support comparison with this monotonicity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_pow_subset_support: At a point outside the support the stalk is the unit ideal. Taking a power commutes with passing to the stalk, and every power of the unit ideal is again the unit ideal. The point therefore remains outside the support of the power.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendLowerDimReduction_eq_concatOfIsMar: The local finite-type hypothesis permits forming the derived triple, and the dimension bound permits calling the recursion on it at the given index. With both tests passed, the construction tries to append the underlying blowup data of the recursive result as a marked continuation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendLowerDimReduction_of_not_locallyOf: The construction first tests whether the structural map of the last stage is locally of finite type. Here the test fails, so the definition returns the given sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.asMarkedData_eq_some_of_isMarked: The certificate says the proposed continuation is marked for the structural map, ideal, mark, and boundary at the last stage. It therefore selects the successful branch of the conversion, which returns the given continuation with this marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.asMarkedSeq_eq_toMarkedSequence_of_isMar: The mark certificate makes the conversion choose its valid branch. In that branch it equips the same blowup data with the supplied markings and takes the resulting marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.asMarkedSeq_toSequenceOfBlowups: The mark certificate identifies the converted sequence with the one obtained by equipping the original blowup data with markings. Forgetting those markings recovers the original underlying sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.concatOfIsMarked_eq_append_of_isMarked: The mark certificate makes the conversion of the continuation succeed. In that case the concatenation operation appends the resulting marked continuation to the initial sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverMap_eq_sigmaOpensDesc: The defining cover map is induced from the open inclusions by the universal property of their disjoint union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_baseField: The cover triple uses the original base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_boundary: The boundary of the cover triple is constructed by pulling back each original boundary component along the cover map in its original position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_dim: The successor dimension of a triple is computed from its underlying scheme. For the cover triple that scheme is the disjoint union of the chosen open sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_ideal: The definition of the cover triple assigns it the pullback of the balanced tuned ideal along the cover map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_mult: The mark of the cover triple is defined to be the tuned mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_scheme: The cover triple uses the disjoint union of the chosen open sets as its underlying scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_structureMorphism: The structural map of the cover triple first maps the disjoint union to the original scheme and then applies the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.cover_eq_reduceAlongHypersurface: The marked sequence on the cover is defined by applying reduction along a hypersurface to the cover triple and its chosen maximal-contact ideal, using the given recursion and invariance data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivedTriple_boundary: To form the boundary, remove the prescribed initial number of entries from the last-stage boundary. The definition then places the supplemental list before the remaining entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivedTriple_mult: The derived triple uses the balanced tuning of the final ideal. Its mark is defined as the tuning exponent of the original mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivedTriple_scheme: The derived triple is formed on the last stage of the given marked sequence, so that stage is its scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivedTriple_structureMorphism: The structural map from the last stage first projects to the original scheme and then applies that scheme's structural morphism. This is the map specified in the derived triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedSeq_length: The empty marked sequence comes from the marked blowup data with no steps. Passing to its sequence of blowups preserves that length, which is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_coverMap_of_isAdmissible: On each open summand the cover map is its open inclusion into the original scheme. These inclusions are étale, and the summands cover the source, so the cover map is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_descendStrictPullback_eq_some: By hypothesis there is a strict descent. The descent operation therefore returns a chosen sequence satisfying that condition, which witnesses the claimed existence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_coverMap_of_isAdmissible: The cover map is étale. Étale morphisms are flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactCover_chosenCoverData: The chosen cover data are obtained by applying the cover construction to the balanced tuned ideal and its tuned mark. The given witness lets the construction choose a cover satisfying the required condition for those inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactCover_maxContactCover: The existence hypothesis selects the branch of the cover construction that chooses a witness to the maximal-contact cover condition. The chosen cover carries that condition by the specification of the witness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_of_descendStri: If a strict descent exists, the descent operation returns a witness, and equality of the two returned values identifies that witness with the stated sequence. Its defining property is the desired strict pullback relation. If no strict descent exists, the operation returns no sequence, contradicting the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_coverMap: The summands are open in the source of the cover map and cover it. On each summand the map is an open immersion, hence locally of finite type. The property is local on the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceAlongHypersurface_eq_appendLowerDi: The construction first processes all entries of the original boundary by boundary separation.
