It then calls lower-dimensional reduction at index zero, putting the final strict transform of the hypersurface in the supplemental list and dropping as many boundary entries as the original boundary had.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceOrder_eq_asMarkedSeq: Admissibility and the nonempty order locus select the branch that trims the boundary, reduces on the resulting cover, and tries to descend. By the given descent identity this branch returns the sequence furnished by the conversion to a marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceOrder_eq_toMarkedSequence: The descent identity expresses the reduction as the marked conversion of the given blowup data. The mark certificate then identifies that conversion with the marked sequence obtained directly from those data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundary_succ: At the successor stage take the previously separated sequence and apply lower-dimensional reduction at the preceding index. In this recursive step the supplemental boundary is empty and the number of entries to drop is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundary_zero: Boundary separation is defined recursively on the number of entries to process. At zero it starts with the empty marked sequence for the given ideal, mark, and boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_coverMap_of_isAdmissible: The cover map is étale. Every étale morphism is smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderReductionHypotheses.orderAtLeastLoc: Nonempty cosupport is one of the order-reduction hypotheses. A point witnessing it excludes equality of the marked order locus with the empty set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactPrincipalization_apply: The maximal-contact assignment applies order reduction to the given triple, with the lower-dimensional family supplied by the indexed reductions. Evaluating the assignment gives the expression on the right.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_append_ne_top: Before the join, the appended center is the original center of the first sequence transported along a stage identification. At the join it is the first continuation center pulled back along the initial isomorphism and a stage identification. Past the join it is the continuation center at the shifted index transported along a stage identification. The total length bound puts each center within its original sequence. All the transporting maps are surjective, so their pullbacks preserve nonunit ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_coverMarkedBlowupData_ne_top: Use the decomposition of the cover sequence into boundary separation and a continuation. The centers in the separation sequence are nonunit by the separation invariant. For the continuation, the derived triple is admissible, balanced, and order bounded, and its boundary has the transformed hypersurface as its first entry. The first-boundary reduction has nonempty centers by its specification, so their ideals are nonunit. Apply preservation of nonunit centers under appending the two sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ne_top_of_surjective_base: A nonunit ideal has a point in its support. Choose a preimage of that point by surjectivity. The support formula puts this preimage in the support of the pulled-back ideal, so that ideal is also nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_base_eqToHom_eq: The identification of equal schemes induces the identity after identifying their underlying points. The given point itself supplies the preimage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_base_iso_inv_eq: Take the image of the given point under the forward isomorphism. The inverse returns the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_pos_of_eq_cons: A list beginning with the specified entry has length one more than the length of its tail, so its length is positive.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_toBlowupSequenceData_iterate: The iterated strict transform computed from the marked sequence is the one computed from its underlying blowup data. Their supports agree, so the given membership transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_append_eq_empty: The length of the appended sequence is the sum of the two lengths. If the continuation has length zero, its endpoint is the endpoint of the first sequence. The final ideal is the first endpoint ideal pulled back along the stage identification, and its locus is empty by the zero-length hypothesis. If the continuation has positive length, the final index lies after the join, so the final ideal is the continuation endpoint ideal pulled back along the stage identification. Its locus is empty by the other hypothesis. In either case pullback along the stage isomorphism preserves emptiness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_eq_empty: Under the isomorphism the order locus of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the given locus. Since the given locus is empty, so is its inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_coverMarkedBlowupData_: Express the cover sequence as boundary separation followed by a marked continuation along the transformed maximal-contact hypersurface. The cover triple is admissible, and maximal contact survives through boundary separation. The continuation on the derived triple therefore has empty final locus at the derived mark. The continuation comparison identifies that locus with the final locus of the marked continuation at the cover mark. If the continuation has length zero, the same comparison at stage zero shows that the locus at the end of boundary separation is empty, using the initial isomorphism of the continuation. The append formula for empty loci now gives the conclusion at the tuned mark of the cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_derivedTriple_ideal_le: The derived triple has order bounded by its mark and is balanced by tuning. Its first boundary entry is the chosen hypersurface, so apply the first-boundary reduction to it. Tuning preserves maximal contact, and strict transforms of a maximal-contact hypersurface remain of maximal contact along the marked sequence. The final marked order locus is thus contained in the support of the final strict transform of the hypersurface. The boundary component tracked by the reduction starts with that same hypersurface and is transformed strictly at each step, except that it may undergo a total transform at the first step. The iterated support comparison puts the hypersurface's strict transform inside this boundary component's support. The boundary reduction makes that final support disjoint from the marked order locus. Since the locus is contained in the support and disjoint from it, it is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empty_of_comap_iso: The pulled-back locus is the inverse image of the original locus. Any point of the original locus would have a preimage under the isomorphism, and that preimage would belong to the pulled-back locus. Its emptiness therefore implies emptiness downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_support_maxContactI: The maximal-contact ideal is the derivative ideal at index one less than the mark. The derivative order-locus formula identifies the old marked locus with the order-at-least-one locus of this derivative ideal, since the mark is positive. The latter locus is exactly its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_support_of_isMa: At a point of the marked order locus, choose a neighborhood from the maximal-contact condition. The disjoint alternative is impossible because the point belongs to the locus. In the coordinate alternative the restricted hypersurface ideal is contained in the restricted maximal-contact ideal. The point lies in the support of the latter by the derivative order-locus formula and the support formula for pullback. Inclusion of ideals reverses support inclusion, so the point lies in the support of the restricted hypersurface ideal. Its image therefore lies in the original hypersurface support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_comap: Restriction of the ideal to an open is defined as pullback along the open inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eq: For a length-zero upper sequence it suffices to show that every lower center pulls back to the unit ideal along any comparison to its stage over the base. Suppose an upper point mapped to a lower center support. Projecting to the original scheme would give a point of the original marked order locus, since every center projects into it. Over the base this image is also the image of the upper point under the smooth morphism. Smooth pullback identifies the upper marked order locus with the inverse image of the original one, so the upper point would belong to the assumed empty locus. Thus all these pulled-back center supports are empty, and the comparison with the length-zero sequence follows.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_reduceA:
Form the self-pullback of the étale surjection. Its projections are étale, smooth, flat and surjective by base change. The given source is Noetherian, so the surjection is quasi-compact. The projections are then quasi-compact as well, and their composites with the structural map are quasi-compact and locally of finite type.

The source structural morphism, marked ideal and boundary all come from downstairs. The two pullbacks of the marked triple to the self-pullback consequently agree, because the two projections have equal composite with the surjection. Use the hypersurface pulled back along the first projection for both triples. It has maximal contact and strict normal crossings for the first triple by smooth pullback and for the second by the equality of triples. The strict comparison theorem identifies the reduction with this common triple and hypersurface as a strict pullback along each projection of the original source reduction. Each such strict pullback is isomorphic to the corresponding canonical base change. Thus the two canonical base changes of the source sequence are isomorphic. The descent theorem for the étale surjection gives a sequence downstairs whose strict pullback is the source sequence. Passing to blowup data and reconstructing preserves this comparison up to isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullback_coverMarkedSeque: The cover triple is admissible, has order bounded by its mark and has dimension at most the original reference dimension. The cover map is étale, smooth, flat and surjective, and the cover's structural map, ideal and boundary are pullbacks of the corresponding original data, using the tuned ideal. The cover hypersurface has maximal contact and strict normal crossings. Apply the étale descent theorem for reduction along this hypersurface. That reduction is the defined cover sequence, so the descended data give the required strict comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.heq_reduceAlongHypersurface_of_eq: First identify the two marked triples. Their schemes agree, so the given equality of the hypersurface ideals is now equality of ideals on the same scheme. The two reductions apply the same family to the same triple and hypersurface. Their resulting blowup sequences agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_bou: Admissibility of the pullback triple follows from the assumed smooth-pullback property, using quasi-compactness of its structural map. The structural morphism of that triple is the composite through the given map and its boundary is the list of pulled-back ideals. Its normal-crossings condition is therefore the one requested.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_reduceAlongHyp: Admissibility of the pulled-back triple follows from smooth pullback. Its dimension successor is at most that of the old triple by the étale dimension bound, hence within the reference bound. The chosen upper hypersurface has the required maximal-contact and normal-crossings properties by hypothesis. The strict pullback theorem for hypersurface reduction applies with these data and the given properties of the comparison map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_map_comap_eq_of_comp_eq: For each list entry, the two successive pullbacks equal pullback along the corresponding composite. Since the composites agree, the two transported entries agree. Applying this at every position gives the list equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismProperty_comp: Both morphisms have the property, which is assumed to be closed under composition. Thus their composite has it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismProperty_pullback_fst_self: The first projection of the self-pullback is a base change of the given morphism, using the pullback square with the two sides interchanged. The property is stable under base change, so it holds for this projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismProperty_pullback_snd_self: The second projection of the self-pullback is a base change of the given morphism. Apply stability under base change to the canonical square.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.baseChange_of_: Flat base change gives a strict pullback of the base sequence along the second map, followed by a strict pullback along the first. Their composite is a strict pullback along the composite map. By uniqueness up to isomorphism it is isomorphic to the given strict pullback along the composite. Transport the intermediate strict pullback relation through this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.congr_hom: Replace the comparison morphism by its equal. The original strict pullback relation then supplies the relation over that morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.congr_sourceSe: Substitute the equality of source sequences into the strict pullback relation. This gives the relation with the second source sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderReductionHypotheses.of_dropTrivialB: Dropping unit boundary entries leaves the dimension, ideal, and mark unchanged. Thus the dimension condition, order bound, and nonempty order locus persist. The assumed admissibility result supplies the remaining hypothesis for the trimmed triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendLowerDimReduction_congr_of_dim_le: If the final structural map is locally of finite type, form the derived triple. Its dimension is at most the original triple's dimension and hence fits both bounds. In each reduction the lower-dimensional family applies the same assignment to that derived triple and index. Both thus try to append the same marked continuation. If local finite type fails, both reductions return the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ne_top_iff_of_surjective: The unit ideal pulls back to the unit ideal, so a nonunit pullback forces the original ideal to be nonunit. Conversely, the support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. If the pullback is the unit ideal, this inverse image is empty. Surjectivity forces the original support to be empty, so the original ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivedTriple_dim_le: The underlying scheme of the derived triple is the final stage of the marked sequence. The stage dimension bound applied at the length of that sequence gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullback_cover_dropTrivia: Pass to the trimmed triple, which satisfies the order-reduction hypotheses. The descent property gives a sequence downstairs whose strict pullback is the cover sequence, so the chosen descent operation succeeds. Its returned sequence also has that strict pullback property by the specification of the operation. Descent of markings marks it for the trimmed boundary, and the restoration property marks it for the original boundary. Principalization for the original triple selects exactly this descent and takes its marked conversion. Forgetting the marking recovers the chosen underlying sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_of_triple: After identifying the triples, the structural maps coincide and both lists lie on the same scheme. The given equality then identifies the lists, so the existing strict normal crossing property gives the required one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_of_triple_eq: Identify the triples, so that the ideals of the proposed hypersurfaces lie on the same scheme. Their given compatible equality then identifies these ideals. The structural maps, marked ideals, and marks agree, so the maximal-contact property transports with them.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_eq_empty: Admissibility gives a smooth structural map over a characteristic-zero field. The order-locus formula for smooth pullback identifies the new locus with the inverse image of the old one. The inverse image of the empty set is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceAlongHypersurface_congr_of_dim_le: Boundary separation for all original entries yields the same sequence under both bounds. The final strict transform of the hypersurface is thus also common. Apply invariance of the appended reduction under enlargement of the bound to this common sequence and hypersurface transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceAlongHypersurface_toSequenceOfBlow: Identify the input triples and then the hypersurface ideals on their common scheme. The reductions now have the same inputs, so their underlying blowup sequences agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundary_congr_of_dim_le: Induct on the number of separation steps. At zero both sides give the empty sequence. At a successor the two prior sequences agree by induction. Apply invariance of the appended lower-dimensional reduction under enlargement of the dimension bound to this common sequence.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_reduceAlongHype: The two reference dimensions are comparable. If the lower reference dimension is smaller, the dimension comparison for hypersurface reduction replaces its lower-dimensional family by the one at the larger reference. Both triples then satisfy the dimension bounds at that reference. If the upper reference is smaller, make the corresponding replacement on the upper side and use the larger lower reference. In both cases use the dimension condition for the larger reference and apply the smooth pullback theorem with that common family.

Compare the boundary-separation sequences under the smooth map, removing unit boundary entries upstairs. The surviving-entry count equals the length of the new boundary, so this comparison reaches the end of both separation sequences. Their final structural morphisms are locally of finite type. The separation invariant gives separation on both sides, and the maximal-contact transform theorem puts the transformed hypersurface and remaining boundary in strict normal-crossings position. The resulting derived triples are admissible. Their dimensions stay within the reference bound, so the downward-closed dimension condition applies. The lower-dimensional continuation theorem now compares the continuations over the final-stage map, using the inherited order bound upstairs. Each hypersurface reduction is the corresponding separation sequence followed by this continuation. The append comparison gives the asserted pullback of the full reductions.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_and_isStrictPullbackBlowupS: An étale map is smooth, so the admissibility theorem applies to the pulled-back triple over its given structural map. Its dimension successor is at most that of the original triple, so the downward-closed dimension condition persists. Smooth pullback preserves the order bound and derivative balancing, and the directly pulled-back boundary retains its positive length. The reduction specification therefore gives a pullback comparison of the two blowup sequences. Each lower center has nonempty support by the specification, and every point of a lower center projects into the cosupport. Since the étale map covers the cosupport, the strict comparison criterion applies and yields the stated strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_withBoundary_cons_of_isMaxCon:
Use the étale equalization of the two maximal-contact hypersurfaces to find two maps from one scheme, each covering the original cosupport. Their pulled-back triples agree, since the maps identify the ideal, hypersurface and common remaining boundary and have the same structural map. The reduction upstairs gives one blowup sequence, strictly comparing to the two reductions downstairs by the étale pullback result.

Use the maximal-contact chain on this common sequence. The original two maps agree along its initial ideal subscheme because the equalization makes them agree on the specified downstairs subscheme, and this equality pulls back. The chain is compatible with each blowup and supplies the required center containments. All lower center images lie in the covered cosupport, and smooth center radicality converts the required support containments to ideal containments. These are the hypotheses of the lifting comparison for two strict pullbacks with one source, which yields an isomorphism between the two downstairs blowup sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_center_of_center_support_subset: The center at the given blowup step is smooth over the field. The radicality property for smooth centers converts containment of its support in the support of the given ideal into inclusion of the given ideal in the center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comap_comp_comp_eq: The subscheme of the pulled-back ideal is the pullback of the original closed immersion. On the canonical pullback, the composite through the first projection and the ambient map is the composite through the second projection and the old closed immersion. The two maps out of the old scheme agree after this immersion, so composing from the pullback gives equality. Transport this equality to the closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_eq_of_heq: Use the given equalities of ideals, marks and boundaries to identify the two types of marked sequences. The given equality between the sequences is then an equality in the same type. Passing to their underlying blowup sequences preserves it.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp_inv: Pull back the closed subscheme along the isomorphism. Its projection to the original closed subscheme is an isomorphism, and its projection to the new ambient scheme is that isomorphism followed by the original inclusion and the inverse ambient map. The pullback ideal is the kernel of this projection. Precomposing with an isomorphism preserves the kernel, giving the stated description.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf: Write the image as pullback along the inverse isomorphism. Pulling that ideal back along the original isomorphism gives pullback along the identity, hence the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.compl_support_comap: The support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the old support. Taking complements commutes with inverse image, so the complement open is the inverse image of the old complement open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_opens_preimage: The isomorphism carries the inverse image open into the given open. The inverse carries the given open into its inverse image because the two ambient maps are inverse. Restrict both maps to these opens. Their composites become the identity after composing with the respective open inclusions. The inclusions are monomorphisms, so the restricted morphisms are inverse. The restriction identity for the forward map gives the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_comap_of_isIso: The inclusion of the pulled-back closed subscheme followed by the isomorphism has kernel equal to the original ideal. The universal property of a closed immersion therefore factors this composite through the original closed subscheme. The inclusion of the original subscheme followed by the inverse isomorphism likewise has kernel equal to the pulled-back ideal and factors in the opposite direction. Compose the two factorizations and check their composites with the closed inclusions. The inverse identities for the ambient isomorphism show that these composites equal the original inclusions. As the inclusions are monomorphisms, the two factorizations are inverse, and the first has the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comap: Image under the isomorphism is pullback along its inverse. Together with the original pullback the two operations form pullback along the identity, which fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comp_comap_of_isIso: The closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal is isomorphic to the original one, compatibly with the ambient map. Thus its inclusion followed by both maps is the original inclusion followed by the final map, precomposed with this isomorphism. Precomposition with an isomorphism fixes the kernel, which is exactly the image ideal in each case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_comap_inv: The image ideal is the kernel of the closed-subscheme inclusion followed by the isomorphism. The formula for pullback along an isomorphism gives the same kernel when applied to the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_strictTransform_of_comm_: Write the image ideals along the ambient isomorphism as pullbacks along its inverse. Commutativity of the square then identifies their pullbacks to the second blowup scheme with the original pulled-back ideals transported by the upstairs isomorphism. In particular the two pulled-back closed subschemes are isomorphic. This isomorphism identifies their open parts off the pulled-back centers, since the complement of support commutes with pullback. The strict transform is the kernel of the map from this open part to the ambient blowup scheme. The two maps agree after transport by the isomorphisms, and precomposing by the isomorphism of opens preserves the kernel. The kernel on the second blowup scheme is therefore the image of the original strict-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_comp: The stage maps of the strict pullback along the source isomorphism are isomorphisms. At stage zero this follows from the base identifications, and at a successor it follows from the pullback square and the preceding isomorphism. Precompose the old closed immersions into the ambient sequence with these stage maps. This preserves closed immersions, and compatibility of the initial maps and transition squares gives the required commutativity. Each new source center is the pullback of the old source center, so their images in the ambient scheme agree. Precomposing with stage isomorphisms leaves the immersion kernels unchanged, preserving the strict-transform identity. The common lengths yield the claimed pushforward relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_eq_imageIdealSheaf_ker: Factor the first morphism through its scheme-theoretic image. In the composite, the kernel is determined by the inclusion of this image followed by the second map. That kernel is the image ideal of the first kernel under the second map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_of_iso_comp: The second morphism is obtained by precomposing the first with an isomorphism. Precomposition with an isomorphism leaves the kernel unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_isomorphic: Compose each closed immersion from the source sequence with the corresponding stage isomorphism of ambient sequences. The sequences have the same length, and these composites are closed immersions. The initial identification and transition identities hold by compatibility of the ambient isomorphisms with the sequence maps. Taking image ideals along the stage isomorphisms carries the old ambient centers to the new ones, so the image-of-center condition persists. It also carries the old strict-transform identity for the immersion kernels to the corresponding new identity, since strict transforms commute with the isomorphisms by their commutative transition squares. These are the required pushforward data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_length_eq_zero: The only stage of either sequence is stage zero. Use the initial isomorphism from the source stage to its base, the given closed immersion, and the inverse initial isomorphism on the target to form the stage immersion. It is a closed immersion and commutes with the two initial identifications. There are no successor stages or centers, so all step conditions are vacuous.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opens_map_comp: A point maps into the chosen open under the composite precisely when its first image lies in the inverse image under the second map. Thus the two open sets have the same points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opens_map_id: The inverse image of any open under the identity has exactly its original points.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eqToHom_of_eq: After identifying the equal indices, the ideals coincide and the stage map is the identity. Pullback along this map fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_comap_mapToEarlierScheme_of_le_of_ind: Induct from the first comparison index to the desired one. At the first index use the given identity. Every next step is unmatched by hypothesis, so the one-step comparison propagates that same equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_comap_mapToEarlierScheme_succ_of_inde: An unmatched center pulls back to the unit ideal from the earlier stage. The transition identity gives the same unit pullback when the center is first taken to the following stage. Away from the center, pulling back the strict transform is the same as pulling back the original ideal along the composite. The transition identity identifies that composite with the earlier comparison map, preserving the asserted ideal equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_of_centers_comap_eq_top: Induct on the stage. At stage zero lift the original map by the inverse initial isomorphism. The same isomorphism makes every compatible map factor through this lift. At a successor the inductive lift pulls the next center back to the unit ideal, which is locally generated by the nonzerodivisor one. Use the universal property of the blowup to lift to the next stage. For a compatible pair of maps into the source and the next stage, its projection to the previous stage factors through the inductive lift. The center pulls back to the unit ideal along that factorization too, so uniqueness of the blowup lift gives the required factorization through the new lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_length_zero_of_comap_cente: The original base map lifts uniquely through every downstairs blowup, since each center pulls back to the unit ideal along every compatible lift. The final lift gives the comparison map from the only upstairs stage via its initial isomorphism. Its factorization property gives the required final pullback square, and there are no upstairs steps. To verify omission of a downstairs center, suppose a point of that center and a point upstairs have the same base image. Choose a point over the pair in the scheme pullback at that stage. By uniqueness of the lift, its projection to the downstairs stage factors through the stage lift. It would therefore give a point in the support of the center pulled back along that lift, contradicting the unit-ideal hypothesis. All downstairs centers can thus be omitted.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_unique: The compatibility of the prescribed map makes the square commute. For a cone over the cospan, compose its map to the identified object with the inverse isomorphism. This gives the required second projection, and the assumed uniqueness of the other component gives the first projection. Any other lift has the same second projection, so composition with the inverse isomorphism identifies it with this lift. The square is therefore a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_eq_comap_lastMap: The marked sequences and their underlying blowup sequences have the same stage schemes and local Noetherian properties. Their blowup maps and centers agree, so the stated recurrences are also strict-transform recurrences for the underlying sequences. Apply the final-stage comparison for those sequences.

At upstairs stage zero, the given ideal comparison holds over downstairs stage zero. Propagate it across the unmatched downstairs steps before the initial matching index. Induct on the upstairs stage using the strict-transform comparison for a matched step followed by any intervening unmatched steps. At the final upstairs stage the matching index is the final downstairs index. The final map is the stage comparison followed by this index identification, whose pullback gives the final ideal equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_succ_eq_comap_ma: At the downstairs step matched with the current upstairs step, the blowup square is a flat pullback and the centers agree by pullback. The strict-transform formula across a flat pullback therefore identifies the next upstairs ideal with the pullback of the next downstairs transform along the comparison to that stage. Any intervening downstairs steps before the next matched index are unmatched. Propagate the equality across these steps, then identify the comparison at the matching index with the stated stage map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_lastMap: The final comparison square is a pullback over the original base-change morphism. Since that morphism is smooth, its base change to the final downstairs stage is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_isPullback_of_smooth_right: The first projection in the pullback square is a base change of the smooth map on the right. Smoothness is stable under base change.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.iteratedStrictTransfo: At stage zero the iterated transform pulls back the unit ideal along the initial isomorphism, giving the unit ideal. For a successor stage apply the single strict transform to the preceding unit ideal. It stays the unit ideal, completing the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_nil: Removing unit entries from an empty list leaves an empty list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_top_eq_top: The total transform of the unit ideal is the unit ideal. The strict transform contains the total transform, so it also equals the unit ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.append_drop_eq_map_comap: Use the given entrywise pullback descriptions of the upstairs lists. Pullback preserves positions and length, so dropping entries commutes with it. Pullback also distributes over concatenation, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_comap_of_isPullback: Express both tuned ideals as sums of weighted products of powers of derivative ideals. Pullback preserves sums, products, and powers. The assumed derivative-ideal compatibility identifies every individual factor after the field extension. Thus, for each exponent choice the two summands agree, and the sums agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeMapAtLength_eq_lastMap: The field-extension map at the length of the sequences is defined to be the final comparison map of the strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_of_eq: The two triples have equal data, so the given admissibility certificate applies to the first triple as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_of_eq: Identify the triples and their structural maps. The two local finite-type certificates are proofs of the same property, so the balance condition transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderBoundedByMult_of_eq: Equal triples have the same ideal and mark, so the second triple's order bound is also a bound for the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_projectionToBase_of_index_eq: Identify the equal indices. The stage identification becomes the identity, and the given pullback square is unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_append_of_fiel: For the underlying blowup data, append the strict pullback of continuations over the final comparison to the strict pullback of the initial sequences. The marked appends have precisely these underlying sequences, giving the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_markedBlowupSequence: Replace each set of marked data by its equal counterpart. The underlying sequences are then unchanged, and the given strict pullback relation applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_markedIdealWithBound: Identify the triples so that the comparison maps have the same source. Their given equality then identifies the maps, and the assignment yields the same source sequence. The existing strict pullback relation gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_morphism_eq: Substitute the equality of the base maps in the strict pullback relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_of_strictPullbackBlowupSeq: The strict pullback gives equality of the underlying sequence lengths. These lengths are the lengths of the marked data, so the desired equality follows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_map_comap_comp: At each entry the two successive pullbacks equal pullback along the composite. Entrywise application gives equality of the lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.list_prod_map_comap: For the empty list, the product is the unit ideal and pullback fixes it. For a nonempty list, pullback preserves the product of the first entry with the product of the tail. Apply the inductive equality to the tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_boundary_length_of_eq: Equal triples have equal boundary lists. Their lengths are equal, and the strict index bound transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_eq_of_eq: The two triples already use the same field, scheme, and structural morphism. The equalities of the ideal, mark, and boundary identify their remaining data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_strictPullbackSeq_appendLowerDi:
The append theorem expresses both lower-dimensional reductions as the initial sequences followed by marked continuations. To compare the continuations, paste the pullback square at the final stages with the original field-extension square. This identifies the final upstairs scheme with the field extension of the final downstairs scheme, compatibly with both projections. The marked ideal and boundary pull back along the final comparison by their strict pullback formulas. Tuning commutes with the field extension, and truncating and extending the boundary commute with entrywise pullback. The two derived triples are therefore identified by the canonical isomorphism after field extension.

Boundary divisor reduction commutes with the field extension for the downstairs derived triple, since the inherited hypotheses apply and the boundary index remains in range. It also commutes with the canonical isomorphism by smooth surjective functoriality for the two identified triples. Composing these strict pullback relations gives one for the assigned continuations over the final comparison. Transport it to the underlying data of the marked continuations and append it to the strict pullback of the initial sequences. The append formulas identify the result with the required reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pred_dim_of_eq: Identifying the triples identifies their underlying schemes and successor dimensions. Apply the given predicate proof to this common dimension.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.of_eq: Replace each sequence by the equal one given in the hypotheses. The original strict pullback relation then has exactly the required source and target sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_congr: Identify the equal structural maps, ideals, and marks. Both tuning constructions then use the same geometric data. The certificates of local finite type are proofs of the same property and do not affect the construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_congr_index: After identifying the equal indices, both boundary lists are on the same stage and the comparison morphism is the identity. Pullback along it fixes each entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq_map_comap_pullbackMapAtLengt: Apply the stagewise boundary comparison with the two equal final indices. The boundary computed from the underlying blowup data agrees with the marked boundary at the last stage. Its entrywise pullback along the final map is therefore the upstairs boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq_map_comap_strictPullbackComp: Identify the equal stage indices, so the stage identification in the composite becomes the identity. The flat-pullback formula for boundaries gives the remaining equality at that stage, using the local Noetherian hypotheses on both sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_comp_eqToHom: With the indices identified, the two ideals are the same and the stage identification is the identity. The composite with the identity is the original morphism, so the pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_projectionToBase: At equal indices the two projections to the base are the same. The identification of their source stages is the identity, and composing with it fixes the projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_congr_index: Identify the two equal indices. The corresponding stage schemes and their ideals then coincide, and pullback along the identity fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_comap_pullbackMapAtLength: The controlled-transform comparison expresses the final ideal upstairs as the pullback of the controlled transform downstairs at the same index. Strict pullback gives equal lengths, so this index is also the final stage downstairs. There the marked ideal is the controlled transform. Transporting to the common final stage gives pullback along the stated final map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_of_isBoundaryD: The defining smooth-surjective pullback property of boundary divisor reduction applies to the two admissible balanced triples. The assumptions give the dimension and order conditions and the required agreement of the nontrivial boundaries and their initial segments. The property supplies the strict pullback relation for their assigned reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastMap_comp_projectionToBase: The stage comparison at the last source index commutes with projection to the original schemes by its pullback square. Strict pullback gives equality of the two lengths. Identifying the target stage at the source length with the final target stage leaves its projection unchanged, so the square gives the claimed equality for the final map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_append_drop: Entrywise pullback distributes over list concatenation. Removing an initial segment commutes with entrywise pullback because that operation preserves positions and length. Substitute the given expression for the pulled-back boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_strictPullback_appendLowerDimRe: The strict pullback of the initial sequences gives a smooth surjective map of final stages. Pullback along that map preserves the tuned final ideal. The boundary comparison identifies the two derived boundaries exactly, because pullback distributes over concatenation and preserves the initial positions to be dropped. Thus the derived triple upstairs is the pullback of the derived triple downstairs. The derived triples satisfy the required order and balance conditions by the tuning theorem. Their dimension conditions and the stated boundary index bounds allow the smooth-surjective compatibility of boundary divisor reduction to compare the two assigned continuations. The append theorem identifies the actual lower-dimensional reductions with the initial sequences followed by these marked continuations, using separation of the dropped boundary components. The canonical identifications with the underlying continuation data preserve the strict pullback relation. Appending that relation to the given one for the initial sequences produces the required witness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_derivedTriple_eq: Both triples use the final upstairs scheme and the same base field. The final comparison identity identifies their structural maps, and smooth pullback of tuning identifies their ideals. Their tuned marks agree because pulling back preserves the original mark. Both use the supplemental ideals pulled back to the upstairs stage, followed by the truncated final upstairs boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackMapAtLength_comp_eq_comp_structu: The projections of the marked sequences are those of their underlying blowup sequences. Commutativity of the final comparison square gives equality of the composites to the original scheme. Postcompose with the original structural map and associate the composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackMapAtLength_comp_eq_pullbackTrip: The structural map of the pulled-back triple is the original base-change map followed by the original structural map. Substituting this description into the final comparison identity gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackMapAtLength_eq_lastMap: The comparison map at the length of the sequence is defined to be the final-stage map of the strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comp_eqToHom: The target identification is an isomorphism, hence smooth. Composing it with the smooth map preserves smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_lastMap: The stage comparison at the final source index is smooth by the stage pullback square. The final map is that comparison followed by the target identification, so it is smooth as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_map: The stage map and the projections to the original schemes form a pullback square. The stage map is thus a base change of the original smooth morphism, so it is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_pullbackMapAtLength: The map at the length of the sequences is the final map of the strict pullback, which is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_comp_eqToHom: An identification of equal targets is an isomorphism and thus surjective on points. A surjection followed by it remains surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_lastMap: Surjectivity is stable under base change for schemes. The stage comparison at the final source index is the base change of the original surjection by its pullback square. Composing with the target length identification preserves surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_pullbackMapAtLength: The map at the length of the sequences is the final map of the strict pullback, which is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedIdealAtLength_comap_pullbackMapAtLe: The final comparison map is smooth and makes the structural maps commute. The structural map downstairs is smooth by admissibility of the derived triple. The smooth pullback formula for balanced tuning therefore moves the pullback inside the tuning operation. The final ideal upstairs is precisely the pulled-back final ideal downstairs, and the original mark is preserved. Substituting these identities gives the tuned ideal upstairs.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_appendLowerDimR:
The last-stage map is smooth by base change. It pulls the final transformed hypersurface back to the upper transformed hypersurface, and the boundary tails of the derived triples agree after removing unit entries. Since the transformed hypersurface is the first entry on each side, the first entries of the boundaries also agree exactly after pullback. Compatibility of the final tuned ideals, structural maps and marks identifies the upper derived triple with the pullback of the lower one after replacing its boundary by the specified upper list.

The derived triples are admissible and satisfy the given dimension conditions. They are order-bounded and balanced by the tuning properties, and each boundary is nonempty because it starts with the transformed hypersurface. Apply the smooth-pullback property of the reduction at boundary index zero to compare their continuation sequences. The separated boundary condition ensures on each side that the continuation is a marked sequence for the original final triple and is actually appended. Concatenate the given separation comparison with the continuation comparison over its last-stage map. The resulting pullback relation is the required comparison of the two appended reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformAtLength_comap_lastMap: On each side the strict transform at the end is the iteration of strict transforms on the underlying blowup data. Smoothness of the comparison at the base implies flatness. The comparison of iterated strict transforms under this pullback identifies the upper final transform with the pullback of the lower final transform along the last-stage map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_restrict: The coordinate ideal is pulled back from the associated coordinate subspace of affine space. Pullback along the restricted chart factors as pullback through the original chart and then along the open inclusion, giving the restricted ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.map_restrict: Restricting the chart to the smaller open means precomposing its original map with the inclusion of that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.HasStrictNormalCrossingsWith.append_of_s: Induct on the list being prepended. The empty list gives the original condition. The induction hypothesis treats the tail, and disjointness of the head component lets the single-component addition theorem prepend it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.HasStrictNormalCrossingsWith.of_append: At a point of the subscheme, choose a coordinate chart for the full boundary. Give each entry of the suffix the coordinate assignment of its index shifted by the length of the prefix. The entry at that shifted position is the same ideal, so the unit and coordinate descriptions persist. Injectivity for assigned coordinates passes to this sublist, and the chart still describes the subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_length: At stage zero the boundary consists of the original entries pulled back along the initial isomorphism, so its length is the original length. Each step takes the strict transform of each old entry and appends one exceptional ideal. Thus each step adds one entry, proving the formula by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_drop: At the successor stage the boundary is the list of strict transforms followed by the exceptional ideal. The number dropped is at most the length of the list of strict transforms, which is the length of the old list. Thus the exceptional ideal remains at the end, and dropping entries commutes with the entrywise transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_eq_mul: The exceptional ideal is the pulled-back center and is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. Its power is therefore cancellable from the two products, giving equality of the factors.
Induct on the first list. For an empty first list the lookup is directly in the second list. For a nonempty first list, remove the first entry and decrement the lookup index. The resulting index is the length of the first tail plus the original offset, so the inductive equality applies.
Induct on the list before the appended tail. The empty case has no index in range. At the head the lookup returns the mapped first entry, while an index in the remaining list reduces to the same lookup on the tail at the preceding index. The induction hypothesis gives the mapped optional result.
The two indices are in range, so each optional lookup returns its corresponding entry. Equality of the optional lookups therefore gives equality of those entries.
Both optional lookups are defined at the given indices. The optional lookup identity for the mapped prefix and appended tail therefore identifies the entry with the image of the original entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_cons_of_dis: At a point of the subscheme choose a chart for the old list. Since the new component's support is disjoint from the subscheme, restrict the chart to the open complement of that support. The new component has unit ideal on the smaller chart, so assign it no coordinate. The other entries keep their former assignments after shifting their positions by one. Their unit and coordinate descriptions persist under open restriction, as does the description of the subscheme. Injectivity of the assigned coordinates follows from the original chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.index_lt_boundary_length: The length at the stage is the original boundary length plus the stage index. An index within the original list is therefore within the stage boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked: The next marked ideal witnesses divisibility by the exceptional power at each step. The controlled-transform identity transfers the required order bound along the center. The comparisons for the projections and boundary lists transfer smoothness of the center and its strict normal crossing condition. Thus all marking conditions hold for the underlying data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_disjoint_boundary_of_l: Induct forward from the stage at which disjointness is given. The original component keeps its index because each step transforms the existing entries and appends the exceptional ideal. Thus the entry at that index is the strict transform of the previous one. If a point lay in both the new order locus and its support, the order-locus hypothesis and the support inclusion for strict transforms would put its image in both previous sets. This contradicts the inductive disjointness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_iUnion_support_boundary_subset: Take a point whose image belongs to the support of an old boundary entry. If the image lies in the center, the point belongs to the exceptional support, which is an entry of the new boundary. Otherwise the point lies in the inverse image of that old support away from the center. This inverse image is contained in its closure, the support of the strict transform by the local Noetherian formula. The strict transform is also an entry of the new boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq_projectionToBase_toB: Both projections begin with the same initial isomorphism. At each successor they precompose the preceding projection with the same blowup map. Induction gives equality at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_subset_preimage: The support of the pulled-back ideal equals the inverse image of the original support. Equality gives the claimed inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_strictTransform_subset_preimage: The total transform ideal is contained in the strict-transform ideal. Hence at any point where the latter has a proper stalk, the total transform also has a proper stalk. The support of the total transform is the inverse image of the original support, giving the inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_boundary_eq_boundar: At stage zero both descriptions pull back the same original boundary along the same isomorphism. At a successor they take the same strict transforms and append the same exceptional ideal. The inductive equality of the preceding lists gives the equality at the next stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_controlledTransform: Both ideals at stage zero are the same pullback of the original ideal. At a successor use the inductive equality and the marked ideal formula to see that the next marked ideal is a quotient of the total transform by the exceptional power. The controlled-transform formula has the same quotient property. Since the exceptional power is cancellable, the two ideals agree.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.compactSpace_of_quasiCompact_toSpec: The spectrum of a ring is quasi-compact. The inverse image of the whole spectrum under a quasi-compact morphism is quasi-compact, and it is the whole source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverEtaleChart_coordIdeal: A chart coordinate ideal is the pullback of the indicated coordinate-subspace ideal in affine space. The transported chart factors through the inverse piece isomorphism and the original chart. Pulling back in these two steps gives the original chart's coordinate ideal pulled back along the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverPieceIso_inv_comp_coverPieceι: The inverse of the piece isomorphism is the factorization of the image-open inclusion through the open immersion from the piece. The defining identity of the factorization gives the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverPieceIso_inv_comp_map_comp_affineSp: The chart on the original piece commutes with the structural maps to the base. Precompose this equality with the inverse isomorphism from the image open to the original piece. The inverse isomorphism followed by the original open inclusion is the image-open inclusion followed by the cover map. This identifies the two composites to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverPieceι_comp_coverMap: The cover map is the map out of the disjoint union induced by the open inclusions into the original scheme. Restricting it to the chosen summand gives its defining open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTripleOpen_ι_comp_coverMap: Factor the image-open inclusion through the inverse of the piece isomorphism followed by the summand inclusion. After composing with the cover map, the summand inclusion followed by the cover map is the original open inclusion. This gives the stated factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_eq_tunedTriple_pullbackAlong: Both constructions use the disjoint union as their scheme and its cover map followed by the original structural map. Both use the original field and tuned mark, and obtain the ideal and boundary by pulling back the tuned ideal and original boundary along the cover map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_coverPieceIso_inv_comp_map: The inverse piece isomorphism is étale because it is an isomorphism. The original chart map is étale by hypothesis, and composition preserves étaleness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_maxContactCoord_or_dis: At a point of the tuned order locus, the upper bound on order forces equality with the positive tuned mark. The maximal-contact coordinate theorem gives an affine étale chart around the point and a coordinate ideal of maximal contact. At any other point, the complement of the tuned order locus is open because the locus is closed. Take an affine étale neighborhood contained in that complement and assign it the unit ideal. Its intersection with the order locus is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isMaxContactCover: For every point choose an affine neighborhood and local ideal with the two alternatives just established. The neighborhoods cover the scheme. The scheme is quasi-compact because its structural map is quasi-compact and the spectrum of the base field is quasi-compact. Choose a finite subcover and carry over its local ideals. It covers the scheme, and each member retains affineness and the required alternative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_coverTripleOpen: Every point of a disjoint union is the image of a point of one of its summands. For such a summand the point lies in the image open of its inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_tunedTriple: The field, structural map, and boundary are inherited from the admissible triple, giving characteristic zero, local finite type, quasi-compactness, smoothness, and strict normal crossings. The tuned mark is positive. The assumed nonvanishing on components supplies the condition for the tuned ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_coverTriple_scheme: Each member of the good cover is affine, and there are finitely many members. The cover triple is their disjoint union, which is affine as the spectrum of the finite product of their coordinate rings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_irreducibleCloseds_of_isEmpty: An irreducible closed subset is nonempty. Any such subset would therefore give a point in the empty space, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_coverMap: Choose an image open containing the point of the disjoint union. On that open the cover map factors as an isomorphism onto the corresponding piece followed by the original open inclusion. Its restriction is an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_fst_of_isPullback: At the image of a chosen point under the second projection, take an open neighborhood on which the given map is an open immersion. Its inverse image under the second projection is an open neighborhood of the chosen point. The first projection on this neighborhood is the base change of that open immersion and is therefore an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_coverPieceι: Each summand of a disjoint union of schemes is an open subscheme. Its canonical inclusion is consequently an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection is the base change of the given open immersion. Open immersions are stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_coverTriple_scheme_le_dim: Admissibility gives a finite upper bound on the dimension of the original scheme. If that scheme is empty, the cover scheme is also empty because it maps to it, and the dimension comparison holds. Otherwise the original scheme has a point, so its dimension is a finite natural number. The image opens cover the cover scheme and each has dimension at most this number by its open immersion into the original scheme. The dimension bound is local on this open cover. Apply the resulting bound to the successor dimensions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_coverMap_comp_structureMorp: The source is affine by the cover property and hence quasi-compact. The target is the spectrum of a field, so any open is empty or the whole target. Its inverse image is respectively empty or the whole source, both quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_coverPieceι: The open associated to a cover piece is its image in the disjoint union. The inclusion of that open has exactly this image, which is also the range of the original immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_coverTripleOpen: Restriction to an open is pullback along its inclusion. That inclusion factors as the inverse piece isomorphism followed by the summand inclusion. Pullback along the composite therefore first pulls back to the summand and then along the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_coverTripleOpen_le: The map from the image open to the original scheme is the inverse piece isomorphism followed by the original open inclusion. It is an open immersion, so the dimension of the image open is at most the dimension of the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_isEmpty: The ordered set of irreducible closed subsets of the empty space is empty. Its unique map to the ordered set for the other space is strictly monotone vacuously. The dimension inequality follows from the bound on chain lengths under a strictly monotone map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_isOpenImmersio: An open immersion gives the source the subspace topology of its image. For a subspace, taking closures in the ambient space embeds the order of irreducible closed subsets, since intersecting those closures with the subspace recovers the original closed subsets. Strict chains therefore give the dimension bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_ne_bot: The closure of the given point is a nonempty irreducible closed subset. The ordered set used to define Krull dimension therefore contains a chain with one member, ruling out the bottom value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_baseField: The tuned triple takes its base field directly from the original triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_boundary: The tuned triple takes the original boundary list as its boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_ideal: The ideal used to define the tuned triple is the balanced tuned ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_mult: The mark in the tuned triple is the tuning exponent of the original mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_scheme: The underlying scheme in the definition of the tuned triple is the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedTriple_structureMorphism: By construction, the structural map of the tuned triple is the original map to the base field's spectrum.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsLocalIsomorphism.comp_isIso: Around a point of the source, choose an open on which the first morphism is an open immersion. Postcomposing this restriction with the isomorphism gives another open immersion. The same source neighborhoods therefore exhibit the composite as a local isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsLocalIsomorphism.isIso_comp: At the image of a source point under the isomorphism, choose an open where the second map is an open immersion. The inverse-image open around the source point is isomorphic to that chosen open. The composite restricted to it is this isomorphism followed by the open immersion, so it is again an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedIdeal_eq_of_mult_eq_one: The balanced tuned ideal is the tuned ideal at the tuning exponent. At mark one that exponent is one, and the tuned ideal with both parameters one is the original ideal. The admissibility hypotheses supply the structural conditions for these identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverMap_flat: The cover map of an admissible triple is smooth, since it is induced from the open inclusions of the cover pieces. Smoothness implies flatness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverMap_surjective: The bound on the balanced tuned ideal follows from the upper order bound and nonempty marked order locus. With this bound a maximal-contact cover exists. The cover map for the chosen maximal-contact cover is surjective because the selected opens cover the scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_inv_eq_comap: Pull back the image ideal under the inverse isomorphism used to form it. Because this map is a closed immersion, the pullback recovers the original ideal. Now pull back along the forward isomorphism. The two successive pullbacks on the image side cancel, leaving that image ideal equal to the pullback of the original ideal along the forward isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_and_dim_eq_withSchemeIdealB: A closed immersion identifies its source with the closed subscheme of its kernel. The given factorization equals the canonical map from the source to that subscheme, because the subscheme inclusion is a monomorphism. Under this isomorphism the structural map on the kernel subscheme is the original structural map of the given source composed with the isomorphism. Smoothness, local finite type and quasi-compactness therefore carry across. The image ideal is the pullback along the inverse identification, so nonvanishing on components also carries across. The field has characteristic zero, the mark is positive and the empty boundary satisfies strict normal crossings. These give admissibility. Finally, the isomorphism of schemes induces a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces, which preserves Krull dimension and hence its dimension successor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_map_coverBlowupSequen: The original cover map is a local isomorphism because each piece maps by an open inclusion. Apply the stagewise preservation result to the strict pullback of the cover sequence along this map, using the stage bound in the reconstructed sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_map_of_isLocalIsomorp: At zero the comparison is the original base map conjugated by the two initial isomorphisms. Composition with an isomorphism on either side preserves the local isomorphism property. At a successor the comparison is a pullback of the preceding comparison. A local isomorphism stays a local isomorphism after base change, since its open-immersion neighborhoods pull back to open-immersion neighborhoods. Induction gives the result at every allowed index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocalIsomorphism_of_eq: Substitute the equality of morphisms. The property requested is the given local isomorphism property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_schemeAt_coverBlowup: The original triple is admissible. Its structural map is locally of finite type and quasi-compact over a Noetherian field spectrum, so its scheme is Noetherian. The order bound gives a good cover and the cover properties make its triple admissible. Its scheme is Noetherian by the same finite-type and quasi-compactness argument. Apply stage Noetherianity to the lower and cover sequences over these starting schemes. In each case Noetherianity implies the required local property at each stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_blowupSequenceData_schemeAt: Reconstruct the sequence of blowups. Reconstruction preserves its length and stage schemes. Blowups of a Noetherian scheme remain Noetherian, so the known stage Noetherianity theorem applies at the given index and transfers to the stage in the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_balancedTunedIdeal_le_tunedMult_: The pointwise upper bound and nonempty marked order locus say that the original ideal has maximal order equal to the mark. The tuning property bounds the order of the tuned ideal by the chosen positive tuning exponent everywhere. The balanced tuned ideal is the tuned ideal at this exponent, and the tuned mark is that exponent. Thus the bound is exactly the one stated.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_sequenceOfBlowups_ideal_le_mult: The cover properties include preservation of the initial bound by the mark at every stage of an admissible marked sequence. Apply that property at the specified stage and point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_appLE_image: The open immersion identifies the chosen source open with its image open. The induced map on their section rings is an isomorphism, hence bijective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coverMaxContactIdeal_coverPieceι: The cover ideal is the finite intersection of the kernels obtained from all local ideal subschemes in their summands. Pullback along one summand inclusion preserves that intersection. Its own kernel pulls back to the corresponding local ideal. Every other kernel pulls back to the unit ideal because the pieces are disjoint. The intersection of these terms is the local ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iInf: Check the ideal sheaves on each affine source open. Its image under the open immersion is affine and the map on section rings is an isomorphism. Pullback on the source open extends the ideal of sections on that image. The sections of the finite infimum are the infimum of the section ideals, and extension across the isomorphism preserves this infimum. These are precisely the section ideals of the right-hand side.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverPieceι_base_ne_of_ne: A point in a disjoint union has its summand index as part of its data. Points coming from distinct summands therefore have distinct images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_iInf: A finite intersection of ideal sheaves has, on each affine open, the intersection of their section ideals. Evaluate that formula on the given affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_of_isMa: At the point, use the local chart in its cover piece. The cover ideal restricts to the given local ideal on every piece, so it is the unit ideal or a coordinate ideal on the transported chart. The pointwise singleton normal-crossings criterion then gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_of_isMaxC: The equality of the restriction with the local ideal on every piece gives the normal-crossing condition at every point. The assumed smooth-divisor property supplies the global divisor condition for the only entry. These two conditions give strict normal-crossing position for the singleton.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_coverMaxContact: The cover ideal pulls back on every piece to its prescribed local ideal. The maximal-contact criterion on the cover applies to this restriction equality and the good-cover data at every piece, yielding maximal contact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_comp_comap_eq_top_of_disj: The support of the kernel of the composite is the closure of its image because the composite is quasi-compact. The range of the open immersion is open and disjoint from that image by hypothesis. It is therefore also disjoint from the image closure. Thus the pulled-back kernel has empty support and is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_comp_comap_self: The open immersion identifies the source with its image open. The scheme-theoretic image of the ideal subscheme in the target restricts on this open to the same closed subscheme under that identification. The defining ideal is the kernel of the composite inclusion, so pulling it back recovers the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_comp_coverPieceι_comap_of: The inclusions of distinct pieces have disjoint images and the second inclusion is quasi-compact. The disjointness result for restricting the kernel of a subscheme inclusion therefore makes this pullback the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_comp_coverPieceι_comap_se: The cover piece inclusion is a quasi-compact open immersion. Pullback along this inclusion recovers the local ideal from the kernel of its subscheme embedded into the cover, by the self-restriction result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_iInf_of_bijective: A bijective ring map gives an order isomorphism on ideals by extension. An order isomorphism preserves infima, so extending the intersection gives the intersection of the extended ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_coverPieceι: A summand of the disjoint union is an open and closed subscheme. The inverse image of a quasi-compact open under its inclusion is the intersection with this closed summand, a closed subset of a quasi-compact space. Thus the inclusion is quasi-compact.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MaxContactCoverProperties.derivedTriple_: The derived triple is on the last scheme of the given sequence. Its dimension successor is at most that of the triple from which the sequence starts, by the stagewise bound. That dimension successor is at most the reference bound by hypothesis. Compose the inequalities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MaxContactCoverProperties.hasStrictNorma: At the specified step the center is smooth over the field under the stage structural map. The combined list has strict normal crossings, the center has strict normal crossings with its tail and the hypersurface ideal is contained in the center ideal. Apply the cover property for adding such a hypersurface to the tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MaxContactCoverProperties.isMaxContactHy: Both consecutive stages are admissible by the stage property. The earlier one has a smooth structural map and the successor is locally Noetherian. The order bound holds on the earlier stage, its center lies in the corresponding marked order locus and has strict normal crossings, and the successor ideal satisfies the controlled-transform identity. Apply the one-step maximal-contact property to this blowup. The structural map at the successor is the blowup map followed by the previous structural map, so that result is the claimed one for the successor data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MaxContactCoverProperties.krullDimSucc_s: Reconstruction preserves the length and each stage scheme. The dimension bound in the cover properties therefore applies to the reconstructed marked sequence at the same index and gives the desired bound on the scheme in the data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_of_eq: Substitute the equality of the two structural morphisms. The marked ideal, mark and hypersurface are the same, so the supplied maximal-contact property applies.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupLiftEqOnControlledTransform: Apply the blowup-lift comparison theorem. The controlled-transform product identity first gives equality of the two projected maps on the transformed subscheme. Around any point of that subscheme, both projected maps therefore land in a common affine neighborhood of their image.
