The affine lift comparison gives equality of the lifted maps on the corresponding open of the transformed subscheme. These opens cover it, so the lifted maps agree there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.existsMaxContactControlledTransforms: The maximal-contact ideal satisfies the one-step containment under controlled transform. The construction from this containment produces the sequence of maximal-contact controlled transforms, with the initial pullback, successive product identities and center containments.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_comap_of_smooth: Identify the structural map upstairs with the composite through the smooth comparison. Derivative balancing is equivalent to the stated power containments for its iterated derivative ideals. Smooth pullback commutes with these iterated derivative ideals and preserves powers and inclusions. Pulling back each power containment downstairs thus gives the corresponding one upstairs, which proves derivative balancing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_schemeAt: The stage Noetherianity theorem applies to the marked sequence of the admissible triple at an index within its length. A Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian, giving the property of the stage scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_isPullback_of_center: For each actual lower blowup choose a point in its center support. Its projection to the base lies in the image of the upper base map by hypothesis, so the pair lifts to the scheme pullback at that lower stage. The lift is in the support of the pulled-back center. Thus every lower center survives pullback. The strictness criterion for pullback sequences then matches all steps and gives a strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_support_subset_of_smooth: The closed subscheme of the center is smooth over a field and hence reduced. Its defining ideal is radical. Containment of the center support in the other support puts the other ideal in the vanishing ideal of the center support. This vanishing ideal is the center's radical and therefore the center ideal itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactIdealComapLeControlled: The successor ideal is the controlled transform by its product identity and uniqueness. Apply the derivative transform bound to the derivative iterate of order one below the mark. Since the mark is positive, the remaining exceptional exponent in the bound is one. This derivative iterate is the maximal-contact ideal, both before and after the blowup. The bound is exactly the desired maximal-contact inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_mem_orderAtLeastLocus_o: The center support is contained in the marked order locus at its stage. Apply the projection result for a point of this stage locus to conclude that its image lies in the original marked order locus.

Induct on the stage. At zero the ideal is pulled back along the initial isomorphism, and its marked order locus is the corresponding inverse image. At a successor the one-blowup order-locus result puts the image in the preceding marked order locus, using the controlled-transform identity and the center condition. Apply induction to that image and compose the projections to obtain membership in the original locus.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_spe: Identify the map of spectra with the spectrum map of the field homomorphism. Strict normal-crossing position is preserved by this field base change, so its result for the singleton boundary is the claimed condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_comap_fieldBase: At the image of the given upstairs point choose an affine neighborhood from the maximal-contact condition. Its inverse image under the field extension is affine. If the lower open is disjoint from the marked order locus and the hypersurface ideal is the unit there, the same holds upstairs by the field-extension formula for the order locus and preservation of the unit ideal. Otherwise base change the étale chart. The lower hypersurface is generated on the affine open by its chosen chart coordinate. Extension of the section ideal gives the ideal generated by the corresponding upstairs coordinate. The maximal-contact ideal commutes with field extension, and the original coordinate belongs to it, so the extended coordinate belongs to the new maximal-contact ideal. It therefore gives the required chart at the upper point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_comap_specMapOf: The map of spectra induced by the field homomorphism is the spectrum of its ring map. Under this identification the pullback scheme, both projections and their finite-type condition are those of the field-base-change theorem. Apply that theorem to the marked ideal and hypersurface.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactHypersurfaceBaseChange: On the extended triple the structural map is the second pullback projection, the ideal is pulled back along the first projection and the mark is unchanged. Apply the maximal-contact field-extension result to the assumed hypersurface using the finite-type and smoothness properties of the original triple. Apply normal-crossings preservation under field extension to the singleton hypersurface list. These supply the two conditions of the comparison.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_iteratedS: At every stage, the transformed hypersurface has maximal contact, so its support contains the order locus that contains the center. The center subscheme is smooth over the field and hence reduced. Its ideal equals its radical, so this support containment implies that the hypersurface ideal is contained in the center ideal. Now induct on the stages. At zero, dropping the original boundary length leaves the empty list, giving the assumed singleton normal-crossings condition. At a successor, the center has strict normal crossings with the boundary tail because it has them with the full boundary. By induction the hypersurface and tail are in strict normal-crossing position. The center containment lets us add the hypersurface to the list with which the center has strict normal crossings, using the stated geometry property. The normal-crossings blowup theorem preserves the condition for the strict transforms of this combined list with the new exceptional ideal appended. The boundary-tail recursion identifies that list with the strict transform of the hypersurface followed by the new tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_comap_iso: At the image point choose an affine neighborhood from the maximal-contact description. Its inverse image under the isomorphism is affine. If the original open misses the marked order locus and the hypersurface ideal is the unit ideal there, the pulled-back open has the same two properties by preservation of order and of the unit ideal. Otherwise transport the étale chart through the isomorphism. Its chosen coordinate ideal is the restriction of the pulled-back hypersurface. The maximal-contact ideal, as the iterated derivative ideal, also commutes with the isomorphism. Thus the coordinate ideal remains contained in the restricted maximal-contact ideal, proving maximal contact on the transported chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_congr: After identifying the structural morphisms and the two ideals, the maximal-contact conditions agree. The two witnesses of being locally of finite type express the same property of the identified morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_iteratedStrictT: The structural map at every actual stage is smooth over the base by admissibility of the marked sequence, so each is locally of finite type. At stage zero the original hypersurface and ideal are pulled back along the initial isomorphism. Maximal contact survives that isomorphism. At a successor, the induction result gives maximal contact for the preceding stage. Apply the assumed one-step maximal-contact theorem to its blowup in the reconstructed sequence. Reconstruction identifies the projection, ideal and blowup with those stored in the data, and the iterated strict transform at the successor is the strict transform used by the theorem. This proves the result up to the given stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_of_eq_of_eq_of_: Substitute the equal structural morphisms, marked ideals and hypersurface ideals. With the same mark, the property to prove is the supplied maximal-contact property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_of_smooth_morphism: A smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation, which implies it is locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_le_of_isReduced_subscheme: On each affine open, the given ideal is the kernel of the section map to the corresponding open in its closed subscheme. An element in the radical has a power in the kernel, so its image in the section ring of the closed subscheme is nilpotent. That section ring is reduced, and the image is zero. Hence the element lies in the kernel itself. Applying this on every affine open proves the inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_maxContact_dim_le_of_de: Apply the general order-reduction result with the upper dimension condition given by the bound n and the lower condition by strict inequality with n. A dimension strictly below one at most n is strictly below n. Thus the required dimension link holds, and the other hypotheses give the relevant reduction and descent data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_maxContact_of_descentHy: For each admissible order-bounded triple satisfying the dimension condition, apply the cover and descent results for the center certificates, the order bound along the sequence, nonempty center supports and resolution. The empty-cosupport result gives the trivial sequence in that case. The pushforward theorem for a smooth divisor uses the lower-dimensional reduction, the boundary-divisor specifications and the link between the two dimension conditions. The descent hypotheses supply field extension and smooth pullback, each in ordinary and strict form. In each pullback property the pointwise bound may be stated using the original mark because extension, pullback and replacement of the boundary preserve it. These are all the conditions of order reduction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_baseField: Replacing the boundary copies the original base field. Thus filtering the boundary leaves that field equal to the original.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_boundary: The boundary of the constructed triple is the old list filtered for entries different from the unit ideal. Its retained entries are in their original order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_def: Remove the unit ideals by filtering the original boundary list, then replace the triple's boundary with that filtered list. This is the trimming construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_dim: The dimension successor depends on the underlying scheme. Filtering the boundary leaves the scheme unchanged, so the dimension successor agrees.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_ideal: Filtering the boundary entries does not alter the marked ideal sheaf. It remains the same field of the triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_mult: Replacing the boundary copies the mark from the original triple, so the two marks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_scheme: The construction changes the boundary on the original scheme. Its underlying scheme is therefore the same scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_structureMorphism: The replacement operation keeps the structural morphism of the triple and changes its listed boundary ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_succ: The recursion takes the strict transform of the previous ideal under the next blowup along its center. This is the stated formula at a successor index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_zero: The zero stage is identified with the starting scheme by the initial isomorphism. The recursion starts by pulling back the hypersurface ideal along this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceOrder_of_orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empt: Admissibility selects the admissible branch of the reduction. In that branch the empty marked order locus selects the empty marked sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformAtLength_eq: The final strict transform is defined by evaluating the iterated strict transform at the length of the sequence.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderReductionHypotheses.dropTrivialBoun: Trimming the boundary leaves the scheme, ideal and mark unchanged, so it carries over the dimension condition, the order bound and nonempty cosupport. The trimming property in the descent hypotheses supplies admissibility for the new boundary. These are the reduction hypotheses for the trimmed triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_support_nonempty: If the original cosupport is empty, the sequence has length zero and there is no index to consider. Otherwise the reduction is reconstructed from a selected strict descent of the cover sequence. The cover centers are proper by the cover properties. The strict pullback comparison forces each corresponding lower center to be proper, because a unit ideal would pull back to a unit ideal. Reconstruction retains the centers and their indices. A proper ideal sheaf has nonempty support, proving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_blowupSequenceData_isStrictPullba: Trim the boundary and use the cover descent property to obtain a sequence downstairs whose strict pullback is the constructed cover sequence. Hence the descent operation succeeds and selects such a sequence. For that selected sequence, the descent hypothesis establishes markedness for the balanced tuned ideal on the trimmed triple. The tuning equivalence then makes it marked for the original ideal and mark on the trimmed boundary. The trimming property restores markedness for the full boundary. Since the original order locus is nonempty and the descent operation succeeds, the definition of maximal-contact reduction returns the reconstructed marked sequence from these selected data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_balancedTunedIdeal_iff_and_orde: Admissibility supplies the smooth characteristic-zero structural map and the positive mark needed for tuning. The given pointwise bound and nonempty cosupport are the maximal-order hypotheses for the marked ideal. Apply the tuning property to the original ideal, its balanced tuned ideal and the underlying blowup sequence. It identifies their markedness conditions and gives equality of the corresponding controlled-transform order loci at each stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isResolution_of_orderAt_le_mult: A marked sequence resolves the ideal exactly when its final marked order locus is empty. If the initial locus is empty, the reduction is the empty sequence and its final ideal is the original one transported along the initial isomorphism, which preserves emptiness. Otherwise use the strict descent of the cover sequence and its markedness for the tuned ideal on the trimmed boundary. The cover reductions resolve the tuned ideal. The final order locus of the descended tuned ideal is therefore empty by flat surjective descent along the cover comparison. The tuning equivalence identifies that locus with the final order locus of the original ideal. Thus the reconstruction resolves the original triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_zero_of_orderAtLeastLocus_eq_e: For the admissible triple with empty marked order locus, the reduction takes the empty-sequence branch. The principalization is that reduction with the prescribed family, so its length is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_controlledTransform_eq: The final comparison map of the strict pullback is surjective, since it is a base change of the surjective base map. Flat pullback of the controlled transforms identifies the final upper ideal with the pullback of the final lower one, using the given divisibility at each lower stage. The sequence lengths are equal by strictness. The final upper order locus is empty, so emptiness descends along the surjective comparison to the final lower order locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_empty_of_comap_eq_e: Suppose a point belongs to the original marked order locus. Surjectivity gives a point over it. Order cannot decrease under pullback, so the point upstairs belongs to the pulled-back marked order locus. This contradicts emptiness upstairs. The original locus is therefore empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_ideal_le_mult: The stagewise order bound in the descent hypotheses applies to any marked blowup sequence of the admissible triple when the initial order is bounded by the mark. Apply it to the maximal-contact principalization at the specified stage and point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxContactHypersurface.comap_of_isOpen: Around an upstairs point choose an affine open contained both in a local open-immersion neighborhood and in the inverse image of a downstairs maximal-contact neighborhood. The resulting map to that downstairs open is an open immersion, hence étale. Restrictions of pulled-back ideals are pullbacks along this restricted map. If the downstairs neighborhood is disjoint from the order locus with unit hypersurface ideal, smooth pullback gives the same properties upstairs. In the coordinate case, compose the original chart with the restricted map. The coordinate ideal and its containment in the marked ideal pull back, giving the coordinate condition at mark one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_eq_self_of_mult_eq_on: Substitute mark one. The balanced tuning formula at mark one gives the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_derivedTriple_emptyMarkedBlowup: The final boundary of an empty sequence is the original list. Dropping its full length leaves the empty list. The derived boundary therefore consists exactly of the supplemental entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_comp_map_eq_comap: Both coordinate ideals come from the same coordinate subspace of affine space. Pullback along the composite chart is pullback along the original chart followed by pullback along the precomposed map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_eq_top_of_orderAt_le_one: The bound by one makes the order-at-least-two locus empty. The derivative order-locus identity at derivative index one identifies this locus with the order-at-least-one locus of the first derivative ideal. The latter locus is its support, so the derivative ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_derivedTriple_emptyMarkedBlowupSeq: The derived ideal is the balanced tuning of the final ideal. At mark one tuning gives back that ideal, and the empty sequence's final ideal is the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_of_eq_derivedTriple_emptyMark: Identify the given triple with the displayed derived triple. The original admissibility and order bound allow the derived-triple balance theorem, which supplies balance for this triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_one_of_etaleCha: At a point on the divisor choose the indicated chart and restrict it to an affine neighborhood. The divisor ideal stays a single coordinate ideal, and its inclusion in the marked ideal persists by pullback. At mark one this is the maximal-contact coordinate condition. At a point off the divisor, choose an affine open disjoint from its closed support. The divisor ideal is unit there. Inclusion of the divisor ideal in the marked ideal puts the support of the marked ideal inside the divisor support. Thus the open misses the order-at-least-one locus as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactInvariant_of_mult_eq_one: At mark one the maximal-contact ideal is the original ideal. The order bound makes its first derivative ideal unit. The product occurring in the invariance condition is therefore the original ideal, giving the required inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_coverMarkedBlo: At mark one the given coordinate charts and the inclusion of the divisor ideal in the marked ideal give maximal contact. The cover comparison for a maximal-contact hypersurface now applies.

The boundary of the cover is the pullback of the original empty list and is therefore empty. Separating all of it gives the empty sequence. The decomposition of the cover reduction as separation followed by a continuation thus has an empty initial sequence. Apply the mark-one comparison for this append.

A smooth divisor admits the required single-coordinate descriptions on étale charts. Its ideal is contained in the ambient marked ideal because the latter is the kernel of the closed subscheme of the given ideal followed by the divisor inclusion. A section vanishing on the divisor also vanishes on that smaller subscheme. Apply the étale-chart version of the cover comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_cover_of_eq_ap:
At mark one tuning preserves the ideal and the mark, so the cover triple's ideal is the original ideal pulled back along the cover. Its structural map is the original structural map composed with the cover. Adding the divisor to the original empty boundary gives an admissible balanced triple. Étale functoriality of first-boundary reduction identifies the reduction of its pullback to the cover as a strict pullback.

On the cover the initial sequence is empty. The derived triple for its continuation therefore has the same map, ideal, and mark as that pulled-back triple. Its singleton boundary consists of the cover's chosen hypersurface at the initial stage. The pulled-back original divisor and this chosen hypersurface both give maximal contact for the same ideal at mark one. Independence from the choice of maximal contact gives an isomorphism of their first-boundary reductions. The assumed append description identifies the latter reduction with the cover sequence up to isomorphism, since the prefix is empty. Transport the strict pullback relation along these isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_of_emptyMarkedBlowupSequenceD: The append identity for an empty initial sequence identifies the resulting marked sequence up to isomorphism with its continuation. Passing to their underlying blowup sequences preserves this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_of_isMaxContactHypersurface_s: The order bound at mark one gives maximal-contact invariance. Both singleton boundaries supply a maximal-contact entry and are admissible. Apply independence of the first-boundary reduction from the choice of maximal-contact hypersurface, with an empty remaining boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_congr: The two triples have the same base field and scheme. The given equalities identify their maps, ideals, marks, and boundaries, hence the triples.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mult_derivedTriple_emptyMarkedBlowupSequ: The derived mark is the tuning exponent of the original mark. That exponent is one at the given mark one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_emptyMarkedBlowupSequen: The final stage of the empty sequence is the original scheme, and its projection is the identity. Composing it with the original structural map gives that map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_derivedTriple_emptyMar: The derived structural map is the final projection followed by the original structural map. For the empty sequence the projection is the identity, so the map is the original one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_ideal_le_mult_along_sequence: Induct on the stage within the sequence. At stage zero the ideal is the original ideal transported along the initial isomorphism and its order is unchanged. At a successor the previous structural map is smooth and the center has strict normal crossings with the boundary. The center lies in the marked order locus, so the previous ideal is contained in the mark-th power of the center ideal. The successor product identity identifies the successor ideal with the controlled transform for this containment. The order bound for a controlled transform applies to the induction bound at the previous stage and gives the same bound at every point of the successor.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundaryLocus_eq_iUnion_support: A point belongs to the boundary locus exactly when it lies in the support of some ideal in the stage boundary. The same listed ideal witnesses membership in the union, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq_map_comap_strictPullbackComp: The strict comparison pairs stages of the same index in pullback squares. Along a flat comparison the initial boundary ideals are pulled back and both strict transforms and exceptional ideals commute with the pullback. The boundary comparison theorem therefore identifies the upper stage boundary with the list of pullbacks of the lower stage boundary in order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iUnion_support_comap_eq_preimage: A point in the left-hand union lies in the support of a pulled-back ideal from the original list. Its image lies in the support of the corresponding original ideal and hence in the union downstairs. Conversely, if its image belongs to one of the original supports, the point belongs to the corresponding pulled-back support, whose ideal appears in the mapped list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundary_of_forall_mem: Induct on the stage. At zero the two boundaries are the images of the original lists under pullback by the initial isomorphism, so the assumed list membership transfers. At a successor an entry is either the strict transform of a preceding boundary entry or the exceptional ideal. The preceding entry transfers by induction and its strict transform occurs in the second list. Both lists append the same exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundary_of_mem_boundary_dropTrivial: Every entry of the trimmed boundary is an entry of the original boundary, since trimming only filters the list. Apply the stagewise preservation of boundary membership to the two initial lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr_map: Identify the structural maps using their equality. The certificate for the first map is then a certificate for the second with the same data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr_mult: Replace the mark by the equal mark in the certificate. Its other data are identical, so the supplied certificate gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_of_isStrictPullbackBlow:
At mark one the balanced tuned ideal equals the original ideal and the tuned mark equals one. The strict pullback comparison has equal lengths. At the given stage the structural morphism of the cover factors through the lower structural morphism via the comparison map, by the pullback square over the bases. The upper stage ideal and center are the pullbacks of the lower ones, and flat comparison gives the upper boundary as the list of pullbacks of the lower boundary. Its boundary locus is therefore the inverse image of the lower locus.

The cover has the required order certificate at this stage by the cover properties. The stage comparison is a local isomorphism by the descent hypotheses and is surjective because the original cover is surjective. Rewrite the cover certificate using the pullback descriptions of the structural morphism, ideal, center and boundary locus, and identify its mark with the lower mark. The certificate descent hypothesis then gives the lower certificate. Finally, the lower structural map equals the projection to the original scheme followed by its structural map, as used in the reconstructed sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_of_orderAt_le_mult: If the mark is at least two, the corresponding certificate is available directly from this inequality. Otherwise admissibility gives mark one. In this case the given center index implies that the initial cosupport is nonempty, since an empty cosupport would produce a length-zero sequence. Use the strict descent of the cover after trimming unit boundary entries. At mark one tuning preserves both the ideal and mark, so the strict pullback certificate theorem gives the certificate for the descended sequence with the trimmed boundary. Every entry of that boundary at the given stage occurs in the full stage boundary, hence its boundary locus is contained in the full locus. Monotonicity of the certificate under this containment gives the desired certificate for the reconstructed original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_strictPullbackComparisonMap_o: The comparison at the specified stage is a base change of the original map, by the strict pullback relation. Surjectivity is stable under base change, giving the stagewise surjectivity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_isoRangeOpens_inv: Composing the inverse range isomorphism with the inclusion of the source open and then the original map gives the inclusion of the image open. Pullback of an ideal along this composite equals the three successive pullbacks, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_orderCertificate_of_isLocal: Surjectivity gives a lift of the given point. Since the map is a local isomorphism, an open around the lift maps by an open immersion onto an open containing the original point. Restrict the upper certificate to this source open using stability under open immersions. Transport it through the inverse range isomorphism to the image open. The composition formula identifies the structural map there, while functoriality identifies the ideal and center pullbacks and the inverse image of the boundary set with their restrictions to the image open. This is the required local certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_of_comap_of_isLocalIsom: For each point downstairs, the local-isomorphism result gives an open neighborhood with the required certificate, obtained from the pulled-back certificate. Apply the local-to-global certificate property to this family of neighborhoods.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_isoRangeOpens_inv: The composite of the inverse range isomorphism and the two subsequent maps equals the inclusion of the image open. Inverse image along a composite is the succession of inverse images, so the two sets agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.rangeOpens_ι_comp: The inclusion of the image open equals the inverse range isomorphism followed by the source-open inclusion and the given morphism. Postcompose with the specified map out of the target and reassociate.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_boundary_of_mem_support_chain: Induct on the stage. At zero the chosen ideal belongs to the boundary, providing a witness. At a successor the support-chain hypothesis sends the point into the preceding chosen support. The induction hypothesis puts its image in the preceding boundary support, so the successor boundary property puts the point in the support of some boundary ideal at the new stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_boundary_succ_of_map_mem_supp: The hypothesis places the point in the inverse image of the union of supports of the previous boundary. This inverse image is contained in the next boundary support by the transform rule, which retains the strict transforms and adds the exceptional ideal. Thus some listed ideal at the next stage has the point in its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasOrderCertificateMultOne_appendLowerDi: The final stage of the given prefix has finite-type smooth structural map, and its boundary is in strict normal-crossing position. The derived triple using that boundary is admissible, within the dimension bound and hence allowed by the downward-closed dimension condition. It is order-bounded and balanced. The chosen boundary index is within its boundary because the previous blowups add entries to the list. Apply the specified reduction at this index. Its shape provides a chain of divisors whose supports contain the centers, beginning with the pullback of the chosen boundary entry. In the special initial step the next divisor is a total transform, and in all other steps it is a strict transform. In each case its support maps into the preceding support. The chain therefore gives a boundary-memory certificate at each continuation stage after interpreting it as marked data. The append theorem identifies the appended reduction with this continuation after the prefix. Certificates pass to that append because they hold on both pieces and are invariant under stage isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasOrderCertificateMultOne_dataAt_of_cen: A point of the center support lies in the chosen support at that stage. The support-chain argument places it in the support of a listed boundary ideal. Thus the center support is contained in the boundary support of the stage data, which gives the boundary-memory certificate with mark one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isInvariantUnderIso_hasOrderCertificateM: Transporting the marked scheme with center along an isomorphism pulls back its ideal and center, takes the inverse image of its boundary support and composes its structural map with the isomorphism. The order certificate is preserved under exactly this transport, so the mark-one certificate holds for the transported data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundary_zero_of_eq_comap: The stage-zero boundary is the list of initial boundary ideals pulled back along the initial isomorphism. The given original ideal is in that list before pullback, so its pullback is a member of the stage-zero list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_coverMarkedBlowupData: Induct on the number of boundary entries separated on the cover. The zero-step separation has no centers. At a successor the previous sequence has its certificates by induction, and the boundary-index reduction extends them to the next append. This gives certificates throughout the full separation. The cover sequence is the full separation followed by the hypersurface continuation, whose certificates are assumed. Invariance under isomorphisms lets the append combine the two families. At the given stage the marked sequence's structural map, ideal, center and boundary locus are those of its stage data, so the stage certificate is the stated one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_eq_of_mult_eq_one: Replace the mark by one. At mark one the balanced tuning construction returns the original ideal, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.continuationOrderCertificate_of_mult_eq_:
The cover triple and the derived triple for its continuation both have mark one, since tuning preserves that mark. At the end of separation the transformed hypersurface still has maximal contact, and the tuning property carries this to the derived triple. The derived triple is admissible, within the dimension condition, order-bounded and balanced, and its boundary begins with the transformed hypersurface. The reduction at index zero supplies a chain of smooth divisors that contain the centers in their supports. The chain begins with the hypersurface pulled back to the initial stage and proceeds by strict transforms, except that the possible first special step uses a total transform. Therefore the strict transform of the hypersurface at the given stage has support contained in that of the chain divisor. Because the mark is one, maximal contact puts the stage ideal support inside that strict-transform support. Both the stage ideal and center thus have support in the smooth chain divisor.

The continuation marked for the original last-stage data has the same ideal as the derived sequence because tuning at mark one leaves the ideal unchanged. It has the same center and structural map as well. Its boundary support contains the derived sequence's other-boundary locus, because each entry after the distinguished hypersurface is the transform of a retained old entry or a newly exceptional ideal. If the shape gives an open center in the divisor at the initial special step, use the open case of the smooth-divisor certificate. At every other step the shape gives an auxiliary ideal with local agreement off the other-boundary locus and a lower principalization certificate. Enlarging that locus to the continuation boundary support preserves local agreement where required and transfers the principalization certificate by monotonicity. The smooth-divisor result now gives the order certificate, which transports to the original continuation data by the identified ideal, center and structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_eq_ideal_of_eq: Use the equalities of the starting ideals and marks. Through the given stage, the controlled transforms reconstructed from the underlying blowups are the ideals of the marked sequence. This gives the claimed stage identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_mem_of_eq_cons_of_ne_zero: The index is positive, so it is one more than the index of the corresponding entry in the tail. The bound on the original index puts the predecessor within the tail. The retrieved entry therefore belongs to the tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.get_zero_of_eq_cons: Replace the list by its description as the head followed by the tail. The zeroth entry is the head.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactHypersurface_congr: Identify the two structural maps, marked ideals, hypersurface ideals and marks by the given equalities. Local finite type is a property of the same map on both sides. The supplied maximal-contact condition now refers to the requested data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundarySupport_of_mem_support_of_me: The boundary list of the stage data is the given sequence boundary at that stage. The specified member and its support point witness membership in the union of the boundary supports.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr_morphism_ideal_ce: Substitute the equal structural morphisms, marked ideals and centers. The certificate then has the same data as the one supplied.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_coverMarkedBlowupData_o: At mark one the continuation certificate holds by the smooth-divisor argument. Supply it to the cover certificate theorem, which combines the boundary separation certificates with those for the continuation. Apply the resulting certificate at the given cover stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_one_of_isSmoothDivisor:
Use the smooth divisor on the whole ambient open in the descent form of a mark-one order certificate. Its pulled-back divisor stays smooth, and the two support containments persist under pullback. The closed-subscheme comparison for this open is an open immersion, and it commutes with the inclusions into the ambient schemes.

If the center support pulls back to an open of the divisor, use the certificate branch with no auxiliary ideal. The required openness on the restricted divisor follows by inverse image under the subscheme comparison. Otherwise take the given auxiliary ideal on the divisor and pull it back by that comparison. Stability under open immersions preserves nonvanishing on components and its principalization certificate. Away from the pulled-back boundary set, pull back the given neighborhoods where the auxiliary ideal agrees with the restriction of the original ideal. The commutative subscheme square carries this local equality to the restricted divisor and identifies the structural map, center ideal and boundary set of the pulled-back certificate. These are the conditions for descent with the auxiliary ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_congr_mult: Replace the original mark with its equal value. The given principalization certificate now has the requested mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ideal_subset_iteratedStrictTrans: The iterated strict transform remains a maximal-contact hypersurface through the stated stage. Its support therefore contains the stage marked order locus. At mark one this locus is the support of the ideal itself. The transforms computed on the marked and underlying blowup data agree, giving the stated inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_maxContact_ne_top: Choose the descended cover sequence of the trimmed triple. Its underlying sequence is the principalization sequence of the original triple. The strict pullback to the cover has nonunit centers by the cover specification. If a downstairs center were the unit ideal, its pullback would be unit, so every center downstairs is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverFaithfullyFlat: The good-cover property makes the cover map surjective. Its local open-immersion form makes it étale and hence flat. Together these are faithful flatness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverSequenceProperties_of_isBoundaryDiv: The predicate of being at most the reference dimension descends along dimension inequalities. Apply the cover sequence results with the given boundary reductions. They give nonunit centers, order certificates at mark one, and a strict descent of the cover sequence. The smooth-divisor comparison gives the required mark-one relation after replacing the boundary by its admissible singleton. Finally reduction along maximal contact empties the final tuned order locus. These five properties give the cover sequence specification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIter_comap_of_isPullback: The given pullback scheme is canonically isomorphic to the scheme obtained by field extension, with its projections identified. The iterated derivative ideal commutes with the canonical field extension by its base-change formula. Pull back this equality along the canonical isomorphism, using the smooth pullback formula for derivatives along that isomorphism. Composition of pullbacks gives the claimed identity for the given square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_comm_baseChange: For every field-extension pullback square and derivative index, apply the iterated derivative comparison for that square. This is the required base-change property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.descentProperties_of_isBoundaryDivisorRe:
Use the tuning equivalence for marked sequences and the local-isomorphism descent of order certificates. The two field-extension comparison theorems supply pullback and strict pullback. Stage comparison maps on the cover are local isomorphisms, and the stages are locally Noetherian, so the tuned marking descends. Restoring unit entries preserves marking, and the stage order theorem supplies the bound by the mark.

Smooth functoriality supplies the pullback clause. For a surjective smooth map it gives strict pullback because every downstairs center is nonunit. This is vacuous for the empty sequence and follows by descent from the cover otherwise. Flatness and surjectivity of the cover give its descent properties. The kernel subscheme comparison transfers admissibility and dimension along the divisor presentation, tuning at mark one fixes the ideal, and the established admissibility results handle trimming and the smooth singleton boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_boundary_filter: The stage boundary is the map of the original list by the iterated strict transform followed by the exceptional entries. Strict transform fixes the unit ideal. Apply the filtered-list identity to this map and use the same exceptional suffix for both lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_of_ne_top: The nonunit head passes the filter and is followed by the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_top: The filter discards the unit head and returns the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_map_filter_append: Induct on the original list before the appended tail. If the head passes the first test, both transformed lists contain its image before the last filter, which keeps or discards it on both sides together. If it fails the first test, it must be unit. Its image is also unit and is removed by the final filter on the side where it still appears. In both cases use the induction hypothesis for the tail, with the appended suffix unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_isAdmissible_dropTrivialBoundary: Removing unit entries leaves the same list of nontrivial entries, since a second filtering keeps all entries of the first result. The admissibility theorem for boundaries with the same nontrivial entries applies to the trimmed triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_isMarked_of_isMarked_dropTrivialB: For each admissible triple and blowup sequence marked for its trimmed boundary, apply the restoration theorem with its ideal and mark. This supplies the marking for the original boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_withBoundary_ker_of_isSmoot: A smooth divisor gives strict normal crossing position for its singleton boundary. The replacement triple retains the original scheme, structural map, ideal, and mark, so the other admissibility properties come from the original triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_withBoundary_of_sameNontriv: Replace the boundary of the already admissible triple by the other list. The lists have the same nontrivial entries, so the normal crossing condition and admissibility transfer to this replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_baseChange: The original balance condition bounds the required powers of each derivative ideal by the corresponding power of the original ideal. Field extension identifies the derivative ideals with their pullbacks, and pullback preserves powers and inclusions. The original inequalities therefore give the power bounds characterizing balance upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBaseChangeInherited: Field extension preserves admissibility and successor dimension, so the dimension predicate is unchanged. The order formula transfers the bound at each image point. The balance comparison transfers the derivative power bounds. Thus all four hypotheses are inherited.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_of_isMarked_dropTrivialBoundary: Restoring unit entries leaves exceptional divisibility, order along centers, and smoothness of centers unchanged. At each stage the two boundary lists have the same nontrivial entries, since strict transforms of unit entries are unit and both contain the same exceptional entries. Thus the strict normal crossing condition with the trimmed boundary transfers to the full boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactInvariantBalancedTuned_of_tu: For each marked ideal satisfying the geometric hypotheses, apply the balanced-tuning invariance result using the given tuning properties. This proves the required general condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxContactInvariant_balancedTunedSheaf: Use the multiplication criterion for maximal-contact invariance. The maximal-contact ideal is the appropriate iterated derivative ideal, and the balanced tuned ideal is the tuned ideal at the positive tuning exponent. The derivative product bound for that exponent is the required inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_maxContact_of_isBoundar: The given boundary reductions provide the cover sequence properties, and their position invariance gives the descent hypotheses together with those reductions. Apply the abstract maximal-contact order-reduction theorem with these properties and the given lower-dimensional reduction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_orderFamily_of_strictTr: For each dimension bound, the maximal-contact principalization gives the required order reduction by the boundary position invariance theorem. The canonical order family is defined by this same principalization with pullback invariance under isomorphisms. Their assignments agree on every triple, so the result applies to the canonical family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisorStableUnderSmoothPullback: A smooth divisor gives a singleton in strict normal crossing position. The smooth-pullback theorem for members of such a boundary makes the pulled-back singleton member a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_maxContact_bas:
The field extension is flat and preserves pointwise order. It therefore pulls back the marked order locus, and the upstairs mark stays unchanged by the boundary replacement. If the original locus is empty, both reductions have length zero and hence form a strict pullback. If it is nonempty, surjectivity makes the upstairs locus nonempty. Trim both triples and identify the upstairs trimmed triple with the extension of the downstairs trimmed triple.

The chosen cover of the extended triple and the extension of the original cover are admissible. Their schemes are Noetherian, giving quasi-compactness of their maps to the field spectrum and the common fiber product's relevant structural composite. The dimension of the extended original cover is bounded by that of the extended original scheme because field extension preserves dimension. The projection from the common fiber product is étale and gives the remaining dimension bound. With these geometric conditions and the established descent, tuning, and hypersurface comparisons, apply the field-extension theorem for maximal-contact reduction with a replaced boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markingDescends: The cover map is surjective and locally an isomorphism, and the induced stage comparisons are local isomorphisms between locally Noetherian stages. Descent of marking therefore marks the downstairs sequence for the balanced tuned ideal at the positive tuned mark. The original order bound and nonempty marked locus show that the original mark equals the maximum order. Equivalence of marked sequences under tuning now transfers the marking to the original ideal and mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactCoverProperties: The construction of cover properties requires the tuning properties, the dimension bound along blowups, and preservation of admissibility under smooth pullback. The established results supply these three inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactHypersurfaceSmoothPullback: Apply the maximal-contact pullback theorem that uses stability of smooth divisors. The smooth divisor theorem supplies that stability.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactHypersurfacesEtaleEquivalent: The étale equalization theorem produces a common étale neighborhood for the two maximal-contact hypersurfaces. On it their pullback ideals agree, which gives the required equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContact_baseChange_isPullbackBlowupSe: The field-extension theorem gives a strict pullback of the two reductions. If the upstairs order locus is empty, the field-extension projection's surjectivity and the order formula force the downstairs locus to be empty too. Both sequences then have length zero and satisfy the pullback relation. If the upstairs locus is nonempty, every center of the upstairs reduction is nonunit by the cover descent argument. Removing isomorphism steps therefore gives an isomorphic sequence. The pullback relation obtained from strict pullback after removal of those steps transports to the upstairs sequence itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContact_isPullback_of_smooth_of_order:
The ideal on the modified upstairs triple is the pullback of the original ideal, with the same mark. If the original order locus is empty, it pulls back to the empty locus, and both sequences have length zero. If only the upstairs locus is empty, its reduction has length zero and the empty-pullback-locus theorem gives the comparison with the downstairs sequence.

When both loci are nonempty, trim the two boundaries. Admissibility persists because the nontrivial boundary entries agree with the appropriate lists. Both chosen cover triples are admissible and Noetherian. The common fiber product is quasi-compact over the base, using the cover projections and Noetherianity. Its étale projection to the upstairs cover bounds its dimension by that of this cover, which in turn is at most the upstairs dimension. The smooth comparison theorem over the two covers now applies, using the established boundary-loop compatibility and descent properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_idem: Every entry retained by the first filter is nonunit, so the second filter retains each entry in its existing order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtBaseChangeEq: The field homomorphism into the characteristic-zero extension gives characteristic zero downstairs. Admissibility gives a smooth original structural map. The order formula for field extension then identifies the order at each upstairs point with the original order at its image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificateLocalToGlobal: Choose a local certificate and its two required properties at each point from the hypothesis. The localization theorem for order certificates combines this family into a certificate on the whole scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionHypotheses: Assemble the geometric properties needed for order reduction. Controlled transforms admit maximal-contact data, and centers project into the original order locus. Smooth pullback preserves balance and admissibility under the stated hypotheses, and étale maps give the required dimension bound. The stage theorem supplies local Noetherianity. The blowup-lift comparison gives equality on controlled transforms, smooth ideals are determined by their supports as required, and the étale equalization theorem compares maximal-contact choices. Finally the pullback criterion gives a strict pullback when all centers are nonempty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullback_fst_of_isStableUnderBaseChange: The first projection is the base change of the second morphism in the cospan. Apply stability under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullback_snd_of_isStableUnderBaseChange: The second projection is the base change of the first morphism in the cospan. Stability under base change transfers the property to this projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_eq_nontrivialPart: For a unit entry both filters discard it, and for a nonunit entry both keep it. Thus they give the same list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_removeUnitIdeals: Removing unit ideals gives the nontrivial part. Filtering that result again does nothing, so it has the same nontrivial part as the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.separateBoundary_pullback_of_smooth: Identify the smooth pullback triple with the pullback whose unit boundary entries have been removed. Admissibility, the dimension bound, maximal contact, and the strict normal crossing condition transfer to this presentation. The pullback theorem for hypersurface reduction with boundary deletion now gives the relation over the smooth map. The equality of triples identifies the resulting source sequence with the desired one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackTriple_eq_pullbackWithNont: Both constructions use the same pullback scheme, structural map, ideal, and mark. Their boundary filters agree because removing unit ideals gives the nontrivial part, so the triples are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheafProperties: The tuned-ideal construction satisfies the inclusion from a successor tuning index and the product bound for two indices. The criterion for the tuning properties applies to these two inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.validBaseChange: The field-extension admissibility theorem applies to the given admissible triple over the original field and the stated extension. Thus the resulting triple is admissible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.validPullbackAlongSmooth: For an admissible triple take a smooth pullback with the stated quasi-compact structural map and compatibility over the base. The admissibility theorem for smooth pullback gives all the conditions for the pulled-back triple.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_comap: Successive ideal pullbacks compose to pullback along the composite of their three maps, in the order from the final source to the original target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_of_comp_eq: Substitute the two descriptions as successive pullbacks of the original ideal. The final pullback on each side is then pullback of that ideal along the corresponding triple composite. Those composites agree by hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_assoc_eq_of_eq_comp: Reassociate the first two maps with the third and replace the inner composite by the given equal map. The assumed equality then gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_comp_eq_comp_comp: Replace the composite along the first path to the intermediate scheme by the given equal one. After reassociating, replace the remaining two maps by their stated equal composite. This gives the second path.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_structureMorphism_eq_of_comp_eq: Write both structural maps as the given maps to the intermediate scheme followed by its structural map. The assumed equality of the composites into the intermediate scheme then gives equality after composing with its structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverBaseChangeMap_condition: The structural map of the cover triple factors through the original scheme. Substitute this factorization into the commutativity identity for the field extension of the cover. Associativity gives the required identity for the two proposed projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_structureMorphism_eq: The structural morphism of the cover triple sends a point first to the original scheme by the cover map and then to the spectrum of the base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.decide_eq_true_iff_self: If the proposition holds, its decision is true. If it fails, its decision is false. These two cases give the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_withBoundary_baseCha: The field-extension projection is surjective, so a boundary ideal pulls back to the unit ideal exactly when it was already unit. Thus removing unit entries commutes with pulling back the boundary. The replacement boundary has the same nontrivial entries as the base-changed boundary, so trimming gives the same list in either case. The two triples share the other data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filter_eq_map_filter_of_nontrivialPart_e: Surjectivity implies that an ideal is nonunit exactly when its pullback is nonunit. The two filters therefore commute with entrywise pullback. Replace each nontrivial part in the assumed equality by its filter expression and use this commutation to obtain the claimed list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filter_map_comap: Induct on the original list. Both operations give the empty list in the base case. At the head, the two tests agree by hypothesis, so both keep the pulled-back head or both discard it. The induction hypothesis identifies their outputs on the tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection is a base change of the opposite flat map. Flatness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_withBoundary_singleton: Changing the boundary preserves all admissibility data that depend on the scheme, structural map, ideal, or mark. The new singleton satisfies strict normal crossings by the given condition, so the new triple is admissible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_congr_hom: Substitute the stated equalities of morphisms into the square. It is the given pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_coverBaseChangeMap: The defining map to the field extension of the original scheme has the two projections specified by the universal property. Paste the proposed square with the field-extension square of the original scheme. The outer rectangle is the field-extension pullback for the cover because its structural map factors through the original scheme. The lower square is a pullback, so cancellation of pullback squares gives the proposed square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_baseChange_of_:
Form the common fiber product of the chosen cover after field extension and the field extension of the original cover. Both projections are smooth, flat, and surjective because they come from the open covers by base change. The two triples agree after pullback to the common fiber product, and admissibility follows from smooth pullback with the given quasi-compactness. Use there the pullback of the chosen hypersurface from the cover after extension. It is of maximal contact and is in strict normal crossing position, and these properties transfer across the equality of triples.

Apply smooth-surjective functoriality of hypersurface reduction along both projections, using this same hypersurface upstairs. It gives a common strict pullback of the two cover reductions. Field-extension functoriality compares the reduction on the field extension of the original cover with the original cover reduction. The given descent relations compare each chosen cover reduction with its base sequence. The faithfully flat comparison of these paths now gives the strict pullback between the two base sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_baseChange_wit: Field extension preserves pointwise order, and replacing the boundary leaves the ideal and mark unchanged. This gives the order bound for the modified triple. If the original order locus is empty, the new one is empty too, so both reductions have length zero and satisfy strict pullback. Otherwise the new locus is nonempty because the field-extension projection is surjective and preserves order. For each triple, choose the marked descent of the cover reduction after removing unit boundary entries. The two descended sequences are the underlying sequences of the desired reductions. Trimming commutes with field extension for boundaries with the same nontrivial entries. Identify the trimmed upstairs triple with the field extension of the trimmed downstairs triple and apply the strict pullback theorem for the cover descents.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_coverTriple_ba: The original cover triple is admissible and has order bounded by its mark. After field extension, admissibility and the order bound persist, as do maximal contact and strict normal crossing position for the pulled-back hypersurface. The two cover dimensions lie within their respective reference dimensions. Apply field-extension compatibility of reduction along the hypersurface. The original reduction along it is the chosen cover sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_descend_of_flat_surject: Compose the given strict pullback relations along each path from the common cover. The two commutative squares identify one composite base map with the other followed by the original base change. Consequently the sequence on the common cover is a strict pullback of both the upstairs sequence and the base change of the downstairs sequence along the same flat surjection. Faithfully flat descent of sequence isomorphisms identifies those two sequences. Transport the canonical strict pullback relation along this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_eq_of_heq: Identify the triples and then the two comparison morphisms on their common scheme. The given condition for every descent witness now applies to the indicated witness and yields the strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_comap_comap: For each entry of the original list, the three successive pullbacks equal pullback along the composite. The lists of these entries therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_eq_map_comap_of_comp_eq: Express both lists as entrywise pullback of the original list along triple composites. The given equality of those composites identifies the resulting entries and the lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_congr: The field, scheme, and mark are common to the two triples. The indicated equalities identify the structural maps, ideals, and boundary lists, so all of their data agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_eq_filter: The nontrivial part keeps exactly entries for which the unit-ideal test fails. The proposed test is true for exactly these entries, so the two filters agree on the whole list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_decide_eq_true_iff_not: When the proposition holds, its decision is true and its negated decision is false. When it fails, its decision is false and its negated decision is true. Thus truth of the negated decision is equivalent to failure of the proposition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_baseChange_eq_empty: Any point in the order locus after field extension has order at least the old mark. The order identity gives the same bound at its image in the original scheme. That image would lie in the empty original order locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_coverBaseChangeFiber_eq: Compare the chosen cover of the extended triple with the field extension of the original cover on their common fiber product. Their projections to the extended original scheme agree by the fiber product identity, so the structural maps to the extension field's spectrum agree. The two maps from the fiber product to the original scheme also agree by the defining equations of the cover base-change map. Tuning commutes with field extension, so both ideals on the fiber product are pullbacks of the original tuned ideal along that same map. The boundaries are entrywise pullbacks of the original boundary along the same map. The field and mark are common to the two constructions, yielding equality of triples.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection is a base change of the given smooth morphism, hence is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_baseChange_fst: The map of spectra induced by the field homomorphism is surjective, since each spectrum has one point. The first projection of the field-extension square is its base change, which remains surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection is obtained by base change from the surjective map. Surjectivity of scheme morphisms is stable under base change.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_map_eq_of_comp_eq_id: The two maps are inverses, so each sends the maximal ideal into the other by the retraction argument. Extension of ideals along such a map cannot decrease the order, since it carries containment in a maximal-ideal power into the corresponding containment. Apply the inequality first to the forward map and then to the inverse on the extended ideal. Extending back gives the original ideal, so the two inequalities give equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_stalkMap_of_isBlowupAlongIdealShea: Restrict to the complement of the center support. The restricted center is the unit ideal, so the restricted blowup is an isomorphism. At the given point, the open immersions from the two complementary opens also induce stalk isomorphisms. The restriction square identifies the composite stalk map on one side with the composite on the other. Composing with the inverse of the source-open stalk map identifies the original blowup stalk map as a composite of isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_maximalIdeal_le_maximalIdeal_of_retr: An element of the maximal ideal in a local ring is a nonunit. If its image under the first map were a unit, applying the retraction would give a unit in the original ring. The retraction sends the image back to the original element, a contradiction. Thus the images of elements of the first maximal ideal lie in the second, and so does the ideal they generate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_preimage_of_isB: If the image point is on the center, it has sufficient original order by the hypothesis on the center. Otherwise the blowup induces a stalk isomorphism. The total-transform ideal is the product of the exceptional power and the transformed ideal, so its stalk lies in the transformed stalk. This makes its order at least the transformed order. The stalk isomorphism identifies its order with the original order at the image. Therefore any point of the transformed order locus maps into the original one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_of_isIso_stalkMap: The stalk of the pullback ideal is the extension of the original ideal stalk along the stalk map. That map is an isomorphism of local rings and its inverse identifies the maximal ideals and their powers. Consequently the extended stalk and original stalk have the same ideal order, which is the pointwise order of each ideal sheaf.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_ne_top_of_eq: Equal triples have equal boundary lists, so the nonunit property for every member transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coverTriple_boundary_ne_top: Each cover boundary entry is the pullback of an original boundary entry. Surjectivity reflects whether an ideal is unit, so every pulled-back entry is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_boundary_eq_removeUn: Both boundary constructions retain exactly those entries that are different from the unit ideal, in their original order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dropTrivialBoundary_eq_withBoundary_remo: The definition of the trimmed triple changes the boundary by filtering for nonunit entries. The filter comparison identifies this list with the output of removing unit ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filter_eq_removeUnitIdeals: Induct on the list. The empty result agrees. For a unit head the stated test is false, and both operations discard it. For a nonunit head it is true, and both retain it. Apply induction to the remaining list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_faithfullyFlat_covers: Base change the downstairs sequence along the original flat map. After removing isomorphism steps it is a pullback sequence. To identify it with the given upstairs sequence, compare them on the fiber product of the two covers. There the two pullbacks of the downstairs sequence are isomorphic by strict pullback uniqueness and commutativity of the fiber product. The assumed comparison identifies the other cover sequence with this one after removing isomorphism steps. Descend the isomorphism first through the faithfully flat projection from the fiber product and then through the faithfully flat upstairs cover. The resulting isomorphism compares the two original upstairs sequences after removing isomorphism steps. The given nonunit center condition on the upstairs cover implies the original upstairs centers are nonunit, so removing isomorphism steps preserves its sequence up to isomorphism. Transport the pullback relation to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_length_eq_zero_of_length_e: The criterion for a zero-length upstairs sequence requires every downstairs center to pull back to the unit ideal along a compatible lift. The downstairs sequence has length zero as well, so it has no centers and the condition is vacuous.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_coverMarkedSequence_of_: Identify the triples and the equal cover comparison maps in the strict pullback data. The given relation then has the required base map and source sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_map_comap: Consecutive pullback of an ideal equals pullback along the composite. Apply this identity to every entry of the list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_congr: The fields and schemes already agree. Substituting the equal structural maps, ideals, marks, and boundaries identifies the two triples.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactPrincipalization_isPullbackBlo:
Smooth pullback preserves the pointwise order bound. If the upstairs marked order locus is empty, the upstairs reduction has length zero. When the downstairs locus is also empty, both reductions are empty and satisfy the pullback relation. Otherwise the empty-pullback-locus property gives the relation with the zero-length sequence upstairs.

If the upstairs locus is nonempty, so is the downstairs locus because order loci pull back. Trim both boundaries and choose strict descents of their cover sequences. These are the underlying sequences of the two principalizations. The covers are faithfully flat, and the upstairs cover sequence has nonunit centers. On the common fiber product the two cover triples agree after smooth pullback and trimming, by commutation of tuning and boundary pullback. Both cover triples have the required tuned order bound. Over the common scheme the pulled-back cover reductions therefore agree up to isomorphism after removing isomorphism steps, by the comparison of hypersurfaces. Faithfully flat descent of this comparison gives the desired pullback of the two descended sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ne_top_of_mem_removeUnitIdeals: The filter retains only nonunit ideals. Hence every member of its output is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_coverTriple_le_mult: The good cover is admissible and has positive tuned mark. The tuning theorem bounds the order of the tuned original ideal by this mark because the original mark is the maximum. The cover map is smooth, so the order on the pulled-back ideal equals the order at the image point. The same bound holds on the cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderReductionHypotheses_of_eq: Equality of triples identifies the admissibility, order, dimension, and order-locus data. The supplied hypotheses on the equal triple therefore apply.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reduceAlongHypersurface_isomorphic_of_is: The identity of the underlying scheme is smooth, flat, and surjective, and pulling the triple back along it gives the same triple. Fix the first hypersurface upstairs. Smooth-surjective compatibility of reduction along hypersurfaces gives this same upstairs sequence as a strict pullback of each of the reductions attached to the two downstairs choices. Descent of sequence isomorphisms along the identity identifies the two downstairs sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_cons_of_ne_top: The nonunit head passes the filter and is followed by the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_cons_top: The first entry is the unit ideal and is discarded by the filter. The remaining result is the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_eq_of_sameNontrivialBou: The relation compares the lists obtained by dropping entries whose unit-ideal test is true. Removing unit ideals applies the equivalent test of being nonunit. Thus the relation gives equality of the two filtered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_map_comap_congr: The final removal of unit ideals gives the same result whether or not unit entries are removed before pullback. Remove them first on both sides and use equality of these initial filtered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.removeUnitIdeals_map_comap_removeUnitIde: Induct on the list. The empty list gives equality. If the head is unit, its pullback is unit too, so it is discarded whether removed before pullback or afterwards. If the head is nonunit, it passes the first filter and is retained in the final list precisely when its pullback is nonunit. The induction hypothesis identifies the outputs on the tails.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackTriple_coverTriple_eq:
On the common fiber product the two paths to the original scheme agree. This makes their structural maps agree because each factors through that scheme. Smooth pullback commutes with balanced tuning, and trimming or replacing unit boundary entries does not affect the underlying ideal or mark. Hence both ideals are pullbacks of the same original tuned ideal along the common path, and their marks agree.

For the boundaries, the modified upstairs list has the same nontrivial entries as the pulled-back original list. Replace it by that list after filtering. Removing unit ideals at intermediate stages gives the same final filtered list, since unit ideals stay unit under pullback. Both resulting boundaries are therefore obtained by pulling back the original list along the common path and then removing unit ideals. The two triples on the fiber product coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackTriple_eq_dropTrivialBound: The smooth pullback triple is the ordinary pullback with all unit boundary entries removed. This is precisely the result of trimming the ordinary pullback triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_pullback_fst_snd_and_surjective_f: The two maps defining the fiber product are smooth, one by composition. Its projections are smooth by base change. The first projection is the base change of the surjective cover map, so it is surjective too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_isomorphic_of_smoothPu:
Both chosen cover triples are admissible, and surjectivity preserves the nonunit property of their original boundary entries.
