Smooth pullback followed by trimming gives an admissible triple on the common scheme. The given identity identifies the two such triples there. The pulled-back cover hypersurfaces are of maximal contact and have strict normal crossing position by smooth pullback. Smooth compatibility of the boundary loop compares each cover sequence with reduction on this common triple using its respective hypersurface, as a pullback after omission of isomorphism steps.

The dimension-bound comparison allows the two reductions on the common triple to use the same reference dimension. Independence of the choice of maximal contact identifies those reductions up to isomorphism. For each given strict pullback witness, removing isomorphism steps yields a pullback sequence, which is isomorphic to its corresponding reduction by uniqueness. Compose these isomorphisms through the two reductions.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_comap_of_smooth: The structural morphism and its smooth pullback satisfy the stated local finite-type conditions. The smooth pullback formula for balanced tuning identifies the pulled-back tuned ideal with the tuning of the pulled-back ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedSheaf_congr: Identify the structural maps and the ideals. The mark is common, so the two tuning constructions have identical inputs. The local finite-type certificates do not change the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_comap_of_comp_eq: Two successive ideal pullbacks are pullback along the composite. Substitute the given equality of that composite with the direct map.
In the concatenated list, skip the entire prefix. The entry at that index is the head of the remaining list. This follows by removing one prefix head at a time, with the empty prefix as the base case.
Substitute the equalities of lists and indices. Both lookups then select the same entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_lastBoundary_comap_lastMap: The two final entries are the strict transforms of their respective starting entries. The surviving-count formula identifies the upstairs starting entry with the pullback of the chosen downstairs entry. The final strict-transform comparison therefore identifies the stated ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_lastBoundary_eq_iteratedStrictTr: The final boundary begins with the original list mapped by the final strict-transform operation. The index lies in that prefix, so its entry is the final strict transform of the original entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_and_boundary_comap_lastMap: The stages on both sides are Noetherian by admissibility, and the smooth base map is flat. The original upstairs ideal is the pullback of the downstairs ideal. Its boundary has the same nontrivial entries as the pulled-back list by construction. The final pullback comparison for marked sequences now gives equality of ideals and agreement of the nontrivial boundaries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_comap_lastMap: At stage zero the ideal transforms are pullbacks along their initial isomorphisms. The projection compatibility to the original schemes makes the upstairs stage-zero transform the pullback of the downstairs one along the comparison to stage zero. Both families then follow the strict-transform recurrence, and admissibility gives the required Noetherian stages. Apply the final strict-transform comparison for the pullback of sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_comap_lastMap_eq_top: The given final entry is the strict transform of the original entry. Its pullback to the final upstairs stage is the iterated strict transform of the pulled-back original entry. That entry is unit, and strict transforms of the unit ideal are unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_eq_append: The recorded final boundary equals the one computed from the underlying blowup data. The boundary concatenation formula writes it as the strict transforms of the original list followed by the boundary computed from an empty initial list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastMap_comp_projectionToBase: The final comparison and projections form a commutative pullback square. The projections of the underlying sequences agree with the marked projections, so its commutativity is the required identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastMap_comp_structureMorphism: Postcompose the identity for projections to the original schemes with the original structural morphism. Reassociate to express the result as equality of the two structural composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_boundary_le_length_lastBoundary: The computed final boundary has the original length plus one entry per blowup, and it agrees with the recorded final boundary. This gives the length inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedIdealWithBoundary_mk_congr: The equalities identify the two structural maps, ideals, marks, and boundary lists on the common scheme over the common field. Thus the triples coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_cons_of_ne_top: View the list as the singleton head concatenated with the tail. Filtering distributes over this concatenation and retains the nonunit head. The new tail is the filtered old tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_singleton_of_ne_top: The single entry is nonunit, so the filter retains it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_top_singleton: The singleton's only entry is the unit ideal, so filtering removes it and gives the empty list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_derivedTriple_eq: Both triples use the final upstairs scheme over the original field. Their structural maps agree by the final comparison, and their tuned ideals agree by the tuning formula for that map. The marks are both the tuning exponent of the original mark. The specified replacement boundary is the pulled-back supplemental list followed by the prescribed suffix of the final upstairs boundary, which is the boundary of the derived triple upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackWithNontrivialBoundary_boundary_: Split the original boundary into the prefix before the chosen entry, that entry, and the suffix after it. Pullback and filtering distribute over this decomposition. The chosen pullback is nonunit, so it remains immediately after the filtered prefix. The length of this prefix is the surviving count at the original index, giving the claimed entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_append: Filtering nontrivial entries distributes over concatenation. The matching filtered prefixes and suffixes thus give matching concatenated lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_append_top: Filtering the appended singleton of the unit ideal gives the empty list. The filtered part of the extended list is therefore the same as that of the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_cancel_left: Filter both concatenations. Filtering distributes over concatenation, and the two filtered prefixes agree by hypothesis. Cancel this common prefix to equate the filtered suffixes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_congr: Replace each list by the equal list for which the relation holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_cons: The two copies of the added entry have the same nontrivial part. Prepend this singleton relation to the given relation between the tails.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_lastBoundary_drop: The full final boundaries agree after pullback and removal of unit entries. Their prefixes corresponding to the full original boundary also agree in this sense, by the prefix comparison and the formula for the total surviving count. Decompose each boundary into this prefix and its suffix. Pullback distributes over concatenation, so cancellation of the matching filtered prefixes gives the relation for the suffixes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_lastBoundary_take: Induct on the original prefix length. At zero both prefixes are empty. At a successor, if the original entry pulls back to the unit ideal, the surviving count stays fixed and the final transform of that entry also pulls back to the unit ideal. Appending it preserves the relation. If the entry survives, the count increases by one, and the final transform comparison matches the two new entries. Apply preservation of the relation under appending these matching entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_nontrivialPart: Once all unit entries have been removed, every remaining entry is nonunit. Filtering again keeps them all in their existing order, so the full list and its filtered list have the same nontrivial entries.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_refl: Filtering the list to its nontrivial entries gives the same list on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_symm: The relation is equality of the lists of nontrivial entries. Reverse this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_take_succ_of_eq_t: The extended prefix is the old prefix with the next entry appended. After pullback the appended entry is unit. Removing it preserves the nontrivial boundary relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_take_succ_of_getE: Both successor prefixes append the indicated next entry. The two new entries agree after the downstairs one is pulled back. Their singleton lists have the same nontrivial part, so the relation persists after appending.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.survivingBoundaryCount_length_eq: Taking the full original length returns the entire boundary. Its entrywise pullback followed by deletion of unit ideals is exactly the boundary used in the pulled-back triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.survivingBoundaryCount_lt_length: The prefix through the chosen component has one more surviving entry than the prefix before it. Its surviving entries form an initial segment of the full filtered boundary because both pullback and filtering distribute over concatenation. The original count is therefore strictly below the full filtered length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.survivingBoundaryCount_succ_of_eq_top: The next prefix is the old prefix with one entry appended. After pullback the new entry is the unit ideal, so filtering removes it. The count is unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.survivingBoundaryCount_succ_of_ne_top: Taking one more entry appends the indexed component to the prefix. Its pullback is nonunit and survives filtering, so the filtered length increases by one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.survivingBoundaryCount_zero: The initial segment of length zero is empty. It remains empty under pullback and filtering, so its count is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedIdealAtLength_comap_lastMap: The final comparison is smooth. Its composite structural map is the final upstairs structural map and is therefore locally of finite type. Apply the smooth pullback formula for balanced tuning to the downstairs final ideal. The ordinary final ideal pulls back to the upstairs final ideal by the sequence comparison. The structural maps agree and the mark is preserved, so the resulting tuned ideal is the upstairs one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.length_boundary_: Field extension pulls back each entry of the boundary list once and in the same order. Entrywise pullback preserves the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_appendLowerDim: The final strict transforms of the two hypersurfaces agree by flat pullback of strict transforms, so the supplemental singleton upstairs is the pullback of the one downstairs. Maximal contact and the initial strict normal crossing conditions give strict normal crossing position for the transformed hypersurfaces together with the remaining boundary at the final stages. This makes both derived triples admissible. The hypersurface is the first entry in each derived boundary, so the reduction at index zero is defined. The given separation of the dropped boundary entries now allows field-extension compatibility for the appended reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackBlowupSeq_reduceAlongHyp: Boundary length is preserved by field extension, so on both sides separate the same number of original boundary entries. Compatibility of boundary separation gives a strict pullback relation between the resulting sequences, and the separation invariant gives disjointness for the boundary entries to be dropped. Reduction along the hypersurface appends the lower-dimensional reduction with the final transformed hypersurface as the supplemental boundary. The compatibility theorem for this append identifies the full sequences as a strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_comap: At stage zero both ideals are pullbacks of the original hypersurface, and initial compatibility equates the two composites. At a successor the comparison square is a pullback, the comparison at the prior stage is flat, and the centers agree by pullback. The local Noetherian hypotheses allow the flat base-change formula for strict transforms. Use the inductive identification of the prior ideals in that formula to compare the next transforms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_comap_eqToHom: Identify the equal indices, so the two iterated transforms are the same ideal on the same stage. The stage identification is the identity and its pullback fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_of_strictPullbackBlowupSeq: The underlying sequences have equal lengths by the strict pullback hypothesis. These lengths are the lengths of the corresponding marked sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_nil_append_boundary: Dropping zero entries and prepending the empty list gives the final boundary. Its length is the original length plus the number of blowups. The index is already within the original length, so it is in range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_strictPullbackBlowupSeq_appendL: The stage dimension bounds put the two derived triples within their reference dimensions. The dimension predicate descends to them. The downstairs derived triple is order bounded and balanced by tuning, and inheritance under field extension supplies admissibility, dimension, order, and balance for its field extension. The original admissible sequences give locally Noetherian stage schemes. With the supplemental boundaries related by pullback, the boundary and separation hypotheses now allow the field-extension theorem for appending the reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_strictPullbackBlowupSeq_separat: Induct on the number of entries processed. The initial sequences both have length zero and hence form a strict pullback. At a successor identify both sequences as the preceding ones with one lower-dimensional reduction appended. Their final structural maps are locally of finite type and the corresponding derived triples are admissible. The boundary index is valid on both sides because the original boundary lengths agree and the final boundaries contain at least that many entries. There are no dropped entries to separate. Apply field-extension compatibility for the append operation to the strict pullback from the induction hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_strictPullback_of_length_eq_zer: Both sequences consist only of their initial stages. Define their comparison by the upstairs initial isomorphism, the given base map, and the inverse downstairs initial isomorphism. It commutes with the initial identifications. The lengths agree, and there are no blowup or center conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictPullbackMapAt_zero_comp_isoObjZero: The initial compatibility of the strict pullback identifies the stage-zero comparison followed by the downstairs initial isomorphism with the upstairs initial isomorphism followed by the base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformAtLength_comap: Apply the stage comparison at the final upstairs index. The strict pullback gives equality of lengths, and the final map is the comparison at this index followed by the identification with the final downstairs stage. Pullback along that identification changes only the index used to describe the downstairs strict transform.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_dropTrivialBoundary_of_eq_nil: Dropping trivial boundary entries filters the boundary list. Filtering the empty list gives the empty list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_eq_range_subschemeι: The support of an ideal sheaf is the underlying closed set of its closed subscheme. The closed immersion has this underlying closed set as its image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_top_of_imageIdealSheaf_eq_top: The composite of the closed-subscheme inclusion with the given map has unit kernel, since this kernel is the image ideal. It therefore factors through the closed subscheme of the unit ideal in the target. This subscheme is empty, so the original closed subscheme is empty too. Its support is empty, which characterizes the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_of_mult_eq_one: At mark one the only derivative index below the mark is zero. The balance condition at that index is the inclusion of the original ideal into itself, so balance holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_subscheme_top: The unit ideal has empty support, which is the image of its closed subscheme. If the subscheme had a point, that image would contain its image point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforward_of_isSmoothDivisor:
The dimension decrease makes the lower-dimensional reduction applicable. If the ambient order locus is empty, the ambient reduction has length zero. At mark one this locus is the support, so the ambient ideal is the unit ideal. An ideal with unit image ideal is itself the unit ideal. The lower-dimensional reduction therefore also has length zero, and the given closed immersion compares the two zero-length sequences.

If the ambient order locus is nonempty, trim its boundary and use the cover comparison for a smooth divisor. Over the faithfully flat cover, the ambient reduction and the boundary divisor reduction for the single divisor have the same strict pullback. They are consequently isomorphic downstairs. Identify the smooth divisor with the closed subscheme of the kernel of its immersion, and transport the given ideal to that presentation. Admissibility and the dimension decrease persist, and composition of image ideals identifies its ambient image with the original ideal. The ambient triple with the single divisor is admissible and is balanced at mark one. Boundary divisor reduction therefore expresses its sequence as the pushforward of the lower-dimensional sequence on the kernel subscheme. Smooth surjective functoriality along the isomorphism of divisor presentations identifies the original lower-dimensional sequence as its strict pullback. Transport the pushforward through this isomorphism on the divisor and the ambient sequence isomorphism already obtained.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toSequenceOfBlowups_heq_of_eq: Identify the two triples, including their underlying schemes. The assignment applied to this common triple has a single underlying blowup sequence, which gives the required equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxContactHypersurface.comap_of_forall: At a point of the pulled-back hypersurface support take a chart as in the hypothesis. The image point lies in the original hypersurface support, so the original maximal-contact neighborhood gives inclusion of its hypersurface ideal in the maximal-contact ideal there. Shrink the upstairs chart to an affine open contained in the inverse image of that neighborhood. Its hypersurface ideal remains the coordinate ideal, and the pulled-back inclusion puts it inside the upstairs maximal-contact ideal by smooth compatibility. At a point off the pulled-back support, choose an affine neighborhood disjoint from it. The hypersurface ideal is unit there. The upstairs order locus is pulled back from the downstairs order locus, which lies within the downstairs hypersurface support, so this neighborhood also misses the upstairs order locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxContactHypersurface.comap_of_isSmoo: The assumed stability makes the pulled-back hypersurface a smooth divisor. At every point of its support, the coordinate theorem for smooth divisors gives an étale chart where its ideal is a single coordinate ideal. These charts meet the hypothesis of the maximal-contact pullback argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxContactHypersurface.isSmoothDivisor: At each point choose the neighborhood supplied by maximal contact. In the coordinate case the hypersurface is already a single coordinate divisor in an étale chart. In the unit case take an étale chart inside the neighborhood, where further restriction still gives the unit ideal. These local forms give a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactHypersurfaceSmoothPullback_of_: A maximal-contact hypersurface is a smooth divisor by its local coordinate description. Apply smooth-pullback stability of smooth divisors and the maximal-contact comparison to this hypersurface, at the given positive mark.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_eq_comap_restrictIde: Restriction is pullback along the open inclusion. Thus each side is pullback along one of the two composites in the commuting square, and those composites agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_le_of_restrictIdeal_: The source open lies in the inverse image of the target open, so the morphism restricts to a map between them. The restriction identity expresses both ideals as pullbacks along that map. Pullback preserves the given inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.balancedTunedIdeal_eq_balancedTunedSheaf: The cover's balanced tuned ideal is defined by the balanced tuning construction for the original field, structural map, ideal and mark. Substituting those data gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_le_and_pow_le_tunedSheaf: The positive mark can be written as n + 1. Take the n-th derivative iterate as the auxiliary ideal. It contains the original ideal. In the defining weighted products for the tuned ideal, choose exponent s at index n and zero at all other indices. The weight of index n is one, so the weighted sum is exactly s. This gives an admitted product for tuning, and the product is the s-th power of the auxiliary ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_coverTriple_of_validPullbac: Balanced tuning is nonzero on components, so the tuned triple is admissible by the admissibility result for tuning. The cover triple is its pullback along the smooth cover map. The cover's structural map is quasi-compact by the good-cover condition. The given preservation of admissibility under smooth pullback therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_coverMaxContactIdeal: At each point the good-cover normal-crossings result supplies an étale chart for the singleton ideal. If no coordinate is assigned to its only entry, the restriction is the unit ideal. If a coordinate is assigned, the restriction is the ideal of that coordinate. This local description is the criterion for a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactCoverProperties_of_tunedSheafP:
Use the one-step strict-transform theorem for maximal contact and the order-locus inclusion under blowup. The assumed dimension inequality gives the bound at every stage. The tuned ideal order bound gives existence of a good cover, and the normal-crossings lemma allows a hypersurface contained in the center to be included with the other divisors. The stage transform and order-bound theorems give stage admissibility and preservation of the mark bound.

For the cover itself, the disjoint union of the chosen opens has dimension at most the original scheme, and smooth pullback of the tuned triple makes the cover admissible. The cover ideal restricts to the local maximal-contact ideals. It therefore has maximal contact and, using the smooth-divisor criterion, satisfies strict normal-crossing position. Together with the assumed tuning properties these verify all the cover properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_balancedTunedIdeal: Choose the auxiliary derivative ideal containing the original ideal and whose power at the tuning exponent is contained in the balanced tuned ideal. The support of the balanced tuned ideal is contained in the support of that power. The latter lies in the auxiliary ideal's support, which in turn lies in the original support by ideal inclusion. Since the original ideal vanishes identically on no component, the balanced tuned ideal cannot vanish identically on a component either.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_balancedTunedIdeal_le_tunedMult: If the original order locus is empty, its balanced tuned ideal is the unit ideal and has order zero. Otherwise the pointwise original bound and nonempty locus give maximal order equal to the mark. The tuning theorem bounds the order of the tuned ideal by the chosen tuning exponent. The balanced tuned ideal uses that exponent and the tuned mark equals it, giving the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_range_pow_ite_eq_pow: Split the product at its final index n. All earlier indices are distinct from n and have exponent zero, giving unit factors. The factor at n has exponent s, so the whole product is that power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_pow_subset: At a point outside the original support, the ideal has unit stalk. Its power then also has unit stalk, so the point lies outside the support of the power. This proves the inclusion for every exponent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.validPullbackAlongSmooth_iff: Expand the named property. It asserts that an admissible marked triple remains admissible after the indicated smooth pullback, with quasi-compact structural map upstairs and the stated compatibility of structural maps. This is exactly the quantified condition.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.boundary_eq_com: At stage zero both lists come from the original boundary, and compatibility of the initial maps equates the entrywise pullbacks. At a successor, each list consists of the strict transforms of the preceding entries followed by the exceptional ideal. The comparison map on the preceding stages is flat. With the local Noetherian hypotheses, flat pullback commutes with the strict transform across the blowup square. Apply this to each entry using the inductive equality. The exceptional ideals also agree by pullback, giving equality of the entire lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.center_eq_comap: The center condition of a strict pullback gives the upstairs center as the pullback of the downstairs one at the step. The marked centers and comparison map are those of the underlying sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.exceptionalIdea: An exceptional ideal is the pullback of the center along the blowup. Substitute the pullback description of the upstairs center and combine the two consecutive pullbacks. Commutativity of the blowup square gives the other composite, whose pullback is the downstairs exceptional ideal pulled back to the upstairs stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.flat_strictPull: The marked comparison map is the stage map of the strict pullback of the underlying sequences. The flat stage-map theorem applies at the same index because passing to underlying sequences preserves length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.ideal_eq_comap_: Induct on the stage. At stage zero both ideals come from the initial ideal, and the stage-zero comparison identity equates the two pullbacks. At a successor, divisibility gives the downstairs controlled-transform identity. Pull it back along the next stage map. The exceptional ideal pulls back to the upstairs exceptional ideal, and pullback commutes with powers and products. By the inductive identity and commutativity of the step square, the other side is the total transform of the preceding upstairs ideal. The upstairs controlled-transform identity has that same total transform. Cancel the common exceptional power, which is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, to equate the next ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.isPullback_stri: Take the strict pullback square for the same index in the underlying sequences. The marked comparison maps and the two blowup maps are the same maps that appear there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.le_toSequenceOf: Passing from marked data to the underlying blowup sequence preserves its length. Substitute this equality into the given weak bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.length_eq_of_st: The strict pullback gives equality of lengths of the underlying sequences. Passing from either set of data to its underlying sequence preserves length, which gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.lt_toSequenceOf: The underlying blowup sequence has the same length as the marked data, so the given strict bound holds for that sequence as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.strictPullbackC: The successive comparison maps and the two blowup morphisms form a pullback square. Its commutativity gives equality of these composites.
The marked comparison is defined to be the corresponding comparison map of the underlying sequences, at the same stage.
The initial compatibility of the strict pullback says that the two composites to the original downstairs scheme agree. The marked comparison uses this same stage-zero map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedBlowupSequenceData.surjective_stri: The comparison map is the stage map of the underlying strict pullback. The original base map is flat and surjective, so the stage-map theorem gives surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_map: At stage zero the compatibility square has the two initial isomorphisms on opposite sides, so it is a pullback. The initial stage map is therefore a base change of the flat base map. At each successor the strict pullback square makes the next map a base change of the preceding flat map. Induct to the stated stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_snd_of_isPullback: The second projection is the base change of the given flat morphism. Flatness is stable under base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback: The comparison data supply equal lengths, the stage maps, their compatibility at stage zero, the pullback square at each blowup, and pullback of each center. These are precisely the conditions for a strict pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_zero_eq: The stage-zero compatibility identifies the stage comparison followed by the downstairs initial isomorphism with the upstairs initial isomorphism followed by the base map. Compose with the inverse downstairs isomorphism to solve for the stage comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_map: The pullback squares and the initial compatibility make every stage comparison a base change of the original morphism. The base-change theorem for flat surjections gives surjectivity at the chosen stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_mem_support_comp: The indicated point of the support is the image of the chosen point under the intermediate morphism. The assumed equality puts its image in the image of the base-change map, contradicting disjointness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_mem_support_comp_comp: Apply the disjointness condition to the support point obtained by the two intermediate maps. Its projection equals the given image of the base-change point, which the condition excludes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hom_apply_congr: Equal morphisms induce equal maps on points. Evaluate them at the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_eq: Replace the first point by the equal second point and apply the given support membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_pullback_appendLowerDimReductio: Write the distinguished final boundary component as the divisor under consideration. Its support misses the inverse image along the final comparison map because its pullback is the unit ideal. The final comparison square is a pullback, so any point of this support whose projection met the image of the original base-change map would lift to a point of its inverse image. Thus the projected support misses that image. The assigned reduction has centers supported on the successive transforms of the distinguished divisor. At stage zero this divisor is the pullback by the initial identification. At each step its new support lies over its preceding support, both for the exceptional initial total-transform case and for every strict transform. Hence each continuation center projects to the distinguished divisor's support. Once the continuation is appended, its centers therefore miss the image of the base-change map. The disjoint-center append theorem extends the pullback relation with the upstairs sequence kept fixed. The append formula identifies the appended sequence downstairs with the lower-dimensional reduction in the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_of_eq_top: The unit ideal has empty support. Thus no point can belong to this support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero_isoObjZero_inv_app: The projection at stage zero is the initial isomorphism. Applying it to the given point transported by the inverse returns the point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appendLowerDimReduction_eq_append: The finite-type and dimension conditions make the recursion choose the given boundary reduction on the derived triple. If the original final order locus is empty, the derived ideal is unit and the reduction has length zero. Such data are automatically marked, and both stage-zero loci are empty. If the locus is nonempty, the original mark is the final maximum order. The tuning theorem transfers markings and compares the order loci, and the disjointness hypothesis permits restoring the omitted boundary entries in place of the supplemental list. In both cases the continuation is marked for the final stage of the original sequence. The concatenation operation therefore appends it, with the established order-locus identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_append: Induct on the first list. The empty list contributes no entries. For a nonempty list the transformed head comes first by the single-entry formula, and the induction hypothesis decomposes the transformed tail followed by the remaining boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_cons: At stage zero every entry is pulled back along the initial isomorphism, so the transformed head precedes the pulled-back tail. At each step both descriptions transform the old entries and append the same exceptional ideal. The induction hypothesis therefore gives the formula at the next stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_eq_ideal: The controlled-transform comparison identifies the iterated transform with the specified marked ideal when the exceptional factors are cancellable. Local nonzerodivisor generators provide the required cancellation at every step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_eq: The two products are equal because both are the same total transform. The exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, as is its power. Cancel this common power from the two products.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.foldr_lcm_consecutive_ne_zero: The least common multiple of the empty list with initial value one is nonzero. In the successor case the first entry is the positive starting integer and the tail begins at its successor. The induction hypothesis makes the least common multiple of the tail nonzero, and the least common multiple of two nonzero natural numbers is nonzero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_top_pow: The unit ideal is the multiplicative identity for ideal sheaves. Every power of that identity is itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_derivedTriple: The ideal assigned to the derived triple is the tuned ideal of the final stage by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBalanced_derivedTriple: For an original mark at most one, the tuned mark is one and every ideal is balanced at that mark. At a larger mark, if the final order locus is empty, the tuned ideal is unit and the required power bounds hold because every ideal is contained in it. Otherwise the original mark is the final maximum order. The tuning exponent is one less than that mark times the least common multiple of the indices up to the mark. The derivative-power estimate at this exponent puts every required power inside the tuned ideal, which is the balance criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_excep: The exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back to the blowup. The blowup property makes this ideal locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_and_orderAtLeastLocus_eq_of_bal: Forget the markings of the tuned sequence and retain its underlying blowup data. The tuning theorem makes those data marked for the original ideal with the tuned boundary, and equates the two order loci at corresponding stages. Replace the first boundary segment by the given segment disjoint from the original order locus. The boundary replacement theorem preserves the marking. The tuned controlled transform is the recorded tuned ideal, so the locus identities take the required form.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_append_of_orderAtLeastLocus_dis: Divisibility, the center order bound, and smoothness of the centers do not depend on the choice of boundary. At each stage remove the strict transforms of the old prefix from the strict normal crossing condition. The replacement prefix has strict transforms disjoint from the current order locus by persistence of disjointness. Each center lies in that locus, so these transforms are disjoint from the center. They may therefore be prepended to the remaining boundary while preserving the strict normal crossing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_of_length_eq_zero: All marking conditions concern blowup steps. A sequence of length zero has no such steps, so the conditions hold vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderBoundedByMult_derivedTriple: If the final order locus is empty, the balanced tuned ideal is the unit ideal, of order zero everywhere. Otherwise the final order attains its upper bound, the original mark. The tuning theorem then bounds the order of the tuned ideal by the tuning exponent. Since the derived triple uses this ideal and exponent, both cases give its order bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_succ: The recurrence takes the strict transform of the preceding ideal along the current blowup with its center, giving the ideal at the successor stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedStrictTransform_zero: At stage zero the iterated transform is defined by pulling the ideal back along the initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_eq_zero_of_orderAtLeastLocus_eq_e: An empty final order locus makes the tuned ideal unit. Its mark is positive, so the derived marked order locus is empty as well. The derived triple is order bounded and balanced, and the given index lies in its boundary. The triviality clause for boundary divisor reduction gives length zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderEq_ideal_length_of_nonempty: The final stage has order at most the mark at every point. A point in its nonempty marked order locus has order at least the mark, hence equal to it. Thus the mark is the maximum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_tuningExponent: For a mark at most one the exponent is one by definition. For a mark at least two the exponent is the product of one less than the mark and the least common multiple from one through the mark. The first factor is positive, and the second is positive by the consecutive-list argument. Their product is at least one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso: An isomorphism identifies the local rings and their maximal ideals at corresponding points. It therefore preserves the order of the pulled-back ideal, so the threshold locus is the inverse image of the original locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_controlledTransform_di: At stage zero both sets are inverse images under the initial isomorphism, so the original disjointness persists. At a successor the marked center and controlled-transform identity give inclusion of the new order locus in the inverse image of the preceding order locus. The strict-transform support also lies in the inverse image of its preceding support. A point of both new sets would therefore give a point of both preceding sets, contradicting the induction hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_controlledTransform_eq: The only index in a sequence of length zero is zero. The original marked order locus is empty, and the positive-threshold locus of the unit ideal is empty. At stage zero each respective ideal is pulled back by an initial isomorphism, so both loci remain empty and are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_ideal_length_le: Apply preservation of the order bound along admissible marked sequences at the final index. The ideal there is the final ideal of the marked data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_derivedTriple: The derived triple is formed at the final stage, with structural morphism the projection to the original scheme followed by its structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_boundary_eq: At stage zero both lists pull back the original boundary along the initial isomorphism. At a successor they apply strict transform entrywise to the preceding list and append the same exceptional ideal. Induction gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedIdealAtLength_eq_balancedTunedSheaf: The tuned ideal at the endpoint is defined by balancing and tuning the final ideal with the original mark, relative to the final structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedMarkedBlowupSeq_eq_derivedTriple_se: Both sequence spaces use the final structural map, the tuned final ideal, the tuned mark, and the boundary formed by adding the supplemental entries to the truncated final list.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_mul_weakTransform: The weak transform here is the controlled transform with exponent one. Its defining product with the first power of the exceptional ideal equals the total transform. That first power is the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.existsMaxContactControlledTransforms_of_:
Start with the original maximal-contact ideal pulled back to stage zero. It equals the maximal-contact ideal of the stage-zero data because the initial isomorphism preserves derivatives. At each subsequent stage define the ideal by pulling back the preceding one and taking the quotient by the exceptional ideal.

Inductively the constructed ideal is contained in the stage maximal-contact ideal. Its support therefore contains the support of the latter, which is the marked order locus. The center lies in that locus, so the assumed support-to-ideal rule puts the constructed ideal inside the center ideal. Its pullback is contained in the exceptional ideal. Since the exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, multiplying it by the quotient recovers the total transform. This is the weak-transform identity, which identifies the successor ideal with the weak transform of the preceding one. The assumed maximal-contact transform bound puts that weak transform inside the new maximal-contact ideal, completing the induction. The initial value, product identities and center containments give the required system of controlled transforms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_pow_one_of_le: The first power of the center ideal is the center ideal itself. The given inclusion is therefore the required inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactIdeal_congr: Substitute the equal structural maps and ideals. The same maximal-contact construction with the same mark is then applied to identical data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToBase_comp: Induct on the stage. At zero the structural map is the initial isomorphism followed by the smooth structural map of the base. At a successor it is the previous structural map composed with the next blowup. The predecessor map is smooth by induction, and the center has strict normal crossings with its boundary. Smoothness of the resulting composite follows from the smoothness theorem for such blowups.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformMaxContactIdeal_succ: Within the sequence the recursion pulls the previous ideal back along the next blowup and takes its quotient by the exceptional ideal. If the successor index is beyond the sequence, the recursion uses the unit ideal. This is the displayed successor formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.weakTransform_le_maxContactIdeal: At the given stage the center has strict normal crossings and lies in the marked order locus, so the stage ideal lies in the mark-th power of the center. The assumed maximal-contact transform inequality applies to this blowup and the controlled-transform identity of the successor ideal. The structural morphism for this calculation is the one at the successor by composition of the projections. Pulling back the given inclusion into the old maximal-contact ideal shows that the total transform of the smaller ideal lies in the exceptional ideal times the new maximal-contact ideal. The total transform is also the exceptional ideal times the weak transform. Cancel the exceptional ideal from this inclusion, since it is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. This yields the required bound on the weak transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.weakTransform_unique: The first power of the exceptional ideal equals the ideal itself. The given product identity is consequently the controlled-transform identity for exponent one. Uniqueness of the controlled transform identifies the candidate with the weak transform.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsBoundaryDivisorReduction.isPullbackBlo: The smooth pullback clause allows a boundary with the same nontrivial part and a matching designated entry. Taking the actual pulled-back boundary makes both comparisons reflexive. The assumptions on both marked ideals then give the stated sequence pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsBoundaryDivisorReduction.isStrictPullb: Apply the strict field extension clause with the actual boundary of the extended datum. Its nontrivial boundary and designated entry agree with themselves, and the specified hypotheses give all the other requirements.

Use the strict smooth pullback clause for the given surjection. The actual pulled-back boundary agrees with itself after removing unit ideals and has the same designated entry. This gives the strict pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.isPullbackBlowupSequ: In the field base-change clause use the actual boundary of the extended datum, so its nontrivial boundary agrees by equality. Apply the clause using the given admissibility and dimension hypotheses.

Apply the smooth pullback clause of maximal-order reduction, taking the new boundary list to be the actual pulled-back boundary. Its nontrivial part equals itself, and the remaining admissibility and dimension assumptions are given.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.isStrictPullbackBlow: Apply the strict field base-change clause to the actual extended datum. Its boundary itself gives the comparison list and meets the requested agreement after removing unit ideals.

Use the strict smooth pullback clause with the given smooth surjection. Choose the pulled-back boundary itself as the comparison boundary, so the required agreement after deleting unit ideals is reflexive. The clause gives the strict comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.mono: Any dimension covered by the new predicate is covered by the original one. Apply this implication to the original input and, in each comparison involving another input, to the other input as well. All the original specification clauses then apply to the restricted predicate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.append: Filter both concatenations. Filtering distributes over concatenation, and each pair of filtered parts agrees by hypothesis. Hence the filtered concatenations agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.map: After mapping each list, discard all unit ideals. The filter identity allows the original unit ideals to be discarded before mapping as well. The original filtered lists agree by hypothesis, so applying the same map and final filter gives equal lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.refl: Deleting the unit ideals from the same list on both sides gives equal lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.symm: The condition is equality of the filtered lists. Reversing that equality gives symmetry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.trans: The first filtered list equals the second and the second equals the third. Composing these equalities gives the stated relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_baseField: The definition of field base change sets the new base to the extension field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_boundary: The base-changed boundary pulls each ideal in the old list back along the projection to the old ambient scheme, preserving the order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_ideal: The new ideal is pulled back along the first projection from the fiber product to the old ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_mult: Field extension retains the original marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_scheme: The ambient scheme over the new field is the fiber product of the old scheme with the new field spectrum over the old field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_structureMorphism: The structural morphism of the base-changed ambient is the second projection of the fiber product, to the new field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_of_forall_not: Each part of the maximal-order specification assumes that the dimension predicate holds at the input's index. The assumption rules this out at every index, so each part holds vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderBoundedByMult_iff: The order bound is the requirement that at every point the order of the ideal is at most the marking. The two sides give the same condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.kerSubschemeIso_hom_comp: The source of a closed immersion is isomorphic to its scheme-theoretic image, defined by the kernel ideal. The original map factors through that image. Composing the inverse of the factorization with the original map therefore recovers the image inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.kerSubschemeIso_inv_comp: The inverse isomorphism identifies the source with its kernel subscheme. Following it by the kernel subscheme's inclusion gives the original immersion by the image factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundaryLocus_iff: The boundary locus is the union of the supports of the boundary ideals at the stage. A point belongs to that union precisely when at least one boundary ideal has it in its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_otherBoundaryLocus_iff: The locus is a union over the valid boundary positions other than the excluded one. Membership in the union is equivalent to finding such a position whose boundary support contains the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_append: Filtering out the unit ideals from a concatenation keeps the surviving entries from the first list followed by those from the second. This is the concatenation of the two filtered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_map_nontrivialPart: A unit ideal that is deleted before applying the map would still be a unit ideal after mapping, and would be deleted by the final filter. Every other entry gives the same mapped value whether it is first filtered or immediately mapped. The final filter keeps that value exactly when it differs from the unit ideal. Induction down the list gives equality with order preserved.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_baseField: Pulling the marked ideal back along a morphism of schemes over the field retains its base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_boundary: Each boundary ideal is pulled back along the given morphism in its original position. This gives the boundary list of the new datum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_ideal: The ideal component of the pulled-back datum is the original ideal sheaf pulled back along the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_mult: The pullback changes the ideal and boundary by pullback and keeps the original marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_scheme: The pullback datum takes the supplied source scheme as its new ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_structureMorphism: The new marked ideal uses the structural morphism to the field specified for the source scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_iff: The condition is defined by deleting all unit ideals from the two lists and comparing the resulting ordered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_baseField: Changing the boundary alone leaves the base field unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_boundary: The boundary replacement assigns the supplied list as its boundary component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_dim: The dimension index depends only on the ambient scheme, which is retained in the boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_ideal: The underlying marked ideal sheaf is copied as part of boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_mult: The marking is copied unchanged when the boundary is replaced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_scheme: Changing the boundary retains the ambient scheme, on which the new list is defined.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_self: Replacing the boundary with its original list gives exactly the original data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_structureMorphism: The boundary replacement retains the structural morphism of the same ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_baseField: Replacing the ambient scheme, ideal and boundary keeps the base field of the existing marked datum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_boundary: The replacement uses the supplied boundary list on the new ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_ideal: The replacement explicitly sets the ideal sheaf to the supplied ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_mult: The replacement datum retains the marking of the old ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_scheme: The replacement datum takes the supplied scheme as its ambient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_structureMorphis: The new scheme is equipped with the structural morphism supplied in the replacement data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.of_two_le: The large-marking case of an order certificate applies as soon as the marking is at least two. The hypothesis gives this bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.of_two_le: A marking of at least two satisfies the large-marking case in the definition of a principalization certificate. That case supplies the required certificate directly.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_orderCertificate_of_subset:
Induct simultaneously on order and principalization certificates. Memory witnesses remain valid by transitivity of containment, and large markings use the same witnesses regardless of memory. In a principalization step that passes to an order certificate, enlarge the recorded containment and apply induction to that order certificate. For either localization case, the old and new memory sets remain nested after taking inverse images in each open.

In a descent step, a point outside the new memory also lies outside the old one, so keep the same local ideal conditions. On every chosen hypersurface the two pulled-back memory sets are nested, so induction gives the descended order certificates for the new memory. All defining cases are preserved, yielding the order certificate with enlarged memory.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_principalizationCertificate_of_su:
Use simultaneous induction on the principalization and order certificates. In the memory cases, compose the old containment with the enlargement of the memory set. Large-marking certificates have no memory condition. In the passage from principalization to order reduction, enlarge the required containment and apply induction to its order certificate. Localization uses that inverse images preserve containments, so the induction hypothesis applies on every chosen open.

For descent to a hypersurface, keep the opens, hypersurfaces and ideals. Any point outside the enlarged memory was outside the old memory, so the required local condition remains valid. The inverse image of the old memory under the hypersurface inclusion into the original scheme is contained in the inverse image of the new memory. Apply induction to each descended order certificate with those inverse images. This covers every constructor and gives the enlarged principalization certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_mono_of_subset: Use the order certificate induction result with the enlarged memory set and its given containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_mono_of_subs: Apply the simultaneous induction result for principalization certificates to the given certificate and the stated enlargement of its memory set.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasReducedCenters_markedBlowupSeq: At any actual stage, the marked sequence gives a center smooth over the field. Its structure map is the center inclusion followed by the stage's projection to the field. Apply the smooth-center ideal criterion to this center and the given ideal whose support contains it. The resulting ideal containment is precisely the required reduced-center condition at this stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isFunctorialPrincipalization_principaliz: The conversion to a principalization sequence preserves both the underlying blowups and the final ideal. Pushforward along the given closed immersions therefore follows from the assumed pushforward comparison for the marked sequences. Field base change and smooth pullback follow from the corresponding marked-sequence comparisons, including their strict forms for field extensions and smooth surjections. Finally the marked sequence resolves the order-one ideal, so its final ideal and hence the principalization's final ideal are the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_baseChange_isPullback: The original and field-extended data both define admissible marked triples of order one. Use the maximum of their dimension indices as a common bound, which leaves both outputs unchanged by coherence. The maximal-order specification at that bound provides compatibility with field base change. Its comparison is the stated pullback along the projection to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_baseChange_isStrictPullb: Form the two admissible order-one inputs over the original and extended fields. Both sequences can be computed at the maximum of their dimension indices by coherence of the reduction levels. At this common level the maximal-order reduction has the strict field base-change property, which gives the strict comparison of the two sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_lastIdeal_eq_top: At the ambient dimension index, the maximal-order specification resolves the admissible marked triple. Resolution at marking one means that the final ideal has empty locus of order at least one. That locus is the support of the final ideal. An ideal sheaf with empty support is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_smoothPullback_isPullbac: Form the admissible marked triples of order one on the original and new schemes, pulling back the ideal and boundary for the latter. Take the maximum of the two dimension indices. Coherence of the reduction levels lets both marked blowup sequences be computed at this one bound. At that bound the maximal-order rule satisfies its specification by dimension reduction. Apply its smooth pullback property to the two admissible triples to obtain the comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_smoothPullback_isStrictP: Use a common dimension bound equal to the maximum of the two dimension indices. The two admissible inputs of marking one give the same outputs at that bound as at their original levels by coherence. At the common level the maximal-order reduction specification gives strict pullback along a smooth surjection. Apply it to the given map and pulled-back input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_toSequenceOfBlowups_eq_o: The marked triple has the dimension index of its ambient scheme. Coherence of the successive reduction levels says that maximal-order reduction at any larger bound agrees with its value at that index. Apply the operation that forgets the markings to this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_baseField: The marked triple uses the supplied field as its base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_boundary: The construction uses the supplied ordered list as the boundary of the marked triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_dim: The dimension index of a marked triple is computed from its ambient scheme. Here that scheme is the original one, so their dimension indices agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_ideal: The ideal of the marked triple is the ideal supplied to its construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_isAdmissible: The field has characteristic zero and the structural map is smooth, locally of finite type and quasi-compact by hypothesis. The ideal is nonzero on components and the boundary has strict normal crossings by the remaining hypotheses. The marking equals one and is therefore positive. Thus every admissibility condition is satisfied.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_mult: The marked triple is defined with marking one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_pullbackAlong: Pullback replaces the ambient scheme and structure map by the specified ones, pulls back the ideal, and pulls back each boundary ideal in order. The field and the marking one are retained. These are precisely the data of the marked triple on the new scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_scheme: The marked triple is formed on the supplied ambient scheme, so its scheme is that input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_structureMorphism: Construction of the marked triple retains the supplied structural morphism to the field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalization_lastIdeal: The conversion from the marked sequence of order one to an ideal blowup sequence retains its ideals, including the final ideal. Hence the two final ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalization_toSequenceOfBlowups: The output of principalization is obtained by viewing the marked sequence of order one as an ideal blowup sequence using the reduced centers. This conversion retains the underlying sequence of blowups, so forgetting the additional data on either side gives the same sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sequence_eq_maxOrderReduction: The marked blowup sequence is defined by applying maximal-order reduction at the dimension index of the ambient scheme to its marked triple of order one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ker_le_ker_of_isReduced: If a power of an element belongs to the kernel, the same power of its image is zero. In a reduced target this forces the image itself to be zero. Thus the element belongs to the kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothSubschemeIdealIsRadical:
The smooth closed subscheme has local rings that are domains, so it is reduced and its rings of sections on opens are reduced. On each affine ambient open the defining ideal is the kernel of the restriction to the subscheme. The reduced-target kernel criterion makes each such ideal radical, so the defining ideal sheaf is radical.

The support of the smooth center is contained in the support of the given ideal. The order relation between supports and vanishing ideals then places the given ideal inside the vanishing ideal of the center's support. This vanishing ideal is the radical of the defining ideal, which equals the defining ideal by the preceding argument.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_eq_transitionMap: A successor transition is defined using the order arrow from its stage to the next natural number in the opposite indexing category.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_blowupMorphism: For every index strictly below the length, the data of the sequence identify the successor transition as the blowup along the center ideal of that index. Apply this property at the given index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastStructMap_eq_projectionToBase: The last structural map is defined as the projection to the base at the index equal to the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_def: The projection to the base is defined by taking the transition to stage zero and then applying the chosen isomorphism from stage zero to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_succ: Factor the transition from the successor stage to stage zero through its preceding stage. Composing with the initial isomorphism gives the successor transition followed by the preceding projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: At stage zero the transition to zero is the identity. Composing it with the chosen initial isomorphism gives that isomorphism itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_fst: The pulled-back transition is the map furnished by the pullback universal property. Its first prescribed projection is the first projection from the later pullback, with an identity on the new base. Removing that identity gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_snd: The pullback universal property prescribes the second projection of the lifted map as projection from the later pullback followed by the original transition on the tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_def: The tower is indexed by the opposite of the ordered set of stages. The transition from the later stage to the earlier stage is, by definition, the image under the tower functor of the opposite of the indicated order arrow.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_self: The order arrow from a stage to itself is the identity, and its opposite is also the identity. The tower functor preserves identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_trans: The composite of the order arrows from the first stage to the intermediate stage and from there to the last stage is the order arrow for the transitive inequality. Take opposites, which reverse the order of composition, and apply functoriality of the tower.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.length_eq: Equal lengths are the first condition in the definition of a strict pullback of blowup sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.of_length_zero: The sequence lengths agree because both are zero. The only stage to compare is stage zero. Use its isomorphism to the source base, apply the given base morphism, and then use the inverse initial isomorphism on the target side. The required equality at stage zero follows by cancellation. There are no successive squares or centers to compare.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.isomorphic_refl: The lengths are equal. Choose the identity isomorphism at every stage. These preserve the initial structural map, commute with all successor transitions, and pull every center back to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comp: The image ideal is the direct image operation on ideal sheaves that takes the scheme-theoretic image of the corresponding closed subscheme. This operation is functorial in the morphism. Applying it to the composite gives the image of the intermediate image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_ker: By definition the image ideal is the kernel of the map of schemes from the given closed subscheme to the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_imageIdealSheaf: Both ideals are defined as the kernel ideal sheaf of the closed subscheme inclusion followed by the morphism to the target.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: Take the generic point of the component and an affine neighborhood where the ideal is generated by a non-zero-divisor. If the whole component were contained in the support, its generic point’s prime ideal would contain that generator. This prime is minimal. Indeed, a smaller prime would give a point specializing to the generic point, and the closure of that point would be irreducible and contain the component. Maximality would identify those closures, forcing equality of the two primes. A non-zero-divisor belongs to no minimal prime, giving the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closure_singleton_iff_fromSpec: Membership in the closure of a singleton is the specialization relation from that singleton’s point. The canonical map from the affine spectrum is an open embedding and therefore preserves and reflects specialization. The closure condition is consequently equivalent on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_primeIdealOf_of_mem_support: On the affine open, support membership means the point lies in the zero locus of the section ideal. In particular, the point is outside the basic open of the given section. The corresponding prime ideal therefore contains that section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_primeIdealOf_of_notMem_basicOpen: In the spectrum of the affine open, the inverse image of the basic open is the basic open of the same section. If the corresponding prime did not contain the section, it would lie in this basic open, and its image would be the original point in the given basic open. This contradicts the hypothesis.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_comp: The restriction of the composite to the target open factors as the restriction of the first morphism to the inverse image open followed by the restriction of the second morphism. Both factors are isomorphisms, so their composite is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_lastStructMap_of_centersL: The last structural map is the projection at the final stage. Apply the stagewise isomorphism result there to the given disjoint open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_lastStructMap_smoothLocus: The smooth locus is disjoint from its complement. All centers lie over that complement by hypothesis, so the last structural map restricts to an isomorphism over the smooth locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_projectionToBase_of_cente: Induct on the stage. Initially projection to the base is the given isomorphism, whose restriction remains an isomorphism. At a successor, the center misses the inverse image of the chosen open because all center points project into the prescribed disjoint set. Hence the restricted center ideal is the unit ideal and the restricted blowup is an isomorphism. Compose this with the preceding restricted projection, which is an isomorphism by induction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedPrincipalizationAmbientIsNoether: Construct the affine-space principalization data using the specified embedding, empty boundary, and smooth ambient structure. The ambient-stage Noetherianity result applies to these data at every stage within the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientLevel: The base ambient scheme is finite-dimensional affine space over a field. Its polynomial coordinate ring is Noetherian, hence so is its spectrum. The initial ambient stage is isomorphic to that scheme. Each successor is a blowup of a Noetherian previous stage and is Noetherian by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: A blowup over the Noetherian target is proper, hence quasi-compact and locally of finite type. These two properties over a Noetherian base give a Noetherian source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_iso: The inverse isomorphism is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Apply the Noetherianity result to it with the given Noetherian scheme as target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType: A morphism locally of finite type over a Noetherian scheme has a locally Noetherian source. Its quasi-compactness makes the source quasi-compact because the target is quasi-compact. These two properties make the source Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: Induct on the stage within the length of the sequence. Stage zero is isomorphic to the Noetherian base. At each successor the transition is a blowup of the previous Noetherian stage, so its source is Noetherian as well.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_lt_nextNontrivialIndex: If the earlier index had a nonunit center, it would be an admissible result for the search. Minimality would then bound the search result by that index, contradicting the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_lt_nontrivialIndex_zero: The first search starts at zero, and the given index precedes its least admissible result. Therefore its center is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_nontrivialIndex_lt: The next search starts just after the preceding retained index. The index in question lies within that search range and before the result. If its center were nonunit the search would have stopped there or earlier, so its center is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nextNontrivialIndex_ne_top_or_len: The index selected by the search meets its defining stopping condition. Its center is nonunit or the index is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nontrivialIndex_ne_top: The indexed search result has a nonunit center or reaches the original length. Since this is a position strictly within the shortened sequence, the retained value is below the original length. Thus the center is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nontrivialIndex_ne_top_or_length_: Both the initial retained index and every successor retained index are results of the same search. In each case the result satisfies the stopping condition of having a nonunit center or reaching the sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_le_center_ne_top_or_length_le: Choose the larger of the starting index and the sequence length. It is at least the starting index and satisfies the stopping condition because it is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_length_le_nontrivialIndex: Use the sequence length as the enumeration index. The retained index function has value at least its argument, so the result is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_towerWithoutIsoB: The shortened transition factors through the stage immediately after the original retained blowup. The map back from the next retained stage to that intermediate stage is an isomorphism, since all intervening centers are unit ideals. The other factor is the original blowup along the retained center. Precomposing a blowup with an isomorphism of its source leaves it a blowup along the same ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_transitionMap_nontrivialIndex_succ: Between the stage immediately after the retained blowup and the next retained stage, all omitted centers are unit ideals. The next retained stage is at most the original length. The transition across this interval is therefore an isomorphism.
