Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_comap_ker_of_isPullback_closedImm: Identify the given pullback with the canonical pullback of the closed immersion. The ideal of the resulting closed subscheme is the pullback of the original defining ideal. The identification is an isomorphism on the source, which preserves the kernel ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_hom: The forward affine-space isomorphism uses the inverse bijection on coordinate indices, so the pulled-back coordinate is the original coordinate at that inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_comp_eq_appTop: A coordinate pulled back along the composite is pulled back first to the intermediate scheme and then to the source, by functoriality of sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_affineSpaceInl_subset_range_opensP: A point of the open maps by the zero-coordinate inclusion to a point whose first projection is its original image in the open. The new point is therefore in the inverse image open and lies in the range of its inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.uliftFinSumEquiv_inl: The indexing bijection places the first block at the beginning of the combined list. The index in this block retains its original position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.uliftFinSumEquiv_inr: The indexing bijection places the second block after the whole first block. Its index in the combined list is therefore shifted by the length of the first block.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_restrict: The chosen zero section is a section of the restricted first projection, so their composite is the identity of the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_restrict_assoc: The restricted projection after the zero section is the identity. Following that composite by the given map therefore gives the map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_ι: The zero section over the open is the chosen factorization of the original zero-coordinate inclusion through the inverse image open. Its composite with that open inclusion is therefore the original inclusion restricted to the given open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_ι_assoc: First compose the restricted zero section with the inverse image open inclusion, which gives the original zero-coordinate inclusion restricted to the open. Then compose both equal maps with the given morphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_basicOpenEmbedding_lastCoordinate: The immersion assigns the inverse of the pulled-back defining function to the last coordinate. Thus the product of that coordinate and the defining function pulls back to one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_projLeft_coord: Pullback along a composite is successive pullback in reverse order. The first projection pulls the specified coordinate back to the corresponding first-block coordinate of the product, which is then pulled back along the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_globalSectionLift: The chosen lift is a preimage under the map on sections of the closed immersion. Applying that map returns the original section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_surjective_of_isAffine: A closed immersion into an affine scheme is induced by a quotient of the ambient section ring, so its map on global sections is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.basicOpenEmbedding_comp_affineSpaceIndex: The structure map of the product factors through the first projection. After this projection the constructed embedding is the original embedding on the basic open. The latter is over the given structural map, yielding the asserted composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.basicOpenToPullbackBasicOpen_comp_projLe: The chosen immersion was constructed with original coordinates in its first block. After the open inclusion and the first projection it is the original embedding restricted to the source basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_appTop_eq_of_isClosedImmersion: The map on global sections of the closed immersion is surjective because its target is affine. Thus the given section has a preimage in the ambient section ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_ι_eq_replaceLastCoord: Membership in the pulled-back basic open depends only on the first projection, and coordinate replacement preserves that projection. The replacement map thus lands in the open. The open immersion universal property gives the factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosedImmersion_basicOpen_pullb: Lift the function defining the source basic open to the ambient affine space. Its pullback along the first projection and then the padded embedding is the original function, since first projection undoes the padding. Thus the inverse image of the ambient pulled-back basic open is the source basic open. Apply the preceding closed immersion construction to this open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosedImmersion_pullbackBasicOp: First embed by adding a zero last coordinate, then restrict the closed immersion to the inverse image of the pulled-back basic open. On that open add the inverse of the pulled-back defining section to the last coordinate. This translation is an isomorphism, so the composite is still a closed immersion. Projection to the first block undoes the zero-coordinate inclusion and is unchanged by translation. The last coordinate starts at zero and becomes the inverse of the defining section. Its product with that section is one on the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_replaceLastCoord: Use the affine-space coordinate construction over the structural map of the open. Take its first-block entries from the open inclusion and use the given section for the last entry. This gives the prescribed pullbacks and structural map. After projecting to the first block, the resulting map and the projected open inclusion agree over the field and on every first-block coordinate, so the projections agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_isUnit_map_zero: A ring map sends zero to zero. In a nontrivial ring zero is not a unit, contradicting the assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_basicOpenEmbedding: The ambient defining section pulls back along the padded original embedding to the source defining section, so the domain is the inverse image of the required ambient open. The constructed immersion has the original first projection and satisfies the inverse-coordinate equation. The codimension result for that construction therefore gives the original codimension plus one. Reindexing the coordinate blocks by an isomorphism over the field preserves the codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_comp_opens_ι: At a point of the closed immersion choose a smooth chart inside the open ambient subscheme. Its composite open inclusion into the larger ambient scheme identifies the chart with its open image. Transfer the smooth coordinate map through this isomorphism, preserving the structural map. The ideal of the larger closed immersion restricts on the ambient open to the original ideal. The transferred coordinates therefore pull back to the same restricted ideal and give the same codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_comp_pullbackBasicOp:
Inside the pulled-back basic open, compare the given immersion with the original immersion padded by a zero and then translated by the inverse defining section. Their first projections coincide by hypothesis, hence their first coordinates and structure maps agree. The product relation determines the last coordinate of the given immersion as the inverse of the pulled-back defining section, which is exactly the last coordinate of the translated immersion. Equality of coordinates identifies the two maps, since the open inclusion is a monomorphism.

Adding a zero coordinate increases the original codimension by one. Restricting to the pulled-back basic open preserves that codimension, and the translation is an isomorphism over the field, so it preserves it as well. The codimension of the closed immersion into the whole ambient space is then the same as in the open by the preceding open-inclusion result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_basicOpenEmbedding: The map is a closed immersion into the pulled-back basic open followed by an open immersion, so it is a preimmersion. Its image is closed within that open. On its image the last coordinate times the lifted function equals one, so the image lies in the closed zero locus of their product minus one. Conversely, any point of that zero locus has the lifted function invertible in its local ring. Indeed the product minus one is a nonunit there, so the lifted function is a unit by the local-ring criterion. Thus the whole zero locus lies in the pulled-back basic open. A subset closed in that open and contained in this ambient closed locus is closed in the whole ambient space. A preimmersion with closed image is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_basicOpenToPullbackBas: The selected map was chosen from the construction of a closed immersion into the pulled-back basic open. It therefore has the required closed immersion property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_image_of_isInducing: Since the topology on the source is induced, its closed subset is the inverse image of a closed subset of the target. Its image is therefore the intersection of this closed subset with the range of the map. The given image lies in the second closed subset, and that subset lies in the range. Thus intersecting the first closed subset with the second gives exactly the image, proving it is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_shiftLastCoord_lastCoordinate_add_: Use subtraction of the inverse unit from the last coordinate as the inverse to addition of the inverse unit. Both transformations fix that inverse unit because it comes from the first projection. Either composite restores the last coordinate by cancellation and fixes the structural map and first block, so both composites are identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_shiftLastCoord_shiftLastCoordSecti: This section is the last coordinate plus the inverse unit, so the established inverse translation gives an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_appTop_ι_basicOpen: On the basic open the defining section pulls back to a section whose own basic open is the whole scheme. Its germ is therefore a unit at every point. A section is a unit if it is a unit in every stalk, so the restricted section is invertible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_appTop_ι_pullbackAlongProjection: The open is the basic open of the section pulled back along the projection. Restricting that defining section to its basic open makes it a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_map_of_not_isUnit_map_mul_sub_one: In a local ring either the product of the two images or one minus that product is a unit. The latter would make its negative a unit, contrary to the hypothesis. Hence the product is a unit, and so its second factor is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_appTop_comp_affineSpaceIn: The zero-coordinate inclusion pulls the last coordinate back to zero. Further pullback along the given map preserves zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_eq: The additional factor is an affine line. The last coordinate is defined as the coordinate of its unique index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_eq_coord: The affine-line index set has only one element. The specified index is therefore the defining index of the last coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_pullbackBasicOpen_iff: The basic open of a pulled-back section is the inverse image of the original basic open. A point belongs to it exactly when its projection belongs to the original open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlongProjection_eq: This section is defined by pulling the given section back along the first projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_replaceLastCoord_inl: The replacement map keeps the original pullbacks of every first-block coordinate. The specified first-block coordinate has exactly the pullback given by the open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_appTop_lastCoordinate: The last entry of the defining coordinate vector is the specified section. The section map sends the last coordinate to that entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_appTop_pullbackAlongPro: The section comes from the first projection, and the replacement map has the same first projection as the open inclusion. Functoriality of pullback therefore gives equal values on this section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_affineSpaceIndexed: The chosen replacement map was constructed over the same structural map as the open inclusion. Composing with the affine-space structure map therefore gives that structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_projLeft: The first projection is determined by its structural map and the first-block coordinates. The replacement map preserves all of these, so its first projection agrees with that of the open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_projLeft_assoc: First compose the replacement map with the first projection. This gives the projected open inclusion. Composing this equality with the given map gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoordSection_eq: The section used for translation is defined as the restriction of the last coordinate plus the inverse of the distinguished unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_appTop_unitOnPullbackBasi: Pullback fixes the underlying unit and preserves the product of the unit with its inverse. Thus the image of its inverse is again an inverse of the same unit, which is unique.

The unit is the restriction to the open of the section pulled back from the first projection. Pulling it back through the map into the open can be computed using coordinate replacement in the ambient space. That replacement fixes the projected section, so the unit's underlying section is fixed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_shiftLastCoord: It suffices to compare the composite with the identity after the monomorphic open inclusion. Both replacements preserve the structure map and all first-block coordinates. The last coordinate of the composite pulls back to the second replacement section pulled back by the first map, which is the original last coordinate by hypothesis. These data determine the map into affine space, giving the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_ι: The map into the open is chosen as the lift of the coordinate replacement through the open immersion. Its composite with that immersion is the replacement map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_ι_assoc: Compose the lift identity with the given morphism after the open inclusion. Associativity gives the displayed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.unitOnPullbackBasicOpen_val: The chosen unit is the one supplied by invertibility of the restricted section. Its underlying section is that restricted section.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_map_center_eq_center_of_isPullback: Use the overlap isomorphism to write the second overlap pullback on the first overlap object. Its compatibility with the overlap base maps allows pasting with the self-pullback square of the cover. The stage comparison square is a pullback, and the comparison maps agree on the overlap by hypothesis. Cancelling the stage square gives a self-pullback square for the stage comparison map. The center pulls back to the same ideal along the two projections of this square by the center compatibility. Flat ideal descent now shows that the pullback of its image along the stage comparison is exactly the original center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_blowup_proj_map_center: The original stage transition blows up the original center, which is the pullback of the image center by hypothesis. The canonical blowup of the image center pulls back along the flat comparison map to a blowup of that same original center. By the universal property, the two blowups are isomorphic over the stage. The comparison map furnished by this identification has the stated commuting equation and pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection in the pullback is obtained by base change of the given flat morphism. Flatness is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_iso_hom_comp: Precompose both projections with the given isomorphism of their source. This identifies the new square with the original pullback square, so it still satisfies the same universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_toBlowupOfMapCenter: The comparison map was chosen to exhibit the original blowup as the pullback of the image-center blowup along the stage comparison. The asserted pullback square is that property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_toBlowupOfMapCenter_projectio: Paste the pullback square comparing the blowups with the earlier pullback square comparing their bases. The resulting maps to the original and new bases are the successor projections, because each transition followed by the preceding projection equals the successor projection. Hence the pasted square is the asserted one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupOfMapCenter_cocycle: Compare the two overlap maps to the blowup of the descended center. Their composites with its projection coincide, since the overlap comparisons commute with the successor transitions and the preceding comparisons agree as maps to the descended stage. The descended center becomes locally generated by a non-zero-divisor on the blowup. It remains so after pulling back through the flat comparison to the local successor and then through the flat overlap projection. The uniqueness part of the blowup universal property therefore makes the two maps to the descended blowup equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupOfMapCenter_comp_proj: The comparison was chosen with a commuting square over the original stage. Its composite with the descended blowup projection is the original blowup transition followed by the stage comparison.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_projectionToBase_eq_fst: At stage zero the base-changed initial isomorphism is the first pullback projection. At a successor, the projection to the new base factors through the previous stage. By induction the preceding projection is the first pullback projection, and the pullback transition preserves that projection. This gives the formula at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups: Construct the descended sequence recursively from the given overlap data. It has the same length as the local sequence. At zero the descended object is the original base and the comparison is the local initial projection followed by the cover. At each successor the recursive blowup construction gives a pullback square with the local successor and identifies the local center with the pullback of the descended center. The tower uses exactly these successor maps. These facts are the required strict pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullback_of_isomorphic_ba: The two sequences over the self-overlap have the same stage objects as the two pullbacks used in the descent datum. The sequence isomorphism identifies their centers and commutes with all successor maps. It also commutes with projections to the overlap base, since it commutes at stage zero and with the transitions. Those projections are the first pullback projections. Thus the isomorphisms and their equations give the descent datum, from which the descended blowup sequence exists.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTowerObjZeroIso_hom: The initial isomorphism of the base-changed tower is the isomorphism given by the first projection from the pullback at stage zero. Its forward map is that projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTower_map: The base-changed tower assigns the induced pullback transition to the opposite of the order arrow between the two stages. This is the stated map by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTower_obj: The base-changed tower is defined at each stage by pulling the original projection to the base back along the given base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_blowupMorphism: For the successor arrow the base-changed tower uses the induced pullback transition between the two consecutive stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_center: The new center is defined by pulling the original center back along the second projection to the original stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_isoObjZero_hom: The initial isomorphism is the first projection from the base-changed stage zero, which is a pullback of the original initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_length: The base-changed sequence is assigned the original length when it is constructed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_schemeAt: The scheme at this stage is the corresponding object of the base-changed tower, which is the pullback of the original projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_baseChangeTower_: The original successor map is the blowup of the original center. Its pulled-back successor square is a pullback, and the projection to the original earlier stage is flat as a base change of the given flat map. Flat base change of blowups gives the claim for the pulled-back center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullback_fst_projectionToBase_zero: The original projection at stage zero is an isomorphism. Construct an inverse to the first projection by lifting the identity on the new base and the new base map followed by the inverse initial projection. The pulled-back square commutes, so the lift exists. Its composite with the first projection is the identity, and the other composite is the identity because both its pullback projections agree with those of the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_pullbackTransitionMap: The pullbacks at both stages are formed over the same new base. The square formed by the pulled-back transition and the two projections to the original stages commutes by the second projection equation. Pasting it with the pullback square at the earlier stage gives the pullback square at the later stage, because the projection from the successor factors through the earlier one. The outer square and the earlier square are pullbacks, so the transition square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_baseCh: The two lengths agree by construction. Take the second pullback projection to the original scheme as the comparison at every stage. At zero its compatibility with the initial maps is the pullback square. Every consecutive transition square is a pullback by the tower comparison, and every center is the pullback along the corresponding stage projection. These are exactly the strict pullback conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp_fst: By the defining projection equation of the pullback transition, its first projection equals the first projection of the later pullback. This expresses that the new base is held fixed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp_snd: The second projection of the pullback transition is the projection to the original later stage followed by the original transition to the earlier stage. This is its other defining projection equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_eq_comp: Both the direct map and the composite preserve the projection to the new base. Along the other projection, the composite is the later projection followed by the two original transitions. By functoriality their composite is the direct original transition, so the second projections agree as well. Pullback extensionality gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_refl: Compare the two maps by their projections from the pullback. On the new base they give the same projection. On the original stage the transition from that stage to itself is the identity, so the second projections also agree. Uniqueness of pullback maps gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_self_eq_id: The order arrow from a stage to itself is an identity. Taking its opposite and applying the tower functor preserves the identity, so the stage transition is the identity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.blowupMorphism_squar: Compose the given equation with the forward base isomorphism. It cancels the inverse base isomorphism on the left and gives the desired commuting square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.center_comap_eq: Pull the two ambient center ideals back along the first stage comparison. The commuting comparison square identifies the pullback through the proposed base isomorphism with the pullback through the second stage comparison and local isomorphism. Each local center is the pullback of its base center, and the local isomorphism identifies them. The resulting equality after pullback descends because the first comparison is flat and surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.exists_iso_succ_blow: Compose the second blowup with the inverse of the current base isomorphism. This presents it as a blowup over the first base stage, along the pullback of its center. That pulled-back center is the first center by the descended equality. The uniqueness of the blowup along a given center yields an isomorphism of the two successor schemes over the first stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.isomorphic_of_: Strict pullback preserves lengths, and the local isomorphism matches the two local lengths, so the original lengths agree. The stagewise pullback squares make the comparisons flat and surjective. Together with the local isomorphism and its center compatibility, these supply the descent data for constructing compatible base-stage isomorphisms through the final stage. The construction gives the initial and transition equations. At each stage faithful flatness descends the center equation. These facts make the base sequences isomorphic.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_isoObjZero_trans_symm_eq: The proposed stage-zero isomorphism passes through the common base using the two initial identifications. After composing both sides with the second initial isomorphism, the two base-comparison equations give maps that agree by the initial local isomorphism’s compatibility. Cancelling the second initial isomorphism gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_compatible_isos_of_le: Induct on the length of the initial segment. At zero, the base-stage isomorphism passes through the common base and satisfies the chart comparison by the stage-zero equation. For a successor, the previous stage isomorphism already agrees with the local one. Faithfully flat ideal descent identifies the two center ideals there. The two blowups along these corresponding centers then have a successor isomorphism commuting with the transition maps. Keep all earlier isomorphisms. To check the new chart compatibility, compare the two maps from the local successor to the second base successor after projecting to the preceding base stage. The transition squares and the local isomorphism show these composites agree. The pulled-back center along their common composite is the local center pulled back to its blowup, so it is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. Uniqueness of the blowup lift gives equality of the two maps, completing the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendIsoFamilySucc_of_le: The enlarged family uses the previous family at any index at or below the previous endpoint, by the first case of its definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendIsoFamilySucc_self: The new endpoint is strictly greater than the previous endpoint. The definition therefore assigns it the newly specified isomorphism, with identity transport at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_and_surjective_of_isPullback_blowup: At zero the comparison square is a pullback because the two stage-zero structure maps are isomorphisms and the square commutes. The comparison is thus a base change of the flat surjective cover. At a successor the stage comparison is a base change of the previous comparison by the given pullback square. Induction transfers flatness and surjectivity at each step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_of_isPullback_of_flat: The projection in the pullback is the base change of the opposite flat morphism. Flatness is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoFamilyOfZero_zero: The initial isomorphism family is defined by transporting the given isomorphism along the index equality with zero. At index zero that transport is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_of_isPullback: The projection is a base change of the given surjective morphism. For any point in its target, choose a point of the other scheme with the same image in the common base. The two points lift to the scheme pullback, proving surjectivity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_lt_apply_of_forall_lt_succ: Each consecutive pair of values through the bound is strictly increasing. Chaining these inequalities from the lower index to the higher one gives the stated strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_strictTransformι: The new strict-transform ideal is the pullback of the original one, which is the kernel of the base-changed strict-transform immersion. Apply the closed-subscheme pullback result for equal kernels to construct the comparison and its pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_subscheme_of_ker_eq: The base change of the original closed immersion is itself a closed immersion. Its kernel is the specified new ideal, so the new closed subscheme is isomorphic over the new ambient scheme to this pullback. Under that isomorphism use the other projection as the comparison to the original closed subscheme. The projections commute and the square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_of_mono_of_comp_eq: Each composite of the two proposed maps becomes the identity after composition with the corresponding ambient monomorphism, by the two factorization equations. Cancellation makes the two composites identities. The maps therefore form an isomorphism with the stated factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_ker: The closed immersion and the immersion defined by its kernel have the same kernel ideal. Each therefore factors through the other by the closed-immersion lifting property. They are monomorphisms, so the two factorizations form an isomorphism over the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_levelMap: The stage comparison is a pullback of the flat ambient comparison along the target projection to its ambient base. Flatness is preserved by pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_strictTransformComparison: The ambient stage comparison is flat, and the square of strict transforms identifies their comparison as its base change along the original strict-transform inclusion. This comparison is therefore flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_strictTransformComparison_str: The chosen strict-transform comparison exhibits the new strict transform as the pullback of the original strict-transform inclusion. Its defining property is exactly this pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_le_length: At the final source index the reindexing is the target length by hypothesis. At any earlier index it is strictly below the target length. Either case gives the weak bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_lt_reindex_of_lt: The chart comparison requires strict increase at each consecutive source index. The chain of one-step inequalities gives strict increase between the two specified indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_ne_of_lt_reindex_zero: The reindexed zero is at most every retained index by monotonicity. An index strictly below it therefore cannot be retained.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_ne_of_reindex_lt_of_lt_reindex_s: An index at or before the given source stage has reindexed value at most the earlier endpoint. An index at or after its successor has value at least the later endpoint. Thus no retained value lies strictly between these consecutive endpoints.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformComparison_comp_strictTra: The strict-transform comparison was chosen with a commuting square of strict-transform inclusions and ambient comparison. The displayed equality is its commuting equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIdeal_comap_transitionMap: Induct on the number of omitted steps between the earlier stage and the reindexed stage. With zero steps the transition is the identity. Otherwise the first omitted center pulls back to the unit ideal on the comparison scheme, since the relevant stage square is a pullback and the step is omitted. The strict transform agrees with the total transform after this pullback because the pulled-back center is unit. Thus pulling the earlier ideal back equals pulling back the next strict-transform ideal along the comparison to that stage. Apply induction across the remaining omitted steps, using composition of the ambient transitions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIdeal_eq_comap: At zero the ideals are the kernels of the original closed embeddings transported to their initial ambient stages. The embedding pullback square remains a pullback after transport by the initial isomorphisms, and the comparison to the original stage zero is flat. Thus the kernel formula for flat base change gives equality there. The omitted initial centers have unit pullbacks, so the equality also holds at the first retained stage. At a successor the ambient comparison square identifies the new blowup with the flat base change of the original retained blowup. The preceding strict-transform ideal and center are corresponding pullbacks, so flat base change of strict transforms identifies the successor ideals at this blowup. All intervening stages before the next retained index are omitted, and pullback across their unit centers preserves the strict-transform ideal. This gives the equality at the next retained index and completes the induction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientCenter_eq_imageIdealSheaf_of_isPu: At each step the pushforward condition defines the new ambient center as the image of the original center under the chosen closed immersion at that stage. The chosen family satisfies precisely this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowdown_comm_of_isPushforwardBlowupSeq: The stage comparisons of the pushforward sequence form commuting squares with every consecutive blowdown. This is the required equation at the indicated step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_strictTransform_iso: The composite from the original strict transform into the target ambient stage is a closed immersion. Its kernel is the image of the original strict-transform ideal, which equals the target strict-transform ideal by the stagewise calculation. Thus this composite and the target strict-transform inclusion have the same kernel. The closed-immersion comparison is an isomorphism of their sources over the target ambient stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_of_isPushforwardBlowup: The chosen stage comparisons in a pushforward blowup sequence are closed immersions at every stage. The lengths agree, so the given index is in range for this property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoObjZero_comm_of_isPushforwardBlowupSe: At zero the pushforward comparison is required to commute with the two initial isomorphisms and the given ambient immersion. The chosen family comes with this equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_succ_eq_strictTransform_of_isPushfor: The pushforward condition identifies the kernel of the next stage comparison with the strict transform of the preceding kernel along the target blowup. Apply this condition at the specified index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length: The two embedded sequences have the same length. Transfer the given index bound along the equality of lengths.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_strictTransformIdeal_levelMap: At zero, the strict-transform ideal is the kernel of the transported embedding. The initial comparison and embedding compatibilities identify the composite into the target initial stage with the transported target embedding. Thus the image ideal equals the target strict-transform ideal. At a successor use the commutative blowdown square and the requirement that the successor stage immersion has strict-transform kernel. The result commuting image ideals with strict transform then applies. The previous strict-transform ideal maps to the corresponding target ideal by induction and the original center maps to the target center by the pushforward condition. This proves the successor equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIsPushforwardSeq_ambientMap: The chart pushforward constructed from the sequence comparison is assigned the given closed immersion as its ambient comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_subset_range_of_ker_le: The kernel containment makes the first closed immersion factor through the second by the closed-immersion lifting property. Thus every point in the range of the first map is the image of a point under the second map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIso_hom_comp_strictTransf: Compose both maps with the target strict-transform inclusion. The comparison isomorphisms commute with the inclusions, and the strict-transform transitions commute with ambient blowdowns. Use the pushforward blowdown square to identify the two resulting composites. Cancellation of the target closed immersion gives the asserted equality.

The chosen isomorphism identifies the two strict transforms over the target ambient stage. Its defining equation says exactly that its composite with the target inclusion is the original inclusion followed by the stage comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIso_zero_hom_comp_strictT: Compose both maps to the original scheme with the target embedding. The stage-zero strict-transform equations replace these composites by the relevant strict-transform inclusions followed by their ambient initial isomorphisms. The initial stage comparison commutes with the ambient initial isomorphisms, and the original embedding followed by the ambient comparison is the target embedding. Hence the composites agree. Cancel the target embedding to obtain equality of the two maps to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeIsoOfEq_hom_subschemeι: Identify the two defining ideal sheaves using their equality. The induced isomorphism of the closed subschemes is then the identity, so both composites to the ambient scheme are the same inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ambientCenter_eq_image: The target center ideal is the kernel of the original center inclusion followed by the stage comparison. This composite is a closed immersion, so the support of its kernel is its range. That range is the image, under the stage comparison, of the range of the original center inclusion. The latter range is the original center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ker_eq_range: The closed subscheme of the kernel ideal has range equal to that ideal’s support. Its inclusion has the same kernel as the original closed immersion, so each factors through the other. The ranges are therefore equal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centerOffDetached_eq_comap: The center off the detached locus is the image ideal of the ambient center restricted to the complement of that locus. The new complement is the inverse image of the old one. In the resulting open-restriction pullback square, the old open inclusion is quasi-compact and the strict-transform comparison is flat. Hence image of the restricted ideal commutes with this pullback. The commuting square of ambient and strict-transform comparisons identifies the new restricted ideal with the pullback of the old restricted ideal. Substituting gives equality of the centers off the detached loci.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapAmbientCenter_eq_comap: The new ambient center is the pullback of the old one. Pull it back again to the new strict transform. The square of strict-transform inclusions and comparison maps commutes, so this composite pullback equals pulling the old center first to the old strict transform and then along the strict-transform comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_ker_subschemeι_comp: The image ideal is defined as the kernel of the map from the closed subscheme of the ideal to the target.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_detachedClosure_eq_preimage: The two strict transforms are Noetherian, so each detached locus is closed and equals its closure. The pullback formula for detached loci therefore also gives the equality for their closures.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedClosureCompl_eq_preimage: The detached closure upstairs is the inverse image of the detached closure downstairs. Inverse image commutes with complements, so the corresponding open complements also pull back.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedIdeal_eq_comap: Both strict transforms are reduced and Noetherian, and their comparison is flat. The original detached closure is a union of irreducible components, and the new detached closure is its inverse image. The flat pullback formula for vanishing ideals of unions of components identifies the new vanishing ideal with the pullback of the original one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocus_eq_preimage: The strict-transform comparison is flat. If a point belongs to a detached component upstairs, closure of that component’s image is an irreducible component downstairs by flatness. The support comparison puts its image in the closed inverse image of the original center, and this holds for the closure as well. Thus the image component is detached. Conversely, if the image of a point belongs to a detached component downstairs, the component lifting property for flat maps gives a component through the point upstairs whose image closure is the specified downstairs component. Its entire image therefore lies on the original center. The support comparison puts the whole upstairs component on the new center, making it detached.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedSchemeComparison_comp_detachedι: The chosen comparison of detached schemes was constructed to commute with their inclusions into the strict transforms. Its defining factorization equation gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedSchemeComparison_comp_detachedι_: Postcompose the commuting equation for the detached comparison with the given morphism and use associativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_detachedScheme: The new detached ideal is the pullback of the original detached ideal along the strict-transform comparison. The closed subscheme of a pulled-back ideal is the base change of the original closed subscheme. Apply this identification to obtain the comparison map, its commuting equation, and the pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_subschemeι_comap: The closed immersion from the pulled-back ideal and the first projection from the canonical pullback have the same kernel. Each therefore factors through the other over the new ambient scheme. Cancellation of the two closed immersions makes the factorizations inverse. Under the resulting isomorphism, take the second pullback projection as the map to the original closed subscheme. It commutes with the immersions and gives the asserted pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_of_forall_reindex_ne: The commuting maps from the given scheme induce a map to the pullback of the skipped ambient stage. Any point maps through the detached scheme, whose support is the detached locus because the strict transform is Noetherian. Its ambient image lies on the skipped center by the definition of detachment. Thus its image in the pullback belongs to the pulled-back center support. But an omitted step has unit pulled-back center, with empty support. This contradiction rules out every point of the given scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_detachedSchemeComparison: The chosen map is the one given by the pullback result for detached subschemes. By that construction its comparison square with the strict transforms is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_strictTransform: The ground input is reduced and all ambient stages within the length are Noetherian. The stagewise reducedness theorem for strict transforms therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_ambientCenter_iff: The new ambient center is the pullback of the original center, so its support is the inverse image of the original support. The commuting square of strict-transform inclusions identifies the image of the given point under the ambient comparison with the ambient image of its strict-transform comparison. This gives the membership equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_strictTransform: The ambient scheme at the stage is Noetherian. The strict transform is its closed subscheme, so its underlying subspace is Noetherian.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_detachedClosure_eq_image: The strict-transform isomorphism gives a homeomorphism on point spaces. It sends the original detached locus to the target locus and commutes with taking topological closure, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_centerOffDetached: The complements of the detached closures correspond under the strict-transform isomorphism, giving a pullback square of open inclusions. The restricted target ambient center pulls back in this square to the restricted original ambient center by the commuting square and the comparison of ambient centers on strict transforms. The center off the detached locus is the image ideal of that restricted center along the open inclusion. Flat base change allows this image operation to commute with pullback along the isomorphism, which gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comapAmbientCenter: The target ambient center is the image ideal of the original center under the stage closed immersion. Pulling that image back along the closed immersion recovers the original center. By the commuting square of strict transforms, pulling back the restriction of the target center is the same as first pulling back along that stage immersion and then restricting to the original strict transform. The result is the original restricted center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_detachedIdeal: The strict transforms are reduced and Noetherian. Their isomorphism is flat and takes the inverse image of the target detached closure to the original detached closure. The target closure is a union of irreducible components. The flat pullback formula for the vanishing ideal of such a union identifies its pullback with the original detached ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocus_eq_image: The strict-transform isomorphism is surjective and sends exactly the detached components to the detached components of the target. Taking their unions therefore sends the original detached locus onto the target one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedSchemeIso_hom_comp_detachedι: The detached-scheme isomorphism was chosen with the condition that its composite with the target detached inclusion equals the original detached inclusion followed by the strict-transform isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_of_preimage_opens_eq: The equality of opens ensures that the forward isomorphism sends the first open into the second and that its inverse sends the second into the first. Restrict both maps using the open inclusions. Their composites are identities by cancellation after the inclusions, and the forward restriction commutes with the inclusions by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_detachedScheme: The strict-transform isomorphism identifies the two detached ideals by pullback. Restrict it to the closed subschemes of these ideals to get an isomorphism commuting with their inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_subschemeIso_of_comap_eq: The ideal pullback equality lets the forward ambient isomorphism restrict to a map between the two closed subschemes. Pulling the equality back by the inverse gives the restriction in the reverse direction. The composites become identities after composing with the closed immersions, so cancellation makes them inverse. The forward restriction has the desired ambient compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_detachedComponents_iff: The strict-transform isomorphism carries irreducible components to irreducible components and reflects that condition. The ambient center support upstairs is the image of the support downstairs under the closed stage comparison. The square with the strict-transform inclusions commutes, so a component image contained in the original center maps to one contained in the new center. Conversely, if its image is contained in the new center, injectivity of the ambient stage comparison forces every original point into the original center. Thus the componentwise containment conditions are equivalent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_irreducibleComponents_iff_image: The two continuous inverse maps give a homeomorphism. They carry irreducible sets to irreducible sets in both directions. If the image of a component lies in a larger irreducible set, apply the inverse map and use maximality of the component. Applying the forward map gives maximality of the image. The same argument with the maps reversed proves the converse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_coe_detachedClosure: The target detached closure is the image of the original closure. The strict-transform map is injective, so the inverse image of that image is the original closure.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_detachedClosureCompl: The original detached closure is the inverse image of the target detached closure. Taking complements and using that inverse image commutes with complement gives the identity of the two opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sUnion_eq_image_sUnion: A point of a set in the source family maps into the image of that set, which belongs to the target family. Conversely, for a point of a target family member, choose a preimage by surjectivity. The inverse image of that member maps onto the member and hence belongs to the source family by the assumed equivalence. This preimage point belongs to the source union, proving the reverse containment.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EmbeddedResolutionRule.toAffineResolutio: The affine rule first uses the chosen embedding of the input scheme, then evaluates the embedded resolution rule at that embedding. Evaluating the definition gives the claimed sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeEmb_comp_baseChangeProjection: The base-changed embedding comes from the universal property of the ambient pullback. Its first component is the projection to the original embedded scheme followed by the original embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeEmb_comp_baseChangeToSpec: The base-changed embedding was defined using the structural map to the extension field as its second component. Composing with the second projection therefore returns that structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_baseChange_ambientToSpec: The original ambient scheme and both field spectra are affine. Their fiber product is therefore affine, with coordinate ring given by extension of scalars.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_baseChangeEmb: The comparison square identifies the base-changed embedding with the pullback of the original closed immersion. A base change of a closed immersion is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_baseChangeEmb: Place the comparison square beside the base-change square for the ambient scheme. Their outer rectangle is the base-change square for the embedded scheme because the original embedding respects the field structure and the induced map respects the extension-field projections. The ambient square and the outer rectangle are pullbacks, so pullback cancellation proves that the comparison square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_baseChangeToSpec: The structural map after extending the field is the pullback of the original structural map. Being locally of finite type is preserved by pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_baseChangeToSpec_amb: The original ambient structural map is locally of finite type by the embedding data. Applying stability under pullback gives the property for the ambient structural map over the extension field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCondition_baseChangeEmb: The original embedding followed by the ambient structural map is the structural map of the embedded scheme. Thus following the projection to the original scheme and then this composite agrees with following the projection to the extension field and then its map to the original field, by commutativity of the base-change square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_baseChangeToSpec: The new structural map is obtained by pulling back the original structural map along the map of field spectra. Quasi-compactness is preserved by this base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_baseChangeToSpec_ambientToS: The original ambient structural map is quasi-compact by the embedding data. Its pullback to the extension field is therefore quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_baseChangeToSpec: The structural map over the extension field is the base change of the original map. Smoothness is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_baseChangeToSpec_ambientToSpec: The original ambient structural map is smooth by the embedding data. Its base change to the extension field is smooth by stability under pullback.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedResolutionRule_isCompatibleWithF: For any field extension and base-changed embedding satisfying the given conditions, the strict field base-change theorem for the embedded rule gives the required comparison. This is precisely compatibility with field base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedResolutionRule_isCompatibleWithS: Take an arbitrary smooth ambient map over the field and a pullback square of embeddings as in the compatibility condition. The smooth pullback theorem for the embedded rule gives the required comparison of output sequences for these data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedResolutionRule_isPullbackBlowupS: The smooth ambient map is flat, so the pullback square of embeddings identifies the new kernel ideal with the pullback of the old kernel. Its nonvanishing condition is the one supplied by the new embedding, and the pulled-back boundary is empty. Apply smooth functoriality of principalization to obtain the comparison of the ambient blowup sequences, identifying the input ideals by their equality. The pullback square of the embeddings and this ambient comparison give the chart comparison for flat base change. Its comparison of induced blowup sequences after deleting unit-center steps is exactly the assertion for the embedded rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedResolutionRule_isStrictPullbackB: After extending the field, the schemes and structural maps retain the affineness and finiteness properties needed by principalization. The ambient projection is flat, so the base-change square identifies the new embedding ideal with the pullback of the original ideal. The supplied nonvanishing and empty-boundary conditions therefore allow application of field functoriality of principalization. This gives a pullback comparison of the ambient sequences, which induces a pullback comparison of the embedded sequences with unit-center steps deleted. The projection of the base-changed embedded scheme is surjective, and the original sequence with unit-center steps deleted has only proper centers. The strict pullback criterion thus removes all reindexing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_congr_left: Replace the source sequence of the existing pullback comparison by the equal sequence. All the same comparison maps and center identities apply.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationAlgorithm_toSequenceOfBl: Use the equality of ideals to identify the two inputs to principalization. The ambient scheme, ideal and boundary now agree, and the proofs of admissibility do not affect the value. The resulting blowup sequences are equal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasProperCenters_embeddedResolutionRuleO: The rule is formed by deleting the unit-center steps of the blowup sequence induced by principalization. Each index within the resulting length therefore has a center ideal distinct from the unit ideal, which is the required proper-center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nilIsStrictNormalCrossingsOfSmooth: For any of the smooth schemes in the statement, the empty list is in strict normal crossing position by the empty-boundary theorem for smooth schemes. Apply that theorem to its structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toAffineResolutionRule_embeddedResolutio: Evaluate both rules on an arbitrary input scheme over its field. The chosen embedding is exactly the affine-space embedding datum used by the affine principalization rule. The comparison of the two principalization constructions for this datum identifies the output sequences. Equality at every input proves equality of the rules.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emb_comp_ambientMap_eq_enlargeAmbient_em: Passing to an embedded blowup sequence retains the given embedding. Composing the retained old embedding with the enlargement map therefore gives the retained enlarged embedding, by the definition of enlargement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emb_comp_comp_eq_of_comp_eq: The ambient enlargement is over the field, so its composite with the new structural map is the old structural map. Precomposing by the old embedding gives the structural map of the embedded scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.enlargeAmbient_ambient: The enlargement datum takes the specified larger scheme as its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.enlargeAmbient_ambientToSpec: The enlargement datum equips the larger ambient scheme with the structural morphism given in its inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.enlargeAmbient_emb: The enlarged datum is constructed by composing the original embedding with the closed immersion into the larger ambient scheme. Its embedding is exactly this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_ker_eq_ker_comp: The ideal sheaf of the image under a composite is the image ideal sheaf of the first kernel along the second map. Since the first map is a closed immersion, applying the kernel composition formula gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_ambientBlowups_en: The image of the original embedding ideal along the ambient immersion is the kernel ideal of the composite embedding. It has the required nonvanishing by the enlarged datum. Apply pushforward functoriality of principalization along the closed immersion of positive étale coordinate codimension, with empty boundary on both ambient schemes. Identifying the image ideal with the enlarged embedding ideal gives the asserted pushforward comparison of ambient sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_embeddedResolutionRule_enlarg: Pushforward functoriality gives the comparison of the two ambient blowup sequences. The enlarged embedding is the original embedding followed by the ambient closed immersion, so this comparison gives a chart pushforward for the embedded sequences. Chart pushforward induces an isomorphism on their blowup sequences after deleting unit-center steps, which are the outputs of the two resolution rules.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleCover_closedEmbeddingIntoAff:
Take the disjoint union of the finitely many chart domains with the map to the source induced by their open inclusions. It is an affine reduced scheme, and its map to the source is étale and surjective because the domains cover. Its structure map is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, the latter because its underlying space is compact and the field spectrum has one point.

For the first embedding take the disjoint union of the charts' smooth ambient schemes. Pasting the pullback squares by coproduct gives the pullback of the target embedding along the induced smooth ambient map. For the second take the disjoint union of the corresponding basic opens in the source ambient scheme. Restrict the source embedding to each basic open and take the coproduct of these pullback squares. In each case the new ambient is affine, smooth and locally of finite type over the field, and quasi-compact by finiteness. The embedding is closed by base change. Its kernel is the pullback of the old kernel along the flat ambient map, so it remains nonzero on components. The composites over the field agree by the pullback squares, and smoothness gives strict normal crossings for the empty boundary.

For the first ambient union use the common threshold to present every summand in affine spaces of the same dimension and coordinate codimension. For the second, presenting each basic open adds one coordinate and one to the codimension of the original source presentation. In either union choose distinct field elements for the finitely many indices using characteristic zero. Put each summand in the slice at its assigned value of one new coordinate. The slice construction gives a closed immersion over the field and increases the common coordinate codimension by one. These are the required presentations of the two embeddings.

Choose a presented local chart through every point of the affine source. Its chart domain is open and contains that point, so compactness gives a finite collection still covering the source. Take the maximum presentation threshold among the selected charts. Their finite cover and the common threshold satisfy the chart assembly theorem, which supplies the two presented embeddings on the surjective étale affine cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_sigmaDesc: The inclusions of the summands give an open cover of the coproduct. The restriction to each summand is flat by hypothesis. Flatness is local on the source, so the whole map is flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isZariskiLocalAtSource_flat: On affine charts flatness is the flatness of the induced ring map. The scheme property associated to this ring-map property is Zariski local on the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isZariskiLocalAtSource_locallyOfFiniteTy: On affine source and target charts, being locally of finite type is the finite-type property of the induced ring map. The source-locality result for this ring-map property gives the corresponding Zariski locality of scheme morphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_sigmaDesc: The disjoint union is covered by its open summands, and the given map restricts to the specified map on each. Each restriction is locally of finite type, so locality on the source proves the result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_specToAffineSpaceExten: Both schemes are affine and the map on global sections is surjective by the coordinate generation result. For affine schemes, such a map defines a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specHomOfGlobalSections_appTop: The scheme map is obtained by taking spectra of the ring map and identifying the spectrum of the ambient global sections with the affine ambient scheme. Naturality of the identification between rings and sections on spectra shows that pullback sends a section to its image under the given ring map, viewed as a section on the source spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_appTop_coo: In the first coordinate block, the defining sections are the pullbacks of the original affine-space coordinates along the map through the ambient scheme. The coordinate formula for a map into affine space gives exactly these sections.
The defining vector uses the sections corresponding to the given ring elements as its second block. Pullback of the coordinate in this block returns its defining section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_appTop_sur: The closed immersion of the ambient scheme induces a surjection on global sections. Lift each ambient coefficient to a section of the first affine space and then pull that section back along projection from the larger affine space. The first-block comparison ensures its image is the corresponding coefficient in the target ring. Each new generator is the pullback of its second-block coordinate. Thus sums and products of these lifted coordinates and coefficients give preimages of all polynomial expressions in the generators. By the generation hypothesis these expressions give every global section of the source spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_comp_projL: After projection to the first block, both maps have the same structural map by the hypothesis that the ambient embedding is over the field. Their pullbacks of the first-block coordinates agree by construction. The coordinate characterization of maps into affine space gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_comp_toSpe: The map determined by the two blocks of sections is constructed over the field, using the structural map obtained through the ambient scheme. Its composite with the target projection is that structural map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_baseChange: After extending the field, the ambient structural morphism is the base change of the original one. Smoothness, local finite type, and quasi-compactness are preserved by base change. The map back to the original scheme is flat, since it is pulled back from a field extension. Flat pullback preserves nonvanishing on components. The new field has characteristic zero, the marking is unchanged and remains positive, and the pulled-back boundary has strict normal crossings by the field base-change result. These are the admissibility conditions.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeProjection: The first component of the induced map into the base change is the projection to the original source followed by the given map. The first projection of the pullback recovers this component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeToSpec: The second component of the induced map is the source structural map to the extension field. Composing the induced map with the target's second projection recovers that component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_baseChangeMap: The comparison square identifies the induced map with the pullback of the given étale map. Étaleness is preserved under this base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_surjective_affine_cover_bas: Quasi-compactness over the field gives a finite affine open cover. Take the disjoint union of its members and the map given by the open inclusions. This union is affine and reduced, and the cover map is étale and surjective. Its structural map is locally of finite type and quasi-compact. After extending the field, affineness and both finiteness properties persist, while the reducedness criterion for the extended union applies because the extended base is reduced. The induced cover map is again étale and surjective by base change. Its two projection identities give the stated compatibilities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pullback_snd_base_eq: The two points lie over the same base point, so they admit a common lift to the scheme-theoretic fiber product. The second projection of this lift is the given point of the second scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_baseChange: The map between the spectra of the fields is affine. Its pullback is the projection from the extended scheme to the original one, hence this projection is affine. Since its target is affine, its source is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffine_baseChange_comp: The composite is a structural map from the given affine source to the field spectrum. Apply affineness of field base change to this structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_baseChangeMap: Place the proposed comparison square beside the base-change square for the target. The right square is a pullback, and the outer rectangle is the base-change square for the source because the induced map respects the structural maps to the extension field. The comparison square commutes by the formula for the first projection. Pullback cancellation gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_baseChange_sigmaOpensDesc: Pull back each summand inclusion along the projection from the extended disjoint union. These open immersions cover that union because every point projects to a point in one summand, and the two points have a common lift to the pullback. Each pulled-back summand also maps by an open immersion into the extended base scheme. This follows by pasting the two pullback squares and using that the original summand maps to the original base by its open inclusion. Since the extended base scheme is reduced, each covering summand has reduced stalks. The covering criterion gives reducedness of the extended disjoint union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk: A scheme is reduced exactly when its local rings are reduced. The hypothesis supplies this condition at every point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk_of_cover: Choose a point over any given point of the target using the covering condition. Its open immersion identifies the two local rings. The source local ring is reduced by hypothesis, so the target local ring is reduced. This holds at every point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_stalk_of_isOpenImmersion: The map on local rings at a point of an open subscheme is an isomorphism. The local ring on the open subscheme embeds into the reduced local ring on the target via the inverse map, so it is reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismProperty_of_isPullback: The square identifies its top map with the base change of its bottom map along the other side. Stability under base change transfers the property of the bottom map to the top map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCondition_baseChangeMap: Associate the first composite so that the original map of schemes is followed by the original structural map. The resulting equality is commutativity of the base-change square for the composite structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigma_jointly_surjective: The inclusions of the summands form the canonical open cover of the disjoint union. Every point lies in the image of one of these inclusions, which supplies the index and the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_baseChangeMap: The comparison square identifies the induced map with the pullback of the given surjection. Surjectivity of scheme morphisms is preserved under base change.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.existsGluedBlowupSequence_of_center_ne_t: Choose a finite affine open cover and take its disjoint union as a surjective affine étale cover. Take a surjective affine étale cover of the self-overlap. Both composite maps from this overlap cover to the first cover are surjective and étale, so the affine rule gives strict pullback comparisons for both. The overlap descent theorem therefore constructs a sequence on the original scheme. Its centers are nonunit because the centers on the original affine cover are nonunit. For any other surjective affine étale cover, choose a surjective affine étale cover of its overlap with the first cover. The affine rule on this common cover is the strict pullback of the rule on each cover. Along the first route it is therefore the strict pullback of the descended sequence. The two maps to the original scheme agree by the pullback square. Descending along the cover of the other chart shows that its sequence is the strict pullback of the descended sequence as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullback_of_pullback_cove: Base change the sequence along each projection from the self-overlap, then to the covering scheme of that overlap. Each of the resulting sequences is a strict pullback along the corresponding composite. The given comparison sequence is also such a strict pullback in both cases, so uniqueness identifies the two sequences on the cover. Faithfully flat descent of sequence isomorphisms gives an isomorphism on the overlap itself. The descent construction for that overlap isomorphism then gives a sequence over the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullback_of_comp_flat_surjective: Form the base change of the target sequence first along the given flat map and then to the flat surjective cover. Over the cover this is a strict pullback of the target sequence, as is the given comparison sequence. Uniqueness identifies these two sequences over the cover. Since the comparison sequence is also a strict pullback of the proposed intermediate sequence, descent of isomorphisms identifies that intermediate sequence with the base-changed target sequence. Transfer the strict pullback comparison across this isomorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.C_sub_map_C_aeval_mem_graphRelationIdeal: Work modulo the ideal generated by the graph relations. In this quotient, each graph variable in the coefficient ring equals its defining polynomial in the original variables. Scalars agree on both sides. Addition preserves this equality, and multiplication by a graph variable preserves it by the corresponding graph relation. Polynomial induction proves that every coefficient polynomial agrees with its substituted polynomial modulo the ideal, which puts the stated difference in the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_graphAlgebra: The algebra structure on the graph ring is given by evaluating each graph coordinate at its defining polynomial and then identifying the resulting polynomial with its element in the graph ring. This is the stated formula for its algebra map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_graphAlgebra_eq_algebraMap_mv: The graph algebra map evaluates polynomials at the defining functions. Evaluation sends a scalar to that same scalar, and the polynomial-to-graph identification respects scalars. Thus passing through the ring of graph coordinates gives the ordinary scalar map to the graph ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_C: Evaluation sends a constant coefficient to its image under the algebra map. The coefficient here is a polynomial in the graph coordinates, so its image is evaluation at the defining polynomials, viewed in the graph ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_X: The evaluation map sends a variable to its prescribed value. The prescribed value is the corresponding original polynomial variable viewed in the graph ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_eq_graphAlgebraEquiv_g: Compare the two maps on the polynomial generators. On coefficients both substitute the defining polynomials for the graph variables. On the original variables both return the corresponding graph ring variables. They preserve addition and multiplication, so they agree on every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_graphRelation: In the graph relation, the first term is the graph coordinate as a constant coefficient. Evaluation substitutes its defining polynomial. The second term, obtained by including that polynomial's coefficients, evaluates to the same polynomial in the graph ring. Their difference is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_map_C: Use polynomial induction. For a scalar, the coefficient inclusion followed by evaluation gives the same scalar in the graph ring. Sums follow by additivity. Multiplication by a variable follows because the coefficient inclusion preserves that variable and evaluation sends it to the corresponding variable of the graph ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraAeval_map_C_graphAlgebraEqui: Represent the graph ring element by its polynomial under the inverse identification. Including the coefficients and evaluating returns that polynomial viewed in the graph ring, hence the original element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphJacobianMinorMatrix_apply: By construction, the entry in the chosen row and column is the partial derivative of the column's polynomial with respect to the row's selected variable.
