Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphPreSubmersivePresentation_jacobiMat: Differentiate each graph relation with respect to its selected row variable. The graph coordinate is a constant coefficient, so its derivative is zero. Differentiation commutes with the inclusion of the original coefficients, so the remaining term is the negative of the included partial derivative of the corresponding defining polynomial. These are the entries of the asserted negative matrix.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphPreSubmersivePresentation_jacobian: Use the entrywise calculation to write the presentation's Jacobian matrix as the negative of the scalar-extended minor matrix. Taking the determinant contributes one factor of minus one for each row and commutes with the coefficient inclusion. Evaluating the determinant in the graph ring undoes that coefficient inclusion on the original polynomial determinant. This gives the claimed signed determinant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphPreSubmersivePresentation_map: The pre-submersive graph presentation is equipped with the given injection from the relation indices to the chosen variable indices. Its selected variable for each relation is therefore the value of that injection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphPreSubmersivePresentation_relation: The pre-submersive presentation retains the graph presentation's relations, which are the graph coordinate minus its defining polynomial for each index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphSubstitutionHom_C: Substitution acts on constant coefficients by substituting the defining polynomials into the graph variables. A polynomial constant in the original variables is therefore sent to this substituted coefficient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphSubstitutionHom_X: The substitution map evaluates the coefficients and sends each original polynomial variable to itself. Applying it to a variable therefore gives the same variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_ker_graphAlgebraGenerators_iff: The generator map evaluates the original variables at their corresponding graph ring elements. This is the graph evaluation map, so its kernel consists exactly of the polynomials evaluating to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_range_graphRelation_eq_ker: Every graph relation evaluates to zero, so their span is in the kernel. Conversely, if a polynomial evaluates to zero in the graph ring, its substituted polynomial is zero by injectivity of the polynomial-to-graph identification. The polynomial differs from its substituted form by an element of the graph relation ideal, so it belongs to that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sub_map_C_mem_graphRelationIdeal: Work modulo the graph relation ideal. For a constant coefficient, the preceding coefficient result gives equality with its substitution. Addition preserves the equality, and multiplying by an original variable preserves it because the substitution fixes that variable. Thus every polynomial agrees with its substituted polynomial after including its coefficients back into the original ring.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_graphAlgebraAway_eq_comp: The ring of graph coordinates acts on the localization through its map to the graph algebra and the localization map. This is the composite of the two algebra maps in the scalar tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_specMap_algebraMap_graph: The localized graph algebra is obtained by inverting the chosen Jacobian minor. The map on spectra of a localization at one element is the inclusion of the corresponding basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_specMap_algebraMap_graphAlgebraAwa: Prime ideals of the localized graph algebra correspond by contraction to prime ideals of the original graph algebra that avoid the powers of the Jacobian minor. These are precisely the points of the basic open of the minor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_specMap_algebraMap_graphAlgebraAw: The graph algebra localized at the chosen Jacobian minor is standard smooth over the ring of the graph coordinates. Its algebra map is therefore smooth. The affine correspondence between smooth ring maps and smooth morphisms of spectra gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMap_algebraMap_graphAlgebraAway_eq_c: Factor the algebra map through the graph algebra by the scalar tower. Taking spectra reverses the order of the two factors, giving the stated composite of scheme maps.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStandardSmooth_graphAlgebraAway: Compose the graph presentation with the presentation adjoining the inverse of the minor determinant. The composite Jacobian is a unit by the product calculation, so this is a submersive presentation. Its sets of variables and relations are finite and can be reindexed by finite sets of the stated sizes. This presentation exhibits the algebra as standard smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_algebraMap_graphJacobianMinorDet: The algebra is localized at the powers of the minor determinant. The determinant itself belongs to those powers, so its image is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_algebraMap_jacobian_graphPreSubme: The Jacobian of the graph presentation is the chosen minor determinant multiplied by a power of minus one. Both factors become units in the localization, so the image of their product is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_jacobian_presentation_graphAlgebr: The Jacobian of the composite presentation is the product of the image of the graph presentation's Jacobian and the Jacobian of the localization presentation. The first is a unit after localization, and the second is a unit because the localization presentation is submersive.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphMorphismToAffineSpace_appTop_coord_: The pullback of each target coordinate is the corresponding entry in the defining vector. In the first block that entry is the restriction of the original coordinate to the open scheme.
The defining vector gives the pullback of each coordinate section. In the second block its entries are the restrictions of the given functions to the open scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphMorphismToAffineSpace_comp_affineSp: The map determined by a vector of sections is a map over the field. Its composite with the target structural morphism is the structural morphism of the open source, given by its inclusion into the original affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphMorphismToAffineSpace_eq_homOfVecto: The graph morphism is the affine-space map over the field with the given vector of global sections. The first block is the restriction of the original coordinates to the open scheme and the second block is the restriction of the given functions.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_hom_apply: Pullback of global sections is contravariantly functorial. Thus the pullback along the composite first pulls the section back along the second map and then along the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ofIdealTop_span: For affine schemes the global ideal of the pulled-back ideal sheaf is extension of the original global ideal along the map on sections. Extension carries an ideal generated by a set to the ideal generated by its images. This gives the stated sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_univ_comap_affineSpac: All coordinates of the space of summed dimension pull back by reindexing to the coordinates in the two disjoint blocks. The projections pull back all coordinates in the first and second smaller spaces to exactly those blocks. Thus the reindexed generating set is the union of the two projected sets. The ideal generated by the union is the sum of the two generated ideals, yielding the equality of pulled-back ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_univ_eq_ofIdealTop: The ideal of a coordinate subspace is generated by the coordinates in the specified set. With every index selected, these are precisely all coordinate sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_ideal_top_eq: Each ideal sheaf on an affine scheme is recovered from its ideal on global sections. Equal global ideals therefore give equal ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphMorphismToAffineSpace_comp_projLeft: Check the structural map and every first-block coordinate. The graph morphism and both projections are over the field, so the structural maps agree. Projection pulls a coordinate back to its first-block coordinate, and the graph morphism pulls that coordinate back to the corresponding original coordinate restricted to the open. These are exactly the pullbacks through the open inclusion and original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_add_of_smooth_graphM:
For any point of the new ambient lift, choose a smooth coordinate chart near its image in the original affine space. The projected point is in this chart by the projection identity. Intersect the inverse image of this chart with the basic open on which the graph map is smooth. The new embedded point lies there because the basic open contains the whole image. On the intersection the graph map is smooth. Its first block is the original projection, so it factors through the inverse image of the original chart in the target graph space. This factor is smooth because its composite with the open inclusion is smooth.

On that graph space over the original chart, use the product of the original smooth coordinate map and the unchanged second block. This product map is smooth and over the field. Composing it with the restricted graph map and reindexing the coordinates gives the required smooth chart. The pullback of its first block's coordinate ideal is the original embedding ideal pulled back to the intersection. The pullback of its second block's coordinate ideal is generated by the graph functions there. The reindexed full coordinate ideal pulls back to the sum of these two ideals. By the given formula for the new kernel on global sections and the affine correspondence with ideal sheaves, this sum is exactly the restriction of the new embedding ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_top_ofIdealTop_eq: On an affine scheme the correspondence between ideal sheaves and ideals of the section ring evaluates a sheaf on the whole scheme. Applying this correspondence to the ideal sheaf associated to the given ideal returns that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_ofIdealTop_ker_appTop: A closed immersion identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image. Its pullback on global sections thus factors as the pullback of the canonical inclusion for the kernel ideal sheaf, followed by an isomorphism. The kernel of the latter composite is the global ideal of that ideal sheaf by the quotient description of the inclusion. The affine correspondence recovers the sheaf from this ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_app: On an affine open, the closed subscheme's map on sections is the quotient by the ideal on that open followed by an isomorphism. The isomorphism is injective, so the kernel is exactly the defining ideal on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIdealTop_sup: It is enough to compare global ideals on the affine scheme. The ideal of the supremum is the sum of the two global ideals, which is also the global ideal of the sheaf associated to their sum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackHasLocalAmbientEmbedding_o: Take the data supplied by the local graph chart, including the affine neighborhood and the pullback square of the new embedding. Use its number of added variables as the presentation threshold. It is at least the relative dimension because it equals that dimension plus the number of equations. The graph codimension result gives smooth coordinate codimension equal to the original codimension plus the number of equations. Reindex the two blocks as a single coordinate set. At a dimension above the threshold, append the additional coordinates as zero coordinates. This is a closed immersion and increases the coordinate codimension by the number of added zeros, giving the required formula. The projection identity and the fact that reindexing and zero-coordinate inclusions are over the field show that all the resulting presentations have the desired structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_smooth_comp_isOpenImmersion: The square formed by the map, the open immersion, the composite, and the identity of the source is a pullback. Indeed a compatible pair of maps into the source and the open must agree after factoring through the given map to the open, because the open immersion is a monomorphism. The original map is therefore a base change of the smooth composite, hence smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_apply: Pullback on sections of a composite applies the pullback of the second map and then that of the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_comp_apply: The map on points of a scheme composite is the composite of the maps on points. At the specified point it applies the first map and then the second.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.det_graphJacobianMinorMatrix_eq_det_jaco: Order the rows and columns by the two coordinate blocks. Derivatives of first-block coordinates in first-block variables give an identity block, and derivatives of those coordinates in second-block variables give a zero block below it. The lower right block is the prescribed matrix of derivatives of the graph sections. The matrix is block triangular, so its determinant is the product of the determinants of the identity and the prescribed matrix. Simultaneous reindexing of rows and columns does not change that determinant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraEquiv_symm_comp_algebraMap_X: The graph algebra map evaluates the chosen graph variable at its prescribed polynomial in the original variables. Applying the inverse graph algebra equivalence recovers that polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphAlgebraEquiv_symm_comp_algebraMap_c: Evaluation of a constant polynomial keeps its scalar, and the graph algebra equivalence preserves the coefficient field. Returning by its inverse therefore gives the original scalar as a constant in the source polynomial ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphCoordinates_inl: In the first block the graph coordinate polynomial is the corresponding original variable, by the definition of the graph coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphCoordinates_inr: The second block is defined by the polynomials associated with the given sections. At the chosen index this gives the polynomial of that section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphJacobianMinorDet_graphCoordinates: The graph minor determinant is the corresponding polynomial determinant viewed in the graph algebra. The block determinant calculation identifies the polynomial with the determinant of the prescribed section Jacobian, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.graphMorphismToAffineSpace_basicOpen_jac:
Factor the localized graph map through the spectrum of the graph algebra. The isomorphism with the Jacobian basic open identifies the first map with the open immersion of that basic open in the graph spectrum. In affine coordinates the remaining map is thus given by the graph algebra evaluation, restricted to the basic open.

This evaluation fixes the coefficient field, so the composite has the same structural map as the graph morphism. On the original coordinate block, it pulls back each variable to the same original variable. On the graph coordinate block, it pulls each variable back to the polynomial of the specified function. Passing through the identifications of polynomials with sections gives respectively the original coordinates and the specified functions restricted to the basic open. The two morphisms therefore agree on every coordinate and on the structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_base_comp: The image of a point of the subset under the composite is obtained by first taking its image under the first map and then under the second. Each point in the iterated image arises in this way, so the images are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_basicOpen_spec_map_ringEquiv: A target prime is the contraction of a unique prime under the ring isomorphism. It contains the original element exactly when the corresponding prime contains its image. Passing to the complements gives equality of the basic opens under the map on spectra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_hom_eq_preimage_inv: A target point is the image of a source point in the open exactly when its inverse image under the isomorphism lies in the open. Thus the image of the open is its inverse image under the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_hom_preimage_eq: Every point in the inverse image of the open maps into the open. Conversely, each point of the open has a preimage under the isomorphism, and that preimage lies in the inverse image open. Hence the image is the whole open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_spec_map_ringEquiv: A ring equivalence induces an isomorphism of spectra in the reverse direction. The inverse is induced by the inverse ring equivalence, since both composites take spectra of identity maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_basicOpenToSpecGraphAlge: The map consists of the basic-open inclusion followed by the affine-space identification with its polynomial spectrum and the isomorphism induced by the graph ring equivalence. An open immersion followed by isomorphisms is an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_specGraphAwayToSpecGraph: The map is induced by localizing the graph algebra at the minor determinant. On spectra, localization at one element is an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.jacobianMatrixOfSections_apply: The matrix is defined by taking the polynomial corresponding to the column's section and differentiating it with respect to the row's selected variable in the second block.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_polynomi: The polynomial of the section is obtained by applying the inverse of the polynomial-to-section equivalence. Applying the forward equivalence recovers the original section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_base_comp: A point lies in the range of the composite exactly when it is the second map's image of a point in the first map's range. This gives equality of the two sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_specGraphAwayToSpecGraphAlgebra_eq: The localization map has image the basic open of the graph minor determinant. The Jacobian basic open in affine space becomes the basic open of its polynomial determinant under the affine polynomial spectrum identification. The graph algebra isomorphism then sends it to the basic open of the graph minor, because the block determinant calculation identifies the two polynomials under that isomorphism. Thus both maps have the same image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_graphMorphismToAffineSpace_basicO: The selected variable map is injective because it preserves the original block and is injective on the added block. The localized graph algebra is standard smooth for this choice, so the induced affine morphism is smooth. The graph morphism on the Jacobian basic open is this smooth morphism composed with isomorphisms at source and target. Hence it is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specGraphAwayIsoBasicOpen_inv_comp: The isomorphism identifies two open immersions with the same image, so it is over their common target. The inverse followed by the localization immersion is therefore the immersion from the Jacobian basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumVariableMap_injective: The map preserves which block an index belongs to. Within the first block it preserves the index itself. Within the second it applies the given injection. Equal outputs therefore come from equal indices in either block.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.colon_eq_top_of_comap_le: If the colon ideal were proper, choose a point of the target affine chart lying in none of its basic opens. Lift that point by surjectivity and choose an affine neighborhood of the lift inside the inverse image of the target chart. The induced ring map is flat. The assumed containment of pulled-back ideals means that the image of the chosen element belongs to the extension of the second ideal. By the flat colon calculation, the extension of the colon ideal contains one. Its generators’ basic opens therefore cover the source chart, including the lifted point. The corresponding original basic open then contains the target point, contrary to its choice. Thus the colon ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_comap_eq: Equality of the pulled-back ideals gives inclusion in each direction after pullback. Flat surjective pullback reflects these inclusions, so the original ideal sheaves are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_basicOpen_of_span_eq_top: The chosen point of the affine open corresponds to a proper prime of its section ring. If the point lay in none of the basic opens of the given sections, that prime would contain all the sections and therefore the ideal they generate. This would make it contain the unit ideal, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_not_mem_basicOpen_of_ne_top: A proper ideal of the affine coordinate ring is contained in a maximal ideal. Take the corresponding prime point of the affine open. Every element of the original ideal belongs to this prime, so the point lies in none of their basic opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_appLE: A flat scheme morphism is characterized on affine charts by flatness of the corresponding ring maps. Apply that affine criterion to the given source chart lying over the given target chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_comap_le: On an affine target chart take an element of the first ideal. The colon ideal consisting of its multipliers into the second ideal is the unit ideal by the flat surjective calculation. In particular one is such a multiplier, so the element already belongs to the second ideal. This gives inclusion on every affine chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_mem_map_colon_of_mem_map: The colon ideal is the kernel of multiplication by the given element followed by the quotient by the ideal. Tensor this exact kernel sequence with the flat target algebra. The tensor of the two units lies in the kernel of the resulting multiplication and quotient map, since the image of the given element belongs to the extended ideal and annihilates the tensor of the quotient unit. Thus the tensor of the units is in the image of the extended colon ideal. Under the identification of the tensor product of the target algebra with the base ring with the target algebra itself, that image lies in the extended colon ideal. The tensor of the units corresponds to one, proving the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_ker_pullback_fst: The pullback ideal defines the base change of the closed subscheme along the morphism. Its ideal is the kernel of the resulting closed immersion, which is the first pullback projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_map_eq_map_comap_of_isPullback: Form the closed subscheme defined by the ideal and pull its inclusion back to the new source. Pasting the two pullback squares shows that its map to the new target is the flat base change of the original closed subscheme’s map to the old target. This original map is quasi-compact, so its kernel commutes with flat base change. The two kernels describe the pullback of the old image ideal and the image of the pulled-back ideal, respectively.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_map_eq_self_of_isPullback: Flat base change on the self-pullback identifies the pullback of the image ideal with the image along the second projection of the ideal pulled back along the first. By assumption the two pulled-back ideals agree. The desired equality thus reduces to taking the image along the second projection of the ideal pulled back along it. One containment is the unit of the ideal pullback and image adjunction. For the other, pull the adjunction counit back along the diagonal section of the projection. Because the projection after this section is the identity, the resulting containment is the reverse one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_ker: The image operation on ideal sheaves is defined by taking the kernel of the closed subscheme inclusion followed by the given morphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coprodDesc_strictTransformToBase_inactiv: Check the two summands of the total space. The projection of the induced blowup sequence restricts to the strict-transform map on the first summand and to the inactive map by definition on the second. The coproduct universal property then identifies the projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInl_inactiveTotalMap: Restrict the successor comparison to the old summand. By its coproduct description, this is the preceding comparison followed by the inclusion of the earlier target coproduct into the later target coproduct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_detachedCoprodMapOfLE: The inclusion of the new summand is the inclusion of the piece detached at this step into the successor coproduct. Composing with the map to the later stage gives the corresponding inclusion there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_inactiveTotalMap: Restrict the successor comparison to the new summand. Its coproduct description gives the comparison of the newly detached scheme followed by that piece's inclusion in the reindexed coproduct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_detachedCoprodInl_detac: The inclusion of an old detached piece into the successor coproduct first includes it in the preceding coproduct and then includes that coproduct as the old summand. Passing from the successor to the later coproduct gives the inclusion of the same piece at the later stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inactiveTotalMap: Apply the inductive description of the inactive comparison on each detached summand to the specified stage and summand index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inactiveTotalToBase: The inactive map to the base is the detached-summand inclusion followed by the projection of the induced blowup sequence. On a piece detached at an earlier stage, that projection factors through the strict transform at the stage of detachment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inr_totalSpaceMap: On the inactive summand the total space comparison is the inactive comparison followed by the target inclusion. Restrict that comparison to the specified detached scheme using its summand formula, then compose with the inclusion into the target total space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_detachedToCoprod_inactiveTotalMap: Induct on the stage of the coproduct. The initial coproduct has no earlier index. At a successor, a piece from a strictly earlier stage factors through the old summand. Apply the induction hypothesis there and compose the inclusion of the corresponding piece with the map to the larger target coproduct. For the piece detached at the current step, the restriction to the new summand gives the asserted formula directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_isEmpty_of_comm_inactiveTotalToBa: Induct on the number of detached stages in the coproduct. At zero, any source mapping to the empty coproduct is empty. At a successor, the pullback of the older coproduct is empty by induction and the pullback of the new piece is empty by the criterion for omitted stages. Base change of their coproduct is the coproduct of these two empty pullbacks, using the summand description of the map to the base. A scheme with the stated compatible maps maps to this empty coproduct, so it is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inactiveTotalMap_succ_eq_desc: At a successor, the recursive map is defined on the old summand by the preceding comparison followed by the map to the later coproduct. On the new summand it compares the detached piece and includes it at the reindexed stage. Identifying the source with this coproduct gives the stated map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inactiveTotalToBase_succ_eq_desc: For each earlier detached piece, both routes through the old summand map it to the base through its strict transform at detachment. The old summand therefore retains its preceding base map. On the new summand the base map is its detachment inclusion followed by that stage's strict-transform projection. These restrictions determine the map on the successor coproduct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_detachedCoprodMapOfLE: Check the two maps on each piece of the older coproduct. Including that piece first in the successor and then in the later stage gives its inclusion at the later stage. The direct map from the older coproduct has the same restriction. Thus the maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalSpaceMap: Restrict the coproduct comparison to the strict-transform summand. This gives the strict-transform comparison followed by the corresponding target inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inr_detachedCoprodMapOfLE: The second inclusion inserts the newly detached piece into the successor coproduct. The map to the later coproduct carries this inclusion to the inclusion of the same piece there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_of_comm_detachedScheme_of_not_me: Compose the given compatibility over the original base with the original base embedding. The strict-transform projection through its ambient stage and the square of base embeddings turn this into compatibility over the ambient base, with the map to the new base followed by its embedding. The emptiness criterion for an omitted detached piece now applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_of_comm_inactiveTotalToBase_of_n: Every summand is indexed by an existing stage omitted by the reindexing, by the two assumptions on the indices. Apply the preceding induction criterion to the compatible pair of maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isEmpty_of_hom_to_initial: A map to the initial scheme induces a function from the source's underlying space to the empty set. Thus the source has no points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_detachedCoprodMapOfLE_inactiv: Induct from the initial stage of the interval to its endpoint. At the initial stage the coproduct map is the identity, so the starting square is the given pullback. At a successor the new detached piece is omitted by the reindexing, so it has empty pullback. The successor map to the base is the coproduct of the previous base map and that piece's map. Its pullback is therefore still represented by the preceding pullback, with the first projection followed by the inclusion of the old summand. This inclusion extends the coproduct map through the successor and proves the induction step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_inactiveSchemeMap_baseMap: Paste the pullback square comparing the detached schemes inside their strict transforms with the pullback square comparing the strict transforms over the bases. The resulting projections are the detachment inclusions followed by the strict-transform projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_inactiveTotalMap: Induct on the source stage. At zero the source coproduct is empty, and every target summand before the initial reindexed stage is omitted. Their pullback is empty, so the two unique projections from the initial scheme give the desired square. At a successor take the coproduct of the previous comparison square and the square for the newly detached piece. This gives a pullback up to the stage just after that piece in the original sequence. Any remaining intervening stages are omitted, so including their pieces preserves the pullback. On the old and new summands the resulting first projection gives the two defining restrictions of the successor comparison, which identifies the resulting square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_fst_eq: Replace the first projection by its equal map in the given pullback square. The universal property stays the same.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_fst_eq_of_snd_eq: Use the two equalities to replace both projections of the given pullback. The same universal property proves the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_snd_eq_of_map_eq: Substitute the equal second projection and the equal map from the first target to the base. This gives exactly the given pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_strictTransformComparison_str: Paste the pullback square for the strict-transform inclusions with the pullback square for the ambient stage projections. Identify the vertical composites as the strict-transform projections followed by the base embeddings. The square for those embeddings is a pullback, and the strict-transform projections commute with the comparison maps. Pullback cancellation therefore gives the desired square over the bases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_totalSpaceMap: The strict-transform comparison and the inactive comparison each give pullback squares over the same map of bases. Take their coproduct on each side. The resulting projections are the projections of the induced blowup sequences, since those restrict to the two component maps. Its comparison is the total space map by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_le_reindex_succ: The bound on the successor places the preceding stage strictly before the end of the sequence. Strict increase of the reindexing across this step gives the required weak inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_lt_reindex: The comparison reindexing is strictly increasing on the stages under consideration. Both given indices are in that range, so it preserves their strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reindex_lt_reindex_succ: The bound on the successor places the preceding stage strictly before the end of the sequence. Apply strict increase of the reindexing across this step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformComparison_comp_strictTra: Postcompose both maps to the original base with its closed immersion into the ambient base. On the first route, express the strict-transform projection through its ambient stage, then commute the strict-transform comparison with the stage inclusions. The ambient stage pullback square commutes with the ambient projections. On the second route, the projection through the new ambient stage agrees with the strict-transform projection followed by the new base embedding, and the comparison square of base embeddings commutes. The postcomposites agree, so cancel the original base embedding, which is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceMap_eq_coprodMap: The total space is the coproduct of the strict transform and accumulated detached pieces. Its comparison is defined as the coproduct map of the strict-transform comparison and the inactive comparison.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_hom_comap_inv: Successive pullback of ideals is pullback along the composite. A comparison isomorphism and its inverse compose to the identity, which pulls the ideal back to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_inv_comap_hom: Successive pullback of ideals is pullback along the composite. The inverse comparison and the forward comparison compose to the identity in this order as well, so the ideal returns to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_map_of_comm_iso: For the first containment, use the image–pullback adjunction on one vertical map. Functoriality and commutativity of the square turn the resulting containment into the pullback of the adjunction counit for the other vertical map. Apply this same containment to the square with the horizontal isomorphisms reversed. Pull it back along the forward isomorphism and cancel the inverse pullbacks to obtain the opposite containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_totalCenter: The total center is obtained by mapping the center off the detached locus along the strict-transform inclusion. Pull its ideal back along the total space comparison. The commutative square of strict-transform inclusions permits this pullback to pass through the image, and the established comparison of the centers on the strict transforms identifies the result with the other total center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInl_inactiveTotalIso_hom: The recursive detached-coproduct comparison is taken summand by summand. Its restriction to the old detached coproduct is therefore the preceding comparison followed by the old-summand inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_inactiveTotalIso_hom: The recursive detached-coproduct comparison is taken summand by summand. Its restriction to the newly detached piece is therefore the comparison of that piece followed by its inclusion on the other side.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_detachedCoprod_compatible: Construct the isomorphism by induction on the stage. At stage zero, both detached coproducts are empty, so use the unique isomorphism between them. At a successor stage each detached coproduct consists of the preceding detached coproduct and the piece detached at this step. Take the coproduct of the inductive isomorphism and the given comparison on the new piece. Its restrictions to the two summands are exactly the required comparison maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowupsWithoutIso_isomorphic: The induced blowup sequences are isomorphic before removing steps. The operation of deleting blowups whose center ideal is the unit ideal preserves isomorphism of sequences, giving the required result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_isomorphic: The two compositions have equal length. Use the total space isomorphism at each stage. At the initial stage the strict-transform comparison respects the map to the base and the detached summand is empty. At each later step the total space isomorphisms respect the transition maps and pull back the corresponding center ideals. These data give the sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalSpaceIso_hom: The total space comparison is the coproduct map of the strict-transform and detached-piece comparisons. Restricting this map to the strict-transform summand gives its comparison followed by the corresponding inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inr_totalSpaceIso_hom: The total space comparison is the coproduct map of the strict-transform and detached-piece comparisons. Restricting this map to the detached summand gives its comparison followed by the corresponding inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_length_of_le_length: The two sequences have equal length. Replacing the length in the given weak inequality gives the required weak inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lt_length_of_lt_length: The two sequences have equal length. Replacing the length in the given strict inequality gives the required strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceIso_hom_eq_coprodMap: At each stage the total space is the coproduct of the strict transform and the accumulated detached pieces. Its comparison isomorphism was defined as the coproduct of the two comparison isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceIso_hom_totalTransition: Compare the composites first on the strict-transform summand, where they agree by compatibility of the strict-transform transitions. On the prior detached coproduct the transition preserves each old piece, and the restriction of its comparison is the preceding detached-coproduct comparison. On the newly detached piece the two composites agree by compatibility with its detachment inclusion into the preceding strict transform. The coproduct universal property gives the equality on the total space.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_of_isIso: An isomorphism is an open immersion, and open immersions are flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleSpace_affineSpaceIndexedBy: A field is an integral domain, and the polynomial ring over it is an integral domain for any set of variables. The corresponding affine scheme has irreducible underlying space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIndependentOfPresentedEmbedding_of_loc: Take any two admissible embeddings of the same scheme and their affine-space presentations. The comparison theorem using the two codimension hypotheses gives an isomorphism of their resolution sequences. This gives independence for every such pair.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_embeddedResolutionRuleOfPrinc:
Enlarge each of the two ambient schemes to its given affine-space presentation and then to the common affine space with both blocks of coordinates. Each embedding used for enlargement is closed and over the field. The componentwise nonvanishing condition persists under composition, and every new ambient space is smooth with empty strict normal crossing boundary. The codimension comparison gives the required positive étale coordinate codimension at each enlargement, using the complementary block for the standard linear inclusions. The enlargement theorem gives an isomorphism of resolution sequences at each step.

The two composite embeddings into the common affine space are the coordinate maps obtained by appending zero coordinates in the other block. The assumed comparison by an ambient automorphism identifies these coordinate maps over the field, so the two sequences in the common affine space are isomorphic by invariance under ambient isomorphisms. Compose this middle isomorphism with the enlargement isomorphisms and the inverses of those on the second side.

The inverse ambient isomorphism identifies the two embeddings over the field and gives a pullback square with the identity of the embedded scheme. It is flat, so the kernel ideal of the new embedding is the pullback of the old one. It is also smooth, so smooth functoriality of principalization applies to this ideal and the empty boundary. Substituting the equality of input ideals gives the pullback comparison of ambient blowup sequences. The chart comparison for the pullback then gives a pullback comparison of induced resolution sequences over the identity after deleting unit-center steps. Every remaining center in the original sequence is proper, so the comparison over the identity is an isomorphism. Reverse its direction to obtain the stated comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_affineSpaceIndexedBy: The structural map for a finite coordinate set corresponds to a polynomial algebra over the field on finitely many variables. That algebra is of finite type, so the map is locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationAlgorithm_toSequenceOfBl: Substitute the equalities of the ideals and of the ordered boundaries. The algorithm then receives the same mathematical inputs, so its output sequence is the same.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec: The structural map of affine space to the field spectrum is affine, since it is induced by the inclusion of the field in the polynomial algebra. Affine morphisms are quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec_finSum: Reindex the disjoint union of the two coordinate sets by a single set of size the sum of their sizes. This gives an isomorphism over the field, since its inverse reindexes by the inverse bijection and both composites fix every coordinate. The structural map is the composite of this isomorphism and the smooth structural map for the single coordinate set. It is therefore smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIndependentOfPresentedEmbedding_embedd: Apply the embedding-independence criterion using smoothness of affine space and the assumed comparison by ambient automorphisms. Its two coordinate hypotheses follow from the smooth-to-étale codimension comparison and the codimension computations for the two standard linear embeddings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearEmbeddingsHaveLocallyConstCodim_of: For arbitrary dimensions, the two standard inclusions into the larger affine space have smooth coordinate presentations in the complementary coordinates. The codimension results for the first and second inclusion give the two demanded statements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyConstCodimImpliesConstantCodim: Take a smooth ambient scheme, the given immersion, and smooth local coordinates in which it has the specified number of defining coordinates. The comparison of smooth coordinate charts with étale coordinate charts gives the étale coordinate codimension with that same number.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_center_eq_top_of_not_mem_range_rei: Suppose a point of the base-changed total space lies over the total center. Its downstairs image lies in the closed image of the center off the detached locus in the strict-transform summand. The resulting strict-transform point lies over the original ambient center. The pullback equation over the original scheme, the commuting embedding square, and compatibility of the strict-transform projection with the ambient projection give compatible points in the new ambient base and the original ambient stage. Lift them to the ambient stage pullback. This lift belongs to the pulled-back ambient center support, which is empty because the stage was omitted. Thus the pulled-back total center support is empty and its ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.congr_hom_apply: Equal scheme morphisms give equal maps on points. Evaluate the equality at the chosen point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowupsIso_hom_fst: The isomorphism identifies the induced stage with the pullback of the corresponding original induced stage. Its first projection is the induced projection to the new base by the defining pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowupsIso_hom_snd: Under the pullback isomorphism, the second projection is the comparison from the new total space to the corresponding original total space. This is its defining second projection equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inr_totalSpaceMap: The total-space comparison is defined on the detached coproduct by its comparison map followed by inclusion of the detached summand downstairs. Restricting the coproduct map to that summand yields the stated formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_inducedBlowupsW: The full induced sequences have the pullback comparison up to empty centers. The shortening theorem for this comparison removes unit-center steps from both sequences and yields the asserted pullback of their shortened sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackUpToEmptyCenters_inducedBlowup: Use the ambient reindexing and the total-space pullback isomorphisms at each stage. The induced sequences have the corresponding ambient lengths, so the indexing inequalities and final-index equality hold. Every omitted original center has unit pullback by the support argument. The first projection gives compatibility with the new base. The transition equation follows by checking both pullback projections. The first agrees by structural-map compatibility, and the second agrees by the total-space transition calculation. Finally the total centers are corresponding pullbacks by the center comparison. These are exactly the pullback conditions up to empty centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.levelMap_succ_comp_transitionMap: The pullback square for the retained step says that the new successor comparison followed by the original transition across the omitted stages and the retained blowup equals the new blowdown followed by the old comparison. The original transitions compose to the full transition between retained indices. Substituting gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformComparison_succ_comp_stri: Postcompose the two maps with the closed inclusion of the earlier strict transform. Compatibility of the strict-transform inclusions with their comparisons and with the ambient transitions reduces both composites to the same ambient map by the stage comparison equation. The closed inclusion is a monomorphism, so the original maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalCenter_eq_comap: Restrict the two ideals to the strict-transform summand. The total centers restrict there to the centers off the detached loci, and their equality after pulling back follows from the flat comparison of those centers. On the already detached summand both ideals are unit, because the total-space comparison sends that summand into the downstairs detached coproduct and the centers have empty restriction there. Equality on both summands gives equality on the total space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalTransition_comp_totalSpaceMap: Check the two composites on the new strict transform and each detached summand. On the strict transform equality is the compatibility of the strict-transform comparisons with the retained transitions. A piece detached earlier travels through the preceding detached coproduct under the new transition. Its corresponding piece downstairs also stays in the detached coproduct throughout the intervening stages, so both paths give its earlier comparison. A newly detached piece maps into the preceding new strict transform. Downstairs its corresponding piece detaches at the retained index and the iterated transition takes it back into that strict transform. Compatibility of the detached comparison with its inclusion makes these two composites agree. The coproduct property gives equality on the total space.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.AffineResolutionRule.center_ne_top: The identity is an open immersion and preserves the structure map. Compatibility of the affine rule therefore gives a pullback comparison of its output sequence with itself over the identity. The preceding result excludes unit centers at every actual stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_isPullbackSequenceOfBlo: The reindexing of a pullback comparison of a sequence with itself is strictly increasing and fixes the final index. A forward induction shows each reindexed index is at least the original one. An induction backwards from the final stage gives the reverse bound, because advancing by one index increases the reindexed index by at least one. Thus every actual center index is matched. By the comparison's support condition the pulled-back center at each matched index has a point in its support. The pullback of a unit ideal has empty support, so none of the centers is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedRuleCompatibleWithFieldExtension: Choose a surjective étale affine cover of the original scheme whose extension is a surjective étale affine cover of the extended scheme. On the extended cover, compare the sequence obtained by two successive strict pullbacks of the global sequence with the affine rule's output obtained by extending the affine output on the original cover. Both are strict pullbacks from the original global sequence along the same composite, by the compatibility of the induced rule with covers and of the affine rule with field extension. Hence they are isomorphic. Delete unit-center steps on both sides. The affine output already has proper centers by open-immersion compatibility, so the deletion preserves it up to isomorphism. The induced rule on the extended scheme also pulls back to that affine output. Descent of an isomorphism along the faithfully flat cover identifies the extended global sequence with the base change of the original sequence after deletion of unit centers. Base change followed by this deletion is a pullback comparison of the required type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_comap_top: Pullback carries the unit ideal to the unit ideal. Its support is empty, so no point lies in that support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_mem_irreducibleComponent_iff_of_fl: The underlying map of a flat morphism is generalizing. Apply the component criterion for generalizing maps to the specified component and point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_mem_irreducibleComponent_iff_of_ge: Suppose the image of the point lies in the specified irreducible component. Its generic point generalizes the image point, so the generalizing property lifts it to a generalization of the source point. Choose an irreducible component through this lifted point. It is closed, so it contains the original point as well. The closure of its image is irreducible by continuity and contains the target generic point, hence contains the whole target component. Maximality of that target component forces equality. Conversely, if the original point belongs to a component with this image closure, its image lies in the closure and thus in the specified component.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.withoutIsoBlow: Surjectivity of the base map makes every stage comparison surjective, so a center is unit upstairs exactly when it is unit downstairs. The two shortening procedures keep the same indices and give equal lengths. At a retained index use the old comparison followed by the identification with the corresponding retained index downstairs. Compatibility at zero follows from the old comparison square for projection to the base. Each shortened transition is an old transition across the corresponding interval. Its comparison square is a pullback by pasting old successor squares and identifying stages. The shortened center equation is the original equation at the retained index. These give a strict pullback of the shortened sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.Isomorphic.withoutIsoB: View the original isomorphism as a strict pullback comparison over the identity of the base. The identity is surjective, so removing unit-center steps preserves the strict comparison. Compare this shortened sequence with the identity strict pullback of the second shortened sequence. Uniqueness of strict pullbacks gives the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_eqToHom: Identify the two equal indices. The centers now coincide and the transport is the identity, whose pullback leaves the ideal unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_comap_comp_eqToHom: Identify the equal stage indices. The transport map is then the identity, so the pullback along the indicated composite reduces to the assumed center equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_projectionToBase: Once the equal indices are identified, the transport map is the identity at that stage. Composing the identity with the projection gives the same projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToHom_comp_transitionMap: Identify both pairs of equal indices. The two transport maps are identities and the underlying transitions are the same, so the composites agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_eqToHom_right: Identify the equal objects on the right. The transport maps become identities, and the given equation identifies the two right-hand morphisms. The resulting square is the original pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_id_of_: Use the stage isomorphisms as comparison morphisms. The initial equation gives compatibility over the identity of the common base, and every commuting transition square with the two horizontal isomorphisms is a pullback. The center equations are exactly those already known for the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lengthWithoutIsoBlowups_congr: Apply the length comparison in each direction, reversing the hypotheses on equal lengths and corresponding unit centers for the reverse comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lengthWithoutIsoBlowups_le_of_center_eq_: The retained-index functions agree. If the first shortened length were greater than the second, at the second shortened length the first retained value would still lie below the common original length. But the second retained value there has reached the original length, contradicting equality of the functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_congr: The two sequences have the same length and the same unit center positions. Apply the comparison inequality in each direction to get equality of the two search results.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_le_of_center_eq_top_: The index chosen by the search in the second sequence is at least the starting index. If it reaches the common length it is an admissible endpoint in the first sequence. Otherwise its center is nonunit in the second sequence and hence also in the first. It is therefore an admissible search result for the first sequence, whose least result is at most this index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_congr: Both first retained indices are the results of equal searches from zero. If the current retained indices agree, the searches for the next ones start at the same successor and again agree. Induction proves equality of the retained-index functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_eq_eqToHom: After identifying the two stage indices, the sequence transition is the identity. Transport along this stage equality is the identity as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_isomorphic_self: Every index is an admissible result for the search starting there, because it either precedes the end and has a nonunit center or is at least the length. The least result is therefore exactly the starting index. Induction makes the retained-index function the identity, and the shortened length equals the original one. Use the resulting stage identifications as isomorphisms. The formulas for the shortened initial map, transitions, and centers then reduce to those of the original sequence under the same stage identifications.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_isoHom_eq_top_iff: Pullback of the unit ideal is unit. Conversely, if the pullback is unit, pull it back along the inverse isomorphism. This leaves the unit ideal on that side, while the two successive pullbacks of the original ideal compose to pullback along the identity. Thus the original ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_nontrivialIndex_eq_of_center_ne_t: The final retained index is the length and is greater than the given index. Take the first retained value strictly greater than it. This cannot be the first retained value, since all indices before that value have unit centers. The previous retained value is at most the given index by minimality. If it were smaller, the given index would lie in the gap between two successive retained values, where all centers are unit. Thus the previous retained value equals the given index, and its enumeration position is strictly before the shortened length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_withoutIsoBl: Use the retained indices of the upstairs sequence and the original stagewise pullback comparisons at those indices. These indices strictly increase, and the final one is the common original length. In each original stage the upstairs center is identified with the pullback center under the comparison isomorphism. Its being nonunit is therefore equivalent to nonempty support on the canonical pullback. The retained-index result says exactly that these steps are kept. The first projection of each stage comparison is the shortened projection to the base. For consecutive shortened stages, compare the two transition composites on both pullback projections. On the first, the projection to the base is preserved. On the second, the pasted strict pullback squares for the old interval give the needed equation. The center condition is the old one at the retained index, so all pullback conditions hold.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_nonempty_iff_ne_top: The support is empty exactly for the unit ideal. Negating this equality is precisely the equivalence between nonempty support and being nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_projectionToBase: The shortened projection goes from the retained stage to the first retained stage and then to the base by the projection from that first stage. The original tower’s projection compatibility identifies this composite with the original projection from the specified retained stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_baseFieldToGlobalSections: A scalar section pulls back from the field. Pulling it back further along the given map is pullback from the field along the composite structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseFieldToGlobalSections_apply: First view the scalar as a section on the field spectrum. Pull back that section along the structural map to obtain its constant section on the scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseFieldToGlobalSections_neg: The assignment of scalar sections is a ring homomorphism, so it preserves additive inverses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ker_coproductSliceMap_eq_of_le_sli: Since the target open lies in one separating open, its inverse image under the coproduct map consists entirely of points from the designated summand. The open immersion of that summand's inverse image and the full inverse image inclusion have the same image in the coproduct, so their source schemes are isomorphic over it. Under this isomorphism both maps restricted to the target open agree by the formula on the summand. The maps are quasi-compact, so restriction pulls back their kernel ideals to the kernels of the restricted maps. Those kernels agree because the maps differ only by an isomorphism of sources.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_sliceSepara: First pull the separating section back to the slice, where it is the scalar product of differences. The remaining pullback along the summand embedding sends that scalar to its section for the summand's composite structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.componentIsoSliceOpen_hom_comp_ι: The chosen isomorphism identifies the two open immersions into the coproduct. Its forward map followed by the inverse image open inclusion is therefore the original summand inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.componentIsoSliceOpen_hom_comp_ι_assoc: Compose the identity over the coproduct with the given morphism. The two resulting composites are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coproductSliceMapReindexed_comp_affineSp: The coordinate reindexing isomorphism preserves the field projection. Thus the reindexed map has the same structural composite as the original coproduct slice map, which is the given structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coproductSliceMap_base_sigma_ι: The coproduct map restricts to the composite of the specified embedding and the slice inclusion on that summand. Evaluating this equality on the given point gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coproductSliceMap_comp_affineSpaceIndexe: On each summand the slice inclusion preserves the structure map to the field. Composing the coproduct map with that projection thus gives the prescribed structural map on every summand. The coproduct universal property gives equality of the whole maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coproduct_globalSections_ext: Use the two sections as coordinates of maps from the coproduct to the affine line over the given base map. The restrictions to each summand agree because they have the same structural map and equal coordinates. The coproduct universal property makes the two maps equal. Pulling back the line coordinate recovers equality of the two sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_componentSliceOpen: The summand inclusion and the inclusion of the inverse image open are both open immersions into the coproduct. Their images agree, so there is an isomorphism between their sources over the coproduct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_sliceAtLastCoord: Construct the map over the field with the old coordinates in the first block and the given scalar in the last coordinate. Its first projection is the identity because it has the original structure map and coordinates. Every source coordinate therefore has a lift to a target coordinate, so the affine closed immersion criterion applies. The pullback of the last coordinate is the chosen scalar section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_translateLastCoord: Use the affine-space map defined by the original structural map, the original first-block coordinates, and the original last coordinate plus the given scalar section. The coordinate rule for the resulting map gives the required structural and pullback identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_comp_sliceAtLastCoor: First add one zero coordinate to the given immersion, which raises its smooth coordinate codimension by one. Then translate the new coordinate to the desired scalar. Translation is an isomorphism over the field, so it preserves coordinate codimension. The composite is the slice immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_coproductSliceMap: A point of the coproduct lies in a summand. Choose a smooth coordinate chart about its image for that summand's slice, which has codimension one more than the original embedding. Intersect the chart with the corresponding separating open, which still contains the point. The restricted chart remains smooth and over the field. On this smaller open the kernel of the coproduct map agrees with the kernel of the summand slice, so the same coordinate equations give the required codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_coproductSliceMapRei: The coproduct slice map is a closed immersion of coordinate codimension one more than that of its summands. Reindexing the coordinates is an isomorphism over the field, so it preserves that codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_coproductSliceMap: The finite coproduct of affine schemes is affine. To lift any section on it, first restrict the section to each summand and lift that restriction to a section on the original affine space using its closed immersion. Pull these lifts back to the product and weight each by its Lagrange basis section in the last coordinate. On the assigned slice only the designated lift remains. Pulling back to each summand therefore recovers the prescribed restriction, so the interpolated section pulls back to the original section on the coproduct. The resulting surjection on global sections gives a closed immersion of affine schemes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_sliceAtLastCoord: The chosen slice is the closed immersion from the coordinate construction. Its first-block coordinates lift every source coordinate, giving the closed immersion property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_sliceSeparatingOpen: On its own summand the separating section is the image of the product of differences from all other slice values. Those differences are nonzero by injectivity of the labels, so the product is a unit in the field. Its pullback is a unit, and its basic open is the whole summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_mem_sliceSeparatingOpen_of_ne: On a different summand, one factor of the separating section subtracts that summand's own slice value and is zero. The pulled-back section is zero, whose basic open is empty. Thus the image of the given point cannot lie in the separating open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_sliceSeparatingOpen_of_ne: On a different summand the product defining the pulled-back separating section contains its own slice value minus itself, which is zero. Its basic open is empty, so the inverse image is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_sliceSeparatingOpen_self: On the designated summand the separating section is the scalar product of differences from all other slice values. The factors are nonzero by injectivity, so the section is a unit. The inverse image of the basic open is the basic open of this unit and equals the whole summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_translateLastCoord_inl: The defining vector retains all the original first-block coordinates, so the specified coordinate pulls back to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_coproductSliceMap: The restriction to each summand is a composite of closed immersions and hence quasi-compact. The inverse image of a quasi-compact target open is the union of the images under the summand inclusions of the corresponding inverse images. Each is compact because the restriction is quasi-compact and the inclusion is continuous. There are finitely many summands, so the entire inverse image is compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_sigma_ι_eq_range_componentSliceOpe: Every point of the specified summand lands in the inverse image of its separating open because that inverse image is the whole summand there. Conversely every point of the coproduct belongs to a summand, and a different summand has empty inverse image of the separating open. Thus the open consists exactly of the image of the specified summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigma_ι_base_jointly_surjective: The underlying set of the scheme coproduct is the disjoint union of the underlying sets of the summands. Each point therefore comes from a point in one summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigma_ι_comp_coproductSliceMap_appTop_sl: Replace the map from the specified summand by its embedding followed by its slice. Pullback of the separating section along that composite is the scalar section of the product of differences evaluated at its slice value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigma_ι_coproductSliceMap: The coproduct map is defined on each summand by its embedding into the first affine block followed by its assigned slice inclusion. Restricting it to the given summand recovers that composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigma_ι_coproductSliceMap_assoc: Compose the formula for restriction to a summand with the given target morphism. Associativity gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_baseFieldToGloba: A slice inclusion is over the field, so pulling back a scalar section gives the section of the same scalar for the slice's structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_lagrangeSection: On the chosen slice the last coordinate is its assigned field element. Evaluate the Lagrange basis polynomial there. On its own slice every factor in the normalizing product is nonzero because the assigned scalars are distinct. The evaluated product cancels its inverse, giving one. On a different slice, the product includes the factor obtained by subtracting that slice's own scalar, so it is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_lastCoordinate: The slice sets the last coordinate to the given scalar. Its pullback sends that coordinate to the corresponding constant section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_pullbackAlongPro: The slice inclusion followed by first projection is the identity. Pulling a section back along that projection and then along the slice inclusion gives the original section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_sliceSeparatingF: Pullback preserves the finite product and differences. On the chosen slice the last coordinate becomes its assigned scalar, while each scalar section remains the corresponding scalar section. Thus the pulled-back product is the section of the stated product of scalar differences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_appTop_sum_mul_lagrange: Pull the sum back term by term. The Lagrange section vanishes on the chosen slice for every other index and equals one for the chosen index. The remaining coefficient, pulled back from the first projection, restricts to the originally assigned section on that slice.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_comp_affineSpaceIndexed: The slice was constructed over the field with the source structure map. Composing its embedding with the larger space's structure map gives the source structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_comp_projLeft: Projection to the first block recovers the original coordinate vector and the original structural map. Hence it is the identity after the slice inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_comp_projLeft_assoc: The slice inclusion followed by first projection is the identity. Composing this with the given map gives the map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sliceAtLastCoord_eq_affineSpaceInl_comp_: Both maps preserve the field structure. Adding a zero coordinate preserves the first block, and translation leaves it unchanged. The last coordinate of the composite is zero plus the given scalar section. These are the same coordinate pullbacks as for the slice, so the maps are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoordIso_hom: The forward map of the isomorphism is by definition translation by the given scalar.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoordIso_inv: The inverse isomorphism is the translation by the negative scalar, whose composites with the forward map are identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoord_appTop_lastCoordinate: The last entry of the translation's defining vector is the original last coordinate plus the scalar section. That is its pullback of the last coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoord_comp_affineSpaceIndex: The translation is constructed over the original structural map to the field, which is therefore its composite with the target projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoord_comp_translateLastCoo: Both translations preserve the structural map and the first block of coordinates. They also fix scalar sections because they are over the field. The last coordinate is consequently translated by the given scalar and its negative in succession, recovering the original coordinate. Thus the composite is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.translateLastCoord_neg_comp_translateLas: Apply the cancellation identity to the negative scalar. The negative of that scalar is the original scalar, giving the opposite composition identity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_coord_inl_eq_C: The first block pulls back through the coefficient inclusion on global sections. The original coordinate therefore becomes its constant polynomial, viewed as a section on the spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_coord_inr_eq_X: The selected generators are the new polynomial variables. A second-block coordinate therefore pulls back to the section of its corresponding variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_ext: The maps on global sections agree on each section by hypothesis. Equality of ring maps follows from pointwise equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_surjective_of_isClosedImmersion: A closed subscheme of an affine scheme is affine and its coordinate ring is a quotient of the ambient coordinate ring. The map on global sections is that quotient map, so it is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_ΓSpecIso_inv_eq_mvPolynomialToSum: The map to the polynomial spectrum is induced by the sum coordinate ring map after the canonical affine identification. Pullback of the section of a polynomial along the map of spectra gives the section of its image by naturality. Pulling back along the affine identification then recovers that image as a section of the sum affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec_eq: The map from the polynomial spectrum is the extended coordinate map for the coefficient inclusion and the new polynomial variables. Its composite with the target structural map is the structure map through the original affine block, by the structural identity for extended coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_appTop_apply_eq: Pullback of sections along a composite is successive pullback in reverse order. Evaluate this functoriality identity on the given section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mvPolynomial_map_appTop_eq: The original embedding is a closed immersion into an affine scheme, so its map on sections is surjective. Changing polynomial coefficients along a surjection is surjective because each polynomial has finitely many coefficients to lift. Apply this to the indicated relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.globalSectionsToPolynomialRing_apply: The map includes the section ring as the coefficient ring. Thus each section is sent to its constant polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.id_appTop_apply: Pullback along the identity scheme map is the identity on global sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_appTop:
First pull the kernel back to the polynomial ring over the original affine-space sections. By the coordinate evaluation formula, it is the inverse image under coefficient change of the ideal of relations in the ambient section ring. The lifted relations map onto those generators. Since coefficient change is surjective, the inverse image is the ideal generated by the lifts plus the kernel of coefficient change. That kernel consists of polynomials whose coefficients lie in the original embedding ideal, so it is generated by the constant images of that ideal.

The map from this polynomial ring to the sum coordinate ring is surjective, so mapping the pulled-back kernel forward recovers the desired kernel.
