The lifted relations map to the stated section generators, and the constant embedding ideal maps to its extension along the first-block projection. This gives the sum in the statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSumCoordinateRing_C: Evaluation sends a coefficient to its pullback along the first projection. A constant polynomial therefore has exactly the stated image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSumCoordinateRing_X: Evaluation sends each new variable to its chosen section, which is the corresponding coordinate in the second block.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSumCoordinateRing_surjecti: Compose the map from the sum affine space to the polynomial spectrum with the extended coordinate map back to the sum space. The composite is over the field because coefficient inclusion followed by the sum coordinate map recovers the original structural pullback on field sections. Each original coordinate goes to its constant polynomial and then to the same first-block coordinate. Each added coordinate goes to its variable and then to the same second-block coordinate. Thus the composite is the identity by the coordinate characterization. For any section of the sum space, pull it back to the polynomial spectrum and regard it as a polynomial. The identity just established shows that this polynomial maps to the given section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_basicOpen_specToAffineSpaceExte: The inverse image of a basic open is the basic open of its pulled-back section. The pulled-back section is a unit, so this open is the whole source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMap_appTop_ΓSpecIso_inv: The identification of a ring with the global sections of its spectrum is natural. Under it, pullback along the map of spectra sends the section of the given element to the section of its image under the ring map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_appTop_mvP: A coefficient section enters the sum coordinate ring by first-block pullback. The projection identity then identifies its pullback on the source with the coefficient pulled back through the original ambient map and the given ring map. A new variable pulls back to its assigned generator. The formula follows on all polynomials because both operations preserve addition and multiplication.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_presentedLocalChart:
Start with the local smooth ambient lift at the chosen point, its affine open domain, and its affine-space presentations above the supplied threshold. The selected closed immersion of the source induces its topology, so choose a basic open in the source ambient scheme whose inverse image contains the point and lies inside the local domain. The function defining this smaller open restricts to a section on the original local domain. Lift that section to the affine space of the threshold presentation using the composite closed immersion of the local domain. Restrict the lift to the smooth ambient lift. Its basic open has inverse image in the local domain equal to the desired smaller open, because basic opens pull back by pulling back their defining functions.

The two resulting open subschemes of the source have the same image and hence are isomorphic over the source. Restrict the original pullback square to the lifted basic open and transfer it along this isomorphism. The restricted ambient remains affine and smooth with the required finiteness properties, and the restricted map of the smaller domain into it is a closed immersion. At every dimension above the threshold, present the lifted basic open in affine space by adjoining an extra coordinate for the inverse of its defining section. The basic-open presentation theorem increases the coordinate codimension by one and preserves compatibility over the field. These data give the requested chart.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpacePresentedSelection_selection: The presented selection is constructed using the affine-space embedding choice as its selection, so reading that component gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithFieldBaseChange_toAffine: Extend the chosen embedding to the larger field. The extended ambient scheme is smooth, so the empty boundary is in strict normal crossing position. The field projection is flat, which identifies the new kernel with the pullback of the old kernel and preserves nonvanishing on components. Thus the embedded rule's field compatibility gives a strict pullback for this extended embedding. Both the extended embedding and the selected embedding over the larger field have presentations by the selection data. Independence of presentations identifies their output sequences. Transport the strict pullback along this isomorphism to obtain field compatibility for the selected affine rule.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithEtaleCovers_toAffineReso: An étale cover is smooth of relative dimension zero, so the smooth pullback comparison gives a pullback of sequences. Since the cover is surjective and the original output has proper centers, the strict pullback criterion gives the required strict comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithOpenImmersions_toAffineR: An open immersion is smooth of relative dimension zero. The smooth pullback comparison for the presented selection therefore applies to every open immersion over the field and gives compatibility of the associated affine rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_presentedSelect:
Choose the surjective étale affine cover of the source with two presented embeddings, one pulled back from the target ambient scheme and the other from the source ambient scheme. Smooth ambient compatibility gives pullback comparisons from the two global sequences, over the composite to the target and over the cover to the source, respectively. Independence of presented embeddings identifies these two sequences on the cover. The comparison from the source is strict because the cover is surjective and the source rule has proper centers.

Base change the target sequence along the smooth map and delete unit-center steps. Its strict base change along the cover is another pullback of the target sequence along the composite, by composition of the two comparisons. Uniqueness identifies this sequence with the first cover sequence. It is therefore isomorphic to the strict pullback of the source sequence. Descent of the isomorphism along the faithfully flat cover identifies the source sequence with the target base change after deletion. Transporting the latter's pullback comparison gives the result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.iso_hom_comp_projectio: Both projections to the base are the transition to stage zero followed by the initial isomorphism. Compatibility with all transitions moves the stage isomorphism past the transition to zero. Compatibility at zero then identifies the remaining composite with the original projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.iso_hom_comp_transitio: Induct on the later endpoint starting from the earlier one. At equality both transitions are identities. At a successor factor each transition through the preceding endpoint. The successor square commutes by hypothesis, and the remaining square commutes by induction. Their composite gives the required equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_comp_projectionToBase: A successor morphism is the transition to the preceding stage. The compatibility of projections with transitions says that following it by the preceding projection gives the successor projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top: At the corresponding step the source center is the pullback of the target center. Pullback of the unit ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_iff: One direction follows because pullback preserves the unit ideal. For the reverse direction, the stage comparison is surjective as a base change of the surjective base map. If the source center is unit, the pullback of the original center is unit, so surjectivity forces the original center to be unit as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_ne_top_of_forall_center_ne_top: If an original center were the unit ideal, its pullback at the corresponding source step would be the unit ideal. The lengths agree, so this contradicts the nonunit hypothesis at that source step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp: The lengths agree by transitivity. Compose the stage comparisons. Their initial equations compose to the required initial equation. Pasting their successor pullback squares gives a pullback square for each composite comparison. The two center pullbacks compose to pullback along the same composite, furnishing the center equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_eq_top_of_comap_eq_top: The support of the pulled-back ideal is empty because it is the unit ideal. This support is the inverse image of the original support. Surjectivity would lift any point of the original support to this empty set, so the original support is empty and the original ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_projectionToBase_of_isPullbac: The iterated transition comparison to stage zero is a pullback. At zero the comparison with the base map is also a pullback, because the initial structural maps are isomorphisms and the square commutes. Paste these squares. The two composite structural maps are the projections to the respective bases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_transitionMap_of_isPullback_b: At equal stages the transition maps are identities, so the comparison square is a pullback. Induct on the difference of the indices. Paste the pullback square for the final successor onto the shorter pullback square from the induction hypothesis. Functoriality identifies both composed transitions with the direct transitions, proving the desired square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic: The two strict pullbacks have the same length, and at each stage they are pullbacks of the same projection along the same base map. The universal property gives a stage isomorphism commuting with both projections. Compatibility with the new base projection gives the initial equation. For the transition equation, compare both composites by their projections to the original stage and the new base. The original-stage projections agree by the consecutive pullback squares, and the new-base projections agree by compatibility with projections to the base. Thus the composites agree. Both local centers are pulled back from the same original center, so the stage isomorphisms preserve them.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_isomorphic_base: Compose the old stage comparison maps with the stage isomorphisms of the base sequence. Initial compatibility follows by composing the initial equations. The new successor squares are pastes of the old pullback squares with commuting squares whose comparison maps are isomorphisms. The center pullbacks along the composite agree with the original centers by functoriality and the center equations of the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_isomorphic_pullback: Replace the source sequence by the isomorphic sequence. Use the inverse stage isomorphisms followed by the old comparison maps. Their compatibility at zero gives the new initial equation. Each new transition square is the old pullback square pasted with a commuting square of stage isomorphisms and is still a pullback. Pullback of the old center equation along the inverse isomorphism gives the new center equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: The projection is the transition to stage zero followed by the initial isomorphism. At stage zero the transition is the identity, so the projection is the initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_of_isPullback_blowupMorphism: The stagewise projection square is a pullback, so each stage comparison is a base change of the surjective base map. Surjectivity is preserved by that base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_self: The order arrow from an index to itself is an identity. The tower functor preserves this identity, giving the identity map of the stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_pullbackIsoOfEq: After identifying the stage indices, the centers and second projections coincide and the comparison isomorphism is the identity. Both sides pull back the same center along the same map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_comp_projectionToBase: At stage zero compatibility with the projection is the initial compatibility. At a successor factor each projection through the preceding stage, use the commuting transition square, and apply the preceding projection equality. Induction proves compatibility with all projections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic: The retained-index functions are strictly increasing enumerations of the same indices with nonempty pulled-back centers and have the same terminal value. Hence the lengths and all the retained indices agree. At each stage map the first sequence to the canonical pullback, identify the pullbacks for the equal indices, and then use the inverse comparison to the second sequence. The first projection equations give compatibility at zero. The transition equations agree because the transport between equal stage indices commutes with pullback transitions. The center pullback formulas similarly identify the centers under the stage isomorphisms. These facts give an isomorphism of sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_isomorphic: Keep the retained indices and compose the old pullback comparisons with the inverse of the stage isomorphisms to the new sequence. The lengths are equal, so the indexing and retention statements still hold. The inverse isomorphisms commute with projections to the base and with the transitions, giving the new comparison equations. The center identity follows by pulling the original center equality back along the inverse isomorphism and using the original isomorphism’s center compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackIsoOfEq_hom_comp_pullbackTransit: Identify each pair of equal stage indices. The comparison isomorphisms become identities, and the two order proofs determine the same transition. Both sides reduce to that transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackIsoOfEq_hom_fst: Identify the equal stage indices. The resulting pullbacks coincide and the comparison isomorphism is the identity, so it preserves the first projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_enumeration_le: Induct strongly on the common index. If the first value were greater than the second value, the second value would occur in the first enumeration at a strictly earlier index by strict growth and equality of the enumerated subsets. At that earlier index the induction hypothesis bounds the first value by the second enumeration’s value there. Strict growth of the second enumeration makes this earlier value smaller than its present value, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_enumeration_unique: The comparison inequality in both directions makes the enumerations equal at every index before both endpoints. If the endpoints differed, the longer enumeration would have a value at the shorter endpoint that must occur at an earlier index of the shorter enumeration. Equality on earlier indices and strict growth would make it strictly smaller than itself. Thus the lengths agree. At their common final index both values equal the prescribed endpoint, giving full equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPullbackBlowupSequence.exists_reindexi: Use the given reindexing and the comparison isomorphisms followed by projection to the corresponding original stages. The comparison equations give a pullback square at each retained stage. If a step was omitted, its pulled-back center support is empty by the retention criterion, so its ideal is the unit ideal. The corresponding pulled-back blowup is therefore an isomorphism. Over any interval of omitted steps the composed pullback transition is an isomorphism, allowing the same stage to be compared with any original index in that interval. Between successive retained indices, apply this identification to the steps after the retained blowup. Pasting with the pullback square at the earlier retained stage, and then cancelling that square, gives the consecutive blowup comparison. The center equations at retained steps are the given ones. On any model of the pullback at an omitted step, the center is unit because it is pulled back from the unit center of the canonical pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_eq_top_of_support_empty: The hypothesis says that the support contains no points. The ideal with empty support is the unit ideal, so the given ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullbackTransitionMap: Express the later index as the earlier index plus the number of intervening steps. The inductive result for a chain of isomorphic one-step transitions then applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullbackTransitionMap_add: Induct on the number of steps. For zero steps the transition is the identity. At a successor the direct transition factors through the preceding endpoint. The preceding transition is an isomorphism by induction and the last step is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Their composite is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_of_iso_pullback: The stated equations identify the two given morphisms with the projections of the canonical pullback under an isomorphism of the source. Transport its pullback universal property across that isomorphism, with the factors in the stated order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_self_eq_id: Compare first and second projections. The first projection is preserved by definition. The second is followed by the original identity transition, so it too is unchanged. The pullback universal property makes the pulled-back transition the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_trans: The two composites agree on the first projection because all pullback transitions preserve it. On the second projection their maps reduce to the corresponding original transitions, and functoriality identifies their composite with the direct original transition. Pullback extensionality gives equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_eqToIso_hom: After identifying the equal indices the centers coincide, and pulling back along the identity transport leaves that ideal unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_pullback_snd_ne_top_congr: Replace the two equal stage indices by a single index. Both center pullbacks then agree, so the nonunit hypothesis gives the conclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_congr_idealSheaf: Equal ideal sheaves have equal pullbacks along the same morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_congr_morphism: The two pullback maps are equal. Substituting one for the other yields equality of the pulled-back ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_iso_hom_ne_top: If pullback along the isomorphism gave the unit ideal, further pullback along the inverse would still give the unit ideal. The two pullbacks compose to the identity on the original ideal, contrary to its being nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_pullback_snd_ne_top_iff_of_iso: The isomorphism of second factors gives an isomorphism of their pullbacks over the new base. Its second projection equation and the ideal compatibility show that the two pulled-back ideals correspond under this isomorphism. Pullback along an isomorphism preserves and reflects the unit ideal, giving the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_comp_eq_of_comp_eq: Postcompose the given equality with the last morphism and reassociate the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_eq_of_eq_of_comp_eq: Replace the first of the two equal maps by the second. The given equation for its composite is then the desired one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToIso_hom_comp_projectionToBase: Identify the equal indices. The transport is then the identity, and composing it with the structural projection leaves that projection unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pullbackIso_of_iso: Compose the original comparison with the pullback isomorphism induced by replacing the second factor by an isomorphic one. The first projection of the composite is unchanged. The second projection becomes the old one followed by the given factor isomorphism, giving both equations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_withoutIsoBl: A retained center upstairs is nonunit, so the original center at its comparison index is nonunit as well, because the former is pulled back from the latter. Each retained index upstairs therefore corresponds to a retained index downstairs. The final index corresponds to the final one by the original terminal equation. Strict increase of all index maps makes the resulting shortened reindexing strictly increasing. For each retained stage, transport the original comparison isomorphism to the matching stage of the shortened base sequence. Its first projection is the shortened structural projection. To check exactly which centers remain after pullback, a nonempty pulled-back center downstairs must have an original comparison step upstairs, by the hypothesis on omitted centers. The ideal of that upstairs step is nonunit because its stage is isomorphic to the canonical pullback. Hence the step is retained. Conversely a retained upstairs step has nonunit pulled-back center downstairs by the center equation. The two transition comparisons agree after the first projection by compatibility of projections to the base. After the second projection they agree because the original transition equations compose across the intervening steps and transport along equal indices commutes with them. Finally the original ideal pullback equations transport to the retained indices. These give a pullback of the shortened sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ne_top_iff_exists_mem_support: The support is empty exactly when the ideal is unit. Therefore a nonunit ideal has a point in its support, and the existence of such a point rules out the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_comap_ne_top_iff_without: At a retained index the shortened sequence has the original scheme and center at that index. Its projection to the base is also the same. The pullback comparison for isomorphic second factors, using the identity at this stage, therefore gives equivalence of the two center conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCongrRightHom_fst: The map between pullbacks is defined using the first projection as its first component. The universal property therefore gives the stated equation with the first projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCongrRightHom_snd: The second component used for the pullback lift is the original second projection followed by the isomorphism of factors. The defining projection equation is precisely the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCongrRightIso_hom_fst: The forward isomorphism is the previously constructed map of pullbacks. Its first projection is the original first projection by the defining equation for that map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCongrRightIso_hom_snd: The forward isomorphism has second component equal to the original second projection followed by the isomorphism on that factor. This gives the stated formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp: On the first projection, both composites preserve the projection to the new base. On the second, the successive original transitions compose to the original direct transition. Equality on both projections yields the equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp_assoc: The two consecutive pullback transitions compose to the direct transition. Postcompose that equality with the given map and reassociate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_self: The transition from a stage to itself preserves the first pullback projection. It also preserves the second because the original stage transition is the identity. Thus it is the identity by uniqueness of maps into the pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_snd_assoc: The second projection following a pullback transition is the original later projection followed by the original transition. Compose that equation with the final morphism and reassociate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_comp_eqToIso: Identify the two equal source indices and the two equal target indices. The transport isomorphisms become identities and the transitions coincide, giving equality of the composites.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_isStandardSmoothOfRela:
Choose affine opens about the given source point and its image on which the induced map of sections is standard smooth of the required relative dimension. Within the target open, choose a basic open of the whole affine target that still contains the image point. Restrict its defining section to the target open and pull it back to the source open. Its basic open is affine, contains the source point, and maps into the chosen target basic open.

The section rings of the smaller opens are the original rings localized at the section and its image. Compatibility of restrictions identifies their map with localization of the original standard smooth map, so its relative dimension is preserved. The section ring of the smaller target open is also the localization of the global target ring at the chosen global section. Precomposing with this localization preserves standard smoothness of the same relative dimension. Finally global sections of the smaller source as an open subscheme are canonically its sections in the original scheme. Transporting the property through this isomorphism gives the required map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_isPushout_of_isStandardSmoot:
Regard the two ring maps as a tower of algebras and apply the standard smooth lifting theorem along the given surjection. It supplies a standard smooth algebra of the same relative dimension over the original base, a surjection from the lift to the given target algebra, and an isomorphism identifying the target with the tensor product of the lift and the quotient base. The isomorphism agrees with the given lift map on the second tensor factor.

For a pair of maps out of the quotient base and the lift that agree on the original base, multiply their values on pure tensors to obtain the induced map from the tensor product. Transport it through the isomorphism. It has the required restriction to the lift by the formula on the second factor. Its restriction to the quotient base is determined by the commutative square and surjectivity from the original base, so it gives the required map there as well. The surjection from the lift to the target makes this induced map unique. This proves the pushout property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tensorProductLiftRingHom_tmul: The two maps agree on the common base ring, so the universal map from the tensor product is defined. On a pure tensor it multiplies the image of the first factor with the image of the second, which gives the displayed equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_isPullback_specMap: Choose the affine neighborhood of the source point on which the induced map of global sections is standard smooth of the given relative dimension. The ambient closed immersion induces a surjection on global sections. Apply the standard smooth lifting theorem for this surjection to obtain the lifted algebra and its surjective map to the source neighborhood's global sections, with a pushout square of rings. Taking spectra gives a pullback square. Use the canonical affine-scheme isomorphisms to identify its three original corners with the neighborhood, the original source of the closed immersion, and the ambient scheme. Naturality of those isomorphisms identifies the arrows with the original maps. The new neighborhood embedding is closed because it comes from the surjection, and the lifted ring map has the required standard smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_specMap_comp_isoSpec_inv: A standard smooth ring map is smooth, so its map of spectra is smooth. The canonical isomorphism from the spectrum of the ambient global sections back to the affine ambient scheme is smooth as well, and smoothness is preserved under composition.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffineOpen_chartDomain: The inverse image of the ambient basic open under the embedding is the basic open defined by the pulled-back section of the source. A basic open in the affine source is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_morphismRestrict_basicOpen: The chart domain is the inverse image of the indicated ambient open. Restriction of the embedding to this open is its base change along the open inclusion, so the displayed square is a pullback.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAdmissible_pullbackAlong_of_smooth: The new structural map is the composite of the smooth pullback map with the original smooth structural map. It is smooth and locally of finite type and is quasi-compact by hypothesis. The pullback map is flat, so the ideal remains nonzero on every component. Smooth pullback preserves strict normal crossings for the boundary, and the original positive marking and characteristic-zero field remain the same. Hence the new marked ideal is admissible.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_specToAffineSpaceExtendCoords_jac: First express the Jacobian section as the determinant of the partial derivatives of the lifted equations. The extended coordinate map on sections changes the coefficients along the ambient immersion and evaluates the new variables at their chosen values. The first operation commutes with partial differentiation and sends each lift to the given relation, so the entrywise image of the derivative matrix is the matrix for those relations. Evaluation sends its entries to the indicated evaluated derivatives. Both operations commute with determinants, and the affine global-sections isomorphism identifies the final value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.jacobianDetSection_mvPolynomialToSumCoor: For each row and column, the partial derivative of a lifted polynomial in the chosen new coordinate maps to the corresponding derivative in the full affine coordinate ring. Thus the Jacobian matrix is the entrywise image of the matrix of partial derivatives of the lifts, expressed in polynomial coordinates. Ring maps commute with determinants. Returning to global sections gives the stated image of the determinant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackHasGraphChart:
At the given point choose an affine open whose embedding into an affine smooth lift is the pullback of the original closed immersion. Choose a standard smooth presentation of the lift over the original ambient coordinate ring. Relabel its finitely many variables and relations by consecutive indices. The presentation chooses a distinct variable for each relation, with the number of variables equal to the number of relations plus the relative dimension. The relabeled variables generate the lift, and evaluation has kernel generated by the relabeled relations because renaming identifies this evaluation with the original presentation. The evaluated Jacobian remains a unit because the relabeling permutes its rows and columns together.

Lift the relations to polynomials over the coordinate ring of the original affine space, using surjectivity on sections of the original closed immersion. The old coordinates and the new generators give a closed immersion of the lift into the larger affine space. Its first coordinate block is the original ambient map followed by the original embedding, and its kernel is generated by the original ambient equations together with the lifted relations. The Jacobian determinant section for the lifted relations restricts to the unit Jacobian on the lift, so its basic open contains the whole image. On that open the graph morphism is smooth by the Jacobian criterion for the distinct chosen variables. The lift is affine and its structural map is smooth, locally of finite type and quasi-compact by composition. Together with the initial pullback square, these provide all the graph-chart data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.aeval_eq_zero_of_mem_span_liftedRelation: Evaluation over the original base agrees with evaluation after changing coefficients to the quotient base, by the scalar tower. Changing coefficients takes each lifted relation to its original relation, which evaluates to zero. Thus evaluation kills the ideal generated by the lifted relations and in particular the given polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.aeval_mk_X_liftedQuotient_surjective: Evaluation at the classes of the polynomial variables agrees with the quotient map on every variable and every scalar. Thus the evaluation is the quotient map, which is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.awayLift_jacobian_algebraMap_eq: The map from the localization restricts to the given map from the lifted quotient. A scalar enters the localization through the lifted quotient by the scalar tower. Its image in the original algebra is therefore the original scalar image because the quotient map is an algebra map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeEquiv_one_tmul: The algebra isomorphism uses the tensor-product map as its forward map. On the given pure tensor its value is the image of the lift multiplied by the scalar image of one, which is the image of the lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeHom_bijective: The map from the tensor product sends a pure tensor to the product of the scalar image and the image of the lifted element. Applying the inverse map recovers the pure tensor because those two factors return respectively to the left and right tensor factors. The equality extends by additivity to all tensors, so the map is injective. For surjectivity, lift any element of the original algebra to an element of the localized lifted algebra and tensor it on the left with one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.invBaseChangeHom_aeval: The inverse map uses a chosen polynomial representative for each element of the original algebra. The representative chosen for the evaluation of the given polynomial differs from it by an element of the evaluation kernel. The map to the base change kills this difference, giving the same value for both polynomials.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.invBaseChangeHom_liftedAlgebraHom: Both the composite through the original algebra and the right tensor factor map are ring maps out of the lifted localization. They agree on the image of its underlying quotient by the preceding formula. The universal property of localization makes them equal on every localized element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.invBaseChangeHom_liftedQuotientHom: Represent the lifted quotient element by a polynomial. Mapping its class to the original algebra evaluates that polynomial at the original generators, which is the same as changing coefficients and then evaluating. The formula for the inverse on a polynomial evaluation sends this to one tensored with the localized class of the lifted polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_jacobian_localizationAway_comp: The Jacobian of the composite presentation is the image of the lifted Jacobian multiplied by the localization presentation's Jacobian. The first is a unit because it is inverted in the localization. The second is a unit by the submersive presentation of that localization. Their product is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_liftedQuotientHom_jacobian: The lifted and original presentations choose the same variables for their derivatives. Coefficient change commutes with partial differentiation and sends each lifted relation to the original relation. Thus it carries the lifted derivative matrix entrywise to the original one and carries its determinant to the original determinant. The quotient map then evaluates these determinants at the corresponding generators. Consequently the lifted Jacobian maps to the original presentation's Jacobian, which is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedAlgebraHom_algebraMap: The lifted algebra map comes from the localization universal property. Its composite with the localization map is the map from the lifted quotient used to construct it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedAlgebraHom_surjective: For any element of the original algebra choose a polynomial representative in the original generators. Lift its coefficients along the surjection of base rings. The class of this lifted polynomial in the localized quotient maps to its evaluation in the original algebra. That evaluation agrees with that of the chosen representative by the scalar tower and hence gives the desired element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedPreSubmersivePresentation_map: The lifted presentation retains the original injection assigning a variable to each relation, so its assignment is the original one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedPreSubmersivePresentation_relation: The new presentation uses the lifted relations to define its quotient. Its relation at the given index is therefore the chosen lift at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedQuotientHom_mk: The map on the lifted quotient is induced by polynomial evaluation because evaluation kills its defining ideal. Its value on the class of a polynomial is the evaluation of that polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_liftedRelation: Changing coefficients along the surjection gives a surjective map on polynomials. Each lifted relation is chosen as a preimage of the corresponding original relation, so changing its coefficients back recovers that relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_eq_zero_of_aeva: The original presentation identifies polynomials evaluating to zero with the ideal generated by its relations. The map to the base change sends each of those relations to zero, so it sends the whole ideal to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_map: Compare the two maps on scalars and variables. On a scalar, the equality follows from the tensor relation moving a scalar from the original base between factors. On a variable the value is one tensored with the localized class of the variable by definition. Both constructions preserve sums and products, so the formula holds for every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_relation_eq_zer: Replace the original relation by the image of its lifted relation under change of coefficients. The polynomial formula sends this to one tensored with the localized class of the lifted relation. That class is zero in the lifted quotient, so the image is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_section_add: The representative of a sum and the sum of the two representatives evaluate to the same element. Their difference maps to zero in the base change, where additivity gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_section_algebra: The representative of a scalar's image and the constant polynomial for that scalar evaluate to the same element in the original algebra. Their difference maps to zero in the base change. The map on the constant polynomial is its scalar image there because it is an algebra map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_section_mul: The representative of a product and the product of the two representatives have the same evaluation in the original algebra. Their difference is killed by the map to the base change. Since that map preserves multiplication, this gives the claimed product formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_section_one: The chosen polynomial representative of one and the constant polynomial one have the same evaluation in the original algebra. Their difference belongs to its evaluation kernel and therefore maps to zero in the base change. The image of the representative is thus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToBaseChange_section_zero: The representative of zero evaluates to zero in the original algebra. The kernel criterion therefore says that its image in the base change is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_range_liftedRelation_eq_ker: Evaluating at the chosen quotient generators is the quotient map, since the maps agree on the variables and scalars. A polynomial maps to zero under this quotient map exactly when it belongs to the ideal generated by the lifted relations.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_lift_of_isStandardSmoothOfRelativ: Choose a finite submersive presentation of the given algebra with the stated dimension and lift it along the surjection of base rings. The lifted submersive presentation has the same dimension because it adds one variable and one relation. The lift construction provides a surjective map to the original algebra and identifies its base change with that algebra by the given tensor-product isomorphism. On the second factor the isomorphism is precisely the lift map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftedSubmersivePresentation_dimension: The lift adds one variable and one relation. The difference between the two finite cardinalities therefore agrees with that of the original presentation, which is its dimension.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups: A strict pullback preserves the intermediate sequence length, so keep the reindexing of the given pullback up to empty centers. The strict comparison gives pullback squares for the maps of all stages to their bases. Paste each with the corresponding square for the intermediate sequence to obtain the stage comparison over the composite base map. The further base map is surjective, so the support of each pulled-back center is nonempty exactly when it was nonempty on the intermediate base. Thus the retained indices are unchanged. Projection to the new base gives the first compatibility of the stage comparisons. Comparison after the other projection follows from the commuting transition squares for the two given sequences, so the new transitions agree by the pullback property. Finally each center is obtained by two successive pullbacks, which equal pullback along the composite comparison. These are all the conditions for the composite pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_comap: The support of a pullback ideal is the inverse image of its support. The given point belongs to it exactly when its image belongs to the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_pullback_snd_nonempty_iff: The map from the pullback along the composite to the pullback along the intermediate map commutes with projection to the stage. It is a base change of the given surjection and is surjective. A point on the pulled-back support upstairs therefore gives one downstairs, and every point on the support downstairs lifts to one upstairs. This proves equivalence of nonemptiness.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsPullbackBlowupSequence.isStrictPullbac: Every original center has nonempty pulled-back support, so the retention condition makes every original step appear among the reindexed steps. The reindexing is strictly increasing and sends the final index to the original final index. The ordered-index argument now makes it the identity through the final stage, and the lengths agree. Use the stage isomorphisms followed by the second projections as the strict comparison maps. The initial comparison follows from the projection equations. For every successor, the transition square is obtained by composing the comparison isomorphisms with the ordinary consecutive base-change pullback square. The center equations become exactly the strict pullback equations because the indices agree.

Every original center is nonunit and therefore has nonempty support. Surjectivity of the base map ensures that the projection of any point of that support lies in its range. Thus every pulled-back center has nonempty support. Apply the criterion for a pullback with no missing centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_eq_self_of_strictMono_of_surjectiv: Strict growth gives the lower bound that every value is at least its index, by induction from zero. For the other inequality use strong induction on the index. If a value exceeded its index, that index would be below the target endpoint, since all values are at most that endpoint. By surjectivity it would have a preimage before the source endpoint. The lower bound puts this preimage at or before the index. An earlier preimage is impossible because the induction hypothesis makes all earlier values at most their indices, and the current index is impossible because its value is assumed larger. Hence every value equals its index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_comap_eq_comap_comp_transitionMap: With the indices identified, the center ideals are the same and the intervening transition is the identity. Both expressions pull that center back along the same composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_pullbackTransitionMap_comp_tr: Identify the two indices with the specified consecutive stages. The extra transitions in the comparison maps become identities, leaving the usual pullback square for the consecutive pulled-back transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_center_nonempty_of_mem_ran: At the given step take a point on the center support. Its image in the base has a preimage in the new base by hypothesis. Together these points give a point of the scheme pullback. Its second projection lies in the original center support, so it belongs to the pulled-back center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_nonempty_of_ne_top: An ideal sheaf with empty support is the unit ideal. Since the given ideal is nonunit, its support is nonempty.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_finite_affine_cover_subordinate: At each source point choose a target cover member containing its image. The inverse image is an open neighborhood, so the basis of affine opens supplies an affine neighborhood contained in it. Such affine neighborhoods cover the source. Compactness gives a finite subcover, and for each chosen affine open retain one index of a target member whose inverse image contains it. This produces all the required data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_opensCoprodMapOfRefi: Composing the refinement map with the target coproduct map gives the source coproduct map followed by the original map. The latter composite is locally of finite type because the source map is assembled from open immersions. The locally finite type property of the composite implies the same property for the refinement map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_affineOpensLePreimageCover: The defining condition for membership is that the open be affine and contained in the inverse image of at least one member of the target cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opensCoprodMapOfRefinement_comp_sigmaOpe: Check equality on each source summand. The route through the target coproduct first maps to the selected target open, then includes it in the target scheme. This is the source open inclusion followed by the original map, by the defining property of the restriction. Thus the two composites agree on every summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_eq_homOfLE_comp_restrict: Both maps become the original map restricted to the source open after composing with the inclusion of the target open. The inclusion is a monomorphism, so the original maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sigmaι_opensCoprodMapOfRefinement: The map from the source coproduct is defined on each summand by restricting the original map to the selected target open and including that open in the target coproduct. Restricting to the specified source summand recovers this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_opensCoprodMapOfRefinement: On each source summand the coproduct map is the restricted smooth map followed by the inclusion of the chosen target summand, which is an open immersion. This composite is smooth on every summand. The summands form an open cover, so the coproduct map is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_resLE: Factor the map through the full inverse image of the target open. The first map is an open immersion and hence smooth. The restriction on the full inverse image is a base change of the smooth map, so it is smooth too. Therefore their composite is smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_symm_com: On a coefficient section the map pulls back through the first projection and returns to polynomial coordinates, giving first-block renaming by the preceding calculation. On each new variable it returns the corresponding second-block variable. Evaluation with the stated coefficient map and variables has these same values, so the ring maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_symm_mvP: Apply the equality of ring maps from the preceding statement to the specified polynomial. This gives the formula as evaluation with old coefficients in the first block and new variables in the second.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_symm_pro: Compare the ring maps on constants and coordinate variables. Pullback along projection fixes constants and takes each original variable to the corresponding first-block variable. These are exactly the images under first-block renaming, so the two maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pderiv_inr_X_inl: The two variables have indices in disjoint blocks. A coordinate variable has derivative zero with respect to a distinct variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pderiv_inr_eval₂_X_inr: The derivative of every substituted coefficient vanishes by hypothesis. For a variable the derivative before and after substitution equals one at the selected index and zero at every other index. By additivity and the product rule the equality extends from constants and variables to all polynomials.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pderiv_inr_renameSumInl: Check constants, sums and products with an original variable by polynomial induction. Constants have zero derivative, and additivity preserves vanishing. In the product case the renamed variable is in the first block, so its derivative in the second-block variable is zero. The other derivative in the product rule also vanishes by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pderiv_mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_s: Express the coordinate-ring map in polynomial coordinates as evaluation, with coefficients included into the first block and variables in the second. Each substituted coefficient has zero derivative in a second-block variable by the first-block renaming result. Thus the differentiation rule for evaluation applies and gives the corresponding derivative of the original polynomial before substitution.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projLeft_appTop_affineSpaceIndexedByToSp: The projection to the first block respects the field structure. Pulling a field section back through the projection and the first block's structure map is therefore the same as pulling it back along the full space's structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projLeft_appTop_mvPolynomialEquivGlobalS: Under the identification of polynomials with sections, a constant comes from the field by pullback. Projection to the first block preserves this pullback, so the constant corresponds to the same constant on the full affine space.

The polynomial variable corresponds to its coordinate section. Pullback along first-block projection gives the corresponding coordinate in the first block of the full space. The section identification sends the indicated variable to that coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.renameSumInl_C: Renaming variables preserves all scalar coefficients, so it fixes a constant polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.renameSumInl_X: Variable renaming takes each variable to the variable at its new index. Here the index is placed into the first block, so the image is the corresponding first-block variable.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closure_image_mem_irreducibleComponents_: Flatness makes the map generalizing. The closure of the image of a component under such a map is a target component by the component-tracking theorem.

Choose the generic point of the given component. The closure of the component’s image is the closure of the image generic point, by continuity and the presence of that point in the image. Every generization of the image generic point lifts to a generization of the original generic point. A component generic point has no distinct generization, since the closure of a generization is an irreducible set containing that component, which must coincide with it. Thus the image generic point has no distinct generization either. In a scheme an irreducible closed set has a generic point. Applying this to the closure of any irreducible set containing the image point’s closure proves maximality of that closure, making it a component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_of_flat: A flat morphism is generalizing. The result for generalizing maps therefore applies to the given ideal under this flat pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_of_generalizingMap: If a source component were contained in the pullback support, its image would lie in the original support. This support is closed, so it would contain the closure of the image. The generalizing-map result makes that closure an irreducible component of the target, contradicting nonvanishing on components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_of_isOpenImmersion: An open immersion is generalizing because every generization of a point of an open set still lies in the open. Apply the nonvanishing result for generalizing maps to this immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.generalizingMap_of_flat: A flat ring map satisfies going down for prime ideals. On affine neighborhoods this lifts any generization of an image point to a generization of the given source point, so the scheme map is generalizing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap: An ideal sheaf pulled back to a source point is proper in the local ring exactly when the original ideal is proper at its image. Accordingly its support is the inverse image of the original support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closure_compl_sUnion_irreducibleComponen: The open complement of the excluded components lies in the selected union, which is closed, so its closure also lies there. Conversely take a selected component. It cannot be contained in the union of excluded components, because that is a finite union of closed sets and irreducibility would put it inside a single excluded component. Maximality would then identify the two components, contradicting the choice. Thus the selected component meets the complement in a nonempty open subset, which is dense in that component. Every selected component therefore lies in the closure.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_complSUnionOtherComponents: The open is defined as the complement of the union of the excluded irreducible components, so its underlying subset is exactly that complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_sUnion:
Let the open in the target be the complement of the excluded irreducible components. Its closure is the selected union, so the support of the kernel of the open inclusion is that union. Since the open is reduced, the kernel is its support's vanishing ideal.

The closure of the inverse image of the open is contained in the inverse image of the selected union because the latter is closed. For the reverse inclusion, take any point above a selected component. Its image is a specialization of that component's generic point. The generic point belongs to the open, because any excluded component containing it would contain the selected component and hence equal it. Flatness lifts this generalization of the image to a generalization of the original point. That lift belongs to the inverse image of the open, so the original point is in its closure. The preimage open inclusion therefore has kernel the vanishing ideal of the inverse image of the selected union. Both open inclusions are quasi-compact by Noetherianity. The flat pullback formula for the kernels of their pullback square gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.compl_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff: Every point lies on an irreducible component. If the point avoids the union of excluded components, any such component through the point must belong to the selected family. Hence the point belongs to that family's union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_sUnion_irreducibleComponents: A Noetherian space has finitely many irreducible components, each closed. The selected family is a subset of this finite family, so its union is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_compl_sUnion_irreducibleComponent: The excluded components are a family of irreducible components of the Noetherian space. Their union is closed, so its complement is open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_vanishingIdeal_of_support: The ideal of the support of an ideal sheaf is its radical. Here the kernel sheaf equals its radical because the source is reduced, and its support is the given closed subset. Thus its kernel is the vanishing ideal of that subset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ringHom_ker_eq: The kernel is contained in its radical. If an element has a power in the kernel, its image has a power equal to zero. The target ring is reduced, so the image is zero and the original element already lies in the kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_scheme_ker_eq: The kernel ideal sheaf is contained in its radical. For the reverse containment, on each affine target open the ideal of the kernel sheaf lies in the kernel of the section map. Sections over the inverse image form a reduced ring because the source scheme is reduced. The kernel of this section map is therefore radical and also contains the radical of the kernel sheaf ideal on that open. These local containments give containment in the kernel ideal sheaf, which is determined by the section kernels.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdeal_congr: Closed subsets with the same underlying set are equal. Their vanishing ideal sheaves are therefore equal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_comp_projectionToBase: The projection from a stage first transitions to stage zero and then uses the initial isomorphism to the base. The composite of the transition from the later stage to the intermediate stage and the transition from there to zero equals the direct transition to zero by functoriality of the tower. Following both sides by the initial isomorphism gives the stated compatibility.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceCoordBlowupChart_comp_affineS: The map from the standard affine blowup chart to the polynomial spectrum is induced by the canonical map into its chart ring. Under the chart-ring identification with a polynomial ring, that homomorphism is the coordinate substitution. Taking spectra and applying the compatibility of the polynomial substitution with the affine-space identification gives the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceSpecIso_hom_appTop_X: Under the inverse affine-space isomorphism, the coordinate pulls back to the section represented by the corresponding variable. Pulling this identity back along the forward isomorphism cancels the two pullbacks, so that section maps to the coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceSpecIso_inv_appTop_coord: The canonical spectrum presentation of affine space is defined using its coordinate algebra. Pulling a coordinate back to the spectrum therefore gives the global section represented by the corresponding polynomial variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceSpecIso_inv_comp_affineSpaceF: Under the identification of affine space with the spectrum of the polynomial ring, the structure map is induced by the inclusion of the field as constant polynomials. The asserted composite is that structure map on the spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_apply_eq_appTop_appTop: Global sections are contravariant in the scheme. Pullback along the composite sends a section first through the pullback of the second morphism and then through the pullback of the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_specMap_ΓSpecIso_inv_apply: The canonical identification between a ring and the global sections of its spectrum is natural in ring maps. Under this identification, pulling a section back along the induced map of spectra applies the original ring map to its representing element. Evaluating at the given element gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_specIdealSheaf_finCoordIdeal: The ideal on the polynomial spectrum is generated by the variables indexed by the center. Its pullback to affine space is generated by the images of those variables as global sections. Each becomes the corresponding coordinate and all selected coordinates occur, so this is the coordinate-subspace ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.down_mem_of_mem_uliftFinset: By construction every index in the enlarged set is the image of an index in the original set. Recovering its original index therefore gives a member of that set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iSup_opensRange_affineSpaceCoordBlowupCh: The homogeneous localizations at the chosen degree-one generators give open charts covering the affine blowup. The generators here are precisely the selected coordinate variables. Each standard chart therefore occurs among the chart opens indexed by the center set, so their union is the whole blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_affineSpaceCoord: The affine blowup of the polynomial coordinate ideal has the blowup property over the polynomial spectrum. The isomorphism with affine space identifies the ideal sheaf there with the coordinate-subspace ideal. Transport the universal property along this base isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_uliftFinset: The enlarged index set is the image of the original finite set under the canonical embedding. Any member of the image has original index in the original set. Conversely, a member whose original index belongs to that set is the image of that index, proving the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMap_coordBlowupSubstUliftFin_comp_af: To compare these maps to affine space, compare their structural maps and the pullbacks of the coordinates. Both preserve the ground field, so the structural maps agree. By naturality of global sections on spectra, polynomial variables pull back according to the polynomial substitution. Under the affine-space identification this matches the coordinate substitution, multiplying the center coordinates other than the distinguished one by the distinguished coordinate and preserving all others. Thus the two maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.up_mem_uliftFinset: The enlarged finite set is the image of the original set under the index embedding. The image of the chosen member therefore belongs to the enlarged set.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_blowupChart_family_isPullback_cov: The blowup restricted to the original chart is the blowup of its restricted center. That center is pulled back from the coordinate subspace of affine space. The chart is étale and hence flat, so the restricted blowup is the base change of the coordinate blowup of affine space. Pull each standard chart of the coordinate blowup back to an open of the restricted blowup. Identify the standard chart with affine space, where its map downstairs is the coordinate substitution. Pasting the pullback squares gives the required chart square. The chart map upstairs is étale by base change, and commutativity together with the substitution being a map over the field gives its structural equation. Since the standard chart opens cover the model blowup, the pulled-back opens cover the inverse image of the original chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_domain_blowupChart_of_isBlowu: The chosen family covers the inverse image of the downstairs chart, because it is obtained by taking inverse images of the standard open cover of the coordinate blowup. The given point belongs to one of these open domains, indexed by a coordinate of the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_isPullback_of_opens: Take the inverse image of the given open under the map from the open subscheme. Its composite inclusion into the ambient scheme is an open immersion, so identify its source with the open subscheme on its image. This image lies in the original open. Transport the inverse-image pullback square along the identification. The factorization of the inclusion and the point membership follow from the definition of this image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_blowupChart_of_isBlowupAlongI: The chosen chart is a member of the family obtained by pulling back the standard affine-space blowup charts along the étale chart downstairs. The family was constructed with a pullback square at each center index. Its square at the given index is the asserted one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSectionsToCoordRelationQuotient_af: Under the polynomial presentation of affine-space sections, the section pulled back from the field is represented by a constant polynomial. Evaluating that polynomial uses only the coefficient map. This first sends the field element to the downstairs section ring and then takes the class of its constant polynomial in the quotient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSectionsToCoordRelationQuotient_co: The affine-space section identification sends the indicated coordinate to its polynomial variable. The evaluation defining the ring map assigns to this variable its class in the quotient by the relations. This gives the stated value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceFin_globalSections_hom_ext: The global section ring of affine space is the polynomial ring under its canonical identification. The maps agree on constants because they agree on sections pulled back from the field. They agree on all polynomial variables because they agree on the coordinates. Ring homomorphisms agreeing on these generators agree on every polynomial and hence on all sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_congr: After substituting the equality of morphisms, both section maps are induced by the same morphism and the same containment of opens. The choice of proof of that containment has no effect on the map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_coord: If the index lies in the center and differs from the distinguished index, the pullback includes one distinguished factor. If the index is the distinguished one, its pullback is unchanged. If it lies outside the center, it is likewise unchanged. The conditional formula records these cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_coord_of_mem: Apply the equality of the two maps around the chart square to this coordinate on affine space. Its image under substitution is the product of that coordinate with the distinguished one, and pullback preserves products. The identifications of global sections of the chart domains with sections on the ambient opens give the stated section formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_coord_of_not_mem: The commutative chart square identifies the pullback of the downstairs coordinate with the pullback along the substitution and then the upstairs chart. The substitution preserves coordinates outside the center, giving the matching upstairs coordinate under the open section identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_coord_self: The chart square makes the two pullbacks of the distinguished coordinate from affine space agree. The substitution preserves that coordinate. Using the section identifications of the open subschemes gives the upstairs coordinate as the image of the downstairs one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_topIso_hom_apply: Use the compatibility of the direct open section identifications with the section maps of the morphism and its restriction. Evaluate the equality of ring homomorphisms on the indicated global section of the open subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_topIso_inv_comp: Replace each inverse section identification by the map induced by the corresponding open inclusion. The resulting composites of section maps come from the two scheme composites around the restriction square. Those composites agree, so the resulting maps on sections agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_affineSectionsToCoordRelatio: Compare the two maps on constants and coordinates, which generate the affine-space section ring. The substitution fixes constants from the field, and the two maps send these to the same coefficient classes because the downstairs chart is over the field. On a coordinate, the substitution gives its chart-variable expression, and the other map gives the class of the corresponding downstairs coordinate. The defining relation identifies these classes in every index case. Thus the maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_coordEvalQuotientHom: The domain chart is affine because the given square makes it a pullback of affine schemes. The affine pullback computation identifies the coordinate quotient with the section ring via the evaluation homomorphism, so the map is bijective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_coordEvalQuotientHom_of_isPull: The chart square is a pullback of affine schemes, so global sections form a pushout of rings. The ring maps from affine-space sections and downstairs chart sections to the coordinate quotient agree on the common ring by the defining relations. They induce a map from the pushout to the quotient. After identifying sections of the upstairs open subscheme with sections on the ambient open, this map is inverse to evaluation. To check evaluation after the induced map, compare the two composites on the rings entering the pushout. They agree on affine-space coordinates and field constants and on every downstairs section. To check the other composite, compare the quotient classes of constants from downstairs and of the polynomial variables. Both classes are fixed, and they generate the quotient. Hence evaluation is bijective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chart_appTop_coordBlowupSubstMap_apply: Apply global sections to the commutative chart square. Contravariance identifies the two successive pullbacks of a section on the common target affine space. Evaluation at the given section is the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_appTop_apply: Global sections are contravariant in the scheme. Pullback along the composite applies the pullback of the second morphism followed by the pullback of the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_hom_apply: The underlying ring map of the composite is the ordinary composition of the two ring maps. Evaluation therefore applies the first map and then the second.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.constToCoordRelationQuotient_apply: The map sends a section to its constant polynomial and then takes its class modulo the ideal of chart relations. Applying the composite to the indicated section gives the claimed class.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_appTop_affineSpaceFi: The substitution morphism is over the field, so composing it with the affine-space structural morphism gives the same structural morphism. On global sections this means that pullback along the substitution fixes each section coming from the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalHom_C: A constant polynomial has no variable factors. Evaluating it applies only the coefficient map, which is the pullback on sections from the downstairs open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalHom_X: Under polynomial evaluation the indicated variable is assigned its corresponding upstairs chart coordinate. Evaluation of that variable gives the stated section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalHom_coordRelation: Evaluate the relation by sending the variables to their upstairs coordinates and the coefficient to its pullback. The pullback formula gives precisely the variable expression in each case. Their difference is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalHom_def: The evaluation homomorphism is defined by pulling back coefficients along the restricted blowup map and substituting the upstairs chart coordinate for each variable. These assignments are exactly the stated polynomial evaluation map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalHom_eq_zero_of_mem_span: Every relation evaluates to zero and hence lies in the kernel ideal of evaluation. The kernel is an ideal, so it also contains the span of the relations. Evaluation vanishes on every element of that span.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalQuotientHom_constToCoordRelatio: The class in question is represented by the constant polynomial of the original section. The descended evaluation sends it to the pullback of its coefficient along the restricted blowup map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordEvalQuotientHom_mk: Evaluation vanishes on the ideal of relations and therefore descends to the quotient. The descended map sends the class of a polynomial to the evaluation of that polynomial, by the defining property of the quotient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordRelation_def: The relation subtracts the coefficient given by the downstairs coordinate from its prescribed expression in chart variables. This expression is the variable times the distinguished variable for a center index distinct from the distinguished one, and is the variable itself in the other cases.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_appTop_affineSpaceFinToSpec_a: Identifying a section of the spectrum of the field with its field element, the pullback to affine space is the constant polynomial of that element. The chart map is over the field, so pulling this section back to the chart and identifying sections on the ambient open gives its image under the section-ring structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_inv_apply: The forward map composed after the inverse of the ring isomorphism is the identity on the target. Evaluating at the given target element gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_inv_hom_apply: The inverse of the ring isomorphism composed after the forward map is the identity. Evaluating at the given element yields the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mk_eq_mk_C_coord: The difference between the substituted chart-variable expression and the constant polynomial of the downstairs coordinate is the relation for this index. Its class in the quotient is zero, so the two expressions have equal classes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialIsoGlobalSectionsAffineSpace: The polynomial constant comes from the ground field by the constant-polynomial map. Under the natural identification of a ring with global sections of its spectrum, this map is the pullback of the structural morphism of the polynomial spectrum. The canonical isomorphism with affine space identifies that morphism with the affine-space structure map, giving the formula.

Pullback from affine space to the polynomial spectrum sends the coordinate to the section represented by the corresponding variable. The inverse identification on sections takes that representative back to the original coordinate. This inverse is the map in the claim.

Both maps first identify the polynomial ring with global sections of its spectrum and then pull those sections back along the affine-space isomorphism. These identical constructions send the polynomial to the same section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.openSectionsToCoordRelationQuotient_appl: Identify the section of the open subscheme with its corresponding section over the ambient open. The map sends that section to its constant polynomial and then to its class modulo the coordinate relations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.openSectionsToCoordRelationQuotient_coor: The pullback of the affine-space coordinate to the open subscheme becomes the downstairs chart coordinate under the section identification. The quotient map on open sections takes the class of the constant polynomial of that coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_comp_eq: Functoriality identifies the composite of the two presheaf maps with the map of the composite arrow. This arrow and the indicated direct arrow have the same endpoints in a poset category, so they are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_eq: Between any two objects of the opposite of the poset of opens there is at most one arrow. The two arrows coincide, so their images under the presheaf coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap: Restriction is pullback along the open inclusion. The composite of the upstairs inclusion with the blowup equals the composite of the restricted blowup with the downstairs inclusion. Functoriality of ideal pullback gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_coordIdeal_of_mem: Use the restriction square to work with the downstairs coordinate ideal.
