The chart substitution sends its generator to the product of the corresponding upstairs coordinate with the distinguished coordinate. The ideal generated by this product is the product of their principal ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_coordIdeal_of_not_me: The restricted pullback is the pullback of the coordinate ideal on the downstairs chart. This coordinate has index outside the center, so the substitution preserves it. The pulled-back ideal is the corresponding coordinate ideal upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_coordIdeal_self: After restricting to the two chart domains, pull back the ideal generated by the distinguished coordinate downstairs. The substitution preserves that coordinate, so the ideal is the distinguished coordinate ideal upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_top: Restricting the pullback is equivalent to pulling back the restricted downstairs ideal. The latter is the unit ideal by assumption, and extension of the unit ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_exceptionalIdeal: The exceptional ideal is the pulled-back center ideal. Restrict the pullback to the chart by using the restriction square. The center is generated by the selected coordinates downstairs. Under the chart substitution all their pullbacks are multiples of the distinguished coordinate and that coordinate itself occurs, so the restricted exceptional ideal is its principal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specIso_hom_comp_map_C: The structural morphism on the polynomial spectrum is induced by the inclusion of constant polynomials. Transport it along the canonical identification of affine space with that spectrum. The resulting morphism is the structural morphism of affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_coordEvalHom: The induced evaluation on the coordinate quotient is bijective by the affine pullback calculation. Given an upstairs section, choose its preimage in the quotient and then choose a polynomial representing that class. The original evaluation of this representative is the section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topIso_hom_comp_appLE: Start with the compatibility of pullback with the inverse section identifications of the two opens. Compose with the direct section identification on each end. The isomorphisms cancel their inverses, leaving the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topIso_inv_appLE_apply: The inverse section identifications commute with pullback along the morphism on the chosen opens. Evaluating this equality of composites on the indicated ambient section gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topIso_inv_eq_ι_appLE: Both maps send a section over the open in the ambient scheme to its section on the whole open subscheme. In the restricted presheaf the extra restriction maps compose to the direct restriction, since the arrows have the same endpoints. This identifies the two section maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_preimage_top: The inverse image of the whole target under any morphism is the whole source. The two opens in the comparison are therefore equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_ι_preimage: Every point of the open subscheme maps under its inclusion to a point of that open. Its inverse image therefore contains the whole open subscheme.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_zero_of_locally_eq_zero: Take the chosen neighborhoods of all points of the open. They cover the open, and the restriction of the section is zero on each. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom identifies the original section with zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_eq_strictTransform_subscheme: The composite morphism from the strict transform to the original scheme kills the kernel ideal of the given closed immersion. The universal property of the closed subscheme therefore factors this composite through that immersion, with the indicated composition identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ideal_eq_span_singleton_of_le: On the smaller affine open the section ideal is the extension along restriction of the section ideal on the larger affine open. Extending a principal ideal sends its generator to its restriction. This restricted section generates the desired ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_strictTransformL: On affine opens of the original blowup the exceptional ideal is principal. Its image on the strict transform generates the pulled-back center. The strict-transform ideal is saturated by this generator, so multiplication by its image on the quotient is injective. This gives the local nonzerodivisor condition. For the universal property, start with a map to the closed subscheme whose pulled-back center is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. Its composite to the original scheme factors through the original blowup. This factor kills the total-transform ideal of the closed subscheme. Locally, a section of the strict-transform ideal is sent into that total-transform ideal by a power of an exceptional generator. The image of the generator generates the pulled-back center on a sufficiently small basic open. It divides a nonzerodivisor generator of that ideal there, so it is a nonzerodivisor and its powers can be canceled. The section therefore vanishes locally and hence everywhere under the factor map. Thus the map factors through the strict transform. The composite is the required map to the closed subscheme by cancellation of the first closed immersion. Uniqueness follows from uniqueness of the lift to the original blowup and from the strict transform inclusion being a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isBlowupAlongIdea: The blowup over a locally Noetherian scheme is proper and thus locally of finite type. A scheme locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_le_ker_strictTransform_subschemeι_co: The kernel ideal of the closed subscheme inclusion is the strict-transform ideal. The kernel inclusion for the composite is equivalent to containment of the pulled-back original kernel ideal in this strict-transform ideal. This containment holds because the strict-transform ideal is the saturation of the total-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_dvd: Write the nonzerodivisor as the product of the divisor and another element. If multiplication by the divisor kills an element, multiplication by this product also kills it. Injectivity of multiplication by the product forces the element to be zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_strictTransform_of_mul_mem: On the affine open, the strict-transform ideal is the saturation of the total-transform ideal by powers of the exceptional generator. If the generator times the section lies in this saturation, multiply by its witnessing power. The next higher power then sends the original section into the total-transform ideal, so the section itself lies in the saturation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrict_basicOpen_mem_nonZeroDivisors: Restriction to the basic open localizes the section ring at powers of the defining section. Localization is flat, so it preserves injectivity of multiplication by the nonzerodivisor. Multiplication by the image is therefore injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIsBlowupOfClosedSubscheme: The ambient blowup is locally Noetherian because it lies over a locally Noetherian base. For the given closed immersion, take the morphism from its strict transform obtained by factorization through that immersion. Its composite with the immersion gives the ambient morphism, and the strict-transform universal property identifies it as the blowup of the pulled-back center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformLiftOfClosedImmersion_com: The strict-transform lift was chosen as the factorization of its composite to the original scheme through the given closed immersion. Its defining factorization identity gives the equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_stalk_of_isOpenImmersio: The stalk map of an open immersion is a ring isomorphism. The ascending chain condition on ideals transports along that isomorphism, so the source local ring is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_le_of_blowup_strictNormalCr: The dimension of the blowup is bounded by that of the original scheme by the strict normal crossings dimension estimate. The structural map of the original scheme is of finite type, so its dimension is finite. On dimensions bounded by this finite value, the conversion to natural-number successors is monotone, giving the stated inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_topologicalKrullDim_of_etaleChart: Choose a nonempty affine open in the chart and a closed point in that affine open. Its composite map to affine space is étale. At a closed point of such an étale scheme the local ring has dimension equal to the dimension of the affine space. The affine open immerses into the original scheme, so the local ring there has the same dimension. The dimension of any local ring is bounded by the Krull dimension of the scheme’s underlying space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_isBlowupAlongId: Take the open complement of the center. The blowup is an isomorphism over that open. Its inverse image is open in the blowup, and its map to the original scheme factors as that isomorphism followed by an open immersion. Both open immersions identify the corresponding local rings, yielding equal dimensions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_isOpenImmersion: An open immersion identifies the local ring at a point with the local ring at its image. The isomorphism identifies their prime spectra and chains of primes, so the Krull dimensions are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etaleChart: The inclusion of the chart domain identifies its local ring at the point with the corresponding local ring of the scheme. The chart is étale over affine space of the stated dimension. The dimension bound for local rings of such an étale scheme applies to this local ring and gives the bound on the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_blowup_strictN: Both schemes are locally Noetherian, and it suffices to bound each local dimension upstairs by the topological dimension downstairs. Away from the center the local rings are identified by the blowup isomorphism. Over the center choose a downstairs étale coordinate chart and a blowup chart above it. The upstairs local dimension is bounded by the dimension of its chart’s affine space. This affine space has the same dimension as that of the nonempty downstairs chart, which is bounded by the topological dimension downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_mono_of_lt_top: The added bottom element maps to zero, which is at most every output. If the smaller input is above bottom, then so is the larger input. Since the larger input is below infinity, both are finite natural numbers, and their outputs are their successors. Taking successors preserves the given inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsBlo: The canonical pullback of the original blowup is a blowup of the pulled-back center. Hence the given blowup of that center is isomorphic over the new base to the canonical pullback. Compose this isomorphism with the projection to the original blowup. The square commutes by the canonical pullback equation and is a pullback because the isomorphism identifies the two squares.

The canonical pullback projection is a blowup of the pulled-back center by the flat base-change result. The given pullback square identifies its vertex with the canonical pullback by an isomorphism commuting with the projection to the new base. Transport the blowup property along this isomorphism.

On the pullback square, pulling the center ideal back from the new base gives the same ideal as pulling the exceptional ideal back from the old blowup. The projection to the old blowup is flat, so the latter ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. For the universal property, take a map to the new base whose pullback of the center ideal has this same property. Its composite to the old base therefore factors uniquely through the old blowup. That factor and the original map agree over the old base and define a map to the pullback. Any other such map has the same projection to the new base and, by the original blowup’s uniqueness, the same projection to the old blowup. The pullback property yields uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: Choose an affine neighborhood downstairs where the ideal has a nonzerodivisor as generator. Choose an affine neighborhood of the given point upstairs inside its inverse image. The induced section map is flat, so the generator maps to a nonzerodivisor. On these opens the pulled-back ideal is the extension of the original section ideal, hence is generated by that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_mem_le: Affine opens form a basis of the scheme topology. Apply the basis property inside the given open neighborhood at the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat: Multiplication by the original element is injective on the source ring because it is a nonzerodivisor. Tensoring this map with the target over the source preserves injectivity by flatness. Under the identification of the tensored source module with the target, the resulting map is multiplication by the image of the element. Its injectivity says that this image is a nonzerodivisor.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_exceptional: The support of the exceptional ideal is the inverse image of the center’s support. At a point of that inverse image, choose étale coordinates downstairs in which the center is a coordinate subscheme, then a blowup chart containing the point. On that chart the exceptional ideal is the single coordinate ideal for the distinguished blowup coordinate. This supplies the strict normal crossings chart with empty boundary list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_exceptionalIdeal: The chart description of the exceptional ideal gives strict normal crossings with empty boundary, so its closed subscheme is smooth over the field. The ideal itself is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, by the defining property of the blowup applied to the pulled-back center. Together these are the smooth divisor conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comp_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: Over the center, the blowup charts are étale over affine space, so the structural morphism is smooth on an open neighborhood of every point there. Over the complement of the center, the blowup identifies with the corresponding open of the original smooth scheme, so it is smooth there as well. These opens cover the blowup, and smoothness is local on the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ι_comp_of_etaleChart: The chart is étale, hence smooth. Affine space is smooth over the field. The structural morphism of the open is the composite of the chart with that of affine space, and smoothness is closed under composition.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: At the image of a point choose an affine open where the ideal has a nonzerodivisor generator. In the open subscheme choose a small affine neighborhood lying over it. Refine their intersection in the ambient scheme to a neighborhood that is basic in the original affine open and lies in the image of the smaller neighborhood. Restriction to this basic open is localization, which preserves the nonzerodivisor. The corresponding inverse-image open in the open subscheme is affine and has an isomorphic section ring. The pulled-back ideal is generated there by the image of the original generator, which remains a nonzerodivisor.

The product equality gives both product containments. Cancel the common locally generated nonzerodivisor ideal in each containment to get both inclusions between the two ideals. They are therefore equal.
Restriction to an open preserves local generation by a nonzerodivisor. Apply cancellation of this common ideal to the equality of products on the open subscheme.
The ideal quotient supplies one solution. Any other solution has the same product with the locally nonzerodivisor factor. Canceling that factor gives equality with the ideal quotient.
Use the ideal quotient of the given input by the locally principal factor. The containment hypothesis ensures that multiplying the quotient by this factor recovers the input ideal.

Fix an affine open and a section of the first ideal. Around each point choose an affine open where the common factor is generated by a nonzerodivisor. Refine the intersection to a neighborhood that is basic in both affine opens. The generator remains a nonzerodivisor after localization, so the product inclusion there allows cancellation. Hence the original section restricts to the second ideal on these basic opens. Clearing denominators puts a power of each defining section times the original section in the second ideal. The powers generate the unit ideal because their basic opens cover. This puts the section in the second ideal on the entire affine open.

The product is contained in the input ideal by the definition of the ideal quotient. Conversely, start with a section of the input ideal on an affine open. Cover that open by basic opens where the common divisor ideal is principal. On each, multiplication by the principal ideal recovers the input ideal from the localized quotient. Clearing denominators therefore gives a power of the basic-open section whose product with the original section belongs to the desired product downstairs. These powers generate the unit ideal since their basic opens cover the affine open. A combination equal to one proves the reverse inclusion.

At each point choose an affine neighborhood where the ideal is generated by a nonzerodivisor. The power of the principal ideal is generated by the corresponding power of its generator. A power of a nonzerodivisor is again a nonzerodivisor, including the zeroth power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.basicOpen_appLE: The basic open of a pulled-back section is the inverse image of the basic open of the original section. The section map to the specified source open also restricts the pulled-back section. Its basic open after restriction is the intersection with that source open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_image_of_isOpenImmersion: An open immersion sends an open subset to an open subset. The open image is defined with underlying set equal to the pointwise image of the given open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_preimage_opens: The inverse image open is defined using the inverse image of the underlying set of points under the continuous base map. Its underlying set is therefore the stated inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_le_exceptionalIdeal_pow: Pullback preserves inclusion and powers of ideal sheaves. Applying it to the given containment puts the total transform in the corresponding power of the pulled-back center, which is the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_controlledTransform_of_mul_eq_comap: Both the stated ideal and the controlled transform multiply by the same exceptional power to give the total transform. The factorization is unique by cancellation of this locally nonzerodivisor ideal, so they agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_controlledTrans: The controlled transform is the ideal quotient of the total transform by the specified power of the exceptional ideal. The blowup property makes this power locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and the total transform is contained in it. Multiplying the ideal quotient by that power therefore recovers the total transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.existsUnique_pow_mul_eq_comap: The specified power of the exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. The pulled-back input ideal is contained in that power by pullback of the original containment. The existence and uniqueness result for division by a locally nonzerodivisor ideal gives the required factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.existsUnique_pow_mul_eq_comap_of_isBlowu: By the defining property of the blowup, the pulled-back center is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. It is the exceptional ideal, so the existence and uniqueness result for dividing by its power applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_ideal_eq_span_singleto: Being locally generated by a nonzerodivisor means that at every point one can choose an affine neighborhood where the section ideal has such a generator. Apply the definition to this point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_mem_subset: The chosen open is a neighborhood of the point. Since affine opens form a basis, an affine open containing that point lies inside it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_basicOpen_ideal_eq_span_singleton: Choose an affine neighborhood of the point where the ideal is principal. Find a neighborhood of the point that is basic both in that neighborhood and in the indicated affine open. The ideal on it is generated by the restriction of the chosen generator. The identification of the basic opens gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ideal_eq_span_singleton_congr: The two affine opens are equal, so they have the same section ring and the given ideal has the same sections on them. Transport the principal generator along this identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_mul_colon: On the basic open the first factor is principal and contains the input ideal. Multiplying that principal factor by the corresponding ideal quotient recovers the input ideal there. The ideal quotient and product commute with this basic-open localization, so the section belongs after localization to the desired product. Clearing denominators gives the indicated power downstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_algebraMap_mem_map: Write the image of the element in the localization as a fraction with numerator in the ideal and denominator a power of the inverted element. Cross-multiplication gives an equality in the localization. Multiplying by another power makes the equality hold in the original ring, so the product of those powers sends the element into the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafColon_ideal: The ideal sheaf is constructed by assigning on each affine open the ideal quotient of the two given section ideals. The localization result makes these assignments compatible, and evaluation on the indicated open gives the defining formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafColon_ideal_map_basicOpen: A basic-open restriction is localization at its defining section. The section ring of the affine open is Noetherian, so the second ideal is finitely generated. Localization therefore commutes with this ideal quotient. Both extended ideals are the section ideals on the basic open, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_ideal_of_mul_le_mul: Multiply a section in the first ideal by the principal generator. The product containment says the result is the same generator times some section in the second ideal. Since the generator is a nonzerodivisor, cancellation identifies the two sections. This proves the section-ideal containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_opensι_le: Every point in the image of the smaller open comes from a point of the open subscheme. All points in the image of that subscheme’s inclusion lie in the defining open, giving the containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_preimage_opensι: The image of the inverse image of a set is its intersection with the image of the map. Here the image of the inclusion is the original open, which contains the indicated smaller open. The intersection is thus the smaller open itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_forall_ideal_le: The order on ideal sheaves is the containment order on their section ideals on every affine open. The given family of containments is therefore the claimed sheaf containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_colon_eq_colon_map_away: Extending the original ideal quotient gives an ideal whose product with the extended second ideal lies in the extended first ideal. This proves one inclusion. Conversely, write a section of the ideal quotient upstairs as a fraction. Multiply it by each of a finite set of generators of the second ideal downstairs. The products belong to the extended first ideal, so for each generator a power of the inverted element puts the product of the original numerator and that generator into the first ideal. Take the maximum of the finitely many exponents. The resulting power times the numerator sends every generator into the first ideal, hence belongs to the original ideal quotient. Its fraction with the denominator multiplied by the same power represents the original section. This proves the other inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comp_appLE: Restricting a target section to the smaller target open and then pulling it back to the source open gives the same section as pulling it back directly from the larger target open. This is compatibility of the scheme morphism with restriction maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_colon_span: Multiplication by the given element sends each generator into the ideal. Since multiplication is linear, it sends every element of their span into the ideal as well. This is exactly membership in the ideal quotient by that span.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_ideal_apply: The product of two ideal sheaves is defined on affine opens by multiplying their section ideals. Evaluating on the chosen open gives this product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_ideal_le_mul_ideal: Evaluate the inclusion of products on the chosen affine open. Evaluation of a product is the product of the section ideals, giving the stated inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_ideal_apply: At exponent zero both sides are the unit ideal. Evaluation on an affine open preserves products, so the equality at each exponent gives the equality at the next.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_opensι: The underlying map of an open inclusion takes each point of the open subscheme to its ambient point. Its image is exactly the underlying set of the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictAppIso_hom: The open immersion identifies an open in its source with its image. The section-ring isomorphism uses pullback from the image open to the given source open. Its forward map is that pullback on sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_cover_basicOpen: The stated cover consists of basic opens of the given sections. Any maximal ideal containing all those sections would give a point in the affine open missed by the cover. Therefore the sections generate the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_forall_exists_mem_basicOp: The given basic opens cover the affine open. If their elements generated a proper ideal, some maximal ideal would contain them all. The corresponding point would lie in none of those basic opens, contradicting the cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_singleton_mul_colon: The product is contained in the original ideal by the defining property of the ideal quotient. For the reverse inclusion, express an element of the original ideal as a multiple of the principal generator, using the given containment in the principal ideal. The multiplier sends the generator into the original ideal and hence sends all its multiples there. It belongs to the ideal quotient, so the original element lies in the product.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.X_mem_coordIdeal: The hypothesis makes the variable one of the specified generators. Every generator belongs to the ideal it generates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.X_mem_nonZeroDivisors: Multiplication by the specified variable increases that variable’s exponent by one in every monomial. The coefficient of each original monomial can be read from the corresponding shifted monomial in the product. If the product is zero, all original coefficients are zero. Thus multiplication is injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.awayCoordGenEquivMvPolynomial_invFun_C: The polynomial-to-chart map evaluates constants by the composition of constant-polynomial inclusion and the canonical chart map. This gives the value of the given constant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.awayCoordGenEquivMvPolynomial_invFun_X: The polynomial-to-chart map is defined by assigning a chart fraction to every nondistinguished center variable and the canonical chart image to every other variable. Evaluating an individual variable gives that assignment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.awayCoordGenEquivMvPolynomial_invFun_X_s: The distinguished variable is excluded from the fraction case by equality of its index with the distinguished one. Its image is therefore its canonical image in the chart ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.awayCoordGenEquivMvPolynomial_symm_comp_: The chart equivalence was chosen with the property that its inverse, composed with the coordinate substitution, equals the canonical chart homomorphism. Applying that defining property gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartToMvPolynomial_apply: By construction, the map first views a degree-zero homogeneous fraction as an ordinary fraction and then applies the localization lift. Evaluating at the given fraction gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartToMvPolynomial_chartRingHom: A downstairs polynomial maps to a homogeneous fraction with its degree-zero image as numerator and one as denominator. The chart-to-polynomial map applies the Rees lift to that numerator. On degree zero the lift is the original coordinate substitution, proving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartToMvPolynomial_mvPolynomialToChart: The composite fixes constants by the degree-zero substitution rule. It fixes any variable outside the fraction case because substitution preserves that variable. In the remaining case, the chart fraction times the distinguished chart variable equals the canonical image of the original variable. Applying the chart-to-polynomial map gives the product of the image of the fraction with the distinguished variable equal to the original variable times the distinguished variable. The distinguished variable is a nonzerodivisor, so cancellation shows that the fraction maps to the original variable. The composite fixes all generators and is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_coordIdealGen: The selected ideal element is the variable together with its membership in the coordinate ideal. Forgetting the membership gives the variable itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_reesDegreeZeroEquiv: The degree-zero identification sends the coefficient to the corresponding constant polynomial in the Rees algebra. Viewed in the full Rees algebra this is exactly the coefficient-ring inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubst_C: The substitution is an algebra homomorphism over the coefficient ring. It consequently fixes the image of each scalar as a constant polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubst_X: The substitution is defined by polynomial evaluation with the stated assignment on variables. A variable evaluates to its assigned polynomial, giving the indicated conditional formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubst_X_of_mem: The hypothesis is exactly the condition for multiplying the variable by the distinguished variable in the substitution. Evaluating the chosen variable therefore gives this product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubst_X_of_not_mem_erase: The condition required to multiply by the distinguished variable fails. The original variable is therefore its own substituted value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubst_X_self: The distinguished index fails the condition of being distinct from itself. Thus substitution leaves the distinguished variable unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_eq_span: The coordinate ideal is defined to be generated by the variables whose indices lie in the chosen set. This is the span of the image of that set under the variable assignment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ringEquiv_away_mvPolynomial: The polynomial-to-chart homomorphism has the chart-to-polynomial map as a left inverse, so it is injective. The homogeneous fraction argument shows it is surjective. Its inverse is therefore a ring equivalence from the chart ring to the polynomial ring. The compatibility of the forward polynomial-to-chart map with substitution is exactly the required equation for the inverse equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homogeneousLocalizationVal_apply: The map from homogeneous localization to ordinary localization sends a homogeneous fraction of degree zero to the same fraction in the ordinary localization. This is the stated underlying-value map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iSup_opensRange_affineBlowupChart_coordI: The basic opens of all degree-one Rees generators cover the blowup. If a point were missed by the charts indexed by the selected variables, its homogeneous prime would contain their degree-one Rees elements. Those variables span the center ideal, so linearity of the degree-one construction would put every degree-one generator in the prime. This contradicts membership in one of the basic opens of the full cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_reesAlgebraToMvPolynomial_powers: The distinguished Rees generator maps to one under the lift. Each power therefore also maps to one, which is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_coordIdeal_coordBlowupSubst: The extended ideal is generated by the substituted center variables. The distinguished variable is among them and is fixed. Every other center variable becomes a multiple of it. Thus the extended ideal is exactly the principal ideal generated by the distinguished variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToChart_coordBlowupSubst: Compare the composite with the canonical chart homomorphism on constants and variables. Constants are unchanged by substitution and then map to their usual chart images. A nondistinguished center variable is multiplied by the distinguished variable under substitution. Under the map to the chart this becomes its chart fraction times the distinguished variable, which is its original chart image. Every other variable is fixed by substitution and goes to its canonical chart image. The maps therefore agree on all polynomials.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToChart_surjective: Multiply an arbitrary chart element by a power of the distinguished chart variable to obtain a canonical image of a downstairs polynomial, using the homogeneous fraction description. Apply the chart-to-polynomial map and then the polynomial-to-chart map. The result multiplied by the same power equals the same canonical image, by compatibility of the substitution with the map back to the chart. The distinguished variable is a nonzerodivisor in the chart ring, so cancel its power. This proves that the chart element lies in the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reesAlgebraToMvPolynomial_algebraMap: The universal Rees algebra lift extends the coordinate substitution on the coefficient ring of the Rees algebra. In particular its value on a degree-zero element from the original polynomial ring is the substituted polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reesAlgebraToMvPolynomial_reesGenerator: The degree-one lift sends a Rees generator to the quotient of its substituted coefficient by the chosen principal generator. The distinguished variable substitutes to itself, so this quotient is one, uniquely by the nonzerodivisor property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reesGenerator_mem_homogeneousIdeal_of_sp: Apply the span argument to the underlying ideal of the homogeneous ideal. Its assumptions and conclusion are the same membership statements for the degree-one Rees elements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reesGenerator_mem_of_span: The degree-one Rees element associated to a coefficient in the ideal depends linearly on that coefficient. Each selected coefficient gives a Rees element in the stated ideal. Additivity and closure under multiplication by degree-zero coefficients therefore put the Rees element of every linear combination of those coefficients in the ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.card_le_ringKrullDim_stalk: The chosen coordinates belong to the point prime, so their germs lie in the maximal ideal. The coordinate parameter theorem supplies a list of sections of length equal to the local Krull dimension, containing all the chosen coordinate sections, whose germs generate the maximal ideal. The coordinates are distinct as sections. Choosing a position for each coordinate gives an injection into the list positions, proving the bound. For an empty choice the bound follows from nonnegativity of the dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_injective: The section ring is nonzero because the affine open contains a point. It is flat over the polynomial ring by étaleness. A nonzero flat module over the polynomial domain is torsion-free and faithful, so the polynomial algebra map is injective. Distinct coordinate variables are distinct in the polynomial ring, and their images are the chart coordinates. These images are therefore distinct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mem_primeIdealOf_of_restrictIdeal_: The section ideal on the affine chart is generated by the specified coordinate, so it contains that coordinate. Since the point belongs to the support, its prime contains the whole section ideal. It therefore contains the coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_primeIdealOf_of_mem_support: At a point of the support every section in the ideal vanishes, meaning the point is outside its basic open. Equivalently the section’s germ is a nonunit in the local ring and lies in its maximal ideal. Contracting the maximal ideal to the affine section ring shows that every such section belongs to the point prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivial_sections_of_mem: The point determines a proper prime of the affine section ring. If zero and one were equal, then the prime would contain one and be the whole ring. Thus the section ring is nontrivial.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_ideal_eq_span: After restriction to the affine open, the ideal is the coordinate ideal of the restricted chart. On an affine chart its section ideal is generated by the chart coordinates at the given indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_singleton_ideal_eq: Apply the formula for the section ideal of a coordinate subset to the singleton. Its set of generators has just the corresponding coordinate, so the resulting ideal is principal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.restrictIdeal_coordIdeal: The original coordinate ideal is the pullback of the corresponding coordinate-subspace ideal on affine space. Restricting it to the smaller open adds pullback along the inclusion. By composition, this is pullback along the restricted chart map, which defines the coordinate ideal there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.restrictOpens_map: The chart on the smaller open is defined by composing its inclusion with the given chart map. This gives the asserted formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.saturation_coordIdeal_of_ne: On an affine open, a section of the saturation has some power of the second coordinate sending it into the first coordinate ideal. Distinctness of the coordinates allows cancellation of that power, so the section is already in the first ideal. The reverse inclusion uses power zero. The affine section equalities give the sheaf equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.saturation_coordIdeal_self: On each affine open the coordinate ideal is principal. The first power of its generator sends every section into the ideal, so saturation by that generator makes the ideal the whole section ring. This holds on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.saturation_mul_coordIdeal: On each affine open in the chart, the product of the two coordinate ideals is the ideal of the first coordinate multiplied by the second coordinate. The two coordinates are distinct, so multiplication by the second is injective modulo the first coordinate ideal. Saturating the product by powers of the second removes the explicit factor and leaves the first coordinate ideal. This calculation on every affine open gives the sheaf equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_restrictOpens_map_comp_affine: The chart’s composite with the structure map of affine space equals the original structural morphism on its domain. Precomposing with the inclusion of the smaller open gives the same equality for the restricted chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_restrictOpens_map_etale: The inclusion of the smaller open is an open immersion and hence étale. Its composite with the original étale chart is therefore étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_span_coord_of_coord_pow_mul_mem: Multiplication by the second coordinate is injective modulo the ideal of the first, since their indices differ. Cancel the second coordinate one factor at a time. Formally, at exponent zero the result is the given membership, and at each successor apply the induction hypothesis to the product with one factor and then use single-factor cancellation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_coordIdeal: If the divisor index is the exceptional one, its strict transform has the unit ideal on this chart. A different center index has the corresponding coordinate ideal after removing the exceptional factor. An index outside the center has the corresponding coordinate ideal directly. These cases give the stated formula.

The total transform is already the corresponding coordinate ideal on the blowup chart, because the coordinate is outside the center. Its index differs from the exceptional index. Saturation by the exceptional coordinate therefore leaves the total-transform ideal unchanged.

The total transform of the distinguished coordinate ideal is the exceptional coordinate ideal itself on the chart. Saturating that ideal by the exceptional coordinate gives the unit ideal. Thus the strict transform is empty on this chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_of_eq_top: The total transform restricts to the unit ideal because the original ideal is the unit ideal on the downstairs chart. The strict transform contains the total-transform ideal. Its restriction thus contains the unit ideal and must be the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_of_mem_of_: On the chart the total transform is the product of the coordinate ideal for the chosen divisor and the exceptional coordinate ideal. Formation of the strict transform commutes with restriction and takes saturation by the exceptional ideal. For distinct coordinates, saturating this product removes the exceptional factor and gives the chosen chart coordinate ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordBlowupSubstMap_coordSubspaceI: Each center coordinate pulls back to a multiple of the distinguished coordinate. The distinguished coordinate itself is one of the center generators and pulls back to itself. Thus the ideal generated by the pulled-back coordinates is exactly its principal ideal, which gives the exceptional ideal sheaf.

A principal ideal pulls back to the ideal generated by the pullback of its generator. The coordinate for the specified center index pulls back to its chart counterpart times the distinguished coordinate. The principal ideal of a product equals the product of the principal ideals, giving the formula for the sheaves.
The coordinate outside the center pulls back to its unchanged counterpart. Extending its principal ideal along the section map gives the same coordinate ideal on the source.
The pullback of the distinguished coordinate is that same coordinate on the source. Its principal ideal sheaf therefore pulls back to the corresponding principal ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordIdeal_center: By the chart square, pulling back the center ideal reduces to extending the ideal generated by the center coordinates along the affine-space substitution. This gives the distinguished coordinate ideal. Its pullback to the upstairs chart yields the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordIdeal_of_coordBlowupSubstMap: A coordinate ideal on the downstairs chart is pulled back from the corresponding ideal of affine space. Compose this pullback with the given map of chart domains. The commutative square identifies this composite with pullback first along the substitution and then along the upstairs chart map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordIdeal_singleton_of_mem: Use the commutative chart square to compute the pullback on affine space first. For this center index the affine-space substitution gives a product of two principal coordinate ideals. Pullback to the upstairs chart preserves their product and gives the two stated chart coordinate ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordIdeal_singleton_of_notMem: Compute the pullback across the substitution on affine space using the chart square. The ideal of the coordinate outside the center is unchanged by the substitution, and pulling it back along the upstairs chart gives the stated ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_coordIdeal_singleton_self: The chart square reduces the computation to the affine-space substitution. It preserves the principal ideal of the distinguished coordinate, whose pullback by the upstairs chart map is the desired chart coordinate ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_appTop_coord: A morphism to affine space specified by a vector of sections pulls each coordinate back to the corresponding entry of that vector. Here the entry is multiplied by the distinguished coordinate precisely for a center index distinct from the distinguished one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_appTop_coord_of_mem: The chosen index lies among the center coordinates and differs from the distinguished index. The substitution therefore pulls back the coordinate to the product of its chart counterpart with the distinguished coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_appTop_coord_of_notM: An index outside the center fails the condition for multiplication in the substitution. Hence its coordinate pulls back to the same coordinate on the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_appTop_coord_self: The distinguished index cannot differ from itself, so its entry in the substitution vector is simply its coordinate. That coordinate has unchanged pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBlowupSubstMap_comp_affineSpaceFinT: The substitution map is defined by a vector of sections over the given base map. By the universal property of affine space, its composite with the target structural map is the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_empty: On affine space the coordinate ideal comes from the ideal of global sections generated by the selected coordinates. With an empty selection this is the zero ideal. Its extension to every affine open remains zero, so the sheaf is the zero ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_singleton: The global ideal of a coordinate subspace is generated by the images of the selected indices under the coordinate assignment. The image of this singleton is the singleton consisting of the indicated coordinate. Taking its associated sheaf gives the principal coordinate ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_mvPolynomialToExceptionalQuoti: The map back from the exceptional quotient sends the images of each coefficient and each variable to the same coefficient and variable. This is checked on a representative of each coefficient class and on the nondistinguished center coordinates. Thus the composition is the identity on the polynomial ring and the given map is injective. For surjectivity, every exceptional quotient element is represented by a chart section, and every chart section is the evaluation of a polynomial over the downstairs ring. Applying exceptional evaluation to that polynomial gives a preimage. The two resulting maps from the downstairs polynomial ring to the exceptional quotient agree on coefficients. They agree on variables because the retained indices map to their chart coordinates, while the other indices pull back their corresponding downstairs coordinates unchanged. This proves the preimage formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mem_ideal_of_mem: On the affine chart the center ideal is generated by the coordinates at the selected indices. The indicated coordinate is one of these generators, so it belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalEval_C: The coefficient map in this evaluation first reduces a section modulo the center ideal and then embeds its class as a constant. Applying the evaluation to a constant yields that value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalEval_X: An individual variable evaluates to the value assigned to its index. This is the designated polynomial or constant associated to the index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalEval_coordRelation: For a nondistinguished center index, the product in the relation evaluates to zero because the distinguished variable is sent to the zero class of the distinguished downstairs coordinate. The original coordinate subtracted in the relation also vanishes modulo the center ideal. At any other index, the variable is assigned the constant class of the corresponding downstairs coordinate, canceling the constant term of the relation. Thus the relation always evaluates to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalEval_eq_zero_of_mem_span_coor: Each chart relation is killed by the evaluation. The kernel is an ideal containing the relations, so it contains their span. This proves vanishing on the relation ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalHomOfChart_coord: The chart coordinate is the evaluation of its polynomial variable. Apply the compatibility of chart evaluation with the map to exceptional polynomials. The image is the specified assignment at that variable’s index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalHomOfChart_coordEvalHom: Under the chart-ring presentation, the evaluation of a polynomial corresponds to its class modulo the coordinate relations. The inverse presentation map recovers that class, and the map induced by exceptional evaluation takes it to the exceptional evaluation of the representative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalHomOfChart_coord_self: The distinguished chart coordinate evaluates to the constant class of the corresponding downstairs coordinate, since its index was omitted from the variable set. That downstairs coordinate belongs to the center ideal, so its class and its constant polynomial are zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalHomOfQuotientCoord_mk: The chart map kills the distinguished coordinate and therefore factors across the exceptional quotient. Evaluating the resulting map on a class is the same as applying the chart map to the representative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_ideal_blowupChart_domai: On the chosen chart the pulled-back center is the distinguished coordinate ideal. The chart is affine, so evaluating this coordinate ideal on its domain gives the principal ideal generated by that coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalQuotientBaseHom_mk: The map from the downstairs center quotient is induced by pulling back a section to the chart and then reducing modulo its exceptional coordinate. This composite kills the center ideal, so applying the induced map to a class gives precisely the class of the pulled-back representative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalQuotientEquivMvPolynomial_mk_: The inverse equivalence sends the constant polynomial of the downstairs class to the class of the pulled-back section, by the coefficient formula. Applying the equivalence to this equality gives the result.

The inverse equivalence sends the variable for a nondistinguished center index to the class of the corresponding chart coordinate. Apply the equivalence to recover the stated variable from that class.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalQuotientEquivMvPolynomial_sym: The ring equivalence was chosen as the inverse of the bijective polynomial evaluation map to the exceptional quotient. Its inverse is consequently that polynomial evaluation map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalQuotientEquiv_mk_appLE: The selected blowup chart has the requisite pullback square. Apply the evaluation formula for classes of pulled-back sections to this chart. Its exceptional quotient identifies that class with the constant polynomial of the original class on the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalQuotientEquiv_mk_coord: The chosen blowup chart satisfies the pullback hypothesis of the coordinate formula for the exceptional quotient equivalence. Since the index is in the center and differs from the distinguished one, its coordinate class corresponds to the variable with that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalVar_of_mem: For a nondistinguished center index, the assignment is defined to take the variable with that index in the polynomial ring over the center quotient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalVar_of_not_mem: For an index outside the nondistinguished center set, the assignment is defined to take the constant polynomial given by the class of the downstairs coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffineOpen_blowupChart_domain: The selected blowup chart is a pullback of the affine-space substitution along the downstairs chart. The downstairs domain is affine by hypothesis, so this pullback chart is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffineOpen_domain_of_isPullback: Both affine spaces and the downstairs open subscheme are affine. Their scheme pullback is affine because it is the spectrum of the pushout of the section rings. The assumed square identifies the blowup chart domain with this pullback, so the domain is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mk_coord_eq_zero_of_mem: The indicated center coordinate belongs to the center ideal. The quotient by that ideal sends it to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToExceptionalQuotient_C: Evaluating a constant polynomial uses only the coefficient map. Here this is the map from the downstairs center quotient to the exceptional quotient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToExceptionalQuotient_X: The evaluation sends each variable indexed by a nondistinguished center coordinate to the class of that chart coordinate in the exceptional quotient. The claimed equality is the defining value on this variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quotientMk_comp_appLE_eq_zero_of_mem: Each generator of the center ideal pulls back to a multiple of the exceptional coordinate. The distinguished generator pulls back to that coordinate itself, and the other center generators pull back to products with it. Thus the entire center ideal maps into the exceptional coordinate ideal. Its image vanishes in the quotient.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.C_coeff_mem_of_minimal_prime: Contract the minimal prime to the coefficient ring and extend it back to the polynomial ring. The contraction is prime and its extension is prime by the polynomial-domain argument. The extension is contained in the original prime, so minimality makes them equal. Consequently every coefficient of a polynomial in the prime belongs to the contraction, and its constant polynomial belongs to the original prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.C_mul_powProd_X_eq_monomial: The product of variable powers is the monomial of the indicated exponent vector with coefficient one. Multiplying it by the constant polynomial changes its coefficient to the specified scalar, giving the stated monomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartMonomialIdeal_eq_span: The chart monomial ideal is defined as the ideal spanned by the chart monomials whose nondistinguished degree is at most the indicated total degree. This is the generating set in the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartMonomial_mem_chartMonomialIdeal: The exponent vector satisfies the degree bound, so its chart monomial is in the specified generating set. It therefore belongs to the ideal spanned by that set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartMonomial_mul_coord_mem_chartMonomia: Increase the exponent at the chosen nondistinguished index by one. Its total degree increases by one, so when the requested degree also increases by one, the distinguished exponent stays unchanged. The product is the chart monomial for this new vector and satisfies the new degree bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartMonomial_mul_coord_self_mem_chartMo: Multiplying by the distinguished coordinate increases its exponent by one and leaves the nondistinguished exponents fixed. As those exponents had total degree at most the original degree, the resulting monomial is an allowed generator at the next total degree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_not_subset_support: Suppose the controlled transform contains an entire irreducible component of the exceptional support. Choose the generic point of that component. Its image lies in the center. Use affine étale center coordinates downstairs and an affine blowup chart containing the generic point. The prime of this point is minimal among primes containing the exceptional coordinate. Indeed, a smaller such prime gives a point of the exceptional support whose closure contains the component, and maximality and uniqueness of the generic point force equality. The controlled-transform section ideal is contained in this prime by the support assumption. The chart identifies the exceptional quotient with a polynomial ring over the center quotient and gives the required coordinate substitution. The order bound on the center puts the original section ideal inside the prescribed center power, and the total-transform identity gives the appropriate factor of the exceptional coordinate. Apply the monomial calculation to put the original ideal in the next power of the contraction of the generic prime. That contraction corresponds to a point of the center because every center coordinate maps into the generic prime. Passing to its stalk gives an order at least one larger than the assumed constant order on the center, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_mem_closure_singleton_of_maximal_i: The closure of the second point is irreducible and lies in the closed set. It contains the first point and hence contains its closure, which is the given maximal irreducible subset. Maximality identifies the two closures. In a scheme points with equal closures are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closure_singleton_eq_of_maximal_i: The maximal irreducible subset is closed because taking its closure preserves irreducibility and containment in the given closed set. Schemes have a generic point for every irreducible closed subset, giving a point whose closure is the required subset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_primeIdealOf_eq: The affine open is isomorphic to the spectrum of its section ring. Take the point of the open corresponding under the inverse isomorphism to the given prime. Its associated prime is the original prime by the inverse identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_comap_pow_succ_of_map_le_span_p: Reduce the chart ring modulo the distinguished coordinate and use the given presentation as a polynomial ring over the center quotient. The chosen prime contains the kernel of this quotient map, so its image is prime and its contraction recovers the chosen prime. It is a minimal prime of the polynomial ring, since any smaller prime contracts to a smaller chart prime containing the distinguished coordinate. Now express an element of the original ideal as a finite linear combination of degree-bound chart monomials, using containment in the prescribed power of the center ideal. Under pullback each summand contains the same distinguished-coordinate power. The assumed containment in that power times the upstairs ideal, and cancellation of the nonzerodivisor power, put the remaining sum in the upstairs ideal and hence in the chosen prime. In the polynomial quotient this sum has one monomial for each selected exponent vector, with coefficients given by the original coefficients modulo the center. Distinct chosen monomials give distinct exponent vectors. The coefficient property for a minimal prime puts each constant coefficient in the image prime, so the original coefficients belong to the contracted prime downstairs. All center coordinates also belong to that contraction, by the chart formulas. Thus each original monomial contributes the designated power of the contracted prime, and each coefficient contributes one more factor. Summing yields containment in the next power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_of_maximal_isIrreducible_subset: The closure of the subset is irreducible and contained in the closed ambient set. Since it contains the original subset, maximality makes the closure equal to that subset, which is therefore closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPrime_map_C: The quotient of the coefficient ring by the prime is a domain. The polynomial ring over that quotient is also a domain. The extension of the prime to the polynomial ring is the kernel of coefficientwise reduction to this domain. It is therefore prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_orderAt_of_ideal_le_pow: Extend the section-ideal containment to the stalk along the germ map. Extension preserves powers, and the extended point prime lies in the maximal ideal. Thus the stalk ideal is contained in the stated power of the maximal ideal, giving the lower bound for its order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_C_eq_ker_map_quotientMk: The coefficientwise quotient map kills a polynomial exactly when every coefficient belongs to the original ideal. Such polynomials form the ideal generated by the constant polynomials coming from that ideal. This identifies the kernel with the stated extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_chartMonomial: Each nondistinguished center factor pulls back to the corresponding chart factor times the distinguished coordinate. Their total degree contributes that many distinguished factors. The initial distinguished power pulls back unchanged. Its exponent is the difference between the requested degree and the total degree of the other factors, so the exponents add to exactly the requested degree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_germ_primeIdealOf_le_maximalIdeal: The stalk is the localization at the point’s prime. Every element of that prime maps into the maximal ideal of the localization. Hence the ideal generated by their images is contained in the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_powProd: A ring homomorphism preserves finite products and nonnegative powers. Apply it to each factor in the product to obtain the corresponding power of the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_powProd_eq_powProd_mul_pow_totalDegr: Apply the homomorphism to each factor. Each image is a power of the product of the assigned target element and the same common factor. Commutativity lets us collect all powers of the common factor into one power with exponent equal to the total degree. The remaining factors give the product of powers of the target elements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_ideal_le_primeIdealOf: On an affine open, a point of the support has prime containing the section ideal. Conversely, if its prime contains the section ideal, then extending to the stalk puts the stalk ideal inside the maximal ideal. This is the condition for membership in the support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_coord_mem_chartMonomialIdeal_succ: Multiplication by the chosen coordinate is linear. On each generating chart monomial it gives a generator at the next degree, using the distinguished-coordinate rule or the nondistinguished rule according to the index. The same containment therefore holds for the entire generated ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_mem_chartMonomialIdeal_succ: Fix an element of the chart monomial ideal. Multiplying it by any of the center coordinates lands in the next chart monomial ideal by the coordinate multiplication result. Multiplication by the fixed element is linear, so the result extends to the ideal generated by these coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.powProd_add: For each variable, a power with the sum of two exponents is the product of the two individual powers. Multiply these identities over the union of the supports, using a factor of one for each zero exponent. Commutativity groups the factors into the separate products.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.powProd_mem_pow_totalDegree: The product of powers and the total degree are taken over the support of the exponent vector. Each base element belongs to the ideal, so the finite product lies in the ideal power whose exponent is the sum of those exponents.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.powProd_single: Only the indicated index can have a nonzero exponent. All other factors are one, so the product is the single specified power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.powProd_zero: The exponent vector has empty support, so the product of powers is the empty product, which is one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_span_image_le_chartMonomialIdeal: At degree zero the chart monomial with zero exponents is one, so the degree-zero chart monomial ideal contains the unit ideal. Induct on the exponent. Products of an element of the previous power and an element of the coordinate ideal generate the next power. By induction and the multiplication result each such product belongs to the next chart monomial ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_pow_mem_pow_sum: For each index, the given element’s specified power belongs to the same power of the ideal. Successively multiply these memberships, using that multiplication of ideal powers adds their exponents. The empty product belongs to the zeroth power. This proves membership for the entire finite product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalDegree_add: Total degree sums the entries of the exponent vector. Every entry of the sum of the vectors is the sum of the corresponding entries. Summing over the union of their finite supports gives the sum of the two total degrees.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalDegree_single: All exponent entries outside the indicated index are zero. Summing the entries therefore gives the specified exponent, including the case when that exponent is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalDegree_zero: The zero exponent vector has empty support. The sum of its exponent entries is the empty sum, which is zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.comap_coordIdeal: The coordinate ideal on a chart is the pullback of the corresponding coordinate ideal on affine space. For the pulled-back chart its map is a composite. Functoriality makes this pullback the pullback to the original chart followed by pullback along the restricted morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.comap_map: The pulled-back chart is defined with map given by the restricted morphism followed by the original chart map. Its map is therefore that composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_comap_map_comp_affineSpaceFin: The original chart commutes with the structural map to the field. Composing its field equation with the restricted morphism gives the composite through the downstairs open inclusion. The restriction square identifies that composite with the upstairs inclusion followed by the original morphism, giving the required equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_etaleChart_comap_map: The restricted morphism and the original chart map are both étale by hypothesis. Étale morphisms are closed under composition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_of_isBlowupAlongId: At a point whose image belongs to the divisor support, take a downstairs coordinate chart for the divisor and shrink it into the complement of the center. The blowup is an isomorphism there, and composing with this isomorphism gives an étale chart upstairs. Its coordinate ideal is the pullback of the original divisor ideal. At any other point choose an upstairs étale chart in the inverse image of the complement of the divisor support, where the pullback is the unit ideal. Thus the pulled-back ideal satisfies the local coordinate criterion for a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_mul_of_disjoint_support: At a point of either divisor, choose an étale chart making that divisor a coordinate divisor. Shrink to avoid the support of the other divisor, which is possible by disjointness. The ideal of the other divisor is the unit ideal there, so the product is the same coordinate ideal. At a point outside both supports choose a chart in their common complement, where both ideals are unit ideals. These local descriptions give the smooth divisor property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_eq_top_of_notMem_sup: Pulling back along the indicated morphism and restricting to the open is the same as pulling back along the composite from the open subscheme. The composite avoids the support by hypothesis. Thus the pulled-back ideal is the unit ideal on that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_mul: Restriction is pullback along the open inclusion. Pullback extends the section ideals and preserves their product, giving the restriction formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_mul_of_disjoint_support: At a point over the center, the image is outside the second support. On the inverse image of that complement the pullback of the second ideal is the unit ideal, so the total transform of the product equals that of the first ideal. The strict transforms therefore agree there, since both saturate the same total transform by the same exceptional ideal. Away from the center strict transforms agree with the total transforms, and ideal pullback preserves products. These two kinds of opens cover the scheme, giving the equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comp_eq_top_of_le_preimage_compl: Every point of the upstairs open maps into the complement of the center’s support. The pullback of the center ideal along the composite from that open therefore has empty support and is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_length_strictTransform_append_ex: The mapped list has the original length, so the next index is the first position of the appended singleton. This holds the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_strictTransform_append_exception: The given index is in the first part of the appended list. Its entry there is the strict transform of the original entry at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_strictT: Choose a downstairs étale chart with distinct boundary coordinates and a coordinate center, then a blowup chart containing the given point upstairs. Assign the exceptional divisor the distinguished coordinate. An original divisor absent downstairs stays absent. An original divisor defined by the distinguished coordinate has empty strict transform on this chart. Every other present divisor has strict transform given by its corresponding chart coordinate. These remaining indices retain their original distinctness and none is the distinguished index. Together with the exceptional divisor they give the required pointwise chart.

Take a downstairs boundary chart and shrink it to the complement of the center. The blowup restricts to an isomorphism, so transporting the chart upstairs gives an étale chart with the same boundary coordinate assignment. On this open strict transforms equal total transforms, which preserve the coordinate and unit ideals under the transported chart. The exceptional ideal is the unit ideal, so it is assigned no coordinate. The coordinate indices that remain are distinct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_strictTra: At every point choose the strict-transform boundary chart for points over the center or the transported chart for points off the center. This proves the pointwise normal crossings condition. The same charts show each member is a smooth divisor, since its ideal is everywhere locally a coordinate ideal or the unit ideal. Thus the full list is in strict normal crossings position.

Apply the strict-transform and exceptional-divisor result to the list with the specified first member. Taking strict transforms entry by entry gives the strict transform of that member as the first entry, followed by the transformed tail and the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_morphismRestrict_of_isBlowupAlongI: Restrict the blowup to the open, where it remains a blowup of the restricted center ideal. The open avoids the center’s support, so this ideal is the unit ideal. The blowup of the unit ideal is an isomorphism by the universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_strictTransform_append_exceptiona: Taking the strict transform of each entry preserves the number of entries. Appending the exceptional ideal adds exactly one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_preimage: The inverse-image square commutes. Restricting the pulled-back ideal along the upstairs inclusion is consequently the same as restricting the original ideal downstairs and pulling it back along the restricted morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_exceptionalIdeal_eq_top_of: The exceptional ideal is the pullback of the center. Its restriction is the pullback along the composite from the given open. This composite avoids the center support, so the ideal is the unit ideal.
The pointwise hypothesis puts the open in the inverse image of the complement of the center. The exceptional ideal is the unit ideal there, since it is pulled back from the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform_eq_comap_o: Restrict the strict transform to the open, which commutes with its formation. The center ideal pulls back to the unit ideal there because the open lies off its support. The strict transform is saturation of the total transform by this unit ideal. Saturation by powers of one leaves every section ideal unchanged.

The pointwise condition says that the open lies in the inverse image of the complement of the center. On such an open the strict and total transforms agree because the exceptional ideal is the unit ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.complOrderEmb_of_complOrderEmbPreimage_e: If the index lay in the removed set, the construction would return no preimage. Otherwise it chooses an index of the complement whose image is the given one. The specified output is this chosen index, so applying the embedding recovers the original index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_comap_subschemeι_erase: At the image of the point, choose a strict normal crossings chart and shrink it to an affine open. The chosen divisor passes through the image, so it is defined there by one coordinate. Its subscheme inherits an étale chart using the complementary coordinates. Each position of the shortened list comes from its original position skipping the removed entry. If that divisor was absent, its pulled-back ideal remains the unit ideal. If it was present, its coordinate differs from the removed coordinate by the original distinctness condition. It therefore restricts to the corresponding complementary coordinate. Distinct original assignments remain distinct under this restriction, giving all the required properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.getElem_eraseIdx_natSuccAbove: Removing an entry preserves all positions before it and shifts each later entry down by one. Hence an index in the shortened list refers to the same original index before the omission and to the next original index at or after it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_sub: At every point of the selected divisor, the chart obtained by removing its coordinate gives distinct coordinates for the other divisors that meet the chart. Apply the local chart criterion to the remaining boundary restricted to this divisor.
Use the given equality to identify the named ideal with the list member being removed. The statement is then the restriction result for that member and its closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_of_forall: The local étale charts give the pointwise normal crossings condition because each present divisor is assigned a distinct coordinate. They also show that each list member is a smooth divisor, since its ideal is locally either the unit ideal or a single coordinate ideal.
