These are the two parts of the strict normal crossings condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_complOrderEmbPreimage_eq_none: Every index outside the removed set has a preimage under the complement embedding, and the construction returns that chosen preimage. Thus a missing result is possible only for an index in the removed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natSuccAbove_inj: The position map is the identity below the omitted position and adds one at or above it. Both formulas are injective within their ranges, and the two ranges are disjoint. Equal output positions therefore have equal inputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natSuccAbove_ne: A position below the omitted position remains below it. A position at or above it is increased by one and is strictly above it. Neither case gives the omitted position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportSuccAboveToCompl_eq_none: If the original assignment has no coordinate, the first alternative holds. If it has a coordinate, a missing transported value means that coordinate has no preimage under the complement embedding and so belongs to the removed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportSuccAboveToCompl_eq_some: For the transported value to exist, the assignment at the corresponding original list position must have a coordinate index. Applying the complement embedding to the returned complement index recovers this original coordinate, by the choice of preimage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.exists_isAffineOpen_mem_le_d: The chart domain is an open neighborhood of the point. Affine opens form a basis, so there is one containing the point inside that domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.restrictToStrictTransform_ch: The chart map on the strict transform is obtained by restricting the upstairs étale chart to the coordinate subscheme defining the strict transform. The construction uses that map without changing it, giving the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.restrictToStrictTransform_do: The chart on the strict transform is constructed on the inverse image of the original blowup chart domain under the closed subscheme inclusion. This is its domain by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.restrict_chart: The chart field of the restricted blowup chart is defined by restricting the original étale chart to the smaller open. Taking this field gives the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.restrict_domain: The restriction is built with the prescribed smaller open as its domain. Taking its domain gives that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupChart.strictTransform_subschemeι_p: The strict transform of the distinguished coordinate divisor has unit ideal on this chart because its total transform is the exceptional ideal and saturation removes it. Its support on this open is therefore empty. Since the image of the strict-transform subscheme lies in its support, no point of that subscheme maps into the chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_top_top_eq_appTop: For the entire target and source, pulling back the target open gives the entire source. Thus the section map on the chosen opens is the global pullback followed by an identity restriction. It equals the global pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupChart_restrict_map_comp_coordBlowu: Precompose the original chart’s compatibility equation with the inclusion of the smaller domain. On one side this restricts the chart map. On the other side the inclusion followed by the original restricted blowup equals the blowup restricted to the smaller domain. This follows after composing both maps with the downstairs open inclusion, which is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_opensι_ideal_top_eq_map: The section ideal of the pullback to the whole affine open subscheme is the extension of the original section ideal along the section map of the inclusion. That section map is the inverse of the canonical section-ring identification, giving the expression in the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_ideal_top_eq_map: The chart coordinate ideal is obtained by extending the affine-space coordinate ideal along the chart map on global sections. Each generating affine coordinate is sent to the corresponding chart coordinate in the global sections of the open subscheme. Transporting the ideal generated by the ambient chart sections along the canonical section-ring isomorphism therefore gives exactly this ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_map_appTop_coord: By definition the ambient chart coordinate comes from pulling back the affine-space coordinate to the open subscheme and then using its section-ring identification. Applying the inverse identification recovers the original pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_complEmbPreimage: The set of complementary indices in question is defined by filtering all complementary indices according to whether their image belongs to the original set. Thus membership is exactly the stated condition on the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_complEmbPreimage_of_complOrderEmb_eq: The complement embedding sends the chosen index to an element of the original set. This is the membership condition for the filtered set of complementary indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opensι_appLE_top_eq_topIso_inv: The inclusion identifies the section ring over the ambient open with the global sections of the open subscheme. The section map of the inclusion on these opens is precisely the inverse of the canonical identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_subschemeι_eq_coordI: On the affine chart, the section ideal of the center is generated by its coordinate set, and the hypersurface is cut out by the selected coordinate. The section map to the hypersurface is the quotient setting that coordinate to zero. Each other center generator maps to the corresponding coordinate on the induced chart, and every complementary center index arises this way. The extended ideal is therefore generated by the retained coordinates. Equality on global sections of this affine open subscheme gives equality of the ideal sheaves there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictToSubscheme_map_comp_affineSpace: The induced étale chart on the strict transform commutes with the structural map obtained from its inclusion into the blowup. The given factorization identifies this structural map with the one through the original hypersurface. Restricting to the chart domain gives the equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictToSubscheme_map_comp_coordBlowup: Compare the two maps to affine space on their structure maps and on the pullbacks of the coordinates. The structure maps agree by the factorization through the original hypersurface. For a retained coordinate, pullback along the restricted hypersurface map agrees with pullback along the original blowup followed by restriction to the strict transform, by the commutative square. The complementary index belongs to the restricted center precisely when its original index belongs to the center. It differs from the new distinguished index precisely when the original index differs from the old one, since the complement embedding is injective. Thus the original blowup equation descends to the same substitution equation in the retained coordinates. These equalities determine the maps to affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_preimage_domain_le_preim: A point of the strict transform lying over the blowup chart maps into its downstairs chart, since the chart domain lies over that open. The factorization through the original hypersurface says that this is also the image of the point under its map to the hypersurface and then to the original scheme. Thus it lies in the specified inverse image.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_saturation_of_flat: To check equality on an affine open upstairs, cover it by basic opens whose points map into affine opens downstairs where the saturating ideal has a single generator. Such basic opens exist at every point. On each of them, flat extension commutes with saturation by powers of that generator. The basic-open equality criterion gives equality on the entire affine open, hence equality of the sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransform_of_flat: The strict transform is the saturation of the total transform by the exceptional ideal. The map upstairs in the pullback square is flat because it is a base change of the flat map downstairs. The exceptional ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor by the blowup property, so its saturation commutes with pullback along this flat map. Commutativity of the square identifies the pulled-back exceptional ideal and total transform with those for the new center and divisor. This gives the strict-transform identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransform_of_flat_of_isLocal: On each locally Noetherian upstairs scheme, the strict-transform inclusion is quasi-compact. Thus the two quasi-compactness hypotheses in the flat base-change theorem are available, and that theorem gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_mem_map_away: In the localization, membership in the extended ideal expresses the image of the element as a fraction with numerator in the ideal and denominator a power of the inverted element. Cross-multiply, then multiply by a further power to obtain equality in the original ring. The sum of the two exponents gives the required power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_mem_map_basicOpen: The section ring on the basic open is obtained by inverting its defining section in the affine section ring. Apply the denominator-clearing result for that localization to the given membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_comap_saturation_of_ideal_eq_span_: On the chosen affine opens, the pullback ideals are extensions along the induced section map, which is flat. Downstairs the sections of the saturation are the saturation by powers of the chosen generator. Upstairs the pulled-back saturating ideal is generated by the image of that generator, so the sections there are obtained by saturation by powers of its image. The equality for flat extension of the ring-level saturation gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_ideal_basicOpen_eq_of_span_e: Take a section of the first ideal on the affine open. Its restriction belongs to the second ideal on every indicated basic open because the two restricted ideals agree. Clear denominators to obtain, for each basic open, a power of its defining section whose product with the original section belongs to the second ideal. The ideal generated by these powers is the unit ideal, since its radical contains the original generators of the unit ideal. A linear combination of these powers equal to one proves containment of the section in the second ideal. Reverse the roles of the two ideals to obtain equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_saturationByPowers_le: For an element of the original saturation, some power of the chosen element sends it into the original ideal. Applying the algebra map gives the same power relation in the extended ideal. Thus the image of each element of the original saturation belongs to the target saturation, and their generated ideal does too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_saturationByPowers_of_flat: One inclusion follows by applying the algebra map to a witnessing power equation. For the other, take an element of the target saturation and fix a power that puts it in the extended ideal. Downstairs, the kernel of multiplication by this power followed by reduction modulo the ideal is the ideal quotient by the power. Tensor the sequence consisting of this kernel, the original ring, and the quotient ring with the flat algebra. The sequence stays exact. After identifying the tensored rings with the target and its quotient by the extended ideal, the chosen element lies in the kernel of the tensored multiplication map. It therefore belongs to the extension of the downstairs kernel. That kernel lies in the original saturation, so the element belongs to its extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_saturationByPowers_iff: The saturation of an ideal by powers of an element consists precisely of the elements that can be multiplied into the ideal by some nonnegative power of that element. The membership equivalence is this definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_basicOpen_cover: If the indicated sections generated a proper ideal, a maximal ideal would contain all of them. Its point lies in the affine open. The covering condition places that point in a basic open of one of those sections, so that section is outside the maximal ideal. This is a contradiction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_subschemeι_apply_eq_zero_of_mem: The section of the ambient ideal maps to zero under the quotient describing sections on the inverse image of the affine open. The map to the smaller open further restricts that zero section, so it also sends the original section to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransform_eq_strictTransform: The chosen strict-transform lift has the required factorization through the original hypersurface. Apply the strict-transform comparison for any map with that factorization to this chosen lift.

The equality can be checked near every point of the strict transform of the hypersurface. Over the center, take a normal crossings chart. The hypersurface must be present since its strict transform contains the point upstairs. Its coordinate belongs to the center set by the ideal containment. The other divisor is absent or a distinct coordinate, so the affine blowup-chart comparison gives the local equality. Away from the center both strict transforms are total transforms and agree by the factorization. The local equalities give the sheaf equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordIdeal_eq_of_map_eq: Each coordinate ideal is obtained by pulling back the same coordinate-subspace ideal on affine space. The chart maps agree, so the two pulled-back ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_locally_restrictIdeal_eq: Choose one neighborhood with equal restrictions for each point. These neighborhoods cover the whole scheme, so the equality criterion on an open cover gives equality of the ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_restrictIdeal_eq_of_iSup_eq_top: Equality on the cover implies on each affine open that the first section ideal is contained in the second, by the basic-open argument. Reversing the equality on the cover gives the opposite containment. The affine section ideals determine the sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_of_hasStrictNormalCros: Use the normal crossings chart at the center point and shrink its domain to an affine open. The selected hypersurface is the first list entry, and the indicated boundary member occurs in the tail. The chart assigns each either no coordinate, giving the unit ideal, or one coordinate. If both have coordinates, those indices differ because the two positions in the list are distinct and the assignment is injective on present entries. Shrinking preserves these descriptions and the center coordinate ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_algebraMap_mem_map: Write the localized element as a fraction with numerator in the ideal and denominator a power of the inverted element. Cross-multiply and then multiply by a further power to make the resulting equality hold in the original ring. The product of the powers times the original element is in the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_restrictIdeal_eq_of_mem_preimage: Choose a blowup chart containing the image of the point. The hypersurface index differs from the distinguished index, because if they agreed its strict transform would be empty on this chart. Shrink the chart to an affine neighborhood of the image and pull that open back to the strict transform. The affine chart comparison gives the required equality on that neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_restrictIdeal_eq_of_notMem_suppor: Take the open of the strict transform lying over the complement of the center. On this open the ambient strict transform of the other divisor agrees with its total transform. The point also lies off the restricted center for the map to the hypersurface, since the two pullbacks of the center agree by the factorization. The strict transform along the hypersurface map therefore agrees locally with its total transform as well. The two total transforms are pullbacks along equal composites, giving the desired equality on this open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_strictTransformSubschemeLift: The kernel ideal of the closed subscheme inclusion is the ideal defining it. Apply the lift for a closed immersion with that kernel to obtain a map from the strict transform into the original closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_strictTransform_lift_of_ker_eq: Identify the ideal with the kernel ideal of the closed immersion. The composite from the strict transform to the original scheme kills that kernel ideal and hence factors through the closed immersion. This gives the required map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_mem_preimage_of_restrictIdeal_e: Choose a blowup chart above the downstairs open containing the image of the point. The hypersurface has unit ideal downstairs, so its strict transform has unit ideal on the chart. Its support is empty there. This contradicts the fact that the point maps into that support by the strict-transform inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_map_eq_of_comp_eq_id: Extend each of the equal image ideals along the second homomorphism. Successive extensions agree with extension along the composite, which is the identity. This recovers the original ideals on both sides, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_restrictIdeal_eq: The equal restrictions have equal ideals of global sections on the affine open subscheme. Those ideals are extensions of the original section ideals along the canonical isomorphism from ambient sections on the open. Extending back along the inverse isomorphism gives equality of the original ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_one_eq_zero: The section ring of the inverse image is isomorphic to the quotient by the given section ideal. If one equals zero in that ring, then the quotient class of one is zero. Thus one belongs to the original ideal and the ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_of_restrictIdeal_eq_of_iSup_eq_: Take a section of the first ideal on an affine open. For each point of that open choose a basic neighborhood inside a member of the given cover. The two section ideals agree on this basic open because their restrictions agree on the cover member. Clearing denominators shows that a positive power of the basic-open section sends the original section into the second ideal. The basic opens of those powers still cover the affine open, so the powers generate the unit ideal. A linear combination giving one shows that the original section belongs to the second ideal there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_comap_of_ker_eq: Identify the ideal with the kernel of the closed immersion. The given map and the canonical strict-transform lift have the same composite with that immersion. Since the immersion is a monomorphism, the maps agree. The canonical lift has the blowup property for the restricted center, so the given map does too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_strictTransformS: The original closed subscheme inclusion has the required kernel ideal, and the chosen lift factors the strict-transform inclusion followed by the ambient blowup. Apply the blowup property for such a lift along a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_subscheme: The inverse images of affine opens of the ambient scheme are affine and cover the closed subscheme. Their section rings are quotients of the ambient affine section rings, which are Noetherian. Quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian, so this affine cover proves that the subscheme is locally Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_colonSpanSingleton: The ideal quotient by the chosen element is defined to consist of the multipliers whose product with that element belongs to the original ideal. This definition gives the stated equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_restrictIdeal_eq_coordIdeal_of_le: Suppose the hypersurface coordinate is outside the center index set. Its image in the quotient by the center is then a coordinate of the induced étale chart, so it is a nonzerodivisor. On the other hand, the hypersurface ideal is contained in the center ideal, so that coordinate maps to zero in the quotient. Since zero is a nonzerodivisor there, one equals zero. This makes the center ideal the unit ideal on the affine chart, contradicting the presence of the given center point. Therefore the hypersurface index lies in the center set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_of_restrictIdeal_eq_top: The support of the restricted ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Since the restricted ideal is the unit ideal, its support is empty. Thus a point in the open cannot belong to the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_comp_comp_eq_id: Functoriality gives the map of the composite of the three arrows. This composite is an endomorphism of an open, hence the identity. Its map on sections is therefore the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_eq_id: Any endomorphism of an open in the opposite of the poset of opens is the identity. The presheaf sends it to the identity on sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_strictTransform_eq_o: The hypersurface is a center coordinate distinct from the exceptional index. Restricting the chart to its strict transform removes that coordinate and identifies the smaller center with the remaining center coordinates. The distinguished index remains and determines the restricted blowup chart. If the other divisor has unit ideal downstairs, both restrictions are unit ideals. Otherwise it is a distinct coordinate, so it has a corresponding retained index on the hypersurface. If this index corresponds to the exceptional one, both strict transforms are empty on the chart. Otherwise both ideals are generated by the retained chart coordinate for that divisor. The chart induced by restriction and the chart for the hypersurface blowup use the same map, so their coordinate ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformSubschemeLift_comp_subsch: The chosen lift is the factorization of the composite from the strict transform to the ambient scheme through the closed subscheme inclusion. Composing the lift with that inclusion gives the original composite by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_base_mem_support: The range of the closed subscheme inclusion on points is the support of its ideal. The image of the given point belongs to that range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_hom_iso_inv: Given an element of the source of the isomorphism, take its image under the forward map. The inverse sends this image back to the original element, so it is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_subschemeι_app: On the affine open, the section map of the subscheme inclusion is the quotient map by its ideal followed by the isomorphism with sections on the inverse-image open. The quotient map and the isomorphism are both surjective.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_strictTransform_mul_exceptional: Over the center choose an étale coordinate chart and a blowup chart containing the point upstairs. If the boundary divisor is absent on the downstairs chart, both transforms have unit ideal on the chart upstairs, and the center point is outside the boundary support. The exponent is zero. If the boundary is a center coordinate, the center is locally contained in its support and the exponent is one. The pullback then contributes one exceptional factor, with strict transform given by the corresponding chart coordinate when its index differs from the exceptional index, and with unit ideal when the indices agree. If the boundary coordinate is outside the center set, it pulls back to the same chart coordinate and gives the strict transform directly. The center cannot be contained in this boundary after shrinking around the point, by the support criterion on a smaller affine chart, so the exponent is zero. Off the center use the inverse image of its complement. The exceptional ideal is the unit ideal and the strict transform equals the total transform there. The local support condition holds vacuously, so take exponent one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_opens_totalTransform_eq_of_notMem: Use the inverse image of the complement of the center’s support. On it the strict transform equals the pullback, and the exceptional ideal restricts to the unit ideal. Multiplying the strict-transform ideal by this unit ideal gives the desired identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inter_support_subset_support_of_mem_coor: The chosen coordinate belongs to the set of center coordinates, so the restricted divisor ideal is contained in the restricted center ideal. Support reverses inclusions of ideals, hence the support of the restricted center lies in that of the restricted divisor. Passing from points of the open subscheme to their images proves the containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_restrictIdeal_iff: Restriction of the ideal is pullback along the open inclusion. The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Consequently the point belongs to the restricted support exactly when its image belongs to the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_inter_support_subset_support_of_notM: Restrict the divisor to the part of the center lying in the affine chart. Because its coordinate lies outside the center’s coordinate set, it restricts to a coordinate on the induced étale chart of the center. It thus defines an ideal locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. If the claimed containment of supports held, this restricted divisor would contain the entire center in that open. The given point makes the open part of the center nonempty, and a locally principal nonzerodivisor cannot vanish along an entire irreducible component. This is a contradiction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocusIsOpenForEmbeddings_canonic: For any admissible embedding, apply the stagewise openness theorem to the embedded blowup sequence produced by the canonical principalization. This gives exactly the openness property for all such embeddings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocusIsOpen_toEmbeddedBlowupSequ: At a stage before the end, the detached locus is the union of the detached irreducible components. By the certificate argument, every such component is disjoint from every irreducible component outside this family. Since the strict-transform space is Noetherian, there are finitely many irreducible components and they are closed. The union of the other components is its closed complement, so the detached locus is open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_detachedComponent_canonicalPrin: At the indicated stage the output of the canonical order reduction supplies a principalization certificate for the initial order-one marked triple. The chart hypotheses supply Noetherianity, the closed embedding of the strict transform, and the local agreement and order-one assumptions at generic points. Generic avoidance of each boundary member implies avoidance of their union. Thus the certificate disjointness theorem applies to the detached and nondetached components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_detachedComponent_of_principali: Use the certificate to obtain the order-one center isolation property. The detached component is an irreducible component whose image is contained in the ambient center. Its image and that of the other component are closed and irreducible because the strict-transform inclusion is a closed embedding, and their generic points are images of the original generic points. The generic point of the other component lies outside the center, since otherwise its closure would lie in the closed center, making it detached. Both generic points avoid the given boundary union. The first has order one and near it the ideal agrees with the vanishing ideal of its component. The second has order one and hence belongs to the input support. If the components intersected, their images would share a point, contradicting the isolation property applied to these two closed irreducible sets.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_iff: Local agreement at a point is defined to mean equality after restricting to an open neighborhood of that point. The displayed condition is exactly this definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_symm: Use the same open neighborhood witnessing agreement. Reverse the equality of the two restrictions on that neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_subschemeι_comp_ι_apply_eq_of_mem: The ambient point belongs to the open, so take its corresponding point in the open subscheme. This point lies in the inverse image of the given set, hence in the closed subscheme support by hypothesis. Since the support is the image of the closed subscheme inclusion, lift the point there. Under the composite inclusion its image is the original point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_isOpen_preimage_support: The open containing the common point also contains the second generic point. The common point lifts to the hypersurface because it lies in the center support, and the generic point lifts because it lies in the input support. The inverse image of the second irreducible closed subset is irreducible, with this lifted generic point. The inverse image of the center support in the hypersurface is closed and is open by hypothesis. Since it contains the lifted common point, it contains the whole irreducible inverse-image subset. In particular it contains the lifted generic point. This contradicts the generic point being outside the original center support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_isSmoothDivisor_of_orderOneCent: The open contains the common point and both generic points. The first subset lies in the center support and the second generic point lies in the input support, so all three points lift to the smooth hypersurface. The inverse-image closed subsets are irreducible with the lifted generic points. Near the first point the residual ideal agrees with the restricted input and hence with the vanishing ideal of the first inverse-image subset. The subset cannot be an entire component of the hypersurface, since its generic point lies in the residual support and the residual ideal is nonzero on components. Its vanishing ideal therefore has order one there by the smooth-divisor hypothesis, and so does the residual ideal. The second generic point belongs to the residual support by the same local agreement with the input there. Center membership, center avoidance, and boundary avoidance transfer by inverse image. The isolation property on the hypersurface gives the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_orderOneCentersIsolated_comap_o: The chosen open contains the common point, hence both generic points. Pull the two closed subsets and their points back to the open subscheme. The subsets remain closed and irreducible, with the lifted points as their generic points. Support and boundary conditions transfer by inverse image. Local ideal agreement transfers by pullback, which also takes the vanishing ideal to that of the inverse-image closed subset. Order is preserved by the open inclusion. Thus the pair satisfies all hypotheses of the isolation property on the open, giving the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_preimage_subschemeι_comp_ι: The composite inclusion is continuous because it induces the source topology. Its inverse image of a closed subset is therefore closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isGenericPoint_preimage_subschemeι_comp_: The composite inclusion induces the topology on the subscheme. The closure of the singleton of the lifted point is therefore the inverse image of the closure of its image. That image is the stated generic point, whose closure is the original closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isInducing_subschemeι_comp_ι: Both the closed subscheme inclusion and the open inclusion identify the source topology with the topology induced from the target. The underlying map of their composite is the composite of these two maps. Composition preserves the induced-topology property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_of_agreeNear: Local agreement gives equal orders at the point. Membership in an ideal’s support is equivalent to its order being at least one. The equal orders therefore give equivalent support memberships.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_eq_mul_of_sub: Both generic points avoid the support of the boundary factor. On a neighborhood of the first, this factor is the unit ideal, so the residual ideal agrees with the original ideal and hence with the first subset’s vanishing ideal. The product order bound gives order at most one for the residual ideal there because the boundary factor has order zero. The center condition gives the residual mark as a lower bound at this point. The mark is at least one, so both mark and residual order equal one. The second generic point lies in the residual support because it lies in the product support but outside the boundary factor’s support. The residual isolation hypothesis now gives a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_forall_opens: The common point belongs to the first closed subset and hence to the center support. Choose its specified open neighborhood, where the pulled-back ideals satisfy isolation. The transfer argument for an open containing the common point gives the required contradiction in the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_isSmoothDivis: Choose the specified hypersurface neighborhood of the common point, which lies in the center. If no residual ideal is supplied, the pulled-back center support is open on the hypersurface, and the connectedness argument forces the second generic point into it. If a residual ideal is supplied, use the isolation property for that ideal on the hypersurface together with local agreement and nonvanishing on components. The hypersurface transfer then gives the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_principalizat: Use simultaneous induction on the certificate and its residual certificate. Centers contained in the boundary and marks at least two satisfy isolation directly. For a decomposition into a boundary factor and a residual ideal, the residual transfer applies using the inductive isolation property. For a certificate given on opens, transfer the local isolation at the common point back to the original scheme. The remaining residual case is a smooth hypersurface reduction, where the hypersurface transfer applies with the supplied data and the inductive property when there is a further ideal. This covers every certificate constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_support_subse: The first closed subset lies in the center support, and so does its generic point. The center support is contained in the boundary set by hypothesis, contradicting avoidance of that set by the generic point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderOneCentersIsolated_of_two_le: The isolation condition assumes a mark equal to one. This is impossible when the mark is at least two.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_isSmoothDivisor_of_smoothOrderO: Local agreement and smoothness give order one at the generic point, so it lies in the input support. If there is no next ideal, the inverse image of the center support in the hypersurface is open by hypothesis. The generic point belongs to the hypersurface and specializes to the given point, so this openness contradicts the assumed separation of the two points by the center. If the next ideal exists, the portion of the closed subset on the chosen open lies in the input support, hence in the smooth hypersurface. Pull back the subset and its generic and distinguished points to this hypersurface. The inverse image is closed and irreducible. Near its points the next ideal agrees with the pullback of the original ideal because the subset avoids the boundary. This in turn agrees locally with the vanishing ideal of the inverse-image subset. The next ideal is nonzero on components, so the subset contains no whole component. Smoothness transfers to its vanishing subscheme by hypothesis. The two center support conditions and boundary disjointness transfer by inverse images. Apply the inductive isolation property on the hypersurface to obtain the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_smoothOrderOneCentersIsolated_o: The chosen open contains the distinguished point of the closed subset, so it also contains its generic point. Pull the closed subset and both points back to the open subscheme. The inverse image is closed and irreducible with the lifted generic point. The structural map and the vanishing subscheme remain smooth by the restriction hypotheses. No component of the open subscheme is contained in the inverse-image subset by the component argument. Support membership and absence at the two points transfer under pullback, as do disjointness from the boundary and local agreement with the vanishing ideal. The stated isolation property on the open subscheme then gives the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleComponents_opens_not_subset_p: Suppose a component of the open subscheme lies in the inverse image of the closed set. The closure of its image is irreducible, so it lies in an irreducible component of the ambient scheme. This ambient component meets the open, and its intersection with the open is irreducible. Its inverse image contains the original component, so maximality identifies them. Thus the intersection lies in the closed set. The intersection is a nonempty open of the ambient irreducible component and is dense in it. Closedness then puts the whole ambient component in the closed set, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_one_of_agreeNear: Near the specified point the ideal agrees with the vanishing ideal of the closed irreducible subset, so their orders there agree. The smooth-vanishing order hypothesis gives order one for this vanishing ideal, since its subscheme is smooth and the subset contains no ambient irreducible component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothOrderOneCentersIsolated_of_princip: Use simultaneous induction on the certificate and its residual certificate. If the center is contained in the boundary, the distinguished point in the center contradicts disjointness. A mark at least two contradicts the order-one hypothesis directly. In the factorization case, around every point of the subset the boundary factor is the unit ideal because its support is contained in the boundary. Thus the residual ideal has the same local agreement with the vanishing ideal. If the residual mark is one, apply induction. If it is at least two, the residual ideal has order one at the distinguished point by the smooth-vanishing order result, contradicting the marked center condition. In the open restriction cases apply the induction hypothesis in the neighborhood of the distinguished point and transfer isolation through the open inclusion. In the hypersurface case apply the restriction argument for a smooth divisor, using the inductive isolation property whenever a further ideal is present. These cases establish the required isolation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_support_of_agreeNear: At each point of the closed set, local equality with its vanishing ideal gives the same support membership as for the vanishing ideal. That support is exactly the closed set. Hence every point of the set lies in the given ideal’s support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_ideal_vanishingIdeal_image_of_: Smoothness of the original source gives pairwise disjoint components at every stage and ensures that every surviving strict-transform point avoids the earlier centers. These are the two extra hypotheses of the local agreement result, which now applies to the chosen component and point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_vanishingIdeal_image_of_forall: Induct on the stage. At stage zero the ideal defines the reduced strict transform and is the vanishing ideal of its image. Delete the ambient images of the other components. These finitely many closed sets omit the chosen point, and on the resulting open the full image equals the chosen component image. At a successor, track the chosen component by its generic point to a preceding component and take an agreement neighborhood at the image of the given point. Intersect this neighborhood with the complement of the center, which contains that image by avoidance. On its inverse image the exceptional ideal is the unit ideal, so the new ideal is the pullback of the previous one. The blowdown is an open immersion there, and component tracking identifies the inverse image of the preceding component with the new component there. Restriction along this open immersion takes the preceding vanishing ideal to the required vanishing ideal, giving agreement near the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_irreducibleComponents_strictTra: The strict transform is smooth over the ground field, so its local rings are regular. At a point where two distinct irreducible components meet, the local ring has at least two minimal primes. A regular local ring is a domain and has only one minimal prime. Thus any two distinct components are disjoint.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClopen_of_mem_irreducibleComponents_st: Each irreducible component is closed, and the Noetherian strict transform has finitely many of them. Because they are pairwise disjoint and cover the space, the complement of the chosen component is the union of the other components. That finite union is closed, so the chosen component is open as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_detachedLocus_of_mem_support_ambient: Choose an irreducible component through the point. If its generic point maps outside the center, the component image is an irreducible closed set whose reduced subscheme is smooth. Along the image the principalization ideal agrees locally with its vanishing ideal, so the image lies in the support of that ideal. It contains no ambient component, since the principalization ideal remains nonzero on every ambient component. Center avoidance also makes the image disjoint from the boundary. The canonical reduction supplies a smooth ambient stage and an order-one principalization certificate. The order-one isolation result then rules out the given point mapping into the center while the generic point maps outside it. The chosen component is therefore detached, and the point belongs to the detached locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_strictTransformι_comp_chartLevelS: The structural morphism of the chart level is the iterated structural morphism to the ground field. Composing it with the strict-transform inclusion therefore gives the smooth morphism just established.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_strictTransformι_comp_schemeAtToS: Induct on the stage. At stage zero, the inclusion of the strict transform and the original closed immersion transported through the stage-zero isomorphism have the same kernel. Their sources are therefore isomorphic over that stage, so the structural map is smooth. At a successor stage, center avoidance places the entire new strict transform over the complement of the previous center. The blowdown is an open immersion over that complement. There the strict-transform description identifies the image of the new strict transform with the inverse image of the preceding support. The preceding closed subscheme is reduced, and its inverse image under an open immersion is reduced as well. The new strict transform is reduced and has that same support, so the two closed subschemes agree on this open. The new structural map is thus the restriction of the smooth preceding map to an open subscheme, transported along an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_vanishingIdeal_image_comp_chartLe: The chosen component is open and closed in a smooth scheme. Its reduced induced subscheme is the open subscheme on that component and is therefore smooth. Composing its closed immersion with the strict-transform inclusion makes it a reduced closed subscheme of the ambient stage. Its image is precisely the closed set used to define the ambient vanishing ideal. Since reduced closed subschemes with the same support agree, the vanishing subscheme is smooth over the ground field.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_and_orderAt_eq_one_reducedVani: At the given stage, componentwise agreement and order one apply to the chosen component and its generic point. The reduced vanishing assignment is exactly the vanishing ideal used in that result, so both statements carry over directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_vanishingIdeal_of_inter_eq: Use the given open as the agreement neighborhood. On each affine open inside it, the restricted section ideals are obtained from those on the corresponding affine open in the ambient scheme. The equality of intersections gives equality of those ambient section ideals. Thus the restricted ideal sheaves agree on every affine open and are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreesWithComponentsOrderOne_of_le: Specialize the induction establishing componentwise agreement and order one at every stage within the sequence to the given stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreesWithComponentsOrderOne_succ: Follow the successor component’s generic point to the generic point of its surviving predecessor. By induction, on a neighborhood of that point the preceding ideal agrees with the predecessor’s vanishing ideal and has order one there. Intersect the neighborhood with the center complement and pull it back. The new generic point lies in this open because the predecessor survives. The exceptional ideal is the unit ideal on the open, so the transform formula identifies the restricted new ideal with the previous ideal pulled back. The blowdown is an open immersion there, and the preceding component image pulls back to the successor component image. Thus their vanishing ideals agree with the transformed ideal on this open. The open immersions identify the corresponding local rings and ideals, so the order remains one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreesWithComponentsOrderOne_zero: The stage-zero ideal is the vanishing ideal of the whole strict-transform image. Remove the finite union of the images of the other components. The chosen generic point remains, since membership in another closed component would put the entire chosen component inside it. On the resulting open the full image equals the chosen component image, giving local agreement of their vanishing ideals. The closed embedding identifies the chosen component image with an irreducible component of the full image and identifies its generic point. The ambient local ring at that point is not a field, so the vanishing-ideal order formula for a maximal irreducible subset gives order one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_strictTransformι_of_isGene: Apply the stage-by-stage avoidance result to the specified stage, component, and generic point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_succ_iff: By definition, avoidance at the successor means that the image under blowdown lies outside the current center and that the same image avoids all earlier centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_zero: There are no earlier centers at stage zero, so every point satisfies the avoidance condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartIsolationHypotheses_reducedVanishin: Each strict-transform space in range is Noetherian and its ambient inclusion is a closed embedding. Its generic points avoid all boundary supports. Near each such generic point the principalization ideal agrees with the reduced vanishing ideal of the component image and has order one. These four results supply all the chart isolation hypotheses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closure_singleton_mem_irreducibleCompone: The closure of a point is irreducible. If an irreducible set contains this closure, choose a generic point of its closure. That generic point specializes to the given point, so the hypothesis makes them equal. The larger set is therefore contained in the original point closure, proving maximality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_comp_of_mul_eq: Pullback along the composite equals successive pullback. Substitute the product for the pullback of the target ideal. On each affine chart of the open restriction the first factor pulls back to the unit ideal, so the ring-level calculation removes it from the inverse image of the product. The resulting chart equalities identify the two ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_eq_comap_mul_of_comap_eq_top: The first ideal has unit inverse image, so the image of the source unit belongs to it. That image is the target unit, making the first ideal the unit ideal. Multiplication by it leaves the second ideal unchanged, and the inverse images agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_base_apply: The map on points of a composite is the composite of the two maps on points. Evaluate it at the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_specializes_iso_hom: Apply the continuous inverse isomorphism to the specialization. Its target becomes the original point, and the hypothesis makes the inverse image of the source equal to that point. Applying the forward isomorphism gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_specializes_of_isField_stalk: The image of the spectrum of the local ring at the point consists of all its generizations. A field has a one-point spectrum. The point and its given generization both lie in that image, so they coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_agreesWithComponentsOrderOne: Induct on the stage using the stage-zero agreement and order calculation. If a successor lies within the sequence, its predecessor does as well. Apply the successor preservation result to the induction hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_avoidsCenters_strictTransformι_of: Induct on the stage. The stage-zero assertion is vacuous. At a successor, the generic point of a component maps to the generic point of a surviving preceding component. That generic point lies outside the current center, and the induction hypothesis says its ambient image avoids all earlier centers. The strict-transform square commutes, so this ambient image is the blowdown of the new generic point. The two facts give successor avoidance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_not_avoidsCenters_of_mem_boundary: Induct on the stage. The initial boundary is empty. At a successor every boundary member is either the newest exceptional divisor or the strict transform of a previous member. In the first case its support is the inverse image of the current center, contradicting the first condition for successor avoidance. In the second case its support is contained in the inverse image of the previous member’s support, since the pulled-back ideal is contained in the strict-transform ideal. The image point then lies on the previous boundary, and the induction hypothesis contradicts the second condition for successor avoidance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.genericPoint_notMem_boundary_support: The ambient image of the generic point of a strict-transform component avoids all preceding centers. If it lay on the indicated boundary member, the boundary-support result would force it to meet a preceding center. This contradiction excludes the generic point from the support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedEmbedding_strictTransformι: The strict transform is defined as a closed subscheme of the ambient stage. Its defining closed immersion induces a closed embedding on the underlying spaces.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt_toEmbeddedBlowupSe: The finite-stage Noetherianity theorem for embedded blowup sequences applies to the sequence attached to the embedding datum and algorithm. Evaluate it at the given stage within the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_ι_comp_blowdown: Over the complement of the center the blowdown is an isomorphism. The given open lies in its source there. The composite from the given open to the previous ambient scheme factors through an open inclusion, this isomorphism, and the inclusion of the center complement. Each factor is an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comap_iso_hom_eq_ker_comp_inv: Factor the original morphism by first composing with the inverse isomorphism and then with the forward isomorphism. The forward isomorphism is an open immersion, so pulling the kernel of that composite back along it gives the kernel of the first factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_congr: Equal morphisms induce the same maps on sections, so their kernel ideal sheaves are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closure_singleton_of_base_mem: The specialization between the two images is reflected by the open embedding from the given open into the target. Thus the corresponding points specialize in the open. The inclusion of the open is continuous and preserves this specialization in the original source, which gives the asserted closure membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_image_strictTransformι_iff_of_notMem: In one direction the open immersion away from the center lifts membership in the previous component to membership in the next. In the other direction continuity and the commuting strict-transform square send the next component into the previous one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_image_strictTransformι_of_mem_image_: The next component is the closure of its generic point. The component downstairs is closed and contains the image of that generic point, so continuity puts the image of the entire next component inside the component downstairs. The strict-transform square commutes, giving the required statement for the ambient images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_image_strictTransformι_succ_of_mem_i: The two ambient component images are the closures of their embedded generic points, and blowdown sends the upper generic point to the lower one. The image of the given point is in the closure of the lower generic point. If that generic point belonged to the center, this closure would be contained in the closed center, contrary to the hypothesis. Thus both upper points lie over the complement of the center, where blowdown is an open immersion. It reflects the specialization between their images, so the given point lies in the closure of the upper generic point and hence in the new component image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_mem_support_comap: The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Membership in this inverse image gives membership of the image point in the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_strictTransform: The ambient scheme at each stage within the sequence is Noetherian. Its strict transform is a closed subscheme, whose underlying closed subspace is therefore Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_avoidsCenters_of_mem_boundary_suppor: Apply the inductive result on boundary support at the indicated stage to the given boundary member and point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_image_irreducibleComponent_subset_bo: An irreducible component of a scheme has a generic point. If the whole component image lay in the boundary support, the image of its generic point would lie there. This contradicts generic-point boundary avoidance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_isField_stalk_strictTransformι_zero: The image of the chosen strict-transform point belongs to the support of the stage-zero ideal. Under the initial isomorphism it therefore belongs to the support of the original embedding kernel. If its stage-zero local ring were a field, it would admit no distinct generization. The initial isomorphism preserves that property, so the closure of the transported point would be an ambient irreducible component. The support of the kernel is closed and contains the point, and hence would contain this component, contrary to the nonvanishing hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_congr_of_inter_eq: Every value of the map lies in the open. Consequently a value belongs to either closed set exactly when it belongs to that set’s intersection with the open. The two intersections are equal, so the inverse images are equal point by point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationOfEmbedding_ideal_zero_e: At stage zero the principalization ideal is the pullback of the original embedding kernel along the stage-zero isomorphism. This is the kernel of the original embedding followed by the inverse isomorphism, also the stage-zero strict-transform ideal. Its support is the image of the strict-transform immersion. The source is reduced, so the kernel is radical and equals the vanishing ideal of that support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_eq_of_eq_ker: By the stated equality the ideal is the kernel ideal sheaf of a morphism from a reduced scheme. Such a kernel is radical by the preceding sectionwise argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ker_eq_of_isReduced: For each affine open of the target, the ring of sections over its inverse image is reduced. The corresponding section map has radical kernel. The affine ideals of the kernel sheaf are contained in these radical kernels, and their radicals remain contained there. The maximality defining the kernel sheaf then gives containment of its radical in the kernel sheaf itself. The opposite containment is automatic.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdeal_ideal_eq_of_inter_eq: The spectrum of the affine open maps into the given open. Since the two closed sets have the same intersection with that open, their inverse images in the spectrum coincide. The section ideals are the vanishing ideals of these inverse images, hence are equal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_vanishingIdeal_image_of_avoids: At stage zero the ideal is the vanishing ideal of the entire strict-transform image. Remove the images of all other components, a finite union of closed sets which omits the chosen point by disjointness. On the remaining open the full image and the chosen component image coincide. For a successor, track the generic point of the chosen component to a preceding component. By induction the preceding ideal agrees with that component’s vanishing ideal near the image of the point. Pull back this neighborhood intersected with the complement of the center. It still contains the point by avoidance. There the exceptional ideal is the unit ideal, so the successor ideal is the pullback of the preceding ideal. On this open immersion, component tracking identifies the pulled-back component image with the chosen successor component image, and the vanishing ideals restrict accordingly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_strictTransformι_of_smooth: Induct simultaneously on smoothness of the current strict transform and avoidance of all earlier centers through that stage. At stage zero the transform is isomorphic to the original smooth scheme, its components are disjoint, and there are no earlier centers. At a successor, choose a component through a given point and track its generic point to a surviving preceding component. Continuity sends the entire chosen component into that preceding component because it sends the closure of the generic point into the closure of its image. The isolation result for surviving components, applied using smoothness and avoidance through the preceding stage, excludes the image point from the current center. The commuting maps and the successor criterion give avoidance through the new stage. The open-immersion argument away from the center then gives smoothness of the new transform, completing the simultaneous induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartLevelStructureMorphism_eq_structure: The chart-level structural map is defined as the principalization sequence’s structural morphism at the chosen stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_of_ker_eq: Equality of the kernels lets each closed immersion factor through the other. Compose the two factorizations and then the corresponding closed immersion. The result is the closed immersion itself, so cancellation shows that the composite is the identity. Applying the same argument in the other order gives an isomorphism over the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_mem_support_center: Restrict the order-one certificate to the whole ambient scheme viewed as an open. It yields the smooth order-one center isolation property for the vanishing-ideal assignment. Apply it to the indicated closed irreducible set, which has smooth reduced structure, contains no ambient component, avoids the old boundary, and has the prescribed local ideal agreement. Since its generic point lies outside the center, isolation excludes the given point from the center as well, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_comap_ker_of_isPullback_isOpenImm: An open immersion is flat, and the pullback of a quasi-compact morphism is quasi-compact. The flat base-change formula for the kernel ideal sheaf applies to the square, identifying the new kernel with the pullback of the old one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ideal: At stage zero the ideal is transported from the input by an isomorphism, which preserves the component condition. At a successor, multiplying the new ideal by the exceptional ideal gives the pullback of the preceding ideal. The exceptional Cartier divisor contains no irreducible component. The componentwise nonvanishing result for this factorization therefore transfers the induction hypothesis to the new ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_ambientCenter_support_of_notMem_d: The image of the chosen component under the closed immersion is closed and irreducible with the image of its generic point as generic point. Because the component survives, that generic point lies outside the center. Its ambient vanishing subscheme is smooth, and previous center avoidance gives local agreement of its vanishing ideal with the principalization ideal throughout the image. This puts the image in the support of the principalization ideal, which contains no ambient component. Previous center avoidance also makes the image disjoint from the boundary. The canonical reduction supplies the smooth ambient structure and order-one certificate. Center isolation now excludes every point of the image from the current center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ker_eq_ker: On any affine open of the target, the ring of sections over its inverse image is reduced. The kernel of the section map to that ring is therefore radical. The kernel ideal sheaf lies inside those section kernels, so each section ideal of its radical still lies inside the corresponding section kernel. The defining maximality of the kernel ideal sheaf gives containment of its radical in the original ideal sheaf. The reverse containment holds for every ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comp_of_iso_hom_eq: Compose the given equality with the final morphism. This identifies the desired morphism precomposed with the isomorphism with the smooth composite in the hypothesis. Transport smoothness across the isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_smooth_iso_hom_comp: Precompose the smooth composite with the inverse isomorphism, which is smooth. The two isomorphisms cancel and leave the morphism whose smoothness was required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_strictTransformι_comp_schemeAtToS: Work on the inverse image of the complement of the current center, which contains the next strict transform by hypothesis. The blowdown is an open immersion there. The commuting strict-transform maps put the next support inside the inverse image of the previous support. Conversely, the closure defining the new strict transform contains every point of that inverse image on this open. Since both strict transforms are reduced, the restricted next transform is the closed subscheme defined by the pullback of the preceding vanishing ideal. It is thus the base change of the previous transform to an open subscheme of the previous ambient stage. Its structural map is smooth by restriction and the compatibility of the stage structural maps.

The stage-zero ideal is the kernel of the original embedding transported to the stage-zero scheme. Its closed immersion therefore has the same kernel as the transported embedding, giving an isomorphism between their sources over the stage. Under this isomorphism the structural morphism is the original smooth map to the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_vanishingIdeal_image_of_smooth_st: The strict transform is smooth over the field and locally of finite type. Its chosen irreducible component is therefore open and closed. Its reduced vanishing subscheme inside the strict transform is smooth over the field. The composite immersion of this reduced subscheme into the ambient stage and the ambient vanishing subscheme of its image have the same support. They are isomorphic over the ambient stage by uniqueness of the reduced closed structure, so the ambient vanishing subscheme is smooth as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformι_notMem_support_of_mem_b: The smooth-source avoidance theorem shows that the image of the given strict-transform point avoids all preceding centers. Membership in the support of a current boundary ideal would force that point to meet a preceding center. Hence it lies outside that boundary support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_detachedLocus_of_mem_detachedComp: The detached locus is the union of the detached irreducible components. In particular, it contains each component in that family.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNear_comap_ι: Choose a neighborhood of the image point on which the two ideals agree. Its inverse image is a neighborhood of the original point. The inverse-image square identifies the restriction of each pulled-back ideal with the pullback of its restriction on the chosen neighborhood. Those restrictions agree, so the pulled-back ideals agree near the original point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_opens_eq_of_le: The inclusion of the smaller open factors through the larger open. Pull back the given equality on the larger open along this factor map. Composition of pullbacks identifies the resulting ideals with the restrictions to the smaller open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafGeometryHypotheses_of_orderAtE: Use the supplied results for order one on a smooth divisor, restriction of local vanishing ideals to a closed subscheme and an open, and equality of order under local agreement. Local agreement is transitive because two witnessing neighborhoods can be intersected and the equalities restricted there. Pullback preserves local agreement, ideal products, and order along open inclusions by the corresponding identities. The remaining conditions follow from the descriptions of open and closed subscheme inclusions, the support formulas for products and vanishing ideals, and the definitions of locally open sets and nonvanishing on components. These facts supply the geometry hypotheses for the vanishing ideal assignment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafGeometryHypotheses_of_vanishin: Order equality under local agreement has already been proved for any two ideal sheaves. Combine it with the three supplied vanishing-ideal properties in the construction of the geometry hypotheses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtEqOfAgreeNear: Take a neighborhood of the given point where the two ideal restrictions agree, and consider the corresponding point of the open subscheme. Order is preserved under the open inclusion for both ideals. The equal restrictions have equal order at that point, giving the original equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_ι: The stalk map of the open immersion is an isomorphism. It identifies the original ideal stalk with the pulled-back ideal stalk and preserves the powers of the maximal ideal. Hence the orders agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdealAssignment_apply: The assignment sends each closed subset to its vanishing ideal sheaf by definition. Evaluating it at the indicated scheme and subset gives that sheaf.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.agreeNearVanishingComapSubscheme: Choose an ambient neighborhood on which the two original ideals agree. Its inverse image in the closed subscheme contains the point. The map from that inverse image to the ambient scheme factors through the chosen neighborhood, so the original equality pulls back to equality there. The pullback of the vanishing ideal along the open inclusion and then the closed immersion is the vanishing ideal of the stated inverse image, by the support containment hypothesis. Thus the two ideals agree near the point as claimed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_opens_vanishingIdeal_eq_vanishingI: The vanishing ideal is radical, and pullback along the open immersion preserves this property. A radical ideal equals the vanishing ideal of its support. Apply this fact to the pulled-back ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_subschemeι_comap_vanishingIdeal: Restrict first to the open, where the ideal becomes the vanishing ideal of the inverse-image closed subset. This subset lies in the support of the closed subscheme. The vanishing ideal restriction formula for a closed immersion therefore applies. The successive inverse images compose to the specified closed subset of the subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_of_isOpenImmersion: The pullback of the radical vanishing ideal along an open immersion is radical. Its support is the inverse image of the given closed set, which is the specified set upstairs. Since a radical ideal sheaf is determined by its support, it is the vanishing ideal upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_subschemeι: Containment of the closed set in the support of the hypersurface ideal gives containment of that ideal in the vanishing ideal. The vanishing subscheme therefore factors through the closed immersion. Its pullback along the immersion is isomorphic to the vanishing subscheme and is reduced. Consequently the pulled-back ideal, the kernel of the corresponding closed immersion, is radical. Its support is the inverse image of the original closed set. A radical ideal sheaf is the vanishing ideal of its support, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_irreducibleComponent_mem: The irreducible component chosen through a point is maximal irreducible and contains the point by its defining properties. It gives the required component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_pullback_lift_comap_subsche: The closed subscheme of a pulled-back ideal is canonically isomorphic to the fiber product of the original closed subscheme with the new base. Its inclusion corresponds to the first projection. Take the forward map of this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.injective_hom_of_iso: The inverse ring map is a left inverse of the forward map. Hence the forward map is injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullback_snd_of_le: The ideal containment makes the second closed subscheme factor through the first closed immersion. That factorization together with the identity on the second subscheme gives a map back into the pullback, whose composite with the second projection is the identity. For the other composite, compare both projections. The second agrees by construction, and the first agrees after the first subscheme inclusion by commutativity. That inclusion is a monomorphism, so the first also agrees. The pullback property proves the inverse identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_of_isLocalization: If a fraction is nilpotent, some power of its numerator is annihilated by an element of the multiplicative set. Multiplying the numerator by this element gives a nilpotent element of the original reduced ring and hence zero. This makes the fraction zero in the localization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_quotient_of_radical_eq: If a class is nilpotent, a power of its representative lies in the ideal. Its representative is thus in the radical, which equals the ideal by hypothesis. The class is zero, so the quotient is reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_subscheme_of_radical_eq: Choose an affine open around the image of a point of the subscheme. Its inverse-image open is affine and has section ring the quotient by the radical section ideal. This quotient is reduced. The stalk at the point is a localization of that ring and remains reduced. All stalks of the subscheme are therefore reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_vanishingIdeal_subscheme: On every affine open the section ideal is the vanishing ideal of the corresponding subset of the prime spectrum. It is radical as an intersection of primes. The subscheme defined by such section ideals is reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_hom_of_iso_le: An element of the kernel has the same image as zero. Injectivity forces the element to be zero, which belongs to the indicated ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_comap_vanishingIdeal_of_preimage_subs: The restricted vanishing ideal is the vanishing ideal of the inverse-image closed set. This set lies in the support of the indicated ideal by hypothesis. The support containment criterion therefore puts that ideal in the restricted vanishing ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_ideal_le: Containment of ideal sheaves is defined by containment of the section ideals on all affine opens. The hypothesis gives precisely these inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_vanishingIdeal_of_subset: A section of the ideal vanishes on its support. Since the specified closed set lies in that support, the section vanishes there as well. This gives containment in the vanishing ideal on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_vanishingIdeal_eq_one: At the point of the closed subset, smoothness of the ambient scheme and of the vanishing subscheme gives an étale chart on which the vanishing ideal is a coordinate ideal. If the coordinate set were empty, the vanishing ideal would be zero on that open, so the entire open would lie in the closed subset. An ambient irreducible component through the point would then have a nonempty open piece in the closed subset. That piece is dense in the component, putting the whole component in the subset, a contradiction. Thus the coordinate set is nonempty. The order calculation for a nonempty coordinate ideal at a point of its support gives order one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_comap_eq_of_isOpenImmersion: For an affine open in the source, its image is affine and the open immersion identifies the two section rings. The pulled-back section ideal is the image of the target section ideal under this isomorphism. The target section ideal is radical by hypothesis, and ring isomorphisms preserve radicals. Thus every section ideal of the pullback is radical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ker_eq_of_isReduced: On an affine target open the kernel ideal consists of sections mapping to zero on its affine inverse image. If a power of a section lies in the kernel, the image of the section is nilpotent. The source is reduced, so its image is zero. The section itself belongs to the kernel, which is therefore radical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_primeSpectrum_vanishingIdeal_eq: The vanishing ideal consists of elements belonging to every prime in the given set. If a power of an element lies in all those primes, the element lies in each prime by primality. Thus the vanishing ideal is radical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_vanishingIdeal_eq_self: The radical of an ideal sheaf is the vanishing ideal of its support. The vanishing ideal of the closed set has that closed set as support, so taking its radical recovers it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comap_subschemeι_comp_of_smooth_p: Identify the pulled-back closed subscheme with the fiber product. By commutativity its composite to the target equals the isomorphism to the fiber product followed by the second projection and the original smooth morphism. All of these maps are smooth by the isomorphism and the hypotheses. Their composite is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comap_subschemeι_of_isOpenImmersi: The second projection of the fiber product is an open immersion, since it is a base change of the given open immersion. It is therefore smooth. Identify the pulled-back subscheme with the fiber product and compose this projection with the given smooth structure morphism.
