Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_comp_of_eq: The equality of ideals identifies their closed subschemes and inclusions. Under this identification the stated smooth morphism is the required one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_vanishingIdeal_comap_subschemeι: First restrict the original smooth vanishing subscheme to the open, which preserves smoothness. The local closed subset lies inside the hypersurface support, so the restricted vanishing subscheme factors through the hypersurface and remains isomorphic to its pullback there. This pullback is smooth by composition with the isomorphic second projection. The vanishing ideal pullback identity identifies it with the closed subscheme of the required ideal on the hypersurface.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_opens_vanishingIdeal: Support of a pullback is the inverse image of support. The support of the original vanishing ideal is the specified closed set, giving the formula for the open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_vanishingIdeal_eq_self: The support of the vanishing ideal is the zero locus of that ideal. For a closed set, taking its vanishing ideal and then its zero locus recovers the set itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_hom_of_iso: The inverse ring map supplies a preimage for each target element. Thus the forward map is surjective.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_of_isO: Apply the certificate pullback theorem with the established stability under open immersions. It gives the certificate for the pulled-back ideals and the inverse image of the boundary under the composed structural morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafGeometryHypotheses_vanishingId: The vanishing ideal assignment has order one at the required generic points of a smooth divisor, preserves local vanishing agreement under restriction to a closed subscheme, and commutes with restriction to opens. Apply the construction of the geometry hypotheses from these three properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.openImmersionStability: Pullback along an open immersion preserves nonvanishing on components. The induced map from the pulled-back closed subscheme is an open immersion, and pullback of a smooth divisor remains a smooth divisor. These three results give the required stability.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_vanishingIdealAssignment_eq_one: Replace the assignment by the ordinary vanishing ideal. Smoothness of the ambient scheme and the vanishing subscheme, together with the absence of any entire ambient component in the closed subset, give order one at each point of the subset by the smooth vanishing-ideal theorem.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothOrderOneCentersIsolated_vanishingI: The vanishing ideal assignment satisfies both the ideal-sheaf geometry and the smooth-vanishing hypotheses. Applying the isolation theorem for a principalization certificate with these hypotheses proves the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothVanishingHypotheses_vanishingIdeal: The order-one theorem for the vanishing ideal gives the required order condition. Smoothness of an open restriction and the smoothness results for the vanishing ideals on a divisor and on an open supply the three smoothness conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_opens_ι_comp_of_smooth: An open immersion is smooth, so its composite with the given smooth structural morphism is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_vanishingIdealAssignment_of_isSmo: Identify the assignments with the ordinary vanishing ideals. The closed subset on the divisor is the inverse image of the original subset, which lies in the divisor on the chosen open. The smooth restriction theorem for vanishing ideals along a smooth divisor gives smoothness of its vanishing subscheme over the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_vanishingIdealAssignment_restrict: Pullback of the vanishing ideal to the open equals the vanishing ideal of the inverse-image closed subset. The corresponding pulled-back subscheme is the open restriction of the original smooth subscheme, so it stays smooth over the field. The ideal equality gives the asserted smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingComapOpens: The assignment is the vanishing ideal sheaf. Pullback along an open immersion takes the vanishing ideal of a closed subset to the vanishing ideal of its inverse image. Apply this to the given open inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpens_mem: The affine opens cover the underlying space, so some affine open contains the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_subscheme_of_isSmoot: The closed subscheme of the smooth divisor has a smooth structural morphism to the field. A smooth morphism is locally of finite type, and the field is Noetherian. Thus the divisor is locally Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maximalIdeal_stalk_ne_bot_of_specializes: Choose an affine neighborhood of the specialized point. It also contains the point that specializes to it. The corresponding primes are strictly ordered because the points are distinct and related by specialization. Choose an element in the larger prime outside the smaller. Its germ lies in the maximal ideal of the stalk at the specialized point. If the germ were zero, some multiplier outside the larger prime would annihilate the original element. That multiplier is also outside the smaller prime, so primality would put the original element in the smaller prime. This contradiction gives a nonzero element of the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_vanishingIdeal_eq_one_of_not_mem: The given closed set is irreducible because it is the closure of its generic point. Enlarge it to an irreducible component of the whole scheme. The enlargement is strict by hypothesis, so its generic point is distinct from the original generic point and specializes to it. The stalk at the original point therefore has nonzero maximal ideal by the specialization argument. The order-one criterion for a vanishing ideal at the generic point of a maximal irreducible subset of its support now applies, taking the subset to be the whole given closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingOrderOneOnSmoothDivisor: The smooth divisor is locally Noetherian by its smooth structure morphism to the field. Apply the order-one vanishing-ideal theorem to the closed subset and its generic point, using that the subset is not an irreducible component.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineAllLevelsSmooth: Use the chosen affine embedding and principalization data. The inductive smoothness result applies to their ambient structure maps at every stage within the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineBoundaryInStrictNormalCrossingPosi: Construct the affine-space principalization data from the algorithm and the ambient hypotheses. The stagewise boundary result applies at every level of these data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineCentersHaveStrictNormalCrossingsWi: Construct the principalization data for the given affine scheme using the specified embedding and ambient hypotheses. Every center of these data has strict normal crossings with its boundary by the stagewise center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundaryInStrictNormalCrossingPosition: At stage zero the boundary is empty and the ambient scheme is smooth, so it is in strict normal crossings position. At a successor the previous boundary has this property by induction, and the current center has strict normal crossings with it. On the Noetherian successor scheme the blowup result gives strict normal crossings for the strict transforms of the old boundary followed by the new exceptional divisor. This is the boundary list defined at that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersHaveStrictNormalCrossingsWithBoun: At every stage before the end, the principalization sequence includes a proof that its center has strict normal crossings with the existing boundary. These are exactly the center conditions for the affine ambient sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_schemeAtToSpec: Induct on the stage. At zero the structure map factors through an isomorphism to the smooth ambient scheme. For the successor, the preceding ambient map is smooth by induction and the current center has strict normal crossings with the boundary. The blowup smoothness result therefore gives smoothness after this blowup. The structural map at the successor is precisely this composite.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineCentersLieOverSingularLocus_princi: Apply the embedded center avoidance result to the affine-space embedding datum for the canonical principalization with radical centers. Its hypotheses are supplied by correctness and functoriality of the canonical algorithm, radicality of smooth centers, the blowup transition result, and the empty-boundary property for smooth schemes. The embedded sequence formed from the chosen datum agrees with the sequence obtained from the affine-space data. Their induced blowup sequences thus have the same center condition, which puts the affine centers over the singular locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupSequence_centersLieOver_congr: Replace the first embedded sequence by the equal second one. The certificates that its transitions are blowups prove the same proposition and do not change the induced sequence data or the center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centerOffDetached_eq_top_of_smooth: The detached locus is open by canonical chart isolation and is closed because the strict transform is Noetherian. A point on the support of the center off the detached locus maps into the ambient center. For a smooth original scheme, the component isolation theorem puts every such point in the detached locus. But the support of the center off that locus lies in its complement. This contradiction proves the support is empty and the ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersLieOver_embeddedResolutionRuleOfP: Suppose a center point projects to the smooth locus of the original affine scheme. Since the embedding is closed, that smooth locus is the inverse image of an ambient open. Choose an ambient basic open through the image point contained in that ambient open. Its inverse image in the original scheme is affine and smooth over the field. Restrict the embedding datum to these opens. The ambient inclusion is smooth, so compatibility of the embedded rule identifies its sequence on this chart with the pullback of the original sequence, with empty centers deleted. The chart sequence has length zero because its source is smooth. Yet the given center point lifts to a point in the support of the pulled-back center over the chart, and such a nonempty center must be retained. This would give a step of the length-zero sequence, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersLieOver_of_withoutIsoBlowups: A point in the support of an original center shows that its ideal is nonunit, since the unit ideal has empty support. The corresponding step is retained in the shortened sequence. The shortened center and its projection to the base are the original center and projection at that index. The shortened sequence’s center condition therefore applies to the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowupsWithoutIso_eq_withoutIsoBl: The shortened induced sequence is defined by first constructing the full induced sequence and then deleting the unit-center blowups.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackSeq_of_smooth: The ambient morphism is smooth over the field and the new embedding is the pullback of the original one along it. These are the hypotheses of the smooth compatibility theorem for the embedded resolution rule constructed from functorial principalization. The theorem gives the required pullback of sequences along the induced morphism of embedded schemes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_morphismRestrict: Restriction of the closed immersion to the target open is a pullback square along the open inclusion. The flat base-change formula for kernel ideals identifies the new kernel with the original kernel pulled back to that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_smoothLocusComplement_iff: The closed complement consists exactly of the points that do not belong to the smooth locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_of_embeddingDatum: The datum identifies the structural morphism with the closed immersion into the ambient scheme followed by the ambient structural morphism. Both maps are quasi-compact, so their composite is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_opens_ι: An open immersion is locally of finite presentation and induces isomorphisms on stalks. Each stalk map is formally smooth, so every point of the open lies in the smooth locus of the inclusion. The inclusion is therefore smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ι_comp_of_le_smoothLocus: Every point of the given open maps to a point at which the structural morphism has formally smooth stalk map. The open inclusion induces an isomorphism on stalks, hence a formally smooth map. Their composite is the stalk map of the restricted morphism and is formally smooth. Since the restricted morphism is locally of finite presentation, this proves smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toEmbeddedBlowupSequence_center_eq_top_o: For a smooth input the center off the detached locus is the unit ideal, so it defines the empty subscheme. The total-space center is the kernel of the map from that subscheme into the total space. A map from an empty scheme has unit kernel, giving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toEmbeddedBlowupSequence_centersLieOver_: The shortened sequence is the embedded resolution rule on the given datum, so every one of its centers lies over the complement of the smooth locus. Every point of an original center belongs to a retained step. The transfer from the shortened sequence thus gives the center condition for the full induced sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_length_eq_zero_of_smoo: Every induced center is the unit ideal for a smooth input. If the shortened sequence had positive length, its first retained center would be nonunit and would come from a step within the original length. This contradicts the unit-center result, so the shortened length is zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineDetachedClopenInCenter: For the arbitrary affine input, apply the result identifying the discarded subscheme with an open and closed subscheme of the current center. That identification at every stage provides the required affine condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineDetachedSmooth: The discarded scheme is isomorphic over the ambient scheme to an open and closed subscheme of the current center. The center is smooth over the field, so this open subscheme is smooth. The ambient compatibility of the isomorphism identifies its structural morphism with the one from the discarded scheme and transfers smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_eq: The boundary update sends each previous boundary member to its strict transform, in the same order, and appends the exceptional divisor from the current blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedClopenInCenter_ofAffine: The ambient stages are Noetherian. At stage zero the principalization ideal is the vanishing ideal of the strict-transform image, so its support is that image. The inductive support theorem then puts the later ideal supports in the union of the strict transform and boundary. Generic-point avoidance shows that no strict-transform component image lies in a boundary member. These facts meet the hypotheses of the result identifying the discarded scheme with an open and closed subscheme of the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedClopenInCenter_of_isNoetherian_o: Work at a fixed stage. The center support lies in the support of the principalization ideal and hence in the union of the strict-transform image and the boundary supports. Each discarded strict-transform component lies in the center. To see that its inverse image in the center is a component, enlarge it to an irreducible set in the center and take the closure of that set’s ambient image. This irreducible closure lies in the finite closed union just described. It cannot lie in a single boundary support, since it contains the original discarded component and that component lies in no boundary member. It therefore lies in the strict-transform image. Maximality of the original component within that image forces equality. Thus the discarded locus in the center is a union of its irreducible components. The center is smooth, so its local rings are domains and distinct components are disjoint. The Noetherian space has finitely many components, making this union open and closed. Its reduced subscheme and the discarded subscheme give closed immersions into the ambient scheme with the same support. They are isomorphic over the ambient scheme by uniqueness of the reduced closed structure.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_mul_weakTransform_succ: The order-one principalization sequence defines the successor ideal by requiring that its product with the exceptional ideal equal the pullback of the preceding ideal. This is the transform equation at the indicated stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_of_range_base_eq: The two reduced closed immersions have the same closed image. For each immersion its kernel is contained in the vanishing ideal of this image, since that ideal is the radical of the kernel. The reduced subscheme given by the common vanishing ideal is therefore isomorphic over the ambient scheme to each source. Compose one inverse with the other isomorphism to obtain the required identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_vanishingIdeal_of_c: The kernel containment gives a factorization of the reduced vanishing subscheme through the given closed immersion. Its image in the ambient scheme is the specified closure, which contains every point of the original immersion’s image. Injectivity of the original immersion therefore makes the factorization surjective on points. The factorization is an immersion and its range is the entire target, so it is a surjective closed immersion. Its kernel has full support and the target is reduced, hence the kernel is zero. This makes the factorization an isomorphism with the stated ambient compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_list_subset_of_isIrreducible: Induct on the list of closed sets. The empty union cannot contain the nonempty irreducible set. For a nonempty list, the first set and the finite union of the tail are both closed. Irreducibility forces the given set to lie entirely in one of the two. In the tail case use induction to choose the desired member.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientLevel_ofAffine: Convert the affine principalization data to their embedded blowup sequence. The ambient stage of this sequence is Noetherian by the finite-stage theorem and is the affine ambient level in question.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_mem_support_vanishingIdeal: The vanishing ideal of the given closed set has that set as its support. Replace the support in the membership assumption by the closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_range_strictTransformι_iff: The strict-transform inclusion is the inclusion of the closed subscheme defined by the strict-transform ideal. Its range is therefore the support of that ideal, which gives the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_comap: The support of a pulled-back ideal sheaf is the inverse image of the support along the underlying map. Evaluating this formula at the point gives the stated equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_mul: On an affine neighborhood, a point is in the support of the product if its prime ideal contains the product of the two section ideals. Primality makes this equivalent to containing at least one of the factors. That is membership in one of the two supports.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_le: Support reverses inclusion of ideals. Any point of the support of the larger ideal is therefore a point of the support of the smaller ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_strictTransform: The point lies in the support of the pulled-back subscheme ideal, so it lifts to that closed subscheme. Its image in the previous scheme avoids the center, so this lift lies in the open used to form the strict transform. Hence the point belongs to the image of the strict-transform immersion. The support of its kernel ideal is the closure of that image and contains the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_strictTransformImmersion: The strict-transform immersion is an embedding on underlying spaces. The image of the inverse image of any quasi-compact open is a subset of the Noetherian ambient space, hence quasi-compact. The embedding reflects this property to the inverse image, proving quasi-compactness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_base_subschemeι: The inclusion of the closed subscheme defined by an ideal sheaf identifies its underlying space with the support of that ideal. Its range is therefore that support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_weakTransform_subset_range_or_bo: At stage zero use the assumed support containment. At a successor, membership in the new ideal support gives membership in the support of its product with the exceptional ideal. The transform equation shows that the image point downstairs belongs to the previous ideal support. If the point lies on the new exceptional divisor, it lies in the new boundary. Otherwise its image avoids the center. The induction hypothesis puts that image in the preceding strict transform or in a preceding boundary member. Away from the center the strict transform contains every inverse-image point of the corresponding support. Thus the original point belongs to the new strict transform or to the transformed boundary member.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.weakTransform_le_ambientCenter: The principalization data require the current ideal to vanish on the current center. This vanishing means exactly containment of the ideal in the center ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineEmbedsIntoAffineSpace: The affine structural morphism is locally of finite type, so its global ring is a finite type algebra over the field. Choose a surjection from a polynomial ring in finitely many variables. Extend it by one variable sent to zero, retaining surjectivity. The map on spectra gives a closed immersion over the field into the corresponding affine space. Its image is contained in the proper coordinate hyperplane of the added variable. Affine space is irreducible, so the support of the kernel contains no ambient component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_univ_of_mem_irreducibleComponents_of_: An irreducible component is maximal among irreducible sets. Since the entire space is irreducible and contains the given component, maximality forces the component to be the whole space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extension_X_last_eq_zero: The extended polynomial map is defined by evaluating the original variables as before and the final variable at zero. In particular it sends the final variable itself to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extension_surjective: Given an element of the target, choose an original polynomial mapping to it. Regard this polynomial as a polynomial in the enlarged variable list using only the original variables. On these variables the extended map agrees with the original map, so the enlarged polynomial has the same image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embedding_and_comp_eq: A surjective algebra map from the polynomial ring induces a closed immersion on spectra. Transporting through the spectrum identifications of the source and affine space preserves this property. The composite to the field spectrum corresponds to the polynomial constant inclusion followed by the algebra map. Since the map preserves the field algebra structure, this composite on rings is the given structure map on global sections. Thus the embedding is over the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducible_univ_affineSpaceIndexedBy: The polynomial ring over a field is an integral domain, so its spectrum is irreducible. The homeomorphism from that spectrum to affine space takes the whole spectrum onto the whole affine space and preserves irreducibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoSpec_hom_comp_spec_map_appTop: The canonical map from an affine scheme to the spectrum of its global sections is natural. Apply naturality to the given map to the field spectrum. The field and the global sections of its spectrum are identified by the standard isomorphism, so the resulting identifications cancel and recover the original morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ker_ne_univ_of_map_X_eq_zero: Under the affine-space spectrum identification, every image prime contains the chosen variable, because the algebra map sends it to zero. The closure of the image is therefore contained in the closed zero locus of that variable. The zero prime of the polynomial ring is outside this zero locus, since the variable is nonzero. Hence the closure is proper. For the quasi-compact embedding map this closure is the support of the kernel ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_def: The ambient boundary at each stage is taken from the principalization sequence at that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_of_dense_preimage_inl_inr: Take a nonempty open of the disjoint union and choose a point in it. The point belongs to one of the two summands, on which the inverse image of the open is nonempty and open. Density in that summand gives a point of the restricted set in this open. Its image belongs to the original open and the original set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_of_isEmpty: Density asks that every point lie in the closure of the subset. In an empty space the condition is vacuous.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_coprod_desc: The map defined on the coproduct restricts to the two given maps on the summands. Their inverse images are dense, so the inverse image under the coproduct map is dense by the summand criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_eqToHom_comp: After identifying the equal sources, the transport is the identity. The two maps therefore have the same inverse image of the subset, which is dense by hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_of_dense_preimage_inl_inr: The inverse image of the target set along the composite from each summand is the restriction of the global inverse image to that summand. These two restrictions are dense by hypothesis. The disjoint-union density criterion gives density of the global inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_of_eq: Equal morphisms have identical underlying point maps and hence identical inverse-image sets. Transfer the given density along this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_of_isEmpty_left: The inverse image in the empty summand is automatically dense, and in the other summand it is dense by hypothesis. The coproduct density criterion gives density on the whole source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_preimage_smoothLocus_of_discardedU: At zero the discarded union is empty and density is vacuous. At a successor the two summands map by the previous union map and the newly discarded map. Their inverse images of the smooth locus are dense by induction and the hypothesis on newly discarded pieces. Density then holds on their disjoint union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToBase_comp_eq: Expand the discarded piece’s projection to the base. The initial strict-transform map to the base followed by the field map equals the initial ambient structural map restricted to the strict transform. The strict-transform projection to zero is compatible with the ambient maps to the field. Substituting these equalities gives the claimed composite from the discarded piece.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToBase_def: By definition the discarded piece maps to the base by inclusion into its strict transform, projection to the initial strict transform, and then the initial map to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_mem_irreducibleComponents_of_conti: The continuous inverse sends the component to an irreducible set. To prove maximality, take any irreducible set containing that image and apply the forward map. Its image is irreducible and contains the original component, so maximality forces it inside the original component. Applying the inverse map forces the larger set inside the desired image, giving maximality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_comp_blowupSequence_projectionToBase: At zero this is the defining formula for the map from the initial strict transform to the base. At a successor, factor the total-space projection through the preceding stage. The total transition on the strict-transform summand is the strict-transform transition followed by the preceding summand inclusion. Use the induction hypothesis for that inclusion and its projection to obtain the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inr_comp_eq_coprod_desc: Factor the final map through the transition using the stated equation. On the previous discarded summand the transition restricts to its inclusion in the preceding total space. On the newly discarded summand it factors through the preceding strict transform, and by hypothesis its composite to the target is the prescribed map. The two composites therefore agree on both summands and are equal by the coproduct property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isProper_eqToHom_comp: Identify the equal source schemes. Transport is then the identity, so the composite is the original proper morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isProper_projectionToBase: Induct on the stage. The initial projection is an isomorphism and hence proper. At a successor, the preceding stage is Noetherian by the Noetherianity theorem for blowup sequences. The next transition is therefore proper by the blowup properness hypothesis. Its composite with the proper preceding projection is the next projection and is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_of_isEmpt: The strict normal crossings condition asks for a local description at each point. The scheme is empty, so every ideal satisfies this condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_reducedIn: The two open summands cover the coproduct. On each, the reduced inverse image is the reduced inverse image under the corresponding given map, which has strict normal crossings. The locality of this condition on the summands proves it for the entire coproduct.

Identify the discarded piece with its open and closed subscheme of the current center. The identification preserves ambient images and matches their irreducible components, so no component of this open subscheme lies in a boundary member. The ambient boundary is in strict normal crossings position and the center meets it in strict normal crossings. The restriction result therefore gives strict normal crossings for the radical of the boundary product pulled back to the open subscheme. Its support is the pullback of the union of boundary supports. By the prescribed description on the discarded piece, this is exactly the inverse image of the original singular locus. Hence that radical is the required reduced inverse-image ideal after transporting through the isomorphism. The strict normal crossings property descends along this isomorphism to the discarded piece.

At zero there are no points at which to check strict normal crossings. At every successor the reduced inverse image restricts on the two summands to the reduced inverse image for the previous union and for the newly discarded piece. The induction hypothesis handles the first, and the calculation using the clopen center description and boundary handles the second. The coproduct criterion gives strict normal crossings on the full union.
Identifying the equal source schemes makes transport the identity. The reduced inverse-image ideal for the composite is then the given one, with its strict normal crossings property.
Equal maps define the same inverse-image closed set and the same reduced vanishing ideal. The strict normal crossings condition therefore transfers.
The empty summand satisfies the pointwise strict normal crossings condition vacuously. The other summand satisfies it by hypothesis. Applying locality on the two open summands gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrongResolution_blowupSequenceWithout: The full induced sequence projects to the base by the blowup transitions, and its projection on the accumulated discarded summand is the coproduct of the maps of the pieces detached so far. At the final stage the strict-transform ideal is the unit ideal, so the remaining strict-transform summand is empty. Induction on discarded pieces therefore gives smoothness over the field, density of the inverse image of the smooth locus, and strict normal crossings for the reduced inverse image of the singular locus on the entire final scheme. The projection is proper as a composite of proper blowups over Noetherian stages. Deleting unit-center steps preserves the final object and map and keeps all retained centers over the singular locus. The shortened sequence is consequently an isomorphism over the smooth locus. These facts give the six strong resolution conditions.

For the given affine scheme construct the principalization data using the specified embedding into smooth affine space with empty boundary. The affine hypotheses supply the blowup transitions, the properties of the discarded pieces and centers, and the ambient boundary conditions at each stage of these data. Apply the strong resolution criterion for the shortened induced sequence, using the stated restriction and properness results.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_comp_base_eq_preimage_preimage: For each point of the first source, membership in the inverse image under the composite means that its second image belongs to the set. This is precisely membership in the inverse image of the second map’s inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.schemeAtToSpec_def: The structural map at stage i is defined by composing the ambient projection to the original affine space with that affine space’s structural map to the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_discardedUnion_comp: At stage zero the accumulated discarded scheme is empty, so its map to the field is smooth. At a successor the prescribed map is the coproduct of the previous accumulated map and the map of the newly discarded piece. After composing with the field map the preceding summand is smooth by induction. The new summand is smooth by the discarded smoothness hypothesis and agreement of its two structural maps. Hence the coproduct is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_eqToHom_comp_comp: Identify the two equal source schemes. The transport morphism is then the identity, so its composition with the given maps is the original smooth composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_from_initial: Every morphism from the initial scheme is its unique map to the target. This empty-source map is smooth, since smoothness is local on the source and there are no points to check.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_eq: The two morphisms are equal. Substituting the second for the first gives the given smoothness hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_isEmpty_left: The restriction to the empty summand is smooth vacuously, and the restriction to the other summand is smooth by hypothesis. The map is the coproduct of its two restrictions, so it is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToZero_comp_schemeAtToSpe: At stage zero the projection of the strict transform is the identity. At a successor, first use the preceding equality to identify the composite to the field after the strict-transform transition. The commuting square with the ambient blowdown replaces this transition followed by inclusion by inclusion followed by blowdown. The ambient structural maps commute with that blowdown, giving the structural map at the new stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToZero_succ: By the recursive definition, the projection of the successor strict transform to the initial one first passes to the preceding strict transform and then applies the preceding projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToZero_zero: The recursion begins at stage zero with the identity on the initial strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformZeroToBase_comp: The initial total-space isomorphism is compatible with the original embedding transported into the initial ambient stage. Composing that compatibility with the initial ambient structural morphism cancels the ambient isomorphism with its inverse. What remains is the original embedding followed by its structure map, which is the original structural morphism over the field. This gives the claimed agreement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformZeroToBase_def: The map from the initial strict transform to the original scheme is the inclusion of its summand in the initial total space followed by the chosen initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_eq_preimage: The zero locus of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original zero locus. These zero loci are the respective supports, giving the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_prod_eq_iUnion: For the empty list the product is the unit ideal and its support is empty. At each step the support of a product is the union of the two supports. Induction yields the union of the supports of all list members.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec_eq: Apply the compatibility of the inverse affine-space isomorphism with the structure maps and precompose with the forward isomorphism. The two isomorphisms cancel, giving the stated expression.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsSmooth: The map from the polynomial spectrum to the field spectrum is smooth because the corresponding algebra map is smooth. The affine-space structural map is obtained from it by precomposing with an isomorphism, so it is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebra_smooth_mvPolynomial: A polynomial algebra on finitely many variables is finitely presented by those generators with no relations. It is formally smooth because lifts of the finitely many variable images across a nilpotent extension define a lift of the entire polynomial map. Together these give smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nilIsStrictNormalCrossingsOnAffineSpace: Use the whole affine space as a coordinate neighborhood at every point, with its identity chart and all coordinates available. This chart is étale. The boundary list is empty, so the conditions assigning coordinate hyperplanes to boundary members and requiring distinct coordinates hold vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringHom_smooth_algebraMap_mvPolynomial: The constant-coefficient inclusion defines the polynomial algebra structure. Smoothness of this algebra is equivalent to smoothness of that ring homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specIso_inv_comp_affineSpaceIndexedByToS: The standard isomorphism between affine space and the spectrum of its polynomial ring is an isomorphism over the ground field. Its inverse commutes with the structure maps, with the spectrum structure map induced by the constant-coefficient inclusion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersLieOverSingularLocus_of_inducedCe: The total-space center restricts along the strict-transform summand to the center off the detached locus. Thus a point of the latter support maps to a point of the total-space center support. The induced-center condition sends this image to the singular locus of the base. The total-space projection restricted to the summand equals the strict-transform projection, so the original point has the same base image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_comp_totalSpaceToBase: At zero the restriction of the initial isomorphism to the strict-transform summand is the defined strict-transform map to the base. At a successor the inclusion of the strict-transform summand commutes with the total-space transition and the strict-transform transition. Use that square to move the inclusion past the transition. The induction hypothesis then gives the preceding strict-transform projection, and composition gives the new one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceToBase_eq_blowupSequence_proje: At zero both projections are the forward map of the same initial isomorphism. At a successor both are obtained by composing the preceding projection with the same successor transition. Induction gives equality at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceToBase_succ: At each successor the recursion defines the projection as the transition to the preceding stage followed by the projection from that stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceToBase_zero: At stage zero the recursion for the total-space projection begins with the forward map of the initial isomorphism to the original scheme.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_add: Pullback on global sections is a ring homomorphism and preserves sums.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_id_apply: The identity scheme map induces the identity ring map on global sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_sub: Pullback on global sections is a ring homomorphism and preserves differences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closedEmbeddingsRelatedByAutomorphism: Each closed immersion into an affine space induces a surjection on global coordinate rings. Use the first surjection to lift the coordinate functions of the second embedding to sections on the first affine space, and use the second surjection to lift the coordinates of the first embedding. In the combined affine space, stabilize the first embedding by adding zero coordinates in the second block and the second by adding zeros in the first. The two families of lifts give the coordinate changes that carry one stabilized embedding to the other over the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_appTop_apply: Global sections are contravariant in the scheme. Pulling a section back along the composite therefore consists of pulling it back along the second morphism and then along the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_affineSpace_sum_comp_eq_of_co: Write the coordinates of the combined affine space as two blocks. The given sections in the first affine space reproduce the second embedding’s coordinates on the source, and the sections in the second reproduce the first. Define an automorphism fixing the first block and adding the first family of sections to the second block. Its inverse subtracts those same sections since the first block is fixed. Define a second automorphism fixing the second block and subtracting the second family from the first block, with inverse given by addition. The first automorphism takes the first stabilized embedding, whose second block is zero, to the map with both sets of embedding coordinates. The second automorphism then cancels the first block and leaves the second intact, giving the second stabilized embedding. Each map is over the base and is determined by its coordinate pullbacks, so the composite gives the required automorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.allLevelsNoetherian_toEmbeddedBlowupSequ: The finite-stage Noetherianity theorem applies to the embedded blowup sequence obtained from the given embedding and algorithm. It gives the required result at every stage at or below the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_detachedClosureCompl: The underlying set of the open complement of the detached closure is the ordinary set complement of that closed subset.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_detachedOpens: The detached open is the detached locus equipped with a proof that it is open. Its underlying set is therefore that locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coprodSwapAssocIso_hom: The forward morphism of the isomorphism was defined to be the map that rearranges and reassociates the three coproduct summands.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint_detachedOpens_detachedClosureCo: Every point of the detached locus also belongs to its closure. Thus it cannot lie in the complement of that closure, and the two opens are disjoint.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_of_eq_vanishingIdea: Substitute the vanishing ideal for the given equal ideal. In a reduced scheme the reduced closed subscheme of a closed open set is isomorphic over the ambient scheme to the open subscheme on that set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_detachedLocus_subset_ambientCenter: A point of the detached locus lies in a detached component. Each such component is defined by requiring its entire ambient image to lie in the center support, so the point’s image lies there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_coprod_desc_cent: The current strict transform is reduced and Noetherian, so the open detached locus is also closed and its reduced subscheme agrees with that open subscheme. The map from the next strict transform is the blowup along the pulled-back ambient center by the strict-transform lift theorem. Its range lies in the complement of the detached locus. Indeed, the preceding support away from the center lies in the ambient image of this complement, and that image is closed. The closure formula for the next support and the commuting blowdown square therefore put every image point in the complement. Restricting the blowup to this open keeps its whole source and restricts its center to the center off the detached locus. On the detached open the latter center is the unit ideal because its support lies in the closed complement. The map on that summand is an isomorphism. The local blowup criterion on these two disjoint opens now gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_coprod_desc_of_d: Because the two target opens are disjoint and the summands map into their respective opens, the inverse image of each open in the coproduct is exactly its source summand. The comparison isomorphisms commute with the restricted maps. Over the first open this identifies the restriction with the given blowup. Over the second it identifies the restriction with the given isomorphism, which is the blowup along the unit ideal there. These two opens cover the target, and the blowup property is local for this cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_lift_of_comp_eq: The given closed immersion has the ideal used to define the strict transform as its kernel. The canonical lift of the strict transform to the original closed subscheme has the same composite to the ambient scheme as the prescribed map. The closed immersion is a monomorphism, so the two lifts are equal. The blowup result for the canonical lift gives the desired property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_totalTransition_: The total center is supported in the previous strict-transform summand. Its pullback to that summand is the center off the detached locus, and its pullback to the already detached summand is the unit ideal. Thus the given blowup on the first summand and the identity on the second form a blowup of the full center. The total transition equals this coproduct map after the canonical rearrangement of the three source summands, as seen by checking each summand. Precomposition with that source isomorphism preserves the blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClopen_of_mem_irreducibleComponents_of: Smoothness over the field gives regular local rings, so distinct irreducible components are disjoint. The scheme is locally Noetherian, so the irreducible components are locally finite. Each component is closed, and its complement is a union of the other components, which is closed by local finiteness. Thus the component is also open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_detachedClosureCompl: Noetherianity makes the detached locus equal to its closure. The stated open is therefore the complement of that locus. Since the locus is open by hypothesis, its complement is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: The field spectrum is Noetherian, and the ambient scheme is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over it, so the ambient scheme is Noetherian. Stage zero is isomorphic to it. At each successor the ambient transition is a blowup of the preceding Noetherian scheme, which gives a Noetherian source. Induction proves the property through the final stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_strictTransform_of_isNoetheria: At zero the strict transform is defined by the kernel of the original reduced scheme’s closed immersion, transported through the ambient isomorphism. This kernel defines a reduced subscheme. At a successor, the preceding strict transform is reduced by induction and the strict-transform immersion is quasi-compact in the Noetherian new ambient stage. The strict transform of a reduced closed subscheme under this blowup is reduced, completing the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_schemeAtToSpec: Induct on the stage for the projection to the original ambient scheme. The first projection is an isomorphism. Each successor factor is the blowup of a Noetherian scheme and is proper, hence locally of finite type. Composing with the preceding projection preserves this property. Composing each stage projection with the original ambient structure map to the field preserves it once more.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_strictTransformToSpe: The strict-transform inclusion is a closed immersion and hence locally of finite type. The ambient stage’s structural map is locally of finite type as well, so their composite has the property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_of_isClosedImmersion: The closed immersion identifies its source with a closed subspace of the target. A subspace of a Noetherian space is Noetherian, giving the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_strictTransform_of_noeth: Apply preservation of Noetherianity under taking a closed subspace to the strict-transform inclusion at the given stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_strictTransformι_blowdown: The new ambient space is Noetherian. The strict-transform immersion is an embedding into that space and its source is Noetherian. Its inverse images of quasi-compact opens are consequently quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_coprod_inl_eq_preimage: Every point of the first summand maps into the first target set. Conversely, a point mapping into that set cannot belong to the second summand, whose image lies in the disjoint second target set. Since the two summands cover the source, it belongs to the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_coprod_inr_eq_preimage: Every point of the second summand maps into the second target set. If a point mapping into that set were in the first summand, its image would also lie in the first target set, contradicting disjointness. It therefore lies in the second summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.schemeAtToSpec_eq: The structural map at a stage is defined by its ambient projection to the original ambient scheme followed by that scheme’s structural map to the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_vanishingIdeal_comp_of: The original smooth scheme is reduced. Its reduced vanishing subscheme on the given clopen set is isomorphic over the ambient scheme to the open subscheme on that set. The open subscheme has smooth structural morphism by restriction. The identification of the immersions transports smoothness to the vanishing subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToSpec_eq: The strict-transform structural morphism is obtained by composing its ambient inclusion with the ambient stage’s structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformι_eq_subschemeι: By construction the strict transform is the closed subscheme of its strict-transform ideal, so its inclusion is the closed immersion defined by that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_centerOffDetached_subset_detache: The center off the detached locus has ideal equal to the kernel of the closed subscheme on the complement followed by the open inclusion. This source is Noetherian, so the composite is quasi-compact and the support of its kernel is the closure of the image. The image lies in the complement of the detached locus, which is closed because the locus is open. Its closure therefore lies in that same complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionsAreBlowupsForEmbeddings_of_de: For any embedding datum the assumed openness holds at every stage. The embedded sequence from the algorithm also has Noetherian ambient stages. The preceding blowup construction applies to these two facts and identifies its transitions as blowups.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionsAreBlowups_of_detachedLocusIs: For a stage within the sequence, openness of the detached locus and Noetherianity give the blowup description on the strict-transform summand. The coproduct argument extends it to the full total transition. The successor arrow of the tower is this transition, so each such arrow is the required blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.union_detachedOpens_detachedClosureCompl: In the Noetherian strict transform the detached locus is closed, so its closure equals the locus. The two opens are the locus and its complement, whose union is the whole space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdealClosureImage_eq: The named ideal is defined by taking the topological closure of the set’s image and then its vanishing ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineDetachedComponentsNotInBoundary: The discarded scheme embeds into the strict transform as a finite union of its irreducible components. The image of a component of the discarded scheme is irreducible, so it lies in one of these closed components. The inverse image of that component under the closed embedding is irreducible and contains the chosen component. Maximality makes them equal, so the image is the entire corresponding strict-transform component. Choose its generic point. Its ambient image avoids earlier centers, so it cannot lie in the support of any current boundary member. If the entire discarded component image lay in the indicated boundary support, it would contain this generic image there, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineStrictTransformEmptyAtLast_of_isFu: The principalization algorithm ends with the unit ideal, which has order zero at every point. If the last strict transform had a component, choose a generic point of it. The componentwise order-one result would give order one for the final principalization ideal at that point, a contradiction. Every point lies on an irreducible component, so the final strict transform is empty. The support of its defining ideal is the range of the inclusion and therefore empty, making the ideal the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.discardedComponents_subset_irreducibleCo: Membership in the discarded family requires being an irreducible component of the strict transform, in addition to being contained in the ambient center. The first condition gives the inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_preimage_eq: A closed embedding induces the subspace topology on its source. By the definition of the induced topology, every source open is the inverse image of an ambient open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_finset_subset_of_isIrreducibl: Induct on the finite family of closed sets. The empty family cannot cover a nonempty irreducible set. When one set is added, split the union into that closed set and the finite closed union of the other sets. Irreducibility puts the original set entirely in one of these two parts. In the second case apply the induction hypothesis to the remaining family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_of_isIrreducible_subset_sUnio: Represent the finite family by a finite list of its distinct members. The same closed sets cover the irreducible set. The finite-family result supplies a member containing it, which belongs to the original family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedEmbedding_discardedι: The discarded scheme is the closed subscheme of the strict transform defined by the discarded ideal. Its inclusion is a closed immersion and hence a closed embedding on points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIrreducible_preimage_of_isClosedEmbedd: Preirreducibility follows by the open-intersection argument. The original set is nonempty and lies in the embedding range, so any chosen point of it has a preimage. Hence the preimage is also nonempty and is irreducible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPreirreducible_preimage_of_isClosedEmb: Let two source opens each meet the inverse image. Express them as inverse images of ambient opens, using the induced topology. Their ambient counterparts each meet the given preirreducible set, so the intersection of the two ambient opens also meets it. Every point of this set is in the image of the embedding, so lift the intersection point. The lift belongs to both source opens and to the inverse image, proving preirreducibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_discardedι_eq_sUnion_discardedComp: The range of the discarded inclusion is the support of the discarded ideal. This ideal is the vanishing ideal of the closure of the discarded locus, so its support is that closure. In the Noetherian strict transform the discarded locus is a finite union of closed components and is already closed. Substituting its definition gives the claimed union.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_or_subset_of_isIrreducible: If the irreducible set were contained in neither closed set, the complements of the two closed sets would each meet it. Irreducibility forces their intersection to meet it, contradicting the given containment in the union.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_discardedLocusOpens: The open subscheme is defined by equipping the discarded locus with its given proof of openness. Forgetting this proof leaves the original locus as its underlying set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedPrincipalizationYieldsBlowups_of: For any affine input and stage, the ambient levels are Noetherian and the current strict transform is reduced. The discarded locus is clopen. The next strict transform maps into its complement, and there the lifted transition is the blowup of the restricted center by the strict-transform blowup theorem. The discarded piece contributes the identity over the complementary open with empty center. The coproduct construction first gives the required blowup on the previous strict transform and then adjoins the identity on the already discarded summands. Thus every total-space transition is the blowup of its total center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_discardedSubscheme_discardedL: The discarded locus is open by hypothesis and closed by Noetherianity. Its closure is itself, so the discarded ideal is its reduced vanishing ideal. The clopen subscheme of the reduced strict transform is reduced and has this same closed support. The unique reduced closed structure therefore identifies it with the discarded subscheme over the strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_of_ideal_eq: Equal ideal sheaves define the same closed subscheme and inclusion. Transport the given isomorphism and its factorization equation along this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_discardedLocus_subset_support: Any point of the discarded locus belongs to one of its discarded components. The defining condition for that component puts its ambient image entirely in the center support. Hence the given point’s image lies there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_mem_irreducibleComponents_of_isOpe: Continuity makes the image of the component irreducible. An irreducible set containing it must lie entirely in the clopen range of the embedding, because it meets the range and cannot meet both it and its complement. The inverse image of this larger set is irreducible under the homeomorphism to the range and contains the original component. Maximality puts it inside that component. Applying the embedding proves maximality of the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_coprodDesc_copro: On the first target summand the given map is the blowup of the restricted ideal. On the second target summand the restricted ideal is the unit ideal, whose blowup is the identity. Their coproduct is therefore the blowup of the full ideal. Reassociate and reorder the three source summands by their canonical isomorphism. The resulting map agrees with the displayed map on every summand, so it too is the required blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_coprodDesc_of_re: The discarded locus and its complement form a two-open cover of the strict transform. On the complement the center off the detached locus restricts to the restricted ambient center, because restricting the kernel of the defining composite recovers the kernel of the restricted closed immersion. On the discarded open the center ideal restricts to the unit ideal, since its support is in the closed complement. The two source summands map into these respective opens. The pullback of the coproduct map to the complement is therefore the specified blowup there, while the pullback to the discarded open is the isomorphism from the discarded subscheme and hence the blowup of the unit ideal. The blowup property is local on the target, so these identifications prove the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_lift_discardedLo: The complement of the discarded locus is clopen and its inclusion into the ambient stage is a closed immersion. Its components are components of the original strict transform, and none is contained in the center, since such a component would have been discarded. The ambient complement of the center meets the original strict transform only in this clopen part. Thus the kernel ideals of the full and shortened closed immersions have the same restriction away from the center, and give the same strict transform in the new ambient stage. The strict-transform blowup theorem applied to the clopen part makes this new strict transform its blowup along the restricted center. The lifting map is the indicated factorization of the strict-transform transition, since both composites to the previous ambient stage agree and the closed immersion is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_transitionMap_of: The total center restricts on the strict-transform summand to the center off the detached locus, by the kernel formula for the inclusion of a closed subscheme in that summand. Its restriction to the old discarded summand is the unit ideal. On the first part the hypothesized coproduct map is a blowup, and on the old discarded summand the transition is the identity. The coproduct blowup result, with the required reassociation of summands, gives the full transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_coprodSwapAssocHom: Use the map that restores the original association and order of the three summands as inverse. Each composite is the identity on every summand, so it is the identity by the coproduct universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_strictTransform: At stage zero the ideal is the kernel of the original closed immersion transported through an ambient isomorphism. Its source is reduced, so the kernel subscheme is reduced. At a successor the ambient transition is a blowup and the previous strict transform is reduced by induction. Its new strict-transform immersion is quasi-compact in the Noetherian ambient stage. The reducedness theorem for strict transforms then applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_comap_ι_eq_of_preimage_subset: Over the given target open, the whole inverse image of the original morphism lies in the specified source open. The restricted sources for the original and shortened maps therefore have the same open image in the original source and are isomorphic over it. Their restricted morphisms commute with this isomorphism. The kernel ideal of each restricted map is the restriction of the original kernel, and the isomorphism makes those kernel ideals equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_ker_of_iso_hom_comp: One morphism is the other precomposed with an isomorphism. On affine target opens this isomorphism preserves exactly which pulled-back sections vanish, so the kernel ideal sheaves agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_of_isClosedImmersion: A closed immersion induces the subspace topology on its source. Every subspace of a Noetherian space is Noetherian, so the source has this property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_of_isOpenImmersion: An open immersion identifies its source with an open subspace of the target. Subspaces of a Noetherian space are Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.noetherianSpace_strictTransform_of_ambie: The strict-transform inclusion is a closed immersion into the ambient stage. Since that ambient space is Noetherian, the strict-transform space is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_strictTransformι_of_noether: The source of the strict-transform immersion is an open subscheme of a closed subscheme of the Noetherian ambient scheme. It is therefore Noetherian. The inverse image of a quasi-compact open is a subset of this Noetherian space and hence is quasi-compact, giving the desired property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_comp_base: A point in the range of the composite is the image under the second map of a point in the range of the first. Conversely, any such image is obtained by applying the composite to a preimage under the first map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_strictTransformMap_subset_discarde: The discarded locus is closed by Noetherianity and is open by hypothesis, so its complement is also closed. Its image in the ambient stage is closed because the strict-transform inclusion is a closed embedding. Every point of the preceding strict-transform support off the center belongs to this image, since the discarded locus maps into the center. Pull this inclusion back along the blowdown and take closures. The new strict-transform support is the closure of the inverse image of the preceding support off the center, so every point on it maps into the ambient image of the complement. Commutativity and injectivity of the preceding strict-transform inclusion put the corresponding point of the preceding strict transform in that complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIdeal_succ_eq_strictTrans: The recursive construction defines the successor ideal as the strict transform of the preceding ideal under the current ambient blowup along its center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformι_eq_subschemeι: The strict transform is defined by its strict-transform ideal. Its immersion is the closed immersion of the subscheme defined by that ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceEmbeddingChoice_eq_affineSpac: The embedding choice assigns to each affine input exactly the datum obtained from the chosen embedding into affine space and its ambient smoothness and empty-boundary properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceEmbeddingDatum_toEmbeddedBlow: Both constructions use the same closed embedding into the chosen affine space, the same structural map, and the same principalization of the embedding kernel with empty boundary. The resulting embedded blowup sequences agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowups_eq_toSequenceOfBlowups: The construction assigns the ambient sequence by running principalization on the kernel ideal of the given embedding, with the empty boundary and the specified nonvanishing condition. Its underlying blowup sequence is the stated ambient tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centerOffDetached_eq: Restrict the pulled-back center ideal to the open complement of the detached closure. Take the inclusion of the resulting closed subscheme into that open, then include the open into the strict transform. The center off the detached locus is defined as the kernel ideal of this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapAmbientCenter_eq: The center on the strict transform is defined by pulling the ambient center ideal back along the strict-transform inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_strictTransformIdeal_le: The total transform is cut out by the pulled-back ideal on the new ambient stage. Its open part away from the center defines the strict transform by scheme-theoretic closure. A section vanishing on the whole total transform vanishes on that open part, giving inclusion in the strict-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedClosureCompl_coe: The open complement of the detached closure consists of all points outside the underlying closed set. This is exactly the set-theoretic complement on the right.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedClosure_coe: The detached locus is already closed by Noetherianity and finiteness of the component family. Its closure therefore equals the locus itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprod_succ: At the successor, the recursive coproduct adds the scheme detached at the preceding stage to the coproduct of all schemes already detached.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprod_zero: At the initial stage there are no detached schemes from earlier stages, so their coproduct is the initial, empty scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedIdeal_eq: The detached ideal is the reduced vanishing ideal of the closure of the detached locus by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocus_eq_sUnion: The detached locus is defined as the union of all the detached components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedAmbientBlowups_eq: The ambient tower of the converted sequence is the ambient blowup sequence supplied by the affine-space principalization data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedInducedBlowupsWithoutIso_eq: The unshortened induced sequences agree by the preceding comparison. Apply the operation that removes unit-center blowups to both sequences to obtain equality after shortening.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedInducedBlowups_eq: The two induced sequences use the same length, total-space tower, initial isomorphism, and centers. Their blowup certificates establish the same propositions and do not affect the sequence data. Hence the sequences agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedResolutionRuleOfPrincipalization: Expand the embedded rule as the shortened induced sequence for the chosen embedding datum. The embedded sequence for this datum agrees with the one obtained from the affine-space principalization data. The comparison identifies their shortened induced sequences, since the proofs that transitions are blowups do not change the underlying data. The latter sequence is exactly the affine resolution rule on the given input.
By definition the embedded resolution rule constructs the embedded sequence from the given datum and then takes its induced blowups with the isomorphism steps removed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_coprodIso_of_isInitial: Define the forward map on the first summand by the given isomorphism and on the initial summand by its unique map. The inverse is the inverse of the given isomorphism followed by the first inclusion. Their composite on the target is the identity by cancellation. In the other order the composite is the identity on the first summand by the same cancellation, and on the initial summand by uniqueness. The coproduct property gives the identity on the whole source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_kerSubschemeIso_of_isClosedImmers: For a closed immersion, the induced morphism from the source to its scheme-theoretic image is an isomorphism. The image is the closed subscheme of the kernel ideal. Take the inverse isomorphism and use the image factorization to obtain the stated equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_strictTransformMap: The strict-transform ideal contains the pullback of the preceding ideal. Thus the ambient blowdown restricted to the successor strict transform kills the preceding defining ideal. It factors through the preceding strict transform by the universal property of a closed immersion, giving the commuting square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_totalSpaceZeroIso: The stage-zero strict transform is the kernel subscheme of the original closed immersion transported into the initial ambient stage. Its identification with the original scheme commutes with that immersion. The stage-zero detached coproduct is initial, so taking its coproduct with the strict transform preserves this identification and yields the required isomorphism of total spaces.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_center: At every stage the induced sequence is assigned the total-space center, which is supported on the strict-transform summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_isoObjZero: The initial object of the induced blowup sequence is identified with the original scheme using the chosen stage-zero isomorphism of total spaces.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_length: The induced sequence is constructed with one step per ambient stage before the end, so its length is assigned the ambient sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_tower: The induced sequence is built with the tower of total spaces and total transitions as its underlying functor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_inr_totalTransition: The old detached coproduct is the first summand of the enlarged detached coproduct, which is the second summand of the new total space. Restrict the new transition first to the enlarged detached coproduct and then to its first summand. The two coproduct identities give inclusion of the old detached coproduct in the preceding total space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalTransition_eq_strictTransformMa: The total transition is defined on the new strict-transform summand as the strict-transform transition followed by inclusion of the preceding strict-transform summand. The coproduct projection rule gives exactly this restriction of the total map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inr_inr_totalTransition: The newly detached scheme is the second summand of the enlarged detached coproduct. Restrict the total transition to that coproduct and then to its second summand. By the defining coproduct identities the map goes through the newly detached scheme’s inclusion into the preceding strict transform and then into the preceding total space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_detachedLocus: The Noetherian strict transform has finitely many irreducible components. Each of them is closed, so the union of the subfamily of detached components is a finite union of closed sets and is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_affineSpaceIndexedBy: The structure map of finite-dimensional affine space is induced by the inclusion of the field in a finitely generated polynomial algebra. It is therefore locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_detachedComponents: A detached component is defined to be an irreducible component of the strict transform whose entire ambient image lies in the support of the current center. Membership is exactly the conjunction of these conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec_: Finite-dimensional affine space is affine and its morphism to the field spectrum is an affine morphism. Such a morphism is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIdeal_succ: The recursive successor step takes the strict transform of the preceding ideal under the current blowdown, using the current center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformIdeal_zero: The recursive strict-transform construction starts from the ideal of the original closed immersion transported into stage zero. This is the kernel of the original embedding followed by the inverse of the initial ambient isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformMap_comp_strictTransformι: The strict-transform map was chosen as a factorization of the restriction of blowdown through the preceding strict-transform immersion. Its factorization equation is the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toEmbeddedBlowupSequence_ambient:349: When the affine-space principalization data are viewed as an embedded blowup sequence, the original affine ambient scheme is assigned directly as its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toEmbeddedBlowupSequence_ambient:397: The construction from an embedding datum takes the smooth ambient scheme specified by that datum and uses it as the ambient scheme of the embedded blowup sequence.
