Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.localization_mk_eq_zero_iff: A fraction equals zero in the localization exactly when a member of the multiplicative set annihilates its numerator. This is the fraction equality criterion applied to the fraction with zero numerator and denominator one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_chartRingHom_eq_span_singleton: Every image of a member of the original ideal is a chart fraction times the image of the chart generator. Thus the extended ideal is contained in the ideal generated by that image. The generator comes from an element of the original ideal, so its image belongs to the extension and the opposite inclusion holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.opensRange_affineBlowupChart_eq_basicOpe: The image of a standard projective spectrum chart is the basic open on which its indexing homogeneous element does not vanish. Here that element is the Rees generator.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGenerator_coe_eq_C_mul_X: The Rees generator is the degree-one monomial with coefficient the chosen ideal element. A degree-one monomial is its constant coefficient polynomial multiplied by the polynomial variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGenerator_pow_one_mem_powers: The first power of the generator belongs to its multiplicative set of powers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGenerator_pow_one_mem_reesGrading_on: The first power of the Rees generator is the generator itself, which is homogeneous of degree one by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.toSpec_eq_toSpecZero_comp: The blowup projection is defined using the projective spectrum's map to the spectrum of the degree-zero part. The degree-zero ring is canonically isomorphic to the original ring, and the induced map on spectra gives the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.val_chartRingHom: In the underlying localization the degree-zero representative is taken with denominator one. This is the ordinary fraction of the specified form.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appLE_image_top_comp_appIso_hom: The open-immersion section isomorphism is the section map from the image open to the whole immersed scheme. Compose it with the restriction of the other map and use functoriality of section maps. The resulting composite is between global sections and is the stated global section map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appTop_eq_appLE_top_top: The inverse image of the whole target is the whole source. The restriction in the specified section map is therefore the identity, giving the global section map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartRingHom_comp_chartSectionsIso_hom: The blowup projection restricted to the chart is the spectrum map induced by the chart ring homomorphism. On global sections this agrees with the original ring homomorphism under the spectrum section isomorphisms. Transport the chart's sections to the image open to get the restricted map in the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartSectionsIso_hom: The chart ring is first identified with the global sections of its spectrum. The inverse of the open-immersion isomorphism on sections then identifies these with the sections on the chart image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartSectionsIso_hom_apply: Apply the defining composite to the chosen element, first using the affine spectrum identification and then the inverse of the open-immersion section isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comp_presheaf_map_eq_of_heq: Identify the open with the whole scheme and then identify the two section maps. The restriction to the whole scheme is the identity, so the composite gives the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ideal_comap_toSpec_chart_eq_span: On the affine chart image, the pullback section ideal is extension of the original ideal along the restricted section map. The chart section identity factors this ring map through the chart ring. On the chart ring the extended ideal is generated by the image of the chart generator. Transporting along the chart section isomorphism carries this generator to the stated section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_comap: Every blowup point lies on an affine chart. There the pulled-back ideal is generated by the chart generator transported to the section ring of the chart image. This generator is a nonzerodivisor in the chart ring, and the section-ring isomorphism preserves that property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.specIdealSheaf_eq_ofIdealTop: Identify the original ring with the global sections of its spectrum. The ideal sheaf is defined by transporting the original ideal to that section ring and applying the affine ideal-sheaf correspondence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.specIdealSheaf_ideal_top: The affine correspondence recovers an ideal from the global sections of its associated ideal sheaf. Here the corresponding ideal is the original ideal transported to the section ring of its spectrum.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.affineBlowupChart_preimage_basicOpen: The open immersion pulls the section on the chart image back to the corresponding global section of the affine chart. The basic-open pullback formula therefore identifies the inverse image with the basic open of that section, which is the basic open of the original ring element under the affine identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.affineBlowup_hom_ext: Choose affine neighborhoods of every source point mapping into a blowup chart under the first morphism and with its chart generator a nonzerodivisor. The second morphism has the same chart preimages because the projections agree. The chart comparison proves equality of the morphisms on each of these affine neighborhoods. They cover the source, so the maps agree globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.basicOpen_chartFraction_le_opensRange: The basic open of the transported chart fraction lies in the image of the first chart. Lift a point of this basic open back to that chart. The preimage of the basic open is the basic open of the chart fraction, and the projective overlap formula identifies it with the inverse image of the second chart. Thus the point also lies in the second chart image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.basicOpen_chartSectionsRingHom: For the chosen open, the chart element gives a section on the chart image. Pulling it back by the restricted section map gives a basic open equal to the intersection of the chosen source open with the inverse image of that section's basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartSectionsRingHom_apply: By definition one first identifies the chart ring with sections on the chart image, then applies the restricted map from those sections to the chosen source open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartSectionsRingHom_chartRingHom: The original ring mapped to chart sections agrees with the blowup projection restricted to the chart. Compose its section map with that of the source morphism. Functoriality over the specified opens identifies this composite with the map to sections induced by the morphism to the original spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.chartSectionsRingHom_mul_pow_eq: Apply the section homomorphism to the given equality in the chart ring. It preserves products and powers. On base-ring elements it agrees with the section map of the composite to the spectrum, yielding the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_specIdealSheaf_ideal: The affine formula writes the pulled-back section ideal as extension of the ideal on the whole original spectrum. That global ideal is the original ring ideal transported through the global-sections isomorphism. The two extensions combine into extension along the indicated map to sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_specIdealSheaf_ideal_eq_span: The projection's map to sections of the source open factors through the chart ring. Extension to the chart sends the original ideal to the principal ideal generated by the chart image of the chosen generator. Extending again to the source sections sends this generator to its image in the stated section ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_chart_affineOpen_mem_nonZeroDivis: Choose a chart containing the image point and an affine neighborhood of the point where the center has a nonzerodivisor generator. Take a basic neighborhood inside both. The affine chart computation and localization show that the chart generator's image and the restricted nonzerodivisor generate the same ideal on it. The chart generator's image is therefore also a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_mem_opensRange_affineBlowupChart: The chart images are the basic opens of the Rees generators, whose union covers the blowup. Membership in that union gives one chart containing the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_mul_pow_eq_chartRingHom: Write the homogeneous denominator as a power of the chart Rees generator. If the recorded degree is its exponent, the numerator is a monomial in that degree. Cross multiplication shows that multiplying the chart fraction by the corresponding power of the original generator's image gives the image of the numerator coefficient. If the recorded degree differs, the denominator's coefficient in its monomial degree vanishes, so the denominator is zero. The inverted set then contains zero, the localization is the zero ring, and the required equality holds with zero coefficient and exponent zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.fromSpec_comp_eq_of_toSpec_eq: The two maps have the same chart preimages because they have the same projection. Compare their section maps on the chosen affine into that chart. For any chart element, multiplying it by a power of the chart generator gives the image of a base-ring element. Both section maps agree on those base images. Their values on the chart element are therefore equal after multiplication by the same generator power. Cancel the power, since the generator image is a nonzerodivisor. The two induced maps on chart sections agree, so the affine morphisms into the chart agree and give the claimed equality after inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isLocalizationElem_eq_chartFraction: The normalized homogeneous localization element and the chart fraction both have the other Rees generator as numerator and the inverted generator to its first power as denominator. Their underlying fractions coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.localization_mk_one_pow: The fraction with denominator one is the image under the localization homomorphism, which commutes with powers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_sectionsRingHom_restrict: The map to sections on the smaller open is the map to sections on the larger open followed by restriction. Extension of ideals along a composite is the composite of the extensions, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_span_singleton_eq: Each generator is a multiple of the other because their principal ideals agree. Substitute one factorization into the other and cancel the generator known to be a nonzerodivisor. The two multipliers then multiply to one. Thus the other generator is a unit multiple of the first and is also a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_opensRange_affineBlowupChart_of_idea: Choose a chart containing the image point and an affine neighborhood on which the pulled-back center has a nonzerodivisor generator. Shrink to a basic open in this neighborhood contained in both the chart preimage and the open where the proposed generator spans the center. On the smaller open both chart generator images span the same ideal, also generated by the restricted nonzerodivisor. The image of the first chart generator is therefore a nonzerodivisor. The proposed generator image is the first generator image times the chart fraction. Conversely the first generator is a multiple of the proposed one. Cancel the first generator to see that the chart fraction is a unit. Its basic open contains the point, so the overlap formula puts the image point in the proposed chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_opensRange_of_mem_basicOpen_chartSec: The basic-open pullback formula puts the image point in the basic open of the chart fraction on the first chart. That basic open is contained in the image of the chart indexed by the other generator, giving the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_preimage_affineBlowupChart_iff: If the point maps into the chart, take an affine neighborhood in its inverse image. The affine chart computation shows that the proposed generator image spans the pulled-back center there. Conversely, the existence of such an affine neighborhood implies chart membership by the nonzerodivisor generator argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.preimage_affineBlowupChart_eq_of_toSpec_: The two maps to the original spectrum agree, so their pulled-back center ideals and maps to sections agree. The criterion for a point to lie in the inverse image of the chart depends only on these data. It gives the same membership condition for both morphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.restrict_basicOpen_mem_nonZeroDivisors: The sections on the basic open are the localization of the affine section ring at powers of the defining section. Localization preserves nonzerodivisors, so the restricted section remains one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.sectionsRingHom_apply: The map to the sections on the chosen open is defined by identifying the ring with the global sections of its spectrum and then applying the morphism's restricted section map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.sectionsRingHom_restrict: The restriction from the whole inverse-image open to the smaller open factors through the larger chosen open. Functoriality of the presheaf identifies the direct restriction with these two successive restrictions. Evaluate their composite with the base section map on the chosen element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.val_chartRingHom: The chart map takes the degree-zero representative of the ring element. Its underlying fraction has that representative as numerator and denominator one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.adjoin_degreeZero_eq_top_of_adjoin_eq_to: Every element belongs to the original-ring generated algebra by hypothesis. The comparison includes this algebra in the degree-zero generated algebra, so the latter contains every element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.adjoin_le_adjoin_degreeZero: The algebra generated over the degree-zero part contains each generator. Viewed as an algebra over the original ring, it therefore contains the algebra generated over the original ring by those elements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebraMap_degreeZero_apply: The algebra structure over the degree-zero part uses its inclusion in the Rees algebra, so its structure map sends an element to that same element in the full algebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebraMap_reesAlgebra_eq_algebraMap_deg: Both maps send the original ring element to its constant polynomial representative in the Rees algebra. The degree-zero equivalence uses this same representative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.finiteType_reesAlgebra_degreeZero: The Rees algebra of an ideal in a Noetherian ring is generated over the original ring by finitely many elements, using finite generation of the ideal. The same set generates over the degree-zero ring by the comparison of generated subalgebras.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isProper_affineBlowup_toSpec: The Rees algebra is of finite type over its degree-zero part, so the projective spectrum projection to that spectrum is proper. The blowup projection follows it by the isomorphism identifying the degree-zero spectrum with the original spectrum. The composite is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isProper_comp_of_isIso: An isomorphism is proper, and the composition of proper morphisms is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.locallyOfFiniteType_affineBlowup_toSpec: The affine blowup projection is proper. Local finite type is part of properness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_adjoin_degreeZero_of_mem_restrictSca: Restricting scalars of a subalgebra keeps its underlying set. Hence membership in this restricted subalgebra is membership in the original degree-zero generated subalgebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_restrictScalars_of_mem_adjoin_degree: The subalgebra with restricted scalars has the same elements as the degree-zero generated subalgebra. The given membership transfers directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.quasiCompact_affineBlowup_toSpec: A proper morphism is quasi-compact. Apply this to the affine blowup projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.universallyClosed_affineBlowup_toSpec: The affine blowup projection is proper and therefore universally closed.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appLE_comp: The section maps are contravariantly functorial. The specified containments give the compatible restrictions, so composing the two restricted section maps gives the restriction of the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appLE_top_top_eq_appTop: For the whole source and target the restriction component is the identity. The restricted section map is therefore the map on global sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appTop_ι_comp_eq_appLE_comp: Express the global section map as restriction to the whole source and target. Functoriality of restricted section maps along the open inclusion then gives the stated factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_lift_toSpec_of_isLocallyGenerated: Choose the local lifts on open neighborhoods of every point. On an overlap their projections to the original spectrum agree, and the pulled-back center remains locally generated by a nonzerodivisor because restriction to opens preserves this property. The affine blowup uniqueness theorem makes the lifts agree there. They glue to a global morphism whose projection is the original map, since that identity holds on the cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_local_lift_toSpec_of_isLocallyGen: Around the point choose an affine open where the pulled-back ideal is generated by a nonzerodivisor. This section ideal is the extension of the original ideal along the map to the open's ring. Express its generator as a combination of images of original ideal elements. After factoring out and canceling the generator, the corresponding multipliers generate one. At least one multiplier is invertible at the point. Restrict to its basic open, where the image of that original ideal element generates the localized ideal and remains a nonzerodivisor. Identify the section ring with the global sections of the open subscheme. The affine chart lifting construction now lifts the restricted map to the blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_mem_basicOpen_of_sum_mul_eq_one: If the point belonged to none of the basic opens, the germs of all the indicated sections would be nonunits and would lie in the maximal ideal of the local ring. Taking germs in the combination equal to one would then put one in that maximal ideal, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_sections_iso_globalSectionsRingHo: Take the section isomorphism of the open immersion from the open viewed as a scheme. The factorization for the global section map of the restricted morphism says precisely that this isomorphism transports the ambient section homomorphism to the global one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_sum_mul_eq_one_of_map_eq_span: The generator of the extended ideal lies in the span of the images of original ideal elements. Write it as a finite linear combination of such images. Each image is a multiple of the generator, since the extension is principal. Substitute these factorizations into the sum and factor out the common generator. It is a nonzerodivisor, so cancellation says that the resulting combination of the multipliers equals one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_affineBlowup_toS: On the affine blowup the pulled-back center is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor by the chart computation. Any morphism with that pullback property lifts by the local construction and gluing argument. Two lifts of the same map agree by the affine blowup uniqueness theorem. These are the blowup conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isIso_ι_appLE: The image of the whole open subscheme under its inclusion is the open itself. The map from its sections as an ambient open to its global sections as a scheme is thus the open-immersion isomorphism on sections, up to identification of equal opens.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebraMap_mul_invSelf: In the localization the inverse of the chosen element is the fraction with numerator one and denominator that element. Its product with the image of the element is one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebraMap_reesAlgebraLiftFun: The lift is defined by choosing a ring element whose localization image is the polynomial evaluation. The specification of this choice is the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_algebraMap_eq_polynomialEvalInvSe: The coefficient of degree i in a Rees polynomial belongs to the ith power of the ideal. Its image is a multiple of the corresponding power of the generator. Evaluating the variable at the inverse of the generator cancels this power in each monomial. The evaluated polynomial is therefore the localization image of the finite sum of the remaining multipliers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_lift_affineBlowup: The global section homomorphism extends to the chart ring by the homogeneous localization lift, since the chosen chart generator generates the extended ideal and is a nonzerodivisor. This gives a morphism from the scheme through the spectrum of its global sections to the affine chart. Compose with the chart inclusion. The chart projection corresponds to the chart structure map, and the lift agrees with the original homomorphism on that map. Naturality of the map to the spectrum of global sections then identifies the projected morphism with the original map. Its image lies in the chart by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_mul_pow_of_mem_pow: The extension of the ideal power is the corresponding power of the extended ideal. Since the extension is generated by the chosen element, its power is generated by the corresponding power of that element. The image of the coefficient is therefore a multiple of this power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.globalSectionsRingHom_eq: The ring map to global sections is defined by identifying the base ring with the global sections of its spectrum, then applying the morphism's map on global sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.homogeneousAwayLift_chartRingHom: In the ordinary localization a base element in the chart is the degree-zero Rees representative with denominator one. The lift on the localization extends the Rees lift, so it sends this fraction to the lifted value of the degree-zero representative. That value is the image under the original ring homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.homogeneousLocalizationAwayVal_apply: This map is the underlying ordinary fraction of a homogeneous localization element, by its definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isUnit_reesAlgebraLift_powers: Every denominator is a power of the Rees generator. The lift sends that generator to one, and all powers of one are units.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.polynomialEvalInvSelf_monomial: Evaluation of a monomial sends its coefficient through the ring map and multiplies it by the specified power of the inverse of the chosen section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLiftFun_add: Pass to the injective localization at powers of the nonzerodivisor. There the lift is polynomial evaluation, which preserves addition. Reflect this equality back to the original ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLiftFun_mul: After passing to the localization, the lift agrees with polynomial evaluation and thus carries a product to the product of its values. The localization map is injective because the inverted powers are nonzerodivisors. The same equality holds before localization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLiftFun_one: The localization at powers of a nonzerodivisor is injective. In that localization, the image of the lift of one is polynomial evaluation at one as a constant, which gives one. Injectivity gives the result in the original ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLiftFun_zero: In the localization, evaluation of the zero polynomial gives zero. The lift agrees with evaluation there, and injectivity of localization at powers of the nonzerodivisor gives zero before localization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLift_algebraMap: An element of the base ring enters the Rees algebra as a constant polynomial. Its lifted value in the localization is just its image under the original ring homomorphism. The injective localization map reflects this equality to the target ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLift_apply: The ring homomorphism packaging the lift is defined by the chosen underlying lift function, so its value is that function's value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesAlgebraLift_reesGenerator: The Rees generator is a degree-one monomial whose coefficient maps to the chosen generator of the extended ideal. Evaluation multiplies it by the inverse of that element and gives one. Injectivity of the localization shows that the lift already equals one in the target ring.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.existsUnique_lif: The blowup universal property applies to the given morphism because its pullback of the center is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. It gives the unique lift over the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.exists_iso: Each blowup projection satisfies the hypothesis for lifting to the other blowup, so obtain maps in both directions over the base. Each composite is an endomorphism over the base and hence is the identity by uniqueness. The resulting isomorphism commutes with the projections by construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.hom_ext_of_comp_: Both maps satisfy the same lifting equation for the given morphism. Uniqueness in the blowup universal property identifies the lifts.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.hom_ext_of_isBlo: The first blowup projection pulls the center back to an ideal locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. The two maps to the second blowup are lifts of that same projection, so they agree by the second blowup's universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.isIso_of_isLocal: The center already has the required local generators, so the identity of the base lifts to a section of the blowup projection. The other composite of this section and the projection agrees with the identity on the blowup because both lift the projection. Thus the section is the inverse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.isIso_of_top: The unit center is locally generated by the nonzerodivisor one. The isomorphism criterion for an already locally principal nonzerodivisor center gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.isLocallyGenerat: Local generation of the pulled-back center by a nonzerodivisor is part of the defining condition for a blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.iso_hom_comp: The pulled-back center is obtained from the old pulled-back center by the isomorphism, which preserves local generation by a nonzerodivisor. To lift an eligible morphism, first lift it to the old blowup, then compose with the inverse isomorphism. Any lift to the new scheme gives a lift to the old one after composing with the forward isomorphism. Uniqueness there and cancellation of the isomorphism give uniqueness here.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor.comap: At the image point take an affine neighborhood with a nonzerodivisor generator of the ideal. Its inverse image under the isomorphism is affine, with isomorphic section ring. The pullback ideal there is generated by the image of the original generator. The ring isomorphism preserves its nonzerodivisor property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appLE_eq_id_of_eq_id: After identifying the morphism with the identity, its map on sections is the identity. The restriction between the two equal opens is also the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_affineOpen_le: Affine opens form a basis. Refine the given neighborhood to an affine open containing the point and lying in that neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_id_of_isLocallyG: Pullback along the identity preserves the center and its local generators. For each morphism satisfying the pullback condition, the morphism itself is a lift to the identity projection. Any other lift equals it because composing with the identity changes nothing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_comap: On each affine neighborhood the pullback along the identity extends the section ideal along the identity ring map. Thus the original nonzerodivisor generator still generates the pulled-back local ideal.

Around a source point take an affine neighborhood mapping into a target affine neighborhood. On these affines the pulled-back unit ideal is extension of the unit ideal and is again unit. Its generator one is a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_top: Choose an affine neighborhood of any point. Its unit ideal is generated by one, which is a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.le_preimage_inv_preimage_hom: A point of the open maps under the inverse and then the forward isomorphism to itself. It therefore lies in the indicated iterated inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_iso: If the image of the element times a target element is zero, apply the inverse isomorphism. The original element then annihilates the inverse image of the other factor. Since the original element is a nonzerodivisor, that inverse image is zero. Applying the isomorphism again shows the other factor is zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.coprod: The two summands give an open cover of the target coproduct. The pullback to either summand is canonically isomorphic to its stated blowup by the summand pullback square. Thus each restriction is the blowup of the corresponding restriction of the center ideal. The blowup property descends from this open cover by the local universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.of_isIso: The unit ideal pulls back to an ideal locally generated by one. Every map to the base lifts by composing with the inverse isomorphism. Any lift must be this composite after canceling the isomorphism, so the lift is unique.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebra_smooth_of_subsingleton: A zero target ring is the localization of the source at zero, since inverting zero forces the zero ring. Localization is formally smooth, and this localization at one element is finitely presented. These properties give smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.appLE_image_bijective_of_isOpenImmersion: The section map of the immersion from the image open is an isomorphism onto sections on its inverse image. This inverse image is the original open. Restricting from it to the original open therefore changes the map only by an isomorphism. The composite is bijective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.base_comp_apply: The map on points of a composite is the composition of the two maps on points. Evaluate it at the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.bijective_of_isIso: Applying the inverse to an equality of images proves injectivity. Applying it to each target element gives a preimage and hence surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_eq_top_of_notMem_support: The support of the pullback is the inverse image of the original support. The image avoidance hypothesis makes it empty, so the pulled-back ideal is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_affineOpen_mem: The affine opens cover the scheme. The chosen point's membership in their union gives an affine open containing it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_iso_pullback_coprod_desc_left: The square for the left summand and its image open is a pullback. The unique isomorphism with the chosen fiber product, taken in the required direction, respects both projections and gives the asserted identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_iso_pullback_coprod_desc_right: The right summand square identifies its source as a pullback. The canonical isomorphism with the chosen fiber product respects both projections, which gives the required equalities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.idealSheafData_ext_coprod: Cover the coproduct by the images of affine opens from both summands. Every point lies in one summand, so this is a cover by affine opens. On a member of the cover, the equality of restrictions to that summand and the section-ring isomorphism for its inclusion give equal section ideals. Equality on the affine cover gives equality of the two sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ideal_eq_of_map_eq_of_bijective: Take an element of the first ideal. Its image lies in the image of the second. By surjectivity, this image ideal membership is witnessed by an element of the second ideal with the same image. Injectivity equates the two elements. Reversing the ideals gives the opposite containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ideal_image_eq_of_comap_eq: By the affine pullback formula, taking the two equal pulled-back ideals on the chosen open gives equal extensions of the original ideals on its image. The section map for the immersion is bijective, so equality of these extensions implies equality of the original ideals on the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isAffineOpen_image: An open immersion identifies each open with its image as a scheme. The image of an affine open is therefore affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_id_top: The identity is an isomorphism and every isomorphism is a blowup of the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_iso_hom_top: The forward map of the given isomorphism is an isomorphism, so the universal property for blowing up the unit ideal applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isPullback_coprod_inl_map: The left square commutes by the coproduct map identity. In any cone over it the first projection has image in the left source summand, so factor this projection through the left open immersion. The factorization has the required second projection after canceling the left target immersion from the cone identity. It is unique because the left source immersion is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isPullback_coprod_inr_map: The coproduct map identity makes the right square commute. The first projection of any cone lands in the right source summand and hence factors through its open inclusion. The other projection identity follows from the cone condition by canceling the right target inclusion. The right source inclusion also cancels, giving uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isPullback_inl_coprod_desc: The left square commutes by the defining factorization of the left summand map through the open. For a cone, the range constraint makes its first projection factor through the left source summand. After canceling the left target open inclusion, the cone identity gives the second projection. The factorization is unique because the left source inclusion is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isPullback_inr_coprod_desc: The right square commutes by the factorization of the right summand map through the right open. The first projection of any cone factors through the right source summand by the range constraint. Its second projection is the one required by the cone equation after canceling the right open inclusion. Cancellation of the right source inclusion gives uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isZariskiLocalAtSource_smooth: Smoothness of schemes is induced by the local smoothness property of the maps of affine section rings. The locality theorem for that ring property gives Zariski locality on the source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ker_comap_of_isOpenImmersion: On an affine open the immersion identifies its sections with those of the affine image. The preimage of the image open is the original open. Apply the affine pullback formula to the composite kernel and use the composition of section maps. Extending a kernel through the surjective section isomorphism gives exactly the first morphism's kernel on that affine. The ideal sheaves therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ker_comp_coprod_inl_comap_inl: The left summand inclusion is an open immersion. The kernel comparison for an open immersion identifies the restriction of the composite kernel with the original kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ker_comp_coprod_inl_comap_inr: The support of the kernel is the closure of the composite's image. That image lies in the closed left summand, so its closure also lies there. The right summand is disjoint from it, so the pullback of the kernel to the right has empty support and is unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ker_ideal_eq_ker_app: For a quasi-compact morphism, the scheme-theoretic kernel on an affine open is the kernel of its map on sections there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_appLE_ker_comp: The source open is exactly the inverse image of the target open, so the restriction in the first section map is the identity. The section map of the composite is the composite of the two section maps. The first section map is surjective, so extension of the composite kernel gives the second kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_ker_comp_of_surjective: The kernel of the composite is the inverse image of the second kernel under the first ring map. Extension along a surjective ring homomorphism of the inverse image of an ideal recovers that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.notMem_of_isCompl: A point in both complementary opens would lie in their intersection, which is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.preimage_image_opens: An open immersion is injective on points. Thus a point maps into the image of the given open exactly when it belongs to that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_comp_coprod_inl_subset: A point in the composite's range is the image under the left inclusion of the image of a point by the first map. Hence it lies in the left range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_fst_subset_range_inl: For each point of a cone over the left square, its first image maps into the left target summand by commutativity. A point of the right source summand would instead map into the right target summand. The two target ranges are disjoint and the source ranges cover the coproduct, so the first image lies in the left source summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_fst_subset_range_inl_of_isCompl: A point of a cone over the left open maps into that open by the cone equation. If its first projection were in the right source summand, its image under the coproduct map would lie in the complementary right open. This contradicts disjointness, so the first projection lands in the left summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_fst_subset_range_inr: The cone condition puts the image in the right target summand. If the first projection landed in the left source summand, the coproduct map would put it in the disjoint left target summand. Thus the first projection lands in the right source summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_fst_subset_range_inr_of_isCompl: The cone condition makes the image of the first projection land in the right open. A first image in the left source summand would map into the complementary left open, which is disjoint. The first projection must therefore land in the right source summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_opens_ι: The inclusion of an open subscheme has that open as its image on points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_ι_disjoint: The ranges of the two open inclusions are the opens themselves. Their intersection is empty because the opens are complementary, so there is no point in both ranges.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ringHom_smooth_of_subsingleton: View the ring homomorphism as the algebra structure on its target. The target is the zero ring, so the smoothness result for such an algebra applies to the homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.smooth_coprod_desc: Smoothness is local on the source. On each of the two open summands of the coproduct, the induced map restricts to the corresponding original smooth morphism. Thus the induced map is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.smooth_of_isEmpty: On each relevant affine source open the section ring is zero because the source scheme is empty. The restricted ring homomorphism is therefore smooth by the zero-target result. The affine criterion gives smoothness of the morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.subsingleton_presheaf_of_isEmpty: If the affine section ring were nontrivial, it would have a prime ideal. The associated spectrum point would map into the original affine open and give a point of the empty scheme. Hence the section ring is the zero ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.surjective_of_isIso: For any target element, its image under the inverse maps back to it. This provides a preimage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.comp_iso_hom: Transport the center by pulling it back along the inverse target isomorphism. Its pullback along the new projection equals the old pulled-back center because the two target isomorphisms cancel. A map to the new target is eligible exactly when its composite with the inverse is eligible for the old blowup. Lift that composite. The same map lifts to the new projection, and any such lift also gives an old lift after composing its equation with the inverse. This gives uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.exists_lift: The given pullback condition is the hypothesis of the blowup universal property. Its unique lift in particular gives a lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.hom_ext: Both maps are lifts of the same morphism under the same pullback condition. The blowup universal property gives uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.lift_comp: The chosen lift is a witness of the existence theorem. Its defining composite with the blowup projection equals the original map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.pullback_snd_of_: The center on the new base pulls back to the restriction of the old pulled-back center by commutativity. The first projection is an open immersion, so local generation by a nonzerodivisor persists. Given an eligible map to the new base, lift its composite to the original base. That lift and the given map have the same image in the original base, so together they determine a map into the fiber product. Its second projection is the given map. Any other lift has that same second projection, and its first projection must be the old lift by uniqueness. The two projections determine the map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowup.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_proj: The chosen blowup and its projection are witnesses of the existence theorem for this ideal sheaf. That choice includes the blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOverLift_comp: The chosen lift from the universal property over the open is chosen with this composite identity. Its projection is the original map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOver_hom_ext: The blowup over the open gives a unique lift of a map with this image and ideal condition. Both proposed maps satisfy its lifting equation, so they coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOver_inf_preimage: Restrict the source to the inverse image of the second open. Its image lies in both opens, and the local nonzerodivisor condition for the pulled-back ideal persists under restriction. An eligible map with image in the intersection already lifts to the old blowup over the first open. Its lift lies in the inverse image of the second open, so it factors through that restriction and has the required projection. Any competitor yields the same old lift and hence the same factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOver_localBlowupMap: The local projection is the blowup on the affine open. Following it by the open inclusion makes it a blowup over that open in the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOver_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: The composite to the ambient scheme lands in the given open. Its pulled-back center is the center from the restricted blowup, which has the required local generators. Any eligible morphism into the ambient scheme with image in the open uniquely factors through the open inclusion. The ideal condition is the same for this factorization by functoriality of pullback, so lift it to the blowup of the restricted ideal. The projection of the lift is the original map. Any competitor has the same projection into the open by cancellation of the open inclusion, so uniqueness there gives uniqueness here.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupOver_overlapMap: The first local blowup is a blowup over its affine open. Restrict its source to the inverse image of the second affine open. The restriction theorem for a blowup over an open gives a blowup over their intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comp_base_apply: The map on points of a composite applies the first point map and then the second. Evaluating at the given point gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comp_gluedIncl_eq_of_comp_localBlowupMap: The common base map lands in the intersection of the two affine opens and has the required ideal condition. Lift it to the blowup over this overlap. Its composites to the two local blowups are the stated lifts, by uniqueness on each open and compatibility of the overlap transition. Their images in the glued scheme agree by the gluing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.eq_liftGlued_of_comp_eq: On the inverse image of any base affine open, the proposed lift has image in the corresponding glued chart because its projection to the base is the original map. It factors through this chart by the open-immersion property. The factorization lifts the restricted base map to the local blowup, and local uniqueness equates it with the chosen local lift. This gives equality with the glued lift on every inverse-image open, hence globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: Take the scheme obtained by gluing the affine blowups and its glued projection. The universal property established for this projection makes it a blowup of the given ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_affineOpe: The chosen open is affine as a scheme. Apply affine blowup existence to the restricted ideal on that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_of_isAffi: An affine scheme is isomorphic to the spectrum of its global section ring. Transport the ideal to that spectrum and form its blowup there. Transport the projection back along the inverse isomorphism. The center transports back to the original ideal, so this is the required blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_spec: Apply the affine blowup existence theorem to the commutative ring underlying the stated spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_spec_of_c: Use the affine spectrum's global section isomorphism to express the given ideal sheaf as the sheaf of an ideal of the original ring. This identification follows by comparing their global section ideals. The affine Rees blowup projection has the blowup property for that ring ideal's sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.gluedIncl_comp_gluedProj: The projection is obtained by gluing the compatible local base maps. Its restriction to each local blowup is the local base map by the gluing property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.gluedIncl_jointly_surjective: The glued scheme is covered by the images of the local blowups. Choose a chart containing the given point and one of its points mapping to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.gluedProj_base_gluedIncl: Evaluate the identity for the glued projection on the local blowup at the given point. Functoriality on points gives the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.hom_ext_of_preimageAffineOpen_ι_comp: The affine opens cover the base, so their inverse images cover the source. The two maps agree on every member of this open cover and therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ideal_map_inv_map_hom: Two successive extensions of an ideal equal extension along the composite of the ring maps. The forward isomorphism followed by its inverse is the identity, which fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_gluedProj: The glued blowup is covered by the local blowup charts. On each chart the pullback of the center has local nonzerodivisor generators, because its projection is the corresponding local blowup projection. This condition descends from the open cover. Every eligible map lifts to the glued scheme by gluing its local lifts. The resulting map projects to the original map and is unique by the local uniqueness argument. Thus the glued projection satisfies the blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_localBlowupProj: The chosen local projection is a witness of affine blowup existence for the restricted ideal, so it satisfies the blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isIso_overlapIncl_self: Every point of the local blowup projects into its own base open. Thus its overlap with itself is the whole local blowup. The overlap inclusion is an open immersion with the same range as the identity, and is therefore an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_comap: The pullback along the composite is obtained by pulling back along the second map and then along the open immersion. The first pulled-back ideal has the stated local generators, and open pullback preserves them.

The triple overlap maps to the first local blowup through the first overlap projection and its inclusion. Both maps are open immersions, by base change and the overlap construction. The pulled-back center on the local blowup has the required generators, which persist under these open restrictions.
The pulled-back ideal on the inverse-image open is the restriction of the already pulled-back ideal on the original source. Its local nonzerodivisor generators persist under this restriction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isOpenImmersion_gluedIncl: The gluing construction puts each local blowup into the glued scheme as an open subscheme. Its canonical inclusion is therefore an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isOpenImmersion_overlapIncl: The overlap map into the first local blowup is the inclusion of an open subscheme, hence an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.liftChart_comp_localBlowupMap: The local lift is chosen to lift the restricted map into the blowup over the affine open. Its composite to the base equals that restricted map by the lift's specification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.liftChart_pullback_condition: On the pullback intersection of two inverse-image opens their maps to the base agree, since they are restrictions of the original map. The common map lands in both affine opens, and the pulled-back center has the generator condition because it is an open restriction. The two local lifts both project to this common map. The overlap comparison identifies their composites into the glued blowup, giving the compatibility needed for gluing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.liftGlued_comp_gluedProj: On each inverse-image open the glued lift is the local lift followed by the chart inclusion. Composing with the glued projection therefore gives the local projection of the lift, which is the restriction of the original map. Equality on the cover gives the global identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_range_gluedIncl_of_mem: Choose a representative of the point in any local blowup. Its image in the base lies in the specified affine open by the glued projection identity. The representative therefore lies in the overlap with that open's local blowup. Transport it to the other side of the overlap and use the gluing identification. Its image in the specified chart is the original point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapIncl_eq: The overlap is an open subscheme of the first local blowup, and its transition into that blowup is defined as its open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapMap_base_mem_inf: The overlap projects to the intersection of the two affine opens by the image property of its blowup over that intersection. Apply this to the chosen point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapMap_eq: The map from the overlap to the base is defined by its inclusion into the first local blowup followed by that blowup's map to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapPullbackLift_comp_overlapIncl: Both displayed composites lift the triple-overlap base map to the second local blowup. The first does so by the triple-overlap lift identity, and the other by the pairwise transition identity. The base image lies in the second open and the pulled-back ideal has the generator condition. Uniqueness of lifts there gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapPullbackLift_comp_overlapMap: The triple-overlap lift is chosen by the blowup property over the intersection of the second and third opens. Its projection is the original triple-overlap base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapPullbackMap_base_mem_inf_left: The triple overlap base map factors through the pairwise overlap for the first and second opens. Its image therefore lies in their intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapPullbackMap_base_mem_inf_right: The pullback projections have the same composite into the first local blowup. Thus the triple overlap base map also factors through the pairwise overlap for the first and third opens, whose base image is in their intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapPullbackMap_eq: The base map on a triple overlap is defined as the first projection to the pairwise overlap followed by its base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTransPullback_cocycle: Every triple-overlap transition preserves the map to the base. Hence the cyclic composite and the identity project to the same base map. Their projections into the first local blowup lift this same map, whose image lies in the first affine open and whose ideal satisfies the generator condition. Uniqueness equates the lifts into that local blowup. The two overlap inclusions into the local blowup are monomorphisms, so equality after projection there determines the map to the triple-overlap pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTransPullback_comp_overlapPullbac: The target triple-overlap base map factors through its first projection. This projection of the transition is the chosen triple-overlap lift. Its composite to the base gives the original triple-overlap base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTransPullback_comp_snd: The triple-overlap transition is a map into a pullback with the given second component. Composing with the second projection gives precisely that component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTransPullback_eq: The transition between triple overlaps is defined by the two indicated maps to the target's pairwise overlaps. Their composites to its local blowup agree by the lift compatibility, so the universal property combines them into the stated map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTrans_comp_gluedIncl: The gluing condition identifies each overlap inclusion with the inclusion from the other chart after applying the transition. This is the stated equality of composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTrans_comp_overlapMap: The transition is the chosen lift of the original overlap's map to the base into the blowup over the reversed intersection. The defining lift identity gives its composite with the overlap projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.overlapTrans_self: Compare the transition and the identity after composing with the self-overlap inclusion. Both composites are lifts to the local blowup of the same map to the base, and the pulled-back center satisfies the required generator condition. The two lifts agree. Cancel the self-overlap inclusion, which is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.preimageAffineOpenToBase_eq: The map to the base from the inverse image of an affine open is defined as the inverse-image inclusion followed by the original morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.pullback_fst_comp_localBlowupMap_eq: The pairwise overlap represents the pullback of the two inclusions into the glued scheme, so the chosen fiber product maps to that overlap with its two projections. The two maps from the overlap to the original base agree by the overlap transition identity. Precompose this agreement with the map from the fiber product to get the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.pullback_hom_ext_of_mono: Cancel the first monomorphism from the assumed identity to equate the first projections. Commutativity of the pullback gives equality of the second projections after composition with the second monomorphism. Cancel it too. The universal property then identifies the two maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_id_base: Every point is its own preimage under the identity, so the range is the whole space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_overlapMap_subset_inf_swap: Every image point of the overlap belongs to both affine opens. Interchanging the order of the two memberships gives the claimed containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_overlapPullbackMap_subset_inf: The two factorizations of the triple overlap base map put every image point in the intersection of the first two and in that of the first and third opens. It consequently belongs to the intersection of the second and third opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_overlapPullbackMap_subset_source: Every image point belongs to the intersection of the first two affine opens, hence to the first open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_overlapPullbackMap_subset_target: Every image point lies in the intersection of the first two affine opens and hence lies in the second one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.range_preimageAffineOpenToBase_subset: A point of the inverse-image open has image in the specified affine base open by definition. The restricted base map has exactly the corresponding image points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ι_base_mem: The inclusion of the open subscheme sends a point to its underlying ambient point in that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ι_comp_liftGlued: The global lift is obtained by gluing the local lifts followed by their inclusions into the glued blowup. Its restriction to the indicated inverse-image open is the corresponding local composite.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupIsIsoOffCenter: Restrict the blowup to the open complement of the center support. The restriction is the blowup of the restricted center, which is unit on this open. A blowup of the unit ideal is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_ι_support_compl_eq_top: Every point of the complement maps to a point outside the support. The restricted ideal has empty support by the pullback support formula, so it is unit.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.of_comap_of_isOp: The pulled-back cover of the proposed blowup is an open cover. On each member the pulled-back center agrees with the center of the local blowup by the commutative square. Its local nonzerodivisor property therefore descends from the cover. Given an eligible morphism, pull the cover back to its source. The center retains its local generators there, so the local blowup properties yield lifts on each member. They agree on overlaps by the local uniqueness criterion, since their projections agree and the generator condition persists on overlaps. Glue the lifts. The result projects to the given morphism by equality on the cover. The same uniqueness criterion identifies any other lift with it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsBlowupAlongIdealSheaf.restrict: The center pulled back to the restricted blowup is the restriction of the original pulled-back center, by commutation of the restriction square. Its local nonzerodivisor generators persist under open pullback. Given an eligible map to the chosen open, compose with the inclusion and lift it to the original blowup. The lift has image in the inverse image of the open, so it factors through the restricted blowup. The factorization lies over the given map by cancellation of the target open inclusion. Any other lift gives the same original lift by uniqueness and hence the same restricted lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor.comap: At the image point choose a target affine neighborhood where the ideal has a nonzerodivisor generator. Inside it choose a basic open about the point lying in the immersion image. The basic open's inverse image is affine, and the open immersion identifies the section rings on these opens. Localization preserves the original generator and its nonzerodivisor property under restriction. Transport the localized ideal and generator by the section-ring isomorphism to obtain the required local generator upstairs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.IsLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor.of_is: Lift the point to a member of the open cover and choose an affine neighborhood there with a nonzerodivisor generator. Its image is an affine open of the original scheme. The section-ring isomorphism for the immersion identifies the pulled-back ideal with the original ideal on this image. Transport the generator back along the isomorphism, which preserves the nonzerodivisor property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.eq_of_comp_eq_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: Pull the base cover back along the common projection of the two maps. On each cover member both maps lift to the local blowup because their composites into the base agree with the map through that member. The center retains its local nonzerodivisor property there because the cover inclusions are open. The local blowup's universal property identifies the lifts. Projecting back gives equality of the two maps on the pulled-back cover, hence globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.eq_span_inv_of_map_eq_span: Extend the given equality of ideals along the inverse ring isomorphism. The composite extension along the isomorphism and its inverse fixes the original ideal. The principal ideal extends to the ideal of the inverse image of its generator.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_affineOpen_mem_le: The affine opens are a basis, so the given open neighborhood contains an affine open containing the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_hom_of_isOpenImmersion_cover: The open-immersion cover pulls back to an open cover of the source. The overlap equations say that the local maps agree on intersections. Glue them to a morphism whose restrictions are the given local maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_pullback_fst_base_eq: The given point lies in the inverse image of the open immersion's image. On this inverse image the map to the base factors through the immersion. These maps define a map to the fiber product whose first projection is the inclusion of the inverse image. Apply it to the chosen point to get the preimage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.hom_ext_of_isOpenImmersion_cover: Pull the open-immersion cover back along the given base map. It covers the source, and the two maps agree on each member by hypothesis. Equality follows from the sheaf property for morphisms on an open cover.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isIso_appLE_of_image_eq: Identify the target open with the image of the source open. The restricted map on sections is then the section-ring isomorphism of the open immersion.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.blowupIsProper: Cover the locally Noetherian base by its affine opens. Each affine open has a Noetherian global section ring. The pullback over it is a blowup of the restricted center, so it is proper by the affine result. Identifying these pullbacks with restrictions gives properness on the target cover. Properness is local on the target, proving the assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.exists_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_isProper_: Apply the affine existence and properness result to the commutative ring represented by the given spectrum.

Transport the given ideal of global sections to the original ring by the affine spectrum isomorphism. The associated ideal sheaf is the given sheaf by the affine correspondence. The affine Rees blowup of this ring ideal has the required blowup property and is proper because the ring is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isNoetherianRing_sections_top_of_affineO: Sections on the affine open are Noetherian because the ambient scheme is locally Noetherian. They identify with global sections of that open as a scheme, and Noetherianity is preserved by ring isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isProper_morphismRestrict_of_isProper_pu: The pullback scheme along the open inclusion is canonically isomorphic to the inverse-image open. Under this isomorphism its second projection is the restriction of the original map. Properness is invariant under an isomorphism of the source and hence transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isProper_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: The properness theorem for blowups over locally Noetherian schemes applies to the given projection and ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.isProper_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_of_i: Identify the base with the spectrum of its global section ring and transport the center along that isomorphism. There is a proper affine blowup for the transported center. The universal properties of it and the given blowup give mutually inverse maps over the spectrum, so the given projection is a composite of the proper affine blowup with isomorphisms. It is therefore proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.locallyOfFiniteType_of_isBlowupAlongIdea: The blowup projection is proper over the locally Noetherian base. Properness implies that it is locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.map_inv_map_hom_eq_self: Extending an ideal along the isomorphism and then its inverse equals extending it along the identity. Identity extension fixes the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.ofIdealTop_ideal_top_eq_self: On an affine scheme, an ideal sheaf is determined by its global section ideal. The sheaf built from the given global ideal has that same global ideal, so it equals the original sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.quasiCompact_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: The blowup projection is proper by the locally Noetherian result, and proper morphisms are quasi-compact.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.algebraMap_mem_reesGrading_zero: The algebra map sends the element to its scalar multiple of one. The degree-zero component contains one and is closed under scalar multiplication.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.coeff_mem_pow: The defining coefficient condition for a Rees algebra element puts its ith coefficient in the ith power of the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.eq_sum_reesComponent: After viewing the Rees elements as polynomials, the stated sum is the finite reconstruction of a polynomial from its nonzero coefficients. The inclusion of the Rees algebra into the polynomial ring is injective, so the identity holds in the Rees algebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.leftInverse_coeAddMonoidHom_reesGrading: The forward map of the direct sum equivalence is addition of components. Decompose a Rees element by the inverse and add the components back. The inverse identity returns the element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_pow_one: The first power of the ideal is the ideal itself, so the given membership applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_pow_zero: The zeroth power of an ideal is the unit ideal, which contains every ring element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_reesGrading_iff_coeff: A degree-n monomial has zero coefficient at every different degree. Conversely, if those coefficients vanish, the polynomial equals the degree-n monomial built from its degree-n coefficient. Equality follows coefficient by coefficient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_reesGrading_iff_monomial: The degree-n component consists of degree-n monomials in the Rees algebra. The coefficient of such a monomial is its degree-n coefficient, which lies in the nth ideal power by the definition of the Rees algebra. Conversely, a Rees polynomial represented by such a monomial is in the degree-n component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.mem_span_reesGenerator_of_eq_monomial_su: At degree one the monomial is itself a Rees generator. At the next degree, the coefficient lies in the product of the previous ideal power and the original ideal. For a product coefficient, its monomial factors as the previous-degree monomial times the degree-one Rees generator. The previous monomial lies in the generated ideal by induction, hence so does the product. The property is preserved under sums because the monomial operation is additive in the coefficient. This proves membership for every coefficient in the next power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.monomial_mem_reesGrading: The specified coefficient gives an element of the Rees algebra by the ideal-power condition. Its other coefficients vanish, so the monomial belongs to its indicated graded component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesComponent_coe: The ith component monomial is constructed from the ith coefficient of the polynomial, so its polynomial representative is the corresponding single monomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesComponent_mem_reesGrading: The component monomial has degree i and all its other coefficients vanish. The coefficient criterion places it in the ith graded component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeOneMonomial_coe: The chosen representative is the monomial of degree one with the given coefficient, so forgetting membership in the Rees algebra gives that monomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeOneMonomial_mem_reesGrading: The coefficient belongs to the first power of the ideal since it belongs to the ideal itself. The degree-one monomial therefore lies in the degree-one component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroEquiv_apply: The ring equivalence is formed from the degree-zero ring homomorphism and its bijectivity. Its forward function is that homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroEquiv_coe_coe: The forward equivalence is the homomorphism taking the degree-zero monomial. Viewed as a polynomial, its value is the original element as a constant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroMonomial_add: The monomial construction in degree zero is additive in the coefficient. Equality of the polynomial representatives gives equality in the degree-zero component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroMonomial_mul: Multiplying two degree-zero monomials keeps degree zero and multiplies their coefficients. The polynomial identity gives the asserted identity in the component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroMonomial_one: The degree-zero monomial with coefficient one is the constant polynomial one. The inclusions of the graded component and the Rees algebra are injective, so the equality holds in the degree-zero component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroMonomial_zero: The degree-zero monomial with coefficient zero is the zero polynomial, hence the zero element of the graded component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroRingHom_bijective: The homomorphism is injective because constant coefficients recover the input, and surjective because every degree-zero element is a constant monomial. These two properties give bijectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroRingHom_coe_coe: The ring homomorphism sends the element to its degree-zero monomial. As a polynomial this is the constant polynomial with the given coefficient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroRingHom_injective: If two elements have the same degree-zero monomial, their degree-zero coefficients agree. These coefficients are the original elements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesDegreeZeroRingHom_surjective: An element of the degree-zero component has every coefficient except the constant one equal to zero. The degree-zero monomial of that constant coefficient therefore has the same coefficients as the element and equals it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGenerator_coe: The Rees generator attached to an ideal element is defined by its degree-one monomial representative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGenerator_mem_reesGrading: The generator is the degree-one monomial of a member of the ideal. The degree-one membership result applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_iSupIndep: An element in the degree-n component has every coefficient except the nth equal to zero. The sum of all other components lies in the kernel of the nth coefficient map because each of those components does. An element in both therefore has every coefficient zero and is the zero polynomial. This is independence of the graded components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_iSup_eq_top: Write any Rees polynomial as the finite sum of the monomials on its support. Each coefficient lies in the corresponding ideal power, so each monomial belongs to its corresponding graded component. The sum therefore belongs to the supremum of those components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_irrelevant_le_span: Decompose an element of the irrelevant ideal into the finite sum of its homogeneous monomials. Projection to degree zero annihilates all terms in positive degree and fixes the degree-zero term. By membership in the irrelevant ideal the projected sum is zero, so the degree-zero term vanishes. Each positive-degree monomial lies in the ideal generated by the degree-one Rees generators by the ideal-power argument. Their sum therefore belongs to that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_isInternal: The components are independent, and their sum is the whole Rees algebra. The internal direct sum criterion gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_mul_mem: Write the two homogeneous elements as monomials of their respective degrees. Their product is the monomial whose degree is the sum and whose coefficient is the product of the two coefficients. It lies in the corresponding graded component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesGrading_one_mem: The constant polynomial one is the degree-zero monomial with coefficient one, so it lies in the degree-zero component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesMonomial_coe: The Rees monomial is defined by the given polynomial monomial with its proof of membership in the Rees algebra. Forgetting that membership gives the polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.reesMonomial_mem_reesGrading: The Rees monomial is represented by a single monomial of degree n whose coefficient belongs to the nth ideal power. The homogeneous membership criterion applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.rightInverse_coeAddMonoidHom_reesGrading: Adding a tuple of homogeneous components and then decomposing it is the inverse identity for the direct sum equivalence. Thus it returns the original tuple.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_ker_subschemeι_comp: The kernel of the composite is the image ideal, so pulling it back gives an ideal contained in the original one by the general image-pullback inequality. For the other containment, its closed-subscheme inclusion factors through the original composite closed immersion because the kernels agree. The projection in the pullback defining the pullback ideal then factors through the original subscheme inclusion, using the monomorphism into the ambient target. Its kernel contains the original ideal, proving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_le_strictTransform: The strict-transform map factors through the closed subscheme of the total transform. Every section in the kernel of that closed immersion therefore vanishes under the strict-transform map. The kernels are respectively the total-transform ideal and the strict-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Fo.comap_schemeImageIdeal: The scheme image ideal is the kernel of the subscheme inclusion followed by the given closed immersion. Pulling this kernel back recovers the original ideal by the closed-immersion kernel formula.
